addons.changelog:
GSE3.3.37 (2026-11-03)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Merge pull request #2205 from LarryThiessen/fix-numeric-bind-key
#2204 Keybinds: a key stored as a number is kept as its string
• Keybinds: a key stored as a number is kept as its string
A user's Keybinds page (3.3.36) errored in loadRows, "attempt to compare
string with number": their spec's binds held [5] beside ["F"], and
table.sort cannot order the two. A number key also never bound (SetBinding
wants a string) and tripped the Action Bar's keybind migration the same way.
How the number got in is not known; nothing in the addon writes one.
GSE.RepairBindKeys (Profiles.lua), run by LoadKeyBindings before the
profile migration, moves every number key in this character's spec and
loadout binds and in every shared profile to its string, unless that string
is already bound.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1
• #2202 Fix error using an item based on range
• Merge pull request #2201 from TimothyLuke/dependabot/npm\_and\_yarn/undici-6.29.1
Bump undici from 6.29.0 to 6.29.1
• Merge pull request #2203 from LarryThiessen/fix-charge-cooldown
#2202 Action bar: a spell recharging a charge shows it on the button
• Action bar: a spell recharging a charge shows it on the button
A spell with charges showed no cooldown on a GSE button while a charge
was recharging: with a charge left the spell's own cooldown is only the
global one, and the recharge, which a bar draws on the button's charge
frame, was never set. Measured on a Druid with a 2-charge, 120 s spell:
after one cast the spell cooldown was the 1 s global one and the charge
recharge 120 s.
The recharge now goes on the button's chargeCooldown frame, as
ActionButton\_ApplyCooldown draws it (the edge), and on the cooldown frame
too, as a cooldown with its swipe and number, so the time to the next
charge shows; the spell's own cooldown shows otherwise. On Retail the
recharge comes as a duration object (C\_Spell.GetSpellChargeDuration), so
secret values in combat pass to the frame; when the object cannot be read
as active, only the edge shows. Older clients read GetSpellCharges. For
overrides on WoW's bars and the GSE Action Bar alike; the bar's own
clears of the charge frame are put back as the cooldown frame's are, and
the frame is cleared when the override comes off or the button empties.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1
(cherry picked from commit 6cfb84b12df1450bcfca1e27a2f893aa65799202)

addons.description:
GSE is an advanced macro compiler for WoW. Unlike WoW's macros, it doesn't get hung up on the success or failure of the current actions. It just sends the commands to WoW and moves on to the next line. This allows for creative approaches to overcome some of the limitations of WoW's macro system. GSE cant break the rules, but it can make them more manageable. Every command available to WoW macros is available to GSE.

GSE uses the concept of a Block of commands. For example you may want to target an enemy if you are not targeting one, cast a spell and use a trinket. In GSE, you would arrange these as a stack and, at the click, send this stack to WoW to execute. WoW will then work from the top of the stack down and attempt to execute each line. As GSE follows all Blizzard's rules, it can only try One GCD ability in the stack, but as it moves on to the next block on the next click, you can try different things in case an ability is on cooldown, etc.

GSE started as a fork of Semlar's GnomeSequencer but has since undergone multiple rewrites and there now remains nothing of the original code.
Features
• Loops
• In-game Editor
• Syntax Highlighting
• Macro Variables and WoW API incorporation
• Share Macro In-game
• Macro Debugger
• Macro Recorder
• Localisation support
• And more...
Popular Destinations
• GSE Official - For issues with GSE - https://discord.com/invite/yUS9R4ZXZA
• GSE Tools - https://gse.tools
• GSE United - For Sequences and help creating in GSE - https://discord.gg/gseunited
• GSE United Websites - For Sequences and help creating in GSE - https://gseunited.com
More Information
• GSE Wiki: https://gse.tools/help

Full Changelog Previous Releases
• #2199 Bartender override bar no longer shows GSE sequences
A LibActionButton bar (Bartender4, ElvUI, NDui) paged to a state GSE did
not take over -- the override, vehicle or skyriding bar -- kept the
sequence icon on empty slots, the watermark on every overridden button
and the sequence's tooltip, though the bar's own actions ran. The icon,
watermark and tooltip now follow overrideShowing, as the cooldown and
count already did, so that state's own action shows.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• #2166 What's New: yellow headings, white body
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_01MgTiaCHhhMgQjtZtJBiN5e
• #2197 States named and paged by the bar's own paging
Bartender4, ElvUI and EllesmereUI let the player choose which page a form
goes to, so a state is named from the bar's page driver ("5 (Prowl / Cat
Form)"), captured as bar addons register it and read back from ElvUI and
Bartender4. The State list is sorted. A bar that pages by its own driver
but is not LibActionButton (EllesmereUI) gets a State column of the pages
it sends a form or modifier to, and a row pinned to any page 1-10 runs
there; Blizzard's main bar and Dominos keep pages 7-10.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context)
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_01MgTiaCHhhMgQjtZtJBiN5e
• #2166 Show updated whats new describing actionbar changes.
• #2197 Fix wiped buttons on Bartender when trying to set different state.
• #2166 Update whats new
• #2195 #2196 A block's icon: one ranked rule for the button, editor and tracker
An icon set on the block always wins. Without one, the first spell, item
or slot named anywhere in the block, ranked: castable with no modifier,
castable under a modifier, a form/stance/stealth, a pet line; then the
same ranks for what this character can't cast (a talent not taken, a
failing [known:]). Within a rank the clause a line would fire now comes
first. GSE.GetMacroTextIconInfo is the one rule; the editor's own copy is
gone and the tracker no longer skips conditions.
The Select Icon menu names the spell as the spec has it and gains Reset,
which clears the block's icon and the pick.
Replaces #2196.

Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Release v9.6.9

• Fix paging settings not applying on spec switch or login
• added new German Localstrings
• Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main'
• Regenerate the locale key list
• Drop Mouseover override checks, clear stale toggle state
Action Bars cannot carry a Mouseover override (noOverrideMouseover), so the
two hover checks for it were dead code. When an override change takes a bar
out of the Toggle Action Bar set, its key is no longer bound, so a leftover
runtime toggle state is now cleared before the visibility pass instead of
pinning the bar until /reload. Also drops a duplicated Never check in the
data bar update.
• Honor Visibility override in hover, toggle key and drag paths
Follow-up to the effective-Never gates: the mouse-motion gate, the
non-driver Show branch, the drag mouseover surfacing and the Toggle Action
Bar key still read the saved mode. They now let an applied override decide,
and \_EAB\_Apply rebuilds the toggle key bindings so a changed override or
profile re-evaluates which bars participate.
• Fix Visibility override not showing Action Bars saved as Never
A Visibility override (spec or conditional) only reached the driver string
builder. Every gate in front of it still read the saved alwaysHidden /
barVisibility, so a Never bar with an Always or Mouseover override stayed
hidden, and an unbound Never bar never got its buttons built.
Add EAB.VisibilityCompat.IsNever(s), which lets an applied override decide
before the saved mode, and use it at every runtime gate: combat and runtime
visibility passes, the Never set, initial bar state, paging, QuickKeybind,
drag and spellbook surfacing, unlock movers, pet, extra, data and XP bars.

• Unit Frames: repaint after Dark Mode is turned off with the panel open
ReloadFramesBody ran ApplyEnemyColors, whose Engine.ForceAll repaints
every frame, before the per-frame pass re-ran ApplyDarkTheme. Turning
Dark Mode off therefore repainted with the dark color hooks still
installed, and ApplyDarkTheme then turned class coloring back on
without repainting: the player bar stayed the dark fill until the next
health event or the panel closed. Run ApplyEnemyColors last. Same single
repaint per reload, so no added cost.
• Cooldown Manager: one rebuild per gear swap, not one per slot
An equipment set fires PLAYER\_EQUIPMENT\_CHANGED once per changed slot,
and each ran a full BuildAllCDMBars (MeasureCall: about 3.5 ms), so a
3-5 slot swap stacked 10-17 ms into one frame. Coalesce them into one
rebuild on the next frame. A swap in combat still needs none: trinkets
cannot be swapped in combat, and the trinket hook already updates its
frames. If combat starts before the deferred rebuild runs (an /equipset
• opener macro), it stays pending and PLAYER\_REGEN\_ENABLED runs it.
In game: six set swaps added no Cooldown Manager frame over 5 ms.…

addons.description:
Game Controller Addon for World of Warcraft

What is ConsolePort?

ConsolePort is an interface add-on for World of Warcraft that provides features and solutions to common UX problems
in order to let you play the game on a controller - with less inconvenience.

Consisting of several independent modules, ConsolePort is a fully-fledged solution to handling all the quirks in a game where gamepad support was not intended,
including interface navigation, custom-tailored UI elements to assist in gameplay, and easy-to-use targeting systems
for end-game content. As of Shadowlands, ConsolePort uses native gamepad controls. No external software is required.

A layout saved by a newer build can carry fields and element types this
build has no definition for. Nested Table.Set now honours the silent
flag the interface already passes at the top level, unknown element
types are skipped, and each element upgrades under pcall so one bad

• Alias a blocked chord to the tap key the engine dispatches it as
A chord holding a button's own modifier never fires; the engine emits the
button's tap without that modifier. The bar already registers the
complement action under the blocked key, but the row swap on a modifier
press released the plain tap claim before the engine dispatched the tap,
so it fell through to the stored ACTIONBUTTON binding on Blizzard's
hidden button. Claims and releases now map blocked keys to their tap key.
(cherry picked from commit d29066cba62c83a86e3ea2da4e9d862b618dd0b9)
• Expose strata and level for artwork
Art used the simple position type, so its strata and level couldn't be
set in the designer, unlike dividers and glyphs which share the same
frame setup. Artwork in MEDIUM strata covers other addons' frames placed
over it, such as a detached unit frame portrait; with the complex
position type it can be moved to a lower strata or level.
Saved layouts are filled with interface defaults on load, so Art
defaults to level 1, where it sits today (one below group bars), instead
of the complex type's level 2.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Rename loadout elements in the bar designer
Elements in the Loadout list could only be copied or deleted, so
reorganizing a layout meant copying an element to the new name and
deleting the old one. A rename button on every element does both in one
step, using the copy popup's name validation. Unique elements get it too,
since a rename doesn't duplicate them.
The element is stored as a copy under the new name, like Copy does:
widgets listen to their props table, so moving the same table would keep
the released frame subscribed and the designer would highlight it too.
Bars are named after their element, so a renamed bar gets a new frame
name. Bindings and action slots don't depend on it.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Allow more than one pet ring
The pet ring was the only unique element besides the toolbar, and its
factory always returned one global frame whatever the element ID, so a
second entry would have driven the same ring. Each element now gets its
own frame. The first ring keeps the ConsolePortBarPetRing name; further
rings are named after their element, like group bars. The toolbar stays
unique.

Edit Mode selections and account setting checkboxes write

addons.changelog:
Polestar 0.3.0 is our biggest release yet, and its heart is a complete overhaul of the leveling routes: routes that make sense. Every step is the one you'd pick yourself, with nothing pointless in between. Each race plays its own starting zone, then one route per faction carries you on from the Barrens or Westfall all the way to 60, and every route was built, checked step by step the way a player follows it, and reviewed round after round before it shipped.

Around the routes, almost everything else grew too: the guide now follows what the game confirms, the arrow walks real paths, every class, profession, reputation, mount, pet and exploration guide has been rebuilt or reviewed against Forever's data, and there's a new look with new map icons and a long list of new helpers. Alongside it come the Polestar Client, a home for community guides on polestar.guide, and a recording program you can join to help improve the routes.

Polestar is still a beta. If something's off, tell us on Discord or GitHub Issues.
Install or update
• With Polestar Client: it installs and updates Polestar for you. Get it at polestar.guide/client.
• With the CurseForge app: update Polestar Guides.
• By hand: download Polestar-0.3.0.zip below (not "Source code"). Delete every old Polestar folder from World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ (forever from launch), then unzip this one there.
• Then quit the game completely and start it again: this release adds addon folders, and a /reload doesn't load new ones.

Polestar_Recorder-0.3.0.zip is the optional Recorder for the recording program (below); Polestar Client installs it for you if you join. SHA256SUMS holds the checksums.
Leveling routes, rebuilt from the ground up
• Your race's own start, then one route for your faction. Every race levels through its own starting zone and joins the shared Horde route in the Barrens or the shared Alliance route in Westfall. Every fix and improvement now reaches every race at once.
• Towns in one visit. At a town or camp you pick up and hand in everything that's ready while you're there, and quests waiting where a flight, a deathskip or your hearthstone lands you are handed in on arrival.
• Work on the way. Quests whose mobs share the same ground are done together in one sweep, and quests you pass on the road are picked up as you pass them, not on a trip back.
• Training where you already are. Class training sits where the route already passes your trainer, weapon trainers come up "while you're here", and riding is learnt at 40 on a visit the route makes anyway.
• The hearthstone used properly. The guide sets your hearth where it will need it next, and never asks you to use it while it's cooling down or bound somewhere else.
• Elite and group quests, your call. They ask whether you have a group, say how many you need, and always leave a solo way past, with the guide keeping you on the route's levels if you skip one.
• Rare drops never hold you up. Quests that start from a rare drop are optional extras you take only if the drop comes.
• Every order players reported, followed. Each report about a route became a permanent fix that every future build keeps, from Tirisfal's Brill to the Barrens' Crossroads.
• Travel that makes sense. Real zone crossings instead of over mountains, boats and portals used where they belong, a flight only from a flight master you know, and level gates where a quest needs a level you might not have yet.
A guide that follows the game
• Steps move on only when the game confirms them: a quest taken or handed in, an item looted, a spell learnt. Opening a window or talking to an NPC no longer ticks anything off.
• In a quest hub every goal of the step stays listed while the arrow moves from person to person.
• A quest its giver doesn't offer is never quietly skipped; the guide tells you and asks you to report it.…

A free, open-source guide addon for World of Warcraft: Forever: step-by-step leveling routes for every race from 1 to 60, a waypoint arrow that walks real paths, and guides for class quests, professions, reputations, mounts and pets.

polestar.guide: every guide, community guides and the docs ·
Polestar Discord: questions, feedback and bug reports ·
Polestar is free; if it saves you a few hours, you can buy me a coffee.

Quick start ·
What it is ·
A look inside ·
polestar.guide ·
Community guides ·
Polestar Client ·
Features ·
Help ·
How the routes are made ·
Building from source ·
Contributing ·
Data and licensing

Play
Install the addon and follow the arrow.
Browse the guides
Every guide, step by step, on polestar.guide.
Write guides
Publish your own routes as a community guide.
Work on Polestar
Fix a guide, build the addon, run the tests.

Quick start
1. Install it one of three ways:
• The CurseForge app: search for
Polestar Guides and
install it, then skip to step 3.
• The Polestar Client: a small app for
Windows, macOS and Linux that finds the game, installs Polestar and keeps
it up to date, community guides included. Skip to step 3.
• By hand: download Polestar-.zip from the
newest release,
under Assets (not "Source code").
2. Unzip it into the game's AddOns folder, so the Polestar folders
(Polestar, Polestar_Guides, Polestar_Codex, Polestar_Nav and the
others, with one Polestar_ folder per client language such as
Polestar_deDE) sit directly inside it:
World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ on the beta client,
forever/Interface/AddOns/ on the forever client. The same zip
works for both; if you have both clients installed, unzip into each one.
In the game's AddOns list they all sit under one "Polestar" heading,
which its arrow folds away.
3. Restart the game completely (a /reload does not load new addons) and
log in. The guide window opens with a guide for your race, level and zone:
follow the arrow, and the goals tick themselves off as you play.

Good to know:
• /polestar guides opens the hub: every guide, Lookup, Dungeons, Talents
and Rares. /polestar options holds every setting; quest markers on the map
are off until you turn them on under Map. Right-click the minimap
button for a short menu.
• /polestar skip moves on for good; /polestar next and prev only look
ahead or back.
• Updating: the CurseForge app and the Polestar Client update Polestar for
you. By hand, delete the old Polestar folders, then unzip the new release
the same way. Coming from 0.2.x, also delete the Polestar_Guides_deDE,
Polestar_Names_deDE kind (one of each per language): Polestar_deDE and
its siblings replace them, and Polestar reminds you at login while they are
still there.
• Memory: the arrow's walking routes (Polestar_Nav) load after login,
never in combat, and each continent's walking maps load when you get there.
Walk real paths (Options, Arrow & routes) off never loads them.
• Optional: Polestar_Recorder (Polestar_Recorder-.zip in the
same release, or from the Polestar Client) records your play for the
recording program that improves the routes. It stays off until you start
sharing in the Polestar Client or type /psrec on.
• Community guides are routes other players publish for Polestar, on
polestar.guide: see
Community guides.
• Something wrong? Click the bug in the guide window, beside Skip: say what
went wrong; the report already holds the step, where you stand, your other
addons and the versions. Copy report and post it in #bugs on the
Polestar Discord: a bot files it for the
developers and replies in your thread when it's fixed. Get the invite is
there if you're not in the Discord yet. Have a GitHub account?
Open on GitHub pre-fills a new issue with your report. /polestar report
opens the window too, and issues
are welcome as well. The release's SHA256SUMS holds the zips' checksums.
What it is
Polestar is one addon for the whole of WoW: Forever. It carries 256 guides:…

Alongside it come the Polestar Client, a home for community guides on polestar.guide, and a recording program you can join to help improve the routes.

Polestar is still a beta. If something's off, tell us on Discord or GitHub Issues.
Install or update
• With Polestar Client: it installs and updates Polestar for you. Get it at polestar.guide/client.
• With the CurseForge app: update Polestar Guides.
• By hand: download Polestar-0.3.0.zip below (not "Source code"). Delete every old Polestar folder from World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ (forever from launch), then unzip this one there.
• Then quit the game completely and start it again: this release adds addon folders, and a /reload doesn't load new ones.

Polestar_Recorder-0.3.0.zip is the optional Recorder for the recording program (below); Polestar Client installs it for you if you join. SHA256SUMS holds the checksums.
Leveling routes, rebuilt from the ground up
• Your race's own start, then one route for your faction. Every race levels through its own starting zone and joins the shared Horde route in the Barrens or the shared Alliance route in Westfall. Every fix and improvement now reaches every race at once.
• Towns in one visit. At a town or camp you pick up and hand in everything that's ready while you're there, and quests waiting where a flight, a deathskip or your hearthstone lands you are handed in on arrival.
• Work on the way. Quests whose mobs share the same ground are done together in one sweep, and quests you pass on the road are picked up as you pass them, not on a trip back.
• Training where you already are. Class training sits where the route already passes your trainer, weapon trainers come up "while you're here", and riding is learnt at 40 on a visit the route makes anyway.
• The hearthstone used properly. The guide sets your hearth where it will need it next, and never asks you to use it while it's cooling down or bound somewhere else.
• Elite and group quests, your call. They ask whether you have a group, say how many you need, and always leave a solo way past, with the guide keeping you on the route's levels if you skip one.
• Rare drops never hold you up. Quests that start from a rare drop are optional extras you take only if the drop comes.
• Every order players reported, followed. Each report about a route became a permanent fix that every future build keeps, from Tirisfal's Brill to the Barrens' Crossroads.
• Travel that makes sense. Real zone crossings instead of over mountains, boats and portals used where they belong, a flight only from a flight master you know, and level gates where a quest needs a level you might not have yet.
A guide that follows the game
• Steps move on only when the game confirms them: a quest taken or handed in, an item looted, a spell learnt. Opening a window or talking to an NPC no longer ticks anything off.
• In a quest hub every goal of the step stays listed while the arrow moves from person to person.
• A quest its giver doesn't offer is never quietly skipped; the guide tells you and asks you to report it.…

Polestar 0.2.6 brings guides that adapt to your character (steps that only show when they apply, goals done along the way, loops and half-level goals), talent plans for every class, sparkle route lines, a Miscellaneous category with the Cozy Sleeping Bag and Library Books, import strings for sharing a small guide as one line of text, skull markers on the mobs your step needs, and an arrow that no longer jerks at every bend in the road. Quest givers, hand-ins, objective counts and dungeon quest XP are corrected from Forever's quest data, and most route reports since 0.2.5 are fixed. Thank you to everyone who reported, tested and sent pull requests: much of this release came from you.

The WoW Forever skin is hidden for now while we fix its border; if you used it, you'll see the default skin until it returns. Still a beta: delete your old Polestar folders before unzipping, then restart the game fully.

Polestar is still a beta. If something's off, tell us on Discord or GitHub Issues.
Install or update
• With the CurseForge app: update Polestar Guides.
• By hand: download Polestar-0.2.6.zip below (not "Source code"). Delete every old Polestar folder from World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ (forever from launch), then unzip this one there.
• Then quit the game completely and start it again if the release adds an addon folder: a /reload doesn't load new addon folders.

Polestar_Recorder-0.2.6.zip is optional. SHA256SUMS holds the checksums.
For players
• On a quest's "Complete" line with no place of its own, the arrow no longer goes blank: it stays on the spot the step sent you to, or on the quest's giver, until the quest is done (#256).
• The arrow no longer jerks left and right at every little bend of a road: it looks up to 30 yards ahead along the path and only turns for corners that leave a 10 yard corridor, still turning at real corners and never past a floor change or a lift (thanks AURUM and Hotline from the Polestar Discord)
• Ashenvale: Alonso's Dragonslayer quests at Mystral Lake no longer hold a character he does not offer them to. Both guides lead everyone to him; take the quests if he offers them, else carry on (thanks Zerkness and Ioney; first fix by c0njure).
• Ashenvale (Alliance): Elemental Bracers counts the five Intact Elemental Bracers before the Divined Scroll, so the target button finds the Befouled Water Elementals (thanks Tazul, #391).
• Items in your bags that are an upgrade for your spec now carry the same green arrow as quest rewards, in the game's bags and in Baganator (Options, Questing, Rewards & gear: Upgrade arrows in bags). The tooltip already said so; now the bag shows it at a glance (thanks Leducia).
• Guide window: a new "Bar at the bottom" option puts the tabs and the step bar at the bottom edge when the window grows upward, next to where it is pinned, so they stay in one place as steps get longer. Off by default (thanks thmastin, and the player on Discord who asked for it, #386).
• The Barrens: the Savannah Lion Hide arrow stays in the Dry Hills, where the Sprung Traps of the same step are, instead of wandering off to the Matriarchs by Ratchet (thanks Fitz; fix by thmastin).
• With "Skip grey quests" on (Options), a guide opened on a character who already did part of the route catches up: the guide window goes over every step already done, faster and faster, while the arrow turns an hourglass over, and stops where you are. Green quests behind your progress that you have not taken are left out too, unless a later quest needs them. With no guide open, or from Start guide, a guide you are past hands over to the next one; the first time, the guides go by from your race's first one. A guide you open yourself stays open where you are. Item, mount, reputation, profession and class guides do every step.
• Chinese and Russian clients now translate missing transport-wait and option labels and the Library Books guide title (thanks HershelW).…

Polestar 0.2.5 brings skins, a new walking router you can tune, the whole addon and every guide in nine languages, full gamepad support, and fixes for nearly every route report since 0.2.4. Thank you to everyone who reported a wrong step, sent a /polestar report or opened a pull request: much of this release came from you.

Still a beta: every guide plays to the end in our simulator for every race and class, and your reports keep the routes honest. Delete your old Polestar folders before unzipping, then restart the game fully.
Skins
New looks under Options › Appearance › Windows › Skin. Polestar's own look stays the default.
• Halo: no frame, a dark veil with soft edges under the text, the game's gold, Fira Sans.
• Hearth: Polestar in warm game colours, with the game's red buttons, check boxes and font.
• WoW Forever, Blizzard and Classic: Polestar drawn in the game's own art: Forever's bronze frames, header rods and plates; retail's metal window frame and minimal controls; Classic's original dialog box, tooltip borders, panel buttons and tabs.

Every window takes the skin, and so does the arrow ("The skin's arrow": a dart that turns green within 40 m, then a ring and a check on arrival; the 3D and flat arrows can still be picked). The font follows the skin unless you pick one.
A new walking router, with a route style
• Walks keep to roads where they aren't much longer, go round steep slopes instead of over them, and stay out of the other faction's towns. When a walk must enter one, the arrow says "Hostile town: Southshore" once.
• Walks keep out of zones far above your level, unless your walk starts or ends there or there's no other way.
• The walk starts from the ground you're standing on, not a roof, rock top or upper floor above you.
• Route style (Options › Guide › Arrow & routes, or the new page in the welcome): Fastest takes the shortest walk over hills and across fields; Balanced (the default) keeps to roads that aren't much longer; Roads stays on roads even when longer.
• The arrow's walk to a trainer, vendor or innkeeper ends on that NPC's floor (the warrior trainer inside Northshire Abbey, not outside it), and boats lead onto the pier beside the ship instead of into the water.
• On a long zone crossing (the Gold Road from the Barrens into Ashenvale), the arrow no longer turns you back once you've walked past the near end.
• Where two zone maps overlap, the arrow leads to people on the map of the zone they really stand in: Kadrak at Mor'shan, Tirion Fordring's hut, the Syndicate camps in Alterac, Tal and Cairne in Thunder Bluff, and more.
Nine languages
• Every guide's titles, tips and notes now read in your game's language on German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Chinese (simplified and traditional) clients, with every NPC, place, item and quest named exactly as your client names them.
• Every interface text shows in your language on all nine clients. French by Yendi, German reviewed by thecodingcortex, Spanish (Spain) by julen92 and Forever Hispano, Spanish (Latin America) by CDVolvik; Options › About says so where a translation was made with AI.
• Forever's own quests, NPCs, objects and items, instances, bosses, factions and flight points use the game's names. Reputation standings, item qualities, gear slots and race names read exactly as the game writes them.
• Setting your home, discovering a flight path, hearthing and flying now complete their steps on non-English clients, and names no longer stay in English when the names pack loads late.
• Settings help lines wrap instead of being cut, and labels make room for longer languages.
Gamepad
• Polestar's windows work with a gamepad, with a new Gamepad page: button names (Xbox letters or PlayStation shapes) and bindings for any Polestar action to a key, a button or a chord. "Browse the guide with the gamepad" lets the D-pad pick a goal. Ported from Ding! by Yendi.…

Test build 2. Not the release. An early build of Polestar 0.2.5 for community testing. CurseForge and the "latest" release stay on 0.2.4.
New since test build 1: no English on non-English clients
• Guides in your language. Every guide's titles, tips and notes are translated into German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. Every NPC, place, item and quest in the text is named exactly as your game names it.
• Every screen uses your game's names. The guide window, Lookup, Dungeons, Rares, Nearby, gear tooltips, travel and the journey panel all show names in your language. Forever-only NPCs are learned the moment you meet them.
• Complete interface translations in all nine languages, including the AddOns list.
• Text is never cut off. Settings, labels, dropdowns and the rare alert make room for longer languages.
• Contributors: the German interface is complete thanks to Peter, the French thanks to Yendi, and the Spanish (Spain) is reviewed by julen92.

The guide texts and six of the interface languages are AI-made for now. If you're a native speaker, tell us what reads wrong.
Install

2. Delete every Polestar folder in Interface/AddOns.
3. Unzip Polestar-0.2.5-test.2.zip there.
4. Start the game again (a full restart, not /reload).

Report problems with the in-game report button, and mention test build 2.

addons.description:
Do you find yourself completing old content just so that you can get literally everything for your Collections? Say no more! ALL THE THINGS will help you with your endeavor by giving you the ability to track your completion for everything.
Features
• Supports tracking of Achievements, Quests, Appearances, Mounts, Pets, Toys, Titles, Decor, and much more.
• Primary Collections Window is movable and resizable.
• Auto Minilist
• Datatext Support
• Multiple Database modules to keep the addon from having to access the Blizzard API.
• Filters to allow you to customize the addon to your preferences.
• Extra tooltip information (Models, Icons, Descriptions, etc.).
• Fanfare music when you learn anything new.
Release Schedule
There are two release types: alpha builds and official releases.
• Alpha Build
• Released at 7:00 UTC every day.
• Official Release
• Scheduled every Sunday.
• Expected to be updated on the first day of any major WoW update, with frequent releases in the following days.

The git version is not a release, but it is still supported.
Why do I need this addon?
• Ability to see what items you are missing from your collection in a more presentable way than Blizzard's UI.
• The UI has information on quests, vendors, rares, dungeons and raids, world events, and more.
Problem? Suggestion?
If you just updated and are getting tons of errors, completely close your game and then reopen it. Updating addons while the game is running can cause problems!

addons.changelog:
Version: 4.24
2026/11/03 Released
❗ Important
• Minimum supported ElvUI version raised to 16.01.
💪 Improvement
• [Unit Frames] Dispel Overlay border now marches. Slot updates that start in combat wait until combat ends.
• [Extra Item Bar] Item list updated for 12.1.5: new openable containers and delve items, soul fragments only at 3 or more. Nebulous Void Cache entries were removed because they are hidden bonus-roll trackers.
• [Event Tracker] Midnight weekly labels for Silvermoon Court, Zul'jarra's Forces, and Slayer's Duellum now use the localized faction name.
• [Context Menu] Guild Invite, Who, Armory, and Report Stats stay hidden when the unit name is secret, so the menu does not error.

版本: 4.24
2026/11/03 发布
❗ 重要
• 最低支持的 ElvUI 版本提升到 16.01.
💪 改善
• [单位框体] 驱散覆盖的虚线边框现在会流动. 战斗中开始的更新会等到脱离战斗后再执行, 避免报错.
• [额外物品条] 更新了 12.1.5 的物品列表, 新增可打开容器和地下堡物品. 灵魂碎片仅在数量达到 3 个或以上时显示. 已移除晦暗虚空宝箱, 它们是隐藏的额外拾取追踪, 不是可使用物品.
• [事件追踪] 至暗之夜每周任务标签 Silvermoon Court、Zul'jarra's Forces 和 Slayer's Duellum 现在使用本地化的阵营名称.
• [右键菜单] 单位名称为秘密值时, 会隐藏公会邀请、查询、英雄榜和报告属性, 避免菜单报错.

版本: 4.24
2026/11/03 發布
❗ 重要
• 最低支援的 ElvUI 版本提升到 16.01.
💪 改善
• [單位框架] 驅散覆蓋的虛線邊框現在會流動. 戰鬥中開始的更新會等到脫離戰鬥後再執行, 避免報錯.
• [額外物品條] 更新了 12.1.5 的物品列表, 新增可打開容器和探究物品. 靈魂碎片僅在數量達到 3 個或以上時顯示. 已移除晦暗虛空寶箱, 它們是隱藏的額外拾取追蹤, 不是可使用物品.
• [事件追蹤] 至暗之夜每週任務標籤 Silvermoon Court、Zul'jarra's Forces 和 Slayer's Duellum 現在使用本地化的陣營名稱.
• [右鍵選單] 單位名稱為秘密值時, 會隱藏公會邀請、查詢、英雄榜和屬性報告, 避免選單報錯.

버전: 4.24
2026/11/03 Released
❗ 중요 사항
• 최소 지원 ElvUI 버전이 16.01로 상향되었습니다.
💪 개선 사항
• [유닛프레임] 해제 오버레이의 점선 테두리가 이제 움직입니다. 전투 중에 시작된 칸 갱신은 전투가 끝난 뒤에 적용됩니다.
• [아이템 바] 12.1.5 아이템 목록을 갱신했습니다. 열 수 있는 용기와 구렁 아이템을 추가했고, 영혼 조각은 3개 이상일 때만 표시됩니다. 숨겨진 보너스 주사위 추적기인 Nebulous Void Cache 항목은 제거했습니다.
• [이벤트 추적기] 미드나이트 주간 표시인 Silvermoon Court, Zul'jarra's Forces, Slayer's Duellum이 이제 현지화된 진영 이름을 사용합니다.
• [컨텍스트 메뉴] 유닛 이름이 비밀 값이면 길드 초대, 누구, 전투정보실, 내 스탯 전송을 숨겨 메뉴가 오류를 내지 않습니다.

Версия: 4.24
2026/11/03 Релиз
❗ Важные
• Минимальная поддерживаемая версия ElvUI повышена до 16.01.
💪 Улучшения
• [Фреймы юнитов] Пунктирная рамка наложения рассеивания теперь движется. Обновления слотов, начатые в бою, выполняются после выхода из боя.
• [Панель дополнительных предметов] Список предметов обновлён для 12.1.5: добавлены открываемые контейнеры и предметы вылазок, осколки душ показываются только от 3 штук. Записи Nebulous Void Cache убраны: это скрытые отслеживатели бонусного броска, а не используемые предметы.
• [Трекер событий] Подписи еженедельных заданий Полуночи для Двора Луносвета, Сил Зул'джарры и Дуэлянтов Зубца убийцы теперь берут локализованное название фракции.
• [Контекстное меню] Приглашение в гильдию, Кто, Оружейная и Статистика отчетов скрываются, если имя юнита скрыто, чтобы меню не вызывало ошибку.

addons.description:
A WoW Classic addon for leveling guides with automatic progress updates
What does it do?
Guides are shown as a list of steps where the progress is updated automatically as much as possible (quests picked up / completed, quest
items looted / mobs killed, etc). Only for some steps completion has to be confirmed manually (such as resupplying, getting new skills, etc).
Locations referenced in the guide are shown on the map and minimap. Also there is an arrow pointing in the direction towards the next step.

World of Warcraft Forever will be fully supported and guides are already being worked on.

It completely supports Burning Crusade Classic and Wrath of the Lich King Classic. There are guides for Draenei, Blood Elf, and Death Knight starting zones, as well as Alliance and Horde Outland and Northrend guides.

Cataclysm Classic is supported as well. Currently there are guides for the Worgen starting zone and for the new zones for leveling from 80 to 85. Unfortunately due to the world revamp old guides for leveling from 1 to 60 will not be useful anymore. Stay tuned for new guides for leveling 1-60.

For Mists of Pandaria Classic there are guides for the Monk starting zones as well as guides for leveling from 85-90.

The addon comes with an editor so even if the number of guides included is small (yet) it is very easy to create your own guides or to import
your favorite guide.

This is for WoW Classic only. It will not run on private servers and/or retail.
Where do I find guides for the addon?
See list of all available guides for a complete list of guides that have been written for Guidelime so far.
How do I write a guide?
How do I write a guide?
How do I publish a guide?
How do I publish a guide?
How do I install the addon?
When you download the zip file from this page (click "Clone or Download" then "Download Zip") you will find a Guidelime folder (inside the Guidelime-master folder). Copy this folder into your Addons folder.

By using this method you will always get to most recent version of the addon (master) including all changes that are being made as soon as they are published.

Alternatively you can also download the addon from https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/guidelime or install it via the CurseForge client or any other addon manager. This way you will get the latest stable release. (Which currently is also being updated in average once a day.)
How do I install a guide?
To install a guide please visit the list of guides mentioned above.

You install a guide the same way you would install any other addon: Copy the folder containing the guide into your Addons folder (in the same folder where the Guidelime folder is in).

You can also use the CurseForge client or other addon manager to install a guide.
What is missing?More guides
If you are a guide creator and you have your own guides that you would like to see in Guidelime feel free to contact me.
Localization
The addon is currently available in English, German, French, Russian and Chinese. If anyone would volunteer to do translations for other languages please contact me.

The guides itself are language specific. Most guides are available in English language only. But using the editor you can create guides in your own language.
How do I open the window again after I closed it accidentally?
Type /lime or go to Interface Options, AddOns, Guidelime, Options and click on show window.

addons.description:
Join the official TellMeWhen Discord! https://discord.gg/NH7RmcP

Ask questions, share configuration, or just hang out.
Find a bug? Have a feature request? Please open an issue on GitHub

TellMeWhen is a WoW addon that provides visual, auditory, and textual notifications about cooldowns, buffs, and pretty much every other element of combat. TellMeWhen is...
Flexible
Icons can track any of the following things:
• Cooldowns
• Buffs/Debuffs
• Reactive abilities
• Multi-state abilities
• Temporary weapon enchants
• Totems/Wild mushrooms/Ghouls/Lightwell
• Rune cooldowns
• Internal cooldowns
• Others' cooldowns
• Diminishing returns
• Spell casts
• Loss of Control effects
• ...And any combination of over 110 other things with easy-to-use conditions.
Customizable
• Icons can be set to show or hide based on the status of their basic element and their usability based on range, duration, stacks, and resources.
• All icons can show the standard cooldown animation to display their status, and are compatible with OmniCC.
• There are over 110 conditions that can be configured to make an icon show only under very specific or very general circumstances.
• You can set a sound to play when important attributes of an icon change.
• You can also set text to be announced/displayed when an icon's attributes change.
• Icons can show at different transparency levels based upon the usability/existence of what they are checking.
• Icons can show status bars on top of them, indicating the required resources and their remaining cooldown/duration in a different way.
• Icons can be skinned with Masque (formerly ButtonFacade).
•
Instructions
To lock and unlock TellMeWhen, type "/tmw" or "/tellmewhen".

When you first log in with TellMeWhen installed, you will see one group of four icons in the center of your screen. To begin using TellMeWhen, right-click on one of these icons, and the icon editor will appear. You need to select an icon type from the dropdown menu and enable the icon, and then configure the icon to suit your needs based on the settings that are available. An explanation of what most settings do can be found in the tooltip displayed when you mouse over a setting.

You can also drag spells from your spellbook, your pet's spellbook, or items from your inventory to quickly set up a cooldown icon for that spell/item. Icons can be spatially manipulated by holding down the right mouse button and dragging them around. When they are dropped on another icon, a menu will appear asking you what you want to do with the icon - Options include Move, Copy, and Swap.

General settings can be accessed via '/tmw options', the Blizzard interface options, or the 'Group Settings' tab of the icon editor.

All available slash commands are:
• '/tmw' - Toggles TellMeWhen between locked (functional) or unlocked (configuration) states.
• '/tmw options' - Opens the general settings configuration for TellMeWhen.
• '/tmw profile "Profile Name"' - Loads a TellMeWhen profile. Profile name is case sensitive, and must be quoted if it contains spaces. (E.g. '/tmw profile "Cybeloras - Aerie Peak"').
• '/tmw enable global|profile groupID iconID' - Enables the specified group or icon (E.g. '/tmw enable 2 4' or '/tmw enable global 3').
• '/tmw disable global|profile groupID iconID' - Disables the specified group or icon (E.g. '/tmw disable profile 2 4' or '/tmw disable 3').
• '/tmw toggle global|profile groupID iconID' - Toggles the specified group or icon between enabled and disabled (E.g. '/tmw toggle global 2 4' or '/tmw toggle profile 3').
• '/tmw counter counter-name +|-|/|*|= number' - Mutate a TMW counter. Counters can be checked in conditions or displayed on icons. (E.g. '/tmw counter casts = 0' or '/tmw counter phase + 1')
• '/tmw cpu' - Enables and displays a UI for measurements of icon performance. This is an advanced feature; no guidance on reading the data will be offered.

addons.description:
BetterBags is a bag replacement addon for World of Warcraft, inspired by AdiBags.
It has a fresh, clean look, updated to the 2026 World of Warcraft art style.

It currently includes most of the features of AdiBags and is being worked on daily.
If you have any feedback, please let us know in the Discord.

BetterBags currently supports the following versions of World of Warcraft:
Retail (including Midnight and the various WoW: Remix versions as they come out)
Classic (Era, MoP Classic, SoD, BC Anniversary, etc.)
Screenshots
The Retail main player bag view with multiple custom categories.

Currency selection in Retail.

Configure Categories in Retail, allows you to pin and sort categories.

Extensive View options that can be fine-tuned by the user.

Summary
• Items are organized into categories and displayed in a Section Grid.
• Optionally, categories are organized into groups/tabs.
• Support for bags, bank, reagent bank, and Warband bank.
• The bag and bank can be anchored to a location and grow in specified directions.
• Customizable categories that hold items with multiple sorting options that can be pinned and toggled.
• Search based categories where the items within the category are defined by a search function.
• Items within categories have multiple sorting and stacking options (stack all, stack non-stackable, don't stack different transmogs).
• Powerful recent items support with customizable duration (mark all new items as recent, flash all recent items).
• Right-click category header to move or vendor all items currently in the category.
• Comprehensive Search that allows you to find an item most properties of an item (Type, Subtype, iLvl, and many more).
• Multiple built-in themes (Default, Simple Dark, Slate, Dark, Parchment, and ElvUI and GW2 UI themes when those are installed), with a declarative theme API for creating more.
• Bags that size themselves to their items, or windows you resize by dragging their corner (Settings > Resizable Window).
• Profiles to allow easy swapping of layouts and categories between characters.
• Category import and export strings to easily share your categories between friends.
• Robust plugin system allows for custom categories, configurations for user fine-tuning and even localization.
• Integration support for Pawn (upgrade arrows) and Simple Item Levels (item level coloring).

More additions are being added all the time.
FeaturesBag & Bank View
BetterBags offers its users a powerful category-based view, which also carry over to the bank.
Section Grid
This view sorts your inventory into their own visually distinct categories, allowing you to categorize items at a basic level that is easier for humans to understand by grouping like items together.

The Section Grid offers:
• Customizable columns and number of items per row.
• Categories can be sorted either alphabetically (top to bottom), size descending, or size ascending.
• Categories can be pinned to the top, enabled, disabled or hidden at will.
• Items within these categories can be sorted alphabetically and then by quality (or vice versa).
• Multiple stacking options for fine-tuning your own experience.
• Built-in categories are named after the item's type and, when turned on in the options, its subtype and expansion (for example Armor - Plate - Classic). A subtype named like its type is not repeated, so quest items read Quest rather than Quest - Quest.

Section Grid View in Retail.
Navigation
Most options and other important information in BetterBags can be reached by left-clicking on the bag button in the top-left corner of the bag (or bank) and bringing up the menu. Hovering over the bag icon will bring up a list of mouse-clicks that can be done for various functions. Some of the important functions in the menu are described in the following sections. Any options not in the menu directly are instead in the options screen (access by choosing Open Options Screen in the menu or the slash command /bb).

Menu in Retail.…

addons.description:
A complete, hand-painted interface replacement inspired by Guild Wars 2. Modular: turn off any part you don't need, the rest stays intact.

Tired of a UI that looks like a spreadsheet? GW2 UI replaces the default interface with hand-painted art, clean frames and smooth animations - so you look at the game world again, not at boxes. Install it, log in, play. Everything is set up and ready.

Runs on: Retail (Midnight) · World of Warcraft: Forever · Mists of Pandaria Classic · Wrath of the Lich King Classic · The Burning Crusade Classic · Classic Era, Season of Discovery, Hardcore and Anniversary
WHY GW2 UI?
• Plug and play - no profiles to import, no addons to combine. One install gives you HUD, unit frames, bags, quest tracker, character window and more.
• Hand-made, not a template - every texture is painted and every window is built for this UI, with the look of Guild Wars 2.
• Plays well with your addons - every module can be turned off. Keep your favorite bag, raid frame or chat addon and use GW2 UI for the rest.
• One UI for every version of WoW - the same look from Classic Era to Midnight, updated with every patch since 2017.
• Ready for Midnight - class powers, auras and the dynamic HUD work with the new secret aura rules.
• Gamepad ready - on Forever, GW2 UI switches to its own gamepad layout automatically.
• In your language - translated into 11 languages.
FEATURES
Some features depend on the game version, for example Mythic+ and the Great Vault only exist on Retail.

HUD - health globe, hand-painted class powers with their own animations, a dynamic HUD that reacts to combat and your class abilities, action bars that fade or hide while mounted, dodge bar, cast bars and a micro bar with detailed tooltips.

Unit frames and groups - player, target, focus, pet, party, boss and arena frames. Raid and party grids with aura indicators and dispel colors. Build the texts of every frame by drag and drop with the text designer.

Questing - immersive quest dialogs, a quest tracker with tracking compass and boss frames, Mythic+ and raid info (deaths, battle res, bloodlust), boss times compared to your best and the achievements you are closest to completing.

Character and inventory - a hero panel for character, reputation, professions, spellbook and talents. Bags, bank and guild bank with sorting, junk handling and item levels. Own loot roll bars and a loot feed that shows what you receive.

Map, chat and tooltips - minimap with configurable buttons, world map with exploration progress, a clean chat with role icons, colored chat bubbles and tooltips with item level, Mythic+ rating and more.

Skins and quality of life - skins for most Blizzard windows like achievements and collections, toasts for rares, full bags and the Great Vault, optional auto repair, fast loot and train all, an AFK screen and a global cooldown ring around the cursor.

Your setup - move and scale every frame in Move HUD mode, save profiles that switch with your specialization and see what is new in the in-game changelog.
GETTING STARTED
1. Install GW2 UI and log in - the UI is ready to use.
2. Type /gw2 settings to open the settings and turn modules on or off, /gw2 lists all commands.
3. Type /gw2 mh to move and scale frames.
4. Type /gw2 kb to bind keys by hovering over a button.

addons.description:
======

RealUI is a minimalistic UI designed to be functional, yet also efficient and elegant.

Information

• Supports retail WoW (Midnight, 12.1.x) and the WoW Forever beta (1.60.x) from the same download.
• Current release is 4.2.4 (Aurora 12.1.5.2).
• As of 4.0.0 the package contains only RealUI's own addons — no bundled third-party
addons (standard embedded libraries such as Ace3, oUF, LibActionButton, and
LibSharedMedia are still included, as in any addon). See "Recommended optional
AddOns" below.
• RealUI includes the modernized setup pipeline, unified profile handling, and display setup stage.
• User settings are automatically migrated from nibRealUIDB to RealUIDB when needed.
• Report issues on GitHub or connect with us on Discord.

What's New in 4.2.0

If you upgraded from an earlier version, run /realui newdefaults: profiles that saved "Cast by me"
for target debuffs are offered the new default there.
• Nameplate debuffs show the ones that matter to your class, the rule Blizzard's own nameplates use,
so the rows are shorter on purpose. "All mine" brings the old rows back; Always show and Never show
lists take spell IDs or spellbook names. The HuD target frame's debuffs default to the same rule.
• Action bar page numbering: each profile can number its pages like Bartender4 (the default) or
like Blizzard. The install wizard's Action Bar Layout step offers the choice.
• Auto-repair on the Durability block: the tooltip shows the auto-repair setting, the estimated
cost and the last repair; Shift + Left Click on the block toggles auto-repair.
• Objective tracker (/realadv → Tracker): a quest item button with a key binding, a fade during
boss fights (not in a Mythic+ keystone), quest log capacity in the top header, green titles for quests
ready to turn in, a "Wowhead link" entry in the quest right-click menus, and an optional mouseover
reveal.
• No more tracker taint. The GetAuraDataByIndex() error in delves and LFR came from addon code
tainting the tracker; the sources in RealUI and Aurora are removed, and the tracker and world-event
bars are skinned again, restyled in place. A few frames keep Blizzard's look, or a plainer one, on
purpose.
• Colour modes: all five of Aurora's colour modes, including the colour-blind ones, are in
/realadv → Skins → Appearance, and the Skins colour pickers follow the mode until you change them.
• The inspect window closes when you change target, as Blizzard's does. The old bundled InspectFix
is removed; on WoW Forever it blocked Inspect Talents.
• Tracker options that changed: a per-instance hide now fades the tracker out, and it stays
clickable. The "collapse modules in" instance option, Difficulty Color and Wrap Text are removed.
• The micro menu stays hidden in a vehicle, the vehicle pitch controls are skinned, and the default zone
text no longer sits on the PvP start timer.

What's New in 4.1.1

A maintenance release. If you upgraded from an earlier version, run /realui newdefaults: the boss
timeline fix is applied through it.
• The Boss Abilities timeline and boss warnings sit where Blizzard's layout puts them, clear of the HuD.
• Trinkets and other items with a long effect description can be upgraded again.
• The LFR, dungeon and battleground ready popups, the ready check, role checks and group invites are
skinned.
• Objects whose nameplate is only a progress bar show that bar with RealUI's nameplates on, and the
minimap stays square inside a house.
• WoW Forever: action bars work on client builds from 1.60.1.70170 on, and Edit Mode no longer errors.
• /realui grid draws an alignment grid for placing frames by hand.

What's New in 4.1.0

WoW 12 hides some combat information from addons. This release brings back what the game allows, adds
new frame features, fixes the layout on 1440p screens, and adds WoW Forever support.

Debuffs you cast now show when a refresh would carry over their remaining duration, PvP icons show for players whose PvP state the game hides from addons, and nameplates stay on whole pixels as they move.

• fix: PvP icons on the HuD show for players whose PvP state the game hides from addons, and the PvP indicator updates when you flag yourself for PvP, not only when you unflag
• fix: the first tooltip after logging in has RealUI's border, like every one after it

• fix: Aurora — the PvP window's activity buttons (Quick Match, Rated, Training Grounds) lose Blizzard's button art, and queueing from them still works

[4.2.2] - 2026-10-15
Summary
A compatibility release for WoW 12.1.5. RealUI 4.2.1 and Aurora 12.1.0.15 list four Blizzard_Deprecated addons as required dependencies, 12.1.5 deletes them, and WoW does not load an addon whose required dependency is missing. Both now load on 12.1.5. Arena frames no longer error in arena preparation, Blizzard's new minimap coordinates no longer show under RealUI's own, and nameplates do less work on every enemy plate.

Arena frames now appear when the gates open, not during preparation. 12.1.5 hides the opponents' specs during preparation, and the unit frame library RealUI uses reads them there.

The !RealUI_Preloads folder is no longer part of RealUI. If you install by hand, you can delete it from your AddOns folder.

Aurora goes from 12.1.0.15 to 12.1.5.0.

• RealUI_Nameplates
• RealUI_Dev
• Aurora

RealUI turns that preparation off, the name tag only class-colours units whose class it can read, and the crowd-control trinket timer skips values it cannot read
• fix: Blizzard's new minimap coordinates, an option in Blizzard's settings, are hidden under RealUI's minimap, where they sat on top of RealUI's own coordinates

Summary
A hotfix for auto-repair. In 12.1, Blizzard sometimes prices an item's repair at tens of thousands of gold after a death, first seen on the Chestguard of Corroded Scales, until you /reload, and repairing really charges that amount. Auto-repair, which is on by default, paid those bills without asking. It now asks first when a bill looks bugged or is over a gold limit you set.

If you saw an unexpectedly large repair: the gold is spent on Blizzard's side; RealUI cannot refund it.

Fixed
• fix: auto-repair no longer pays a repair bill that looks bugged. Repair cost is lost durability times a per-item rate, so after a death every slot should cost about the same per durability point. When one slot costs over ten times the median, an undamaged slot has a repair cost, or the total is over ten times what the equipped gear accounts for, a Yes/No popup names the slot and suggests /reload instead of repairing. No leaves your gold alone and the Durability tooltip shows "declined"; closing the merchant closes the popup

Summary
A feature release. The objective tracker is no longer tainted, which ends the GetAuraDataByIndex() error in delves and LFR, and the tracker and world-event bars are skinned again. Nameplate debuffs show the ones that matter to your class, action bars can number their pages the way Blizzard's do, all five colour modes can be chosen in RealUI, the Durability block shows your auto-repair setting, and the tracker gets a quest item button and several smaller additions.

If you upgraded from an earlier version, run /realui newdefaults. Profiles that saved "Cast by me" for target debuffs are offered the new default there.

The objective tracker. Since August the tracker's own layout state was being written under addon taint, blamed on RealUI or RealUI_Skins. That is what produced the GetAuraDataByIndex() error. addons.description:
Dominos is an addon that replaces your main bar with movable parts that offer
additional customization. Dominos is used primarily for its action bars,
which feature:
• Customizable layout settings (spacing, vertical bars, opacity, scale, etc)
• Customizable action bar paging (so that you can change what your bars do when shapeshifted, etc)
• Customizable visiblity (so that you can make bars transparent, or show up only when in combat, etc)
• Masque support for button styling,
with individual settings per bar
• LibKeyBound is implemented for quickly binding keys
• Any other addon that works on Blizzard UI for action buttons should also work with Dominos, too.
This includes things like tullaRange, AdiButtonAuras, and OmniCC
UsageGeneral Settings
The main options menu in Dominos can be found by either right clicking the
minimap icon or via the /dominos slashcommand. On the main options menu,
you will find sections for configuring shared bar settings and profiles.
Moving Stuff Around
To move around or hide bars, you will want to enter configuration mode. You
can do this by either one of the following ways
• Left clicking the minimap button
• Clicking Configure Bars... from the main options menu (accessible from /dominos)
• Using the slash command /dominos config
• Once in configuration mode, you can drag around bars using your mouse
Customizing Individual Bars
Most per bar settings can be found in context menus. To access these settings,
right click or alt left click the bar in configuration mode.
Binding Keys
Dominos implements support for LibKeyBound
for quickly binding keys. Quick Binding mode can be entered by either the standard keybound shortcut (/kb)
or by clicking the Bind Keys... button in the main options menu.
Slash Commands
Dominos provides a large set of slash commands for usage in macros and bulk
adjustments. The complete set of slash commands can be found on the wiki

addons.description:
=====================

This addon collects information about your character and presents a text version suitable for running in Simc

Usage
=====

Type /simc in-game to display text input that you can copy/paste to SimulationCraft.

/simc nobags will only output character on your gear, not items in your bags.

/simc minimap will toggle the minimap icon.

/simc [Item Link] can be used to add additional items to the output. For example, type /simc, add a space, then
shift left-click an item (from chat, a recent boss drop, or an item from a vendor) and that item will be added as a
comment below bag items in the text. WoW chat does have a character limit so the output may only contain the first 2-3
items that you link.

FAQ
===
Why are some item names missing from the comments?
First, this warning does not impact the sim in any way - it only makes it a bit harder to know which
line is for which item for people reading the input.

Some addons that do big database updates can unintentionally cause problems for others. Usually it's
completionist or transmog addons (All The Things, Can I Mog It, etc) that need to do a bunch of work
on login and that can sometimes prevent the SimulationCraft addon from being able to show item names.

If you run /simc again a bit later once the database updates are done, it should resolve the issue and show
the item names in comments. You may need to run /simc a couple of times for the info to be available.

Maintainers

• navv
• seriallos
• aethys
• Theck (retired)

addons.description:
Discord: https://discord.gg/KgeQhjv9Rd

Voiced dialogue, lore and text for World of Warcraft Forever. The other clients' code is
still here, with no new work going into it.

Spoken is one download: Spoken itself and its three modules, Spoken Quests, Spoken Places and
Spoken Readables. Each is a folder of its own, grouped under Spoken in the
AddOns list. Spoken plays every line and owns the settings page, the minimap button, the queue
and the narrator window or subtitles; each module reads one kind of text and has a page of its
own under Spoken's settings. Every module comes installed. A player who does not want one
switches it off on its card on Spoken's page, disables it in the AddOns list, or deletes its
folder. The voice packs are separate downloads. Spoken_Developer, the debug log, is for
developers and is not in the zip.

| Folder | Addon | Voices | Voice packs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spoken | Spoken | nothing itself: it plays every module's lines | — |
| Spoken_Quests | Spoken Quests | quest dialogue and NPC gossip | All, or Alliance · Horde · Shared · Gossip — or all in one from GitHub |
| Spoken_Readables | Spoken Readables | books, letters and other in-world texts | CurseForge · GitHub |
| Spoken_Places | Spoken Places | zone and subzone lore | CurseForge · GitHub |
| Spoken_Bosses | Spoken Bosses | the story of each dungeon and raid boss | CurseForge, in Places and Bosses · GitHub |

make package-spoken builds the download, Spoken-.zip, with every module built by
its own packager. A module's voice pack holds its recordings; the module has nothing to play
without one, and the pack does nothing without the module.

The sound packs are not on Wago. Each is 280 to 452 MB and Wago's upload endpoint refuses a
file this size, so a pack comes from CurseForge or from a GitHub release, one tag per pack,

/vX.Y.Z. English quests are the four split packs on CurseForge, and the same four in
one quests-audio zip on GitHub. scripts/audio-github-release.sh cuts the release from the
machine that built the audio, since the audio is outside git and no runner can rebuild it.

On the stores, spoken is Spoken and ships the zip above, and spoken-english is a meta addon
that pulls in Spoken and every English voice pack. spoken-quests, spoken-zones and
spoken-books are retired. Each has a page in publishers/ that says so.
The module folders were SpokenQuests, SpokenZones and SpokenBooks until 3.0.0-beta.3,
and those names belong to the retired projects, so the modules moved to Spoken_Quests,
Spoken_Places and Spoken_Books; Spoken_Books has since become Spoken_Readables. The voice
packs name Spoken as their dependency. Folders an older release left behind (SpokenPlayer,
VoiceOverRedux, ZoneLore, and a full old copy of a module under its old name) are found at
login, and the player is asked to delete them.
What players see
Narrator styles. Spoken shows a line in one of four ways, five with DialogueUI, chosen
on the Spoken settings page or in the welcome window on first login:
• Subtitles Only, the default unless DialogueUI is installed: the speaker's name
and the words low in the middle of the screen over a soft shadow, at most four lines at a
time. A longer line turns its pages as the voice reaches them, one fading out before the
next fades in. The words show whole, with the word being read lit; Type Words Out in the
settings types them in instead, a little ahead of the voice. Stop or Replay, skip and Report
appear on hover.
• Small Window (Minimal Classic): a round portrait, the speaker's name and the title (a
slim progress bar under them with Show Progress Bar on), with the controls and the queue on
interaction. See docs/minimal-classic/.
• Large Window: the game's Talking Head frame where the client has its art: a bigger
portrait, with the speaker's name, the words, the controls and a count of the lines waiting
beside it in one box.
• DialogueUI, offered only with the DialogueUI…

2026-10-12 — Updates after the first profiler release
This changelog covers changes after Carbonite-v12.1.0-00020-Profiler-Changed-Only.zip through Carbonite\_Export\_Hotfix\_Changed\_Only\_vs\_Master6\_2026-10-12.zip. Related updates are consolidated below, newest first.
Latest changed-only package
• Prepared the cumulative changed-only package against Carbonite-All-in-One-Retail-Classic-master(6).zip, carrying the quest catalog integration, diagnostics redesign, and corrected Export/tooltip files.
Export and tooltip hotfix
• Fixed both Export errors caused by calling GetStringHeight() on an EditBox.
• Sized exported reports using wrapped line count, font height, line spacing, and text insets so the complete report remains scrollable at supported text sizes.
• Fixed the diagnostic tooltip SetText argument error by supplying numeric alpha before the wrapping flag.
Diagnostic interface redesign
• Added a shared diagnostic window with Map, Quest, and Both scopes and Overview, Functions, Compare, Help, and Export views.
• Put recording state, session measurements, quest activity, and suggested next steps on Overview; moved detailed comparisons, settings, and raw reports into separate views.
• Added ranked timing bars, explicit millisecond units, aligned numeric columns, and one zero-based scale within each selected view.
• Added adjustable text size, screen fitting, and stable snapshots. Refresh updates the displayed measurements; changing views keeps the same snapshot.
• Added the Select report → Ctrl+C workflow for copying complete reports, with client/build details, catalog counters, function timings, comparisons, and retained samples.
• Replaced competing Map profiler implementations with one measurement source shared by the scoped displays. Map and Quest recording states, references, and resets remain independent.
• Assigned quest-owned objective-area update timings to Quest diagnostics.
• Distinguished retained samples from earlier runs from current-session measurements. Earlier samples cannot become a new idle reference or silently enter current comparisons.
• Preserved earlier split Map captures within the shared sample capacity and identified older references requiring recapture.
• Kept unavailable Lua heap measurements distinct from measured zero values.
• Kept combined markers visible in both scopes and preserved the other scope's marker when clearing one scope.
• Updated PROFILER.md with the interface workflow, measurement definitions, comparison requirements, command reference, and measurement limits.…

About
Masque is an add-on for [World of Warcraft] that provides a skinning engine for button-based add-ons through a library-based API.
FeaturesLibrary
• Easy-to-use API accessible through [LibStub]
• Group-based skinning engine
• Independent saved-variables
• Support for most button types and regions
• Support for third-party skins
GUI
• Load-on-demand settings panel
• Global, per-add-on and per-group settings
• Skin, Color, Gloss and Shadow options
• Full profile support, including per-spec profiles (Retail only)
Requirements
• An action bar, aura or inventory add-on that supports Masque.
• All required libraries are included.
Options
To access Masque's options, use the /msq or /masque chat commands. You can also access the options via the Interface Options Window or by clicking on Masque's icon in a DataBroker display.

Release History

12.1.7Skins
• Due to all game versions now using a similar AutoCastOverlay template, the following changes have been made:
• The AutoCast/AutoCastShine and AutoCastable regions have been deprecated.
• For Classic clients, Masque will now look in the AutoCast_Frame.Classic and AutoCast_Corners.Classic fields for the respective Classic settings.
• Masque will automatically redirect those fields to the respective skin definition if the parent field exists. Otherwise it will use the default settings.
• Eg: If AutoCast_Corners exists within the skin, Masque will point AutoCast_Corners.Classic toward AutoCastable if AutoCast_Corners.Classic is missing.

Download on [CurseForge].

Are you having an issue with Total RP 3? Check the [F.A.Q] and our [troubleshooting page]!

> “I recently switched over to Total RP 3 and it is so much better! […] Total RP 3 is probably the best [roleplay add-on] that I found.”
> — Anne Stickney @Shadesogrey, in Blizzard Watch — Episode 95
> Senior Editor and Lore Columnist for the Blizzard Watch website

Helpful links
• Join us on [Discord]!
• Avoid losing all your profiles: sync up your saved data to an online storage. Here’s a guide!
• Don't know how to install an add-on? Check our [installation guide]!
• Check out Myth's excellent TRP3 guide for an in depth tour of the add-on's features. Big thanks to him!
Description
Total RP 3 aims to be the best way to customize, describe and drive your role-play interactions by combining powerful customization features with a clean and accessible user interface. With Total RP 3, you can fully customize all the characteristics of your characters and companions (pets, battle pets, mounts), like the name, the description or even attach an image to represent them.

Our goal is to bring the simplicity and user-friendliness of add-ons like MyRolePlay but without sacrificing your freedom when defining your roleplay characters, while still adding neat features that you'll never want to live without.

Total RP 3 can work alongside other roleplay addons like MyRolePlay and XRP, allowing for a truly seamless roleplaying experience regardless of which addon others may choose.

Total RP 3 is also a fully modular add-on. You choose exactly which features you want to use so you won't have to navigate through a complex user interface if you don't want to.
Main features
• You can customize your characters and companions (battle pets, pets, and mounts) with a powerful profile system allowing you to quickly switch between your different profiles.
• Keep track of all the characters and companions you met with the directory, a repository of profiles you have encountered.
• Find other Total RP 3 users on the world map to see where people tend to gather. You can choose to hide yourself from the map, or to only show yourself while you're in-character.
• A customizable target frame containing useful interactions for your roleplay target, like opening their profile, playing their theme song, or altering your relationship with that character.
• Chat customizations like OOC and emote chat coloring as well as full role-play names using custom colors in the chat. (Details on Chat Formatting)
• NPC speech to mimic NPC chat, whispers, yells and emotes.
• Total RP 3 can communicate with MyRolePlay, XRP and most other roleplaying add-ons so you can see and read through other players' profiles, even if they are using a different roleplaying add-on.
• A customizable toolbar with useful actions like switching from one profile to another, switching from IC to OOC, from AFK to DND, switching languages, and more!
• Import your existing profiles from Total RP 2, MyRolePlay or XRP. (Tutorial)
• Mature profile filtering to warn you before opening profiles that may contain mature content.
YouTube videos
• Are you a new role-player? Check out this great beginners guide to Total RP 3 by Dizhon!
• Here's a video from Kraken Latte detailing the basics of Total RP 3, including the setup and backing up of your profiles.
Total RP 3 modules spotlightTotal RP 3: Extended, by Kajisensei & Ellypse
This awesome module brings the new creation system. Create items, readable documents, campaigns with quests, customized NPCs and dialogs, loots. Use the inventory system to show items you are wearing and inspect other players' inventory. Create stashes that other players will be able to inspect. Trade items with other players safely thanks to our security level system that allows you to define authorizations per item and be sure you won't suddenly shout weird stuff because of a cursed item!

addons.description:
Clicked is a World of Warcraft addon with the goal of improving keybinds and macros. The addon adds a configuration window from where all keybinds can be configured to do something.

There is an extreme amount of freedom in configuring exactly what a keybind does by creating bindings. A binding can do anything from casting a spell to using an item to running a custom macro. Alongside from configuring what a binding does, you are also able to specify the exact target priority for that binding and configure the conditions under which the binding should load.

When configuring multiple bindings on one keybind, Clicked will automatically combine their functionality and allow the keybind to perform either action depending on the context.

Additionally Clicked adds support for the binding of all mouse buttons in case you prefer clicking on a unit frame to cast something.
Features
• Create keyboard and mouse button bindings for spells, items, cancelauras, and custom macros
• No performance impact during gameplay
• Create globally available bindings, or profile specific bindings
• Easily import your action bar layout
• Cast spells without action bars
• Cast spells by clicking on unit frames
• Easily select spells from the spellbook
• Easily import the entire spellbook
• Configure binding target priorities
• Configure binding load conditions
• Configure macro conditionals
• Configure multiple bindings on the same keybind
• Configure custom macros without taking up a macro slot
• Configure a unit frame blacklist
• Automatically unload and unlock keybinds while in a vehicle
• Visualize your keybinds on a virtual keyboard
Configure binding target priorities
You can use the binding target interface to configure the exact target priority. When the binding is activated, Clicked will try to cast the assigned spell or item on each target configured, if the conditions of a target are not met, or if the target does not exist it will try the next target until a valid target is found.

You can mix and match a variety of targets and target conditions in one binding, Clicked will automatically adjust the UI so that the targets list always makes sense, for example it won't allow targets after selecting yourself as a target, since that will not be reachable ever.

A full list of all available targets:
• Default behaves like the default behavior you would get from putting an ability on your action bar
• Player (you)
• Target
• Target of target
• Mouseover target
• Target of mouseover target
• Focus target
• Cursor position will cast on your cursor's position, mainly for placable AoE abilities
• Pet
• Pet target
• Party 1-5
• Arena 1-3

In addition to the unit to cast on, you can also configure (optional) modifiers for that target:
• Friendly
• Hostile
• Alive
• Dead
Configure binding load conditions
You can configure the exact load conditions on a per-target basis, through this interface you can specify the exact requirements that have to be met for this binding to activate. For example you can configure a binding to only load when a talent has been selected, when you're in war mode, or when you're in a specific zone.

A full list of all available load conditions:
• Never load will prevent the binding from loading entirely
• Player Name-Realm checks if your name/realm matches the input
• Class checks if you are of the selected class(es)
• Race checks if you are of the selected race(s)
• Talent specialization checks if you are in the selected talent specialization(s)
• Talent selected checks if you have the selected talent(s) active
• PvP talent selected checks if you have the selected PvP talent(s) active
• War Mode checks if you are in the selected War Mode state
• (not) in zone(s) checks if you are (not) in the specified zone(s)
• Spell known checks if you can currently cast the specified spell or ability
• In group checks if you are in the specified group type (solo, party, raid)…
