[3.0.0] - 2026-11-01
In-game validation of audio playback and the recent Retail and Forever compatibility changes is still pending.
Added
• WoW: Forever / Camelot interface declaration (16001) and outgoing-message detection using the character name and surname API, with the previous name comparison retained as a fallback.
• Four integrated sound packs containing 148 extra sounds: Effect Pack 01 (61), Notification Pack 01 (48), Notification Pack 02 (27), and StarCraft Pack (12).
• A Sound packs settings page with individual toggles and a Reload UI button, including Brazilian Portuguese text. All packs are enabled by default; preferences are saved across configuration profiles and applied after reloading the UI.
• A README covering features, installation, configuration, game interfaces, sound packs, and support.
• Sound-pack regression tests covering defaults, saved preferences, reload behavior, independent activation, registration paths, and sound counts.
Changed
• Updated the Retail interface declaration from 120007 to 120105. Retained Mists of Pandaria Classic (50504) and Classic Era (11509).
• Integrated the sound-pack definitions directly into the main addon.
• Sound playback now reads directly from LibSharedMedia instead of depending on the sound-selection widgets' global table.
• Excluded development tests from release packages.
• Adopted the Keep a Changelog structure in CHANGELOG.md and configured tagged releases to publish only the matching version's notes.
Fixed
• Ignored words now treat Lua pattern characters, such as %, [ and +, literally while preserving existing case-sensitive word-boundary matching.
• Zone and custom channels now use independent notification intervals, so activity in one channel does not suppress another channel's notifications through the shared CHAT_MSG_CHANNEL timer.
• Missing or invalid sound references are skipped before playback. Failed playback attempts no longer consume the notification interval.
• Channel-specific rules now ignore unrelated chat events and avoid inspecting restricted channel names, IDs, or sender flags.
• Player-specific and ignore-list rules now skip invalid or restricted sender names safely.
• Added a local fallback for clients without the secret-value inspection function.
• Zone and Newcomer Chat settings no longer require their chat colors to be initialized before displaying their labels.
Removed
• Removed the four standalone sound-pack manifests and four redundant startup files. Each integrated pack now uses one sound-definition file and its audio assets.
addons.description:

Choose different sounds for incoming and outgoing messages, individual players, player groups, and chat channels. The required libraries and extra sound packs are included.
Features
• Separate incoming and outgoing sounds for guild, officer, whisper, Battle.net whisper, party, raid, instance, community, say, yell, and emote messages where supported by the game client.
• Sound settings for General, Trade, Local Defense, Newcomer Chat, and custom channels.
• Custom sounds for individual players and user-defined groups of players.

• Output through the Master, Sound Effects, Music, Ambience, or Dialog audio channel.
• Multiple chat types can be selected together to change their sounds in one step.
• Twelve built-in CSC sounds, Murloc Aggro, and four extra sound packs containing 148 sounds.
• Access to sounds registered by other addons through LibSharedMedia.
• Saved configuration profiles, a minimap launcher, and temporary muting.
• A LibDataBroker launcher for compatible display addons.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for previewing Blizzard's XML frame templates — like
TextureAtlasViewer, but for templates.

Pick a template from the list and tv builds a live instance of it with the client you are
running, so you see exactly how that template renders there: art, fonts, and any atlas
remaps that client applies. Underneath the preview, tv shows what the client reports
about the template — its widget type, what it inherits, its KeyValues, and the file that
defines it — plus the addon it comes from and the size the instance rendered at.

Every template is listed: the ~3,600 that Blizzard's UI defines (including those of
addons that load on demand) plus any other addon's templates the client knows about.
Curated templates come first. Many templates render nothing useful until they are given
text, a title or data, so a curated entry carries a small setup that does what
Blizzard's own UI would do, and renders as soon as you select it. Everything else renders
raw, without setup, when you ask for it.
Usage
• /tv or /templateviewer toggles the window; /tv opens it with the search
filled in. Search matches template names first, then a curated template's category or
another template's addon, then descriptions.
• Curated templates have gold names. For any other template, Render builds it raw;
tick Auto-render to render templates as you select them. Building a template runs
its scripts and the instance stays until you /reload, which is why it isn't automatic.
• Some templates change Blizzard's UI when built: they create frames with fixed global
names (replacing Blizzard's frames of that name) or register with Edit Mode. tv warns
before rendering those (Render anyway), Auto-render skips them, and /reload puts
everything back.
• Templates from addons that load on demand are dimmed until their addon is loaded;
Load loads it, which runs that Blizzard addon for the rest of the session.
• Scroll on the preview to zoom, drag to pan; Reset View fits the template back into
view, Background cycles the backdrop colour.
• Click the template name field to select it for copying.
• /tv audit compares the client's C_XMLUtil.GetTemplates() with tv's catalog and saves
the report to the TemplateViewerAudit SavedVariable (written on /reload or logout).
• The window won't open in combat and closes when combat starts, because some templates
are protected.
Status
Supports Retail and WoW Forever; each loads its own list of the templates its client
defines, so the same template can be compared across both. Curated so far:
UIPanelButtonTemplate, ButtonFrameTemplate. Classic flavors are planned.

addons.description:
https://www.patreon.com/deadlybossmods
History:
Initially, the Heroes of the Storm countdown sounds were added to DBM-Core directly. These expanded the countdown sound options with several Characters that launched with base game. Since then, several more character countdowns have been added to game such as Illiden, Li'Li, etc. I weighed for a while on whether I should keep adding new files to DBM core and continuing to inflate the media foot print, or split the package into a stand alone before adding additional media options.

I have finally decided now is best time to split the media out of core and into stand alone. Then I can more easily update the Heroes of the Storm counts without worrying about how big it gets in media size since it's not something you have to redownload often (versus dbm which can be downloaded daily, or more if using alpha versions).

You might wonder, why concern self with how big the DBM download is. Believe it or not, MANY players still play on rural internet connections or on connections that have limited bandwidth monthly caps. A few megabytes per download can make a big difference for a very active user who updates DBM daily. Not to mention the many thousands of users who download the file directly from deadlybossmods.com as well. Not that the bandwidth is killing us by any means but it's still inefficient. I want the core package to be more minimalistic so when core is updated it's a small download and all the media to be stand alone from now on.

addons.description:
The WeakAuras you know, running on WoW Forever (client 1.60.1).
Open the options with /wa or /weakauras, or with the minimap icon.
⚠ Before you import auras
WoW Forever looks like Classic, but it runs on the modern game engine (12.1).
That engine changed what addons are allowed to see, so many auras made for
Classic Era, SoD or Retail will not work as they are:
• Auras that read the combat log (CLEU triggers, "Combat Log" events) never
fire. The combat log is closed to addons on this engine.
• Most combat data is hidden from addons during combat. Musca Auras
lets the game draw it (timers, bars, texts set to only %p or %s), but conditions
and thresholds on that data wait until combat ends.
• Some old game functions no longer exist. Custom code calling them errors
and must be updated to the modern C_ API (C_Spell, C_UnitAuras, C_Item...).
• Talent load options list the talents of your own specialization: select it alone in Class and Specialization. Aura (Modern)
spell lists take a spell ID or a spell name; a name is replaced by the IDs of all its ranks.

In short: expect to adapt most of the auras you import, especially the ones
with custom code. Damage taken, for example, works through UNIT_COMBAT:player
instead of the combat log.

Read the tutorial: how WeakAuras works on Forever, and
step-by-step recipes for auras that keep working in combat.

Coming from ForeverAuras? Paste your exported strings in the import window:
they are converted (tutorial, section 10).
Utility packs
/wa, then Packs: 24 packs for every class, each installed in one click.
• Combat: Ready Flash, Combat Text, Combat Items, Engineering Items, Shield Meter, Center Mark.
• Group and Buffs: Buff Check, Raid Coverage, Pre-Pull Check, Conjured Supplies, Announcements.
• Target and Enemies: Target Debuffs, Nameplate Aggro, Crowd Control, Armor Shred, Enemy Targets.
• Character: Level Progress, Character Stats, Group Experience, Equipment Sets.
• World: World Reminders, Campfire, Guild Campfires, Object Highlight.

Group Experience and Guild Campfires only show the players who also run the pack.

TOGBankClassic Changelog[v1.10.1] (2026-10-31) - One Stack Per OrderBug Fixes
• MAIL-ONE-STACK-001: an order that fits in one stack went out as several attachments. The
operator, 2026-10-31, with a mail to January-Atiesh carrying 7 Mountain Silversage as a stack of 5
and a stack of 2: *"why does it send a stack of 5 and a stack of 2 instead of making it one stack
of 7?"*. CalculateFulfillmentPlan's first phase takes any bag stacks that add up exactly, so 5 + 2
won over splitting, and MAIL-SPLIT-MERGE-001 only merged when a split was needed anyway; each
extra attachment costs 30c postage. CalculateFulfillmentPlan (Modules/Mail.lua) now replaces
any plan that takes more than one attachment with a one-attachment plan when the order fits under
the item's max stack: the largest stack smaller than the order is attached, and the rest is moved
onto it from the smallest other stack that covers it. Moving all of a stack is a pickup rather
than a split (tog_liftOntoCursor), because the client cannot split a whole stack; that also
frees a bag slot. Applies to Fulfill Oldest, the row's Fulfill icon and the hand-off split. When
no single stack covers the rest (7 from 3 + 2 + 2 with nothing bigger), the stacks still go as
they are. Tests/multifill_spec.lua gains three examples; three Tests/mailcoverage_spec.lua
examples about slot handling now use items whose max stack rules out a merge, and the planner
example now expects the merge. Confirmed in game by the operator the same day: *"tested the fix in
game, it works now"*. The cost: a 5 + 2 fill that went straight to ATTACH now takes a SPLIT click
first, trading one click for 30c postage.
• Peer Review 349c7141 on MAIL-ONE-STACK-001. B1: the whole-stack move was decided from the
plan's stack count, so a source stack that grew between picking the order and the SPLIT click would
be moved whole, and ATTACH would then wait forever for a merged count it could never read.
tog_liftOntoCursor now decides from the live stack, and both the SPLIT phase and the Split popup
refuse (the batch restarts) when the source no longer holds what was planned. B2: the popup no
longer moves a whole stack into an empty slot when its target changed -- that changed nothing --
and says the stacks changed instead. F4: tog_oneAttachmentPlan builds its target through
tog_mergeTarget, so the same-item and max-stack rule lives in one function. N1: its comment now
says the list must already be sorted. Tests/multifill_spec.lua gains four examples (source grew
before SPLIT, popup source changed, popup target changed, unknown max stack).
Improvements
• The CurseForge page names the sister addons by their current titles, Ultimate Profession Master
and Ultimate Tools (Peer Review inbox thread f2dc805e, routing TOGWiki's report). Older patch notes
keep the names they shipped with.

TOGBankClassic Changelog[v1.9.1] (2026-10-17) - Safer Order SyncBug Fixes
• MUT-ID-001: a received order change could overwrite a different order. Peer Review eee82c0f,
Q1. Guild:ApplyRequestMutation (Modules/RequestLog.lua) keys the merge by entry.requestId
and looks up requests[requestId] for its permission checks, but mergeRequest stores the
snapshot as it arrived, so a mutation whose request.id differed from its requestId put one
order's record under another's key. An "add" passes when the snapshot's requester is the sender,
so a peer could replace any order with a newer snapshot of its own. Every sender in this addon
sets both ids from one value, so only a mismatched or hostile peer reaches it. A mutation whose
two ids differ is now refused. Tests/requestlogcoverage_spec.lua, confirmed red with the check
switched off. Not wire-visible: nothing this addon sends changes.
• ADD-OWNER-001: an "add" could take over or close someone else's existing order. Peer Review
e5b7e0c8, R1, the other half of MUT-ID-001. The add check only compared the snapshot's requester
with the sender, never the order already held under that id, so a peer naming itself requester
could send a newer snapshot of another player's order and mergeRequest replaced it: the order
changed hands, or arrived cancelled or complete without the cancel and complete permission
checks, which run only for those mutation types. An add for an order already held is now refused
unless the sender is that order's requester; the requester's own add arriving twice still merges.
The only sender of an add, Guild:AddRequest, mints a fresh id, so a modified client is needed to
reach it. Tests/requestlogcoverage_spec.lua: a takeover and a cancelling add are refused (red
with the check switched off), and the requester's repeated add still merges.
• ADD-OPEN-001: a requester could close or fill their own order by re-sending it as an "add".
Peer Review 70aaa39f, S1, the last piece of the same class. With ADD-OWNER-001 the requester is the
one sender an add for a held order still accepts, and the add branch never looked at the
snapshot's status or Sent count, so an add carrying complete, fulfilled, or a Sent count
closed the order past the banker-only complete check. An add is a new order: Guild:AddRequest
sends it open with nothing Sent, and the payload is serialized when it is sent, so a later
change to the order never rides on it. An add with any other status, or a Sent count above zero,
is now refused. Tests/requestlogcoverage_spec.lua, red with the check switched off.
• **REQ-GATE-002 / BYID-ASKED-001 / SYNC-OWNER-001: the full-record request sync bypassed all three
fixes above.** Peer Review 385b8033, T1. MUT-ID-001, ADD-OWNER-001 and ADD-OPEN-001 live in
Guild:ApplyRequestMutation; the by-id record sync (togbank-rd2, and the older requests-by-id
on togbank-rm / togbank-rd) reached Guild:ApplyRequestSnapshot with no sender, no roster check
and no check that the id was ever asked for, and mergeRequest replaces a held record wholesale
when the incoming one is newer. So one whispered record from anyone, guildmate or not, could change
an order's requester, status, quantity or Sent count, and one tombstone could delete it. Three
checks now stand on that path:
• REQ-GATE-002 (Modules/Chat.lua, IsRequestSyncPeer): every by-id answer and every request
index (togbank-ri, and requests-index on togbank-rm / togbank-rd, whose tombstones also
delete orders) is dropped unless the sender passes IsInCurrentGuildRoster -- the same peers
REQ-GATE-001 already required for the queries.

2026-10-15: *"curious if an 'account mode' can be added so that all requests per-account are shown
in the requests window regardless of which toon you're on."* Every character that logs in is noted
account-wide (accountCharacters in TOGBankClassicOptionDB.global, written by
Events:PLAYER_LOGIN and again whenever the Requests filters update). When the account has more
than one, the Requester dropdown offers "(N) My characters" at the top, and it shows the requests of
all of them. Picking it turns account mode on (requests.accountMode), so the list opens there on
every character; picking any other requester turns it off. Bankers still open on their own Bank
filter. Modules/Options.lua (NoteAccountCharacter, GetAccountCharacters,

• SEARCH-007: the Requests search box now matches every column. The operator, 2026-10-15:
"the search requests needs to filter off the data in any column, right now it doesn't". SEARCH-006
matched only Date, Requester, Bank and Item, so a quantity, a sent count or the status shown by the
date's glyph found nothing. # and Sent are now marked search = true in COLUMNS, and
ColumnText returns what each column shows: the quantity as 3x, the date followed by its status
word (open / fulfilled / cancelled, matching the glyph), and the banker followed by the sister-guild
name XGUILD-LABEL-001 prints beside it. Only Actions, a row of buttons, is not searched.
Modules/UI/Requests.lua; Tests/searchbox_spec.lua (its old assertion that the quantity was not
searched is reversed, and it now loads the real Guild and RequestLog modules for the status and
guild name). Checked in the Classic Era client by the operator, 2026-10-16.
• **LOCALE-SENDTRIM-001: in a guild with players on different client languages, an order mailed
with the Fulfill buttons could go uncredited.** Peer Review 4d7fc1c4. At send time
Mail:OnSendMail (Modules/Mail.lua) cuts each order on the mail to what is really attached, and
it matched the attachment by name: the slot's name from GetSendMailItem is in the banker's
language, the order's is in the requester's, so a German requester's order on an English banker's
mail matched nothing and was dropped. The send slots now record their item id
(GetSendMailItem's second return), each order on the mail carries its request's itemID
(PrepareFulfillMail and FulfillStep), and the cut matches by id. Random-suffix variants share
one base id, so every order first takes the slots matching its id AND name, and only then what is
left by id alone; otherwise, with one variant detached by hand, its order took its sibling's slot
and the wrong order was credited (found in this fix's self-audit, specced). An order with no stored id
(from a pre-REQ-001 client) still matches by name, which is safe because such an order was found
in the banker's bags by that same name. GetSendMailItem returns the id second in every flavour's
UI source (Classic Era, TBC, MoP, Forever; Peer Review f6aa732c). Tests/multifill_spec.lua, red
with the name match.
The same bug sat one call further on (Peer Review f6aa732c, F3/F4): Guild:FulfillRequest
(Modules/RequestLog.lua) matched orders only by lowercased name, so a mail the banker built by
hand, or a stack hand-added to an addon mail, credited nothing when the two clients' languages
differed (a German banker mailing 20 Teufelsstoff left an English order for 20 Felcloth open).
FulfillRequest now takes an optional item id and matches on it when the order has one, serving…

TOGBankClassic Changelog[v1.8.1] (2026-10-09) - Oldest Order FirstBug Fixes
• BANKCOLLECT-SHARE-001: at the bank, Fulfill Oldest skipped a newer order for the same item.
crimsonmane, Discord 2026-10-08: Fulfill Oldest "does not fulfill the oldest order first" when a
second player orders the same item plus more. Mail:FindOldestBankFillableOrder
(Modules/Mail.lua) measured every order against the whole bag count, so the stack I pulled for
the older order also "covered" a newer order of the same item, and the newer one was never
collected for -- it then could not be filled at the mailbox, and only that player's other items
went out. The bags are now handed to open orders oldest-first, and each order's shortfall is what
is left after the older orders' share. Tests/bankcollect_spec.lua pins both the search and the
click-through. Not yet checked in a game client.
• **FCFS-001: at the mailbox, Fulfill Oldest mailed a newer order ahead of an older one for the same
item.** The operator, 2026-10-09: *"you are supposed to fill the oldest order first. first come
first server"*. Mail:FindOldestServiceableOrder (Modules/Mail.lua) picked the oldest order the
bags could fully fill and skipped any it could not, so a newer, smaller order for the same item went
out first and spent the stock the older order was waiting on. I had described that skip as by design
in this entry and in my Discord reply to crimsonmane; it contradicted the operator's rule. Now the
first order for an item that cannot be filled yet holds its place: no newer order for that item is
sent until it is. Orders for other items still go out, since they do not use the same stacks.
Mail:FindMoreOrdersFor (the same person's other orders riding on one mail) now leaves the stock
other people's older orders need, so riding along cannot jump the queue either. The three
fulfillment searches share one "oldest" ordering and one item key. The envelope's tooltip and the
Requests "?" help in Modules/UI/Requests.lua said unfillable orders "are skipped"; both now
describe the first-come-first-served rule, as does the Fulfill Oldest feature line on the
CurseForge page. Four examples in
Tests/bankcollect_spec.lua, including crimsonmane's case. Not yet checked in a game client.
Internal
• SUITE-SPEED-001: the whole forward test run fits in one run again. Every spec builds a fresh
copy of the addon, and libraries that load once per run (AceComm, AceEvent and the other Ace
mixins, AceAddon's queue of addons waiting to load, VersionCheck's listener list) kept a strong
reference to every earlier copy, so the run held tens of thousands of dead frames and each reset's
garbage collection grew slower; late files took 40 seconds or more that take under one alone.
env.reset in Tests/env_togbank.lua now clears those references, and a test window's close
releases its tab contents instead of only hiding them. Measured: objects left after browse_spec
30,800 to 5,400. The forward run passes whole (1970 examples, 2026-10-09) and matches the three
reverse parts (545 + 722 + 703). Clearing the handler lists means no spec can rely on an addon copy
from an earlier file still hearing messages; the reverse parts passing is the check on that. No
addon code changed.

Ultimate Bank Changelog (formerly TOG Bank / TOGBankClassic)[v1.11.1] (2026-10-31) - Tidy-UpBug Fixes
• WIPE-001: any guild member could wipe every guildmate's data. Guild:Wipe's guard read
if not guild and not CanViewOfficerNote(), so it stopped only a guildless non-officer: any member
could send /togbank dev wipeall, and a guildless officer reached a nil concatenation. The receive
branch (Modules/Chat.lua, wipe-command) never asked who sent it. Sending is now officer-only
(with a chat line saying so), and a heard wipe is obeyed only from the home guild's GM or an
officer (Guild:WipeSenderAuthorized, Modules/Guild.lua) -- never a bank character on its note,
never a sister guild's officer. Found by the 2026-10-31 docs audit, which also found README.txt
calling it officer-only. Tests/settings_spec.lua pins both sides.
• DEBUGLOG-FILTER-001: /togbank debuglog [N] [filter] ignored the filter. Since CMD-001 the
dispatcher hands the first word and the remainder separately; the handler read the first word
only. It joins both again, and a non-numeric first word is the filter (/togbank debuglog MAIL).
Tests/chatcommand_spec.lua drives the typed command.
• ARCHIVE-TOOLTIP-001: the Requests window's Archive tab tooltip said "Completed and cancelled
requests", but the tab splits by age alone, so an old open request is there too. Both tab tooltips
now say what the split is (Modules/UI/Requests.lua).
Internal
• DEAD-DELTA-FLAGS-001: deleted FEATURES (DELTA_ENABLED, FORCE_DELTA_SYNC,
FORCE_FULL_SYNC), PROTOCOL.MIN_DELTA_SIZE_RATIO and PROTOCOL.DELTA_SUPPORT_THRESHOLD
(Modules/Constants.lua), DeltaComms:ShouldUseDelta and its Guild:ShouldUseDelta wrapper, and
the /togbank dev forcedelta / forcefull commands (Modules/Chat.lua). The decision function had
no caller, so the flags and both commands changed nothing while printing "ENABLED". /togbank dev
protocol no longer claims delta sync is "enabled/disabled" against the dead threshold; it prints
the protocol v2 share.
• Docs audit: docs/Curseforge_Description.html and README.txt checked against the code.

scanning setting, developer feature flags), corrected /togbank wipeall (it is /togbank dev
wipeall), the settings locations (the Officer tab's sections), the request flow (not a mail), the
license (MIT, not GPL v3), the tab position of Shop, the full General/Bank/Officer settings lists,
the request-limit status text, the companion addons' names (Ultimate Tools, Ultimate Profession
Master), and the support route (Discord). README.txt gained the v1.11.0 highlights.

BRAND_COLOR (ffFF8000, the legendary orange Ultimate Profession Master uses as

BrandVersion() draws the name in the orange, so every window title (UI:WindowTitle) and
/togbank version read "Ultimate Bank v1.11.0" in the brand colour.

addons.description:
WoW quests are full of the language you actually want to learn — but they fly by. You accept, scan for the objective, and the words are gone.

QuestWordHunter keeps the quest on screen as clickable text. See a word you don't know? Click it, add a meaning, mark it Learning. Next time it turns up in another quest it is already coloured. After a while you have a real vocabulary list built from the game, not from a textbook.

What you get
Controller support includes the map and quest-log side tabs: X / Square opens the selected quest's reader and Y / Triangle opens the library. In the library, LB/RB changes tabs and LT/RT changes pages; the D-pad selects controls, A / Cross activates them and B / Circle returns. Lists and settings use the same selection outline, and left/right adjusts a selected slider. The English panel scrolls with up/down or LB/RB. With the voice engine loaded, the reader's triggers replay and pause/resume speech. Explicit WordHunter bindings take priority. ConsolePort uses its own interface cursor and configured button hints; addon windows and side tabs are registered through its public API.
• Quest text you can click instead of retyping into a notes app
• Colours and underlines for New, Learning, Known and Ignored, so you see progress in the paragraph itself — keep both or pick one
• A meaning, a personal note, and the sentence the word came from
• Previous / Next in the word editor, on the row with Cancel and Save (also the arrow keys when no box has focus, and LB/RB on a controller), so a quest can be read word by word without the mouse
• An optional recall check: a word you have been learning for a day asks how well you knew it, 1 to 5, before it shows its meaning. Words that keep scoring low are difficult, and you can export them for a flashcard app
• A word list and simple stats — /whw words, /whw stats
• A quiet Ready for Known hint after five different quests and two weeks. It never promotes anything by itself
• Separate lists per language, so German and French don't mix
• Windows you can move, resize and theme — /whw settings
• A controller works too: the D-pad moves between words; the reader and editor show which buttons open, save, close or switch reading mode. Needs the game's own controller support; the full map is under Settings

Buttons stay in English. Quest text stays in the language you set in WoW.

Assign shortcuts under Options → Key Bindings → AddOns → WordHunterWoW. The reader's footer and the word editor show the current bindings and update when you change them. With controller support enabled in both WoW and the addon, hints use the client's controller button labels, including its selected Xbox/PlayStation glyphs. Explicit WordHunterWoW controller bindings override the panel's default controls. Unassigned keyboard actions have no invented default. The editor's arrow keys and recall ratings 1–5 work locally outside combat; arrows move the text caret while typing. Enter saves from the translation field, and Escape closes the windows.
Quest library
Open /whw quests, or click the WordHunterWoW book side tab beside the Quest Log.
The library follows your learning language from Settings. The reader displays
English alongside that language when both texts are available. Words and recall
ratings are saved separately for each language.
The German Dictionary includes German and English Classic quest texts,
plus native Forever cache records; no separate quest-data addon is needed.
Text actually seen in your client takes
precedence, and offers are archived immediately so you can study them after a
fast party has completed the quest.
No quest needs to be selected. The library opens on My quests, containing
this character's current and completed quests. **Show only current quests in
quest log hides the completed-only entries. The All in game quests** tab
contains all quest records stored for this game client. Both tabs display English…

Validation: Save-to-RB replay reproduced token 5 -> 1 before the fix and token 5 -> 6 after it. The existing 76 archived Lua suites give the same 70 passes before and after, with no new regressions. Sources and packaged Lua compile with Lua 5.1. Live visuals and physical gamepad behavior remain to be confirmed.

The reader and word editor now show assigned keyboard shortcuts and the controller button labels reported by WoW. Hints update when bindings or controller settings change.

addons.description:
This addon collects ingame text from book items and objects, and allows them to be read anywhere. To open the frame, a button on the Minimap and AddOn Compartment Frame are both provided, as well, as the slash command /lorekeeper or /lorek.

Items are collected upon closing a text item or text object. Items can't be retroactively collected from past books (otherwise it would be very easy to make this addon and data contributions wouldn't be necessary). Usually a copy of an item is stored in the collected data if the text content has changed due to a quest progression (ie artifact books). If the player-saved data is different from locally stored data, it will instead usually display the player-saved data. Some game objects are not real text items but in fact are NPCs in disguise using gossip text (which this addon does not collect). Mail items (when available) are collected and stored in the mail module upon closing the "Plain Letter" item itself, rather than necessarily scanning the mail. Plain Letters with no sender name (ie letters transferred cross-server or from NPCs) can't be stored as the GUID data is unavailable for some reason.

Eventually the plan is to implement a collection-based system and track progress on various achievements, not too unlike mount, pet, or transmog collection, but with a focus on ingame lore items. It will be a continuous work-in-progress, as collecting a baseline of known texts will take some time.
Lorekeeper now also supports Text to Speech
For additional voice chat options you can visit the Blizzard Support Page. More "Natural Voice" options can additionally be found and set up with NaturalVoiceSAPIAdapter.

To help contribute your own data, you can submit your data on the github issue template or place it in the #addon-dev channel in my discord. You'll need to find a file located here: retail\WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\Lorekeeper.lua If you would like to be credited for your submission, please provide a username or some sort of online handle by which you want to be addressed as (this is public info in an addon). Do not include Lorekeeper_Mail.lua as it is not a necessary upload and contains your personal mail items and custom items. It will not be contributed to the addon.

Happy hunting!

addons.description:
This addon enables Masque (CurseForge, Wago, WoWInterface) to skin built-in WoW inventory elements. An up-to-date version of Masque is required for it to work.

If you like the base WoW interface and don't want to use a separate bag or inventory mod, you're in the right place.

You can install this addon from CurseForge, Wago, or WoWInterface.
Features
Masque Blizzard Inventory can currently skin the following elements, according to your game version:
• Backpack
• Main Bags
• Combined Backpack
• Reagent Bag
• Bank (including Warband Bank)
• Guild Bank
• Mail
• Merchants
• Loot
• Character
• Inspect Character
• Equipment Flyouts
• Keyring (Classic before Cataclysm and Forever)
• Bag Bar (Classic and Forever)

Each element type is its own group so you can configure them independently from Masque's Skin Settings.

The Warband Bank and Bank use the same inventory elements in Retail, so they share skin options as well.

An additional options panel is provided to hide background and slot artwork that might clash with certain Masque skins.
Forever Support
World of Warcraft: Forever has a unique mixture of Classic and Retail inventory features, and should be fully supported.

In Forever, bags are grouped as follows:
• Main Bags includes all common bags including the Keyring
• The Reagent Bag is always skinned independently
• The Backpack is skinned independently unless you have enabled the Combined Backpack
• The Combined Backpack takes over the Backpack and Main Bags, except the Keyring, which is still skinned from the Main Bags group
• Bank Bags are now part of a combined Bank that works like the Combined Backpack and cannot be skinned independently
Classic Support
Classic versions available in the US are fully supported. Elements not available in Classic will not appear in Masque's Skin Settings.

In Classic, all bags are consolidated to a single Bags group, including the Keyring. This is due to the way the game reuses Bag windows.

Most interface frames in Classic are built using a single background image, rather than multiple layers, so the options to hide background and slot artwork are not feasible. Adding this feature would require drawing replacement artwork and including it with the addon, so it is not planned.

I don't play Classic so testing is somewhat limited, but I'll do my best to address bug reports promptly.
Compatibility
This addon is intended to skin the base WoW interface. Addons that heavily modify parts of the base interface may conflict. If you experience a conflict, use Masque's Skin Settings to disable the affected group and reload your UI. This should allow the other addon to control the interface without interference.

If you'd like to see Masque support in a conflicting addon, try sending a feature request to that addon's author directly.
Localization
If you'd like to help localize this addon, please submit translations here.
LLM Policy
LLM ("Generative AI") agents are not used for development of this project and such contributions will not be accepted.
Other Mods
If you want to skin the built-in action bars as well, check out Masque Blizzard Bars (CurseForge, Wago, WoWInterface)!
Special Thanks
Thanks to StormFX, the author of Masque, for a ton of feedback and development tips and for creating a logo for the addon.

addons.description:
This addon provides a modern update to merchant (vendor) interfaces in WoW.

You can install this addon from CurseForge, Wago, or WoWInterface.
Features
Merchant Plus adds an additional tab to all WoW merchants, which provides the following enhancements:
• Wider vertical scrolling list to allow more information to be viewed at once
• Sortable columns of item data
• Optional columns containing additional item data

An options panel is included to configure basic settings.
Planned Features
In future updates, the following major improvements are planned:
• Additional data columns and options to choose the visibility and order of them
• Filtering based upon data in one or more columns
• Searching based upon data in one or more columns

There is no specific timeline for these features to be completed.
Forever Support
World of Warcraft: Forever has the same interface features as Retail, so it is fully supported.
Classic Support
Merchant Plus requires interface features only available in Retail. Blizzard periodically backports features to Classic versions, so the required functions may be available eventually. Until that time, Classic support is not planned.
Compatibility
This addon does not replace the existing UI, but it makes many changes to the merchant window, so it may conflict with other addons that modify the contents or layout. Addons that replace the window will prevent Merchant Plus from appearing entirely. ElvUI is supported when the Blizzard Merchant Frame skin is enabled. Other addons that re-skin the merchant window may cause layout problems.

Ideally, Merchant Plus will not be the cause of any conflicts. If you discover any, please report them, and I'll fix what I can from the Merchant Plus side.
Localization
If you'd like to help localize this addon, please submit translations here.
LLM Policy

XephUI1.3.0 (2026-10-15)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• updates
• Merge pull request #4 from ljosberinn/feature/action-tracker
add action tracker
• Merge pull request #3 from ljosberinn/feature/break-timer
Feature/break timer
• add action tracker
• Document the break timer module
• Drop the scope block around the parked icon's layout
• Inline the break timer's single-use functions
Eleven of them had exactly one caller. The geometry helpers fold into the
callers that used them, the two icon acquisitions and the positioning fold
into the phase that enters them, and the two per-addon message handlers
collapse into the event script, which drops the duplicated rank check and
StartBreak tail they each carried.
The timeline hooks were guarded by a flag on a path that only ever ran once,
so they now install at load instead.
Kept as functions: EnterParkedPhase, ValidateParkedLayout and OnUpdateTick,
each of which would push its single caller past a readable length.
• Inline the break timer's single-use constants
The layout inputs, the clamp bounds, the throttle and the tick interval each
had exactly one reader, so the numbers now sit at the point of use with the
comments that justified them.
Also declares BigWigs and DBM-Core as optional dependencies. The boss mod
check runs at our own ADDON\_LOADED, where neither is otherwise guaranteed to
have loaded; OptionalDeps forces both ahead of us when installed and is inert
when they are not.
• Do nothing when BigWigs or DBM is installed
Both render their own break display, and competing with that means double
bars. Checked at login rather than at our own ADDON\_LOADED, since neither is
guaranteed to have loaded by then.
The BigWigs callback registration goes with it. It existed to catch a solo
/break, which dispatches locally and never reaches the wire, but without a
boss mod installed there is no /break to issue. CHAT\_MSG\_ADDON on both
prefixes is now the only ingest path.
The start throttle stays: a single /break puts both wire formats on the air
so that BigWigs and DBM users alike see it, so every break still arrives
twice.
• Drop the break timer's saved variables
A break no longer survives a reload. BigWigs already persists its own break
and re-fires BigWigs\_StartBreak on login, which the callback registration
picks up, so the saved break only ever covered a client running neither
BigWigs nor DBM that reloaded mid-break.
The fallback display loses its remembered position with it and is now fixed
rather than draggable. TearDown absorbs EndBreak, which existed only to clear
the saved break.
• Drop icon setting compat from the parked break icon
The parked icon no longer mirrors IconSize, ShowSpellName, ShowTimer or
FlipHorizontally, and the name text it needed is gone with them. At a
non-default IconSize it is now the wrong size against the event it hands off
to, but still correctly positioned, since track offsets are independent of
icon size.
The countdown is unconditional rather than gated on ShowTimer, and the four
setting-updater hooks that existed only to re-derive all of this go with it.
• Render BigWigs and DBM break timers on the encounter timeline
Ingest /break from either addon and display it ourselves. Above the long
track's maximum event duration the break is a replica icon parked at that
track's entry offset; at and below it, a real C_EncounterTimeline script
event takes over and runs the last minute natively.
Ingest is dependency-free: a CHAT_MSG_ADDON listener on the BigWigs and
D5 prefixes covers both wire formats, and rank is validated against the
event's own sender rather than the name in the DBM body, which strips realm
spaces and hyphens and so does not round-trip cross-realm. BigWigs' callback
registry is used additionally when it is loaded, because a solo /break
dispatches locally and never reaches the wire.

Blizzard's offsets, which do not exist until the timeline has been shown and…

addons.description:
The controller / gamepad addon for WoW Forever: quality-of-life tweaks that make playing
with a controller even better. Works with Xbox, PlayStation (DualSense) and Switch Pro controllers.
Everything is set up and used from the controller, no keyboard step needed. Every module but
Controller and Wheel works with the mouse and keyboard too: the windows follow what you used last
(the pad's legend and cursor with the pad; buttons to click, the wheel to scroll, tooltips on hover
and Esc with the mouse).

Free on CurseForge.

Each feature is its own addon (enable only the ones you want in the AddOns list); all of them need
the core, Improved Forever:

| Addon | What it does |
|---|---|
| ImprovedForever | The core: button glyphs, the configuration panel, the Bindings tab (every press on one drawing of the controller, and its keyboard / mouse press), bag clean-up, touchpad corners, the game data (QuestieDB's, recipes) and the item verdict every module shares. Required. Holds the former Controller module. |
| ImprovedForever_Wheel | Wheels on R3 combos, the recent action slot. |
| ImprovedForever_Vibration | Vibration on game events and spell casts. |
| ImprovedForever_Minimap | Names beside the minimap's dots (herbs, ore, quests, NPCs, party members: you choose), gathering alerts. Formerly Gather. |
| ImprovedForever_Map | The peek map. |
| ImprovedForever_Chat | The chat with the controller: pick a line, then an item or other link in it. |
| ImprovedForever_Auction | The controller auction window, prices over time, tasks. |
| ImprovedForever_Junk | Finds and marks junk, sells it with the vendor's Sell All Junk, destroys it from the bags or the loot window. Formerly Destroy. |
| ImprovedForever_Wiki | Everything about an item. |
| ImprovedForever_Journal | A diary of your days, read as a book. |
| ImprovedForever_Fishing | Fishing from the controller: fishing mode, a cast bar of its own, the session's stringer, the Fish Collection. |
| ImprovedForever_Camp | Sitting by a campfire as a cutscene: the HUD gone, black bars, the camera cutting between shots round you, your day told back from the Journal, the camp's benefits when they come, what's said near you as subtitles. |
| ImprovedForever_Immersion | The game's HUD made immersive: the target's health across the top, yours bottom left in the same look in a ring of your experience, your health and power as lines along the bottom edge, your pet and party as cards, the gamepad bar as Hogwarts Legacy's spell diamonds bottom right, the chat as just its lines until used. Needs Journal and Spoken. |
| ImprovedForever_QuestTracker | The objective tracker, rebuilt as the game's own: sorted quests (zone, level, title, distance, completed), an objective complete sound, full controller support. Formerly Improved Quest Tracker. |
Features
• Wheels on R3 combos, laid out like the game's radial menu. Built in: Quest Items and
Consumables (each fills itself from your bags) and Emotes. Make wheels of your own, mixing
spells, items, macros, emotes and chat phrases you add (D-pad up / down picks a phrase's channel on
the wheel), or a shaman's totems, or a trinket swap. Aim with the right stick.
• Recent action slot on R3, placed in Edit Mode.
• Touchpad corner actions.
• Chat lines: with the chat open on the controller, D-pad Up picks its lines, left / right the links in a line
(their tooltips); Cross opens an item in the Wiki, Square puts the link in your message.
• Button overrides for L3 click and double-click.
• Vibration on game events and spell casts, with per-action patterns.
• Junk: what the bags no longer need is marked junk (the game's coin on its slot), from quests (QuestieDB's
data), your professions' recipes, auction prices, your class and whether it's soulbound. L2 + L3 on a bag item
marks it junk or not junk, remembered per character. A vendor's Sell All Junk sells it all. Its Destroy…

• Willo knows WoW Forever at launch: its spells, talents, items, quests and racials, like Ruthless for humans.

• Willo sounds better: she reads every answer all the way through, her voice holds up when a voice service is slow, and on a Mac it no longer crackles.
• Translations stay whole: no English mixed in, in German, French, Portuguese, Swedish, Italian, Russian, Ukrainian or Romanian. A Russian, Ukrainian or Romanian story shows once it's translated.
• Fixes: 13 lore entries corrected, reports and shared text say which version of WoW they came from, and the website and lore page read better on phones.

• The lore, retold: the stories of the starting lands and the zones after them are rewritten and read anew in both narrators' voices, and a story no longer opens by repeating its summary. More zones follow.
• Willo cheers your big moments: a new level, a quest you carried a long time, an epic or your first mount gets one short, cheery line from her, never in a fight. Ask her to chime in more, less or not at all.
• Willo is quieter while you play: she no longer drops lore remarks on her own; ask her to chime in more to bring them back.
• Willo for Mac: Willo now comes for Mac as well as Windows.
• Willo works without the add-on: she finds your game by herself, answers from the first second, typed or out loud, and fixes the add-on in one click when it isn't loading.
• Willo changes things your way: ask her to change her color, size, voice or keys and she does it with Undo, or have her ask first. Her talk key works anywhere, and she answers out loud sooner.
• Azeroth Survivors picks: Willo picks your cards by the numbers, weighs your whole build, plans ahead and tells you when to reroll or banish.
• Translations and fixes: French, German, Spanish and Portuguese lore uses your game's own names in more places, and 28 lore entries are corrected.

• The rewritten lore is read aloud again: the places, people, items and quests that were rewritten tell their new story in both narrators' voices, and their hidden passages are recorded too.
• Quest givers pause between sentences: the quest-giver voices no longer rush, with a natural breath at the end of each sentence.
• Willo knows your Azeroth Survivors build: she reads your save (talents, gear, perks, zones won) so her picks fit the build you have.
• Willo on stream: her chat popup over the game now shows in your OBS Browser Source, and closing it removes it from the stream.
• Playlist opens from every page, even while a story page, History or the Road is open.
• Pack names you can read: Ukrainian and Russian packs show their English names in Options unless your game font can draw the native ones.
• Downloads page, smoother: voice cards Setup can't install yet go straight to CurseForge, and Willo's card turns dark in dark mode.
• Corrected lore in 33 entries.

• Books are read aloud: open a book, letter or plaque and the narrator reads each page as you turn it, with Listen
to hear it again. They come with the More quests (levels 40+) voice pack.
• Rewritten lore, read aloud: the rewritten places, people, items and quests tell their new stories in both
narrators' voices, hidden passages too.
• Willo remembers you: tell her to remember that you main a hunter and she keeps it in mind, with Undo under her answer.
Settings › Privacy & sharing lists everything she remembers, each with Forget.
• Romanian and Swedish: Lore Forever in Română (translated by Indurin) and Svenska, as language packs.
• A simpler downloads page: your language and narrator are picked for you. Choose The add-on, Storyteller or
Everything, and Setup comes ticked for what you picked.
• Which voice pack am I missing? Options > Narration voices says whether you have all of a narrator's stories or
names the project to install, and a quest's play button names the pack for its level.
• Quest dialogue by level: three downloads, 1–25, 26–50 and 51–60. Have the quest pack? Add 26–50 and 51–60 to
keep hearing quests past level 25.

so they sit together. Item stories now come with Quest Stories 40+.

addons.description:
Displays a bar on screen that allows quick access to enchanting, jewelcrafting, and inscription professions by presenting a Disenchant/Prospect/Mill button and all of the breakable items you have for that profession next to it. Also displays a bar for any locked junkboxes in your inventory if you're a Rogue. This allows one-click access for breaking down items instead of finding the item in your bag, clicking the appropriate profession/skill button, and clicking the item for each and every item you want to break. For prospecting and milling, you will see the number of items you have alongside the number of times you can break it. In the prospecting screenshot on the right, the player has 169 total Saronite Ore in his bags which will allow for 33 total prospects.
Usage
By default, if you have the appropriate profession and items in your inventory, a bar will appear with the profession ability followed by any items that are eligible for breaking. You can hold shift to drag the bar around if you want to move it. Clicking the profession button will activate that ability (disenchant/prospect/mill) and clicking an item will break it. You don't have to click the profession button first as simply clicking the item will automatically break it down. Right-clicking an item will place that item on the ignore list so it won't show up in the list again. The ignore list can be managed in the addon's configuration panel.
Configuration
Typing /brk will open the configuration settings (or you can get to it from Blizzard's Interface options) which consist of:
• Hide if no breakables: this will control whether you see the profession button or not when nothing breakable is detected
• Max number to display: this controls the highest number of items that you will see next to your profession button. If this is 5 but you have 10 breakable items in your bags, you will only see 5 at a time.
• Show soulbound items: aimed at enchanters, this controls whether or not you will see items that are soulbound as breakable items or not.

addons.description:
Beta for World of Warcraft Forever (Interface 16001).

Yellow ! start markers for normal quests, blue ! for repeatable, red-orange ! for dungeon and raid, class-colored ! for class quests, and copper ! for profession quests on Blizzard’s native world map.

Forever already has a modern quest tracker and objective pins for quests in your log. This addon does not replace that. It adds start locations for unaccepted quests.
Requirements
• World of Warcraft Forever only (not Retail, Classic Era, or Cataclysm Classic)
• Folder name must be exactly ForeverQuestPins
• No other addons required (not TomTom or HereBeDragons)

TomTom is an optional waypoint provider. The default is Blizzard Map Pins.
Features
• Yellow ! pins for normal quest starts, blue ! for repeatable, red-orange ! for dungeon and raid, class-colored ! for class quests, and copper ! for profession quests
• Map pin tooltips with [level] quest name (Forever tracker level when available; Questie inline name when the client has not loaded a title) and NPC names (IDs only if debug is on)
• NPC mouseover tooltips listing quests you can accept and quests ready to turn in (on by default)
• Pins stay on the map art in windowed and fullscreen layouts
• Nearby spawn points for one quest group share one pin (up to six per quest). Hover to see the spawn count in the tooltip and every spawn location on the map. Turn off Show spawn clusters to show one pin per quest instead
• Overlapping starts on the same spot stack into one pin
• Shift-click a pin to hide it (every quest on a stacked pin) for the current character; restore with Reset hidden quest pins in settings or /fqp unhide
• Adjustable low-level range: choose how many levels below you a quest must be before its pin is hidden (default 9)
• Optional auto-accept and auto-turn-in when talking to NPCs (off by default; hold Shift to skip once)
• Seasonal / holiday starts (Lunar Festival elders, Darkmoon Faire, …) off by default
• AQ opening war effort commodity pins in Orgrimmar / Ironforge on by default (turn off in settings if the stack is too noisy)

Quest coordinates, quest-giver IDs, turn-in targets, and restrictions come from QuestieDB Forever data, with holiday and instance-tag policy from Questie. The Go tool go run ./cmd/fqp build-db generates the addon database. Quests without a usable spawn stay in the database for tooltips and prerequisites but may not get a map pin.
addons.name: forever-quest-markers

addons.description:
Bulk mail reception made really easy
Addon Description
Bulk mail reception made really easy. This addon allows you to selectively pick mails to open from the inbox, open all mails with money or open all items.
Key Features
There are many bulk email openers available to choose from. However Bulk Mail Inbox has several unique features:
• Shows a dialog with all items and money in your mailbox.
• Allows you to take individual items even if they were all sent in one email.
• You can mark multiple items to take without taking all.
• Allows easy comparison of items in the mail list with items you're currently using (just hold shift down while hovering the items).
• Inbox pagination and filtering.
• Clicking on a column header now sorts that header. Before clicking on any header just rotated the sorting to a new column.
• Sorting is reversed if you click on the header which currently is sorted.
• Better placement of the tooltip (now sits next to the frame that opened it)
• Pressing and releasing the shift key while hovering an item will now properly show/hide the comparison window.
• Fixed opening of mails is now throttled to prevent errors and as a result opening a lot of mails is now much better.
• The list of items is updated during auto opening emails.

addons.description:
Gold and currencies, always in view.

Aurarium is a World of Warcraft addon that tracks gold and currencies across characters. It brings recorded balances together in clear overviews and makes changes over time easy to follow.

> ⚠️ Important! This addon requires Arcane Wizard: Library. See Installation & Quick Start for installation details.
Key Features
Gold Display - Shows the current gold balance in a customizable display that fits into the game interface.

Gold and Currency Overview - Brings recorded balances together in different views, providing an overview of individual characters and the account.

Chart - Explore your balance history in a chart and choose the period you want to examine.
Features
Individual features and display options can be configured in the addon settings. Aurarium supports an account profile and character profiles.
Gold Display
• Shows or hides the compact gold display independently of balance tracking.

addons.description:
One library for every addon.

Arcane Wizard: Library is a World of Warcraft addon that provides the shared foundation for all Arcane Wizard addons. It brings common functionality together in one place, making it easier to develop and maintain the addons that use it.
For Players
Install Arcane Wizard: Library alongside your Arcane Wizard addons and keep it enabled. It provides the shared functionality they need, runs in the background, and has no interface of its own.
For Developers
Arcane Wizard: Library provides reusable components that simplify addon development and maintenance. Shared functionality can be maintained centrally and used across multiple addons. Other addon developers are welcome to use the library in their own projects.
FeaturesAddon Context
The library provides shared addon registration, access to settings, minimap and Addon Compartment integration, and debug output.
Frames, Tables & Controls
Reusable windows, scrollable tables, tabs, and input controls match Blizzard's native appearance for each supported game version.
Prebuilt Windows & Dialogs
The library provides ready-to-use changelog windows, link popups, and confirmation dialogs.
Utilities
Shared helpers handle character identifiers and copy nested tables.
Settings
The library integrates addon options into Blizzard's settings menu with reusable layouts, profile support, and native key binding controls.
How to Integrate
1. Add the following to your .toc file:

> ## Dependencies: ArcaneWizardLibrary

2. Set the dependency on the CurseForge project page to ensure users download it automatically.
Library Revision
X-Revision in ArcaneWizardLibrary.toc is an integer maintained separately from the release version and exposed as ArcaneWizardLibrary.ADDON_REVISION. Increase it when addons need to distinguish changes to the library's public functions or behavior. Builds preserve the revision.

Each Arcane Wizard addon declares its minimum revision as X-Library-Revision in its TOC and checks it before using the library. Equal or higher revisions are accepted. A missing, invalid, or older revision stops addon startup and reports the required and installed revisions in chat and through the Lua error handler. SavedVariables are left intact.

When an addon starts using newer library functionality, raise only that addon's minimum revision to the first revision providing it. Higher library revisions must continue to support addons that require earlier revisions.

addons.description:
Your unfinished WoW: Forever Legacy challenges, on the world map, for the zone you're looking at.

Legacy Forever shows unfinished challenges on the world map and tracks the ones you choose.

Discover an area and its shading lifts as the corner's percentage goes up. Click the corner to fold it away.

Half of Ashenvale explored: the shield's number is what's left on this map, and its menu lists it by challenge.

Zoom out and each zone with dungeon objectives left gets a badge.

Challenges you track sit in the objective tracker under the game's own header, with live progress.

Tick a challenge in the menu to track it.
Features
• Map button in the world map's top-right button column: a Legacy shield with a number inside, the unfinished objectives on the map you're viewing. Its menu lists them by challenge, with a tick box to track each one. Challenges with no fixed place are grouped the way the Legacy panel groups them.
• Tracker: a Legacy section in the objective tracker, under the game's own All Objectives header, lists what you track, with live progress. A zone ticked in the map menu tracks just that zone, such as "0/12 Explore Felwood". Click a challenge to open it in the Legacy panel, or right-click to stop tracking it. How it lists steps.
• Map pins on dungeon and raid entrances, with the challenge each counts toward and its Legacy points. With AtlasLoot installed, tooltips also show its recommended level range. Left-click a pin to travel there: with Shortest Path Forever it plans the whole journey, otherwise it sets the game's own waypoint. If another addon already marks entrances, the map menu turns these pins off.
• Undiscovered areas are shaded darker in their real shape on the zone map, so you can see where to go at a glance. Hovering one names it and, when a Legacy challenge counts it, shows the challenge, its points and how many of the zone's areas are left. The map menu turns the shading off.
• Zone completion, Guild Wars 2 style: how much of a zone's areas, dungeons, raids and Legacy objectives you've done, as a percentage in the map's corner, a badge on each zone of a continent map and, if you tick it, the tracker. Flight paths, local reputations and, with Questie, quests can be added under "What counts". A finished zone gets a toast and a sound. What it counts.
• No fixed location lists challenges whose remaining work isn't tied to a place, such as levels, skills and ranks.

Progress comes from the game each time, so it matches the Legacy panel and follows whichever challenge set your character sees.
addons.name: legacy-forever

releases.changelog: • Legacy data now names the 1.60.1.70755 build. The legacy challenge data is regenerated from the new Forever client build, so the addon's own data carries the build it came from. The regenerated values match the previous build, so nothing a player sees changes.

• World-map drawings share Forever Core's private canvas. Pins, scale and right-click behaviour come from the shared canvas helper, which leaves Blizzard's map tables untouched.
• Screenshots keep their content on the data build. Map metadata, tiles and overlays pin the generated data build while window chrome keeps the reviewed UI art build.

• Dungeon entrances follow the world map's filter. Turning off Show instance entrances also hides Legacy's dungeon and raid pins, while exploration and completion information remain visible. Thanks to cjber for requesting the compatibility audit (#235).
• The map menu stays beside the map's own controls. Questie's and other Krowi map buttons stack on the left, so they no longer push Legacy's menu down an empty slot on the right. Thanks to cjber for requesting the compatibility audit (#235).
• Exploration tooltips remain available with Leatrix Maps. Revealed ground stays clear until you hover an unfinished area, which still highlights and shows its Legacy information. Thanks to cjber for requesting the compatibility audit (#235).

• Preview screenshots use the pinned client art build. The rendered scenes now take their window art from the repo's pinned UI art build through Forever Core's shared renderer, so a preview cannot show chrome the shipped client does not draw. Data generation stays on the client build it already targets.

• Compare observed flight paths with guild and group members. /lf leaderboard ranks distinct paths observed at flight masters on the same client ruleset. Peer totals are player-reported. Sharing starts on; /lf share off, the map menu or Flight-path records in Settings stops sends and peer comparisons while keeping personal history. Unknown rulesets keep only your personal row. Thanks to cjber for requesting the peer leaderboard work (cjber/forever-core#49, #231).

• After a reinstall or a move to a new PC, your next change always reaches the guild. Before, others could keep showing your old data.

• Craft List: the crafter on an item row is shown by short name, and one of your own characters is preferred.

• Works on every game language. Professions now show correctly, with icon and rank, between players on different client languages, for example German and English.
• No sync during combat. GuildCrafters stays quiet while you fight and catches up a few seconds after. The open window is not refreshed in the middle of a fight either.
• Old data cleans itself up. Members who left the guild disappear from Crafting, Mats and the tooltips right away, and are removed from your saved data after 7 days. A profession you dropped is hidden from the guild right away and removed after 7 days. If the member or the profession comes back within that week, nothing is lost.
• /gc sync asks the guild for fresh data now, instead of waiting for the next automatic update.
• Status line at the bottom right of the window: when you last received data, and how many guild members with the addon are online. Hover it for details.
• /gc tooltip on|off turns the "Crafted by" and "Guild has" lines on item tooltips off or on. Inside the GuildCrafters window they are always shown.
Improved
• Lighter in large guilds: the Crafting tab opens and searches with far less work when many members use the addon, and guild roster updates no longer cause extra work.
• After a reinstall or a move to a new PC, your next change always reaches the guild. Before, others could keep showing your old data.
Fixed
• /gc help showed "tankealer|dps|uto" instead of "tank|healer|dps|auto".
• Craft List: the crafter on an item row is shown by short name, and one of your own characters is preferred.
Good to know
• The footer texts in Craft List and Mats are shorter, to make room for the status line.
• Cleanup only happens on your own computer. Guild members on 0.14 keep seeing departed members until they update.

Position

1.2.0WoW Forever
• Add support for WoW Forever 1.60.1 / Interface 16001.
• Add a Forever-specific purple pet XP bar and compact pet-level medallion.

• Automatically hide the pet level at the client level cap.
• Add optional overrides to always show the XP bar or pet level.
Options

• Add persistent Show XP Bar and Show Pet Level settings.
• Add visibility-behavior overrides and a Defaults button.

Compatibility and maintenance
• Preserve Classic Anniversary 2.5.6 / Interface 20506 and Classic Era 1.15.9 / Interface 11509 support.

addons.description:
Your Hunter has an XP bar. Why shouldn't your pet?

A World of Warcraft Forever and Classic (Anniversary, Seasons, Hardcore, Era) addon that adds a compact XP bar and level display to your Hunter's pet frame, so you can track your pet's progress without constantly opening the Pet window.

Designed to feel like a natural extension of Blizzard's UI, it's lightweight, unobtrusive, and stays out of the way when the information is no longer useful.
Features
• Pet XP bar and current level at a glance
• Automatically hides the XP bar when your pet can't gain XP
• Automatically hides pet level at max level
• Options to show, hide, or always display either element
• Forever and Classic XP bar color presets plus a custom color picker
• Moveable and lockable with persistent positioning
• Native Blizzard-style appearance
• Supports WoW Forever, Classic Anniversary (TBC), and Classic Era (Hardcore, SoD). Not tested with Classic (MoP).
Commands
/pxp options — Open settings
/pxp lock — Lock the display
/pxp unlock — Unlock for repositioning
/pxp reset — Reset its position
Acknowledgements
Inspired by PetXPBar by weryis and PetXP by waggz81

PetXPBarPlus is maintained by StormtrooperTK421 on GitHub. Please submit issues and I'll do my best to troubleshoot, replicate, and resolve any issues as well as add recommended features.

addons.changelog:
Language-aware catalogs
• Respect the selected addon language for catalog labels, item-name search, set previews, classes, inventory slots and permission roles.
• Recognize locale aliases such as enUs/enGB and esMX. Auto follows the game-client text locale, not Windows.
• Bundle 24,312 English item names and all 154 skill labels in English, French and Spanish. Import available localized quests, NPCs, objects and achievements.
• Support modern item APIs, request uncached English names once, and refresh loaded names without resetting the entered quantity.
• Do not silently fall back to French when another language is selected. Missing translations are explicitly labeled with the record ID; mismatched-language native tooltips use a localized summary instead.
• Translate the remaining compatibility warning and Auto setting label.
Collections and bulk tools
• 24,335 items, 141 client-referenced mount spells and 277 client-defined equipment sets.
• Selectable, confirmed all-mount and verified GM-spell learning, with captured-target protection. Existing all-compatible-skills previews remain available.
• Direct T1, T2, T3 and BiS filters, plus responsive four-button toolbars.
• Nine sourced Classic Era PvE Phase-6 candidate collections, with availability-checked item IDs and source links.
Important limits
• This is not a claim of 100% translation of every custom record. English offline item coverage is 24,312 / 24,335; French and especially Spanish exports still have gaps. Matching-language client APIs can resolve additional item/spell names. Full coverage reports are included in docs/LOCALIZATION.md and docs/LOCALE_COVERAGE.json.
• Five newly exposed mount references await matching-language names; server learnability and faction/race restrictions are not bypassed.
• All 27 original tier sets are visible. The 18 original T1/T2 sets with missing member metadata remain inspectable but cannot be granted. T3 uses verified member IDs.
• Phase-6 collections are verified subsets of sourced recommendations, not complete optimized loadouts or guarantees for custom realm balance.
• Chat transport is unchanged from 0.11.1. The reported "Interface action failed" error has not been reproduced or confirmed resolved in the live client by this release.
Installation
Download ForeverGM-0.12.0.zip, extract its ForeverGM folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the previous addon files, then run /reload. Select English (enUS), or Auto on an English game client. Existing SavedVariables are kept. The SHA-256 file is supplied alongside the ZIP.
Validation
58 TOC modules parse in Lua 5.1 mode; static dataset/locale checks and 6,313 mocked runtime assertions pass. All 93 packaged files were checked against the source and locally installed copy. Mocked tests do not claim successful live-client rendering or server command acceptance.
addons.description:
An icon-driven Game Master toolkit for WoWForever.

ForeverGM brings searchable game data, illustrated collections, skill management and server commands into one resizable in-game panel. Browse immediately, inspect an entry, then choose the action you need. No external application or database connection is required while playing.

Download the latest release · Changelog · Command reference · Report an issue
Compatibility
Targets WoWForever Classic beta 1.60.1, with Interface 16001, and its ForeverCore / TrinityCore-derived server using Vanilla world data converted from VMaNGOS. The local executable observed on 2026-10-16 is build 70374 (previously 70338); automated mock tests are not a live-client execution guarantee.

This is not a generic addon for every VMaNGOS server, the original 1.12 client, or official retail WoW. Command syntax, permissions and available IDs may differ on another server. See compatibility notes.

An authorized GM account is required for privileged actions. ForeverGM does not grant permissions or bypass server-side RBAC.

ForeverGM 0.11.1 — Immediate chat commandsFixed
• Isolated commands now send directly from the button or confirmation click, instead of deferring every action to OnUpdate.
• Commands use the normal chat API as a whisper to your own character, matching the verified ForeverCore command parser. No delayed public SAY messages are sent.
• Replaced the misleading "awaiting server response" label with "Sent to chat: .command", in English, French and Spanish. The addon also echoes the sent command locally in chat.
• Optional response observation expires after eight seconds. It never blocks subsequent commands or automatically retries a command.
• Transport failures are reported without being recorded as successful sends.
Safeguards retained
• Confirmation dialogs for marked operations.
• Rate limiting for rapid clicks and bulk queues (default 0.45 seconds).
• Queue cancellation, target-change protection, input validation and the existing combat guard.
• Server RBAC remains authoritative. Sending a command does not prove server-side success.
Verification
• Static validation: 53 TOC modules, 680 command records, dataset/locale/version/texture checks passed.
• Lua 5.1 syntax checks passed.
• 2,269 mocked-runtime assertions passed, including immediate sending, chat recipient/channel, modern and legacy chat APIs, no-response progress, failure handling and cancellation safeguards.
• No live GM command was executed by the automated tests. Check the actual result in-game after updating.
Install / update
Download ForeverGM-0.11.1.zip below, extract its ForeverGM folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, and replace the previous addon files. Run /reload, then /fgm. A safe first check is the server info command in the addon.

• Click a statistic to open its populated collection.
• 16 essential shortcuts: 12 explicit GM commands plus weapon/profession previews, self-only class learning and settings.
• Every dashboard GM command asks for confirmation and uses the existing validated, rate-limited executor. No speculative server-side toggle state is shown.
• Player-target/build banner, formatted counts, hover feedback and a responsive vertically scrolling layout.
• No irrelevant pagination, search/filter controls or empty inspector on the dashboard. Real collection pages keep their pagination.
New minimap launcher
• Original circular gold/teal eye-and-key medallion designed for small-size readability.
• Larger 38px click area, hover and pressed feedback, without the old overlapping tracking border.
• Left-click toggle, right-click settings, saved drag position and hide option are preserved.
• Drag coordinates now use the minimap's effective scale.
Documentation and verification
• Updated English README and changelog; new English/French/Spanish dashboard labels.
• 53 Lua TOC modules parse in Lua 5.1 mode; static dataset/locale, version and transparent-TGA checks pass.
• 2,229 mocked-runtime assertions pass, including tile navigation, collection layout restoration, resizing, shortcut confirmations and minimap interaction.
• Actual WoW rendering and live command outcomes still require in-game checks; catalog counts are not live realm statistics.
Install / update
Download ForeverGM-0.11.0.zip below. Extract the ForeverGM folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, replacing the previous addon files, then enable the addon and run /reload followed by /fgm.

Target: WoWForever Classic beta 1.60.1.70338 / Interface 16001, with the matching ForeverCore fork. Server permissions remain authoritative.

English README · Changelog · Asset design brief

ForeverGM 0.10.1
First public release of the icon-driven WoWForever GM toolkit, including the complete 0.10.0 collection and responsive-interface update.
Highlights
• Browse 154 skills, 32,337 spells, 24,288 items, 198 equipment sets and 48,793 quests, plus NPCs, GameObjects, mounts, languages, teleports and achievements.
• Class/category filters, illustrated cards, favorites, name/ID search and full-result pagination.
• Resizable responsive window, saved geometry, scale settings and a draggable minimap launcher.
• Preview and grant compatible skills, weapon skills or professions, with separate learning/maximizing choices and target-change cancellation.
• 680 matching-core command records, 12 GM shortcuts, confirmations and a rate-limited cancellable queue.
• English, French and Spanish in-game localization.
Fixed in 0.10.1
• Quest navigation, cards and detail views now use client-verified icon FileDataID 134939 instead of an unavailable legacy texture path.
• Added a detailed English README, portable validation and GitHub Actions checks.
• Added clean deterministic archive packaging and SHA-256 checksums.
Installation
Download ForeverGM-0.10.1.zip below (the installable asset, not the automatic source archive). Extract its ForeverGM folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/, enable the addon and enter /fgm or /reload.
Target and verification
Built for WoWForever Classic beta 1.60.1.70338 / Interface 16001 and the matching ForeverCore fork. Server RBAC remains authoritative. Other clients/cores are not guaranteed compatible.

Static integrity checks and Lua 5.1 parsing passed; 1,693 mocked-runtime assertions passed. These do not claim real-client visual QA or live server success for every command.
