NeatPlatesUnreleased
• Fixed Forever Lua errors when class-colouring spell targets or interrupt attribution by using an addon-owned colour formatter. Fixed party-aggro name colouring returning a table instead of numeric RGBA values.
• Fixed duration text remaining blank for secret cast timestamps on Forever/Retail by formatting Blizzard duration objects directly, and cleared timer references on cast/plate cleanup.
• Restored cast-bar spell targets and duration styles on Forever when the client supplies readable values, retaining native timer handling for secret cast times on modern clients.
• Centered Forever's adjustable click area on the theme's health bar instead of the underlying Blizzard frame, preserving saved dimensions and stable bounds during hover enlargement. Name-only plates retain their previous placement.
• Fixed Forever nameplate clicking and mouseover areas using the client's per-plate hit-test API instead of unavailable legacy sizing APIs. Clickable width/height, display offsets, and friendly/enemy click-through now apply to the real hitbox, independently of target/mouseover enlargement; the green preview follows those bounds.
v468-ce7.5.1
• Added a project-level MIT license with attribution for the original NeatPlates and Tidy Plates projects.
• Added an updated README covering supported WoW versions, configuration, credits, licensing, and repository information.
v468-ce7.5
• Restored the Threat Percentage widget on Retail and Forever using the modern UnitDetailedThreatSituation API.
• Added secret-safe threat percentage rendering without inspecting or transforming protected combat values in Lua.
• Kept the existing threat percentage implementation unchanged for Classic, TBC, and Mists of Pandaria clients.
v468-ce7.4
• Optimized critical nameplate update paths by avoiding redundant Blizzard frame traversal, full refreshes for alpha-only changes, repeated callback allocation, and repeated custom-color parsing.
• Added secret-safe health-based coloring for Retail and Forever using Blizzard's supported curve APIs.
• Added secret-safe low-health opacity highlighting for Retail and Forever, passing protected opacity values directly to the UI without inspecting them in Lua.
v468-ce5
• Added a dedicated Stacking Nameplates section to the main NeatPlates options panel.
• Added a localized notice explaining that actual nameplate stacking is controlled by Blizzard's Nameplate settings in MoP Classic Phase 5+.
• Added a Spacing Offset slider for Blizzard's nameplateOverlapV CVar, with deferred application after combat when needed.
• Added Display Offset X and Display Offset Y sliders to move the NeatPlates overlay relative to Blizzard's real nameplate anchor.
• Added visible live value readouts for the new stacking-related sliders.
• Added localization keys for the new stacking options, with German translations and safe fallback text for other locales.
v468-ce4
• Fixed nameplate stacking/spreading in MoP Classic Phase 5 by keeping Blizzard's nameplate UnitFrame active as the layout anchor while NeatPlates draws the visible plate.
• Updated NeatPlates to follow Blizzard's nameplate stacking behavior instead of overriding it internally.
• Replaced the NeatPlates stacking checkbox with a localized notice explaining that stacking is now controlled through Blizzard's Nameplate settings.
v468-ce3
• Added a custom NeatPlates addon icon and assigned it to the visible NeatPlates modules in the addon list.
• Fixed an instance-related nil CVar issue when restoring Blizzard nameplate sizing for default Blizzard nameplates.
• Fixed the Slim Vertical theme failing to render nameplates when a legacy WoW font object name such as GameFontWhite was passed through the font setup path.
v468 (2025-09-21)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Use default blizzard plates for "softinteract" units, as these are usually inanimate objects with special nameplates
v468-ce2
• Added a new profile option: Ignore Blizzard Alpha.…

addons.description:
A complete replacement for WoW's default Friends frame. Groups, nicknames, raid management, a proper WHO list, Quick Join, and a lot more - all in one addon that works on Retail and Classic.
FeaturesFriend Management
• Custom Groups - Create as many groups as you want, give them names and colors, and drag friends between them. Reorder groups by dragging their headers.
• Favorites and In-Game - A pinned Favorites group and a dynamic "In-Game" group that automatically collects friends playing the same game.
• Nicknames - Assign a personal nickname to any friend, independent of their note. Nicknames show up everywhere: the list, tooltips, context menus.
• Multi-Select - Hold Shift to select multiple friends at once for bulk group assignment.
• Global Sync - Your group assignments carry over between characters and connected realms automatically.
Sorting and Filtering
• Dual Sort - Primary and secondary sort by Status, Name, Level, Zone, Game, Faction, Guild, Class, or Realm.
• Quick Filters - One-click buttons to show only Online, Offline, WoW friends, Battle.net friends, and more.
• Search - Real-time search across names, character names, notes, and nicknames.
Name and Info Formatting
BetterFriendlist gives you full control over how friends are displayed. Two independent format strings - Friend Name and Friend Info - each come with several presets and a fully custom mode using tokens:

Friend Name controls the primary line. Presets include "Name (Character)", "BattleTag (Character)", "Nickname (Character)", "Character Only", "Name Only", or "Custom". In custom mode you can combine tokens like %name%, %battletag%, %nickname%, %character%, %note%, %realm%, %level%, %zone%, %class%, %game%.

Friend Info controls the secondary line below the name. Presets include "Level, Zone", "Zone Only", "Level Only", "Class, Zone", "Level Class, Zone", "Game Name", "Disabled", or "Custom" with the same token set.

Character names can be class-colored automatically, and faction icons (Alliance/Horde) can be shown next to character names.
Streamer Mode
A privacy toggle that replaces Real IDs with BattleTags (or nicknames, or notes) everywhere in the addon - the friend list, tooltips, and context menus. Useful for streaming or recording without leaking personal information.
Raid Frame
A full 40-man raid roster built into BetterFriendlist. Members are shown in their raid groups with class colors, class icons and role icons.
• Drag and Drop - Move members between groups by dragging them.
• Configurable Shortcuts - Assign modifier+click combinations to common actions: Main Tank, Main Assist, Promote to Assistant, or Promote to Leader. Each shortcut can be individually enabled or disabled.
• Ready Check Display - Visual ready check status on each member button.
Quick Join
Browse groups that your friends are currently forming or queued for, and request to join with a single click. Shows which friends are in each group and what roles the group still needs. Available on Retail.
WHO Frame
A rebuilt WHO list with a cleaner layout and more functionality than the default.
• Search Builder - A flyout panel with dedicated fields for Name, Guild, Zone, Race, and Class instead of remembering Blizzard's cryptic /who syntax. Fill in what you want and hit Search.
• Responsive Columns - Name, Level, Class, and a variable column (Zone, Guild, or Race) that adapts to the frame width. Click any column header to sort by it.
• Ctrl+Click Filtering - Ctrl+Click a value in the Zone, Guild, or Race column to instantly search for that value.
• Double-Click Actions - Configurable to either Whisper or Invite the selected player.
• Class-Colored Names - Player names and class columns use class colors. Levels are colored by quest difficulty.
Customization
• ElvUI Skin - Native ElvUI skinning when ElvUI is detected.…

addons.description:
Parchment Reader is an in-game library for World of Warcraft. Save stories,
notes, roleplay material, and other long-form text, then read it in a focused,
resizable window.
Features
• Create, edit, and organize saved books and notes.
• Rename books while keeping their bookmarks and reading positions.
• Recover deleted saved books and notes for 30 days through a quiet Trash window
in Settings > General > Maintenance.
• Switch between Library, Favorites, and the 20 most recently opened books.
• Search titles and collections by default, or enable the compact Aa scope
to find a complete phrase in book content within the active collection.
• Open a content result with Enter or a click, highlight the matching phrase,
move between occurrences, and return without replacing saved reading progress.
• Read continuously with automatic position saving.
• Group books into collections.
• Add, rename, navigate, delete, and restore bookmarks, ordered by reading position.
• Reopen the bookmark list at the selected bookmark. Repeated + Here clicks
at the same exact point select the existing bookmark and keep its name.
• Keep older duplicate bookmarks independently usable, including rename and Undo.
• Read clearer bookmark titles and excerpts with separate progress percentages,
wrapped hover excerpts with continuation ellipses, and a theme-colored rename pencil.
• Capture text quickly without leaving the game through Quick Note.
• Resume the last saved Quick Note in its current collection, or start a new
note without losing an unsaved draft.
• Use Compact Mode or minimize the reader to a movable floating icon.
• Assign a shortcut that switches a visible Reader into or out of Compact Mode.
• Keep the Reader or minimized launcher in its saved screen position between
sessions, and pin the Reader to prevent accidental movement or resizing.
• Enable keyboard navigation only when the book page has focus, leaving
gameplay keys available to WoW at other times.
• Configure reader size, font, transparency, shortcuts, and minimap access, with
an optional transparent background override while in combat.
• Choose Off, Always, Smart, or Custom reader transparency. Custom reveals a
live 0–100% slider and a Transparent until hovered checkbox. Text keeps its
opacity; at high transparency in a light theme, use Azeroth Glass or enable
Transparent until hovered to keep reading comfortable.
• Choose Azeroth Glass, Light Parchment, or Warm Parchment, and assign the
sun/moon theme switch independently. Themes update open windows immediately.
• Choose Hallow's End appearance across the reader, editor, Quick
Note, and settings. A pumpkin control returns to the previous ordinary theme;
Holiday appearance in Settings controls availability.
• Discover seasonal appearance through a localized invitation, with improved
collection scrollbar dragging and clearer list-row separators.
• Find settings in Reading, Appearance, Controls, and General, with a live font
sample and theme previews.
• Choose the interface language independently of the WoW client: English,
German, French, Russian, Spanish, or Brazilian Portuguese.

addons.description:
This is a UI modification primarily designed around the key layout of the Logitech G13, with the goal of keeping as close to the feel and look of the vanilla UI as possible while implementing a few changes to suit more modern sensibilities.

It has support for both Classic Era and Forever, with the same general concepts but unique art for each. Forever also has support for the Razer Tartarus V2 Pro.

There are a variety of options, such as selecting the end cap artwork and moving things such as the Unitframes or the Map into more preferable places.

This AddOn is largely designed around edit mode, and as such it uses standard frames as much as possible. When the edit mode functionality isn't available, manual control of the frames has been taken instead.

The visual bar art has all been created by modifying the original assets. Details down to the levelup pips have been preserved and kept correct. The Keyring is automatically enabled regardless of level to keep the visual design consistent, and there's an option to enable the talent button at all times.

addons.description:
PlateColor is a lightweight World of Warcraft nameplate addon built for players who want clean visuals and fast combat awareness without complex configuration. Its design focuses on simplicity, low overhead, and practical improvements that make nameplates easier to read in real combat.

It provides targeted customization for the most important nameplate elements, including name text, health bars, cast bars, auras, threat indicators, execute lines, target and focus markers, and personal resource display. Rather than trying to cover everything, PlateColor keeps its scope narrow and useful.

The addon is designed for players who prefer a minimal setup that works well out of the box. It avoids unnecessary menus and complicated layers of options, while still delivering the information that matters most in combat.
🌟 Features
• Minimalist, lightweight design – Optimized for performance.
• Clean and readable – Nameplate enhancements designed for clarity.
• Core Support – Health bars, cast bars, auras, threat, and markers.
• Personal Resource Display – Better visibility for your own resource bar.
• Simple Setup – No complex configuration or menu bloat.
🛠️ About the Author
Built by a long-time Mythic+ player. Features are added based on practical need and real gameplay requirements.

PlateColor 是一款面向魔兽世界姓名板的轻量级插件，适合希望获得更清晰战斗信息、但不想面对复杂设置的玩家。它的设计重点是 极简、低负担和实用增强，让姓名板在战斗中更易读、更直观。

插件提供了对姓名板核心元素的针对性调整，包括姓名、血条、施法条、光环、仇恨提示、斩杀线、目标与焦点标记，以及个人资源条。PlateColor 不追求大而全，而是专注于战斗中真正需要的信息展示。

这是一款面向喜欢干净界面、开箱即用体验的插件。它刻意避免冗余菜单和复杂配置层级，同时保留对战斗识别最有价值的内容。
💎 特性
• 极简轻量化设计 – 极致的代码优化，确保战斗流畅。
• 清晰直观增强 – 强化姓名板视觉层级，信息获取更迅速。
• 核心功能支持 – 完善支持血条、施法条、光环、仇恨和标记调整。
• 个人资源条显示 – 针对性优化个人资源条展示。
• 配置简单 – 没有复杂的设置负担，上手即用。
👤 关于作者
由一位 资深大秘境玩家 制作。功能会根据实际需求和玩法需要，持续添加对应功能。

命令
| 命令 | 功能 |
|------|------|
| /pc 或 /platecolor | 打开设置界面 |

快速安装
1. 下载最新版本 Releases
2. 解压到 World of Warcraft\retail\Interface\AddOns\
3. 确保文件夹名为 PlateColor
4. 启动游戏，在角色选择界面确认插件已加载

依赖
• 本插件不依赖其他插件，独立运行
• 如安装了 LibSharedMedia-3.0，可自动使用其注册的状态栏材质

addons.changelog:
ChangelogA note on WoW 12.1 addon development
Retail 12.1 protects more combat, aura, cooldown, and unit data as secret values. Addons can often display those values only by handing them directly to Blizzard-owned widgets instead of reading or formatting them, which is why one visual layer may keep working while related text or logic disappears; safe fixes increasingly require narrow ownership boundaries between Blizzard and other addons.

Release note rule: each version entry must include only what changed since the previous release (delta-only).
Do not repeat older items from prior versions in newer entries.
Writing workflow: Tools/CHANGELOG_GUIDE.md. Lead with player benefits, then explain substantial development work and remaining limits.
5.35.1-JuNNeZ (2026-10-31) - Blizzard Raid Bar Stays HiddenHighlights
• Blizzard's raid bar stays hidden when you turn it off. With Show Blizzard Raid Bar off at /az -> Group Frames, the bar could come back on every map change while your group was listed in the Premade Group Finder, until you switched the option on and off again. It now stays hidden, and the option is the only thing that decides. Thanks to Luciful for the report.
Access and known limits
• If the game shows the bar during combat, it stays visible until combat ends, because it cannot be hidden safely before then.
• Checked offline only so far, not yet confirmed in game.
5.35.0-JuNNeZ (2026-10-31) - Raid Panel, Rogue and ShamanHighlights
• A raid and party panel of AzeriteUI's own. It shows member and role counts, raid group filters for AzeriteUI's large raid frames, target and ground markers, ready check, role check, a 10-second countdown, all assist, party/raid conversion, difficulty and ping permission menus, and leave buttons. It is on by default for grouped players, sits folded out at the left edge and moves with /lock. Settings are at /az -> Group Frames -> Raid / Party panel; /azraidtools previews it. Actions you have no rights for are disabled. Thanks to Luciful for the request.
• Target markers lite: a small separate marker bar. Off by default, and it works with the full panel switched off. Choose which markers it shows and in what order, as a row, a column or two rows. Left-click sets a marker, Shift-click sets a ground marker and the clear button removes all target markers, or all ground markers with Shift. Settings are at /az -> Group Frames -> Target markers lite; /azmarkerlite previews it once enabled.
• Rogue theme (WIP): Venom & Steel. Choose it at /az -> Themes or with /azrogue on. Health endcaps are Twin Guard, Serrated, Venom Vial or None, with a separate Venom Vial or None choice for the cast bar.
• Shaman theme (WIP). Choose it at /az -> Themes or with /azshaman on. Health endcaps are Maelstrom, Tides, Lava Totem or None, with a separate Ancestral Totem or None choice for the cast bar.
• Something extra.
Development
• The raid panel keeps Blizzard's panel out of it. Markers use the game's own secure button actions, with no custom secure code and no changes to Blizzard's raid panel. Changes made in combat wait until it ends, and group administration is never replayed automatically. New steel and gold panel artwork was painted to match the toolbar, and all ten languages are translated.
• Theme work focused on fit. Both themes went through repeated in-game review and repainting of their casings, buttons and crystal holders, and the shared art checks now also verify source images and how crystal casings seat. Both also work with Lite+ crystal and orb mixes.
• Crystal and orb casings stay in front. Live testing showed the game lowering these casings during resource updates, so they now return to the correct layer afterwards, waiting for combat to end if needed.
Access and known limits…
addons.description:
This is an unofficial fan-edited version of AzeriteUI 5 by GoldpawsStuff.

AzeriteUI is a complete custom World of Warcraft user interface replacement for Retail (WoW 12.1 — Midnight) and WoW Forever beta (1.60.1). This JuNNeZ Edition includes additional bug fixes, compatibility patches, and quality-of-life improvements not found in the original release.

> Note: This is a personal project maintained independently. For official support, use the original AzeriteUI or visit the Discord where JuNNeZ has a channel for this addon.

Table of Contents

• Objectives Tracker

5.34.1-JuNNeZ (2026-10-25) - More Consistent Tooltip BordersHighlights
• More addon tooltips use the AzeriteUI border, including world-map icon tooltips that use Blizzard's shared tooltip styling. Previously, only a fixed list of known tooltips received the skin. Thanks to Luciful for the report.
Development
• Broader coverage with exceptions for sensitive frames. Compared other UIs' approaches before extending the existing styling hook. Embedded tooltips, forbidden frames and dropdown menus remain excluded. Offline tests cover addon tooltips appearing later, theme changes and restoring their original border when AzeriteUI tooltip styling is switched off.
Access and known limits
• Checked offline only; in-game rendering and taint checks on Retail and Forever are still needed. Addons that draw their own tooltips without Blizzard's shared styling may still need separate support. MapNotes coverage has not yet been confirmed in game.
5.34.0-JuNNeZ (2026-10-24) - Hide the Activity ButtonHighlights
• WoW Forever, China realms: hide the Activity button on the minimap. The clock button on the left of the minimap (活动) opens Blizzard's event web page. Tick /az -> Minimap -> Hide Activity Button to remove it; untick it to bring it back where it was. It is off by default and only listed on the China client. Thanks to Dcryfm for the request and the /fstack.
Development
• Built from Blizzard's own code and other UIs. Forever's minimap code shows the button only while there is an event link, which in practice means the China realms. ElvUI, QUI, EKMinimap, RealUI and EllesmereUI were checked first; AzeriteUI hides it the way ElvUI does, by moving it into a hidden frame, so Blizzard showing it again for a new event does not bring it back. A new offline test covers hiding, restoring, other regions and combat.
Access and known limits
• China realms on WoW Forever only. The same hiding was confirmed in game on a China client with a one-line test command; the switch itself has not yet been tried there.
5.33.0-JuNNeZ (2026-10-24) - Hide the Day and Night IndicatorHighlights
• WoW Forever: hide the day and night icon on the minimap. Until now, turning off /az -> Minimap -> Day and Night Indicator only swapped AzeriteUI's icon for Blizzard's. The new /az -> Minimap -> Hide Day and Night Indicator removes both, so the minimap ring stays clear. It is off by default, and the Day and Night Indicator switch is greyed out while the icon is hidden.
Development
• Hidden without breaking Blizzard's icon. Blizzard's own indicator is made invisible rather than removed, so Edit Mode and the day/night change keep working underneath, and switching the option off brings back whichever icon you had chosen. The offline test for the indicator now covers hiding, including when the game cannot say whether it is day or night.
Access and known limits
• Forever only, as Retail has no day and night cycle. Checked offline only; not yet confirmed in game.
• The switch is on the Minimap options page only, not in the frame settings that open when you click the minimap in /lock.

5.32.1-JuNNeZ (2026-10-24) - Queue Eye Without Blocked ActionsHighlights

Your oath now follows you, and is checked.
• Your pledge is saved in a character macro called HonorBound Save, so it follows your character to other computers. Don't edit or delete it. If it's deleted, HonorBound recreates it from this computer's copy.
• Verification: play HonorBound didn't see (addon off, another computer without it, a crash) is measured from /played at login. Up to 2 hours, or 2% of your play since the pledge if that's more, is allowed; beyond that your oath breaks. /honor shows where you stand.
• Character macros full? A dialog asks you to free one (Open macros / Retry). Not now, once confirmed, stops saving to a macro on that character; turn it back on in Options > AddOns > HonorBound or with /honor save.

addons.description:
WoW Forever has no RP-PvP realms. HonorBound is how we build one anyway.

Swear the oath on a character and you stay flagged for PvP, for good. Every
other sworn player sees a crest on your portrait, your nameplate and your
name in chat, so you always know who has given their word, and who is fair
game.
What it does
• Keeps you flagged. Once sworn, you can't turn PvP off from your portrait.
If something unflags you, like leaving a dungeon, your next action bar
key or click flags you again. Keep playing and you won't notice.
• Gives you 5 minutes. If you stay unflagged for 5 minutes, your oath
breaks and your crest is gone. The clock waits while you're inside a
dungeon or away from the keyboard.
• Shows the crest. Sworn players wear a blue (Alliance) or red (Horde)
crest in place of the usual PvP icon (on portraits and party frames), on
nameplates, and in chat. Hover it
to see the level they swore at.
• Can't be faked. On portraits and nameplates, a crest only shows while
the game says that player really is flagged. Inside dungeons and raids,
where nobody can be flagged, sworn players keep their crest, and party
members waiting outside still see it.

You only see crests on other players who also use HonorBound, so share it
with your guild and friends.
addons.name: HonorBound

addons.description:
A small addon that copies the Gossip / Quest / Book Item text into the chat frame and displays it as though an NPC were speaking in /say.

Much of the time, players skip over quest text, dialog, or book items and not even read them. Gossip Text altogether is disabled by default. Rather than forcing it to be enabled for everyone, this addon will grab the text while still printing the text into chat. Other addons for enabling gossip text frame like NPC RP Gossip Text Re-enabler are there for you - and GossipChatter is fully compatible with NPCRPGossip.

There aren't really any options that come with this yet as it's a fairly simple function. So far this covers: Gossip dialogs, Quests / Quest Turnins / Quest Progress, and Book items found across the world.

Gossip Chatter now also supports Text to Speech

For additional voice chat options you can visit the Blizzard Support Page

New options have been added for text to speech, including choosing voice options per target gender, adjusting the rate and volume for each voice, and an auto-play speech feature complete with a toggleable button and option to interrupt queued messages.

A link to my discord for addon projects and other things can be found here.

addons.description:
An addon that aims to bring in "speakable" ingame languages and dialects in a lightweight and accessible way.

This addon intentionally only obfuscates messages on the user side. As an example, if a player said "[Orcish] Hello friend", the addon skins it over and the user sees it as "[Orcish] Mokra zugzug" (or some other combination of languages). Non-addon users would not see this obfuscation, and instead see the original message, "[Orcish] Hello friend". This is done for a few reasons:
1. Obfuscating the messages forces users to install the addon. Not only does this prevent reporting harmful messages, but starting off an addon as an exclusive club will be very difficult to get moving and can create dangerous cliques.
2. Sending translations to players requires addon data. It'd still be miniscule and mostly insignificant, but every bit counts especially in an environment that's high population where user bandwidth may be throttled. This addon intentionally doesn't utilize any addon bandwidth at all. Any information used from TRP3 is solely from its API or via Saved Variables. This addon is made simple to intentionally work with other addons like CrossRP and with ingame items like Elixir of Tongues without sending addon data to translate.
3. This isn't a true translator. While it has a "dictionary", this simply runs words of a certain letter count through a parser. The sole purpose is to match a 3 letter word to another 3 letter word and make sure that the word stays the same every time it's used. This is what is known as the "hash" for this addon, and ensures something like "lol" will always translate to Orcish "kek" instead of randomly choosing "lok", "mok", or any other 3 letter example.
4. This addon doesn't translate true ingame languages. If somebody is speaking genuine Orcish, you as an Alliance player likely won't be able to see this translation. Likewise, this will not translate your own true Shalassian to non-Nightborne. Unfortunately this is just simply a limitation and runs into that area of sending translations via addon messages. If you want to avoid this issue, request that players instead use items like the Elixir of Tongues, join group with the player (grouped messages translate), OOC speak in Common (or other languages) while IC speaking in another language, or maybe ask Blizzard to lift these restrictions altogether. Likewise, it's outside of the addon capability to translate ingame languages you don't know, such as an NPC speaking Titan.

Some of the addon slash commands can be accessed via /languages, /language, or /lang. Sub-commands include prefix to toggle a langauge prefix on/off, open to display the options, and minimap to show/hide the minimap button.

Other slash commands include the ability to set your currently-spoken language directly in the slash command, such as /lang darnassian or /darnassian.

There are a few other features of this addon:
• Converting messages into glyph textures per character
• Total RP 3 Profile Compatibility
• Integration into speech bubbles (while not in instanced content)
• Optional automatic shapeshift language (currently only for Shadowform / Metamorphosis with Shath'yar / Demonic)
• Dialect converter (ie "dwarven accent")
• Dictionary (ie "Giant's Heart" = "Grommash")

Some things which are still planned:
• Potentially adjust for "true languages" (ie Horde characters speaking Orcish where the language tag isn't actually detected)
• Text color selection option (This is currently limited by buggy performance issues, so is currently not implemented)
• Finishing language glyphs for languages without them

addons.description:
Your macro is broken. You will find out mid-pull.
No syntax check. No spell verification. No history. Blizzard's macro frame is a text box, and it has been for twenty years.

MacroForge is the editor that should have shipped with the game. It checks every line as you type, tells you what your macro would do right now, keeps every version you ever saved, and swaps whole macro sets when you change spec — without emptying your action bars.

It catches the mistake before the boss does
• Live analysis — every command, condition and spell checked against your own spellbook
• "Did you mean…?" — /csatsequence becomes /castsequence, a misspelt spell gets the closest match
• Plain-language explanation of every line, right next to the code
• One-click fixes — click an issue to jump to its line, click Fix to correct a mistyped command
• Live test — one click and the panel shows which clause fires right now, on which target, and follows as you change target, hover a unit or hold Shift
• Live 255-character counter, with the shortener one click away
One window, built for speed
Everything opens inside it: templates, history, sharing and duplicates are pages of the window (Esc goes back), and the spell list, commands, condition builder and icon picker slide in next to the code. Search by name or content. Filter to what is broken, what sits on a bar, what nobody uses. Drag a macro straight onto your action bars. Right-click for duplicate, share, move between Character and Account, or its full history.

Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+Z undo · Ctrl+F search · ↑ ↓ walk the list · Del delete

Your macros follow your spec
Save your character macros as a set — Raid, M+, PvP, whatever you run. Bind it to a spec. Change spec, and the right set is in place before the pull. Macros that exist in both sets keep their action bar slots, and anything you changed is saved into the set before it swaps.
Nothing is ever lost
• Every version of every macro is kept — including the edits you make in Blizzard's own frame
• Deleted a macro? It is in the Trash, body intact, one click from coming back
• Automatic backup before every set swap or restore
• Unsaved changes are marked, and MacroForge asks before dropping them
Also in the box
190 templates — stances, traps, totems, seals, curses, druid forms, focus interrupts, mouseover heals: 11 for every class and 16 to 21 per class on WoW Forever, every spell checked in the client. Browse any class, not only yours. Spell names are resolved from spell IDs, so they are always in the client's language.

Audit — one panel listing every macro that needs attention, worst first.

Share — export a macro as a short code, send it to another MacroForge user in game, or paste any macro copied from a guide: it is named for you.

Condition builder — build [@mouseover,harm,nodead] from menus instead of memorising it.

Your language — the whole addon, analysis and explanations included, follows your client's language:

English · Français · Deutsch · Español · Español (México) · Italiano · Português (Brasil) · Русский · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

Blizzard's /macro window gets a MacroForge button: the macro you selected there opens here.

2.1.0

Overlord Forever 2.1.0

Weekly reset: each region now runs its own week. The campaign starts and resets at your region's weekly reset (Americas on Tuesday, Europe on Wednesday, Korea and Taiwan on Thursday morning). 2.0.8 keeps the beta's Tuesday schedule: update before the first reset.

Roleplay PvP: this new ruleset now runs its own campaign (map, ranking, channel), apart from Roleplay and PvP. On that ruleset, update required: 2.0.8 still counts it with Roleplay.

Launch: Overlord Rank starts again from zero for the game's launch (from the weekly reset of Tuesday 3 November). Ranks earned on the beta do not carry over.

Translations: place names now match the game's own names in French, Spanish, Portuguese and Chinese; Anad'Ora Moonwell is translated in every language; capture messages, tooltips and the tutorial reworded in all languages.

Plays alongside 2.0.8: maps and captures cross, but the ranking only catches up between clients on 2.1.0. In Korea and Taiwan, update before you play: updating after the launch starts your week again.

2.0.8

Overlord Forever 2.0.8

Ready for launch: 2.0.8 is the minimum version from launch. Older versions no longer exchange maps or captures with it: update required.

Fronts: a capture made with another version of a front (other points) is no longer shown or applied: no more impossible siege timers coming from another version.

Network: relayed messages travel in larger pieces, so the relay sends fewer messages.

Chat channels: the Overlord channel waits for your own channels at login and normally takes the number right after them. It no longer takes General's or Trade's number, so your channel numbers and colours stay as you set them.

Overlord panel: once you close it, it stays closed at your next login, even on a new day.

2.0.7

Overlord Forever 2.0.7

Smoother play: a full pass over the addon to reduce stutters and CPU spikes, mostly in the interface. Overlord also creates far less throwaway data, so it causes far fewer short pauses.

World map: closing and reopening the map on the same front no longer rebuilds every circle and path; zooming and maximising do much less work.

Ranking and PvP Groups: both windows are prepared quietly about half a minute after a loading screen, so the first click opens them faster. Scrolling the ranking only redraws the rows that change.

Overlord panel: the nearby-enemies counter and contested outposts no longer trigger heavy work every few seconds.

Floating next objective (option): the small window now also shows the capture timer and its bar while a point is being captured.

Instances: the action bar shortcut is no longer touched inside dungeons and battlegrounds, like the rest of Overlord.

Plays alongside 2.0.6: nothing changes in what players exchange.

2.0.6

Overlord Forever 2.0.6

Lighter on your computer: the minimap circles now follow the pace you move at instead of being recalculated at every frame. They glide just as before, with far less work while walking or riding. With a rotating minimap they still follow every frame.

Rank badges on nameplates: when news about a player's rank arrives, only that player's badge is redrawn, instead of every nameplate in sight once a second.

Overlord panel: the list of the front's points is prepared once, instead of several times a second.

/ov perf: the measure also shows its three heaviest moments and what ran in them.

Plays alongside 2.0.5: nothing changes in what players exchange.

2.0.5

Overlord Forever 2.0.5

Top ranks seen by everyone: from rank 11 (Dragon Lord, Warmaster, Crown Prince, Sovereign, Overlord), other players now see your rank badge next to your name, in the ranking and on nameplates, in your faction and in the other one. Each client checks a rank for itself before showing it, so a badge can take a few weeks of play to appear, and a rank once shown is kept.

Update required: older versions neither announce nor show these badges.

Captures on the world map: a point being taken keeps its defender's colour (grey for a neutral point) under stripes in the attacker's colour, with its orange edge.

New outpost in Feralas: Anad'Ora Moonwell, near the entrance of Dire Maul, a guild outpost open all the time, like Lesi's Bear Cave in Darkshore. Players on 2.0.4 or older do not see it.

Mines on the compact map: a bigger mine icon, sized like the capture points' icons, with the reserve written larger in an arc just above it.

Smoother maps: map icons and faction emblems keep their place and size while the world map is zoomed or scrolled, also with world map addons that scroll freely, and the minimap circles follow the minimap's zoom right away.

Minimap button tooltip: the front you are on, its points held by the Alliance, the Horde or nobody, and your rank with your Glory.

PvP Groups: the faction emblem breathes while the search connects and listens for groups.

addons.description:
============
Implements an alternative to C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage() to securely send messages in chat channels in response to a hardware event such as a mouse click or a keypress.

How it works

Use MessageQueue.SendChatMessage() in your add-ons and macros to send chat messages instead of C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage(). MessageQueue will then wait for a hardware event to send the message. A callback that will be executed after the message has been sent can also be provided so you can write your code in an asynchronous way.

Any of the following hardware inputs allows the queue to run: mouse click, mouse wheel, keyboard, gamepad stick or button. Unlike keyboard inputs, mouse and gamepad inputs are consumed by an invisible frame that shows up at the topmost level so any click on an action may fail if MessageQueue needs to send a message at the same time.

Use with AutoHotKey

MessageQueue can be used in conjunction with AutoHotkey and the provided PixelTrigger.v*.ahk script to automatically send hardware events to the World of Warcraft window when needed.
• For AutoHotKey v1.1, use PixelTrigger.v1.ahk.
• For AutoHotKey v2.0, use PixelTrigger.v2.ahk.

The script monitors the color of the top left pixel of the WoW window and sends a keypress on the PAUSE key every time the pixel turns gray (#333333). The WoW window doesn't need to be active but the top left corner should remain visible on the screen and not be covered by another window for the script to work.

The AutoHotKey script only works on Windows. If you're running MessageQueue on Mac, you'll need to trigger your hardware event manually.

If you wish to use another hardware event than the PAUSE key, make a copy of the PixelTrigger.v*.ahk script and edit it accordingly (instructions are provided within the script comments). Make sure to keep your copy of the script out of the add-on folder since it could be automatically deleted if you use an add-on manager.

Please be aware that the use of AutoHotkey is not against Blizzard's ToS and you won't get banned for just using it along with WoW. It's commonly used by players with disabilities. Only obvious abuse such as spamming or automating complex actions can get you banned. Do not use any other script than the provided PixelTrigger.v*.ahk unless you know what you're doing. Anyway, the use of AutoHotKey and the provided script is not mandatory for MessageQueue to work, it just adds convenience.

API documentation

MessageQueue.SendChatMessage
MessageQueue.SendChatMessage("msg" [,"chatType" [,languageID [,"target" [, "callback"]]]])

Add a message to the queue if the target requires a hardware event (chatType is either "SAY", "YELL" or "CHANNEL"). For any other chatType, the message is sent instantly.

Arguments are the same as the regular C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage function.

The optional callback function will be executed when the message has been sent. The callback should not contain any other code requiring a hardware event.
MessageQueue.Enqueue
MessageQueue.Enqueue(func)

Enqueue a function that requires a hardware event to run. The function may not perform more than one action requiring a hardware event.

Shares the same queue as MessageQueue.SendChatMessage().
MessageQueue.GetNumPendingMessages
messageCount = MessageQueue.GetNumPendingMessages()

Returns the number of messages awaiting in the queue.
MessageQueue.Run
MessageQueue.Run()

Runs the first message awaiting in queue. Should only be called in response to a hardware event. If for some reason the message fails, it won't be possible to attempt it again.
MessageQueue.Clear
MessageQueue.Clear()

Clears the entire queue.

Integration guide

The integration of MessageQueue in your add-on is pretty straightforward.

First, add MessageQueue as a required dependency for your add-on by adding the following in the .toc file:
## RequiredDeps: MessageQueue

Then, just replace C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage() calls by MessageQueue.SendChatMessage().…

addons.description:
============

Load and save songs in game for the Musician add-on.

The song list is accessible from Musician main menu on the minimap or by clicking the list button in the main import window.

To save the current song to the list, press the Save button in the main import window or in the song editor.

Highlight a song to show the action buttons (play, rename, share, delete).

Type /mus help to get the command list.

Special thanks to Mystic Zaru, Eldorias and Oliira-Moonguard for the demo songs!

Command list

Open song list
/mus list

/mus songs
Save the current song
/mus save []

If omitted, the song name shown in the import field will be used.
Load a song
/mus load (|)
Load and play a song
/mus play (|)
Load and preview a song
/mus preview (|)
Filter song name
/mus find

/mus search

/mus filter
Delete song
/mus delete [(|)]

/mus del [(|)]

/mus remove [(|)]

If no song name or number is specified, the currently loaded song will be deleted.
Rename song
/mus rename [ []]

/mus ren [ []]

/mus mv [ []]

If no parameter is specified, the currently loaded song will be renamed.
Restore demo songs
/mus demosongs

addons.changelog:
• Edit Layout: Revert puts one element back where it was when you opened Edit Layout, and Default place puts a game element back where the game puts it, as Edit Mode does.
• Edit Layout: a Layout list in the bar to switch Edit Mode layouts and to make, copy, rename, delete, import and share them. A change shows after a /reload.
• Fixed: your other characters are asked again whether to use MelloUI's Edit Mode layout. Since 2.0.0 only Oldschool asked, so with the Modern or Default skin the others kept the game's own layout under MelloUI's windows.
• Fixed: when the game turns MelloUI's Edit Mode layout down, the installer says so in the chat and over the Keep countdown instead of finishing quietly.
• The game's Edit Mode tells you when it still shows your layout from before a MelloUI change: close it without saving to load the change. /mello layout apply says when a /reload is needed.
• New: /mello layout check, a report of your Edit Mode layout to copy and send when it does not look right.
• Fixed: MelloUI's Edit Mode layout now goes in on every screen and UI scale, from the installer and from every profile load. Where it can't fit exactly, it is fitted as close as the screen allows and the installer says which parts overlap; it never leaves the game's own layout.
• Fixed: loading a profile on the screen it was made for now offers MelloUI's Edit Mode layout when it is not the active one, so the action bars, the experience bar, the bags and the micro menu go where the profile places them.
• Fixed: a change in Edit Layout while the game's Modern or Classic preset is active uses MelloUI's copy of it made before, instead of making another copy ('Modern (MelloUI) 2', '3' ...) each time.
• Edit Layout: switching, making or deleting an Edit Mode layout from the Layout list, or saving into a copy of the game's preset, now takes effect with the list's Reload now button (the game switches layouts only with a reload).
• Edit Layout: drop one of the game's elements snapped against another and it attaches to it, as in Edit Mode: it follows the other one after a /reload. Its box says what it is attached to, with Detach.
• Edit Layout: the game's damage meter's Frame Width and Height show at once while you change them.
• Edit Layout: the player frame's box takes in the damage meter's tab on its side, so it moves and snaps with the tab; under Oldschool the party frames' box reaches over their tabs too.
• Default skin: the player frame wears the Forever client's own high-resolution pictures (the frame, its class-resource and vehicle frames, the rest glow and the level circle), so it stays sharp when scaled up.
• Loading a profile made on a screen of another size or shape offers Fit to this screen, so a shared layout lands right on your screen. A saved profile remembers the screen it was saved on.
• A Supporters page in the settings, under Profiles, lists the people who help keep MelloUI going. Thank you, all of you!
• The map zoomed out to the whole world shows the capitals with a gold seal and their name, the boat and zeppelin docks, the dungeon and raid entrances and your quests. Towns show as small seals once you zoom into a continent.
• Every boat and zeppelin connection is drawn on the map as a soft gold trail from dock to dock.
• Map pins of one kind that touch become one with a count; click it to zoom in. The map's layers menu can hide Cities and towns.
• Dungeon maps: inside a dungeon or raid the map opens on its own map, with Dungeon Info's bosses and loot beside it. The classic dungeons and raids show Blizzard's own drawn maps; Forever's own dungeons (City of Dalaran, Ruins of Lordaeron, Hall of Thanes, Excavation Site) the fan-made maps of Santiago Reyes, used with his kind permission. From outside, click a dungeon's door on the map or its row in Dungeon Info to see its map. Turn it off on the Map page (Dungeon Maps).…
addons.description:
Download: latest release · on CurseForge · MelloUI Oldschool (the painted skin) · voice pack, optional: part 1 + part 2 · changelog

Discord: discord.gg/gdpQ6ep7bW · help, bug reports and every new release

Support: patreon.com/Mello_UI · MelloUI stays free; supporters get a thank-you role on the Discord

Everything is a switch. On your first login the installer sets MelloUI up with you, fitted to your screen. Type /mello for the settings any time.
The look
• Three skins: Default (the game's own look), Modern (MelloUI's own) and Oldschool (painted RPG art, a separate download).
• Fonts, bar textures, colours and icons in one place, and Dark Mode for the whole UI.
• The game's windows dressed to match, and a Fader that hides parts of the UI until you need them.
Frames and bars
• Unit frames for you, your target, focus and pet, with a designer: click a part, drag it.
• Party and raid frames with indicators for heals, shields and debuffs.
• Frame effects: heals, shields, cooldowns and buffs land on the frames, and a halo shows who has aggro.
• Personal Display: your health, power and big cooldowns under your character, and a swing timer.
• Nameplates with threat, combo points, crowd control, quest marks and your debuffs; class medallions over your party; glints on herbs, veins and quest items.
• Action bars, cast bar, XP and reputation bars, and a Level Up Card with your gains and new spells at every level.
• Minimap with a Services row (the nearest repair, inn, flight master and more) and one tidy group for other addons' buttons.
• Damage meter: a race bar in fights, numbers on your frames and a fight history.
Chat
• A cleaner chat with channel tabs, chat buttons and a whisper window.
Quests and travel
• A world map of its own: one seamless map with your quests, party, route, dungeons and other addons' pins.
• Route finds the quickest way over roads and flights; an arrow and a marker in the world lead you.
• Quest Tracker and a Quest List of every quest near you.
• Dungeon Info: every dungeon's bosses, loot and drop rates.
• Guide addons: RestedXP, Follow The Arrow, APR and TomTom steps show on the map, the marker and the tracker, with one arrow at a time.
Quality of life
• Auto repair and junk selling, Restock for your supplies, quests accepted and handed in for you.
• Reminders for low supplies, mail, repairs, training and missing buffs.
• Bags sorted by kind, item quality gems, a junk Discard button and cooldown numbers.
• Combat text, gains beside your character, on-screen notices, quieter error messages, FPS and latency, and dark tooltips.
Sound
• Voice Over: quest givers read their text aloud, with subtitles.
• Custom Sounds for clicks, windows and alerts, in each skin's style.
And
• Edit Layout: move and size anything, the game's Edit Mode parts too. Your layout follows your screen's shape.
• Profiles to save, share and import your setup.
• The settings in English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese and Korean.

• The map zoomed out to the whole world shows the capitals with a gold seal and their name, the boat and zeppelin docks, the dungeon and raid entrances and your quests. Towns show as small seals once you zoom into a continent.

From outside, click a dungeon's door on the map or its row in Dungeon Info to see its map. Turn it off on the Map page (Dungeon Maps).…

• Heal and cooldown effects on the unit frames are bolder and play across the whole frame: the portrait and the bars each get their own part of the moment, and the gold border lights all round the frame, its top where the name is too.
• A heal bursts with a shockwave and stars flung off the frame, a heal over time seals onto the portrait, a shield's barrier closes round the frame in its own shape, Blessing of Protection stamps its crest onto the portrait, Lay on Hands drops a column of light, a resurrection unfolds wings behind the frame, a group heal runs through the group as a wave, Chain Heal bursts along the bars of every frame it reaches.
• Cooldowns: a roar sends square shockwaves out of the frame, a taunt springs a red !, Shield Wall, Barkskin and Dispersion clamp steel guards onto it, Last Stand and Vengeance beat a heart, Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Ice Block grow a golden barrier, Evasion and Deterrence leave afterimages.
• In a raid they stay inside each frame. The Quiet look keeps its own.
• Buff Landings: a buff landing on your group plays on its frame: motes spiral round the portrait into the buff's star while a light runs along the frame, in its school's colour (Fortitude gold, Mark of the Wild green, Arcane Intellect blue, Shadow Protection violet, Battle Shout amber), whoever cast it. A group buff runs out from the caster's frame, a buff on your target lands on the target frame too, and in a raid each frame only glints. Buffs you can only cast on yourself play nothing. Its switch is in Heal Effects.
• Party frames: Flip Horizontally (Party > Layout) mirrors the party portraits for a party on the right side of the screen: the portrait on the right, the name, level, bars, icons and buffs to its left. The effects play mirrored too.
• The frame previews in the configurator: a part you drag stays inside the preview, and the preview fits the frame with every part shown on it. The party portraits' preview shows the members' aura row as the game does.
• Indicators: right-click one on the preview to remove it, and size its time and stacks right under the preview (Party or Raid > Indicators).
• Indicators: spell groups (Party or Raid > Indicators). Drag a whole group onto your frame: your heals over time, your shields, your other buffs, defensives from others, their own defensives, haste and power, speed and freedom, group buffs, lockouts (Forbearance, Weakened Soul), and debuffs by their kind. Each group holds every class's spells, read from the game's own spell data, each with its switch; move a spell to another group, add one by name, or show them in your own order with a colour each. Every class starts with a set of its own; lists you made yourself stay as they are.
• Party and raid frames: one look. A party in raid frames now wears the look you set on Raid; the Party page is for the party frames with portraits.
• Hide Combat Flash, unticked, now shows a soft halo round each unit frame's own shape while it has threat: amber when close to pulling, red while holding the enemy. It fits the player, target, focus, pet and party portraits in every skin, and the game's own flash, which never fitted the frames, stays hidden.
• Hide Heal Numbers (Unit & Group Frames > Player, its portrait): your portrait no longer shows the green numbers of the heals you take; damage, misses and mana gains still show.
• Your party stays in one place when you switch between raid frames and portraits, and your raid frames keep their top-left corner when you change how many stand in a column (the top-right for a party flipped to the right).
• Damage Meter: your numbers and your party's now sit in a small tab on the end of the name plate, on your player frame and on each party frame, in the frame's own look; yours move, scale and fade with your frame (Your Values no longer has its own box in Edit Layout). The party's no longer turn on the game's Show Party Pets, which is back to your own setting.…

• Route: Repair, Innkeeper, Flight Master and the other service buttons route to the nearest one at once again. Since 1.1.0 a click could take several seconds while far ones were measured that could never be the nearest.
• Route: routes to the other continent are found faster, and while one is found "Loading navigation..." shows with its bar, as on the first route of a session.
• Route: a route to a place the roads don't reach (inside a building, on a ledge, behind a fence) starts at once instead of after several seconds.
• Fixed: after one route from a spot the roads don't reach, routes to the other continent could keep failing until you learned a new flight point.
• Route uses less memory: the roads go in with about half the memory thrown away, and finding a route leaves far less behind, so MelloUI's memory reading swings much less.
• Swing Badge: the strike shows when your blow lands, not when the swing starts, and a critical hit or a parry shows on the blow it belongs to.
• Fixed: an error in fights from the Personal Display's Big Cooldowns when the game keeps aura updates secret.

• Dungeon Info: each dungeon and raid has a Trash section: the rare and epic drops of its other creatures, with who drops each and the chance.
• Dungeon Info: a new look. Every dungeon and raid shows its picture, cut to fit and never stretched (Forever's own dungeons, such as the Hall of Thanes, the Excavation Site and Dalaran, their loading screen): on its row in the list, behind its name at the top of its page, and on its bosses' pages.
• Dungeon Info counts what falls in front of you: a boss's kills and drops, and the corpses you loot with their rare drops, so drops the data does not know get a chance too. /dungeoninfo export puts what you have seen in a text to post in MelloUI's Discord; it goes into the next update for everyone.
• Dungeon Info: with DungeonJournal installed, its loot lists for the bosses and the trash show in Dungeon Info too.
• Dungeon Info: the bosses of Forever's own dungeons (the Hall of Thanes, the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site) list their loot, and the classic dungeons Forever changed (the Deadmines, Wailing Caverns, Shadowfang Keep ...) show Forever's drops: from DungeonMaster's lists, by MalkDev. A drop's chance shows once it has been seen falling.
• Dungeon Info shows the drop rates players collect for Everloot (everloot.app, CC BY-SA 4.0) for the bosses of Forever's own dungeons, whose loot is not in the game's files, as they come in.

• Fixed: after learning a new stance or form, the game could block MelloUI's actions in a fight and drop to a few frames a second until a restart. A blocked action now costs MelloUI next to nothing, so the game recovers by itself, and /mellobug counts repeats instead of listing each one.
• Fixed: the installer said your screen was too small for Mello's layout, at any UI scale, whenever some of your own settings did not fit it. It now says it is your settings.
• Combat Text: an aura that comes and goes again within a few seconds (a warlock's Demonic Knowledge as the pet moves in and out of range) is shown once, not every time.
• Fixed (MelloUI Oldschool): popups that ask you to type something, such as renaming a hunter pet, show their text box again.
• The Dungeon Info button on the map is drawn from a copy made for its size, sharp like the other icons.

addons.description:
World of Warcraft addon that allows configuring a custom client locale to be respected by addons that use AceLocale.
Usage
• Run /addonlocale to show the currently configured locale, if any.
• Run /addonlocale set to configure a custom locale for addons.
• Run /addonlocale reset to reset any custom locale configuration and allow the default client locale to be used.
Integration
AddOns that use AceLocale will automatically be configured to use the appropriate locale. Otherwise, AddOns should check for the presence of a GAME_LOCALE global variable and use that in-preference to the return from [GetLocale], as shown below. It may also be beneficial to list !!AddonLocale as an optional dependency in your TOC.
addons.name: AddonLocale

Changelogv1.8.1
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Faster again: since v1.7.1, checking whether a quest objective is done rebuilt the list of
every place its monsters stand each time (on level steps, for each quest of your log). Ding
reads the objective's text first and keeps that list once built.
v1.8.0
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Problem with this step? An orange flag in the guide window's title bar, right beside the
NPC directory's pin (with a gamepad: up from the first line in focus mode), its own key binding
(Settings > Keybinds, a button or two like the others) and /ding bug. A window shows in plain
words what the report will contain: the guide, the step and its place in the guide's file,
where you stand, your character's level, race, class and side, the step's quests and the ones
of your log the next steps need, with their counters, what the arrow points at, the settings
that change your route, Ding's and the game's versions. Never your character's name, your
realm or your account.
• Pick what went wrong among four ready answers (handy with a gamepad) and add your own words if
you can type, then Create the text: 1. the address of the GitHub page to open, 2. the text
to paste into it, each selected by its button for Ctrl+C (an addon cannot copy for you). Ding
keeps your last 20 reports in its saved variables (WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\Ding.lua),
so a player without a keyboard can send that file instead; "Restore all defaults" keeps them.
v1.7.1
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• The arrow no longer leads to monsters you have already killed enough of, when the game names
them in your language and Ding only knows their English name (Forever's own monsters, the
Skyborne start among them): it matches the quest's objectives by their order too. Their
marks and counters above the nameplates come back the same way.
• "Choose quest rewards" never takes a piece your class cannot wear (a druid's reward was taken
in mail): only what you can wear counts as an upgrade, and when none is, the reward that
sells for the most among what you can use. The chat says which reward Ding took and why.
v1.7.0
Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.
• Dungeon quests: a new pack, Ding! - Dungeon quests (Settings > Guide, under
"Dungeons"), with one guide per dungeon for your side, listed by level (the ones above your
level are greyed, you can still pick them). Each guide takes you to every quest giver of that
dungeon and through the chains that lead to them, in an order that keeps the trips short, then
to the dungeon's entrance, then through the dungeon with a note for each quest (which boss or
monster drops what, where it waits), and back to the turn-ins and the quests they open. Every
dungeon from Ragefire Chasm, the Deadmines and Wailing Caverns to Blackrock Depths, Lower
Blackrock Spire, Dire Maul, Scholomance and Stratholme, and Forever's own: the Hall of Thanes,
the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site of the Wetlands and the City of Dalaran.
• The first step of each chain says what it brings (a weapon of your choice, armor of your
kind, a ring, a big amount of XP) and when it is long or far away; very long or far chains are
optional and say why. A quest that starts from a drop shows only once the drop is in your bags.
Raids, the Upper Spire and the level 60 armor-set chains are not in the pack.
• A step that takes you to a dungeon's entrance now passes once you are inside: the game gives
no position in a dungeon, and the step stayed on screen for the whole run.
• "Take this guide up where I am" keeps your place: it stops only on a quest of your log still
to finish or a quest of the route you never took. With "Elite quests" turned on, it used to
send you back to the first elite quest of the section.…
addons.description:
A free, open-source leveling guide for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60). Ding
shows what to do next, points the way with its own arrow and moves forward on its own as you
accept, complete and turn in quests. It is built from the ground up to be played **with a
gamepad**.

Download on CurseForge

> Version 1.8, released during the Forever beta.
> Alliance 1–60: Human, Dwarf/Gnome and Night Elf starting zones up to level 20, then a
> common route to 60. Horde 1–60: Orc/Troll, Tauren and Undead starting zones up to
> level 20, then a common route to 60.
> Levels 30 to 60 have not been played in game yet (the beta stops at 30): they are checked
> by the offline tools only. Please report what you find in the
> issues.
addons.name: Ding!

addons.description:
Key Bind Profiles is a lightweight addon designed to improve the management of keybinds in World of Warcraft. Blizzard’s default system only allows for character-specific keybind settings. This addon extends functionality by allowing specialization-specific profiles that automatically load when you switch specializations.
Features
• Profile Management: Create and save keybind settings into profiles that can be reloaded anytime.
• Specialization-Specific Profiles: Assign profiles to specific specializations for automatic loading upon switching.
• Auto-Save Functionality: Keybinds are automatically saved when changed, with the option to disable this feature for manual control.
• Persistent Settings: The profiles retain settings even after quitting the game.
Usage
To manually manage profiles, through a macro for example, access the addon's interface menu or use the following chat commands:
• /kbp save: Saves the current profile.
• /kbp save [profilename]: Saves to a specified profile. Overwrites if it exists, or creates a new one.
• /kbp load [profilename]: Loads an existing profile.
• /kbp delete [profilename]: Deletes an existing profile.
• /kbp list: Lists all existing profiles.

Manual keybinds saving is available through the 'Save Keybinds' button or by using the /kbp command.
Storage and Backup
Keybind settings are stored in the following directory:
/World of Warcraft/_/WTF/Account//SavedVariables/KeyBindProfiles.lua

Important: Deleting your WTF folder will remove all stored keybinds. To prevent loss of data, keep a backup of the KeyBindProfiles.lua file. If you reinstall the game, restore this file to retain your settings. It's not possible to recover keybinds if you lose this file.
Compatibility
This addon has been tested and works with:
• Default Action Bars
• Bartender
• Dominos

addons.changelog:
Changelogv0.9.0
New
• Effects: new options page to control the buff and debuff icons the game draws. On enemy nameplates (mostly what you cast on them): show or hide, size and position. On the target frame: buffs and debuffs separately, their size, and the same on the focus frame. On you (next to the minimap): your buffs and your debuffs (curses, poisons...) separately. Buttons to Blizzard's panel that chooses which buffs and debuffs the Cooldown Manager tracks, and to Edit Mode.
• Hide any frame by its name: put the mouse over it, type /fstack, and write its name on the Effects page or with /rcm hide . Write it again to show it back.
• The addon never reads the effects: it only hides, resizes or moves Blizzard's icons, so it also works in combat, and everything goes back to Blizzard's look when you set the defaults again.
v0.8.0
New
• Save your interface: new Interface options page (also /rcm ui). A snapshot keeps your frame positions (the active Edit Mode layout), all your keybindings (with Shift, Ctrl and Alt combinations), all your account and character macros (also the ones that are not on a bar) and what is on action bars 1 to 8: spells, items, macros, mounts, toys, pets and equipment sets. Snapshots belong to your account, so you can restore them on any character.
• Restore chooses which parts to put back. Positions are saved as an account Edit Mode layout named "Ruscuu" plus the snapshot name and the interface reloads to apply them; missing macros are created again and changed ones get their saved text back, and anything the character doesn't know is listed in the chat. Only out of combat.
• Export a snapshot as text to keep it or share it, and import it on another account.
• Export everything / Import everything: all your snapshots and style profiles in a single text, to move them to another game version (for example, from the beta to the release) or another computer. Importing replaces snapshots and profiles with the same name, so a fresh install gets your style back.
v0.7.2
Fixed
• Threat meter: the bar could still stay purple in combat when an enemy was attacking you. The color is now painted on the bar's texture (which accepts the values the game hides), and if the threat level can't be used it falls back to whether the enemy is attacking you (red) or not.
• /rcm debug shows whether the game hides the threat level and where the bar's color came from.
v0.7.1
Fixed
• Threat meter: in combat the bar stayed purple ("hidden by the game") even when the enemy was attacking you. The game hides the threat level in combat, but the addon now passes it to a color curve, so the bar shows the right color (green, yellow, orange or red) without reading the value.
• Threat meter: changing the width (and the other size, position and color options) now updates the meters already on screen right away.
v0.7.0
New
• Threat meter on enemy nameplates: above each enemy you are fighting, your threat as a bar, a percentage or both (100% means you would pull it), colored by the danger: low, about to pull it, pulled but barely, and attacking you. New Threat options page: what to show, width, height, position, every color, the number's size, color and place, and a 10-second test to adjust it out of combat. Needs enemy nameplates turned on (V key).

Fixed
• Shooting with a wand no longer makes every cooldown light up: the golden border on the Cooldown Manager and action buttons, and the active cooldowns bar, now ignore the short lock each wand shot puts on all spells (the game doesn't report it as the global cooldown). Real cooldowns keep showing while you shoot.
• /rcm debug shows which spell is used to recognize that lock.
v0.6.2
Fixed
• Characters of different classes no longer mix their spells and icons. Each class now gets its own profile the first time you log in with it (a copy of Default's look, without spells from other classes), used by every specialization until you pick another one.…
addons.description:
Español abajo

Ruscuu visual style for Blizzard's Cooldown Manager in World of Warcraft: Forever: square icons with neon purple borders, purple bars, styled cooldown numbers, a pulsing golden border when a cooldown is about to end, and one-click themes.

It only changes how things look — it never reads combat data, so it follows Forever's addon restrictions. Everything it changes can be customized and goes back to Blizzard's look instantly when you turn it off.
Features
• Ruscuu style for the four Cooldown Manager viewers (essential, utility, buff icons, buff bars): square icons, icon crop, borders (custom or class color), swipe color, swipe edge, finish flash, bar texture and colors (custom or class color).
• Active cooldowns bar: only the cooldowns that are running, in one centered line together with the active buffs (icons and bars), with a flash and an optional sound when each one ends. Choose any spell (spellbook, pet, by ID or name), your trinkets and any item, their order, the icon size and spacing, and where the bar goes (drag it or set its position). Test it for 10 seconds from the options.
• Keybinds on Cooldown Manager icons: the key that casts each spell, taken from your action bars.
• Golden border during the last seconds of a cooldown, on action buttons and Cooldown Manager icons: seconds, color, thickness, glow and blink style/speed — and you choose which spells get it.
• Border when a buff is about to end, on the Cooldown Manager's buff icons and bars.
• Threat meter on enemy nameplates: a thin bar above each enemy you fight that fills with your threat and turns yellow, orange and red as you get close to pulling it.
• Effects: control the buff and debuff icons the game draws: on enemy nameplates (show, size, position), on the target and focus frames (buffs and debuffs separately, size) and on you (your buffs and your debuffs, like curses). Hide any other frame by the name /fstack shows.
• Choose which cooldowns are shown through Blizzard's own Advanced Cooldown Settings, one click away.
• Cooldown numbers on the Cooldown Manager and action bars: font, size, outline and color for every text.
• Works with Bartender4, Dominos and ElvUI action bars.
• Themes: Ruscuu Neon, Minimal, Dark, Class color and Blizzard style.
• Profiles per specialization that switch automatically, plus rename, duplicate and reset. Each class starts with its own profile, so spells never mix between characters.
• Import / Export your style as a text string to share it.
• Save your interface: snapshots of your frame positions (Edit Mode layout), all your keybindings, all your macros and your action bars (spells, items, macros, mounts, toys, equipment sets). Restore them on any character, choose which parts to restore, and export them as text. Export everything puts all your snapshots and style profiles in one text to move them to another game version (for example, from the beta to the release). Only out of combat.
• Options with live preview, help on every control, values you can type and a Defaults button on each page.
• Minimap button with the Ruscuu bear (round or square minimaps).
• English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese and Russian.
Commands
| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| /rcm or /rcmf | Open options |
| /rcm cooldowns | Choose which cooldowns are shown (Blizzard's panel) |
| /rcm test | Preview the golden border for 5 seconds |
| /rcm skin | Reapply the style |
| /rcm minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |
| /rcm ui | Save or restore your interface (positions, keybindings, action bars) |
| /rcm hide | Hide or show again any frame by its name (see /fstack) |
| /rcm debug | Diagnostic information |
| /rcm reset | Reset all settings (asks first) |

addons.description:
DOINK is an addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that tells your guild
about your adventures. It watches for nine kinds of in-game event
(level-ups, loot, deaths, quest turn-ins, boss kills, profession skill-ups,
new mounts, duel and Mak'gora wins, and battleground wins) and announces the
ones you choose in guild, officer, party or raid chat the moment they
happen, with real item links:

Discord too. The free, open-source
DOINK companion mirrors the
same events to a Discord channel of your choice as class-coloured embeds
with Wowhead links, so your guild's Discord sees every ding, epic and boss
kill even when nobody is online. See
Discord mirroring.

> Two parts, one optional. The addon alone does all the guild chat
> announcements. Discord posting requires the companion, a separate
> program (Windows, or Linux) you download from the GitHub releases page and run
> alongside the game: WoW addons cannot reach the internet, so without the
> companion nothing goes to Discord. Install the addon from here; get the
> companion from GitHub if you want Discord.

No dependencies and no libraries: install it and it works. Settings are on
a normal options page (Esc → Options → AddOns → DOINK) and can also be set
with /doink commands.

Guild already linked to Discord? Blizzard's guild chat link shows DOINK's
lines in your Discord channel with no companion at all; see
below.
Credit: Dink
DOINK is heavily inspired by Dink,
the RuneLite plugin by pajlads that posts your
Old School RuneScape achievements to Discord. The idea of an addon that
notices your milestones and tells your friends, the Discord embeds, the
per-event toggles and the name all come from Dink. DOINK is not affiliated
with the Dink project; it's a from-scratch WoW take on the same idea, built
within what a WoW addon is allowed to do. If you play OSRS, go use Dink.

addons.description:
Incognito adds your specified name in front of your chat messages. Incognito Resurrected can be enabled for guild (and officer), party, raid, world, custom, and community chat.

Midnight and Forever API changes limit prefixing while addon restrictions or secret-value chat lockdown is active (encounters, Mythic+, PvP matches, and some maps). Open-world combat still prefixes.
Example
[Guild] [Yourchar]: Some chat message

becomes

[Guild] [Yourchar]: (Yourname): Some chat message
Usage
Use the GUI (/inc or /incognito) or slash commands:
• /inc — Open the configuration dialog
• /inc name — Set the name shown in front of your messages
• /inc debug — Toggle debug output
• /inc help — Show slash-command help

/inc2 and /incognito2 still open the same panel.
Options
• Use global profile — Share settings across characters, or turn this off for a per-character
profile
• Enable — Add your name to chat messages
• Name — The name displayed in your chat messages
• Color Name by class — Color the prefix with the sender's class color
• Hide name if it matches your character's name — Skip the prefix when it would repeat your
character name
• Guild — Guild and officer chat (/g, /o)
• Party / Dungeon / Raid / Battleground / Arena — Instance toggles are skipped on Retail and
Forever while restrictions are active
• World Chat — General, Trade, LocalDefense, and Services (all or none)
• Channel — Custom channels, comma-separated
• Community — Community channels (Retail)
• Debug — Debug output

addons.description:
Guild Search is World of Warcraft addon to help guild leaders and officers. It allows searching the guild roster, particularly the notes and officer notes. Many guilds will keep meaningful notes in those fields including the the player names for alts. It is very useful to be able to search a large guild roster to find characters. For example, with the recent rise in compromised accounts, if the right information is in the notes, it makes it easy to find all the alts of a player and demote them.

It has options to allow configuring which fields will be searched.

Guild Search displays the following items:
• Class-colored character name
• Level
• Note
• Officer Note
• Rank
• Last Online

You can search the following data:
• Character Name
• Note
• Office Note
• Rank (off by default)
• Class Name (off by default)
• Realm

You can also choose to display one of the following fields:
• Realm
• Total XP
• Weekly XP
• Total Rank
• Weekly Rank

You can also edit the following items for a guild member:
• Public Note
• Officer Note
• Rank

You can bring up the search window via:
• Chat command /gsearch
• LDB launcher
• Minimap button

The Last Online column is an approximate based on the data available in the guild roster. It will always be at least an hour off because the smallest unit of time the roster provides is hours.

addons.changelog:
Pagle1.0.0 (2026-11-04)
The first release. Pagle is a fishing addon for World of Warcraft: Forever, for progression and collection, with a few quality-of-life touches beside them. It watches what you catch and rewards it. It never fishes for you.

It comes as six addons in one download: Pagle itself and five Modules, the Ledger, Hunts, Stats, the Tackle Board and QoL. Turn any Module off in the AddOns list and nothing of it loads. Pagle keeps recording your Catches either way, so a Module you turn back on catches up on everything it missed, in one card.
Pagle
• New to Pagle? A Letter arrives at your first login and opens a short Field guide. After that, notes appear beside each first moment and window, and a First evening list in the tracker shows what to try. /pagle guide opens the guide again.
• Every Cast you make is written into one Catch log, shared by every character on your account. Everything the Modules show is read from it.
• Open any of it from Pagle's entry in the addon compartment by the minimap, or with /pagle. Pagle's settings live in the game's own Settings panel, where its search finds every option.
• When you earn something, Pagle says so in the moment: a toast writes the fish's name out in ink while its stamps come down, a banner drops its seal for a new Angler Level, and a Legend gets the whole screen. A Session that earned something ends with a summary card.
• Every catch gets a toast: its size band and length over the fish's name, with a colour you've caught before named after a small gem and its rarity on the ring (the medallion keeps the fish's icon; a colour's art fills it only the first time you catch it). Past your Interruption budget (40 every 5 minutes, which you can change) it steps down to a quiet one-line Nod, and a bigger moment for the same catch shows instead. "Show every catch" turns it off.
• The Interruption budget keeps announcements from talking over your fishing, Cozy mode holds them all for the end of the Session, and the Animations setting stills the motion if you'd rather it kept still.
• Shift-drag a toast to move where toasts and Nods appear; Reset on the Announcements settings page puts them back.
• Pagle Coins are paid for progress and things achieved, never per Catch: a level-up pays 40 Coins and a Prestige 1,500. Spend them in the Curio Shop on looks: toast styles, sound sets, bindings and tracker frames. The stock never rotates, and nothing in it buys a title or a star.
• The Curio Shop prices run in six tiers, from 250 Coins to 25,000. They are paced so that an angler fishing an hour and a half a day can afford a first look within the first hour, a quarter of the stock in about 40 hours of fishing and the whole of tiers 1 to 5 in about 720.
• The Curio Shop lists each slot's looks cheapest first: the one you start with, then the ones for sale from tier 1 down to the dearest. It only sells: a look you earn stays out of it, owned or not, until it can be bought too, and is seen in the Fish Journal's Collection instead.
• The Field report: seen a fish in new waters, or outside its usual hours? /pagle report gathers what Pagle doesn't know yet for you to post on the issue form. It never names your characters.
• No Companion? /pagle export, or Copy for the website in Pagle's settings, turns your Catch log into a Paste string to paste on the Pagle website, part by part for a long log. It offers what's new since your last export, or everything.
