addons.description:
Pagle is a fishing addon for World of Warcraft: Forever, named after Nat Pagle and meant to be the only fishing addon you need.

Progression and collection come first, with optional quality-of-life touches beside them.

It watches what you catch and rewards it. It never fishes for you.

Fish Journal ·
Hunts ·
Wagers ·
Stats ·
Tackle Board ·
Moments ·
Curio Shop ·
Fishing key ·
How it works ·
Companion

Every Cast you make is written into one log, shared by every character on your account, and everything Pagle shows is read from it. Open any of it from Pagle's entry in the addon compartment by the minimap, or with /pagle.
Get it
Pagle is one download of six addons. Unzip it so every folder lands in Interface/AddOns, then /reload.

> [!NOTE]
> Pagle runs on World of Warcraft: Forever only, and 1.0 is in English only.

The Fish Journal
The Ledger keeps your life as an angler in the Fish Journal, a leather-bound book of parchment pages. Every Catch earns XP toward your Angler Level, doubled by Fresh Water after a break from fishing, and at the top you can Prestige for an emblem and climb again. Each Species earns up to three stars, each zone a Zone Mastery rank from Visitor to Master, and the Junk Museum, Treasures and the Trophy Room fill in as you go.

Fish you haven't caught stay nameless. A riddle sets the scene, and a plain hint is there when you'd rather just know. Legends, the named catches you won't land on an ordinary day, arrive with a splash and a title to sign the Journal with. Your longest of each Species is kept as well, from Tiddler to Monster.

Browse the collection: Prestige frames, Legends, zone crests and bindings

Hunts
Hunts are the catches worth planning for: a fish that bites by night, in one season or during an event, or a catch that only counts under conditions of its own, such as a grouper by moonlight. The Hunts board, a leather notebook, lays them out on a timeline of what's biting now, what opens soon and what comes later. Each Hunt completes in bronze, some go on to silver and gold, and finishing a themed set earns its title. The board counts your Casts at each Hunt without pretending to know the odds, and the Hunts you pin follow you in a tracker under the minimap.
Pagle Wagers
Pagle Wagers are Hunts themed on one or two zones and put on the table for about three days at a time. Land every Hunt's first mark before the wager closes to settle it. Any number can be on at once, each one starts fresh and pays again, and every wager you settle climbs a ladder of titles.

Stats
Stats keeps your own numbers in the Stats book: every Session, your lifetime totals, and what bites in each water you've fished. Your odds for each fish come only from your own Casts, and always say how many Casts they rest on. A Dry spell counts the Casts since you last caught something and says plainly when the wait is unusual. Every Cast is its own roll; nothing is owed. Watch up to three Dry spells on the live tracker. Stats shows numbers when you ask, and announces nothing.

The Tackle Board
The Tackle Board is opt-in: a cork board where three Notices go up each day and an Expedition each week, such as "4 different Species in Feralas". Fish where you like, and they fill in as you go. They never expire, so a missed day banks rather than vanishes, and each one can be taken down, once a day, for a fresh one of another kind. Each day with a goal done keeps your Campfire burning, Kindling carries it through a day you couldn't make, and your longest Campfire is kept for good. Every goal done ties a new fly in your Fly Box.

It comes as six addons in one download: Pagle itself and five Modules, the Ledger, Hunts, Stats, the Tackle Board and QoL. Turn any Module off in the AddOns list and nothing of it loads. Pagle keeps recording your Catches either way, so a Module you turn back on catches up on everything it missed, in one card.
Pagle
• New to Pagle? A Letter arrives at your first login and opens a short Field guide. After that, notes appear beside each first moment and window, and a First evening list in the tracker shows what to try. /pagle guide opens the guide again.
• Every Cast you make is written into one Catch log, shared by every character on your account. Everything the Modules show is read from it.
• Open any of it from Pagle's entry in the addon compartment by the minimap, or with /pagle. Pagle's settings live in the game's own Settings panel, where its search finds every option.
• When you earn something, Pagle says so in the moment: a toast writes the fish's name out in ink while its stamps come down, a banner drops its seal for a new Angler Level, and a Legend gets the whole screen. A Session that earned something ends with a summary card.
• Every catch gets a toast: its size band and length over the fish's name, with a colour you've caught before named after a small gem and its rarity on the ring (the medallion keeps the fish's icon; a colour's art fills it only the first time you catch it). Past your Interruption budget (40 every 5 minutes, which you can change) it steps down to a quiet one-line Nod, and a bigger moment for the same catch shows instead. "Show every catch" turns it off.
• The Interruption budget keeps announcements from talking over your fishing, Cozy mode holds them all for the end of the Session, and the Animations setting stills the motion if you'd rather it kept still.
• Shift-drag a toast to move where toasts and Nods appear; Reset on the Announcements settings page puts them back.

• The Curio Shop prices run in six tiers, from 250 Coins to 25,000. They are paced so that an angler fishing an hour and a half a day can afford a first look within the first hour, a quarter of the stock in about 40 hours of fishing and the whole of tiers 1 to 5 in about 720.

Forever Classmate v0.26.0What changed
• Audited all nine classes against Blizzard’s November 3 Forever launch notes. Replaced retired Paladin, Rogue, Druid and Shaman cues with learned launch abilities, including Unsealed Wrath, Shank, Primal Bite and Lightning Mastery. Venom is a temporary proc; it no longer counts as Rogue upkeep.
• Added selected readable effects and cooldowns to existing class slots: Garrote, Death Mark, Rake, Lacerate, Reckless Swings, Slam, Missile Barrage, Penance, Amplify Curse, Stormstrike and Totemic Call. Existing layouts and settings carry forward.
• Corrected the bear, boar, carrion bird and bat family guide entries to match Blizzard’s Forever overview. Pet guide entries remain family guidance, not evidence of an individual pet’s skills.

Use /reload after updating. Checks use mocked APIs; live launch-client aura names and combat restrictions still need validation.

Forever Classmate
One compact, class-aware companion for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Version 0.26.0 supports all nine classes. Forever Classmate detects the player class and starts only that module; other class modules create no frames, events, or polling. Every module has separate saved settings while movement, locking, scale, minimap access, and combat fading remain consistent. Full bars use the same 426-pixel rendered width as Forever's default desktop Main Hand swing timer; Hunters can switch to a 42-pixel range icon.

The interface follows the WoW client language: English and Simplified Chinese (zhCN) labels for bars, settings, warnings, and tooltips. Spell and character names come from the client; curated rare-pet names may remain in English. Other client locales use English.
Class companions
| Class | Live helper |
| --- | --- |
| Hunter | Range brackets and validated yards or an optional red/green range icon; ammo, target of target, facing, Hunter's Mark, aspect, pet care, family guidance, and optional player Inspect |
| Shaman | Four totem slots with live or marked estimated timers, weapon imbue, elemental shield, mana, Totemic Recall, and learned Maelstrom, Riptide, Lightning Mastery, Stormstrike and Totemic Call cues |
| Paladin | Mana, active seal, target judgments, Unsealed Wrath aura, and learned Holy Strike/Holy Shock/Consecration readiness |
| Warrior | Rage, current stance, shout upkeep, Rend/Deep Wounds, and learned cues including Overpower, Slam and Reckless Swings |
| Rogue | Energy, combo points, both weapon coatings, Slice and Dice upkeep, Poised and Venom procs, target poison or bleed, and reactive abilities |
| Druid | Current form and its live power type, Mark/Thorns, target bleeds and DoTs, Poised and other readable procs, plus Primal Bite and Shifting Power |
| Mage | Live mana meter, armor and absorb-shield status, personal target setup, Hot Streak/Fingers of Frost/Arcane Blast/Missile Barrage state, and learned cooldowns |
| Priest | Mana, self buffs, Shadow target effects, Penance and other healing or Shadow abilities, and Forever's race-specific Priest spells |
| Warlock | Mana, health, Soul Shards, armor, demon presence, target DoT/Bane/Curse, and learned abilities including Amplify Curse |

The seven standard class bars discover every learned active racial and surface the one most useful now, while hover details list the others. This includes Forever racials such as Will to Survive, Elune's Light, Eureka!, Shatter Curse, Read Ley Line, and Skysight, plus the twelve race-specific Priest spells. “Context” means the game currently reports the racial unusable; the addon does not guess why.…

| Mage | Live mana meter, armor and absorb-shield status, personal target setup, Hot Streak/Fingers of Frost/Arcane Blast state, and learned cooldowns |
| Priest | Mana, self buffs, Shadow target effects, healing or Shadow abilities, and Forever's race-specific Priest spells |
| Warlock | Mana, health, Soul Shards, armor, demon presence, target DoT/Bane/Curse, and learned abilities |

The seven standard class bars discover every learned active racial and surface the one most useful now, while hover details list the others. This includes Forever racials such as Will to Survive, Elune's Light, Eureka!, Shatter Curse, Read Ley Line, and Skysight, plus the twelve race-specific Priest spells. “Context” means the game currently reports the racial unusable; the addon does not guess why.

Resource percentages use Forever’s native percent API when exact power values are restricted. Class cues come from the live spellbook and aura/cooldown APIs. They adapt to learned talents without hardcoded Classic spell IDs and do not infer a specialization, prescribe a fixed rotation, or cast anything. When the client cannot supply a useful live state, its bar status disappears; confirmed observations and explicit cast-based estimates remain visible.

Warrior, Rogue, Druid, Priest, and Warlock can show slim multi-target DoT bars to the right of the main bar. Each row identifies an enemy, your active effect, and its readable remaining time. The strip tracks the current target and nearby enemies that have active nameplates; it clears a row when the effect expires or its nameplate disappears. It cannot continue tracking an offscreen enemy whose aura state Forever no longer exposes. Turn it off with Show multi-target DoT bars in your class settings. The original 426 × 56 bar stays the same size.…

addons.description:
Forever GuideMate is a minimalist, free, open-source questing guide for World of Warcraft: Forever. It shows the next quest step and tracks destinations with Blizzard Map Pins or optional TomTom. It reads your quest log.

Blizzard Map Pins is the default waypoint provider. Choose optional TomTom under Navigation in addon settings.

It does not accept quests, choose rewards, move the character, or take protected gameplay actions. A guide the character cannot use says Ineligible. Coordinates in the shipped guides have not been validated in the Forever client.

Opening an authored guide midway resumes a valid saved step or returns to the earliest unfinished eligible route step. After starters, Forever Casual Route (Alliance or Horde) is the 1–60 spine: Casual leveling order with Forever quests woven on top, as one flat guide (no zone chapter title). Use Skip on Casual or dungeon guides to hard-skip a step and its dependents after a confirm; Loremaster cannot skip. Sync resyncs from the quest log and keeps skips; Reset skips on this guide in options clears them. Completed quest history comes from the client, and verified quest prerequisites are followed automatically. If a giver does not offer an expected quest and no verified prerequisite is registered, the tracker stops with a diagnostic instead of silently skipping the quest.

Quest-step rules are in docs/guide-authoring.md. Loremaster weave rules are in docs/zone-loremaster-guides.md.

All guides except Miscellaneous follow their authored action order. Miscellaneous includes exploration and books. Loremaster currently shows Coming Soon!

The leveling route is quest-only. Its reference includes grinding and level-up stops that are intentionally omitted, so matching quest order does not establish sufficient XP at every transition.
Guide Types
• Class Quests
• Dungeon Quests
• Leveling Quests
• Loremaster (Coming Soon!)
• Raid Quests
• Miscellaneous

[2.8.1] - 2026-11-03
On WoW Forever, quest icons on nameplates no longer cover the level beside the health bar, and on retail Everything Quests is marked up to date for patch 12.1.7.
Bug Fixes
• Nameplate quest icons covered the level on WoW Forever. Forever shows a nameplate's level in a small badge just right of the health bar, where the quest icon and its count started, so they covered it. With the Position set to Right, the default, they now start just after the level badge, level with the health bar. With a nameplate addon that replaces the game's own nameplates, such as ElvUI, they sit where they did before. The X offset now counts from the end of the badge, so if you had changed it, setting it back to 0 puts the icons just after the badge.
Notes
• Patch 12.1.7. On retail Everything Quests is now marked up to date for patch 12.1.7, so the game will not treat it as out of date once 12.1.7 is out.
• A new description in the AddOns list. On Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever, Everything Quests' description in the game's AddOns list now names more of what it does there, such as the Quest Browser and Quest History, and no longer says "limited and growing" or "a work in progress".
addons.description:
A unified replacement for the Blizzard quest experience — objective tracker, world-map overlays, nameplate quest icons, an account-wide quest history, and a quest chain guide. Runs on retail, Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever.

Watch the Everything Quests video tutorial

Overview
Everything Quests replaces Blizzard's quest tracking and builds on the rest of its quest experience for World of Warcraft: Midnight, and also runs on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever (see Classic support below).

1. An on-screen objective tracker that replaces the default ObjectiveTrackerFrame, provided by EQ Objective Tracker and installed automatically alongside this addon
2. Nameplate Quest Icons — a quest icon plus the remaining count or percent on objective mobs in the 3D world
3. Interactive World Quest pins on the world map and zone maps, plus a docked World Quests panel (retail)
4. A standalone Chain Guide window for browsing quest chains: Midnight's on retail, and on WoW Forever every chain your character can take
5. An account-wide Quest History log with a backfill of past completions, on every version Everything Quests runs on
6. Branded Quest POI overlays on zone maps, and on Classic, objective spawn markers on both the world map and the minimap
7. A Quest Browser on Classic, for looking up almost any quest in the game before you accept it, plus shareable quest links in chat on every flavor
8. Quest progress on game tooltips — a bag item names the quest that wants it, how many are still missing, and which group members still need it too
9. Coordinate readouts on the world map and under the minimap, for the cursor and for your own position
10. Optional auto-accept / auto-turn-in for quest dialogs (Alt to pause)
11. Group quest features — quest announcements in party or raid chat, escorts and other group quests joined for you, and your group's quest progress on quest markers and tooltips

Open Options with /eqs, from the minimap button, from the Everything Quests icon on the tracker, or via Game Menu > Options > AddOns > Everything Quests.

Classic support
Everything Quests runs on Classic Era (1.15), Burning Crusade Classic (2.5) and WoW Forever (1.60). On Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic, support is deliberately partial: what ships is what was measured working on a live client, not the whole addon. WoW Forever loads the same feature set plus a Chain Guide of its own. Elsewhere in this README, "Classic" covers all three unless a flavor is named.

Era and TBC were measured identical across every game API the addon reads, so one implementation covers both. They differ only in their generated dataset — TBC ships its own, because Era quest data has nothing for Outland or for the Blood Elf and Draenei starting zones. WoW Forever has its own dataset too: the Classic Era data adjusted to Forever's maps, plus quests gathered by playing Forever itself and the WoW Forever quest data of AllTheThings. Each flavor's TOC lists exactly one set. They define the same globals and are alternatives, never companions.

Working on Classic Era and TBC
• Objective markers on the world map and the minimap, drawn from a generated coordinate database rather than from the client, which exposes no quest coordinates at all
• Objective kind icons — a colored badge per kind, red for something to kill, amber for something to loot and green for something to use, each with a dark outline so a busy zone stays readable. An objective inside a dungeon is marked at the dungeon entrance, with an archway of its own
• Turn-in markers at every location a finished quest can be handed in, and markers for quests you can pick up, gated on level, race, class, prerequisites, reputation, completion, and whether a holiday quest's world event is actually running…

[2.8.1] - 2026-11-03
On WoW Forever, quest icons on nameplates no longer cover the level beside the health bar, and on retail Everything Quests is marked up to date for patch 12.1.7.
Bug Fixes
• Nameplate quest icons covered the level on WoW Forever. Forever shows a nameplate's level in a small badge just right of the health bar, where the quest icon and its count started, so they covered it. With the Position set to Right, the default, they now start just after the level badge, level with the health bar. With a nameplate addon that replaces the game's own nameplates, such as ElvUI, they sit where they did before. The X offset now counts from the end of the badge, so if you had changed it, setting it back to 0 puts the icons just after the badge.
Notes
• Patch 12.1.7. On retail Everything Quests is now marked up to date for patch 12.1.7, so the game will not treat it as out of date once 12.1.7 is out.
• A new description in the AddOns list. On Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic and WoW Forever, Everything Quests' description in the game's AddOns list now names more of what it does there, such as the Quest Browser and Quest History, and no longer says "limited and growing" or "a work in progress".

[2.8.0] - 2026-10-25
Quest History comes to Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic, and the About tab links the new Everything Quests video tutorial.
New Features
• Quest History on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. Every quest you turn in is recorded across your characters, with what it paid and, for a quest you accept from this update on, how long you held it. The Quests page lists them to search, filter by character, date or type, and sort, and the Stats page shows your streak, your activity day by day, your totals, trends over time and this session. Each character's past quests are added the first time it logs in after this update, without dates. The Type filter uses the Quest Browser's groups, and right-clicking a quest opens its Quest Browser page where it has one. Open it with /eqs history or from the History tab in the options window. There is no Chain Timeline page, because it lists the Chain Guide's chains.
Improvements
• A video tutorial. There is now a video tutorial for Everything Quests on YouTube. The About tab's Tutorials card lists it: click YouTube to copy its link.
• Updated Korean. Some of the Korean wording is updated. Translated by labrie75.
Known Issues
• Some past quests in Quest History show as "Quest #12345" on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. A past quest added the first time a character logs in after this update takes its name from the game or from Everything Quests' quest data. When neither has it, the quest keeps its number, because these versions of the game cannot be asked for a quest's name.

[2.7.0] - 2026-10-18
A search box in the options window finds a setting by name and takes you to it, and on WoW Forever, quests new to Forever that belong to a dungeon and need no earlier quest now count as dungeon quests.
New Features
• Search your settings. The options window has a search box at the top of its sidebar. Type a word and it lists the settings and cards that match it, by name or by the card or tab they sit on, each with where it sits, such as Map > Coordinates. Click a result, or press Enter for the first one, to open its tab, scroll to it and light it up for a moment. It searches names, not tooltips.
Improvements
• Two more hand-in markers. Crocs of the Sky and From the Ashes, in the Wetlands on WoW Forever, now have a marker where you hand them in.
Bug Fixes
• Dungeon quests new to WoW Forever count as dungeon quests. A quest new to Forever that belongs to one of its dungeons and needs no earlier quest now counts as a dungeon quest: "Dungeon and raid quests" under "Hide these quests on the map" hides it, the Quest Browser tags it "Dungeon or raid", and Quest History's Type filter lists it as one. That is about half of the dungeon quests new to Forever that are marked on the map. Before, none of them did.
• The Great Windborne Cat Spirit is for druids. On WoW Forever it was marked for every class at level 20. It is the Skyborne druids' version of The Great Cat Spirit, so it is now marked only for druids.
• No "Races: Alliance, Horde" on Skyborne quests. For ten quests only Skyborne characters can take, nine of them on Zephras Isle, the Quest Browser said "Races: Alliance, Horde", which reads as open to everyone. It now shows no race line for them, as for any quest the data does not limit by race.
Known Issues
• About half of the dungeon quests new to WoW Forever that are marked on the map still do not count as dungeon quests. One that follows an earlier quest and starts outside the dungeon, such as Unending Torment in Undercity or Destruction in Deadmines, is left out, because many quests like that are handed in somewhere else.
• Some Skyborne quests are marked for other characters. Many Zephras Isle quests can only be taken by Skyborne characters, but Everything Quests cannot yet record "Skyborne only" in its quest data, so they are marked for other characters, a character who is not Skyborne can see a Zephras Isle zone in the Chain Guide, and the Quest Browser can say "Races: Alliance" for a quest only the High Order can take.

[2.6.1] - 2026-10-17
On retail, the World Quests tab's reward filters now show the ring color each kind of world quest wears on the map, and the PvP and Pet battles rows finally have their icons.
Improvements
• A legend for the world quest ring colors. In the World Quests tab, each reward filter's icon is now round and sits inside the ring that world quests of that type wear on the world map, so the list of filters is also a guide to the ring colors. Hover the "Filters by reward type" title to read what the rings mean, including the larger yellow ring of the world quest you are following.
Bug Fixes
• PvP and Pet battles icons. The PvP and Pet battles reward filters in the World Quests tab, and their rows in the reward summary of the World Quests panel beside the world map, showed no icon, because they pointed at icons the game does not have. They now show a PvP icon and a pet battle icon.

[2.6.0] - 2026-10-17
WoW Forever's quest data grows from 323 Forever quests to 534, more of them know the level and faction they need, and the second Destruction in Deadmines quest is marked near its own quest giver.
New Features
• 211 more WoW Forever quests. Everything Quests now knows 534 quests new to WoW Forever, up from 323. Most of them come from the WoW Forever quest data of the AllTheThings addon, which it publishes under the MIT License, and the rest were gathered by playing Forever. 530 of them have a marker where you pick them up and a Quest Browser entry, every one of them named, and 501 of those carry the level they need. Tirisfal Glades, the Wetlands, Mulgore, Durotar, Teldrassil, the Barrens, Silverpine Forest and Stormwind City gain the most, and quests for Forever's new dungeons are among them.
Improvements
• More Forever quests know what they need. 26 Forever quests that were marked with no level requirement now carry one, so Show of Force and the others are no longer marked before you are high enough to take them. 23 quests that were marked for both factions, most of them on Zephras Isle, are now marked only for the faction that can take them.
Bug Fixes
• The second Destruction in Deadmines quest was marked at the wrong quest giver. On WoW Forever it was marked at Sentinel Hill, on the Alba Fairmoon who gives the first Destruction in Deadmines, rather than at the Alba Fairmoon who offers it in the south of Westfall. It is now marked where she was seen.
Known Issues
• Some Skyborne quests are marked for other characters. Many Zephras Isle quests can only be taken by Skyborne characters, but Everything Quests cannot yet record "Skyborne only" in its quest data, so they are marked for other characters, a character who is not Skyborne can see a Zephras Isle zone in the Chain Guide, and the Quest Browser can say "Races: Alliance" for a quest only the High Order can take, or "Races: Alliance, Horde" for one only Skyborne characters can take.
• Dungeon quests new to Forever do not count as dungeon quests. This includes every quest for Forever's new dungeons. "Dungeon and raid quests" under "Hide these quests on the map" does not hide them, and the Quest Browser and Quest History do not list them as "Dungeon or raid".
• A few quest chains new to Forever show every step at once. Where the quest data does not say which step comes first, or says it only for some characters, Everything Quests marks them all, so a few quest givers, such as one in Thunder Bluff and one in the Wetlands, show two to four quests with the same name.
• Some Chain Guide zones belong to the other faction. On WoW Forever, Alliance characters see an Orgrimmar zone holding the Horde's Ahn'Qiraj war effort quests, and Horde characters an Ironforge zone holding the Alliance's, because those quests carry no faction in the quest data. Warlock class chains also list the other faction's warlock trainer, because the quest data gives a few of their quests to the wrong faction.
• Many quest givers new to Forever have no name yet. Their markers still show where to go, but the tooltip, the Quest Browser and the Chain Guide cannot say who is standing there.

Added
• AddOns List: the new AddOn Sets option (off by default) adds a Sets dropdown beside Disable All, to save which addons are on under a name and turn that set back on later.
• Auto Decline: the new Guild Invites and Guild Charters options (off by default) turn down guild invites and requests to sign a guild charter, even from friends and guildmates.
• Comprehend Scrolls: a new module for Mages: right-click a scroll you read with Comprehension in your bags to cast Comprehend Scroll on it, without opening the spellbook. Not in combat. On by default; it does nothing for characters without the spell.
• Combat Alert: the new Play Sound option (off by default) plays the raid warning sound as you enter combat and a soft chime as you leave, for when you're looking somewhere else.
• Fishing Cast: the new Louder Bobber option (off by default) turns sound effects up and music down while you fish, so the splash is easy to hear, and puts your own volumes back after you stop, even after a reload or disconnect mid-cast.
• Item Tooltips: the new Repair Cost line (off by default) shows what repairing damaged gear costs, on gear you wear or carry, without a merchant's repair cursor.
• Flight Timer: the new Sound on Landing option (off by default) plays the ready check sound a few seconds before you land, on a flight you've taken before, so you can tab out on long flights.
• Forever Quest Icons: the new Quest Details option (on by default) puts the icon after the quest's name at the top of its details, in the quest window and on the map.
• Minimap Node Icons: a new module that puts the herb's or ore's own icon on each tracking dot on the minimap while Find Herbs or Find Minerals is on. Off by default. Its Tint Unusable option (off by default) turns an icon red while your skill is too low to gather it, and Gray Out Trivial (off by default) turns it gray once gathering it no longer raises your skill.
• NPC Nameplates: the new Skip Pets, Skip Totems, and Skip Companions options (off by default) leave players' pets and minions, totems, or companions with Blizzard's own nameplate instead of a name and title.
• Profiler: a new page in Settings (/fpp profile) that records how much CPU each module takes, heaviest first, beside Forever++'s total CPU and memory. A module made of parts folds open to show what each part takes. Nothing is timed until you press Record.
• Quest Levels: a new module that shows a quest's level before its name, like the quest log's [12], in a quest giver's list and at the top of the quest's details. On by default. Its Color by Difficulty option (off by default) colors the level gray through red by how it compares with yours.
• Quest Tracker: the new Current Zone Only option (off by default) tracks only the quests of the zone you're in, and tracks the others again when you get there. The quest your map follows always shows.
• Talent Planner: the new Level-Up Reminder option (off by default) says in chat which talent your plan takes next when you gain a talent point.
• Tooltips: the new Hide Health Bar option (off by default) hides the green health bar under player and NPC tooltips.
• Unusable Items Tint: the new Auction House and Loot options (off by default) tint red the items you can't use in the auction house's search results, and in the loot window and on loot rolls.
• Waylaid Crates: a new module for filling Waylaid Crates. Its Waylaid Crates entry in the auction house's categories lists every item your crates still need, less what's already in your bags and bank.
• Waypoints: the new Follow Selected Quest option (on by default) points the arrow to the quest selected on the map instead of your map pin, and back to the pin when no quest is selected. Its Show Quest Name option (on by default) shows the quest's name under the distance.
• Waypoints: the new Point to Corpse option (on by default) points the arrow to your corpse while you're a ghost, ahead of a quest or your map pin, and back to them once you're alive.…
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for WoW: Forever that adds to and changes the default UI in small, separate modules. It doesn't replace the UI: every change is meant to look like Blizzard shipped it, needs no setup, and can be turned off on its own.

Download it from CurseForge or Wago.
Modules
Everything is on by default except where noted. Each module can be turned off, and most have options.

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| Automation | |
| Auto Decline | Turns down duel requests, and optionally party invites, guild invites, and guild charters, and says in chat who asked. Can let friends and guildmates through for duels and party invites. Off by default. |
| Auto Dismount | Gets you off your mount or stands you up when a spell, flight, loot, or attack fails because you're mounted or sitting. Can also leave shapeshift forms (off by default). |
| Auto Gossip | When an NPC has only one thing to say, or one service beside small talk, and no quests, picks it for you, so the bank, shop, trainer, or flight map opens straight away. Hold the Skip Key (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or none) to choose yourself. Off by default, and so is its Other NPCs option. |
| Auto Release | Releases your spirit when you die in a battleground, unless you can resurrect yourself or someone is resurrecting you. Hold the Skip Key (an option, None by default) to stay where you fell. Off by default. |
| Auto Screenshot | Takes a screenshot when you level up, earn an achievement, or defeat a boss, and can for good loot, reputation, PvP ranks, titles, battlegrounds, and deaths. Can hide the interface for the shot, and for the ones you take with the Screenshot key too, and can show your /played time when you level up. Off by default. |

releases.changelog:
Added
• Chat Levels: a new module that shows each player's level before their name in chat, colored like a quest of that level. Forever++ remembers players you group with, your guild and friends, your /who results, and players you see nearby, so the level shows for players far away too. Off by default.
• Class Colors: the new Offline Friends option (on by default) colors offline friends in the friends list by the class Forever++ last saw them as.
• Gear Probe: a new Run button under Testing in the Debug module's settings (and /fpp gearprobe) that saves what the client says about your gear, its item comparison, your talents, and your stats, for the developers.
• Item Tooltips: the new Disenchant line (off by default) shows what disenchanting green, blue, and purple gear gives on average, priced from Auction Prices while that's on, or else the material it most likely gives. Hold Shift for every outcome and its chance.
• Item Tooltips: the new Color Stats option (on by default) shows each stat on gear in its own color, including Equip: bonuses like hit and spell power.
• Item Tooltips: Auction Prices can use Auctionator's prices instead of scanning: turn on Use Auctionator's Prices. Your own saved prices are kept for when you turn it off.
• Macros: a new module that makes macros shared by your characters, each with its own checkbox, and deletes them when they're turned off. The first is Smart Buff: it casts the buff your friendly target (or you) should get from you at the best rank you know, skips buffs they already have or a stronger one, buffs you instead when they can't get anything from you and says why, and warns in combat when it can't change to fit a new target. Off by default.
• Minimap Button: the new Swap Clicks option (on by default) opens the quick toggles with a click and settings with a right-click, and Error Keys on Left-Click picks which click the error keys go on. Menu Side opens the quick toggles to the left or right of the cursor.
• Upgrade Arrows: a new module that puts Blizzard's green arrow on gear that beats what you wear, judged by stat weights for your class and main talent tree (or one you pick, with a Feral Bear profile for Druids). It marks your bags and bank, merchants, loot and loot rolls, the best quest reward, and the auction house, each with its own checkbox. A ring is judged against your weaker ring and a two-hander against both hands. Pick the arrow's corner, size, and padding, and show the percentage beside it or in the tooltip. Options show every item's score, mark worse gear with a red arrow, judge gear up to 5 levels above yours, leave profession tools and the reagent bag unmarked, and hide small differences. The weights start from a template per talent tree, and the Stat Weights page (/fpp weights) has a slider per stat, per profile, with Import and Export of Pawn strings. Off by default.
Changed
• Item marks, tints, and tooltip lines do much less work, so bags open more smoothly while leveling.
• Auto Stow: also puts away weapons you draw yourself, once they've been out for the Delay. Pressing Sheath starts the Delay again.
• Auto Weapon Buff: using a stone, oil, poison, or lure from an action bar puts it straight on your weapon too. Not in combat.
• Chat Copy: the window looks like Forever++'s other windows.
• Item Tooltips: Sell Price also shows on quest reward tooltips, so you can see what each choice sells for.
• Minimap Node Icons: costs much less while you play: it checks the minimap about once a second instead of ten times, and does nothing while Find Herbs and Find Minerals are off. A new dot may take a moment longer to get its icon.
• Profiler: also times work modules put off for a moment, like redrawing bag marks.
• Quest Tracker: the background is a little darker by default, 40% instead of 30%, unless you set its Opacity yourself.
• Settings: a module's warnings and limits sit in a gray line under its description on the Modules page.…

Added
• AddOns List: the new AddOn Sets option (off by default) adds a Sets dropdown beside Disable All, to save which addons are on under a name and turn that set back on later.
• Auto Decline: the new Guild Invites and Guild Charters options (off by default) turn down guild invites and requests to sign a guild charter, even from friends and guildmates.
• Comprehend Scrolls: a new module for Mages: right-click a scroll you read with Comprehension in your bags to cast Comprehend Scroll on it, without opening the spellbook. Not in combat. On by default; it does nothing for characters without the spell.
• Combat Alert: the new Play Sound option (off by default) plays the raid warning sound as you enter combat and a soft chime as you leave, for when you're looking somewhere else.
• Fishing Cast: the new Louder Bobber option (off by default) turns sound effects up and music down while you fish, so the splash is easy to hear, and puts your own volumes back after you stop, even after a reload or disconnect mid-cast.
• Item Tooltips: the new Repair Cost line (off by default) shows what repairing damaged gear costs, on gear you wear or carry, without a merchant's repair cursor.
• Flight Timer: the new Sound on Landing option (off by default) plays the ready check sound a few seconds before you land, on a flight you've taken before, so you can tab out on long flights.
• Forever Quest Icons: the new Quest Details option (on by default) puts the icon after the quest's name at the top of its details, in the quest window and on the map.
• Minimap Node Icons: a new module that puts the herb's or ore's own icon on each tracking dot on the minimap while Find Herbs or Find Minerals is on. Off by default. Its Tint Unusable option (off by default) turns an icon red while your skill is too low to gather it, and Gray Out Trivial (off by default) turns it gray once gathering it no longer raises your skill.
• NPC Nameplates: the new Skip Pets, Skip Totems, and Skip Companions options (off by default) leave players' pets and minions, totems, or companions with Blizzard's own nameplate instead of a name and title.
• Profiler: a new page in Settings (/fpp profile) that records how much CPU each module takes, heaviest first, beside Forever++'s total CPU and memory. A module made of parts folds open to show what each part takes. Nothing is timed until you press Record.
• Quest Levels: a new module that shows a quest's level before its name, like the quest log's [12], in a quest giver's list and at the top of the quest's details. On by default. Its Color by Difficulty option (off by default) colors the level gray through red by how it compares with yours.
• Quest Tracker: the new Current Zone Only option (off by default) tracks only the quests of the zone you're in, and tracks the others again when you get there. The quest your map follows always shows.
• Talent Planner: the new Level-Up Reminder option (off by default) says in chat which talent your plan takes next when you gain a talent point.
• Tooltips: the new Hide Health Bar option (off by default) hides the green health bar under player and NPC tooltips.
• Unusable Items Tint: the new Auction House and Loot options (off by default) tint red the items you can't use in the auction house's search results, and in the loot window and on loot rolls.
• Waylaid Crates: a new module for filling Waylaid Crates. Its Waylaid Crates entry in the auction house's categories lists every item your crates still need, less what's already in your bags and bank.
• Waypoints: the new Follow Selected Quest option (on by default) points the arrow to the quest selected on the map instead of your map pin, and back to the pin when no quest is selected. Its Show Quest Name option (on by default) shows the quest's name under the distance.
• Waypoints: the new Point to Corpse option (on by default) points the arrow to your corpse while you're a ghost, ahead of a quest or your map pin, and back to them once you're alive.…

Fixed
• Item Tooltips: Waylaid Crate Costs shows each bundle's price again, instead of No price, which 0.8.2 broke.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/xIGBClutchIx/ForeverPlusPlus/compare/v0.8.3...v0.8.4

Fixed
• Auto Weapon Buff: right-clicking a stone, oil, poison, or lure in your bags puts it on your weapon again, which 0.8.2 broke.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/xIGBClutchIx/ForeverPlusPlus/compare/v0.8.2...v0.8.3

Changed
• Auto Weapon Buff: when no equipped weapon can take the item, like a weightstone with only blades, it says so in red at the top of the screen instead of bringing up a cursor. On by default; turn it off with Warn When No Weapon Fits.
• Buff Timers: Show Clock has an Under 1 Minute choice, for a clock only on auras about to run out.
• Character Window: the new Equipped Weapon Skills option (on by default) colors the Skills tab's bars green for the weapons you have equipped, instead of blue.
• Chat History: no longer saves whispers, so they aren't written to your saved settings file.
• Console Variables: laid out like the Modules page: Changed, All, and the game's own categories on the left, each with how many match the search, and their console variables beside it with each one's help text under its name. The Changed group replaces the Changed Only checkbox.
• Item Tooltips: the new Waylaid Crate Costs option shows beside each bundle a Waylaid Crate takes what buying it costs at the auction house, from your scanned prices. It can go under each bundle instead, or be turned off.
• Quest Tracker: the new Sort by Level option (off by default) lists tracked quests by level, lowest or highest first, instead of in the order you tracked them. It waits for combat to end.
• Settings: the Changelog page lists the releases on the left, like the Modules page, with the selected one's notes beside it in larger text. Releases since the version you last saw are marked NEW, and a search box shows only the changes that mention what you type.
• Talent Planner: counts the Legacy perk Talented: with it, plans get talent points from level 5 instead of 10, still 51 at most.
• World Map: Points of Interest draws spirit healers as a glowing spirit instead of a tombstone, so they aren't mistaken for your corpse.
Fixed
• Already Known: the Tint look no longer turns white the red icons of merchant items you can't use, and the bags only look up items that can be known, like recipes, mounts, and pets.
• Auto Decline: a friend or guildmate you let through gets Blizzard's usual invite popup again instead of one showing only their name, and a declined group finder invite closes its popup too.
• Auto Screenshot: a second shot right after another no longer shows the interface with Hide Interface on, and a shot the game never reports no longer stops the ones after it.
• Auto Weapon Buff: a window over your bags no longer has its clicks taken by a stone, oil, poison, or lure under it.
• Buff Timers: never shows a negative time, like -1:59, on an aura about to go away.
• Commands: /rl and /clear are left to another addon that has them even after you've typed a slash command, and turning one on says so in chat.
• Currency Bar: stays on screen on smaller screens, and Reset Position puts it back where it starts.
• Error Catcher: a link or color in an error shows as plain text in its chat message, and it keeps the last 100 errors with shorter stacks, so its saved file stays small.
• Flight Timer: turning Bar on during a flight shows the bar for the rest of it.
• Hide Beta Feedback: turning it off puts the quest windows' feedback alert back as it was.
• Hide Filter Reset: turning it off gives the mouse back only to the parts that had it before.
• Item Tooltips: your own auction house searches keep an item's lowest price instead of the last one listed.
• Player Nameplates: a player who turns hostile, like in a duel, gets Blizzard's own nameplate back, health bar and all. So does an NPC that turns hostile with NPC Nameplates on.
• Player Nameplates: puts your game settings back at login if it was turned off in combat just before a reload. So do NPC Nameplates, Auto Dismount, and World Map's Coordinates.
• Quest Nameplates: an objective that needs 100 of something shows as 37/100, not 37%. Creatures that showed up during a fight get their quest icon once it's over.
• Recipe Colors: turning it off clears the tint from every recipe row, not only the ones on screen.…

Changelog2.7.0New
• Chat module: extras on top of Blizzard's chat windows, on their own Chat settings page. Web addresses become clickable links that open a box to copy from; a copy icon at the right end of the tab row (or /tempus copychat) opens the selected window's text for copying; recent lines are saved and shown again after a reload or relog; timestamps can be set to 24-hour, 12-hour or off; and tabs and buttons can hide until the mouse is over the window. Lines the game hides during boss fights and Mythic+ runs are passed through untouched, because addons cannot read, search or save them. If Prat is loaded, switch off its matching modules so lines are not linked or stamped twice.
• Damage meter skin: Blizzard's built-in damage meter gets a Tempus panel, a flat title bar with recoloured buttons and dropdowns, flat bars with the class colours kept, and Tempus fonts and scrollbars (Skins > Damage meter, with an opacity slider). Applies after a reload.
• Gathering node icons: ore and herb spots on the minimap get a small icon of what they are (Minimap > Gathering nodes). The game does not tell addons what its own tracking blips are, so Tempus learns a node when you mine or pick it (the icon is the first item looted). A node you gathered recently is shown dim until it has probably respawned (the game cannot say whether a node is up). The list starts empty and fills as you gather.
• Tempus theme: a new look and the default for new profiles. Panels get an edge and a soft glow in your accent colour, a faint light along the top, and Tempus's own bar texture and the Inter font. Pick it under Appearance > Theme; the bar texture and font are separate choices there too.
• Combat colour: the accent switches to its own colour while you are in combat, so the whole interface shows when a fight starts (Appearance, on by default). There is also a new Class colour accent.
• Recent damage: on unit frames, nameplates and party and raid frames, a hit shows as a red chunk that drains away behind the health bar ("Show recent damage" on each page).
• Animations: the settings window, bags and the target frame fade in; your player frame glows and pulses red below a health threshold (Unit frames > General); cooldown icons flash when they are ready again; and dispellable debuffs make a group frame's tint breathe. Appearance > Animations turns them all off.
• Focus frame: a Tempus unit frame for your focus, with its own cast bar (Unit frames > Focus). Shown on clients that have a focus.
• Interrupt-aware cast bars: target and focus cast bars turn amber while your interrupt (Kick, Pummel, Shield Bash, Counterspell, Earth Shock, Spell Lock) is cooling down, and a mark at the bar's end shows you can interrupt now. Uninterruptible casts get a grey shield and edge, and an interrupted cast flashes.
• Automation module (General > Automation): accepts quests and hands in finished ones (it never chooses between rewards or pays gold, and Shift skips it), hides repeated red errors such as "Ability is not ready yet", loots everything at once when auto-loot is on, and an optional AFK screen fades the interface and turns the camera while you are away.
• Tidier minimap buttons: the tray and hide-until-mouseover now also catch addon buttons that do not use LibDBIcon (Healium, TalentsForeverBook, the ForeverUtilities class helpers and others), and addon buttons lose Blizzard's round gold ring for a flat square Tempus edge (Minimap > Square addon buttons). Two new Addon buttons choices, Row under the map and Column on the left, line every addon button up 1px apart along the map, always visible.
• Minimap footer: the clock and coordinates move into a slim bar under the map, and addon buttons line up in a row beneath it (or a column on the map's left), 1px apart; click the footer to fold the row away. Blizzard's zone text (where Questie writes its own coordinates) no longer shows next to Tempus's.…
addons.description:
A complete World of Warcraft interface in one clean look: buff timers, unit frames, nameplates, party and raid frames, action bars, searchable combined bags, a square minimap, an info bar, a combat strip (Combat Pulse), and skins for Blizzard's windows. Every part is a module you can turn off.

Built for the new Classic client (interface 16001), where the game hides health, auras and range from addons in combat. Tempus is written around that: hidden values go straight from the game into bars, text and colours, and auras are drawn by the game's own aura containers, so everything keeps updating mid-fight.
Screenshots
| Nameplates | Party & raid frames |
|---|---|
| | |
| Buffs & debuffs | Action bars & info bar |
| | |
| Unit frames | |
| | |
Modules
• Buffs & Debuffs: icon or bar timers, a watch list for buffs you never want to forget, expiry warnings, click to recast or cancel.
• Unit Frames: player, target, target-of-target and pet, with cast bars, portraits, combo points and live target auras.
• Nameplates
• Colours for threat (tank or damage role), execute range, class and reaction.
• Con at a glance: a coloured strip, relative level (+3 / -2), elite pips or a 1-5 danger rating; grey mobs shrink and fade.
• Cast bars that show when a cast can be interrupted, your own interrupt with its cooldown, and who stopped a cast.
• Alerts for spells on your watch list, and a purple edge on enemies carrying a buff you can dispel or steal.
• Your debuffs, purgeable buffs and crowd control.
• Party & Raid
• Healer-ready frames: range fading, incoming heals and absorbs, and dispellable debuffs with a coloured tint.
• Your HoTs with timers, role and leader icons, aggro borders, and a raid grid for up to 40.
• Built-in click-casting with starting bindings for Druid, Priest, Shaman and Paladin; Clique also works.
• Mouseover keybinds: hover a frame and press a key (up to 8 per class) to cast on that player, in combat too.
• Drag the corner grip on an unlocked party or raid box to resize the frames, or pick a Compact, Standard or Large preset.
• Party and raid frames can list tanks and healers first.
• Cooldowns: a row of icons with cooldown swipes for spells you pick, plus your trinkets.
• Combat Pulse: one compact strip that gathers the fight. The layered DPS bar from Blizzard's damage meter (live, your peak, group top) and a thin swing line, plus small cues that appear only when they matter: an interruptible target cast (with your interrupt's cooldown), a buff you can purge, threat trouble and the execute range. Three modes: Minimal (urgent cues only), Standard (DPS, swing and cues) and Full (everything, including peak and group top numbers). Each signal can be switched off; the threat role and execute threshold follow the Nameplates settings. Swing timing needs the Swing timer module. A test mode shows every cue out of combat.
• Vendor: sells grey items and repairs gear when a merchant opens.
• Bags: combines carried bags and personal bank storage, with instant multi-word search, native item interactions, filter chips, a bag bar, item level and upgrade marks, cooldowns, a gold and currency footer, and grid or automatic category views with foldable sections and your own custom categories. It also remembers every character's bags and bank: the Alts button browses them, even offline, and item tooltips show what your other characters hold. If another bag addon is enabled, Tempus asks which one should own the bags for that character.
• Profiles: share your settings as a text string (Export / Import on the Profiles page).
• Action Bars: restyled bars with fading, hotkeys and range colouring, plus a movable, restyled micro menu and bag buttons.…

• Tidier minimap buttons: the tray and hide-until-mouseover now also catch addon buttons that do not use LibDBIcon (Healium, TalentsForeverBook, the ForeverUtilities class helpers and others), and addon buttons lose Blizzard's round gold ring for a flat square Tempus edge (Minimap > Square addon buttons). Two new Addon buttons choices, Row under the map and Column on the left, line every addon button up 1px apart along the map, always visible.
• Minimap footer: the clock and coordinates move into a slim bar under the map, and addon buttons line up in a row beneath it (or a column on the map's left), 1px apart; click the footer to fold the row away. Blizzard's zone text (where Questie writes its own coordinates) no longer shows next to Tempus's.…

Changelog2.6.0New
• Native Bags module: combined carried bags and personal/reagent bank windows with instant multi-word search, native item interactions and sorting, plus grid and automatic category views. Filter chips (gear, consumables, quest, junk), a bag bar that highlights or isolates one bag, item level and bind-on-equip tags, upgrade arrows, cooldowns, durability tint, and a footer with slots, currencies and gold. Category sections fold when you click their headers, items sort by quality and item level, and Tag lets you build your own categories. New installs enable it; upgraded profiles keep it off until enabled. When another bag addon is active, Tempus asks which one should own the bags for that character.
• Other characters in Bags: Tempus saves what each character carries and keeps in the bank and reagent bank. Alts in the bag header opens a menu of every saved character and storage, shown in the same window (read-only, with search, filters, grid and category views). Your own bank is listed there too, so you can browse it away from the banker. Item tooltips gain a line per character, such as Bags 4 Bank 12. The bank saves while it is open; characters appear after you log into them once. Turn it off, or forget the other characters, on the Bags page.
• Mouseover keybinds for healers: hover a party or raid frame and press a key to cast on that player, in combat too. Up to 8 per class, with Shift, Ctrl or Alt (Party & raid frames > Click-casting).
• Resize group frames by dragging: unlock the UI and drag the grip in the corner of the party or raid box; the frame width and height follow the settings sliders.
• Group frame size presets: Compact, Standard and Large set frame sizes, spacing, text and aura sizes for party and raid in one click (Party & raid frames > General).
• Minimap button tray: "Addon buttons" on the Minimap page can now collect every addon minimap button into a tray. Right-click the Tempus button, now a square in the map's lower right corner, to open the grid of buttons; left-click still opens settings. The tray closes when you move away. Around the edge and Hide until mouseover still work as before.
• Hide names on group frames: "Show player names" on the Party and Raid pages turns names off for a compact grid of bars and health text.
• Party frames by role: the party can list tank, healer, then damage (Party > Arrange by); party order is still available.
• Combat Pulse bar scale: choose Auto or a Fixed maximum DPS for the end of the bar (General > Combat Pulse). In combat the game hides DPS, so Auto can only size the bar from earlier readable fights and early-fight bursts can fill it; a fixed maximum avoids the guesswork.
Changed
• New profiles show health percent on group frames by default.
• Changing the accent colour recolours the settings window, move boxes and bags straight away; some Blizzard skins still need a reload.
• The bag bar and micro menu lose Blizzard's bronze frame, and their buttons are one size.
• Dropdown menus widen to fit their longest label, open toward the side of the screen with room, and scroll when the list is long.
Fixed
• Vendor: the "sold grey items for" total was always 0 on clients without the old GetItemInfo. It now reads prices from C_Item.GetItemInfo and falls back to the gold you actually received.
• Bags: moving a window by its body now saves its position, and stacks of 1000 or more show as 1k.
2.5.0New
• Combat Pulse: one compact combat strip. It combines a layered DPS bar from Blizzard's damage meter (purple to your live DPS, gold to your peak, red to the group's top), a thin swing line, and small cues for an interruptible target cast, a buff you can purge, threat trouble and the execute range. Choose Minimal (urgent cues only), Standard or Full; every signal can be switched off, and threat and execute follow your Nameplates settings. Settings, a test mode and reset position are under General > Combat Pulse. Unlock the UI to move it.

addons.description:
Formerly Pandy Guild Management: same addon, same folder, same saved data.

Bugs, ideas or questions? Join the Discord
(or type /pgm discord in game).

A guild manager and group finder for Midnight and WoW Forever, built for big
raiding guilds:
• Guild overview: class, race, level and activity breakdowns, professions,
Mythic+ spread and a vitality score for the whole guild
• Raid teams: built automatically from the tags in your guild notes, with
roles, Core/Trial/Bench, raid-buff coverage and per-team attendance
• Guild sync: teams, raid nights and alt links shared with everyone running
the addon, editable only by officers and raid leaders
• Alts: detected from alt ranks, guild-note formats and your own account
• Raid attendance: recorded automatically, no setup
• Play-time activity: average and peak online, the guild's busiest times,
and when each member usually plays
• Roster, professions and history: searchable, sortable, with safe
promote/demote buttons

Type /pgm (or /pandy) to open it, click the panda button on the minimap,
or click it in Blizzard's AddOns button there. If the window ever ends up
somewhere you can't drag it back from, /pgm reset puts it back in the
middle at normal size.

The minimap button can be dragged around the minimap's edge, and minimap
button collectors pick it up. Right-click it for Settings, where it can be
turned off (or /pgm minimap). It's also a LibDataBroker launcher, so
Titan Panel, ChocolateBar, ElvUI data texts and other broker displays can
show it, with how many guildies are online.

addons.description:
Less clicking. More playing.

Commodum is a World of Warcraft addon that makes everyday gameplay more convenient. It handles routine tasks and lets you adjust parts of the interface to suit your preferences.

> ⚠️ Important! This addon requires Arcane Wizard: Library. See Installation & Quick Start for installation details.
Key Feature
Quality of Life Tweaks - Enable the quality-of-life tweaks you want to use and configure them individually.
Features
Individual features and display options can be configured in the addon settings. Commodum supports an account profile and character profiles.
User Interface
• Keeps the in-game clock in 24-hour format, including after login or a UI reload.
• Automatically shows the faction whose reputation just changed on the reputation bar.
• Hides loot notifications for items, gold, and personal currencies, each separately.\*

\ This feature is only available in Retail.*
Merchant Actions
• Automatically repairs all damaged items using personal funds when a repair merchant window opens.
• Automatically sells sellable poor-quality (gray) items from the bags when a merchant window opens; locked items are skipped.
• At merchants, automatically sells items marked by right-clicking while holding a modifier key, skipping locked and unsellable items.

Arc Auras3.1.7
Clearer option names, percent signs, a Reincarnation template for Shamans, and an Export selection fix.
Improvements
• Shorter option names - Rows inside a text's box no longer repeat its name (Font, not Duration text font).
• Percent boxes - Sliders that set a percent show the % sign.
• Clearer sizes - An icon's Width and Height say what 0 does: the group's size, or 36 for an icon outside a group.
• Reincarnation template - Shamans get a Reincarnation square in Add > Spell Cooldown that tracks the ID its cooldown really runs on, so the icon shows it right after you come back.
Bug Fixes
• Export selection - Opens the Export tab with the string ready, whatever tab you had open.
• Defaults page - The line about icons that keep their own value no longer gets cut off.
3.1.6
Pick what you import from the Cooldown Manager, and fixes for totem icons and glows.
New Features
• Pick what you import from the Cooldown Manager - From Cooldown Manager now opens a window where you tick the spells and buffs you want, and choose Aura or Totem only for each Tracked Buff.
Improvements
• Smooth window dragging - Text and borders no longer jitter while you drag or resize a window. Thanks Laxx for the assist!
Bug Fixes
• Totem icons - Call Dreadstalkers shows the Dreadstalkers again, not the Charhound, and Summon Demonic Tyrant extends it.
• Glows - Unticking a glow no longer locks its options; you can tick it back on.
3.1.5
Stealth and dead-target looks, an active border, and performance and bug fixes.
New Features
• Own looks: Stealthed and Target is dead - A look can wait on being stealthed, or on your target being dead (a finisher greyed on a corpse).
• Active border - The border takes its own color while the aura is up, a skin's border too.
Improvements
• Performance - Arc Auras does less work in the background.
Bug Fixes
• Bug fixes - General fixes, including issues around cutscenes.
3.1.4
Ring bars, the aura picker for bars, and an Add window that always fits.
New Features
• Ring bars - Aura and cooldown bars can be a ring that drains around, with its own thickness, start and border.
• Aura picker for bars - Aura bars get the same Cooldown Manager squares as aura icons when you make them.
Improvements
• Aura picker - Folds after you pick an aura; click its title to open it again.
• Aura bars with several IDs - The Tracking tab shows and edits every ID the bar tracks.
Bug Fixes
• Add window - The form no longer runs out of the window under a long aura list.
• Texture rings - A texture shown as a ring now goes all the way around.
• Big setups - Importing several characters from Arc UI, or keeping layouts for many characters, no longer slows the game to a crawl: each character only builds what it can load.
• Graphics memory - Icons, glows and bars that are not on screen no longer hold on to graphics memory.
3.1.3
Arc Pings and Kick Assist modules, Custom Icons in one place, items that show while equipped, and charge spell fixes.
New Features
• Arc Pings and Kick Assist - Now modules on the Modules page, off until you switch them on; the Arc UI import brings their setup.
• Show while equipped - Item icons for trinkets and other gear can show only while worn (Arc UI's Hide when unequipped imports as this).
• Import groups only - The Arc UI import can bring your layouts and groups in empty.

addons.description:
Accountant Classic helps you track the gold your World of Warcraft characters earn and spend.

It records session activity and long-term totals, helping you understand where your money comes from and where it goes. Track income and expenses from vendors, loot, quests, repairs, mail, trades, and other in-game sources.
Features
• Track gold earned and spent during each play session.
• Keep running income and expense totals for each character.
• Review daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly summaries.
• Switch quickly between characters to review their financial history.
• Store character data separately by realm, including characters with the same name on different realms.
• View location summaries to see where you earned or spent the most gold.
• Use an optional floating money frame to monitor your current money in real time.
• Open the main window from the minimap button, a key binding, the floating money frame, or the /acc command.
Usage
Open Accountant Classic by using one of the following methods:
• Click the Accountant Classic minimap button.
• Type /acc in the chat window.
• Assign a key binding in the WoW Key Bindings settings.
• Right-click the floating money frame, if it is enabled.

The floating money frame displays your current money while you play. Right-click it to open the Accountant Classic window.
Character and Realm Data
Accountant Classic keeps financial data separate for each character and realm.

This means characters with the same name on different realms do not share records. You can switch between saved characters from the Accountant Classic interface to compare their income, expenses, and historical summaries.

addons.changelog:
023
Bags that fit what is in them, and sorting you can do from the bag.
Bags
• Columns is now the most the bag uses, not what it always uses. The bag
is as narrow as it can be without anything taking an extra row, so it no
longer carries empty space down its right-hand side.
• Rows before widening is gone. The bag no longer grows past your Columns
setting; one too full for the screen scrolls instead.
• Categorize mode keeps the bag's shape. It used to widen until every
category sat on one line. Now it stays the width it always is and simply
gets longer.
• Arrange your categories from the bag. In Categorize mode (middle-click
the bag's portrait) every heading has Hide / Show and a pair of
arrows, and + New category at the bottom makes a new one. A hidden
category keeps its items but only appears in Categorize mode.
• Fixed: moving a category up sometimes did nothing.
• Fixed: the heading lines stopped short after the bag changed width.
Unit frames
• Choose how names read on each bar: full name, first name or last name.
It is under Text when you select a bar in BazUI Edit Mode, and on the Bars
page. Anything without a last name shows its first name. Forever only -
retail has no surnames.
Floating Text
• Fixed: other people's fights showed up as yours. Outgoing numbers are
now only what happens to your target while you are fighting, and each hit
shows once. In a group, a number on your target can still be a party
member's - the game does not say who dealt a hit.
Also fixed
• **Ticking a box in BazUI's settings no longer makes the whole interface
stutter.**
• **The quest log could be dragged off the map, and then vanished after a
reload.** It is part of the map again and moves with it.
addons.description:
The Baz Suite as one addon, built for World of Warcraft: Forever.

BazUI replaces a stack of separate addons (BazCore, BazWidgetDrawers, BazChat, BazBags and parts of BazBars) with a single install: one options window, one profile system, one skin.

Status: in development. Two clients are supported: WoW: Forever, which BazUI is built for, and retail, which is kept working alongside it. No Classic flavour is supported. The Codex is Forever only.
Modules
| Module | Source | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core | BazCore | Ported |
| Drawers | BazWidgetDrawers + BazWidgets + BazBrokerWidget | Ported (Minimap, Minimap Buttons, Info Bar, Zone Text, Quest Tracker, 20 pack widgets, LibDataBroker feeds as widgets; delve, Great Vault, currency and pet-journal widgets dropped) |
| Chat | BazChat | Ported (tabbed chat replacement: channels per tab, timestamps, history, copy, combat log) |
| Bags | BazBags | Ported (Classic bags plus keyring; categories, pinning, search) |
| Bars | BazBars | Ported (bars, spells, items, macros, mounts, equipment sets, flyouts, keybinds; no toys or pets) |
| Unit Frames | new (written by Codex) | Built (health, power, casting, experience and reputation as bars you create, floating or docked to an action bar or to each other; no portraits) |
| Auras | new | Built (four rows of buffs and debuffs that float or dock to any bar, left/center/right aligned, secure right-click cancel) |
| Notifications | BazNotificationCenter | Ported (toasts, history panel, bell; 15 sources, no Mythic+, Vault, rares, collections or talking head) |
| Micro Menu | new | Built (Blizzard's micro buttons on a movable bar as round ring-framed icons) |
First run
A fresh install starts with the BazUI layout: player frame centered above the bars, target frame at the top, a 14-slot bar along the bottom with a 6-slot bar either side (Blizzard's own action bar is hidden; drag your abilities onto the BazUI bars), bags docked right in categories mode, chat bottom-left, the micro menu top center, and the minimap drawer on the right. Every piece can be moved in BazUI Edit Mode or changed in Options > AddOns > BazUI. Updating never changes existing settings.
Commands
• /baz (or /bazui, /bui) opens the options window.
• /baz profile , /baz profiles, /baz default manage profiles.
• /bwd toggle|show|hide|open |list drives the drawer.
• /bbg (or /bazbags) toggles the bag panel; /bbg sort, /bbg categorize.
• /bb (or /bazbars) for bars: create, delete, duplicate, export, import, scale, padding, reset.
• /bazframes opens the Unit Frames options; /bazauras opens the Auras options (/bazauras reset resets the layout).
• /bnc toggles the notification panel; /bnc dnd, /bnc clear, /bnc history, /bnc test.
• /bazmicro opens the Micro Menu options; /bazmicro reset moves the bar back to the top center.
• /bazchat (or /bc) for chat: copy, clear, lock, unlock, restoredefaults; /cc clears the active tab.
