releases.changelog:
023
Bags that fit what is in them, and sorting you can do from the bag.
Bags
• Columns is now the most the bag uses, not what it always uses. The bag
is as narrow as it can be without anything taking an extra row, so it no
longer carries empty space down its right-hand side.
• Rows before widening is gone. The bag no longer grows past your Columns
setting; one too full for the screen scrolls instead.
• Categorize mode keeps the bag's shape. It used to widen until every
category sat on one line. Now it stays the width it always is and simply
gets longer.
• Arrange your categories from the bag. In Categorize mode (middle-click
the bag's portrait) every heading has Hide / Show and a pair of
arrows, and + New category at the bottom makes a new one. A hidden
category keeps its items but only appears in Categorize mode.
• Fixed: moving a category up sometimes did nothing.
• Fixed: the heading lines stopped short after the bag changed width.
Unit frames
• Choose how names read on each bar: full name, first name or last name.
It is under Text when you select a bar in BazUI Edit Mode, and on the Bars
page. Anything without a last name shows its first name. Forever only -
retail has no surnames.
Floating Text
• Fixed: other people's fights showed up as yours. Outgoing numbers are
now only what happens to your target while you are fighting, and each hit
shows once. In a group, a number on your target can still be a party
member's - the game does not say who dealt a hit.
Also fixed
• **Ticking a box in BazUI's settings no longer makes the whole interface
stutter.**
• **The quest log could be dragged off the map, and then vanished after a
reload.** It is part of the map again and moves with it.

022
Settings save the ordinary way again.

WoW: Forever used to forget every addon's settings when you logged out, so
BazUI kept its own somewhere the game did remember. Blizzard has fixed that,
and BazUI now saves just like any other addon.

Nothing for you to do: your layout, bars, profiles and positions all carry
over.
Changed
• Nameplates for friendly pets. Pets, minions, guardians and totems on
your side can have nameplates like everything else. Whether they get one
is the game's own setting, and it starts off, so the switches for it are
now on the Nameplates page under Friendly pets.
• The Codex is Forever only. It is built around Forever's own content,
so it no longer appears on retail.
Fixed
• The Legacy button on the micro menu had no icon. It now wears the
same art as the Codex's Legacy tab.
Removed
• The settings report in chat at every login.
• /baz sv and /baz persist. Both were only there for the old saving
problem.
• "Other addons' settings" on the Quality of Life page. Those switches
kept other addons' settings through the same problem, and those addons
remember their own now.

021
**A new module, cast bars on nameplates, and several things that had quietly
never worked.**
Floating Text — new module
Numbers rising off the fight: what you hit for, what hit you, what you
healed, and the misses and dodges in between, in BazUI's own font.
• Two areas, Incoming on the left and Outgoing on the right, each placed
by dragging it in Edit Mode. Which one a number lands in is not a guess:
the game says who took the hit.
• Colour by direction, which is the thing a screen full of white numbers
cannot tell you — your damage and damage to you are different colours, and
so are heals in each direction. Damage schools override where a spell has
one.
• Crits drawn larger and optionally marked with stars, because size alone
only reads as a crit when there is an ordinary hit beside it.
• Merging, off by default, for when the same mob is hitting you four
times a second. Crits are never merged — folding one into a total throws
away exactly the thing you wanted to see.
• The game's own numbers can be turned off, both the scrolling text and
the ones drawn over the mob. Those are two different settings in the game
and turning one off leaves the other running, which is why this needs two
switches.

It starts off. It draws over the middle of the screen, and a module that
begins doing that unannounced is one you go hunting for the switch to.
Nameplate cast bars — new
A bar under the plate while a unit is casting, coloured by whether you can
do anything about it:
• Green — you can interrupt this, right now.
• Amber — you could, but your interrupt is still on cooldown.
• Red — this one cannot be interrupted by anyone.

Your interrupt comes from your spellbook rather than your class, so a
warrior gets Pummel or Shield Bash depending on what is in their hands, and a
druid only counts Feral Charge while in bear form. There is a spell-ID
override if yours is not on the list.

On a class with no interrupt — a hunter, a paladin — green never appears,
because there is nothing for it to mean. Casts show in a plain colour and
only the ones nobody can stop are marked red.
Fixed
• The dockable target cast bar never appeared. It asked whether the unit
was casting in a way the game refuses to answer for anyone but you, took
that refusal as "not casting", and stayed hidden forever. It works now, and
wears the same three interrupt colours as the nameplate bars.
• Raid target markers never showed. The skull, cross and square are
picked from a number the game will not hand over, and BazUI gave up rather
than draw the wrong one. The right symbol appears now.
• Six of the eight unit bar wordings collapsed into "current / max".
Name, Level, Name and level and Current all show properly again. The three
that need a percentage still cannot always have one, but each now falls
back to the nearest thing it can say rather than all of them landing on the
same answer.
• A unit's level vanished from its bar whenever the game would not let
the name and the level be joined together. Both show.
• Numbers in the aura rows could sit on top of each other — two hits in
the same instant rise at the same speed from the same line, so they stayed
exactly parallel. They are spaced apart in time now, and the rise
separates them.
Changed
• Cast bars, aura rows and floating text all follow your skin, including
when you change it.
• The manual and several settings descriptions were rewritten. A few had
drifted into explaining how things work rather than what you will see.

020
Your buffs and debuffs finally work during a fight.

This is the big one, and it needs a word of explanation because the fix is
not what you would expect.

On WoW: Forever, the moment a fight starts the game stops telling addons
anything at all about auras. Not "some auras" — every buff and every debuff,
on you and on your target, becomes unreadable. Ask anyway and the game
answers with an error.

So BazUI's aura rows froze. Whatever you happened to have when the fight
began stayed on screen, unchanging, until it ended. A debuff you applied
mid-fight never appeared at all — which, for a damage-over-time spell that
expires before the fight is over, meant it was never visible once.

There is no way to read that data. There is a way to show it.

The game ships an aura display system meant for addons to use. BazUI now
hands it a unit, a filter and somewhere to draw, and the game fills it in.
Nothing about your auras is ever read — which is exactly why it works
while everything else is refused.

What that means in practice:
• Debuffs on your target appear the moment you apply them, and their
timers count down properly.
• Buffs you gain mid-fight show up, instead of after it.
• Stack counts keep counting.
• Right-click still cancels one of your own buffs, in combat or out —
and it now cancels that specific aura rather than a position in the row,
so it can no longer cancel the wrong thing when something above it drops
off.
• Weapon enchants are a proper part of the row now instead of a
stand-in, with the game keeping their timers.

It looks identical to before. If anything misbehaves, **Let the game draw
the icons** at the top of Auras > General puts the old rows back, with no
reload needed.

One change worth knowing: the game deliberately does not tell an addon *how
many* auras there are, so a row can no longer shrink to fit its contents. It
holds the size you set it to, full or empty. Floating, you will not notice.
Docked in a drawer, an empty row now keeps its space.
Fixed
• Blizzard's action bar could come back with a taint on it. Hiding one of
the game's Edit Mode frames ran a pile of their own layout bookkeeping
while BazUI was the one asking, and one of their fields ended up marked as
ours. That is what was behind the blocked SetPointBase errors, and
probably the cooldown errors on the override bar too. BazUI now hides
those frames the plain way and touches none of their bookkeeping.
• Picking an ability up off a bar made Blizzard's bar flicker. It was
being hidden a frame late. Now it is hidden immediately, and suppressed
frames are made transparent as well as hidden — which also means a reload
during a fight no longer leaves the game's frames sitting visible until
the fight ends.
• Out-of-range coloring did nothing with "target where you're looking."
It only ever checked your hard target, and soft targeting does not set
one, so icons never dimmed for anyone playing that way.
• The "new slot" marker appeared on slots that already existed. Aim past
the end of a bar whose last slot is empty and it offered to add a slot on
top of one that was already there. It now only appears where a slot would
genuinely be created.
• **/baz persist said it could not tell what an addon saves, and gave an
example that read like a stutter.** It now says plainly which addons it
covers. It looks after a few that have actually been tested, and does not
guess at others — restoring the wrong table over a live one would break
the addon it was trying to help.
New
• /baz auras reports what the game will and will not let BazUI see
about auras right now, and what each row is holding. Run it in combat and
it explains, in words, why nothing is readable.
Changed
• A fresh install starts with an updated layout, including the nameplate
Focus settings added in 018, which had never made it into the starting
arrangement. Existing setups are untouched.

019
**The quest catalog is readable, and reloading mid-fight no longer looks like
the addon fell over.**
Fixed: the quest pages
• Descriptions were never shown. Every quest page fell back to nothing
where it should have fallen back to the catalog, so **4,306 quest
descriptions were sitting in the addon and reachable by nobody.** They are
on the page now.
• The header stays put. Title, facts line and rule are pinned; only the
quest scrolls under them. The rewards block scrolls with it instead of
being stranded.
• XP and coin moved up onto the Rewards heading, right-aligned — XP
first, because there is always XP and there is not always coin. The last
row used to be one number sitting alone.
• Fonts. Several lines were quietly resolving to the game's font instead
of yours.
• An objective that only repeats the summary is no longer printed twice.
• A quest with a summary and no story crashed the page. Ten of 4,316 rows
were affected.
• Profession bars read full when they were nowhere near it.
Fixed: reloading in combat
The game refuses almost everything an addon does to the interface while you
are fighting, so a /reload mid-fight comes back half-arranged. That part is
unavoidable. What was wrong was how it looked and how it recovered.
• A notice now says so, on the left of the screen, in words: nothing is
wrong, nothing needs fixing, it sorts itself the moment the fight ends.
Click to dismiss.
• **The minimap no longer leaves a piece of itself in the middle of the
screen.** It was coming back as a bare overlay with the tracking dots on
it. Nothing touches the minimap now until combat is clear.
• Blizzard's action bar no longer appears when the fight ends. It was
absent during combat and arrived the moment you were safe, which is
exactly backwards. BazUI was standing in the middle of Blizzard's own
show-the-bar function when it tried to hide it, and the game refused them
both.
Changed: the codex tabs
• The rail is in a sensible order. Today, Progress, then Quests —
which is the biggest page in the addon and was sixth — then the things you
are part-way through, then your gear, then the two pages about the game
rather than about you. Legacy, an archive of things that no longer exist,
was third.
• You can rearrange it. Hold a tab for half a second, it lights green,
drag it up or down. The same hold and drag that moves a widget inside a
drawer. Reset page order in the codex settings puts it back.
• The wishlist is a page of the Items tab, not a tab of its own. It is a
list of items and you read it while you are looking at items. Two buttons
at the top of that page switch between them.
New
• Hide TomTom's coordinates. Puts away the little block showing where you
are standing. TomTom's own setting is left alone, so turning this off gives
you the block back exactly as TomTom had it.
The manual
• A page for the Quests tab, which had none: the filters, the columns,
what a row does, and how to read Seen in game against Unconfirmed.
• Reloading in the middle of a fight has a page, as does **two Edit
Modes** — the game's moves the game's frames, BazUI's moves BazUI's, and
opening one closes the other.
• The micro menu's manual is gone. It is a widget now, so it is written
up with the widgets.
• Six other guides had drifted in a week and were corrected.

addons.description:
A standalone World of Warcraft: Forever addon (Interface: 16001, client 1.60.1) that shows
experience, reputation, honor, pet experience and skills in one "island" flush to the top
centre of the screen. Built from scratch for the Live mockup: no other
addon is required and no other addon's code, strings or art is used.

Pure Lua, no XML, no build step. The art shipped is the small 32-bit power-of-two TGAs in
Media/ (rounded corners, gloss, ring, disk, caution stripes, gear) plus the TTFs in
Media/Fonts/: Open Sans Bold/ExtraBold/Medium (shipped as UIFont-*) as the primary face
and Alegreya Sans as the fallback, with a final fallback to the game's Fonts\FRIZQT__.TTF.
The progress-bar texture comes from the game client (Interface\TargetingFrame\UI-StatusBar).

The bundled fonts are third-party open fonts and keep their own licences. Alegreya Sans and
Open Sans Medium are SIL OFL 1.1 (Media/Fonts/OFL.txt); Open Sans Bold and ExtraBold are
Apache License 2.0 (Media/Fonts/LICENSE-OpenSans-Apache-2.0.txt). See
Media/Fonts/CREDITS.txt for the per-file attribution.

Secret or missing values now drop only their own row, and the baseline keeps its last known number so later level-ups still have something to diff against.
• Merge pull request #7 from gridrek/smooth-kills-to-level
Smooth Kills to level with a recent-kill average and rested pool
• Merge pull request #6 from gridrek/fix-kill-parsing
Fix kill XP parsing so quest XP isn't counted as a kill
• Merge pull request #5 from gridrek/smooth-comet-pulse
Run comet pulse every frame instead of at 20 Hz
• Smooth Kills to level with a recent-kill average and rested pool
Kills to level divided the XP left by the last kill only, so mixing mob
levels made it jump (one level-5 mob at level 9 took it from ~70 to
~200). It now averages the last 10 kills at the current level.
The rested bonus is parsed out of each kill and the rested pool is spent
in the estimate instead (each kill is doubled until the pool runs out),
so the estimate doesn't double when rested runs out. Recent kills are
saved with the session so the estimate survives /reload, and reset on
level-up since mobs are worth a different amount at the new level.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Fix kill XP parsing so quest XP isn't counted as a kill
buildPattern escaped the "%" of %s/%d before converting them to captures,
so every kill pattern looked for literal parentheses and never matched.
All XP messages fell through to the digit fallback, which never yields a
mob name. As a result:
• any XP gain (including quest turn-ins) replaced the per-kill XP, so a
big quest made Kills to level drop to ~1
• kill streaks never counted real kills, and gain text never named the mob
Escape everything except "%", and map each format's captures explicitly
(mob name, amount). Only messages that name a mob update the per-kill XP.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Run comet pulse every frame instead of at 20 Hz
The idle comet sweep stepped itself with ns.After(0.05) and advanced by a
fixed 0.05s per step. Timers fire on the first frame past their delay, so
in practice it updated ~15 times per second at 60 fps and ran slower than
its configured timing, which looked choppy next to the per-frame pulses.
Step it on every frame and advance by real elapsed time (ns.animClock),
capped at 0.1s per frame so hitches don't skip the sweep. The step
callback is created once and reused to avoid per-frame closures.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

addons.description:
Tradeskill addon for WoW: Forever. It works out which crafts are worth making,
scans the auction house for the prices that answer depends on, and manages a
craft queue, a shopping list and a posting list around it.

Built without Ace3 or LibStub, because neither is known to work on Forever yet.
The small framework in Core/ is written for this addon instead, so it does not
have to wait for anyone else to update theirs.
Layout
| Folder | What is in it |
|---|---|
| Core/ | Slash commands, settings, checking what the game supports, saving your data between sessions, and spacing out requests to the auction house |
| Data/ | Everything read from the game: prices, auction scans, recipes, bags and bank, your own listings, vendor prices |
| Logic/ | Craft cost, profit, the queue, starting crafts, posting, and export/import |
| UI/ | Theme, reusable widgets, the main window, the auction house side panel, and the seven tabs |
| Probe/ | /bts probe, which checks what the running game actually supports instead of guessing |

Blackthornes_TS.toc lists every Lua file in load order. A file that is not in
it does not load, and WoW says nothing about it.

addons.changelog:
Add /simf as an alias for /sfexport and /simsforever, including save and clear.

The export popup now closes automatically after Ctrl+C, Cmd+C, or Ctrl+Insert, with a brief delay to let the game finish copying.

Checked with Lua 5.1 and mocked WoW UI events. In-game verification is still needed.
addons.description:
Exports WoW Forever character data for SimsForever.

Run /simf, /sfexport, or /simsforever to open the export. Press Ctrl+C to copy and close the window, then paste at SimsForever.

Exports equipped gear plus equippable gear in carried bags.
Some Notes
• Bank contents are included if the bank window is open.
• Current resources, spell costs, and pet spell details are added for diagnostics.
• SimsForever selects starting resources and uses internal spell and pet data.
• Unreadable optional fields are omitted without warnings.
• CurseForge packages version tags automatically.

addons.description:
Für WoW Forever 1.60.1.70425 / Interface 16001. Alle Funktionen liegen im einzigen Addon-Ordner ForeverTools: Händler & Taschen, Quests, Materialien, Paladin, GTFO, Threat Plates, Decursive, Anti Fett Finger und Auto Rank. Jedes Modul ist in der gemeinsamen Übersicht einzeln schaltbar.

HTML-Anleitung herunterladen – im Browser öffnen oder direkt an Freunde weitergeben. Die Quelldatei liegt unter Anleitung.html.
Für Freunde: einmal einrichten
1. ForeverTools.zip herunterladen und öffnen.
2. Den darin enthaltenen Ordner ForeverTools nach Interface\AddOns ziehen.
3. WoW vollständig neu starten und ForeverTools aktivieren. Fertig.

Die Datei liegt danach direkt unter Interface\AddOns\ForeverTools\ForeverTools.toc. Das fertige Paket enthält keinen zusätzlichen ForeverTools-main-Ordner. Menü: /ad, /forevertools oder das Schmiede-Symbol an der Minimap. Separate Installationen von Anti Fett Finger und Auto Rank sind nicht erforderlich.
Ein Update aktualisiert alles
Neu in 1.7.4: Der Update-Helfer wird nicht mehr durch unbestätigte Windows-Meldungen angehalten. Update.cmd prüft den tatsächlichen Start, erkennt bereits laufende ältere Helfer und zeigt Startfehler an. Protokolle liegen lokal unter %LOCALAPPDATA%\ForeverTools im Unterordner des Spielclients.

Seit 1.7.3: Das Funkeln der Quest-Gegner wurde entfernt. Ausrufezeichen, Fortschrittszähler und das Funkeln der Sammelobjekte bleiben erhalten.

Seit 1.7.0: Quest-Gegner erhalten ein gelbes Questzeichen mit kompaktem Fortschritt wie 2/7 über dem Namen. Quest-Sammelobjekte können funkeln und zeigen den Zähler beim Darüberfahren im Tooltip. Einstellungen: /ad → Quest-Gegner → Optionen. Die Funkeloption passt Umrandungen und bei Bedarf die Partikeldichte an; vorherige Werte werden beim Abschalten wiederhergestellt. Nach dem ersten Update einmal WoW vollständig neu starten.

Jägermunition: Unter /ad → Händler & Taschen → Optionen ist „Jäger: Köcher / Munitionsbeutel auffüllen“ standardmäßig aktiv. Beim Öffnen eines passenden Händlers kauft das Addon die beste Munition für eure Stufe und angelegte Fernkampfwaffe: Pfeile für Bogen/Armbrust, Kugeln für Schusswaffen. Es füllt nur den verfügbaren Platz im passenden Köcher/Munitionsbeutel und berücksichtigt Gold und Händlervorrat. Ohne passenden Beutel wird nichts gekauft. Umschalt beim Öffnen des Händlers gedrückt halten, um den Munitionskauf einmal auszusetzen.

Die Menü-Fußzeile zeigt den zuletzt geprüften GitHub-Stand.…

Das Funkeln der Quest-Gegner und die zugehörige Menüoption wurden entfernt. Das gelbe Ausrufezeichen, der Fortschrittszähler und das Funkeln der Quest-Sammelobjekte bleiben erhalten.

Prüfung: Alle 212 Tests erfolgreich. Nach dem Update die Windows-Fertigmeldung abwarten und im Spiel /reload eingeben.

Update-Aufträge bleiben erhalten, wenn der Windows-Helfer erst nach dem Klick startet oder neu gestartet wird. Nur erfolgreiche Updates werden als erledigt gespeichert.

Im Spiel erklärt ForeverTools jetzt den Ablauf: Windows-Meldung „Update fertig“ abwarten und danach nochmals /reload eingeben. Nach dem Laden wird der erfolgreiche Auftrag bestätigt.

Falls der bisherige Helfer nicht mehr aktualisiert: ForeverTools.zip über die bestehende Installation kopieren, den alten Update-Helfer über sein Symbol neben der Windows-Uhr beenden und Update.cmd im installierten ForeverTools-Ordner starten.

Prüfung: 216 Lua-Tests und Updater-Tests einschließlich verspätetem Start, Neustart und Downloadfehlern erfolgreich. Echter GitHub-Download mit Dateiprüfung ebenfalls geprüft.

Benötigte Quest-Gegner funkeln jetzt zusätzlich golden, auch im Kampf. Der Effekt verwendet dieselben Lichtpunkte wie die Quest-Sammelobjekte.
• Eigenes Häkchen unter /ad → Quest-Gegner → Optionen → Quest-Gegner ebenfalls funkeln lassen; standardmäßig aktiv.
• Mehrere benötigte Gegner können gleichzeitig funkeln. Tote Gegner und erfüllte Ziele werden nicht mehr markiert.
• Das Gegner-Funkeln ist unabhängig von Sammelobjekt-Funkeln und Tooltip-Zähler schaltbar. Ausrufezeichen und Fortschritt bleiben beim Abschalten des Funkelns sichtbar.
• Wiederverwendete Namensplaketten erhalten keine veralteten Effekte. Die Reichweite bleibt durch die Namensplaketten des Clients begrenzt.

Geprüft: 215 automatisierte Tests und alle Updater-Prüfungen. Die Darstellung des neuen Gegner-Funkelns ist im Spiel noch zu prüfen.

Installation: ForeverTools.zip entpacken und den enthaltenen Ordner ForeverTools nach Interface\AddOns kopieren. Bestehende Installationen können den Update-Button verwenden und anschließend /reload eingeben. Wer erstmals von einer Version vor 1.7.0 aktualisiert, sollte WoW für die nativen Sammelobjekt-Effekte einmal vollständig neu starten.

Quest-Gegner und Quest-Sammelobjekte sind jetzt in ForeverTools integriert.
• Gelbes Questzeichen mit kompaktem Fortschritt (z. B. 2/7) über benötigten Gegnern; erledigte Ziele verschwinden.
• Tötungsziele werden zusätzlich aus dem Questlog erkannt, ohne Anklicken.
• Funkeln für Quest-Sammelobjekte und Questzeichen mit Zähler im Objekt-Tooltip, unabhängig schaltbar unter /ad → Quest-Gegner → Optionen.
• Eigene Lichtpunkte an allen verfügbaren Questobjekt-Ankern; ergänzte native Hervorhebung und Partikeldichte. Die zuvor geänderten Einstellungen werden beim Abschalten wiederhergestellt.
• Diagnose: /ftquest und /ftquest sparkle.

Geprüft: 211 automatisierte Tests. Das Sammelobjekt-Funkeln wurde im Forever-Client bei „Pigmente für Farben“ bestätigt. Weitere Sammelquests sind nicht einzeln im Spiel geprüft. Reichweite und verfügbare Objekt-Anker bleiben durch den Client begrenzt.

Installation: ForeverTools.zip entpacken und den enthaltenen Ordner ForeverTools nach Interface\AddOns kopieren. Bestehende Installationen können den Update-Button verwenden. Nach diesem Update einmal WoW vollständig beenden und neu starten, damit die Weltobjekte mit den Funkel-Einstellungen neu geladen werden.

addons.description:
A configurable HUD for shamans on World of Warcraft: Forever: the buffs, imbues and cooldowns a shaman watches, as icons you can arrange anywhere. Requires WoW: Forever (interface 16001).

More screenshots: options gallery.
Download
• CurseForge
• Wago
• GitHub releases — download ShamanForever--forever.zip (not GitHub's Source code archive, which has no Libs/ folder)
Features
A collection of highly configurable HUD elements designed to help shamans playing World of Warcraft: Forever.

Some highlights include:

Totem bar: Fully configurable totem bar replacing the default or active totem frames: drop, pick and dismiss totems, Call of the Elements and Totemic Recall, out of range warning, key bindings, themes, and more.

Shield helpers: Lightning Shield and Water Shield tracking. Style and animate based on charges left.

Shock trackers: Earth, Flame, and Frost Shock monitoring for cooldown, range, mana.

Flame Shock: Track Flame Shock on your target with style and animations based on time left or debuff missing.

Purge: Show and glow an icon when your target has a purgeable magic buff, with buff duration filter.

Weapon Imbues: Rockbiter, Flametongue, Frostbrand, and Windfury imbue status. Warn when missing.

Swing timer: Melee swing timer shown as a bar.

Dedicated ability and proc trackers: Custom made indicators for shaman abilities such as Stormstrike, Fire Nova, Chain Lightning, Riptide, Lightning Mastery, Rage of the Farseer, Nature's Swiftness, Mana Tide Totem, Earthbind Totem, Tremor Totem, Grounding Totem, Stoneclaw Totem, Totemic Call, Elemental Focus, Maelstrom Weapon, Flurry, Improved Stormstrike. Not just cooldowns, also event, duration and condition-based warnings and animation styles.

Utility and reagent trackers: Water Walking, Water Breathing, Reincarnation. Know when you are low on reagents, see Reincarnation cooldown, get warnings on buff expiry or when drowning.

Racial trackers: All shaman races have their racial abilities included; Stoneform, Blood Fury, Shatter Curse, Berserking, Rapid Regeneration, Skysight, Walk on Air, War Stomp.

Extremely customisable styling: Font and text styles, border options, bar textures, including those from other installed addons through LibSharedMedia.

Layout and preview system: Drag and drop element groups live on the screen and quickly adjust size, scale, opacity. Get a sense of the action with preview modes. Structured group-based layout for consistency of layout.

Many opacity and idle settings: Control the opacity of all groups, plus dedicated "idle when" logic to allow setups like hiding an element when it's on or off cooldown, when a buff is up or down, only in combat, and more.

... and many more! Feature requests are highly encouraged. Please help us make this addon more valuable for all shamans!
Usage
• /sf opens the options window (or use the minimap button).
• Key bindings for the totem bar: Escape > Options > Keybindings > ShamanForever, or use the Quick Keybinds feature.
• /sf lock to unlock positioning.
• /sf preview shows your HUD in various modes to get a sense of it in action.
Feedback
Ideas, requests or problems are welcome, any of these ways:
• A post in #feedback on Discord.
• A comment on CurseForge.
• An issue on GitHub.

addons.description:
Picks quests for your level in WoW: Forever and, with Shortest Path Forever, walks you to each one.

Adventure Guide Forever suggests quests for your level and quest log, in a short route. Shortest Path Forever walks you to each stop; without it, the game's waypoint does.

Questie draws the quest markers; the guide adds route rings. With RestedXP installed, a one-time prompt lets you keep its display or follow its guides in Adventure Guide.

Each number is a stop on the route: a pickup, an objective or a hand-in.

Choose a journey and follow its route, checking off its quests as you go.

Choose a journey from the world map's quest log. Expand a header for more choices.

Finished stories are recorded once for this character.

Follow a RestedXP guide in the Adventure tab, with its engine handling progress.
Features
• RestedXP guides. Choose a guide from the Continue cards and follow its steps on the map and tracker. RestedXP handles completion; Shortest Path Forever handles travel. RestedXP’s item and target windows keep their own settings and positions. Turn off Use RestedXP guides to return to Adventure Guide's suggestions.
• Map guide. The active RestedXP guide comes first while Use RestedXP guides is on; otherwise Quests in your log.
• Quest difficulty. Choose the highest recommended quest level relative to yours in Route settings. The default, +2, avoids orange and red pickups. Accepted quests remain visible.
• Dungeon journeys. Follow quest pickups, preparation chains and hand-ins with Shortest Path Forever. Right-click a dungeon card for AtlasLoot bosses, drops and native item tooltips. Tweaks Forever handles automatic dungeon maps.
• Journeys. Finish loose ends, follow a zone's story, find nearby zones suited to your level or take class quests. Journey choices explain why each fits. Dungeon and battleground journeys are opt-in.
• Full guide. Expand the map guide for the whole route, then the area's Questie outline. Later entries stay as outline until Questie confirms them.
• Choose and go. Pick a journey on the map to start guidance with Shortest Path Forever, or the game's waypoint. A setting makes choosing preview only. Stop clears only guidance the addon started.
• A route that stays with you. Your choice survives new quests, travel and reloads. Ready hand-ins and nearby pickups come first. Town stops group quest givers into a checklist.
• Playing in a party. Quests someone in your party also has count as a little nearer, so you tend to do them together, and a pickup a party member already has says so. Party members with the guide tell each other which quests they have through hidden addon messages, at most one every 15 seconds and never in combat. Turn off Favour quests your party has in Route settings to stop it.
• Your order. Drag steps or right-click to move them earlier or later. Moves that break quest order are greyed out. Back to suggested order restores the plan.
• Where to do an objective. The guide skips a place whose mobs are 3 or more levels above you for a lower one on the same map. Next spot in the step's menu moves the arrow to the nearest other camp, even where you stand.
• Givers that don't offer a quest. If a giver doesn't offer the quest the guide sent you for, the guide says so once in chat and drops it, trying again after a level-up or a hand-in that could open it up.
• Reward upgrades. When a quest offers rewards to choose from, the game's green arrow marks each one that beats what you wear: your armour type, a main stat your class uses and a higher item level.
• Story milestones. Finishing a proven quest chain shows a short popup, once per character.
• Stories and search. Stories read as chapters without naming later quests. Search puts the best match first and shows which of a quest's requirements you meet. For a locked quest it names the earliest quest in its chain you can take, and a shift-click adds that one.…

addons.description:
Small quality-of-life tweaks for WoW: Forever that look like they came with the game.

Tweaks Forever can accept and turn in quests, standing down while Polestar does. It can name rares near you in chat, and it repairs and sells junk at merchants. Gear groups, maps, nameplates and more sit beside them in the game’s settings.

When another addon already does one of these jobs, that feature is greyed out and its tooltip names the addon, so the two never fight.

The junk coin marks what sells with your greys at a merchant. Also dungeon entrances and nameplates.

Inside a dungeon or raid the map opens on its painted sheet, and a click on an entrance shows it from outside, with a button for each floor.

Every dungeon and raid entrance, with retail's icons. Blackrock Mountain lists all four.
Features
Every feature has its own setting; docs/features.md has the detail.
• Quests. Quest levels on map tooltips, the tracker and quest dialogs, a gold tint on quests added in Forever, a coin on the reward choice that sells for the most, Abandon quests with one confirmation, the tracker sorted nearest first with distances, and bindable keys for your nearest quest's item and target.
• Automation. Accepts and turns in quests, skips one-option gossip, opens the flight map, accepts summons and group resurrections, releases in battlegrounds, declines duels (friends and guild can be let through), and accepts party invites from friends or declines strangers'. Hold Shift to talk normally. Off until you turn it on, as are invites from a whispered keyword and skipping loot confirmations.
• Faster auto loot. Takes everything at once instead of waiting for the loot window.
• Repairs and junk. Repairs at any merchant, from guild funds when allowed, and sells grey junk through the game's own Sell All Junk, plus up to 12 marked stacks per visit. Everything stays in buyback. Alt+Right-click marks an item with the game's junk coin when Mark items as junk is on. Hold Shift as a merchant opens to skip both for that visit.
• Gear groups. Ctrl+Right-click a bag item to put it in a named, coloured group, then equip the whole group in one click. Items show a coloured strip, border or dots. A fishing pole keeps the weapons it replaced as a Before fishing group.
• Map extras. Unexplored areas in a blue tint on the world and zone maps (off until you turn it on), each zone's level range coloured like quest levels, your and the cursor's coordinates, and every dungeon and raid entrance marked with retail's icons.
• Dungeon maps. Inside a dungeon or raid, or when you click its entrance, the world map shows the client's own painted map, with its area names and boss rooms, a button for the floor and a Back to map button. The maps come with WoW: Forever; no extra addon is needed.
• Movable windows. A Windows tab in Edit Mode moves and scales 21 Blizzard windows, per layout (not with the gamepad UI).
• Nameplates. A taller bar in retail's own frame, name and level above, your target outlined, and cast bars with the spell's icon.
• Spell reach. A small icon for each attack you track on every enemy nameplate: full colour in reach, solid red out of it. Off until you turn it on.
• Tooltips. A thin rounded border over charcoal, class-coloured names and a health bar inside. The style is charcoal, retail's navy, or the game's own border.
• Questie extras. Needs Questie or its QuestieDB addon. Quests listed when you point at a minimap giver, your progress in a creature's, quest item's or object's tooltip, items that start a quest marked, with a quest icon by its nameplate, and Questie's markers in the game's own quest symbols.

Rare alerts (off by default) name nearby rares in chat; click the name, or press a bound key, to set a waypoint to it. In a group, a pull warning says in chat when your threat passes the tank's.…
addons.name: tweaks-forever

releases.changelog: • A warning before you pull aggro. In a group, a chat line tells you when your threat on your target has passed the tank's, so you can stop before the mob turns on you. It warns once, then again only after you drop back below the tank or change target. Turn it off under Interface in Tweaks' settings; nameplates coloured by threat are the game's own Nameplates option.

• Bug reports keep distinct errors apart. The report groups caught errors on their full text rather than the shortened text it shows, so two errors that differ only past the display limit are listed separately. The BugGrabber section's heading now appears only when it has an error to add, so a report with nothing from BugGrabber no longer carries an empty heading.

• The data now names the 1.60.1.70755 build. Zone level ranges, camp benefits, dungeon and raid entrances, class trainer spells, world map overlays and Forever's added quests are regenerated from the new client build. The regenerated values match the previous build, so nothing a player sees moves and only the build stamp in each file changes.

• Repeated errors stay distinct in reports. Tweaks now keeps the full error text when grouping caught errors, so messages that only differ after the display limit are not merged, and BugGrabber entries already captured by Tweaks are omitted from the report.
• Screenshot art keeps its reviewed build. The renderer records its UI-art pin independently of shared tooling updates, and changing it requires fresh screenshots.

addons.author: Claypaenguin
addons.changelog:
Added
• Healer low mana indicator: shows "Healy low on mana!" (with the healer's name) while your group's healer is at or below a mana threshold you choose (20% by default), and hides it again once they're above it.
• On/off toggle, adjustable threshold, and an "Only inside dungeons" option.
• Its own font, outline, size and position, like the other alerts.
• Uses group roles, so the healer needs the Healer role (automatic with the Dungeon Finder).
• No sound: WoW Forever hides mana values from addons, so the game itself decides when the text is visible, and the addon can't react to it with a sound.
• Solo test mode for the healer indicator: treats you as the healer while you're not in a group.

Changed
• The settings window now scrolls, to make room for the healer section.
addons.description:
Small personal addon with three features:
• Combat text: text that fades in and out when you enter or leave combat.
• Party death alert: text, plus an optional sound, when a member of your 5-player group dies. Raids are ignored.
• Healer low mana indicator: text that stays on screen while your group's healer is at or below a mana
threshold you choose (20% by default), and disappears once they're above it. It uses the group roles, so it
works with the Dungeon Finder or roles set in the group menu. Solo test mode treats you as the healer
while you're not in a group, to try it out alone. There's no sound for this one: WoW Forever
hides mana values from addons, so the addon can only hand them to the game's display code (see Notes).

Each feature can be turned on or off on its own, with its own font, outline, font size and position.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that answers one question when you hover a
weapon: can I use this, and if not, where do I learn it?
Features
• Your skill. Weapons you know show your current skill, for example
"You know this weapon skill (50/60)".
• Where to train. Weapons your class can learn show the weapon master,
their city and district, map coordinates, the cost, and any level
requirement. The first trainer listed is the one nearest to you.
• Other trainers. Hold Shift to list every other trainer for that weapon.
The tooltip updates as you press the key.
• Map pins. Ctrl + Right-Click a weapon in your bags, on your character or
at a merchant to pin its trainer on the map. TomTom is used if you prefer it.
• Forever changes. Weapons Forever added to a class are tagged
"New in Forever": two-handed axes and maces for Shamans, one-handed axes for
Rogues, and polearms for Druids.
• Weapons you can't use say so in red.

addons.description:
A warlock helper for World of Warcraft: Forever, in the spirit of Necrosis.
Features
• The grimoire: a tome on the bar showing your soul shard count. It fills with fel light as shards build up. It also tracks shards gained this session, can sort shards into a soul bag or a bag you choose (Ctrl-click to sort now), and has an optional cap that offers to delete extra shards (always asking first; Ctrl-mouse wheel sets it).
• Healthstone: creates your highest learned rank, or uses the stone in your bags. Glows when your stone is outdated; shift-right-click deletes it (with a prompt) so you can make the new rank. Right-click trades it to your friendly target.
• Soulstone: creates the stone, or uses it on your mouseover, then your target, then yourself. A 30-minute timer warns you before it expires. Optionally announces the soulstone to your group and whispers the target.
• Weapon stone: left-click for Firestone, right-click for Spellstone. Creates the stone or applies it to your main hand, and glows when the enchant is missing or about to expire.
• Curse and Bane menus: left-click casts your default, right-click opens the menu, and the spell you pick becomes the new default. Banes are separate in Forever.
• Buff menu: Demon Armor/Skin, Soul Link, Demonic Sacrifice, Shadow Ward, Unending Breath, Detect Invisibility, Eye of Kilrogg, Sense Demons. Glows when you have no armor on.
• Crowd control menu: Banish, Fear, Howl of Terror, Subjugate Demon, Death Coil. Glows when your target can be banished or subjugated.
• Demon menu: the demons you know. Shift-click casts Fel Domination first.
• Mount button: your best warlock mount, Dreadsteed or Felsteed.
• Summoning: left-click Ritual of Summoning, right-click Portal of Summoning, with a group announcement.
• Requests: collects summon requests ("123", "summon") and healthstone requests ("hs") from group chat and whispers. Click a name to target and summon them, or to open a trade with a healthstone. It shows offline, dead, and already-summoned players, and syncs with other Grimoire warlocks.
• Warlocks panel (shift-click the book, or /grim raid): every Grimoire warlock in your group, their curse, and who holds their soulstone. The leader or an assistant can click a curse to assign it, and that warlock's curse button switches to it.
• Life Tap button: shows mana per tap and taps to full. Out of combat it glows when your mana is low and your health is high.
• Range: curse, bane and crowd-control icons turn red when your target is out of range.
• Visibility: always shown or only in combat, optionally hidden in cities and inns, and optional fading until you mouse over it.
• Tome colors: Void, Shadow, Fel and Blood.
• Timers: estimated Banish, Fear, Howl, Subjugate and Death Coil bars, started from your own casts, with warnings before Banish and Subjugate end.
• Shadow Trance alert when Nightfall procs.
• Chat lines for soulstones, demon summons and mounts. These go to party/raid only; Blizzard blocks addons from using /say in the open world.
• Keybindings for every button: Key Bindings → AddOns → Grimoire. With ElvUI, /kb hover binding works on Grimoire buttons, including individual spells in the menus.
• Works with other addons: a LibDataBroker feed (Titan Panel, Bazooka, ...), an entry in Blizzard's AddOns menu by the minimap, and Masque skins for square buttons.
• Ring layout: the book in the center with the buttons in a circle around it, like Necrosis. Start angle, size and direction are adjustable. Menus open outward. Three styles:
• Grimoire (default): Grimoire's own art. A leather tome with a fel sigil sits in an iron bezel whose 20 sockets light up with your soul shards, surrounded by iron-rimmed round buttons.
• Flat round: thin-rimmed round buttons in your ElvUI colors.
• Square: ElvUI's action-button style.
• Menus close on their own shortly after the mouse leaves, even in combat. Right-click keeps a menu open (shift-right-click for Curses and Banes).…

BigChatBox v7.0.0 - I intend to live foreverAll versionsNew
• WoW Forever support. BigChatBox now loads on the Forever client with its own TOC.
• The setup wizard, the built-in styles and the two help windows now also work on TBC Anniversary, Mists of Pandaria Classic and Classic Era.
Change
• Patch notes now show only the notes for the current version.
• Restart Setup keeps your snippets, saved styles and chat history; only settings are reset.
• Chat messages from BigChatBox use its blue name tag, and the lockdown messages are translated.
• A message with several lines (multiline box or a multi-line snippet): a line starting with / stops the send, so commands are never posted as text. Lines over 255 characters are split instead of cut off, and more than 10 messages asks first.
• The whisper name suggestions keep the realm for players on other realms, so the whisper reaches the right person.
• History tab: Wipe Entire History now says it also clears Recent Whispers, and no longer reloads the UI.

By Dukul

ℹ️ About
BigChatBox replaces and enhances the default World of Warcraft chat input box with a fully customizable, movable, and resizable chat experience designed specifically for the Midnight expansion (12.0+).

Style your chat box exactly how you want with custom borders, textures, fonts, transparency, scaling, snippets, autocomplete, history tools, and LibSharedMedia support.

BigNoteBox v2.0.0All versionsNewExplorer view
• Explorer view: your notes as a grid of icons over the whole window, like a file explorer, with its own toolbar, multi-select, drag and drop, and a status bar. Turn it on or off in Settings > Modules > Explorer view.
• Explorer view: Small, Medium and Large tiles, List, Details (sortable columns) and Flat, in the View menu.
• Explorer view: View menu options to put pinned notes first without sections, or favorites first.
• Explorer view: New folder with selection, and Remember the open note (Settings > Modules > Explorer view)
• Explorer view: with the Reference Box's auto-open on, clicking a note opens its Reference Box when it has attachments or tasks.
Folders
• Folders: sort your notes into folders, with a color each, in the note list and the explorer. Folders come along in backups. Settings > Modules > Folders.
Help book and patch notes
• The help book: every help topic in one book, with chapters, a search and a Glossary. Open it with the new Help button on the top bar or /bnb help.
• Right-click a button on the formatting or rich toolbar to open its help topic.
• The help book has a Features tab (what BigNoteBox can do, A-Z), which replaces the old Features window.
• Patch notes: every release back to v1.6.9 in the help book's Patch notes tab. After an update a toast opens the new release there, and no pinned patch note is added to your note list any more.
Spelling and text shortcuts
• Spelling: red wavy lines under misspelled words, English (US) or English (UK), as you type or with the Check spelling button. Settings > Modules > Spelling.
• Spelling: right-click a marked word for suggestions, Add to dictionary or Ignore, and a Correct spelling window that goes through them one by one.
• Spelling: repeated words (the the) are marked, with options to ignore UPPERCASE words and words with numbers.
• Spelling works in Focus mode and sticky notes too.
• Key bindings: Check spelling (F9) and Correct spelling (F10)
• Text shortcuts: type brb and it becomes "be right back". Make your own in Settings > Modules > Spelling, with an "Only with !" option.
Writing notes
• Find and replace in a note: Ctrl+F or the new button on the formatting toolbar, in the editor and Focus mode.
• Rich notes: underline and strikethrough, two new buttons on the rich toolbar.
• Rich notes: dividers, a new button on the rich toolbar.
• Rich notes: {code}...{/code} shows text exactly as typed, tags and all.
• Links to BigNoteBox itself: the link button's new BigNoteBox tab links a note to a Settings page or window.
• An open note has two new buttons: Note settings on the formatting toolbar, and Situation on the action bar.
• Note right-click menu: Favorite, Pin, Lock, Rename and Delete are a row of icons at the bottom. Rename is new.
• Sort menus: Reset sort, and Make this the default.
Note Capture, player and NPC notes
• Note Capture: quest, book and dialogue notes can be rich notes, one setting per kind in Settings > Modules > Note Capture.
• Note Capture: quest notes show when you accepted or turned in the quest, its level and kind, a Wowhead address and a waypoint link.
• Note Capture: the NPC's name in a quest or dialogue note links to that NPC's own note.
• Note Capture: captured notes get the zone as a tag, and optionally the subzone.
• What an NPC says now goes into that NPC's own note instead of a note of its own.
• Dialogue UI: a BigNoteBox button beside its Copy Text button.
• Player and NPC notes made from a target or inspect get dividers between their sections.
• NPC notes are round like player notes, with an Elite or Rare frame (Retail and Forever)
Other languages in notes
• Notes with Korean, Chinese, Japanese, Cyrillic or Greek text use a font that can show them, and get a language shield on the title row and tooltip.
Accessibility
• Settings > Modules > Accessibility: a new page, starting with Motion settings for the sticky note animation.…

By Dukul

ℹ️ About
BigNoteBox is a full in-game notepad companion for World of Warcraft.

Create, organize, and manage unlimited notes directly inside the game. Notes are stored account-wide with optional per-character scope, allowing both global planning and character-specific tracking.

It has folders, a search that finds any note from anywhere, sticky notes, notes that show up in the right place, tasks, alarms, rich formatting, history, backups, sharing and much more.

BigNoteBox v1.30.0All versionsNew
• Settings profiles: Settings > Advanced starts with Profiles. Keep different settings and window layouts for different characters (a bank alt, a raider): clone the one you use or start a blank one with the setup wizard, rename, delete, and export / import a profile as a code to share. Danger Zone can reset just the profile in use, or all settings and profiles.
Change
• Right-click menus: the menu of an item or spell link, and of a Reference Box entry, shows its icon beside the name; a web link's menu leaves out https:// and www. so more of the address shows. The menu of a link to another note has Open as sticky note, Share note, Copy note to clipboard and Copy / Move to...
• Right-click menus: an item, spell or other game link in the note you are editing (also in View and Focus mode) has Add to Reference Box. A web link's menu shows a link symbol in front of the address.
• Reference Box: Insert at text cursor reads Insert at bottom of note until you click into the note's text, and puts the link on a new line at the end instead of being greyed out.
• Focus mode: link menus work there. • Settings > Backup: three buttons, Full backup (notes, templates, tokens, tag colours and settings profiles), Settings backup (profiles only) and Selective backup (pick JSON or Markdown and which notes and parts go in). • Simplified Chinese: settings profiles, the new Backup page and the new right-click menu lines are translated.

BigNoteBox v1.29.0All versionsNew
• Right-click a link in a note, rich or normal, for a menu: Send to chat, Show and Try on for items; Set waypoint, Show on map, Send to chat and Copy /way for waypoints; Open note and Share to chat for links to other notes; Send to chat and Copy link for web links.
• The right-click menu in the note text now holds the note token groups, the same as the toolbar's token button, in place of the old insert rows; new token {{datetime}} for the date and time together.
• Links to other notes show in that note's title colour, and follow it when it changes.
Change

• Reference Box right-click menus show the entry's name at the top and an icon on every row.
• The note token lists call their groups Here and now and Character, and their tooltips say how tokens fill in rich and normal notes.

• Settings > Backup shows the Rescue section only while there are notes to rescue, at the top of the page, so the page no longer needs a scrollbar.
• Simplified Chinese: everything added since the last translation is translated (templates, tags, note tokens, links, Rescue and more).

• Up and Down move through the token list again in notes, Focus mode, sticky editing and the tl;dr boxes.
• Pressing Enter at the bottom of a note scrolls the note along, so the line you are typing stays in view.
• Clicking the note title to rename it frames only the title, not the tl;dr line above it.

Changelog1.2.4Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery, and TBC Anniversary
• Expanded vendor pricing to supported item tooltips across inventory and bank, mail, merchants and buyback, professions, quest rewards, and the Auction House.
• Added per-context options with saved preferences and a Defaults button.
• Preserved Blizzard's native tooltip behavior when a context is disabled.
• Known limitation: TBC Anniversary quest-log reward stacks may show only the unit Vendor price.
WoW Forever
• Standardized supported item tooltips on Vendor and Vendor xN labels, including mail, professions, buyback, Auction House, and quest rewards.
• Corrected the Map & Quest Log reward tooltip to use Vendor instead of Sell Price.
• Kept Blizzard's native price values and preserved existing Auctionator integration.
• Removed unused Forever tooltip formatting helpers and superseded quest-reward workarounds.
Architecture
• Continued shared Compat.lua, Options.lua, and VendorPricePlus.lua architecture across supported clients.
• WoW Forever, Classic Era, and TBC Anniversary were tested during 1.2.4 development; the known TBC quest-log reward stack limitation remains.
1.2.3WoW Forever
• Standardized bag and inventory vendor-price labels on Vendor and Vendor xN.
• Added Forever Auctionator coexistence with a clean three-row presentation: Vendor, Auction, and Vendor xN for stacks.
• Removed the redundant native Sell Price presentation when Auctionator and VendorPricePlus are both active.
Compatibility
• Hardened stack-price calculations against protected/secret numeric values.
• Action-bar item counts on supported legacy tooltip paths can recover a readable inventory count without performing arithmetic on a protected GetActionCount() value.
• Falls back safely when a readable stack count is unavailable instead of allowing a protected value into price arithmetic.
Community
• Incorporated the defensive secret-count approach reported and prototyped by Dirtimoney, adapted to VendorPricePlus's current compatibility architecture.
1.2.2WoW Forever
• Fixed protected/secret stack-count errors when hovering stackable items on action bars.
• Restored Unit Price information for stackable action-bar item tooltips.
• Fixed incorrect Unit Price detection on recipe tooltips.
• Fixed duplicate Sell Price information on quest-offer reward tooltips.
1.2.1WoW Forever
• Fixed missing Sell Price on selectable quest rewards in the Map & Quest Log.
• Fixed protected/secret tooltip geometry errors when hovering item actions such as food and water on the action bar.
• Kept Forever price-row formatting on Blizzard's safe tooltip layout path instead of measuring protected FontString geometry.
1.2.0WoW Forever
• Added WoW Forever client detection and modern tooltip compatibility.
• Added compact Sell Price formatting with right-aligned money values.
• Added Unit Price directly beneath Sell Price for stacked item tooltips.
• Added support for Inventory & Bank, Mail, Merchant & Buyback, Professions, and Quest Reward contexts.
• Added missing vendor pricing to Forever quest reward tooltips.
• Added a Blizzard AddOns settings panel with per-context enable/disable controls.
• Added persistent settings through VendorPricePlusDB.
• Leaves the Forever Auction House unchanged because its tooltip already reports the correct per-unit vendor value.
Architecture
• Added Compat.lua as the client/API compatibility layer.
• Moved third-party addon support into Integrations.lua.
• Added Options.lua for settings and configuration UI.
• Added human-readable comments around compatibility and tooltip behavior.
• Preserved the established non-Forever Vendor Price Plus behavior for supported Classic clients.
Compatibility
• WoW Forever: tested successfully.
• TBC Anniversary: regression tested successfully.
• Classic Era: regression tested successfully.
• Mists of Pandaria Classic and Retail: not currently tested or advertised as supported.
1.1.3
• Previous production release.
addons.description:
Version 1.2.4

Vendor Price Plus is a lightweight World of Warcraft addon that makes vendor values easier to read while preserving Blizzard's familiar item tooltips.
Features
• Displays vendor values in supported item tooltips, using Vendor for an individual item and Vendor xN for a stack when its count is available.
• Supports Inventory & Bank, Mail, Merchant & Buyback, Professions, Quest Rewards, and Auction House tooltips, subject to client capabilities.
• Provides a Blizzard AddOns options panel to choose where vendor pricing appears. All supported contexts are enabled by default; Defaults restores these settings.
• Leaves Blizzard's native tooltip behavior in place when a context is disabled.
• Coexists with Auctionator without intentionally duplicating its vendor-price rows or disrupting its usual ordering.
• Retains the same independently installable addon across supported Classic clients and WoW Forever.

Exact tooltip behavior may vary by client and context. In WoW Forever, vendor-price formatting uses the client's modern tooltip processing path. In Classic clients, the addon preserves the relevant legacy tooltip behavior.
Commands
• /vpp — Open Vendor Price Plus settings.
Compatibility
| Client | Version 1.2.4 status |
| --- | --- |
| WoW Forever | Tested, including quest rewards |
| TBC Anniversary | Regression tested during 1.2.4 development |
| Classic Era | Previously supported; final 1.2.4 regression test pending |
| Classic Era Hardcore and seasonal variants | Expected to follow Classic Era behavior; not separately verified for 1.2.4 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | Not tested or advertised as supported |
| Retail | Not tested or advertised as supported |

The TBC Anniversary quest-log reward tooltip may display the unit vendor value without a total stack value. See CHANGELOG.md for release history and known limitations.
Acknowledgements
Vendor Price Plus builds on the original Vendor Price addon by Ketho17 and Icesythe7. Historical author credits remain in the addon metadata.

addons.description:
PixelPerfectUIScale is a lightweight World of Warcraft addon that ensures your UI always uses a pixel-perfect scale.

It calculates the correct scale using:

768 / screenHeight

…and applies it automatically on login and whenever display or UI scale settings change.
✨ Features
• Automatically enforces pixel-perfect UI scale (768 / screenHeight)
• Optional custom modifier for 4K / ultrawide monitors
• /ppscale modifier
• Example: /ppscale modifier 1.5 → (768 / screenHeight) × 1.5
• Supports values between 0.5 and 3.0
• Saved between sessions
• Safe handling during combat (scale changes are deferred until after combat)
• Listens for key scale-related events:
• PLAYER_LOGIN
• PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD
• DISPLAY_SIZE_CHANGED
• UI_SCALE_CHANGED
• EDIT_MODE_LAYOUTS_UPDATED
• Optional syncing of Blizzard uiScale CVars so the Settings UI stays consistent
• Midnight-compatible (no protected calls or combat taint)
💬 Slash Commands
| Command | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| /ppscale status | Show desired vs current scale (base, modifier, and result) |
| /ppscale modifier | Set a multiplier for custom scaling (e.g. 1.25) |
| /ppscale now | Force scale reapply immediately |
| /ppscale debug | Toggle verbose debug output |
| /ppscale cvars on/off | Toggle writing to Blizzard uiScale CVars |
❓ Why use this instead of the WeakAura?
• No dependency on WeakAuras
• Lightweight and always active
• Midnight-safe — handles combat restrictions automatically
• Future-proof — continues working even if WeakAuras is not updated for future expansions

addons.description:
The guild addon for the Short Kings of World of Warcraft: Forever.

Everyone's gear, talents, professions, recipes and raid readiness in one window.

No website, no server, no uploads: it all travels over the guild's addon channel.

Install ·
What's inside ·
Commands ·
FAQ ·
Roadmap ·
The look

> [!NOTE]
> Not run in game yet. Short Kings is built against Blizzard's own Forever
> 1.60.1 interface code and tested against a simulated WoW client. The
> pictures here are drawn by the browser preview from
> the addon's real colours, fonts and layout. Item icons are placeholders;
> in game you see the real ones.

🧨 What's inside
| | What you get |
|---|---|
| 🏰 Overview | The guild at a glance: who's around, raid readiness, data health, professions, recipes and recent milestones |
| 👥 Roster | The whole guild in one sortable, searchable list, with alts folded under mains and a raid-attunement view |
| 🛡️ Character | Anyone's gear, talents, professions, cooldowns, attunements and reputations |
| ⚒️ Crafters | Search an item or recipe and see who in the guild can make it, online first |
| ⚙️ Settings | Sharing and privacy switches, display options, window size, tools and a live status read-out |
| 🧨 Everywhere | /sk, a minimap button, "Crafted by" lines on item tooltips, chat reminders and a copyable debug report |
🏰 Overview
The first tab: six sections in three columns, set like a spec sheet. Each
section has a link to the place where you can act on it.
• Guild: members, players (alts counted once), online now, running Short Kings, shared their data, and levels in bands (60, 50–59, 40–49, 1–39). Open roster.
• Raids: the one big number, days until raids open on 9 Dec. Barrow Deeps (10) and Hyjal Summit (20) need no attunement, so it counts your level 60s. Onyxia's Lair (40) shows attuned / not attuned / unknown, and how many have the quest done but the Drakefire Amulet out of their bags. Onyxia list.
• Data health: members without Short Kings data, profiles older than a week, profession windows never opened, and anyone on an old Short Kings (you included). "All good" when there's nothing to fix. Oldest first opens the Roster with missing and oldest data on top.
• Professions: characters per crafting profession, how many are at 300 (or the best so far), nobody in red where the guild has a gap, and one line for gathering. Find a crafter.
• Recipes: recipes the guild knows, from how many crafters, and how many only one character knows, with examples, so you can see where there's no backup. Search recipes.
• Recent milestones: level-ups (every 10 levels), profession 75/150/225/300, Onyxia attunement and new recipes. Hover for when, click to open the character, Grats types "Grats Bramble on level 60!" into guild chat (you press Enter).

The line above the columns shows your guild, members and who's online.
Milestones are worked out by your own addon and kept on your computer
only (the last 50); nothing extra is sent. Turn them off in Settings.
👥 Roster
• Every guild member, including people without the addon.
• Columns: Name in class colour ((you) in pink on your characters, +2 when alts are folded in), Level, Rank, Spec (main tree and points), Professions, iLvl, Online (a dot, then online, on alt or how long ago), Version (orange when out of date) and Data (how fresh their profile is; orange after a week).
• Status dots: 🟢 online with Short Kings · ⚪ online without it · ⚫ offline.
• Sort by clicking a column (an arrow marks the sorted one). Online members come first.
• Search by name, profession, spec, class, rank, a word from their note, or an alt's name. A search with no matches says so.
• Group alts (on by default) shows each player once, under their main.
• Counter: characters, how many have data, how many need an update, and whether a newer Short Kings is out.
• Copy gives the list exactly as shown, as plain text for Discord. Notes are never included.…

addons.description:
When you level up, a small window in Blizzard's own trainer style shows what you gained and which class skills you can now buy, with their price.

Why players install it
• See your gains at a glance. Health, mana, talent points and stats you got from the new level.
• Know what to train. New class skills for your level, with icon, rank and price.
• Blizzard look, no libraries. Zero cost when idle, tiny cost when it works.
What you see
A small window in Blizzard's own trainer style opens when you level up:
• Gains. One line per stat that changed, each stat name in its own color, shown as old value, a green up arrow, then the new value (for example Stamina 25 ▲ 26). Talent points show as ▲ +1 Talent points.
• Skills. New class skills for your level under New skills, new ranks of skills you already have under New ranks. Each row shows the icon, name, rank and price. The price turns red when you cannot afford it. Hover a row for the spell tooltip.
• What changed. A new rank lists what changed from the rank before it, like patch notes: for example Healing: 47-58 → 76-91 or Mana cost: 30 → 45. Missed ranks under Not yet learned show it too.
• Long lists. Not yet learned and Weapon skills show their first 5 rows; click +N more to scroll through the rest right in the window, and Show less to fold it back.
• Learning from trainers. The addon learns skills and prices from class trainers you visit. Until your race has visited its trainer for the new level, the window adds a line telling you to visit your class trainer.

The window closes by itself after a few seconds. Hover it to keep it open, drag it to move it, or press the X to close it. If you level up in combat, it waits until combat ends.
Settings
Open them with /lui or under Options, AddOns, Level Up Info.

| Setting | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enabled | Show the window on level-up | On |
| Duration | Seconds before the window closes (3 to 30) | 10 |
| Wait for combat to end | Hold the window until you leave combat | On |
| Scale | Window size (0.5 to 1.5) | 1.0 |
| Reduced motion | Close the window at once instead of fading | Off |
| Show minimap button | Show the minimap button (left-click: preview, right-click: options; drag it around the minimap) | On |
| Reset position | Put the window back at its default spot | |
| Clear skill data | Forget the skills learned from trainers | |
| Test | Close the options and show a preview of the window | |
Commands
• /lui opens the settings.
• /lui test shows a preview of the window right now.
Game versions
• WoW: Forever
• Classic Era
• TBC Anniversary

addons.changelog:
• The Manners macro on an action bar casts. Clicking its slot, or pressing
its key, did nothing on Classic Era: the game does not let a macro press a
button that runs another macro, and that is what the old macro did. The
macro now carries the cast itself: Manners writes what the prompt would cast
into it, out of combat, whenever the prompt changes, so a press of the slot
buffs whoever the prompt shows and hands your target back, as a press of the
prompt does. It says no line: that goes out only with a press of the prompt,
which looks one last time at whether the cast can land. In the last moments
of a global cooldown, with nobody to buff, or while the macro window is open,
it holds only its first line and a press says why; in a fight it keeps what
it held when the fight began. An older Manners macro is updated for you. A
#showtooltip you put on top stays; a macro you have changed in any other
way is left as it is, and Manners says so once.
• The prompt is made of something. Glass is now a pane of cut glass with a
metal bezel round the spell icon, which brightens under the pointer. Framed
wears a rim like the game's tooltips. Toast's gold is hammered and worn, and
the ring round its icon is a twist of rope.
• A new look: Forge. Forged iron and a riveted band, with the reason
glowing in a slot beside the icon like a bar of heated steel. A favour
arriving raises heat from the slot, and while it is owed the slot breathes
three times and rests. A buff landing flashes the icon white-hot and throws
sparks along the band; a refusal quenches the slot to steel with a puff of
steam. That makes ten looks, each a card under Look.
• The prompt arrives with light. On Glass, Framed and Minimal, two thin
rules of light draw out from the icon along the top and bottom edges as the
prompt comes up, and the words follow a beat behind. A favour arriving runs a
glint along them, in place of the band of light that used to cross the panel.
• A landing is felt, a refusal is heard. When a buff lands on Glass, Framed
or Minimal, the panel's edge lights in the reason's colour (Minimal lights its
two rules instead), a wave of light bursts from the icon across the panel, and
the wash of colour fades away instead of cutting off. A refusal flashes the
edge red, cracks the ground under the words, makes the top rule sputter,
turns the icon grey and shakes the words. Animations on Calm keeps the
fades and the grey icon and none of the movement.
• Flash when someone buffs me is no longer greyed out on Minimal with the
icon hidden, since the glint answers it there.
addons.description:
**Somebody buffed you. One click buffs them back, and your target is handed
straight back.**

A priest buffs you in passing. By the time you have picked them out of a dozen
nameplates, they are gone. Manners saw who it was, worked out what you owe them
and put one button on screen. Click it, or press your key: they get their buff,
your own target comes straight back, and the favour is remembered through a
reload or a disconnect.

The same button offers your group, people who ask for your buff in chat, and
passers-by who are missing it, so buffing a stranger costs one click instead of
a minute of squinting at names. It looks after you too: your own armor, aura,
aspect or shield, and the poison, stone, oil or lure for each weapon, come up as
"You" when they are missing. In a dungeon or a raid it offers one group cast for
a whole party when you carry the reagent, puts your group first at a ready check
and when somebody is brought back, offers only the raid groups you were given,
and offers a top-up at the moment that suits each buff's length.

Setting it up takes one page. /manners opens Start here: four numbered
steps (who to buff, one key, see it, say thanks). The first time, two questions
set the defaults for you, or Skip keeps them.

Runs on every live client: WoW Forever 1.60.1, Classic Era 1.15.9,
Burning Crusade Classic (Anniversary) 2.5.6, Mists of Pandaria Classic
5.5.4 and retail (Midnight) 12.1.5.

• Flash when someone buffs me is no longer greyed out on Minimal with the
icon hidden, since the glint answers it there.

• Fel Armor, from the Season of Discovery rune. A Warlock who has learned
Fel Armor from the rune vendor is reminded of it, and offered it, before Demon
Skin (issue #3). Without the rune, nothing changes: Demon Skin, and Demon
Armor from level 20.
• The prompt no longer vanishes in a fight. The built-in looks (Glass,
Framed and Minimal) were drawn at about half strength in combat, on top of
your Opacity, so a low Opacity could make the prompt disappear. It now keeps
your Opacity in a fight. Dim the prompt in combat on Look turns the dim
back on for anybody who wants it, takes effect at once even mid-fight, and is
greyed out on the looks that show a fight their own way. The old switch is
now called Keep the prompt still in combat, which is all it ever did.
• Your own buffs come back before they drop. Your own buffs, and the ones
you put on yourself (Thorns, Arcane Intellect, an armor), are now offered
again shortly before they run out, even with If they already have it on
Skip. On When to offer, Top up my own buffs this long before they end
asks for an earlier reminder, up to ten minutes (never more than half the
buff's length), so it comes up before you pull. *Top up my own buffs before
they run out* turns it off.
• /manners clicks now says which mouse button a press arrived as and
whether it was a down or an up click, to tell a bar macro or a key binding
from a click on the prompt in a report.
• Reset this page on Look puts the combat dim back too.
• How many to list is always a whole number of rows: an imported settings
string or a hand-edited file with a fraction listed a different number in
the preview than on the prompt.
• Ready for a future Forever client number. Manners recognises WoW Forever
by its own project id as well as its interface number, so a new Forever
version cannot be mistaken for Burning Crusade Classic.

• A check for a new client. /manners selftest launch asks the game about
the looks, the action bar slot, the controller keys, the tooltip and the
prompt's layout, says what it answered, and puts back everything it
touched, so a report can be pasted when something there does not draw right.
• Short of mana for one blessing, still no blessing over yours. Too low on
mana for Kings (or another blessing), you are no longer offered a cheaper one
for somebody already wearing the Kings you gave them, or for yourself.
• Blessing of Sanctuary from another paladin, at a lower rank than the one
you would cast, is no longer taken as covering them (Classic Era and
Burning Crusade).

• A smaller tooltip, and a choice of where it goes. Hovering the prompt, or
a name in its list, now shows the name, the spell, one line of why and
"Hold Shift for more"; holding Shift gives the full tooltip as before. On
Look, Tooltip on the prompt chooses Short, Full, *Only while
holding Shift* or Off, and Tooltip position puts it above or below the
prompt and its list (on the side with more room) or where the game puts its
own tooltips. The note that shows while the prompt is unlocked stays.
• No target, none handed back. Pressing the prompt with nothing
targeted now leaves you with nothing targeted, instead of possibly
bringing back an old target from earlier.
• A blessing of yours you switched off still counts. A paladin who gives
Salvation or Might by hand, with it off under Who to buff, is no longer
offered Kings for somebody wearing it.
• Raid groups you switched off. A passer-by who joins one of them is no
longer offered from memory for the next few seconds.
• Somebody you ignore who asked while grouped is not offered once the
group is gone.
• A see-through panel is see-through. With the panel colour's opacity
turned down, Glass and Framed no longer leave a dark box behind.
• Controller buttons on the prompt follow the game when it recognises the
controller or when its modifier buttons change, without a reload; and
Start here only says to drop the macro when it is Manners' own on the
cursor.
• The look cards speak your language. The sample on each card under
Look is written in your game's language, not English.
• Long counts keep clear of the name. A count of 100 or more no longer
crowds the name in any look, and on Arcane the count follows the key when
the key steps aside.
• A new resolution or UI scale lays the prompt out again at once (after the
fight, in one), so its list hangs on the right side without a reload.

• Put Manners on an action bar, and on a controller. *Put Manners on an
action bar* on Start here (and /manners macro) makes the macro and puts it
on your cursor: drop it on any slot of any bar. The slot shows the spell a
press would cast, with its cooldown and range, changing as the prompt
changes, and the macro's own icon when there is nobody to buff. A controller
button bound under Options > Keybindings > Manners presses the prompt like
a key, and the key shown on the prompt reads as the button's picture, a
held trigger as the buttons you press.

addons.changelog:
Added
• Scores count everyone. With the companion, a stone's score now adds
up every player's appraisals and disparagements (one per computer), not
just your own characters'. Your vote counts straight away, even before
the companion has shared it.
• Found counts. Hovering a stone on the minimap or world map shows how
many players have found it.
• Get the companion from inside the game. Without the Soapstone
companion, nobody else sees your stones and you don't find theirs. Type
/soap companion for a window with its download link, ready to copy
into your browser. Until the companion is set up, it also opens a few
seconds after you log in (not after a /reload); tick **Don't show this
again** if you'd rather it didn't. Shift-clicking the minimap button
