releases.changelog:
Added
• Scores count everyone. With the companion, a stone's score now adds
up every player's appraisals and disparagements (one per computer), not
just your own characters'. Your vote counts straight away, even before
the companion has shared it.
• Found counts. Hovering a stone on the minimap or world map shows how
many players have found it.
• Get the companion from inside the game. Without the Soapstone
companion, nobody else sees your stones and you don't find theirs. Type
/soap companion for a window with its download link, ready to copy
into your browser. Until the companion is set up, it also opens a few
seconds after you log in (not after a /reload); tick **Don't show this
again** if you'd rather it didn't. Shift-clicking the minimap button
opens it too, and the button's tooltip now says plainly when your stones
aren't being shared.

You need the Soapstone companion to share stones. Without it, nobody else sees your stones and you won't find theirs. Get the companion (Windows; macOS coming soon).

Install the addon: get it on CurseForge (the CurseForge app keeps it up to date), or download Soapstone-v0.6.0.zip and unzip it into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, so you get AddOns\Soapstone\Soapstone.toc. Then restart the game.

Fixed
• Stones can't carry WoW formatting codes any more. A stone's words, or
a player's name, could include codes for colours, links or pictures, and
the game drew them in tooltips, chat and the stone window, so a stone
could pass itself off as a system message. They now always show as
plain text.
• A stone can't take over another player's stone. A stone claiming the
same id as one by someone else is refused, so nobody can replace your
stones in other players' games.

Install: download Soapstone-v0.5.1.zip and unzip it into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, so you get AddOns\Soapstone\Soapstone.toc. Then restart the game.

> Newer companion: Soapstone Companion 0.2.0 shares stones through the shared server. The 0.1.0 preview below only talked to a test server on your own PC.
Added
• Stones on the world map. Every stone you know of now shows on the
world map, so there's always somewhere to head for. Sealed stones (ones
you haven't been to yet) are bigger and glow softly. Stones you've read
and your own sit back, and appraised ones are gold. Hovering a pin says
how far away it is and in which direction, but never what it says: you
still have to stand where it was left to read it.
• A count under the world map: "Durotar: 4 sealed soapstones to find ·
2 read", for whichever zone or continent you're looking at.
• Guide me there. Click a stone's pin on the world map, or type
/soap guide for the nearest sealed stone. With TomTom installed,
its arrow points the way. Without it, Soapstone uses the game's own map
pin and in-world marker. The waypoint clears itself
once you're close enough to read the stone, and a map pin you set
yourself is never touched. /soap guide off stops guiding.
• The Soapstone companion (early preview). A small app for your
system tray that shares stones between players through a shared
database, and installs and keeps Soapstone up to date for you. This
release includes a first preview, Soapstone-Companion-v0.1.0-setup.exe.
It talks to a test server on your own PC, so it doesn't share stones with
other players yet; a public server comes next.
• With the companion running, Soapstone loads its stones (and drawings)
when you log in or /reload, and tells you if a stone of yours couldn't
be shared, and why. The minimap button's tooltip and /soap stats say
when it last synced.
• Soapstone keeps a list of your drops, edits, deletes, appraisals and the
stones you've opened, for the companion to upload, including stones you
left before this update. /soap stats shows how many are waiting.
• Sync. Shift-click the minimap button, or type /soap sync, to share
your latest changes and pick up new stones from the companion right away
(it reloads your UI). The old player-to-player zone sync moved to
/soap net sync.
Fixed
• Stones missing since the October 5 beta patch are back. The patch
changed how WoW Forever identifies itself, so Soapstone took it for a
different game and hid every stone left before it. Stones dropped since
then were filed under the wrong game too. All of them show again.
Changed
• Each character reads stones for themselves. A stone your main has
read is still sealed for your alts until they've stood there too,
including stones your other characters left. Stones you'd already read
before this update stay read for everyone.

Install: download Soapstone-v0.5.0.zip and unzip it into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, so you get AddOns\Soapstone\Soapstone.toc. Then restart the game.

Companion preview (optional): Soapstone-Companion-v0.1.0-setup.exe installs the companion for your Windows user (no admin prompt). It finds WoW Forever, installs Soapstone if it's missing, and sits in your system tray, starting with Windows (you can turn that off in its tray menu). It's an early preview for testing: it talks to a test server on your own PC (http://127.0.0.1:8787, from server/ in this repo), so it doesn't share stones with other players yet. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Choose More info, then Run anyway.

Removed
• The chime when you reach a stone you can read. The "somewhere close" cue
still plays as you approach, and the minimap button still glows while
you're in range.

Install: download Soapstone-v0.4.1.zip and unzip it into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, so you get AddOns\Soapstone\Soapstone.toc. Then restart the game.

Added
• Sounds: a crystal settling into place as you set a stone down, and an
aura fading away as you delete one. /soap sound off mutes them with the
other cues.
• /soap sound previews any sound cue (near, read, appraise,
disparage, drop, delete) and names the sound it played.
Changed
• What you type is what they'll read: writing a stone ("Leave a
Soapstone" → Write) and editing one ("Edit Soapstone") use the same
message box, in the stone window's text size, centred, and wrapping at
the same width. On Write the window sits snugly around the box; Draw
grows it for the drawing editor.
• "Edit Soapstone" no longer shows an "Editable for …" countdown: the clock
is paused while you edit, and the stone's Edit button shows the time
left.

Install: download Soapstone-v0.4.0.zip and unzip it into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, so you get AddOns\Soapstone\Soapstone.toc. Then restart the game.

Safety fixes for the companion and the shared server, and Soapstone 0.5.1 included.
Fixed
• Stones can't fake system messages any more. WoW formatting codes in a stone or a name (colours, links, pictures) are shown as plain text. The shared server now refuses them too.
• Nobody can take over your stones. A stone claiming the id of someone else's is refused.
• Fairer scores. One computer counts as one appraisal and one find per stone, however many characters it shares as (up to 20).
• Quieter syncing. The companion syncs every 3 minutes while WoW is running and every 30 minutes otherwise; a /reload or logout still shares your changes within seconds.

The shared server also gained rate limits, a starter word filter, a 12-hour limit on edits, and sanity checks on dates. See SECURITY.md for what Soapstone protects and the risks we know about.
Install
1. Download Soapstone-Companion-v0.2.2-setup.exe below and run it, or install it over an earlier version. It installs just for your Windows user, with no admin prompt, and updates Soapstone to 0.5.1.
2. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Choose More info, then Run anyway.
3. Restart WoW once so it picks up the new files. After that, a /reload is enough.

A fix for anyone who used the 0.1.0 preview: your existing stones now upload to the shared server.
Fixed
• Stones you left with the 0.1.0 preview now reach the shared server. The preview talked to a test server on your own PC. Once that server had your stones, Soapstone stopped listing them as waiting, so 0.2.0 never sent them to the shared server. Now, the first time the companion syncs with a server, it sends everything your characters already have: your stones, your appraisals and the stones you've opened. If a daily limit holds some back, it tries again the next day until they're all in.

Everything else is as in 0.2.0: the companion shares stones through the shared server and installs or updates Soapstone (0.5.0 is included).
Install
1. Download Soapstone-Companion-v0.2.1-setup.exe below and run it, or install it over 0.2.0. It installs just for your Windows user, with no admin prompt.
2. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Choose More info, then Run anyway.
3. Restart WoW once so it picks up the companion's data. After that, a /reload is enough.

Check your download: the installer's SHA-256 is 3ccdce5197eab02a57184ac024da066e50aa58628136637acbfc1abef35bc485 (in PowerShell: Get-FileHash .\Soapstone-Companion-v0.2.1-setup.exe). Soapstone-v0.5.0.zip is dad96fb610f6e4894cc6d90fd03d6d1154dd39dacdd649385a0a5a6f299f68a8. Only download Soapstone from this page.
Beta
Expect rough edges. If something looks wrong, please open an issue.

The Soapstone companion now shares stones between players. It's a small app for your system tray that connects Soapstone to a shared database: stones other players left (and their drawings) show up in your game, and yours reach them.
What it does
• Shares your stones: your drops, edits, deletes, appraisals and the stones you've opened upload within seconds of a /reload or logout.
• Brings back everyone else's: stones from the zones you've visited arrive at your next login or /reload. Shift-click the minimap button (or type /soap sync) to sync right away.
• Installs Soapstone for you: it finds WoW Forever and installs or updates the addon (0.5.0 is included). It never touches SavedVariables, a copy you changed by hand, or a newer version you installed yourself.
• Stays out of the way: it lives in the system tray and starts with Windows (untick Start with Windows in its tray menu to stop that). Click the tray icon to see what it's doing.

It only reads and writes Soapstone's own files, the way the WeakAuras Companion does, and never touches the game itself.
Install
1. Download Soapstone-Companion-v0.2.0-setup.exe below and run it. It installs just for your Windows user, with no admin prompt.
2. The installer isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Choose More info, then Run anyway.
3. Restart WoW once so it picks up the companion's data. After that, a /reload is enough.

If you'd rather install the addon by hand, Soapstone-v0.5.0.zip is attached too; it's the same as in the 0.5.0 release.
Upgrading from the 0.1.0 preview
Install over it. It switches from the local test server to the shared one by itself.
Beta
This is the first version that talks to the shared server, so expect rough edges. If something looks wrong, please open an issue. Windows only for now.

addons.description:
Chattery is a World of Warcraft addon that removes the size limit on chat messages, similar to addons like Emote Splitter or Unlimited Chat Message.

Features
• Automatically splits long chat messages into chunks the game can support
• Preserves TRP chat highlighting across messages
• A character counter on the chat editbox
• Optional auto capitalization and punctuation
• Undo (ctrl-z) support if you accidentally delete your message
• 100% human-written code
CompatibilityFriends
• Works great alongside Eavesdropper, Languages, and Yapper EditBox.
Conflicts
• Incompatible with other chat message splitters like Emote Splitter or Unlimited Chat Message.
• Outdated RP addons often cause issues when sending chat messages while in instances, or in combat. Ensure your addons are up-to-date, and uninstall any that haven't been updated for Midnight.
• The most common suspects are Listener and CrossRP. If you have those enabled, you will encounter issues sending messages until they're updated for Midnight.

Source on GitHub ·

| /fmodels | Alternative to /models, with the same arguments |

AzeriteUI6 Change Log
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. Be aware that the [Unreleased] features are not yet available in the official tagged builds.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog
and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.
[1.0.17-RC] 2026-10-26
Added

Changed
• Now fully disables our own Action Bars when a conflicting addon like Bartender4 or Dominos is detected.
• May or may not make a few more Minimap icons fade out until moused over.
Fixed

[1.0.16-RC] 2026-10-22
Added
• Now creates an EditMode preset named "Azerite UI Default" if it doesn't exist, and applies it. The preset is a work in progress, more will be added to it.
• Added the command /resetlayout to forcefully reset the aforementioned EditMode layout. Might change that command later. Or add a button.

• Added simple toggle switches for Player, Pet, Focus, Target and Target of Target Unit Frames to the options menu.
Changed

Fixed

• Fixed the detection of conflicting addons, since apparently the whole API for this had changed.
[1.0.9-RC] 2026-10-18
• Fixed a bunch of things that magically broke.
• Updated a bunch of things that weren't previously updated.
[1.0.8-Alpha] 2026-10-17
Added

Fixed

• Now embeds all libraries directly in our repository, no externals. All credits appropriately given in the pkgmeta to ensure author rewards.

AzeriteUI 6.0 is a custom user interface for World of Warcraft.

Update: Currently in the process of unifying all current WoW versions into this addon. Elements and features that are blocked in Retail and Forever will not be included in the Classic versions either. This is not a bug, it's intentional to provide a unified user interface experience across versions again. Note that the addon currently is very limited, and I won't be answering questions related to when or if features will be available. It's a "wait and see" situation.
Configuring the UI
• /az Opens the options menu. The full and proper graphical options menu is not yet finished! In addition to the options menu we can also configure the user interface with the chat commands listed below. Note that the maximum number of bars is 8 for Retail and Forever, but 5 for all the Classic versions of the game.
• /enablebar n Enables action bar n (replace n with 1-8, pet or stance)
• /disablebar n Disables action bar n (replace n with 1-8, pet or stance)
• /resetpositions Resets all positions and sizes of our movable frames. Does not affect Blizzard's EditMode or frames controllable from it.
• /resetsettings Resets all settings like visible/enabled unit frames and action bars.
/lock
Toggles the movable frame anchors for this user interface. (Note that most of the default Blizzard elements are controlled by the game's own EditMode, so you need to enter it to move or scale these.)
• Mouse Wheel to scale/size a frame.
• Shift + Left Mouse Button to return a frame to its previous position.
• Shift + Right Mouse Button to return a frame to its default position.
/setbar
This command is used to configure a visible actionbar. It controls layout and number of buttons. Meant as an additional source of configuration, not a replacement for the options menu.
• barID (Required) The ID of the bar. This is 1-8 in Retail and Forever, 1-5 in other versions.
• layoutType (Optional) The layout type of the bar. This is either grid or zigzag, where grid is a standard bartender-like layout, and zigzag is the kind of layout the primary action bar by default has from button 9. This argument should always come directly after the barID.
• keywordPair (Optional) Pairs of keywords and numbers to configure the bar:
• zigzag from n This includes layoutType and directly follows barID. The zigzag pattern starts at button n, which can range from 1-12.
• max n Maximum number of buttons on the bar, where n can range from 1-12. Applies to all layoutTypes.
• size n The maximum length/width of a bar in number of buttons before a new line of buttons begin. Only applies to layoutType grid.
• fade from n Fade out the buttons starting from button number n.
• nofade Single instruction indicating this bar shouldn't fade at all. Only needed to disable a fade that was previously set.
• right left up down
• These are keywords that need to come as a pair of two; one horizontal, one vertical. These decide the growth of the bar. If you start with up or down, the bar will grow vertically first, typically a sidebar. If you start with right or left, the bar will grow horizontally first. To grow the bar right and have a new row start beneath it, you should use right down.
Example Layout Commands

AzeriteUI6 Change Log
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. Be aware that the [Unreleased] features are not yet available in the official tagged builds.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog
and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.
[1.0.18-Alpha] 2026-11-03
Added
• Added XP bar to the Classic Minimap.
• Added the forgotten Minimap backdrop texture to the Classics.
• Added a character specific GamePad layout to the EditMode in Forever, since GamePads are more officially supported there. If you wish to enable GamePad usage in non-Forever clients, use /console GamePadEnable 1. Note that a specific GamePad EditMode layout is not created for this UI in any other clients than Forever.
Changed
• Adjusted the default Classic Tooltip position to match Retail.
• The default EditMode preset created by this UI is now Character specific, not Account wide.
Removed
• Removed any existing Account wide EditMode presets created by this UI.
[1.0.17-RC] 2026-10-26
Added
• Added XP bar to the Retail/Forever Minimap.
Changed
• Now fully disables our own Action Bars when a conflicting addon like Bartender4 or Dominos is detected.
• May or may not make a few more Minimap icons fade out until moused over.
Fixed
• Fixed an issue that caused a reset of the settings through the options menu to fail.
[1.0.16-RC] 2026-10-22
Added
• Now creates an EditMode preset named "Azerite UI Default" if it doesn't exist, and applies it. The preset is a work in progress, more will be added to it.
• Added the command /resetlayout to forcefully reset the aforementioned EditMode layout. Might change that command later. Or add a button.
[1.0.14-RC] 2026-10-21
Added
• Added fading options to the Action Bar menus.
• Added simple toggle switches for Player, Pet, Focus, Target and Target of Target Unit Frames to the options menu.
Changed
• Changed the options menu structure a bit, moved the module listing into the addon listing on the left.
Fixed
• Fixed an issue where neither ours nor the default nameplates were shown.
• Fixed the detection of conflicting addons, since apparently the whole API for this had changed.
[1.0.9-RC] 2026-10-18
• Fixed a bunch of things that magically broke.
• Updated a bunch of things that weren't previously updated.
[1.0.8-Alpha] 2026-10-17
Added
• Added a basic graphical options menu accessible with /az or through the Blizzard Options. Work in progress.
Fixed
• Fixed an issue where Multi Action Bar 2-8 all displayed the contents of the Primary Action Bar.
[1.0.7-Alpha] 2026-10-08
• Now embeds all libraries directly in our repository, no externals. All credits appropriately given in the pkgmeta to ensure author rewards.
• Added basic support for all current versions of the game:
• Classic Era 1.15.9.
• Burning Crusade Anniversary 2.5.6.
• Mists of Pandaria Classic 5.5.4.
• Forever 1.60.1.
• Midnight 12.1.0.
Added
• Added a chat based system to configure action bars. Currently in Alpha mode, will post usage information later. Note that this is not meant to replace a GUI, it's simply an addition that was faster to write and will provide the functionality until then. The commands will remain even when the GUI is done.
[1.0.5-RC] 2026-08-17
Fixed
• Fixed a bug causing the addon to break when the library LibSharedMedia was loaded. This is used by a lot of addons include nearly every addon showing timer bars.
[1.0.4-RC] 2026-08-12
• Updated toc version for WoW Retail Client Patch 12.1.0.
• Started fixing things for the WoW 12.1.0 API.
• Started updating for latest oUF changes
[1.0.2-Alpha] 2026-07-19
• Updated toc version for WoW Retail Client Patch 12.0.7.
[1.0.1-Alpha] 2026-05-26
• First public commit.

addons.description:
This is a simple plugin for the addon Bagnon that displays the label BoE on items in your bags that can still be traded or sold at the Auction House. No more accidental vendor sales of BoE epics from World Quests!

If you don't like the rarity coloring of the text, or find it hard to read, you can toggle it with the commands listed below. The settings are saved globally for all your characters.
Chat Commands
• /boe enable color - Enable rarity coloring of text.
• /boe disable color - Disable rarity coloring of text.

addons.description:
WeakAuras-lineage auras for World of Warcraft: Forever — working in combat.

EverAuras is a fork of M33kAuras (itself a fork of
WeakAuras 2), rebuilt for the World of Warcraft: Forever
client. Forever runs on the mainline (retail) engine and inherits the 12.1 "secret values" system,
which makes ordinary aura and cooldown data unreadable to addons the moment you enter combat,
anywhere: questing, dungeons or raids. Ported-as-is, WeakAuras is blind exactly when you need it.

EverAuras is not blind. It never reads the secret data; it hands the display to the game engine
and lets the client draw it.

> Status: beta (0.9.8), built on M33kAuras fd03b21 (release 5.20.7-rg4-m99) and developed against
> the Forever beta client (interface 16001). Blizzard patches can still break things; please report
> what you find on Discord or in the
> issues.
What works in combat
| Display | How |
|---|---|
| Your own auras on player / target / focus / pet, and your buffs on a group member (Specific Unit party1–4, raid1–40; debuffs there by Debuff Type only), by spell name (every rank you know, re-resolved as you level) or exact spell ID — show when present, show when missing, or both | The engine draws them through Blizzard's CustomAuraContainerTemplate. "Missing" is rendered by geometry the engine controls, so the icon genuinely disappears while the aura is up. |
| Time left — an icon that shows only while the aura has less (or more) than X seconds left (Remaining Time on Show On: Aura(s) Found), and the classic "missing or about to run out" icon (a Missing trigger plus Found + Remaining Time triggers, Required for Activation: Any Triggers) | The icon is engine-drawn text whose colour comes from a curve over the remaining time. The game evaluates the curve; the addon never reads the time. |
| Other triggers next to an aura trigger — e.g. in combat, target attackable, talent known | The engine draws the aura part; WeakAuras evaluates the other triggers itself, which works for plain data (health and power amounts stay secret). |
| Animated glow on engine-driven icons, textures and bars — Button Glow, Pixel Glow, Autocast Shine and Proc Glow, with your colours and settings — shown only while the display is (aura present, missing, or running out; a bar keeps the glow's anchor area) | The glow runs inside a frame whose width the engine controls from the aura, so it is clipped away exactly when the icon is. Everything is created inside that frame, because Blizzard refuses to move frames into it, and everything moves by animation (Path, FlipBook), because the game refuses to let addon code re-position anything anchored to its aura frames while an aura is shown. For the last X seconds of an aura, a clip anchored to the fill edge of a bar the game sizes by the remaining time opens exactly when X seconds are left. A display with a missing and a time-left part chooses where the glow goes. |…

A fix release for the latest WoW Forever beta update, which caused a flood of Lua errors for many addons, InvurseUI included.

Fixes
• No more Lua errors from the beta's new addon restrictions. The beta now hides some unit information from addons ("secret values"), especially in combat, and addons that tried to read it threw errors. InvurseUI now treats hidden information as unknown and carries on.
• Threat glow: when the game hides a mob's threat information, that nameplate simply shows no glow instead of erroring.
• Level beside the name: works with names the game hides in combat. If the level itself is hidden, it's shown without the difficulty color.
• Unit frame colors: class and power colors no longer error when that information is hidden.
• The addon no longer errors if a future build removes a Blizzard function or event it hooks.

Install
Download InvurseUI-2.1.zip, unzip it into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ (replacing the old InvurseUI folder), and restart the game. Your settings carry over from 2.0.

🤖 Generated with Claude Code
addons.description:
A lightweight addon for World of Warcraft Forever that makes subtle changes to the stock Blizzard UI. It grew out of Forever Nameplates and keeps that addon's threat glow, then adds a few small touches elsewhere:
• Nameplates: a threat-colored glow around the health bar, and the mob's level shown next to its name (16 - Forest Spider) instead of in a box on the right.
• Textures: flat bar textures for the player, target and party frames, the raid frames, the damage meter and, optionally, the nameplates.
• Fonts: change the font used across the standard UI.
NameplatesThreat glow
| Glow | Tank mode (default) | DPS / Healer mode |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 Safe | You have solid aggro | — |
| 🟡 Warning | You're about to lose aggro, or you're about to take it back | You're close to pulling aggro |
| 🔴 Danger | Someone else has aggro (including a mob already hitting a groupmate) | You've pulled aggro |
| No glow | Out of combat, friendly or dead | Everything else |
Level beside the name
The level box on the right of the bar is removed and the level is shown in front of the name instead, colored by difficulty. Elites get a + (16+ - Defias Overseer), and mobs too high to tell show ??. The health bar uses the freed-up space.
Textures
Choose Flat (solid color), Smooth (flat with a very light shade) or Blizzard default, and pick where it applies:
• Player, target and party frames (health and mana)
• Raid frames
• Damage meter
• Nameplate health bars (off by default)

With a flat texture, player, target and party health bars are classic green, or class colored for players if you prefer.

Switching an area back to Blizzard's textures asks you to reload the UI.
Fonts
Pick a font for the standard UI. The built-in game fonts are always listed, along with the bundled Roboto family (Regular, Medium, Bold, Condensed and Condensed Bold, under the SIL Open Font License) and any fonts other addons register with LibSharedMedia. Floating combat text picks up the new font after you log out and back in.
Options
Type /iui or go to Esc → Options → AddOns → InvurseUI. Each section (Nameplates, Textures, Fonts) has its own page.
Slash commands
| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| /iui | Open the options panel |
| /iui tank / /iui dps | Switch threat mode |
| /iui toggle | Turn the threat glow on or off |
| /iui size | Set the glow thickness |
| /iui alpha | Set the glow opacity |
| /iui reset | Reset all settings to their defaults |
| /iui help | List these commands |

/fnp still works as an alias.

Fixed

• The label of a character leaves as soon as you clear your target, and no longer jumps to someone else while you turn the camera.
• The minimap is moved up only where Wanderer's look puts it: placed elsewhere by you or another addon, it stays there.
• The quest tracker's dashes get their color back when its look is turned off.
• The junk sale reads your bags more surely.

Wanderer 0.43.1Changed
• Wanderer's stacked layout takes a new look, shaped in game: the stance bar over the highest bar with the vehicle's exit beside it and the swing timers above its right end, the pet and totem bars against the main bar, the cast bar under your portrait with the durability beside it, the tooltip left of the game's menu. The clean layout follows the same look around its own bars.
• The damage meter sits over the bags in both layouts.
Fixed
• The target's line no longer comes in front of your windows; the game's bank and auction house windows, kept out of sight behind Wanderer's, are never placed back on the screen.
• With the minimap in Wanderer's style, the game's ring no longer flashes back after a change of settings.
• Lighter: the quest tracker dressed once per drawing, what you play read once.

Wanderer 0.43.0New
• What you play: a list of the ways your class is played (a bear and a cat for a feral druid), chosen by you and kept for each character. The green arrow, the tooltips and the extensions judge your gear for it; nothing is guessed.
• Three looks of Wanderer's own, offered on a new step of the welcome screen and in the options: the minimap with soft edges, its icons apart and the zone, time and coordinates below it; the quest tracker in small golden capitals on a transparent ground; a quiet bar at the top of the screen (the menu, the reminders, your extensions' windows, the other addons' icons), which takes the minimap button's place.
• The Wanderer addons you do not have yet are offered in Wanderer's menu and on a step of the welcome screen; your extensions' news show with Wanderer's.
Changed
• An item is "better" only in your class's best armor type: cloth is never better for one who wears leather.
• A weight changed, what you play or your talents: the comparisons are judged again at once, in Wanderer and its extensions, without a reload.
• Quest levels in the colors of your quest log.
• Every action in Wanderer's windows is a real button.
• The ways to play of the welcome screen go further: the immersive ones also make the profiles by place (all the interface and the damage meter in dungeons, a quiet city), the dungeons' one shows the damage meter, and the minimap in Wanderer's style comes with each of them.
• Wanderer's Edit Mode layouts set the game's damage meter on the right of the action bars, over the bags.
• Lighter: only your language is loaded; the quest tracker and the minimap follow the game's events rather than timers.
Fixed
• With a two-handed weapon, an off-hand item is no longer said to be better, and a one-hander is weighed against the two-hander alone.
• Windows behave as on a desktop: none is pushed under another or hidden behind the map any more, with a title bar or not, the game's or another addon's; the last opened or clicked comes in front.

Wanderer 0.42.0New
• One engine for every window of Wanderer and its extensions: the same transparency (never so faint that text is hard to read), the same headings, tables, buttons, questions and tooltips everywhere.
• The extensions learn from Wanderer which of your items your quests ask you to carry (Wanderer Bags marks them, Wanderer Auction never offers them for sale).
Changed
• Lighter at login: what features removed long ago had left in your saved settings is let go (about 40 % of the file), and the record of who gives which quest forgets the quests you have done.
• The stat weights button sits under the character sheet, never hidden.
Fixed
• Opening the map no longer pushes the windows already open under it.
• The reminders and private messages windows keep their place and size again.

[0.6.2]
• Emote phrases. Cast phrases now have a sibling: wave, bow, cheer or
/hello, and every so often your character says something to go with it --
Corvin waves. Corvin calls out "Hello there!" -- in whatever tongue you are
speaking, accent and all. Switch it on in the new Emotes section of Cast
Phrases, below Spells. It has its own chance (30% to start with) and its own
two pauses -- after any emote line, and before the same emote speaks again
-- set apart from the spell ones, so a cast line never silences an emote.
The shipped lines are speech that follows the game's own emote ("Corvin
bows before you." then "Corvin says "At your service.""), never the action
a second time.
• Changed: cast and emote phrases follow the Emote channel. A phrase goes
out as an emote, so its quoted speech is now translated (and accented) only
while Emote is ticked under Chat Channels -- the same switch as a typed
/e. With it off, the line is still said, in plain English. Emote is off
by default, so tick it if you want your phrases in your tongue. Thirty-four emotes ship with lines, in a list of
their own, where you can reword, weight, remove or add to them exactly as
you would a spell's. To write lines for an emote that isn't listed, type it
-- /dance -- in the box beside that list. /glyphic cast emotes turns it
on and off from chat.
• Settings pages are split into sections. Every page now has titled
sections with a divider above each -- Spells, Emotes and Hearing other
players on Cast Phrases; What you speak, Full immersion, Your voice and Your
languages on Languages & Fluency; and so on -- instead of reading as one
long page.
• Fixed: out-of-character (asides) were garbled by Full immersion.
Glyphic has always left text in parentheses alone when you speak, but a
listener with Remove in-game learned languages on garbled the whole line
anyway -- so a quick "(brb, door)" in a tongue they had not studied reached
them as gibberish, as though it had never been sent. Parentheses in chat now
stay legible on their end too. Quest text is unchanged.
• Fixed: accents no longer add an interjection to OOC text. A long line in
parentheses could still come out as "(back in five, sorry all), mon.",
because the length check counted the words inside the aside. Only words the
accent actually speaks count now, and a line that ends in an aside is left
without a flourish.
• The Troll accent is thicker at the top of the slider. From 45% it uses
the habitual "be" -- "I'm not really sure I be wantin' to go dat way." --
once per line, and every time from 70%. It also picks up "don'", "ain't"
and "cyan'" for don't, isn't/aren't and can't.
• Changed: the Troll accent no longer says "I an' I". At heavy strength
"I think I will" read "I an' I tink I an' I will" -- and it is not something
WoW's trolls say in the first place. It is gone entirely.
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft roleplay addon that turns your chat into the languages and dialects
of Azeroth, in the style of the classic Tongues addon. It covers 66 languages, from the
eldritch Old God (Shath'yar) tongue and the playable-race languages through to beast,
elemental and faction tongues. You can also drop the language entirely and speak plain
English in a spoken accent instead: Dwarven, Troll, Pirate and more. There's a
Wordle-style language trainer in there too, for earning fluency and decoding what other
people say.

Your character can speak out loud as well, using the game's own voice actors. 30,572
recordings from 2,560 speakers, already sitting on your disk, pinned to whatever your
character says when you cast.

Runs on every client: Retail (Midnight), Forever, and Classic (Vanilla / Cata / Mists /
Wrath), all from a single install. A feature-detected compatibility layer (Compat.lua)
adapts the UI and chat APIs to whichever client it loads on.

The playable-race languages use Blizzard's own in-game language parser word lists
(documented on Wowpedia / Warcraft Wiki), the same word tables the game uses to mask
speech you can't understand. Each word you type is replaced by a word of the *same
letter-length* from that language's list, so the output runs the length of the input and
reads like the real in-game language.

Translation is deterministic. The same word in the same language always produces the same
output, so sentences stay internally consistent and any two people running the addon
generate identical text.

Nothing happens until you ask it to. A new character starts out of character, knowing no
tongue, set to None (speak plainly) with no accent, so installing the addon won't change
a word you type. Pick a language, learn it in the trainer or set your fluency, and flip to
in character when you want to be heard in it.

Features
• 66 languages and dialects. The 11 core playable-race and Old God languages, plus dozens
of generated tongues: beasts and creatures (Wolf, Bear, Serpent, Cat, Bird, Raptor…),
factions (Dark Iron, Gilnean, Goblin, Ogre, Vrykul, Furbolg…), and the elemental and
eldritch ones (Kalimag, Titan, Draconic, Nerubian, Nazja, Ethereal…). The Troll and Elf
sub-dialects share their parent's vocabulary but bend it, so Amani, Gurubashi and
Drakkari come out recognisably Zandali without being identical to it.
• Accents, which flavor your English with a spoken dialect rather than translating it.
There are eight: Dwarven ("I cannae do this, aye!"), Troll ("da voodoo, mon."),
Orcish, Draenei, Goblin, Gilnean, Vrykul and Pirate. Each has its own strength
slider, so you can go subtle or thick.
• A language trainer, called Decipher. It's a Wordle-style minigame: pick a language,
solve daily-style word puzzles, climb reputation ranks, and build fluency, shown on
live progress bars. Solving words unlocks partial decoding of that language before
you're fully fluent.
• Fluency you earn by playing, two ways, both switchable on the trainer panel.
Overhearing another player's tagged speech slowly teaches you that tongue. And
finishing a quest teaches you one word of the language its giver spoke -- literally
one word: fluency is already the fraction of words that come through clear, so a word
out of Orcish's hundred is one percent, and a hundred quests makes you fluent. Zandali
is 77 words and Gnomish is 128, so those take 77 and 128 quests. While levelling only
green-or-better quests count, so you can't farm a starting zone; at the level cap,
where nothing pays experience any more, everything counts. A small draggable toast
says Word Learned! and shows you the word with what it is the word for --
Pikialo = learned -- over the tongue and your count. The pair is real: Blizzard's
word lists carry no meanings, but the client picks a tongue's word by hashing the
English one, so "learned" renders as exactly one Taur-ahe token every time. That…

releases.changelog:
[0.6.2]
• Emote phrases. Cast phrases now have a sibling: wave, bow, cheer or
/hello, and every so often your character says something to go with it --
Corvin waves. Corvin calls out "Hello there!" -- in whatever tongue you are
speaking, accent and all. Switch it on in the new Emotes section of Cast
Phrases, below Spells. It has its own chance (30% to start with) and its own

The shipped lines are speech that follows the game's own emote ("Corvin
bows before you." then "Corvin says "At your service.""), never the action
a second time.
• Changed: cast and emote phrases follow the Emote channel. A phrase goes
out as an emote, so its quoted speech is now translated (and accented) only
while Emote is ticked under Chat Channels -- the same switch as a typed
/e. With it off, the line is still said, in plain English. Emote is off
by default, so tick it if you want your phrases in your tongue. Thirty-four emotes ship with lines, in a list of
their own, where you can reword, weight, remove or add to them exactly as
you would a spell's. To write lines for an emote that isn't listed, type it

on and off from chat.
• Settings pages are split into sections. Every page now has titled
sections with a divider above each -- Spells, Emotes and Hearing other
players on Cast Phrases; What you speak, Full immersion, Your voice and Your
languages on Languages & Fluency; and so on -- instead of reading as one
long page.
• Fixed: out-of-character (asides) were garbled by Full immersion.
Glyphic has always left text in parentheses alone when you speak, but a
listener with Remove in-game learned languages on garbled the whole line
anyway -- so a quick "(brb, door)" in a tongue they had not studied reached
them as gibberish, as though it had never been sent. Parentheses in chat now
stay legible on their end too. Quest text is unchanged.
• Fixed: accents no longer add an interjection to OOC text. A long line in
parentheses could still come out as "(back in five, sorry all), mon.",
because the length check counted the words inside the aside. Only words the
accent actually speaks count now, and a line that ends in an aside is left
without a flourish.
• The Troll accent is thicker at the top of the slider. From 45% it uses
the habitual "be" -- "I'm not really sure I be wantin' to go dat way." --
once per line, and every time from 70%. It also picks up "don'", "ain't"
and "cyan'" for don't, isn't/aren't and can't.
• Changed: the Troll accent no longer says "I an' I". At heavy strength
"I think I will" read "I an' I tink I an' I will" -- and it is not something
WoW's trolls say in the first place. It is gone entirely.

[0.6.1]
• Fixed: a Lua error when quest text worked out who was talking to you. On
Midnight the client hands an addon some unit text as a "secret" value, which
looks like ordinary text right up until it is read, and the tooltip of
whoever was standing in front of you is the likeliest place for one. Reading
the NPC's reputation faction threw attempt to index field '?' (a secret
string value) on those units -- so the quest you were being offered stayed
in plain English, and you got an error window for it. Their race and their
side are screened the same way now, as is /glyphic quests, which was
reading all three to tell you why a troll was speaking Orcish.
• Fixed: Glyphic no longer builds a hidden tooltip on modern clients. It
was the fallback for reading a unit's faction on clients with no tooltip
data API, which is the Classic flavours and nothing else. Setting a unit on
a tooltip runs Blizzard's own tooltip code, and running that from an addon's
own execution is what produces bad argument #1 to 'UnitPlayerControlled'
inside GameTooltip_UnitColor -- an error with no Glyphic file anywhere in
it, which is the kind nobody can trace. Retail and Forever answer the same
question as data, so there was nothing to fall back for.

[0.6.0]
• Full immersion. A new option under Languages & Fluency: *Remove in-game
learned languages*. With it on, Common and your racial tongues stop being
automatic -- you read them exactly as well as your fluency in this addon
says you do, and no better. A night elf who never studied Orcish cannot read
Orcish, whatever her character sheet says.
The garbled text is the game's own. Glyphic uses Blizzard's actual word
tables and Blizzard's actual hash, so a line hidden by the addon reads the
way a line hidden by the client reads -- right down to "lol" coming out
"Kek". Partial fluency works the way the game's does too: the same words
stay legible every time, so re-reading a line never changes what it said.
Off by default and it stays off; this is not something to discover after an
update. NPCs have their own separate switch, since a boss callout is a
mechanic as much as it is flavour. Which channels it applies to follows your
existing Chat Channel settings.
• General, Trade and custom channels, under a switch of their own. Full
immersion works by taking back a translation the client already performed, and
those channels never got one: the game attaches no language to them at all,
which left a hole you could see through. The stranger beside you was
unintelligible in /say and perfectly intelligible one channel over.
Closing it means lending those lines a tongue they never had, so it is asked
for by name and off by default. The tongue is your own faction's -- the same
one the people around you are speaking, so a line of Trade chat reads as the
language of the person standing next to you rather than as a fifth thing.
Emotes are left alone either way. An emote is narration, not speech, and
running "Thrall waves." through a tongue has the narrator speaking a foreign
language about somebody in the third person.
The Mythic challenge turns it on and holds it there. Trade chat is how a
player finds a group, a summon or a portal, which is why no other tier takes
it -- on the three tiers you level through, losing that is a cost nobody
signed up for. On Mythic, being unable to ask is the run.
• Quest text, gossip and the objective tracker, under a third switch of
their own, nested under the NPC one and off even when everything above it is
on. Everything else immersion touches is text the client would have garbled
by itself; a quest window carries no language at all, so hiding one is the
addon's own idea and has to be asked for by name rather than arriving with
the rest.
An orc quest giver hands you an offer in Orcish; a night elf hands you one
in Darnassian. It's remembered per quest, so your journal still reads in the
tongue of whoever gave it to you long after they're out of sight.
Quests already in your log when you switch this on fall back to your own
faction's tongue -- Orcish for Horde, Common for Alliance. Nothing in the
game will tell an addon who gave you a quest after the fact, so this is
knowingly the wrong answer for the tauren who actually handed it over; the
alternative is a log that stays in English forever for everything you were
carrying that day. Handing one in replaces the guess with the truth, since
returning to the giver is the second and last occasion they and the quest
are in the same place, so the log corrects itself as you play.
A quest with nobody behind it is a separate case and stays in plain words:
one you start by right-clicking something in your bags, or by walking into
a place, or off a bulletin board. There is no API that says "this came from
an item" and none is needed -- the absence of a speaker is the signal, and
it is recorded as an answer so those never get swept into the guess above.
Working out which tongue that is takes some doing, because the game does not
tell addons an NPC's race and never has -- race is a thing player characters
have, and a quest giver is a creature with a model. Asking is not an option,
so Glyphic reads two things it can see and takes the stronger one.…

[0.5.6]
• Fixed: importing a profile threw an error. The settings were applied
correctly and the interface still reloaded, so nothing was lost or left
half-imported -- but the confirmation threw a Lua error on its way out,
which is not what you want to see on the screen that just told you your
settings were being replaced. The same fault was waiting on the "import
failed" path.

[0.5.5]
• The tongues your race already speaks are shown by default. Hiding them
is defensible -- the game already translates those for you -- but it reads
as the addon being broken: a night elf opens the list, finds no Darnassian,
and reasonably concludes it is missing. The option is still there under
Languages, and turning it back on sticks.
• Fixed: the accent list on the project page and in the README still named
Darnassian, Tauren, Forsaken and Pandaren, which were retired back in
0.2.14. There are eight accents and now the documentation says so. Nothing
changed in the addon -- it was the description that was wrong.

addons.description:
Join the Discord

Bring the grit, craft, and character of Warcraft into your interface.

Jiberish's Frostforge adds sculpted artwork around your portraits, health and power bars, cast bars, action bars, and minimap. Build a matching look for your class, race, or faction—from Paladin wings and Priest stonework to Druid roots and Shaman totems.

The Igloo · Artwork gallery · Getting started · Compatibility · Report an issue

Artwork showcase using the addon's actual textures. See the gallery for labeled previews and an early in-game capture.

Current source: 0.9.2 · Development preview. Retail and Forever packages are built separately. Automated checks cover behavior, artwork fitting and packaging; live-client compatibility and custom layouts still need player testing. There are no packaged GitHub releases published yet. To test from source, build an installable ZIP.
Make it your own
• 42 matching themes: 13 classes, 26 races, and Alliance, Horde and Neutral. Each has portrait, unit-frame, action-hub, minimap and cast-bar artwork.
• Independent artwork toggles: use portrait surrounds, full unit-frame shells and cast-bar borders separately on Player, Target and Focus.
• Automatic identity: follow a unit's class, race or faction, or choose a fixed design. Recognized city NPCs use the matching existing race artwork; for example, Undercity → Undead and Stormwind → Human.
• Fit your layout: adjust size, offsets, scale and layers. Portrait art, unit-frame art and cast borders each have their own strata. Unit-frame shells have separate width, height and position controls. Bold cast borders have their own width, height, weight and spacing.
• Stock Blizzard controls: hide the portrait image or surround, adjust text, use stone and class gradients on health, and choose custom power colors or gradients—including party and raid bars. Move Target/Focus buff/debuff groups and cast bars with separate position controls.
• A shared stone material: choose Frostforge Stone in compatible EllesmereUI, ElvUI and other LibSharedMedia status-bar texture menus.
• A Warcraft-style settings workshop: searchable artwork collections, per-component controls, reset options and copy/paste settings backups.
• Character profiles: save named setups and assign them per character. New alts start separately; copy a layout or deliberately share one. Profile guide.

Your frame provider continues to handle health and power values, casts, names, portraits, auras and clicks. Frostforge's decorations are click-through. Full unit-frame styling can apply fill textures and fit power-bar spacing to the artwork; disabling it restores the provider's layout and any fills it managed. The separate stock-wide stone toggle can keep Blizzard bars textured even without shells.
Works with your UI
These are the integrations implemented in the current build. Support depends on the provider's enabled modules and layout; this table is not a claim that every combination has been validated in game.

| UI / addon | Portrait art | Full unit-frame shells | Cast-bar borders | Action hub |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blizzard UI | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| EllesmereUI | Yes, with a separate portrait | Yes, for compatible bar layouts¹ | Yes | Yes |
| ElvUI | Yes, with a separate portrait | Yes¹ | Yes | Yes |
| Blinkii's Portraits | Yes | Uses another provider | Uses another provider | Uses another provider |
| mMediaTag & Tools | Yes, through ElvUI | Uses ElvUI¹ | Uses ElvUI | Uses ElvUI |

¹ ElvUI and Ellesmere full shells require horizontal health with power attached and aligned below it. ElvUI inset/mini/offset power and detached, above-health or vertical power layouts do not receive a full shell. When power is hidden or absent, complete artwork follows health with a dark empty power opening. Separate/circular portraits give the closest portrait fit; portraits drawn inside health bars have no separate surround to decorate.…

addons.description:
English | Español

Addon for World of Warcraft: Forever and WoW Classic Era (including Hardcore and Season of Discovery) that helps you get ready for dungeons.
It plays a sound when you pass near a vendor and your bags are almost full or your gear is damaged, sells your junk and repairs for you, and includes a notes window and an expense tracker.
Features
• Nearby vendor alert: plays a sound when you see a known vendor and your bags are over 80% full (configurable).
• Learns vendors automatically: each vendor is saved the first time you open their window, including whether they can repair.
• Auto-sell greys when you open a vendor, with a summary of the gold earned.
• Auto-repair if the vendor can repair and you have enough gold.
• Low durability warning when any gear piece drops below 30% (configurable).
• Notes: a small window to write your to-dos, movable and collapsible. Each character has its own notes.
• Expense tracker: what you spend on repairs and earn from sales, by week, month and total, with the balance.
• Minimap icon: left-click opens notes, right-click opens expenses. Drag it to move it.
• English and Spanish: follows your game language, or choose one with /va lang.
• Custom sound: use your own audio file.

Special bags (quivers, ammo pouches, soul bags) don't count towards the fill percentage.

addons.description:
Lightweight, native-first quality-of-life improvements for WoW Forever.

GitHub releases · CurseForge · WowUp Hub (link coming soon)

Murgle is for players who like Blizzard's UI, but want it cleaner, less intrusive and a little smarter.

It removes unnecessary clutter, automates repetitive interactions and exposes useful native functionality without replacing the game's interface with a large addon framework.

> Blizzard, just cleaner.

Lightweight by design
Performance is a core part of Murgle's design rather than an afterthought.

The in-game profiler reported 0% average CPU and approximately 459 KB memory
during testing. These are reported measurements, not a claim of zero CPU cost.

Murgle has:
• No external runtime libraries
• No Ace3 or LibStub
• No permanent polling loops
• Settings UI created only when opened

Murgle prefers Blizzard's own APIs, CVars and UI elements wherever possible.

Its general approach is:

Native Blizzard functionality → one-time change → event → narrow hook

Continuous background processing and replacement systems are deliberately avoided.

> Performance figures were measured during in-game testing and may vary depending on enabled features and client state.

HighlightsClean up Blizzard's interface
Remove the parts of the default UI you don't need while keeping Blizzard's underlying interface intact.
• Hide Micro Menu
• Hide Bag Bar
• Hide XP bar
• Hide macro names
• Fade action bars during combat, including 0% opacity to hide them visually
• Hide totem timers
• Hide Talking Head
• Hide Boss Banner
• Hide large zone text
• Hide Objective Tracker headers
• Adjust Objective Tracker font size
• Control Objective Tracker visibility
• Show the buff collapse arrow only on hover
• Block new help tips
• Block standard loot-reward toasts

A cleaner minimap
Keep Blizzard's minimap, but strip away unwanted artwork and buttons.
• Square Minimap with a subtle border
• Hide minimap rim
• Hide day/night artwork
• Hide minimap header
• Hide zone text
• Hide clock
• Hide calendar
• Hide tracking button
• Hide zoom buttons
• Hide addon compartment

Square mode uses the existing Blizzard minimap rather than replacing it.

Compact Blizzard unit frames
Murgle cleans up Blizzard's existing secure unit frames instead of replacing them.
Player
• Compact Player Frame
• Remove portrait and decorative artwork
• Hide player level
• Hide resting artwork and animation
• Optional player-name hiding
Target
• Compact Target Frame
• Cleaner artwork and presentation
• Optional enemy-player faction icon filtering
Target of Target
• Compact Target-of-Target frame

Native health, power and unit-frame interactions remain intact.

Native nameplate visibility
Control when Blizzard's own nameplates are shown without processing individual nameplates.

Available modes include:

Game settings · Combat · Hidden

Game settings means Murgle steps aside and respects your normal WoW configuration.

Quest automation without losing control
Automate predictable quest interactions while leaving anything that needs an actual decision to the player.
• Auto-accept eligible quests
• Auto turn-in when no reward choice or money cost is involved
• Hold Shift to keep an interaction manual
• Automation is bypassed during combat
• Reward choices, uncertain quest states and special confirmations remain manual

Murgle intentionally keeps quest automation conservative.

World Refresh handling
Murgle can handle WoW Forever's World Refresh warning through the specific native refresh UI.

Choose between:

Just hide

Hides the automatic warning. This does not cancel the scheduled transfer.

Accept & hide

Accepts the transfer and hides the warning.

> Accept & hide is not recommended for Hardcore characters.

Manually opened prompts remain available.

Spell Queue Window
Adjust WoW's native Spell Queue Window directly from Murgle.
• Adjustable 0–400 ms
• Blizzard default clearly marked at 400 ms
• On-demand latency-based suggestion…

addons.changelog:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
This project adheres to Semantic Versioning
Format inspired by Keep a Changelog

Changelog[7.0.0] - 2026-10-13
AzUI Color Picker is now ABCS – Advanced Bar Coloring System, as it colours far more than AzeriteUI's health bar. Your settings, profiles and share strings carry over as they are; the folder is still AzUI_Color_Picker, and /ahui works next to the new /abcs.

More unit frame addons, rules with two conditions and on every bar, rules you can try and turn around, new conditions and effects, heal and absorb overlays, a colour vision preview and /ahui check, on a lighter engine. Then the rest of your UI: class resources, threat and casting rules, a sound when a rule starts, setups shared through a link in chat, and translations on CurseForge.
Added
• Class resources (More Bars, off by default): combo points, holy power, chi, arcane charges, soul shards, essence and runes take your health bar's colour or their own colour and effect, on AzeriteUI (5.x, JuNNeZ Edition, AzeriteUI6), ElvUI, Unhalted Unit Frames and oUF layouts. Points that are not filled stay as faint as their addon draws them; Monk stagger keeps its own colour, as it says how heavy the stagger is. A rule can show on them too ("Show on: Class resources"), and Every bar includes them.
• Threat rules: "Threat: I have aggro", "Losing aggro" (tanking, with someone close behind) and "About to pull aggro" (above the tank without tanking). Casting rules: while you cast, channel, or either. Midnight can hide both answers in some content; the rule then waits rather than guess, turned around or not. Their events are only looked at while such a rule exists.
• A sound when a rule starts showing: raid warning, ready check, alarm clock, boss whisper, whisper, friend online or quest complete, on the Master channel so it is heard with sound effects off. Picked with the speaker on the rule's row (the classic window has a Sound list); picking one plays it, and Try plays it too. Logging in or changing profile shows rules without a sound.
• Two more ready-made rules: about to pull aggro when you are not the tank (orange heartbeat, raid warning sound) and a tank losing aggro (red pulse, alarm).
• Share in Chat (Share page): puts [ABCS: name] in your chat box for you to send. Anyone with the addon sees it as a link; clicking it fetches the parts you ticked from you with addon messages and opens them in the import preview, which says who they came from. Nothing changes until Import. Your last five links keep working after a log out, whenever you are online to answer. Where the game restricts addon messages (instances in combat, encounters) the click says so instead of waiting, and a request that gets no answer gives up after twelve seconds.

Current version: 7.0.0

Formerly AzUI Color Picker. Your settings carry over, and /ahui still works next to /abcs.

Lightweight Ace3-powered addon that lets you recolour and animate your own player health bar in AzeriteUI, ElvUI, Shadowed Unit Frames, Unhalted Unit Frames, Z-Perl, PitBull 4, any oUF layout or on the default Blizzard player frame, along with your pet frames, power bar, cast bar, class resources, heal and absorb overlays and Blizzard's personal resource display.

Supports World of Warcraft Retail 12.1 (Interface: 120100, 120105) and WoW Forever / Camelot 1.60.1 (Interface: 16001). Forever uses its own TOC and current-pet/stabled-pet layout. On Forever, AzeriteUI5 – JuNNeZ Edition and AzeriteUI6 (1.0.7 and later) both colour their player and pet frames.

✨ Features
• Static RGBA colour picker (alpha supported)
• Effects: Gradient, Flow, Spectrum, Pulse, Breathe, Heartbeat, Two-tone, Flicker, Sweep and Rainbow (Cycle / Ping-Pong / Chaos), with a shared speed slider, Pulse Depth, Sweep Time, smooth fades and Reduce Motion
• Rules: a colour and effect while you are in combat, have aggro (or are about to pull or lose it), cast or channel, mounted, flying, resting, stealthed, dead, in a role, a group, a specialization, an instance, a Mythic+ run, a delve, a zone, a vehicle or War Mode, at a time of day, with or without your pet, or while any of several buffs or debuffs is on you; two conditions in one rule ("in a raid and in combat"), each can be turned around ("not in a group"); colour a rule by your health; on your health bar, pet frame, power bar, cast bar, class resources or every bar; a sound when it starts; Try a rule for five seconds, or add a ready-made rule (see the Rules Cookbook)
• Colour by Health: your bar runs from your colour to a low-health colour
• Quick palette on the minimap button's right-click, slash commands and key bindings
• Share strings: export your setup as one line of text and import someone else's, or share it in chat as an [ABCS: name] link other players with the addon can click
• Profiles, per character or per specialization, or just a preset per specialization
• More bars: Blizzard's pet frame, your power bar, your cast bar, your class resources (combo points, holy power, chi, arcane charges, soul shards, essence, runes), the heal and absorb overlays and Blizzard's personal resource display
• Your colour is always kept: effects and pet colours are only applied on screen, never saved over your chosen colour
• Presets: save, rename, delete, plus six ready-made packs (Class Fantasy, Elements, Pastel, High Contrast, Midnight, Class Colours)
• ABCS Studio: the options window, with a live preview of your bars (it can show them as they look with each common kind of colour blindness), a colour wheel, recent colours, preset swatches you drag into order, playing effect cards, rules written as sentences, Undo, search across every setting and pet, a gem on every setting you have changed with one click to put it back, and keyboard navigation
• Pet gallery: every pet as a card with its portrait, plus a turning 3D model of the selected pet, its own colour and a pulse or rainbow effect
• Filters and search for call slots and stabled pets, and Use for all to give a pet's colour to its whole family
• Specialization colours for Ferocity, Tenacity and Cunning (Retail)
• Editable pet family colours that work in every game language
• Choose where pet colours go: your health bar, the AzeriteUI pet frame, or both

Other unit frame addons, a cast bar, buff and debuff rules, preset packs, a count of changed settings, keyboard navigation and nine translations.

[3.0.3] - 2026-10-14Fixed (3.0.3)
• The press flash and pulse showed only on the main action bar. On Blizzard's other bars the overlay could be taken for a skin failure while the bar was still hidden at login, so the button's own label was written as well and drawn over the flashing text. A button that is not on screen no longer falls back to its own label, and a button whose own label AHOS writes into flashes that label.
• The buttons and tooltips on the Status, About & Support and Abbreviations settings, Smart Frame Layering, Export Current Profile, and the addon's popups and chat messages are translated into every language AHOS ships (57 strings that were English everywhere). The About and Help text in English is the current one.
[3.0.2] - 2026-10-13Added (3.0.2)
• A scrollbar beside every page of the options window that runs past the bottom, so the settings below the fold are not taken for missing: a thumb in the theme's accent, as long as the share of the page in view, that drags, with a click on the track paging up or down. The search results, dropdown lists, the Lua condition field, a key's card and the log and export windows have one too. It shows only while there is something to scroll.
Fixed (3.0.2)
• A key press flashed or pulsed the text twice, once when the key went down and again when it was let go. A click that follows a key going down on the same button is now the same press; a mouse click still flashes on the click.
[3.0.1] - 2026-10-13Added (3.0.1)
• Hide the Range Dot (Display page): the dot the game puts on a button with no key while its action is in range is hidden, also while AHOS is turned off. Off by default.
Changed (3.0.1)
• The controllers on the Controller tab are redrawn: the Xbox, DualSense and Switch Pro bodies follow the real controllers' outlines, the Steam Deck is taller with a trackpad under each stick, and every button sits where it does on that controller.
• Pulse now flashes in the Flash Colour too, as well as growing; the colour can be picked for either.
Fixed (3.0.1)
• With Hide Original Hotkey Text on, a button with no key showed the range dot (●) that Blizzard and LibActionButton (AzeriteUI, Bartender4, DiabolicUI) put on it. It now shows nothing, also after the bar redraws it. A key AHOS cannot read still shows the button's own text.
• Pressing a key bound to a button on Blizzard's bars did not flash or pulse the text: the game runs those keys through ActionButtonDown and MultiActionButtonDown, which AHOS now listens to as well as clicks.
• Empty buttons on Blizzard's extra bars (bottom right, bottom left, right, left and bars 5-7) showed the main bar's key for their number: the sixth button showed "6", the twelfth "a-c-s-1". AHOS asked the button to redraw its label without saying which bar it is on, and Blizzard then reads the main bar's binding. AHOS now passes the bar's own binding type, as Blizzard does, so an empty button stays empty and turning AHOS off puts back each bar's own keys.

• Changing a Display, Keybinds or Abbreviations setting in the options window briefly lights up the overlays on your real action bars, so you see the change on your own UI and not only in the preview.
• The Font list draws each font's name in that font.…
addons.description:
A modular, robust hotkey overlay system for World of Warcraft action bars, with dedicated support for Blizzard bars, AzeriteUI, Bartender4, Dominos, DiabolicUI, LUI and Neuron.
Version 3.0.3 Highlights
• When the hotkey text shows: fade it out of combat, show it only on mouseover per bar or while a modifier is held, or write a Lua condition of your own. A different colour and size in combat, and a flash or pulse when you press a button.
• /ahos edit: drag the hotkey text into place on your own bars; Shift-drag moves one bar. Bars can also have a place of their own.
• Presets and Tank, Healer and Damage templates, snapshots with /ahos rollback, /ahos profile , and switching profile by specialization or talent loadout.
• Shadow colour, glow and a background plate; mouse button icons; both keys on a button with two; Follow Masque Skin.
• LUI and Neuron support; Russian, Ukrainian, Korean and Taiwanese keyboards, with their letters drawn in the game's own fonts on any client.
• Sharp new switches and sliders, Keycap Gold as the default theme, and the classic Ace3 window removed.
Features
• Profile-specific keybind abbreviations with editable modifier, mouse, numpad, special-key, function-key, and gamepad mappings
• Minimap icon and options panel access
• Overlay frame strata control
• Modular, event-driven updates
• No taint, nil, or registration errors

addons.changelog:
Mana potion timing, the five-second rule and live mana regen for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Potions, runes, gems and your own mana spells light up the moment they fit your missing mana.

Install: CurseForge app, or unzip into Interface/AddOns.

Full Mana Forever 0.9.0

Works together with unit frame addons (asked for in the comments):
• Only markers (under Mana bar): hides the bar's fill, background and border. The potion markers, the five-second strip and the texts stay, so you can lay them over the mana bar of your unit frame; match length and thickness to that bar
• Move the bar separately (under Move texts freely): the bar gets its own place, apart from the icons; unlock the frame and drag it. Reset position puts it back next to the icons
• Above other frames: icons, bar and texts are drawn above other addons' frames
• Bar length goes in steps of 10 (was 20), to match a unit frame exactly
• The texts (mana numbers, seconds, regen) always lie above the bar; dragged onto the bar they no longer go under it
• Seconds (under Five-second rule): the countdown number can be switched off, the gold strip alone shows the rule
• The five-second strip runs down smoothly instead of in steps; the mana fill eases to its new value where the game supports it
• Item list cleaned up: Diet McWeaksauce (a test realm item that never reached the live game), Tessa's Tonic, Restored Mana Potion, Full Moonshine (unclear where they come from), Mug of Shimmer Stout and Tea with Sugar (quest rewards that share the potion or rune cooldown with better items) are no longer listed. You can still add any item yourself
• Read Leyline (Skyborne, renamed by the game from "Ley Line reading"): in combat the regen now stays green for 30 seconds after the cast, as the spell's own text says since the 17 October patch (was 15). The items and spells of the addon were checked again after the patch: all unchanged; the new fourth rank of Mana Tide Totem is found by itself

Bug reports: https://github.com/KesaObscura/FullManaForever/issues
addons.description:
Full Mana Forever – mana potion, five-second rule and mana regen addon for WoW Forever
An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW Forever, "Classic+", client 1.60.1) for healers
and every other mana user. It lights up your mana potion, Demonic/Dark Rune, mage mana gem,
mana item or own mana spell (Evocation, Innervate, Mana Tide Totem, Inner Focus, Life Tap,
Eureka!, Read Leyline) the moment it is ready and fits into your missing mana, so nothing
is wasted: drink on cooldown, stay near full mana, and never panic-chug at 5 %. A compact mana bar
shows the five-second rule (5SR) and your live mana regen per second, also in combat.

| Right potion for the missing mana | Live regen and five-second rule | Own mana spells |
|---|---|---|
| | | |

| See it coming: grey with a countdown, then it lights up | Five-second rule: 5 to 1 at 0.0/s, then the regen runs again |
|---|---|
| | |
How it works with Forever's addon rules
In Forever your current mana is a secret value: addons cannot read or compare it.
Full Mana Forever never tries to. It gives the game a step curve
(C_CurveUtil + UnitPowerPercent), the game evaluates it and returns a secret alpha,
and that alpha is applied straight to the icon. Nested frames multiply their alpha, which
gives "ready and deficit big enough (and enough health for runes)".
Item cooldowns, item counts and maximum mana are readable and handled normally.

The addon never uses an item for you. Put your potions on the action bar and press them
when the icon lights up.
Features
• One icon per cooldown group: mana potions, Demonic/Dark Rune, mage mana gems, other
mana consumables, and use effects of equipped gear.
• Right potion for the deficit: with several potions in your bags the icon shows the
strongest one that will not overflow.
• When to light up setting: No waste (default) waits until the whole potion fits;
More per fight uses the average restore (earlier, sometimes a small overflow);
Strongest only.
• Runes are safe: shown only if you keep a set share of health after the rune
(30 % by default).
• Own mana spells: Evocation, Innervate, Mana Tide Totem, Inner Focus, Life Tap and the
racials Eureka! (gnome) and Read Leyline (Skyborne): every ready spell gets its own icon
when your mana is at or below its own threshold (sensible defaults per spell, set in the list
below); Life Tap when its mana fits.
• Mana bar with markers: a thick marker where an icon lights up, thin ones where a
stronger potion becomes the best fit. Icons stand in the order they light up (highest
threshold first), so lit icons never leave a gap. Icons in a row or a column, bar on any side;
color, thickness, length, icon size and spacing are adjustable. For unit frame addons: *Only
markers* (no fill, background or border: lay the markers and the five-second strip over your
unit frame's mana bar), Move the bar separately (its own place, apart from the icons) and
Above other frames.
• Five-second rule and mana regen on the bar: a gold strip (and the seconds, can be switched off) after a spell
that costs mana, and the regen running right now ("14.8/s"), also in combat. The regen turns
green when it is above your normal rate, red while Resurrection Sickness holds it down. The
mana numbers, the seconds and the regen also show without the bar, and each can be dragged anywhere ("Move texts freely").
• Mana text like the game's status text: number, percentage or both, with its own switch
and text size.
• Show: solo / in a party / in a raid, optionally only in combat.
• See it coming: icons already show in the last seconds of their cooldown (5 s by default,
up to 60), grey and counting down like the action bar; at 0 only when ready.
• Sound when your potion is ready again (optional, off by default): three sounds of the addon's own.
• Items and spells (/fmf items): every supported item, on/off per item, add your own;
your class's mana spells with their threshold and, if you lack one, why (level, talent,
trainer).…

Mana potion timing, the five-second rule and live mana regen for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Install: CurseForge app, or unzip into Interface/AddOns.

Full Mana Forever 0.8.11
• No more gaps in the row or column of icons: the icons now stand in the order they light up, the one with the highest mana threshold first. When your mana drops, new icons appear at the end and the lit ones stay where they are; the potion slot keeps its place when a smaller potion turns into a bigger one. Install: CurseForge app, or unzip into Interface/AddOns.

Full Mana Forever 0.8.9
• Regen colour after death: the lowered regen under Resurrection Sickness (or anything else that takes at least half of your Spirit or Intellect) is no longer taken as your normal regen, so your normal regen no longer turns green with the up arrow once the debuff ends. Gear with a few points less Spirit still counts as normal
• While such a debuff lasts, the regen is shown red with a small down arrow
• Major and Superior Mana Draught (battlegrounds) share the potion cooldown, as the game shows: in battlegrounds they now use the potion icon (the strongest that fits) instead of a second icon that always went on cooldown together with it
• More potions in the potion slot, all with the shared potion cooldown read from the game: Forever's Restored Mana Potion (20 % of your max mana, so it fits at every level), Tessa's Tonic, Diet McWeaksauce, Mug of Shimmer Stout, Full Moonshine and Forever's second item IDs of the Minor and Lesser Mana Potion (usable from level 1; one row in the list with the original, counted and switched together). Wildvine Potion is listed but off by default (it may restore nothing)
• Forever's Power Recycler (20 % of your max health into 20 % of your max mana) in "Other consumables", with the health check of the runes; also Tea with Sugar and, for mages, the Scroll of Minor Evocation
• Gear: Earthen Sigil (trinket) and, for druids, the Veildust Medicine Bag (off-hand)

addons.description:
This addon provides a button that can be used with a variety of hearthstones including a unique skin made of the Hearthstone game cardback textures.
Commands
Commands can be accessed via /hearthbag or /hb. Subcommands include:
• /hb combat
• Toggle the moveable combat frame
• /hb anchor
• Set the Hearthbag Parent to the frame under your mouse or to the specified frame name (BagItemSearchBox, Minimap, PlayerFrame)
• /hb reset
• Reset to your Hearthbag to centered position
Limitations
The Hearthbag frame won't be displayed on certain frames during combat due to limitations, as the frame will become "Protected". The Combat Frame is an optional frame for Hearthbag to still remain accessible during combat.

addons.changelog:
Guild-tabard consistency for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Install: unzip Livery-1.0.0.zip into World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/ so that Livery/Livery.toc is inside Livery/, restart or /reload, then type /livery.
• Two buttons: Use my guild / Use target set the reference tabard.
• A MATCH / NO MATCH frame beside your target, naming what differs.
• A list of every sister guild you have targeted, in hierarchy order (OLYMPUS, OLYMPUS II, III, IX...).
• More: a share code so other officers check against the same reference, sister-guild name rules, frame options.
• ? in the window explains the three steps.

Known beta issue: the current client does not read saved variables back at login (Blizzard bug), so keep your share code handy and re-import it after logging in. Livery-1.0.0.zip.sha256 is the checksum of the zip.
addons.description:
A WoW: Forever addon that keeps a family of sister guilds ( 1,
2, II, ...) wearing an identical guild tabard. Capture one
reference design, target other players, and get an unmistakable MATCH / NO
MATCH next to the target frame, plus a list of every sister guild you have
seen and how it compared.

Local-only: no network calls, no chat, whisper, guild or addon messages,
nothing posted anywhere on your behalf.
addons.name: Livery
