Замените папку ForeverNet в Interface/AddOns и выполните /reload, сохранив SavedVariables. После первой установки CJK перезапустите клиент. Обновление обоих игроков обеспечивает одинаковое поведение интерфейса/транспорта.

ForeverNet 0.4.0 BetaEnglish
This Beta brings the interface and production planner improvements made since 0.3.3 into a new release for World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1 (70124), Interface 16001.
• Dark profession-style panels with readable text, measured card heights, native side tabs and thin scrollbars. Recipe-scroll icons and corrected layering for Settings and Update windows.
• Recipes and network profiles grouped by profession, collapsible sections, item cards and skill ranks. Compact search and combined profession, recipe-type and crafter filters. Items shared by several crafters appear once.
• Favorite up to 5 player profiles and 5 recipe items, with favorites shown first. Favorite profiles persist across sessions; ordinary network profiles expire after 30 minutes without updates. Own recipes and personal bank snapshots remain saved.
• Clearer production chains: what to get followed by what to craft, with quantities, crafters and full material costs for each step. Choose to get an intermediate material ready-made or craft it; expand other known recipes to choose a different route. Stock is used first, and changing a choice recalculates the original target. Choices apply to the current plan.
• Bundled static Korean and Chinese fonts, including Latin and Cyrillic coverage, for translated text, buttons, window titles, input fields and tooltips. Asian language names are readable before selection. Fonts are based on Noto Sans CJK and included under SIL OFL 1.1; addon code remains MIT.
• Localized exchange-channel names and updated translations across the supported WoW locale codes.
Installation
Download ForeverNet-0.4.0.zip, extract its ForeverNet folder into your Forever client's Interface/AddOns/, and fully restart the game so the new font files and metadata load. Existing ForeverNetDB saved data is retained. Update all participating players for consistent behavior.
Validation and current limits
All 27 automated Lua 5.1 test groups passed, including multi-client networking, persistence, alternative material routes, interface layout and font coverage. The package was checked against the source files and installed game copy, including all three fonts and their license. Actual rendering and usability still need feedback from the game client.

Crafting, trading and installation of addon updates remain manual. Blueprints and Camping use manual capability flags; plans do not guarantee an optimal route or a crafter's availability. Recipe favorites bookmark items: to retain recipes known only by another player, favorite that player's profile too. Compatibility with other WoW clients is not confirmed.

Author: Andrew Woolfi · Source · Support
Русский
В Beta собраны улучшения интерфейса и планировщика после 0.3.3. Целевой клиент — World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1 (70124), Interface 16001.

Выбор действует в текущем плане.…

This update fixes duplicate characters and improves guild/group cooperation in WoW: Forever.
• Recognizes Forever's first name and surname across native and compact chat forms. Your Network page lists other players; they see one profile for you. Existing self duplicates are merged, preserving recipes and the newest personal bank snapshot.
• Groups each output item into one catalog row while keeping different crafters and recipe variants available. The crafter list shows each person once.
• Fixes normal party routing, discovers participants automatically, and sends existing requests to newly connected participants. Requests take priority over profile transfers; throttled sends are retried.
• Adds automatic network refresh controls: on/off and 1, 2 or 5 minutes. Manual Sync remains available.
• Supports all 12 WoW locale codes with automatic detection and a language selector. New translations are machine-assisted and need further native-speaker review.
• Adds /fn updates: optional notifications about newer versions reported by participants, a GitHub download link and manual installation instructions. The addon does not query the internet or install updates in game.

Install: extract ForeverNet-0.3.3.zip into Interface/AddOns. Update both participants and use /reload; restart after first installation. Open the addon with /fn, settings with /fn settings.

Target: Forever 1.60.1 (70124), Interface 16001. Automated Lua 5.1 checks cover native Forever party and guild transport, self echoes, catalog deduplication and complete request lifecycles. Actual client rendering and live multiplayer behavior still need in-game verification. Blueprint/Camping declarations remain manual; crafting and trading are performed by players.

addons.description:
Minimalist solo/party/raid unit frames with click-casting — Cell/Healbot-Click/Grid/VuhDo style.

Compatible with WoW 12.0 Midnight and WoW: Forever (Classic+, interface 16001).
Notes for WoW: Forever
Forever runs the Midnight UI codebase on a level-60 Vanilla ruleset, so VoidBox
adapts itself at login:
• Dispel highlighting is derived from the spells in your spellbook (Vanilla has
no specializations)
• Downranking: drag a lower rank from the spellbook onto a click-cast slot
to cast that exact rank; the list shows it as "Rejuvenation (Rank 1)". A
top-rank binding shows "(Rank max)" and follows you up as you learn new ranks.
• Range checking and HoT/shield tracking use Vanilla spells and cover every rank
• Click-casting: mouse bindings work normally. On builds where
loadstring_untainted is missing, the client cannot compile secure snippets,
so keyboard bindings switch to global override bindings on @mouseover proxy
buttons. VoidBox prints a notice at login when that happens. Scroll-wheel
click-casting is off on that path unless enabled in Options: it then casts
on the friendly unit under the cursor (including your own character and
players outside your group) and zooms the camera anywhere else.
• Aura rows use native AuraContainers. Addon code cannot read auras in
combat any more (enumeration raises, per-spell lookups answer nil), so the
debuff, HoT and dispel rows are rendered by the client itself: VoidBox
declares a filter and styles the buttons it is handed, and never touches the
aura data. They keep working in combat as a result.
• Known beta client bug: early Forever builds write SavedVariables on exit
but never read them back, so settings can reset between sessions. That is a
client issue, not an addon one.
Usage
1. The small purple square to the left of the frames lets you drag to reposition
2. Right-click the purple square to open configuration
3. In config, Click-Castings tab: drag a spell from the spellbook onto a slot
4. Bindings are saved per class (not per character)
Features
• Compact raid frames with health and mana bars
• Click-casting with drag & drop from spellbook or macro UI
• Universal "Press to Bind" system: keyboard, mouse, scroll wheel, MMO mouse
• Capture any combo: Ctrl+F1, Shift+Numpad5, Alt+Right Click, etc.
• Keyboard bindings activate on hover (SecureHandlerWrapScript)
• Full modifier support (Shift, Ctrl, Alt) with any input
• Health percentage display (secret-value safe)
• Per-class bindings — all your priests share the same bindings
• Mousewheel scroll bindings (with modifier support)
• Profile system (layout/appearance profiles)
• Minimap button (LibDBIcon): left-click toggle frames, right-click config
• Separate tank frame (optional): dedicated movable panel for tanks only
• Percentage-based scaling system (50%-150%, live preview, no reload)
• Base frame: 80×55px at 100% scale
• Independent width/height scale sliders (step 10%)
• Aura indicators:
• Debuffs (HARMFUL): up to 4 icons with stack count badges, centered row
• HOTs/shields (player-cast only): up to 4 icons with stack badges, centered row
• Tracked buffs: add any spell (e.g. Thorns) from the Auras tab by dragging it
from your spellbook; it shows in the HoT row when you cast it
• "+N" indicator for other healers' HOTs/shields on the target
• Stack badges: dark background, gold text, red at 5+ stacks
• Screen auras (Auras tab): icons, bars or drawings anywhere on screen while a
buff or debuff is up, missing or running out, or while a spell is usable
• Recommended auras per class and spec (druid, mage), added in one click
• Role icons (tank/heal/dps) — real atlas icons
• Threat border (red/yellow)
• Range check (reduced opacity when out of range)
• Dead / Disconnected / Incoming resurrection / Ready check icons
• Role sorting: Tank > DPS > Healer (6 presets)
• Tooltip anchored to bottom-right of screen (non-intrusive)
• Config UI: scaling, class colors, orientation, role order, lock/unlock
• Theme color: purple (#9966FF)…

addons.description:
A standalone replacement for World of Warcraft's default objective tracker.

It is the tracker half of Everything Quests,
extracted so you can use just the tracker without the rest of EQ. It does not require
Everything Quests, and never will.

The relationship runs the other way: as of Everything Quests v1.38.0, EQ has no tracker of its
own and installs this one as a dependency. There is one copy of the tracker code now, so a fix
lands in both places at once.

Discord ·
CurseForge ·
Report a bug
Status
Retail, Classic Era (1.15.9) and TBC Anniversary (2.5.6) are all supported. The Classic
gaps listed below are real ones rather than a disclaimer. Please report anything you find
rather than assuming it is known.

WoW Forever support is a work in progress, so expect bugs. The tracker shows your quests
there, and with Everything Quests and TomTom installed the quest you are following gets a TomTom
arrow, as on Classic. The retail-only sections, such as world quests and scenarios, have stayed empty
there so far.

On retail it tracks quests and campaign quests, world quests and bonus objectives, scenarios
and delves, achievements, professions, and endeavors, covering both the Traveler's Log monthly
activities and the neighborhood tasks you have tracked.
What works on Classic today
Quest tracking and the customization around it: sorting, manual drag ordering, per-quest
pinning, filters, To-Do Mode, section visibility and ordering, zone headers, the card layout, fonts
and colors, profiles, row tooltips, and the row right-click menu. Blizzard's own quest watch frame is
suppressed so you do not get two trackers.

The tracker keeps its own list of which quests you are tracking rather than using the game's,
which on these versions is capped at five quests and cannot track a quest automatically when
you accept it. So "Auto-track accepted quests" works, "Show only tracked quests" can show more
than five, and shift-clicking a row in the game's own quest log tracks and untracks exactly as
it always did, with its checkmarks showing this tracker's list.

Timed quests count down on the row. An escort or a bombing run shows the time left where a
retail world quest shows its expiry, counting in seconds through the last minute, and
the game's own floating timer box is hidden so you are not left with two timers.

You can also focus a quest, which these clients have no super-tracking for. Click a row's
icon to focus it and click the icon again to clear it, or use Focus in the right-click menu.
The focused quest's title is tinted. If Everything Quests and TomTom are both installed,
focusing a quest also points a TomTom arrow at it.
What is missing or limited on Classic
• No map pins. Those come from the companion addon - see below. The TomTom arrow needs it
too, so on the tracker alone a focused quest is the tint and nothing more.
• World quests and bonus objectives, scenarios, achievements, endeavors and tracked recipes
have no section. Most need APIs these clients do not have.
• No Find Group button. These clients have no group finder for quests.
• The zone progress bar stays empty. Its zone routing data covers Midnight only.
• Distance sorting does nothing, because the distance API is retail-only.
• Some options still appear that cannot do anything on Classic, for the same reasons.
Questie
If Questie is loaded, EQ Objective Tracker offers once to hide Questie's own tracker, and
that choice becomes a permanent toggle on the General tab. It only hides the frame, and
Questie's own disable path is never called. The game blocks hiding it during a fight, so
if Questie shows its tracker then, it is hidden again as soon as the fight ends.

Tracking and untracking from this tracker's row menu go through its own list rather than the
game's watch functions, so the hooks Questie places on those do not fire for anything you do
here.
Everything Quests, the companion addon…

[2.10.3] - 2026-11-03Bug Fixes
• With Simplify tracked achievements on, an achievement with more than twelve criteria and its first twelve done showed a single finished criterion instead of the ones still left to do. Finished criteria that Simplify hides no longer use up the twelve lines an achievement shows, so up to twelve unfinished ones now appear, and Simplify Mode, which did the same, now shows the first unfinished one. Reported by Rubio9.

[2.10.2] - 2026-11-01Bug Fixes
• Classic Era and TBC: with the quest log scrolled, its tracked checks landed on the wrong rows and Shift-clicking a quest could toggle a different one. Checks now stay on their own quests, and Shift-click toggles the quest you clicked.
• Classic Era and TBC: Shift-clicking a quest in the quest log to link it with a chat box open also changed whether it was tracked. It now only links.
• A world quest you tracked yourself could be lost at login if the game had auto-watched it first, such as when you log in standing in its area. It now stays tracked.
• A quest item button now updates its cooldown sweep and charges right after you use the item, rather than at the tracker's next update.
• Under the Distance sort, a quest accepted while standing still now takes its place right away rather than sitting at the bottom until you move.
• A tracked recipe's currency reagent count now updates when the currency changes.
• A tracked recipe with a reagent the game could not answer for could stop the whole tracker from drawing. The tracker now keeps drawing, though that reagent's count may read low.

[2.10.1] - 2026-11-01Bug Fixes
• The first quest you accept after logging in with an empty quest log, such as a new character's first quest, now shows its NEW tag. It was being saved as a quest you already had, so it never got one.
• The first click on the About tab after logging in could end in a "script ran too long" error on Classic Era. Its changelog now lists the 30 newest versions instead of all of them, which makes that click far lighter, and the rest are on CurseForge.

[2.10.0] - 2026-10-30New Features
• Every sort order except Zone and Manual can now be reversed. On the sort button's menu (turn on Show the sort button on the tracker), pick the order already in use again to reverse it, and once more to turn it back: Level then runs from highest to lowest, Title from Z to A, Distance from farthest to nearest, and so on. Quests that tie on the order stay in alphabetical order, quests with no known distance stay at the bottom, and the sort button's tooltip says when the order is reversed. Picking another order, on the sort button or on the Tracker tab's Sort Order list, or hiding the sort button turns the reverse off. Requested by Hermonii.
Bug Fixes
• During Abundance, the Abundance Bag bar now shows under the event's objective, as it does in Blizzard's tracker. Blizzard's scenario tracker draws two groups of event widgets under a scenario's objectives, and EQ Objective Tracker never drew either, so anything placed there was missing. Other events and delves that use them now show them too. Reported by hohoook.
• With Questie installed and Hide Questie's quest tracker on, killing quest mobs in a fight no longer causes a blocked action error ("Interface action failed because of an AddOn", which error reports named as Questie's). EQ Objective Tracker now waits for the fight to end before hiding Questie's tracker, and unticking the box during a fight brings Questie's tracker back when the fight ends. Unticking it now brings back only a tracker EQ Objective Tracker hid, so a Questie tracker that Questie had already hidden itself, with no quests tracked or by its own option to hide in instances, stays hidden.
• The zone progress bar now shows in Eversong Woods outside Silvermoon City on game clients that are not in English. It found that zone by its English name, so on every other language it drew nothing there.
• In a scenario or delve, an objective whose text only just wraps onto a second line no longer overlaps the objectives around it. Its height was worked out for a slightly wider line than the one drawn.
• /eqot status no longer prints the word twice in its scenario spells reading ("spells spells secret").
• On Russian game clients, the font lists now offer the 25 bundled fonts that have Russian letters, plus WoW Default (Friz Quadrata) and WoW Arial Narrow. Until now none of the bundled fonts was offered there, so the tracker's default font, GothamXNarrow Black, could not load, and the tracker quietly used Friz Quadrata instead. If you play on a Russian client and never picked a font, your tracker now shows GothamXNarrow Black, the default font it was always meant to have. Fonts without Russian letters stay out of the lists there, so no font can turn Russian text into blanks. Korean and Chinese clients are unchanged: none of the bundled fonts has Korean or Chinese characters, so the game's own fonts for those languages stay in use.
Improvements
• /eqot status now names the two groups of event widgets under a scenario's objectives on its widgets line, lists a widget type it cannot read instead of leaving it out, and says when the sort order is reversed.
• Updated for World of Warcraft patch 12.1.7.

[2.9.0] - 2026-10-24New Features
• To-Do Mode, on its own card on the Tracker tab, turns the Quests header, and the Campaign header on retail, into four counts: your unfinished quests in the zone you are in, the ones ready to turn in there, every quest there and every quest you have. Click a count and the section shows exactly those quests, with the count you picked underlined. It starts on your unfinished quests in the zone, each character remembers the count it picked, and a header stays up while a count you show is above 0, so you can always switch back. While it is on it decides which quests are in your zone, so Show only quests in current zone is dimmed and keeps your own setting for when you turn it off. The quest type filters, Show only tracked quests, pinned quests and every other section stay as they are, and the counts follow them. Quest popup boxes and pinned quests show whichever count you pick, as they always have. The card can hide any of the four counts, give each one its own color with a Class button, and size them. Off by default, on every version of the game. Requested by Tjuv.
• Two new count colors on the Appearance tab's Quest Colors card, Count Color: Half Done and Count Color: Mostly Done, color a count like 5/10 from half done and one like 7/10 from seven tenths done. Both start unset, so no count changes color until you pick one, and Mostly Done takes Half Done's color while it is unset. Requested by Tjuv.
Improvements
• /eqot status now has a To-Do Mode line naming the count you picked and the four counts of each quest section.

addons.description:
A clean replacement for World of Warcraft's scrolling loot and combat text. Loot Pro gives you two feeds you can place anywhere, one for loot and money and one for combat, experience, and reputation, with a color and an on and off switch for every kind of message. On top of that it adds the loot tools the default UI never had: a session recap with gold per hour, alerts for the items you are hunting, gear markers, a block list, and automatic gray selling. It works the moment you install it, and every extra stays off until you turn it on, apart from a loot spec reminder that only speaks up when something is wrong.

Contents
1. What it does
2. Quick start
3. General: looting, the minimap button, and updates
4. Layout: placing and styling the two feeds
5. Notifications: what shows up, and in what color
6. Recap: your session at a glance
7. Watch: alerts for items you name
8. Rare Drops: alerts, gear markers, and loot spec
9. Block: hiding loot by name
10. Vendor: selling grays
11. About
12. Item tooltips
13. Slash commands
14. Minimap button
15. Flavor differences
16. Reset All Settings
17. Dependencies
18. Gallery
19. Found a bug

What it does
Loot Pro replaces the default scrolling combat and loot text with two feeds you control.

The combat feed shows combat start and end, experience, skill gains, honor, reputation, and Delve companion experience.

The loot feed shows money, currency, and item loot.

Each feed has its own size, fade time, maximum line count, font, and outline, and its own text alignment, position, and line order. Every kind of message has its own color and its own on and off switch. Out of the box you get clean text with inline item icons and a running total of how many of each item you own.

Everything past that is optional and off by default, so you turn on only what you want. The one exception is the loot spec reminder, which is on from the start because it only speaks up when your loot spec does not match the spec you are playing.

Loot Pro never equips, trades, or destroys anything. Two features do act for you once you turn them on, and both are off by default: Speedy AutoLoot takes items from a corpse on your behalf, and automatic gray selling on the Vendor page sells gray items while a merchant window is open.

Quick start
1. Install and log in. Your loot and combat text is already running through Loot Pro.
2. Type /lp, or left-click the minimap button, to open the settings.
3. Go to the Layout page, tick Unlock Windows at the bottom left, drag the two feeds where you want them, then untick it. Closing the settings window locks them again as well.
4. Click Start Test Mode at the bottom right to fill both feeds with sample lines while you pick fonts, sizes, and colors. The samples follow your current settings, so you see each change as you make it. The button turns into Stop Test Mode while they run, and closing the window stops it too.

If the settings window is in the way, drag it aside by its title bar, or make it smaller with Scale on the General page.

That is enough to use it. Everything below is optional.

The settings window has nine pages, listed down its left side: General, Layout, Notifications, Recap, Watch, Rare Drops, Block, Vendor, and About. It opens on the page you used last. Unlock Windows and Start Test Mode sit at the bottom of both the Layout and Notifications pages, so you can drag a feed or watch your changes land without leaving the page you are tuning. A setting that does nothing while another one is off is dimmed until that one is on, and every slider takes a typed value if you click its number.

Where an option below is marked Retail only, the Classic versions leave it out. WoW Forever runs on the Retail client and keeps it, see Flavor differences.

[3.2.0] - 2026-11-03New Features
• The settings window can now be moved out of the way and made smaller. Drag it by its title bar and it can hang partly off the left, right, or bottom edge of your screen, so you can see your feeds while you set them up. Its title bar always stays on screen, and it opens wherever you left it, even after a /reload. Reset All Settings puts it back in the middle. Scale on the General page now goes down to 50%. Thanks to Glamishi on CurseForge for the suggestion.
Bug Fixes
• /lp whatsnew reset now always shows the latest notes again at your next login. When the newest release had only fixes, it showed nothing.

[3.1.2] - 2026-11-02Improvements
• Added support for the upcoming retail patch 12.1.7, so Loot Pro is not flagged as out of date when it goes live.

[3.1.1] - 2026-10-25Bug Fixes
• Turning off "Keep busy feeds up longer" now takes effect right away. Lines kept lingering for the longer busy time until you reloaded, and with "Pause fade while hovering the feed" on, they could vanish early without fading.
• Several gains of the same currency in quick succession now all count. When the amounts matched, as when AoE looting with Speedy AutoLoot, only the first gain reached the loot feed and the session recap. A gain the game reports twice still counts once.
• Bonus roll loot now counts as your own loot. It reaches the session recap and Notable Drops, and it can trigger watch and rare drop alerts. Before, it was treated as a party member's loot. (Mists of Pandaria Classic)
• Items you craft or get refunded now show as yours. They use your own minimum quality, still show with Display Party Loot turned off, show how many you own, and lose the "You create:" or "You are refunded:" text in Clean Mode. They stay out of the session recap and alerts, since they were not looted.
• With Clean Mode on and Use Coin Icons off, looted money now shows as + 12g 50s 20c instead of the full chat sentence.
• Test Mode's sample lines now follow Enable Clean Mode, Show Item Totals, and Use Coin Icons, so you can see those settings change while you tune them.
• Shift-clicking a framed loot row to link it in chat now uses the game's current chat function, so it keeps working once Blizzard removes the old one.
• Hide Blizzard's loot toasts no longer appears on Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, and Mists of Pandaria Classic, where it had nothing to hide.
• A saved setting with the wrong kind of value, such as after hand-editing the saved variables file, now goes back to its default at login instead of causing an error on every loot.
• A mistyped /lp command now says it is unknown instead of opening the settings window, and extra spaces between words no longer break a command. /lp config, /lp options, and /lp settings still open the window, and /lp help now lists /lp whatsnew reset.
• The watch list no longer accepts a shift-clicked currency, which could never trigger an alert, and says so. A full watch or block list now says an entry is already on the list instead of calling the list full.
• Automatic gray selling now credits the stack you actually sold when its size changed during the sale.
• Loot quality is now read correctly from item links written with the game's named quality colors, keeping rare drop alerts, line colors, and quality limits accurate. (Retail and WoW Forever)
Improvements
• With Text Alignment set to Center, framed loot rows without an icon now center their text like the money and text rows beside them. Rows with an icon keep the icon on the left with the name beside it.
• The settings window now runs on the newest version of the library the Everything addons share. Loot Pro's colors no longer pick up another addon's color when that addon opens the color picker while you are choosing a Loot Pro color.
• The minimap button's tooltip now says Toggle Lock, the same as the General page.
• Under the hood, the loot and chat handling was reorganized so future updates have room to grow, and finished feed rows let go of their item details sooner.

[3.1.0] - 2026-10-24New Features
• Text Alignment, Text Position, and Newest Line, three new settings on each feed's card on the Layout page, set separately for the loot feed and the combat feed. Text Alignment lines the text up with the left edge, the center, or the right edge of the feed. Text Position places the lines at the top, in the middle, or at the bottom of the feed's area when they do not fill it. Newest Line chooses whether a new line appears above the others or below them. All three work in the text feed and in framed rows, where Right also moves item icons to the right edge. Your feeds look exactly as they did before until you change them. Thanks to berserk_mcnulty62 on CurseForge for the suggestion.
Improvements
• Match the Combat Feed now also copies the combat feed's text alignment, text position, and newest line.

[3.0.0] - 2026-10-17New Features
• A brand new settings window. Loot Pro's options now open in the same window as Everything Quests, EQ Objective Tracker, Everything Delves, and Cooldown Master. A sidebar on the left holds nine pages: General, Layout, Notifications, Recap, Watch, Rare Drops, Block, Vendor, and About. Each page is laid out in cards. The window opens on the page you used last. Every setting carries over exactly as you left it, and nothing resets.
• Unlock Windows and Start Test Mode sit at the bottom of the Layout and Notifications pages, so you can drag a feed or fill both feeds with sample lines without leaving the page you are tuning. Start Test Mode turns into Stop Test Mode while the samples run, and closing the window still locks the feeds and ends the test. Unlock Windows replaces the Lock Windows button, and the minimap's Toggle Lock keeps it in step.
• Click any slider's number to type an exact value.
• Match the Combat Feed, at the bottom of the Loot Feed card on the Layout page, gives your loot feed the combat feed's font, text size, outline, fade, frame size, max lines, and frame scale in one click. It replaces Sync Combat Layout to Loot and Sync Combat Fonts to Loot.
• What's New now appears only for releases that bring new features. A release with only fixes stays quiet, and the next feature release lists it too, so nothing is missed. If you have been away for several versions, it lists everything since you last looked. Under Updates on the General page, choose a Popup window, a quiet Chat link, or Off, and Show What's New opens the notes any time.
Improvements
• The Colors and Custom tabs are gone. Each color now sits at the right end of the switch for the line it paints, on the Notifications page, with the Quest Items color beside Color quest items. Start Test Mode shows your colors in the real feeds. Custom's feed settings joined the Layout page, which has one card for the loot feed, one for the combat feed, and one for settings that cover both. Custom's other settings are on the General page.
• Settings that do nothing while another one is off are dimmed until it is on. Show Item Totals dims while Clean Mode is off, Combine repeated drops while Framed loot rows is off, and the Rare Drops triggers until Color loot line by rarity, Flash the loot frame, or Play alert sound is on.
• Many settings that had no tooltip now have one, and three are corrected. Show Item Totals says it needs Clean Mode, Use Coin Icons explains when framed rows show coin icons anyway, and Show Combat Follower XP says it needs Display Experience.
• Clearer labels. "Inject Item Totals (e.g. 14)" is now "Show Item Totals", "Use Coin Icons (Clean Mode only)" is "Use Coin Icons", Display Combat Start, Display Combat End, Display Reputation Gain, and Display Reputation Loss are no longer in capitals, and the two combat text boxes no longer say "(Enter to Save)".
• The Watch and Block lists show each entry on its own row with an X to remove it, and a watched item shows its icon and its name in its quality color. Press Enter or Add to add an entry, or shift-click an item into the box. The count beside the box shows how full the list is, and says so when the list is full or the entry is already on it.
• The Recap page shows your session at a glance: Session time, Total gold, Gold per hour, and Items looted across the top, then where your gold came from, items per hour, and your loot by quality. Currencies and Notable Drops have their own cards, and Reset Session and Pause Timer sit at the bottom of the page.
• The About page shows your version and the game client you are on, links to Discord, CurseForge, GitHub, Report a Bug, and What's New, every slash command (now with /lp pause), the tutorials, the other addons (now with EQ Objective Tracker), and the whole changelog.
• Links open in a copy box you cannot accidentally type over.
• The Options Window scale on the General page now stops at the largest size that fits your screen.…

Release Notes[1.1.0] - 2026-10-08
Added
• Experimental support for WoW Classic Era (1.15). The compass banner, its background, the center line, the compass detail levels and the settings page all work there. SuperTracking (the marker, distance and ETA) doesn't, because Classic Era doesn't have the game features it relies on. See the new Compatibility table in the README for how well each client is supported.
• Banner background: an optional dark fade behind the compass banner (Off, Subtle, Medium or Strong), so the directions stay readable over bright scenery. It's off by default. Set it in the options page or with /wayfinder background . Thanks to mcbgamerguy on CurseForge for the suggestion.
• Show center line: an option to hide the line at the middle of the banner. Set it in the options page or with /wayfinder centerline enable|disable. Thanks to CyberzerkerGaming and mcbgamerguy on CurseForge for asking for it.
• /wayfinder debug eta records ten seconds of ETA data for troubleshooting.
Changed
• The options page now looks like Blizzard's own settings pages: a label on the left and its control on the right, a highlight and tooltip as you hover a row, and a scroll bar when the window is short. Compass detail and Banner background are now steppers (arrows around the current value). Settings that only affect the banner are greyed out while it's turned off, and "Reset position" is now a "Banner position" row.
• Whether the banner is turned on is now remembered between sessions. It used to always come back on at login.
• The banner no longer hides itself in every instance. It now hides only where the game doesn't report which way you're facing (inside most dungeons, for example), and comes back on its own when it does. That also fixes the compass freezing in place in a few dungeons, which was the reason for hiding it in all of them. In places like your garrison it now stays visible. When the banner is hidden for this reason, a message near the top of the options page says why.
• The ETA is now worked out from how quickly you're closing in on the target, and shown as a steady countdown. It appears about a second after you start moving, ticks down smoothly, and shows -- as soon as you stop or move away. Before, the seconds could flicker up and down, especially at long distances.
Fixed
• The ETA always showed -- while flying, because the game reports a current speed of zero in the air. It now works the same on foot, on a mount, flying or Skyriding, and on a taxi.
[1.0.1] - 2026-09-26
Fixed
• Changing Nameplate Style (Options > Nameplates) could throw a Lua error every frame while the preview cast bar animated. Wayfinder's options page was built from Blizzard's shared Settings controls, and that left Wayfinder's "taint" on control frames Blizzard later reused for its own settings. Thanks to u/xJayoftheDeadx on Reddit for the detailed report and suggested fix.
Changed
• The options page is now a single page built from Wayfinder's own controls. The About info (icon, version, author) is at the top, and there's no separate About page anymore.
• Compass detail is now a set of radio buttons instead of a dropdown.
[1.0.0] - 2026-09-24
Changed
• Promoted from beta to a stable release. No functional changes since 1.0.0-beta.2 - the only blocker was the WoW: Forever beta's SavedVariables-not-read-back bug (see 1.0.0-beta.1's "Known issues" below). Blizzard has since fixed it upstream (Forever beta build 70009), it's been verified in-game against Wayfinder's own settings, and 1.0.0-beta.2 confirmed the automated release pipeline (CurseForge, Wago, and WoWInterface) publishes cleanly.
[1.0.0-beta.2] - 2026-09-24
Changed
• Docs/comment cleanup: removed the SavedVariables-bug notes from code comments, Wayfinder.toc, and DEVNOTES.md now that it's fixed upstream (Forever beta build 70009) - see 1.0.0-beta.1's "Known issues" below for the original context.…

addons.description:
Mail the items you choose to your alts, each to the right one, when you open a mailbox.

For World of Warcraft: Forever, retail, Classic Era (Season of Discovery and Hardcore included) and TBC Anniversary. Source code, issues and releases: github.com/yannlugrin/FlagUp.

> Please report what goes wrong or any suggestion (see Reporting a problem).
Features
• Rules by category. Choose what goes where by the game's item categories (Trade Goods › Herb to your alchemist, Metal & Stone to your blacksmith), or item by item. A specific item comes first, then a subcategory, then a category.
• Keep some in your bags. For a specific item, keep a number in your bags and send only the rest, or don't send it.
• Full stacks only. Send only full stacks of what stacks; the rest waits in your bags until it makes a full one.
• Shared by your characters. The rules are the same for all your characters that can mail each other: on Forever, those of one ruleset and faction; on retail and Classic (Era and TBC Anniversary), those of a realm and its connected realms, both factions (on retail, mail goes to the other faction only between your own characters of one realm; on Classic, never); a character can override a rule for itself: another recipient, don't send, another number to keep, other qualities, full stacks or not.
• Any alt. Pick from the characters you logged in with Flag Up, or type the name of an alt on another account. On retail and Classic, characters of the realm you play show without their realm.
• At the mailbox. A panel next to the mailbox lists what will be sent, alt by alt, with the postage; uncheck an item to keep it this time. Then it sends mail after mail and shows each one sent, or failed with the game's reason.
• This time only. At the mailbox, change how many of an item go, or drop an item on an alt's heading or items to send it all there; the rules stay as they are.
• Alt tabs. Your alts with nothing to receive show as tabs beside the mailbox panel, with their class icon or one you pick; drop an item on one to send it all there. The rules window's Characters tab chooses which characters get a tab, changes their icon and forgets a typed name.
• Not worth the postage. An item worth less to a vendor than its postage (30 copper a stack) starts unchecked, so you don't pay to mail it; check it to send it anyway. A setting turns this off, another one does the same for items no vendor buys.
• Automatic or on demand. Send as soon as the mailbox opens, or only when you click Send. A key you choose (Shift by default) does the opposite while you hold it, like the game's auto-loot key.
• Ignore an item. From the mailbox panel, stop offering an item, for all your characters or only the one you play. The rules window shows it ignored, and its Ignored tab lists every ignored item by category, to take one back.

Show or hide the rules window with the minimap button, the tab with Flag Up's icon beside the mailbox panel or /flagup open. Right-click the minimap button for a menu. The add-on compartment next to the minimap opens the settings.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /flagup | List the commands |
| /flagup open | Show or hide the rules window |
| /flagup settings | Open the Flag Up settings |
Looks
The windows use the default game look. With EllesmereUI installed, they take your EllesmereUI theme.
Reporting a problem
Open an issue on GitHub with what you did, what you expected and what happened.

[1.0.0] - 2026-10-23
First release for the live game of World of Warcraft: Forever. What Who's Who does:
• One identity for all your characters: link the characters you play, pick your main, set a nickname, and a different nickname or main in each guild if you like.
• You decide who sees it: your guild, your friends (WoW friends, and Battle.net friends playing WoW: Forever), your party or raid, or the people you whisper. Nothing is shared until you link a character.
• Recognise people across their alts: the People tab lists the identities shared with you, with their characters, who is online and when you last saw them; their nickname shows in chat, in tooltips and, if you want, on nameplates.
• Your own nicknames and notes for anyone, seen only by you, and links you make yourself for players who don't use Who's Who.
• Guilds: once the guild master or an officer enables Who's Who, guildmates pass on each other's identities, and the Guild tab lists the guild by identity. Officers can require members to link their characters in the guild, link characters for the whole guild, and suggest a nickname or a main to a member.
• Guild invites for your alts: when the guild allows it, an alt outside the guild asks for an invite with the Invitation… button in My identity; an officer online gets a dialog and invites it with one click.
• Privacy: your identity is signed with a key that stays on your computer, BattleTags are never sent, and Forget me removes you from everyone's list.
Changed
• Saved data: the first time you play the live game, Who's Who starts over as on a first install: what it saved during the beta, your identity included, is gone with the beta. Your settings stay.
Fixed
• Window: other windows now come in front of the Who's Who window when you click them, instead of staying behind it.
addons.description:
Link all your characters into one identity, choose who can see it, and recognise people across their alts.

For World of Warcraft: Forever. Source code, issues and releases: github.com/yannlugrin/WhosWho.

> What is marked coming isn't built yet. Please report what goes wrong or any suggestion (see Reporting a problem).
Features
• One identity for all your characters. Link the characters you play and pick your main: you're shown under its name, or under a nickname if you set one. The first time you log in on a character, Who's Who asks whether to link it. Manage it all in the My identity tab, or with /ww link, /ww main and /ww nick.
• A different nickname or main in each guild. In My identity, In my guilds sets the nickname and the main a guild's members see; everyone else sees your usual ones.
• You decide who sees it. Share with your guild, your friends (WoW friends, and Battle.net friends playing WoW: Forever, whatever character or server they play), your party or raid, or the people you whisper. Guild and friends are on by default, and nothing is shared until you link a character or accept a guild's rule.
• Recognise people across their alts. When someone shares their identity with you, the People tab lists them with their characters, who is online and when you last saw them. Their nickname shows next to their name in chat and in their tooltip, on every character they linked, and the tooltip lists their other characters.
• Your own nickname and notes. In the People tab, give anyone your own nickname for them and write notes about them, seen only by you, or forget them. The start of the note shows in their tooltip.
• Always up to date. Your identity reaches the people you share with when you log in, level up, log out, join a group or a guild, add a friend, turn a sharing option on or whisper someone, and people who come online or join your group later get it too. The people you whisper keep getting it for a time you choose in the settings (3 hours by default).
• Link players who don't use the add-on. Start a person from one of their characters and link their other characters to them, or add an alt you know to someone's shared identity. A small mark shows what the player didn't share themselves.
• Right-click any player, from their unit frame, the guild roster, your friends, recent contacts or their name in chat, to link their character to a person, show that person, make it their main or unlink it.
• Your whole guild, known to everyone. Once the guild master or an officer enables Who's Who for the guild, in a new tab of the guild panel, guild members pass on to each other the identities guildmates shared, so you recognise every guildmate who uses Who's Who, even one you've never been online with. The window's Guild tab then lists your guildmates by identity, and the members not known yet.
• Guilds that link alts to mains. The guild master or an officer can require it. Each member is asked first: link their characters in the guild, share them with the guild only without linking them, or refuse, and Who's Who then shares nothing with that guild. Only the guild sees the characters they didn't link.
• Guild links. The guild master and officers can link members' characters for the whole guild, from the Guild tab's right-click menu: to a member's identity, or to a new person for someone who doesn't use Who's Who. Every member sees them; what a player shares about themselves always comes first.
• Guild requests. The guild master and officers can suggest a nickname or a main to a member, from the Guild tab's right-click menu. The member accepts, edits or refuses it, and the officers see which requests are done.…

[1.0.0] - 2026-10-23
First release for the live game of World of Warcraft: Forever. What Who's Who does:
• One identity for all your characters: link the characters you play, pick your main, set a nickname, and a different nickname or main in each guild if you like.
• You decide who sees it: your guild, your friends (WoW friends, and Battle.net friends playing WoW: Forever), your party or raid, or the people you whisper. Nothing is shared until you link a character.
• Recognise people across their alts: the People tab lists the identities shared with you, with their characters, who is online and when you last saw them; their nickname shows in chat, in tooltips and, if you want, on nameplates.
• Your own nicknames and notes for anyone, seen only by you, and links you make yourself for players who don't use Who's Who.
• Guilds: once the guild master or an officer enables Who's Who, guildmates pass on each other's identities, and the Guild tab lists the guild by identity. Officers can require members to link their characters in the guild, link characters for the whole guild, and suggest a nickname or a main to a member.
• Guild invites for your alts: when the guild allows it, an alt outside the guild asks for an invite with the Invitation… button in My identity; an officer online gets a dialog and invites it with one click.
• Privacy: your identity is signed with a key that stays on your computer, BattleTags are never sent, and Forget me removes you from everyone's list.
Changed
• Saved data: the first time you play the live game, Who's Who starts over as on a first install: what it saved during the beta, your identity included, is gone with the beta. Your settings stay.
Fixed
• Window: other windows now come in front of the Who's Who window when you click them, instead of staying behind it.

[0.5.0] - 2026-10-22
This version no longer exchanges with the earlier ones: everyone needs it to keep sharing.
Added
• Characters: your record now keeps each linked character's race, and when it reached the highest level, for features to come.
• Updates: once a session, Who's Who tells you in chat when another player's is a newer release than yours (any newer version while yours is a pre-release). You can turn it off in the settings, under Updates.
• /ww status and the Diagnostic page show the newest Who's Who version another player's add-on announced this session.
• Guilds: in My identity, "In my guilds" sets a nickname and a main for each guild your characters are in; only that guild's members see them.
• Guild requests: the guild master and officers can suggest a nickname or a main to a member, from the right-click menu in the Guild tab; the member accepts, edits or refuses it. Officers see each request, and whether it's done, in the member's panel and in a Requests list, and dismiss it there.
• Guild invites: from a character outside your guild, "Invitation…" on its line in My identity's "In my guilds" asks the guild's officers you know of to invite it (or whisper ginv to one); the officer is asked whether to invite it when another character of your identity is in the guild. The guild master or an officer turns it on in the guild's Who's Who settings.
• Nameplates: a new setting shows the nickname above or below the name on friendly players' nameplates, outside dungeons and raids. It's off by default, and may not work with nameplate add-ons.
• Battle.net friends: with the Friends scope, your Battle.net friends playing WoW: Forever share identities with you as your WoW friends do, whatever character or server they play.
Changed
• Add-on compartment: clicking Who's Who's entry opens its settings, as other add-ons do; the minimap button still shows the window. The diagnostic mode's lines are now always in English.
• Protocol: a new version of Who's Who's protocol, which no longer exchanges with the earlier ones. It skips the records and guild lists it already holds without unpacking them.
• Guild sharing: a guild member who is also your friend now gets both your linked characters and what your guild's rule adds. With your Guild scope off, a member of a guild enforcing linking who is not your friend sees only the characters its rule adds, without your nickname.
Fixed
• People: a player's old identity, whose characters now show under their new one, no longer stays in your saved data without any character.
• Guild sharing: in a group, the characters a guild enforcing linking adds to your record are no longer sent to group members outside that guild.

[0.4.3] - 2026-10-19Fixed
• Guild links: a member who logged in while no officer they had met was online no longer stays without the guild's links for the session: an officer passes them on as soon as one is online.
• Guild lists: a member whose list was more recent but lacked the guild's links or other members no longer waits for luck to get them: the first member holding them who takes that list announces its own back, and the member takes it.

[0.4.2] - 2026-10-19Changed
• Guild lists: in a large guild, Who's Who no longer freezes the game for a moment each time it announces you or receives a guild list: your own list is hashed again only when it changed.
• Records received: checking a record's signature no longer makes the game stutter: the check is spread over more frames, in smaller pieces.
• Messages from other players: Who's Who no longer handles them during combat, and handles at most one record or guild list per frame, so a burst of them no longer lowers your frame rate.
• Combat: Who's Who no longer checks signatures or sends records and guild lists during combat; they wait for its end.
Fixed
• Mac: Who's Who could fail to load on Mac, leaving an empty window on screen.

[0.4.1] - 2026-10-18Fixed
• Guild lists: logging out no longer makes guild members ask you for your guild list or settings, which you could no longer send.

B.O.L.T Changelog
(Brittle and Occasionally Lethal Tweaks)

Entries below the marker are added automatically by the release workflow from commit messages — newest first.
v8-1 (2026-11-01)
• fix: Skyriding keys no longer get stuck turning after landing mid-turn
• - While A/D (or W/S with pitch control) is held, the key overrides now wait until you release it before switching, so the release reaches Turn/Pitch and the movement stops. Taking off while holding a key no longer leaves you strafing either
• - Landing in combat can't be handled that way (addons can't change bindings in combat); a stuck key there is detected and fixed by tapping it once after combat
• - Fixed the remap never applying in v8-0: the secure snippet couldn't read the key list because its attribute names started with "_"
• Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
v8-0 (2026-11-01)
• refactor: overhaul for Midnight 12.1.5 and WoW: Forever [major]
• - Supports Midnight 12.1.5 (120105) and WoW: Forever (16001) from one TOC; modules that need modern-only systems (Skyriding, Key Share, Smart Teleport, Achievement Tracker) hide themselves on Forever
• - Skyriding now switches key overrides through a secure state driver, so A/D and W/S return to normal the moment you land, even in combat
• - Settings rebuilt from declarative tables on non-deprecated templates; the settings page now appears in Options without typing /bolt first
• - Admin panel and hardcore/dismount chat triggers work again; settings are saved account-wide and the password typed in chat is no longer sent to the channel
• - Transmog Presets ported to Midnight's outfit API: presets are staged in the transmog window and confirmed with Blizzard's Apply button
• - Auto Rep Switch uses FACTION_STANDING_CHANGED, so it also works in instances and detects every gain (not only rank-ups)
• - Achievement Tracker no longer hitches (time budget was 500 ms per frame instead of ~2 ms) and can't get stuck after a scan error; un-ticking Exploration now persists
• - Toy picker restores your Toy Box filters after scanning instead of changing them
• - Wowhead links cover toys, mounts, auras, currencies, NPCs, quests and achievements, use the Forever database on Forever, and only claim Ctrl+C if it is unbound
• - Smart Teleport works again after being disabled and re-enabled
• - Fixed: settings that defaulted to true could not be turned off; Copy Target Mount wrongly reported uncollected mounts; Edit Mode switching no longer taints Edit Mode; missing TRP3 keybinding name
• - Shared helpers for dialogs, chat sending and the game menu watcher; removed dead code

Rolling build of the uwucrew tools. Each file is rebuilt automatically whenever its part of the code changes on main.

uwucrew Sync app installs the addon, keeps it updated, syncs your characters to Discord and shows them:
• Windows: uwucrew-sync-windows-setup.exe. If SmartScreen warns, click More info → Run anyway.
• Mac (M1 and newer): uwucrew-sync-mac-arm64.dmg. Mac (Intel): uwucrew-sync-mac-x64.dmg. Open it and drag the app into Applications.
• Linux: uwucrew-sync-linux-x86_64.AppImage. Make it executable and run it. If it won't start (Ubuntu 24.04 and newer), run it with --no-sandbox.

Setup: open the app, run /sync link in Discord and paste the code into the app. Then play: it syncs each time you log out or /reload. The app updates itself.

The uwucrew-sync-mac-.zip and latest.yml files are for the app's automatic updates; you don't need to download them.

uwucrew Sync addon on its own: UwucrewSync.zip. Unzip into your WoW Forever Interface/AddOns folder. Not needed if you use the app.
addons.description:
Discord bot for uwucrew, a World of Warcraft: Forever guild.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /help [post] | In-Discord guide: quick start plus topic pages (characters, raids, LFG, loot, timezones, officer tools). post:true (Manage Events) posts the full guide in the current channel, one message per section. Rerun it to update the guide; it replaces its previous messages |
| /char add/remove/main/prof/list/view | Register characters by Forever's first + last name (e.g. Asha Brightvale), with class, race, role, level, main/alt and professions. view shows a synced profile: gear (linked to Wowhead), item level, professions, gold, played time, lockouts, reputation |
| /quests [character] | A character's current quest log (up to 40), grouped by zone with objectives, Wowhead links, ready-to-turn-in markers, and which guildmates are on the same quest |
| /sync paste/link/unlink | Sync characters from the uwucrew Sync addon: paste the in-game code, or link the desktop app for automatic syncs |
| /ding | Update a character's level and announce it (with a special shout for the first to hit 60) |
| /leaderboard | Race to 60: highest levels, ties broken by who got there first |
| /roster [class] [alts] | Guild roster grouped by class, with role counts |
| /crafters
| Who has a profession, by skill |
| /craft | Who can craft a specific item, from recipes the addon syncs when someone opens their profession window |
| /progress | Raid progress from synced lockouts: bosses down per raid, first-kill dates, best clear this week |
| /event create/cancel | (Manage Events) Raid post with Tank/Healer/DPS/Tentative/Absent buttons and a ping reminder before start. Also shows in Discord's Events tab. Can repeat weekly or every 2 weeks (the next one is posted when the current one starts). cancel series:true stops the repeats |
| /sr reserve/list | One soft reserve per person per raid |
| /lfg | 5-man group finder (1 tank / 1 healer / 3 DPS), pings everyone when full |
| /loot give/history | Loot log (giving is officer-only) |
| /attendance | Signup rate over the last 10 raids |
| /rolepanel | (Manage Roles) Posts a panel in the current channel: Join uwucrew (gives the member role) and toggles for the Tank/Healer/DPS Discord roles, which it creates if missing |
| /apply | Application form → officer channel with Accept/Decline (accept grants the member role + DMs them) |
| /timezone | Set your timezone once. Search by city (london) or by what your clock says right now (8:15 pm) |
| /forever | Launch and raid dates, new dungeons and the raids announced so far |

Group channels: /lfg and /event create each get a private text channel and voice channel (turn off with channels:false). Only the organizer and people signed up can see them, and access updates as people join or leave. The channels are deleted GROUP_TTL_HOURS after the start time, once voice is empty. They're deleted right away if the event is cancelled or everyone leaves an LFG group. Set GROUP_CATEGORY_ID to keep them under one category.

Bench: if a raid has a size and it's full, role signups go on the bench. When a spot opens, the oldest bench signup is moved in and DM'd.

Times: type them naturally in /event create when:, e.g. friday 8pm, tomorrow 20:00, nov 10 7:30pm or in 2 hours. They're read in your /timezone, or you can name a zone (sat 9pm CET). As you type, the autocomplete shows exactly how it was read. Leave it empty to pick from the next week's 8 PM slots. Event posts use Discord timestamps, so everyone sees times in their own timezone.

Click a signup button again to withdraw. Signups use your main character's name. Edit src/game.ts as Forever info firms up.

addons.description:
Mentor and new-player matchmaking for WoW Forever. Flag a character as a
Sprout (new or returning, looking for help) or a Mentor (experienced,
offering help), see who else on your realm cluster has done the same, and
whisper or invite them from a roster window.
Usage
| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| /sprout | Toggle the roster window |
| /sprout role off\|sprout\|mentor | Set this character's role |
| /sprout note | Set the note others see next to your name (max 80 chars) |
| /sprout config | Open the settings panel |
| /sprout status | Show channel and roster status |
| /sprout debug | Toggle protocol logging in the chat frame |

A minimap button opens the roster on left-click and settings on right-click;
it can be hidden in settings. The roster window has two boxes, Sprouts and Mentors. Each row shows name,
level, class and zone. Left-click a row to whisper; right-click for Whisper,
Invite to party and Add/Edit private note. Hovering a row shows the player's
note and your own private note about them. Private notes are account-wide;
role and own note are per character.

Players are identified by their Forever name, "First Surname". There are no
realms on Forever; any -Realm suffix the client attaches is ignored.

Scope: discovery runs over a hidden custom chat channel, so it reaches your
connected-realm cluster and faction, not the whole game.
How it works
• On login the addon silently joins a hidden custom channel
(JoinTemporaryChannel with no chat frame) and retries until the channel
list has populated. Join/leave notices for it are filtered from chat.
• Presence is exchanged with addon messages over that channel using a
registered prefix. Messages are version;TYPE;key=value;... strings, so
fields can be added later without breaking older clients.
• Each active player broadcasts a heartbeat (HB) with role, level, class,
zone, note and its own heartbeat interval. The interval starts at 2 minutes
and stretches as the roster grows (up to 10 minutes) so per-client traffic
stays roughly flat on crowded clusters. BYE is sent when switching to Off
and, best effort, on logout.
• Roster entries expire after 3 missed heartbeats of the sender's own
interval. The roster is in memory only and rebuilt every session.
• WHO is sent on joining the channel and, for the first 2 minutes after
that, when the window is opened or refreshed. Beyond that heartbeats have
already filled the roster and WHO is not sent. Active peers answer HERE
after a 0-10 s random delay; requests arriving while a reply is pending
share that one reply, so bursts of logins do not multiply traffic.
• Characters set to Off still join the channel and can browse, but never
announce themselves or answer WHO.
• Sending goes through AceComm and ChatThrottleLib, which paces traffic and
re-queues messages the client rejects with the addon-message throttle.
Performance notes
Nothing runs per frame; all work is event or timer driven. Per client, a
heartbeat costs a few string matches and one small table, and roster memory
is a few hundred bytes per player. The roster window keeps a fixed pool of
row frames (only as many as fit on screen) and rebinds them to the visible
slice of the sorted roster, so drawing cost does not grow with population.
While open it redraws at most once per second on roster changes.

addons.description:
A fancy LDB reputation display, show faction reputation and reputation change history
Addon Description
Sexy Reputation is an LDB reputation display. In addition to an interactive tooltip, Sexy Reputation will also keep track of daily reputation changes as well as session changes. This is meant to be a worthy successor to FuBar_FactionFu, and much more.
Features:
• Displays all factions in a tree, with the option to fold/unfold each tree.
• Ability to track progress of a faction in the LDB text display.
• Doesn't use Blizzard functionality to hide, show or track reputation (which means no other addons will mess with the display).
• Shows hidden reputation for certain faction groups, such as Horde and Shattrah city.
• Tracks historical faction gains, displaying session, today, yesterday, week and month in a tooltip as you hover over the faction.
• Option to only show factions that has shown a gain or a loss today
• Customizable colors for the reputation standing levels.
• Option to show standing and reputation either as a bar or as text
• Ability to toggle rep gains, reputation level, standing and reputation percentage on and off.
• Support for MoP friendship faction.
Planned Features
• Option to have alternating colors in the faction tooltip, so you can more easily follow the lines.
• Graphing options to visualize rep changes in the past 30 days, or more.
• Customizable font.
• Customizable reputation bar texture.
• Whatever else I can think of.

Levelbound1.2.1
Fixes:
• Leveling up outside a group no longer raises an "AddOn tried to call the protected function" error. The
game blocks addons from sending emotes on their own, so Emote Level-Up Message is now Print Level-Up Message and
shows the line in your own chat instead.
1.2.0
Gain indicator:
• The gain indicator can sit to the right or left of its bar, centered on it. Where there is no room beside the
bar, such as in fullscreen, it sits above that end of the bar instead.
• With segmented bars, gains beside the bar gather in one stack next to the whole row, labeled by type as when
detached, and grow in the chosen direction.
• A new Animate switch, on by default. Turned off, the indicator and the detached stack appear in place and fade
without moving.
• A new Animation Style for indicators beside the bar or detached: Rise, as before, or Slide Outward, away from
the bar. With Slide Outward, the segmented and detached stacks line up side by side instead of on top of each
other, and the detached stack can grow left or right.
• The Gain Indicator and progress type previews show the indicator beside the bar when it is set there.

Party level-up notices:
• Two new anchors, Right of Bar and Left of Bar, place the notices beside the bar, the first one centered on it.
Where there is no room beside the bar, they sit above that end of the bar instead.
• The same Animation Style as the gain indicator, for notices beside the bar or detached: Rise, as before, or Slide
Outward, with the notices side by side growing away from the bar. Detached, they can grow left or right.

Fixes:
• When a type gains again while its line is still in the detached stack, that line moves to the front, so the
stack's lines fade from the oldest first instead of an older line sliding back before it fades.
• All new text is translated into German, Spanish, French, Italian, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and
Chinese.
1.1.0
New looks:
• A first-time install now asks you to choose a style: Blizzard or Modern, each with a preview of the experience bar.
• Blizzard border: the default experience bar's own frame, with beveled ends, Blizzard's dividers and the bar at
Blizzard's height. Text inside the bar is turned off, since there is no room for it.
• Levelbound Blizzard bar texture: the default experience bar's two-tone fill, in any bar color.
• Pip party markers: Blizzard's rested-experience tick, in each member's class color. On the Blizzard border they
start at Blizzard's own size and place.
• The 1 Pixel and 2 Pixel borders are now one Pixel border with a Border Width from 1 to 10. Your saved border is
kept.

More control:
• XP dividers can mark every 10% or every 5% of a level.
• Party markers can sit on the bar's center, top or bottom edge, with a vertical offset. Top-Edge Notch is now
Notch and points into the bar from either edge.
• Bar width moves in 1-pixel steps and can go up to your screen's width.
• Text shown on hover now fades in and out.
• Your level-ups are announced as an emote to players nearby while you are not in a group, so others see
Levelbound in action. It is on by default and can be turned off on the Level-Ups page's Announcements tab.
• Level-up messages in emote, party and guild chat now start with a star icon.

A tidier settings window:
• Settings are split into tabs. Layout, Appearance, Text and Visibility share one Layout page; the Gain
Indicator, each progress type, Markers and Level-Ups have tabs of their own.
• Every page has a short description under its title.
• A bar's own size and each text slot's style show whether they follow the shared setting, with a button to go
back to it.
• Previews keep the same size as you change settings, and draw bars at a steady width.
• The Appearance preview replays the gain effect while Gain Shimmer is on; hovering the Markers preview fades the
markers in as on the real bar.
• More of each preview can be clicked to find its setting: the ring around a bar finds Border Style even with no…
addons.description:
Levelbound replaces Blizzard's experience and reputation bars with its own. It shows how far you are through the level, how much rested and turn-in XP you have waiting, how fast you're leveling this session, and where the rest of your party is.

Download on CurseForge. Works on Retail and WoW: Forever.
Experience bar
• Rested XP and XP from completed quests you haven't turned in are drawn on the bar in their own colors.
• The bar tracks your XP per hour for the current session and estimates your time to the next level, pausing while you AFK.
• Time played, time at this level and session time are all available as text or in the tooltip.
• Custom notice for gaining exp.
Other progress
Levelbound also tracks these, when your game version has them:
• Pet XP
• Reputation
• Honor
• House Favor
• Neighborhood Endeavors
• Trading Post

Put them all on one segmented bar, stack them as connected bars, or place each bar separately with its own size.
Party markers
Party members who also run Levelbound show up as markers on your XP bar, placed at their own progress toward their next level. Hover a marker for detailed information on their progress and rate. When a party member levels up, you get a notice on screen, a chat line and a sound. Each one can be turned off.

Markers work in 5-player groups, including dungeon finder groups, and hide automatically in raids.
Sharing
• Shift-click a bar to put a line like [Levelbound] Level 42 · 63% · 18.4k to go · ~1h 12m at 48k XP/hr in your chat box.
• /lb share party (or instance, raid, guild, say) sends the line directly.
• Optionally announce your own level-ups to party or guild, and post an XP summary at the end of a dungeon or delve.
Customization
In-depth customization options so you can tailor the visuals to your liking.

Open settings with /lb, the minimap button or the addon compartment.

/lb edit opens edit mode, where you can drag the bars into place.
Translating
Translations are welcome by pull request. See TRANSLATING.md.

Advanced, and the gain indicator's offsets sit with its amount text. A bar's own size shows only in Independent

Reforged UI1.8.4 (2026-10-24)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Keep the time capsule above the minimap with the top bar hidden (#35)
With the top bar hidden, the time capsule moves to the console on top of the micro buttons. It can be dragged there in Edit Mode or with Shift held out of combat (consoleOpts.clockSpot, /rui clock reset).
• Describe the Skyborne themes as they look now (#36)
The CurseForge description still showed the pre-#5 look. It now describes each faction's class-coloured console: High Order in arcane violet, frost-white and silver; Windshapers in storm blue, ember gold and slate.
• Add a UI size slider for a smaller console and top bar (#34)
Options get a "UI size" slider (70-100 %, default 100) and /rui size:
the console and top bar shrink by that factor. Edit Mode's places for
the target's auras and the cast bar follow when the slider is let go.
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that replaces the bottom of the screen with
the Warcraft III console, with a theme for every playable race: Human, Dwarf,
Gnome, Night Elf, Orc, Tauren, Troll, Undead (Forsaken or Scourge) and
Skyborne (High Order and Windshapers).

The console is a port of a WoW 1.12 console addon: its layout, art, fonts and options menu,
rebuilt for the current engine (Edit Mode, secret values, protected frames).
All console art and the font in ReforgedUI/art are the original addon's. Reforged UI
adds the top bar with the day/night clock and data broker feeds.
What it does
Left to right, as in the original addon with its "Center UI" option, which is always on:
the console sits in the middle of the screen with the original addon's chat width (on a
16:9 screen it fills the width, on 21:9 and 32:9 screens the rest of the
screen stays free on either side).
• Minimap block: a square minimap with mouse-wheel zoom, the zone name on
its bottom or top edge, the tracking button in the round slot below it, the
mail slot (a grey letter when there is no mail) and three action slots
beside it. Other addons' minimap buttons go in a compartment: click the bag
just above the map's top-right corner to open or close a flyout of them
(Blizzard's own buttons line up along the top edge of the map); the minimap's day/night indicator is hidden (the top bar has the
clock).
• Portrait block: animated 3D portrait (click to target yourself,
right-click for your menu), health and power bars under it, rest/combat,
group leader and PvP icons. The background pulses red under the low health
threshold.
• Hero screen: name, level and class, the experience bar with rested
experience (hover for the numbers, right-click for its colour: purple,
blue or none) and four stat icons. Each shows main hand, off hand (block
chance and value with a shield), ranged, ammo (yellow under 400, red under
200), spell power, healing, armour (the default for the fourth),
strength, agility, intellect (with Warcraft III's hero attribute art),
crit chance (the best of melee, ranged and spell, with the Blademaster's
Critical Strike icon) or nothing (an empty socket), chosen per class from each icon's right-click menu
or the options menu. Druid forms and Ghost Wolf swap
the icons like the original addon.
• Target: by default the hero screen switches to your target, as
selecting a unit in Warcraft III: its portrait, name (coloured by reaction
or class), level and classification, health and power bars with numbers,
your combo points and its cast bar. Your own bars under the portrait stay
yours; clearing the target brings your hero back. "Wall plate" in the
options (or /rui target plate) instead puts the target in a small
portrait arch standing on the wall above the stats panel. Either way the
target's target is a small unit icon above the portrait (blue when it is
you, else green, yellow or red), with the target's buffs and debuffs
beside it (above the plate in plate mode). Those are Blizzard's own aura
icons: in combat the game lets no addon read a target's auras, so
Blizzard's target frame stays with everything but its auras made
invisible, and the "Reforged UI" Edit Mode layout places it (buffs on
top) so the icons land there.
Left-click targets, right-click opens the unit menu.
For the target's health nearer the middle of the screen, the options'
"Target bar" (or /rui targetbar on) adds a small free-standing bar with
its name, level, health and power, in either mode. It is click-through
until you hold Shift out of combat (or open Edit Mode), then drag it anywhere; its place
is saved on its own and never touches the Edit Mode layout.
• Action grid: action bars 1-3, twelve slots each. These are Blizzard's
own buttons, moved into the grid and reskinned, so bindings, paging,
cooldowns and proc glows work as usual. The stance buttons (Paladin auras,
Warrior stances, Druid forms, ...) stand in a row on the wall above the grid,…

addons.description:
Alluneve-Debug is a standalone debugging framework for World of Warcraft Retail addon developers. It provides a shared API for structured, severity-based logging without having to build and maintain your own logging infrastructure or flood the chat with diagnostic messages.

Diagnostic messages are retained in independent, per-addon rolling histories. When a Lua error can be attributed to a registered addon, Alluneve-Debug automatically submits a flight-recorder report to !BugGrabber, containing events from 60 seconds before and 10 seconds after the error by default. This gives developers a timeline of what their addon was doing around the failure, rather than just a stack trace.

The recorder can also be triggered manually or through the API, allowing developers to investigate unexpected behavior that doesn't produce a Lua error.
Features
• Shared debugging API with DEBUG, INFO, WARN, and ERROR severity levels.
• Independent per-addon session logs, limited to approximately 1 MiB of estimated memory per addon.
• Automatic flight-recorder reports for attributed Lua and recognized taint errors.
• Manual recording triggers and session-log submission through the API or slash commands.
• Always-on diagnostic recording with optional chat output, independent of combat.
• Efficient paged FIFO storage, a single global cleanup ticker, and frame-budgeted cleanup to minimize performance spikes.
• Reports accessible through !BugGrabber and compatible viewers such as BugSack.

Error attribution is best-effort. Only diagnostic events supplied by participating addons are recorded.

For integration instructions and API documentation, see INSTALLATION.md.

addons.description:
Record your WoW: Forever journey from level 1 to 60, then relive it on the web.

Journey Forever turns the saved files your addons already write into a recap page for each character: the path you walked, levels, quests, dungeons, loot, gold, deaths, and screenshots of the big moments.
How it works
1. Play. Install the Journey Forever addon (plus, optionally, Road to Sixty and Journey Tracker for path and stats data).
2. Log out. WoW writes each addon's SavedVariables file to disk.
3. Upload. Drag your WTF\Account\ folder and your Screenshots folder onto the website.
4. Share. Each character gets a journey page, private by default, public with one switch.
What's in this repo
| Folder | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| addon/ | The in-game addon: automatic screenshots (dungeon cleared, epic loot, level up) and /jf note entries. |
| website/ | The site that reads your saved files and builds the journey pages. Hosted on Cloudflare; its README covers running it locally and deploying. |
