In-game companion addon for World of Warcraft: Forever. Talent guides in your talent window, a dungeon quest panel beside the group finder, route guides with waypoints, and one-line character export for wowforeverbuilds.com.

Nothing is sent anywhere. The addon reads your own character and the quest log, and every piece of data it needs ships inside it.

• The next talent glows, and pulses while you have a point to spend.
• Talents the guide still wants show the level of their next point; ones it does not take show a red x.
• A panel beside the talent window lists the whole order, level by level.
• On level up, chat tells you what to take, and warns you when you spend a point off the guide.

/wfb guide list lists the guides for your class, /wfb guide 3 picks one, /wfb guide off turns it off.
Dungeon Journal beside the group finder
Open the group finder and the Dungeon Journal opens next to it, with a Dungeon Journal button above the window to show and hide it.
• Follows what you do: queue for a dungeon, tick one in the finder or walk into one, and the journal switches to it. The Dungeons button picks any other.
• The quest list on the left shows the level you can pick each quest up at, its faction crest, and YOU HAVE IT, TURN IN, DONE or PRE-QUEST. The Alliance and Horde crests at the top switch whose quests are listed.
• Click a quest and the right page reads like the quest log: objective, where it starts (with a Show on Map button that puts a pin on the world map), who takes it, notes on sharing and what happens inside, the chain before it, and the rewards with their icons and tooltips.
• A Bosses tab lists the dungeon's bosses with the quests that need each one.
• Questlines that open a dungeon chain are listed above it, and your quest log marks those quests with [D] or [D>].
• XP for your character: the reward and the dungeon total use your level, by the game's rule (full XP up to 5 levels above the quest, then 80%, 60%, 40%, 20%, 10%). Base figures come from the beta client's quest data.

/wfb quests opens the panel from chat.
Route guides with waypoints
/wfb route opens a panel that walks you through an errand the quest log does not point you to, stop by stop.
• The current stop gets a map pin, or a TomTom arrow when TomTom is installed.
• Chat tells you what to do when you arrive, and picking up the stop's quest moves you on to the next one.
• Routes can be faction-specific: each character sees only its own faction's version.
• Progress is kept per character.
• On the world map: a Routes button in the corner picks a route, and its stops show as numbered pins (green = current, gold = still to do, grey = done) on the zone map and on the continent. Hover a pin for what to do there; click it to make it your current stop.
Minimap icon
Left click opens the route guides; right click opens a menu with the routes, the Dungeon Journal, a tick to turn the talent guide on or off, the talent window and the character export. Drag it around the minimap. /wfb minimap hides or shows it.

The first route is the Cozy Sleeping Bag (up to 3% more experience while you rest in it). More routes are added in updates as they are found: hidden quest chains, collectibles and other errands worth the trip. /wfb route list lists the routes, /wfb route next / /wfb route back move between stops, /wfb route stop clears the waypoint.
Settings page
The addon has its own page under Options → AddOns → WoW Forever Builds (or /wfb options): switch each part on or off, pick your talent guide and your route from a dropdown, and open any panel from there. Switches: minimap icon, talent guide, its order panel and chat messages, the quest panel opening with the group finder, the [D] marks in the quest log, the Routes button and pins on the world map, arrival chat, and the TomTom arrow.

1.0.0 — 2026-11-04
• First stable version of Tessera, made for WoW Forever. New here? Type /tessera: the quick tour shows the essentials, and the demo mode (Help tab) shows every block and every style.
• In short: more than 40 information blocks (gold, bags, durability, FPS, latency, clocks, date, XP, quests, professions, reputation, mail, WoW Forever's own systems...), launcher blocks for minimap and addon buttons, and DataBroker both ways.
• Blocks dropped against each other merge like the tiles of a mosaic: bars, columns, corners. Screen edges, ready-made layouts, 19 styles, profiles and sharing as text.
New
• German, Spanish (Spain and Mexico) and Brazilian Portuguese translations. Claude (an AI) made them and nobody has reviewed them yet: you can correct them with CurseForge's localization tool.
• Streamer mode, for streams and videos: other players' names, your other characters, your guild's name and your gold show as ***. Turn it on in the General tab, with a key binding, or with the new Streamer mode block (hidden by default).

Fixes

• Each character's data (its own profile, its gold and gold history) is now saved under its full name, as WoW Forever has no realms: it no longer depends on the server's name, which may change. Your settings carry over on their own at your next login.

addons.description:
Download: CurseForge · Wago · GitHub releases

Written by an AI (Claude) from my ideas; I test every version in game; no human reads the code line by line.

TL;DR: Gold, bags, FPS, Legacy points… in small blocks that snap together like mosaic tiles. Made by a player who can't code and an AI that can't play (yet). So I test it a lot.

Tessera is a World of Warcraft addon for WoW Forever that shows small information blocks
(gold, bags, durability, FPS, latency, time, XP, quests...) and launcher blocks (minimap and
addon compartment buttons). Each block can be styled and placed on its own, and blocks placed
against each other merge into a single frame, like the tiles (tesserae) of a mosaic.

It only uses data provided by the game itself, and embeds no library. LibSharedMedia is used
when another addon provides it, to offer that addon's fonts, backgrounds and borders, and
LibDataBroker to exchange data with DataBroker addons.

> Made for WoW Forever. I build and test Tessera on WoW Forever. Its own systems
> (Legacy, camping, Comprehension, PvP) are still young and may change, so a game update can break
> a block until Tessera catches up.
What makes it different?
• Blocks that snap together. Drag a block against another and they merge into one bar. Build a top bar, a column, a corner cluster, or keep each block on its own.
• Made for WoW Forever. Legacy points (next reward, challenges per category), Comprehension (with the scrolls in your bags), Camping (buffs and kit), Honor, weapon skills.
• One look for everything. Every block shares the same tooltips and the same style: Blizzard's look, FlareUI, ElvUI, EllesmereUI, or fantasy styles built from the game's own frames.
• In your language. English and French from day one, plus German, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.
• Looked after. Each version is tested in game, and your layouts carry over from one version to the next.
• Ready to stream. Streamer mode hides other players' names, your other characters, your guild's name and your gold in one click.
• DataBroker both ways. Show your other addons' DataBroker objects as blocks, or share Tessera's blocks with Titan Panel, Bazooka or Arcana (formerly ChocolateBar).
Why make Tessera when addons like it already exist?
I love bars like Arcana (formerly ChocolateBar) and Bazooka. I used Broker_Everything a lot, and I spent hours building small bars with a single piece of info each, to put them in just the right spot on my interface. My favorite was StatBlock Core by Funkeh: free-floating blocks, one per piece of info, that I could put anywhere. It hasn't been updated since 2022. And tooltips didn't look the same from one broker addon to the next, French was often missing, and many of those addons were no longer maintained.

When the WoW Forever beta came out, I came back to WoW and found FlareUI: an interface with a fantasy look, not a futuristic one. Seeing what players were building with AI's help, I wanted to try something: a small thing just for me, that did exactly what I asked for.

That's how Tessera was born. It was never meant to be published. I wanted to learn how it works when you start a GitHub repo from scratch and release an addon. Then I put it through more testing than I gave the Forever beta itself, and the ideas kept coming. Some are in Tessera today. Others are on the way (see below).

So I decided to make it available to as many players as I could. That meant watching closely what the AI does: the right WoW words in every language, and code checked with the tools real addon developers use.
Where it is going
Plans, not promises:
• Accessibility for players with disabilities: Tessera follows the game's own accessibility settings and only adds what its blocks need. From 1.3, every new feature is checked with text twice as big, in high contrast and without a mouse.…

Firekeeperv0.3.1 (2026-09-20)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• (docs): Write the 0.3.1 changelog (#53)
• (fix): Make the campfire buttons light an actual campfire (#52)
• (fix): Offer only the camp objects you are actually carrying
addons.description:
An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that helps a group build a good campsite.

A basic campfire holds three objects, each player may add one, and those objects share a
one-hour cooldown. Camp buffs do not stack with the equivalent class buff, so the
Incense Candle's Intellect is wasted if a mage is standing right there. The game does not
tell you what the people around the fire can place. Firekeeper does.
What it does
• Plans the fire. Everyone running Firekeeper shares which camp objects they can
place and when their cooldown is up. The planner picks one object per player, never
two with the same effect, and skips any buff your group's classes already cover.
• Tracks the shared cooldown, across your alts, adjusted for the Legacy perk
Field Guide.
• Announces the camp to party, raid, or say, so people know what is up and how many
slots are free.
• Finds a fire. /fk host tells other Firekeeper users where your camp is and how
many slots are free; /fk find lists the ones you have heard about, nearest first, and
/fk find 2 drops the game's own waypoint on one. Hosting is off until you ask for it.
• Says what your trades can place. /fk train lists each profession with the camp
objects you can already put down and how much skill the next one needs.
• Finds your guild. /fk guild lists guildies running Firekeeper with the distance
in yards and which way to walk. Sharing your own position is off until you turn it on.
• Names the buffs you are missing. /fk buffs reads what everyone at the fire is
actually carrying and says who can fix it, which is also how the planner knows a camp
object would be wasted. When the client will not show auras it says so instead of
guessing.
• Says what it does not know. /fk gaps lists the camp objects still missing from
the data and /fk caps prints which APIs this client actually allows.
Status
Early, and honest about it. Forever's beta opened on 17 September 2026 and the game
launches on 4 November 2026. Two things are still unsettled:

1. The data. Every camp object and every buff amount is in, read from the client's own
tooltip data. It is datamined rather than seen in game, so it is all marked reported. Every entry in Data/CampObjects.lua carries a
confidence level, and anything not yet seen in game is marked with a ? in the
panel. See docs/DATA.md.
2. The API. Blizzard has published no addon notes for Forever. Every uncertain call is
probed once at login (Core/Capabilities.lua); when something is missing the addon
drops to a simpler mode instead of erroring. See docs/RESEARCH.md.

If addon-to-addon messages turn out to be unavailable, Firekeeper still works as a
single-player planner over what you can see and type.
The panel
/fk opens it, or left-click the flame on your minimap. Everything the addon does is in
there — the slash commands are a shortcut, not the only way in. Five tabs:

| Tab | What is on it |
| --- | --- |
| Camp | What is on the fire, who should place what, what would be wasted, who is on cooldown. Announce to chat. |
| Place | Every object you can place, as icons. Green is the best choice here, red would be wasted, greyed out means you cannot — including when you simply have none in your bags, which it counts for you. Click one and it places it — the button uses the item, so you never leave the panel. The campfire buttons light a real fire the same way, using a kit from your bags, and the flame on the title bar lights the biggest one you are carrying. On a client that will not allow it, the button records the placement instead and says so. |
| Buffs | Every camp buff and what would cover it: missing, available from somebody standing here, already on the fire, or already covered by a class buff. Below it, the class buffs your group is missing. |
| Find | Camps other people are hosting, and how far — click one to put a waypoint on it. Host your own. Guildies nearby, with distance and direction, and the switch for sharing your position. |…

addons.description:
A tower-defense minigame you play inside WoW: Forever: on flight paths, in queues, or whenever you have five minutes.
• Four campaigns in the spirit of Warcraft III: the Horde, the Alliance, the Sentinels and the Forsaken. Eight levels each, 32 in all, fought on the real zone maps of Azeroth, from the Valley of Trials to Shadowfang Keep.
• Twenty towers, five per campaign, each with two specializations, and a hero for every campaign: Thrall, Bolvar, Tyrande and Sylvanas, each with an ability that turns a wave.
• Creeps and bosses with tricks: stealth that only some towers can see through, healers, spiders that split when they die, summons, blinks, stomps and enrages. Each campaign's story is told in briefings, battle cries and boss lines.
• Easy in and out: close the window and the game pauses, mid-wave included. A /reload picks up the same moment.
• Mouse only: no keybinds, so every key stays yours while you play on the side.
• Something to chase: three stars per level, Heroic mode, and Warmarks to research your towers in each campaign's Armory.
• Drawn with WoW's own art: zone maps, spell icons and creature portraits from the game itself. The addon ships no images.

Solo, free, and for WoW: Forever (interface 16001). Found a bug, or a level that's too hard or too easy? Please open an issue: balance feedback is very welcome.

RaidMapv1.1.0 (2026-10-14)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Auto-open relevant map inside an instance
• Add Hall of Thanes map, and minor fixes
• Text on slides: one line, one size, typed in place
A Text tool beside Arrow and Path. Click the map and type; Enter or a click
elsewhere keeps it, Escape drops it. Click text to edit, drag to move,
right-click to delete. Pipes and control characters are stripped and the
text is capped at 50 letters, so it saves, syncs and exports intact. Each
edit is one undo step and one publish. No export format change; older
clients carry text along without drawing it.
Also: version 1.1.0 in the TOC, updated credits, and mapdata.py's
snapshots and reports are now gitignored and kept locally.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Present Mode alone presents and follows; publishing survives DBM
The editor no longer sends slide focus or follows it. The Present window keeps
its own board and slide: its arrows and menus move it and, for anyone who may
publish, tell the group; a focus that arrives moves it and nothing else. In a
party everyone may publish, so paging through a pack in the editor used to
drag everyone else's editor along, and a presenter's board change cleared the
author's undo history.
LibSerialize is now registered as RaidMap-LibSerialize. Under the shared name
LibStub handed RaidMap DBM-Core's r6, which divides by each number it writes;
the game raises "Division by zero" for that, so with DBM enabled any pack
holding a 0 (every new board does) could not be published or exported.
A publish that fails now leaves the pack as it was. The revision used to move
first, so each failed click put the sender a revision ahead, and their client
then ignored everyone else's updates of that pack as stale. Snapshots for
history and export strings are taken from a copy without the history instead
of lifting it off the pack, which a failed serialize used to lose for good.

addons.changelog:
Crafter's Journal0.36.0
• Crafted tools in the right place, and required steps can't be removed. A tool you craft (Runed Golden Rod) now shows up at the step that needs it instead of at the start of the route. When a crafted item can't be bought (it binds when picked up, or nobody sells it), its row says so and has no ✕.
• Clearer essence conversions. The row now says what to convert and how many times ("Convert 129 Greater Magic Essence into 387 Lesser Magic Essence · right-click the Greater Magic Essence in your bags (129 times)"), and to buy them first if you don't have them.
• The current step counts skill points, not crafts. The highlighted step said "2 of 12 crafts" even when those 2 points came from crafting something else (like Bolt of Woolen Cloth for a later step), as if you had made 2 Woolen Capes. It now says "2/10 points · ~10 more crafts": how far you are in the step, and about how many more of that recipe you need.
• Professions in a steady order. The home page and Patterns sort the cards the same way: your professions first, then the rest. Within each group they follow a fixed order: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Leatherworking and Tailoring, then the secondary professions, Cooking and First Aid. Before, each page sorted differently and the order changed as you leveled.
• Error log. The addon now keeps a record of its own Lua errors and of actions the game blocks, grouping repeats with a count. They still show up as usual (error window, BugSack…). Type /cj errors to list them and /cj errors clear to empty the list. When reporting a bug, this list helps a lot.
• A star over the NPC you're sent to. Clicking a trainer, vendor or auctioneer row still sets the route, and if that NPC is nearby it's also targeted and marked with the star raid marker, so it's easy to spot in a crowd. Clicking again removes the star. It does nothing in combat or if the NPC isn't nearby. In a group, only the leader or an assistant can set markers.
• A new route planner: it looks at the whole route, like a GPS. The old planner picked the best recipe one skill point at a time, then corrected itself in several passes. That was slow and could settle for a route that isn't the best overall. The new one looks at the whole route, the way a sat-nav finds the shortest road. It proposes complete paths from your level to your target, each recipe paying its trainer (and any tool it needs) once. It walks each path with real Auction House prices, intermediate crafts and what's in your bags. Then it improves the best one: craft or buy each material, try other recipes for a step, move step boundaries. Across 49 test scenarios (every profession, several skill ranges, with and without bags) it found a cheaper route in 33 and the same one in 16, and never a worse one, in about the same time. It also avoids zigzag routes, like alternating Bolt of Woolen Cloth and Woolen Cape every point. It also remembers the route it gave you, so when your bags change (turning scraps into leather) it keeps that route unless another one is really better. Started routes don't change. tools/route_qa.py compares it with the old planner.
• Sell to the vendor from the vendor window. When you open a vendor, the Crafter's Journal window next to it now also lists what the Profit view says to sell to the vendor and you carry in your bags: how many and what you get. Click a row to sell it, or "Sell all". As with buying, it only sells when you click.
• Real vendor prices. Forever's vendors don't always pay what the game data says: Hillman's Shoulders sell for 6s 59c, not 11s 99c, and the route counted the higher price. When you sell something to a vendor, the addon now notes what you actually got and uses that from then on. Hillman's Shoulders are already corrected.…

A World of Warcraft: Forever addon to level every profession the cheapest way and keep track of your recipe collection.
• Cheapest route from your current skill to the cap, step by step, with real Auction House prices.
• Trainers by rank, with a waypoint to the nearest one.
• Every recipe of each profession: which you know, which you can learn now, and where to get the rest.
• English and Spanish.

Download it from CurseForge (link coming soon).

They're now learned at the trainer at the right level (the trainer cost shows as "?" since it isn't known yet).
• Fixed recipes you learn automatically. Linen Bag and a few other recipes are learned automatically in Forever; the route no longer sends you to pay the trainer for them.

• Start route. New "Start route" button under the summary: it locks the route you've chosen. While you buy on the Auction House, from vendors or take items from your mailbox, neither the route nor its cost change, and what you buy for it no longer shows up as free materials. Steps you've already passed are marked as done. Prices are frozen too: a new Auction House scan doesn't change the route's totals (not even after a reload) until you choose — "Update prices" keeps the same route with the new prices, "Recalculate route" looks for a new route. Playing never unlocks it (leveling up, buying, crafting), and when you reach your target it stays as "Route completed!" until you recalculate. Changing it on purpose does: "Recalculate route", the target, an option icon or removing a recipe.
• Live progress while you craft. With a route started, the step you're on is highlighted and shows how many crafts you've done and how many are left ("11 of 22 crafts · 11 left"); finished steps turn grey with a ✓ as soon as you reach the end of them, and you get a "Route completed!" message when you hit your target.
• Planned and actual. With a route started, the summary at the top shows a second row with what you've actually spent and earned since you started it: vendor and Auction House purchases, trainer costs and deposits, and what you get for selling what you craft (to vendors, and Auction House sales read from your mail). Only route items count.
• Shopping list at the vendor. Opening a vendor that sells something on your shopping list shows a window right next to it: what you're still missing, with a "Buy all" button (or click a row to buy just that one), and what you already have, greyed out. Purchases go one at a time and are checked when they arrive.
• Auction House purchases waiting in the mail. Auction House purchases arrive by mail in Forever: they're now counted as spent when you buy them, and the shopping list counts them as yours while they wait in your mailbox ("2 in the mail"), so it doesn't ask you to buy them again.
• Sell and post from the Profit view. With a vendor open, click a crafted item to sell what the route says to sell; with the Auction House open, click it to post it at the suggested price. Otherwise the click marks the nearest vendor or auctioneer on your map. Nothing is ever bought or sold without your click. The Profit view also shows how many of each item you've sold since starting the route.
• Craft from the route. Click a crafting step and it opens your profession with that recipe selected and starts crafting what's left of that step (at most what your materials allow). Your WoW health, power, combo points and cast bar — live on your RGB keyboard.
Download
• RGBUnitBars-0.2.0.exe — the desktop app. Run it once: it sits in the system tray, starts with Windows and wakes up when WoW is open. No Python or setup needed. OpenRGB 1.0 is bundled and started in the background automatically if you don't already run an OpenRGB SDK server.
• RGBUnitBars-0.2.0.zip — the addon (also on CurseForge). Extract into World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\ (or _classic_era_).

Use Windowed or Windowed (Fullscreen) mode in the game. Configure everything in-game with /rub.

Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unrecognized app (the exe is not code-signed yet): click More info → Run anyway.
What's new in 0.2.0
• Tray app: status, keyboard in use, Start with Windows, log, update notice
• Bundled OpenRGB, started hidden when needed and stopped on exit
• Lighter polling while WoW is closed or loading
• Addon: one-time popup with the app link, /rub app, Get the desktop app button in the settings
addons.description:
Your World of Warcraft health, power and combo points — live on your RGB keyboard.

The Keychron K3 Max currently connects by USB cable; Bluetooth support is planned.

| Class / resource | Keyboard layout (top → bottom) |
|---|---|
| Class | Default rows |
|---|---|
| Rogue | 2 combo · 2 health · 2 energy |
| Warrior, Hunter | 3 health · 3 power |
| Druid | 2 health · 2 power · 2 cast; power colour follows form |
| Other classes | 2 health · 2 power · 2 cast |
• Health uses your class colour (green when it would clash with your resource) and fades to red, pulsing below 25 %. Health and resource colours can be changed per class in /rub.
• Combo points are enabled by default for rogues only; they light up in five groups and flash at 5 — finisher time.
• Level-ups fill the keyboard with a hot-orange disk expanding from the center, keeping passed keys dimly shimmering until the return phase contracts a vertical orange band with two fading sparks; lighting stays off after death until you release your spirit, then a neutral gray-white wave continues until resurrection.
• Test these effects in-game with /rub dev levelup or /rub dev dead; run /rub dev clear afterward to restore your actual alive/dead state. /rub dev lists these commands.
• Empty parts of a bar stay faintly lit so you always see the full scale.
• Optional cast bar: its own rows, or taking over the health / power rows while you cast. Row order, fill direction and colour are set in /rub.

Works on WoW Forever / Classic beta (Interface 16001) and Classic Era (11509). No memory reading, no input automation: the addon draws one row of 24 dark pixels at the edge of the game window and the desktop app reads it.

A tiny World of Warcraft addon that lets you move and resize the Need / Greed / Pass loot roll window.
Made for WoW Forever (_classic_beta_, Interface 16001), also flagged for Classic Era.
Usage
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /rollmove | Show or hide the blue drag box |
| /rollmove scale 0.5-2 | Set the roll window scale |
| /rollmove reset | Restore the default Blizzard position and scale |

While the box is shown: drag it with the left mouse button, scroll to resize, right-click to lock.
The position is saved account-wide and reapplied every time a new roll appears.

• Chat idle hiding, chat-specific modes, and typing box hiding (#5)

• Chat modes: chat gets its own modes instead of the combat-based
ones: Always, When active (new default) and While typing.
• When active: chat hides once the visible chat window has had no
new message, and you haven't typed, for the idle time (set in the Chat
row; default 10s). The next message brings it back.

with the rest of chat.

boxes' focus, instead of the ChatEdit_* globals, which may not exist
in this client.

macros still load).
• Defaults: unit and boss frames now default to Combat/Target, and
Cooldown Manager to Never.

on a new message

addons.changelog:
Changelog1.0.3
New:
• Windfury procs. The icon flashes above the bar, in the blue of the imbue
so it does not read as the Stormstrike cue. This client announces no cast for
the proc, so the extra attack itself is what gives it away: two blows landing
within a few hundredths of a second of each other. A Searing Totem ticking
next to a swing looks the same from the outside, so size decides, and what
your weapon hits for is learned from the fight rather than written down here.
It starts measuring again whenever you change weapon. No sound by default:
every cue this client offers is a user interface blip.
• Improved Stormstrike. The talent resets the cooldown every time you dodge
or parry, which made a watch that only counts down wrong for half the fight.
Avoiding a blow now counts as a possible reset: while the client still
reports the cooldown it is asked and believed, and while it does not, what it
said earlier is used. Whether you have the talent is read off the talent
tooltip, learned from the fight, or set by hand with /ft cdreset.
• Four more cues to choose from, and /ft wf, /ft wfprobe and /ft cdtest
to see what any of this is doing.
1.0.2
Fixed:
• Totemic Recall and Totemic Projection were showing up as totems. The word
"totem" was being matched inside longer words, so anything "totemic" counted.
• The little arrows above each slot drew on top of the world map. They are gone
entirely, and the bar now fades out while the map is open.

New:
• Shield button. Casts Lightning Shield, or Water or Earth Shield if you
know them, and shows the charges left rather than a clock, because charges
are what run out. It warns you once if you enter a fight without one.
• Cooldown watch. A sound and a quick icon flash above the bar the moment a
watched ability comes back. Stormstrike is watched by default; /ft watch
adds or removes any other. Only speaks up in combat. If the client
stops reporting cooldowns mid-fight, the duration learned earlier keeps the
count going.
• Pick a spell by hovering its icon. The totem slots, the shield and the
imbue all open their list on hover now. The call button does too, and offers
Totemic Recall and Totemic Projection alongside Call of the Elements.

Removed:
• The Purge button. It was a plain cast button with nothing to show, since this
client does not let addons read enemy auras.
1.0.1
Swing timer, rewritten around what this client actually reports:
• It no longer starts when you right click a target from out of range. Auto
attack being on is not evidence of a swing, so the bar now waits for a hit to
land and anchors the cycle there.
• Hits are matched by cadence instead of by where they fall in the window. Your
swings arrive one weapon speed apart; a Searing Totem ticking on the same
target does not, and no longer steals the rhythm. A bad anchor used to lock
the timer into a wrong phase forever, because every real swing landed in the
half that was being rejected.
• Taking a hit no longer reset your swing. The unit filter included
"targettarget", which in a melee fight is you.
• The cycle chains into the next swing instead of freezing at 0.0s, and keeps
running when the client stops reporting your attack speed mid-fight.
• One colour throughout, with "~" marking a predicted cycle.

Weapon imbues:
• Detected from the weapon tooltip. This client reports no temporary enchant
through GetWeaponEnchantInfo and puts nothing in your buffs.
• The enchant is named after the short form plus its rank ("Rockbiter 3"), not
after the spell ("Rockbiter Weapon"), so matching now works out which word is
generic by comparing your known imbues against each other.
• Time left shown in minutes, green while it is up and orange in the last
minute.
1.0.0
First release.
• Totem bar with countdowns, quick recast and per-slot flyouts
• Totem sets, castsequence button, generated macro and sync with the game's
totem bar
• Expiry, destroyed and out-of-range warnings with a selectable sound…
addons.description:
Shaman totem management for World of Warcraft: Forever.

A bar with live totem timers, saved totem sets, one-click recasting, weapon
imbue tracking and a swing timer. Built and tested on the Forever beta
(interface 16001).
Features
Totem bar - one slot per element with the active totem's icon, a countdown
and the seconds remaining. Left click casts or recasts that element, right
click destroys the totem. An arrow on each slot pops up every totem of that
element so you can swap it without opening any window.

Totem sets - save combinations of up to four totems and switch between
them. The set drives the bar, a /castsequence button, an optional real macro
you can drop on your action bar, and the game's own totem bar, so Call of the
Elements places exactly the totems you configured.

Warnings - before a totem expires, when one is destroyed early, and when
you walk out of its range. Choice of alert sound, on the effects channel so it
follows your volume settings.

Weapon imbues - a button that casts your chosen imbue and shows how long
the current one has left, plus a warning if you enter a fight without one.

Swing timer - a bar tracking your melee swing, coloured differently when it
is measured from a landed hit versus predicted from your weapon speed.
Slash commands
/ft open the configuration
/ft lock lock the bar in place
/ft set switch to another set
/ft makemacro create a macro for the active set and put it on your cursor
/ft sync write the active set into the game's totem bar
/ft sound cycle the warning sound
/ft check diagnostics for the bar
/ft selftest in-client checks
Notes on this client
Forever hides some data from addons ("secret values"). Where that happens the
addon says so instead of guessing:
• Totem data is hidden in combat, encounters and PvP. The addon learns each
totem's duration when it can see it, then keeps its own clock and draws the
estimated countdown in blue.
• Enemy auras cannot be read at all in combat, so there is no purge alert.
• The combat log is not available to this addon, so the swing timer falls back
to prediction when no hit event reaches it.
Testing
tests/ holds a stub of the WoW API that loads the addon outside the game,
plus a linter that flags any global function the addon calls that has not been
verified to exist on the target client.
addons.name: ForeverTotems

addons.changelog:
The Lan Krew ToolKit is world PvP, celebration, and learning tools for a group of friends who play WoW: Forever together. This is its first release. It runs on ByteTerrace Core, the framework addon that ships beside it.

| What | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Game | WoW: Forever 1.60.1 (interface 16001) |
| Download | TheLanKrewToolKit-0.1.0.zip, under Assets |
| Folders | ByteTerrace_Core and TheLanKrewToolKit |
| Settings | Type /tlk. |
| Commands | Type /tlk help. |

To install, extract the zip into forever\Interface\AddOns. Both folders must be turned on. The full documentation is in the README.
Krew
The Krew is everyone in your group who runs the toolkit. When you group up, a card shows who's in it, and /tlk krew lists each member's version.

The Krew shares these moments, each as a card or a raid warning:
• Level-ups
• Flawless victories
• First blood and kill sprees
• Riddles solved in the Scholar's challenge
• Everything in Warband

Each one can be switched off. Krew messages are hidden addon messages to your own party or raid. They never whisper or use public channels, and they never send on a timer. Nothing is sent during chat messaging lockdown: battlegrounds, arenas, dungeons, and raids.
Warband
Warband is world PvP for a Krew that takes the war seriously. An account-wide ledger tracks who the Krew fights and who it protects, and every member sees the same ledger.

| Kind | How someone gets there | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grudge | They kill one of the Krew, and you accept the card. Or type /tlk grudge. | The Krew tallies kills each way: Krew 3 : 5 Bob. |
| Mark for death | Type /tlk mark. /tlk unmark lifts it. | The Krew hunts them. |
| Champion | Type /tlk glory. Works on either faction. | The Krew aids them. |
| Guild at war | Type /tlk war. /tlk peace ends it. | Every member is an enemy, with a tally each way. |

Each command takes your target or a name, and /tlk war takes a guild name too. With mouse and keyboard, a player's right-click menu offers the same choices.
• Killed by an enemy player? A card names them and the killing blow: "Slain by Bob. Ambush for 700." Select it to hold the grudge, or right-click it to let it go.
• Nameplate badges mark the ledger: a skull for marks, a cross for grudges, a square for guilds at war, and a star for champions.
• Sightings raise a raid warning when someone in the ledger shows up, and tell the Krew where. In a brawl, the alerts merge into one summary.
• Nearby enemies is a small window that lists the enemy players you and the Krew saw in the last 2 minutes, marked ones first.
• Rivalry records keep every enemy player you meet: class, level, guild, times seen, where, and the score. Type /tlk rival . Tooltips show the score too.
• Vengeance settles the score for everyone when a marked or grudge enemy goes down.
• Rally calls the Krew to you with a raid warning and a map waypoint. Type /tlk rally.
• Enemy gatherings send the Krew a card when five or more enemy players show up in one place. Select it to set a waypoint. It's how you find the other faction's world events.

Type /tlk ledger to list everyone and every war, and /tlk forgive to remove someone. Put /tlk rally and /tlk mark in macros, so a controller can press them too.

Turn on enemy nameplates. Sightings and gatherings see only what your nameplates see.
Sounds
You bind your own sounds to game moments. The addon ships no audio.

1. Put .ogg or .mp3 files in TheLanKrewToolKit\Media\. The file names are in the README's sound tables.
2. Restart the game. The game sees only files that existed at launch, so /reload isn't enough.
3. Type /tlk sound to test one.

Numbered copies, such as FinishHim2.ogg through FinishHim5.ogg, play at random.
• Combat and quests: combat start, with an optional fade when combat ends, and a quest ready to turn in.…
addons.description:
Addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, held to the same correctness and performance bar as Puck.

| Addon | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ByteTerrace_Core | The shared framework (Lua global ByteTerrace): state, commands, input, events, and modules. See the architecture. |
| TheLanKrewToolKit | Utilities for The Lan Krew. |
| ByteTerrace_DevTools | Development only (## X-DevOnly), and never shipped. /btdev dump records the client's globals for tlk api-sync, and /btdev probe records the client's answers to calibration probes for tlk probes. |

addons.description:
A small, no-frills texture pack for LibSharedMedia-3.0. It adds 14 popular statusbar textures, including a clean copy of the Retail castbar fill. Any addon that lets you pick a bar texture from a list can then use them.

There is no settings window, no slash command and no code running during gameplay. Install it and the textures show up in your other addons' texture lists.
What it does for you
Most unit frame, castbar, nameplate and meter addons get their texture lists from LibSharedMedia. Out of the box those lists are often short, and the full SharedMedia pack adds hundreds of fonts, sounds and borders you may never use.

Shared Media Basic adds only the bar textures people actually reach for, in about 0.5 MB:
• More choices in your texture dropdowns. Open the texture setting in EnhanceQoL, Details!, Plater, WeakAuras, Cell, Grid2, Quartz, Bartender or any other LibSharedMedia addon, and the textures below are listed there.
• Your old profiles keep working. Texture names match the original SharedMedia addon, so a profile that uses "Smooth" or "BantoBar" finds its texture again instead of falling back to a flat default.
• The Blizzard castbar look in custom castbars. Use the default UI castbar fill in any castbar addon.
• No performance cost. The addon only registers file paths when you log in. It adds no frames, events or updates.
Included textures
Classic SharedMedia textures (same names as in the original SharedMedia addon):

BantoBar, Smooth, Smooth v2, Flat, Minimalist, Otravi, Glaze, Gloss, Aluminium, Charcoal, Melli, Melli Dark

Blizzard castbar textures:
• Blizzard Castbar: the Retail castbar's gold fill, as it looks in the default UI.
• Blizzard Castbar (Gray): the same pattern in grayscale, so it takes on any bar color you choose.
About the Blizzard Castbar textures
The Retail castbar fill is an atlas texture, which LibSharedMedia can't use directly. These two textures are cut from that atlas. The rounded end caps are removed so the bar lines up cleanly with the borders your castbar addon draws.
• Choose Blizzard Castbar and set the bar color to white for the exact default-UI look.
• Choose Blizzard Castbar (Gray) to keep the Blizzard pattern with your own color, such as class colors or red for non-interruptible casts.
Example
Using EnhanceQoL's castbar:

1. Install Shared Media Basic and restart the game. New texture files are only picked up on a full restart.
2. Open EnhanceQoL's castbar settings.
3. Set the bar texture to Blizzard Castbar (Gray) and choose a color. Your castbar now has Blizzard's texture with your own border and color.

The same steps work for health bars in your unit frame addon, bars in Details!, nameplates in Plater, and so on.
Requirements
• Works with any addon that uses LibSharedMedia-3.0. The library is bundled, so nothing else is needed.
• Supports Retail and Classic.
Scope
This project stays deliberately small: basic, widely used statusbar textures and nothing else. If you need fonts, sounds or a large media library, use the full SharedMedia addon alongside or instead of this one.

Titan Spacer adds up to ten independent spacer plugins to Titan Panel. Use them to organize, separate, or align plugins on any Titan bar.

Titan Panel is required.
Features
• Ten individually configurable spacers (Spacer #01 through Spacer #10).
• Compact, wide, symbol, and symbol-free display styles.

How to use
1. Right-click a Titan Panel bar.
2. Open the Interface category. Its name may vary with your game language.
3. Enable one or more Spacer entries.

Each spacer has these menu options:
• Show Symbol — displays -- or --- in the spacer.
• Larger Spacer — increases its width.
• Display on Right Side — moves the spacer between the left and right sides of its current Titan bar.
• Bar Position — moves the spacer left or right relative to other plugins on the same side.
• Hide — removes that spacer from the bar without changing its settings.

addons.description:
Customize Blizzard's Raid and Raid-Style Party Frames with buff indicators, clearer role icons, threat warnings, and more.

Supports retail (Midnight) and WoW Forever.
Features
• Buff indicators: Track buffs as spell icons or coloured squares. Arrange them in groups that close gaps automatically when buffs disappear. Add duration text, stack counts, cooldown swipes, and steady or pulsing glows.
• Role icons: Keep Blizzard's icons or use tiny symbols. The Tiny tank & healer preset makes tanks and healers easy to spot while leaving damage roles unmarked.
• Threat warnings: Choose a square, circle, or full-frame border with a solid or glowing edge. Set your own colours for high, insecure, and secure threat, enable blinking, or hide threat indicators for tanks.
• Absorb shields: Adjust shield visibility and opacity. Optional overshields show shield coverage beyond full health, with several textures to choose from.
• Name styling: Change font size, position, outlines, and shadows. Use class colours, shorten long names, hide server names, convert Cyrillic to Latin, or hide names for dead and offline units.
• Raid markers and party leaders: Adjust icon size and position. Optionally hide the leader icon during combat.
• Frame options: Show your own party frame while solo and enable Crisp frame borders for more even separators.
• Profiles: Save different setups and switch automatically between party and raid profiles. Buff indicators can also have separate sets for each specialization.
• Live previews: See changes in settings using your character's name and your actual frame dimensions and scale.
Getting started
1. Type /brf or /betterraidframes to open settings.
2. For party frames, enable Use Raid-Style Party Frames under General or in Blizzard Edit Mode.
3. Open a feature's section, enable it, and adjust its settings while watching the preview.

Use Blizzard Edit Mode to change the overall frame layout, frame size, and Blizzard aura sizes. A Follower Dungeon is a handy place to try your setup with a full party.
Positioning and previews
Choose Position, such as Top left, Center, or Bottom right, then fine-tune with X/Y offsets. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves up. Raid Markers, Party Leader, Threat, Role Icons, and Name use this same approach. Existing placements are preserved when upgrading.

Previews update as you edit. They use your current party or raid frame size when available, with Edit Mode or the last known size as fallbacks. Large previews shrink to fit. Sample raid markers, leader icons, roles, shields, and threat levels let you try settings even while solo.
Adding buff indicators
1. Open Indicators, choose Add group, and select a position such as Bottom right.
2. Choose Add indicator inside the group. Enter a buff name or aura ID, or pick one from Buffs, then click Add.
3. Select the group to adjust growth direction, spacing, and position. Select an individual buff to change its appearance and text.

New indicators start as spell icons. In Display, switch to a coloured square, adjust size, add a glow, or filter to buffs you cast. In Text, show remaining duration or stack count.

For example, put Echo and Dream Breath in a Bottom right group. Both follow the group's spacing and growth direction; when one buff disappears, the other closes the gap automatically.

You can reorder, copy, or move indicators between groups. Under a group's Advanced settings, Above Blizzard icons brings the group in front of Blizzard's built-in icons.

Use Default for all specializations or create a separate set for a particular spec. Export and Import share indicator sets, including their group settings.

Show Blizzard buff icons controls Blizzard's standard buff display separately from your custom indicators.

addons.description:

/pct or the minimap button opens the options.

/pct preview toggles on and off the preview mode.

/ipct also works in place of /pct

addons.description:
Guild soft reserve with points, entirely in game.

World of Warcraft Classic · “Forever” client (Interface 16001)

English ·
Français ·
Deutsch ·
Español ·
Português ·
Italiano ·
Русский ·
简体中文 ·
繁體中文 ·
한국어

CorpSR runs your guild's soft reserves (SR) in game: each member reserves the items they want, the loot master hands out the loot, and the addon reads the /rolls, ranks them and keeps the history. Every SR you lose gives you points on that item, so your next roll is stronger.

There is no website, no export, no spreadsheet. The data travels only through the guild addon channel, and every member keeps a full copy: an absent officer never loses anything.
Features
• Weekly SRs: 2 per week (GM setting), on any item from any raid. Double SR allowed.
• Points: you lose an item you reserved → +10 points on it. Your SR roll = roll + points.
• Clear priority: SR > +1 > +1 looted > +2 > Transmog, read from the roll range.
• Raider window: the item, your points, one button per roll type, a timer bar, “Pass”.
• Loot window for the master looter: live rolls, ties, a winner of your choice, leftovers (guild bank, disenchant).
• Raid announcements for the start and the end of each item.
• Handing over: trade attempt, ready whisper, list of what is still owed, a disenchanter for the session.
• !SR by whisper for pickups (PUGs) and anyone without the addon: no need to install it.
• Full history: every change is written down; corrections and cancellations need a reason and can be undone.
• GM settings: values and rights rank by rank, full reset.
• Demo mode to try everything without sending anything to the guild.
• 10 languages: English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Korean.
The rules
| Roll type | Roll | Total |
|---|---|---|
| SR | /roll 110 | roll + your points on the item |
| +1 (main spec) | /roll 100 | roll |
| +1 looted (main spec, already won an item in +1 this week) | /roll 100 | roll |
| +2 (off spec) | /roll 50 | roll |
| Transmog | /roll 20 | roll |
• The highest category wins, whatever the rolls: an SR always beats a +1. Inside a category, the highest total wins. On a tie, the tied players roll again.
• Points: you roll with the points you already have (0 the first time). Once the item has been rolled, everyone who reserved it, was in the raid and didn't get it earns +10 per SR on it (+20 with a double SR). The winner earns nothing and, if they won with an SR, goes back to 0 on that item. Players who click “Pass” earn nothing either.
• Points are kept when you change items: they wait in reserve until you reserve that item again.
• An item won uses up your SR for the week: if several bosses can drop it, you can't SR it again until next week.
• +1 looted: from your first +1 win of the week (or of the session, GM setting). SR, +2 and transmog wins don't count.
• Only your first valid roll counts. If N copies drop, the N best win.
• Pickups (players outside the guild) follow exactly the same rules as guild members: SRs (by whispering !SR), points, every roll type.
• All values (points, number of SRs, double SR, roll ranges) are GM settings.
A raid session
Officers

1. Session tab → New session.
2. The master looter loots the boss: the loot window opens by itself. You can also Alt + left click an item in your bags.
3. Pick the item, then Start: your click announces the item in raid chat, with the ranges and the time.
4. Rolls come in live. When time is up, Validate (or Reroll ties): your click announces the winner.
5. CorpSR tries to open a trade with the winner and puts the item in it. Otherwise a whisper is ready on a button. The To hand over tab remembers who is still owed what.
6. Nobody wants it? Guild bank or disenchant.

Raiders
• My SR tab: click an item to reserve it, click it again for a double SR, right click to remove one. SRs lock when the first item of the week is rolled (or when an officer locks them).…

addons.description:
Une interface complète et modulaire pour WoWForever.

Cadres, barres d'action, chat, sacs, hôtel des ventes, outils de groupe et de raid : tout se règle dans une seule fenêtre, /corp.

Modules · Installation · Commandes · Apparence · Pensé pour WoWForever · Crédits

Présentation
CorpUI remplace l'interface du jeu par un ensemble de modules cohérents, du cadre du joueur jusqu'à l'hôtel des ventes. Chaque module s'active ou se coupe à part, se règle dans la même fenêtre et suit le profil du personnage.
• Une seule fenêtre de réglages : une colonne de pages (Interface, Groupe et raid, Outils), une recherche dans toutes les options, un aperçu en direct des cadres pendant qu'on les règle.
• Une apparence plate et sobre : fonds neutres, liserés fins, accent à la couleur de la classe, avec une disposition d'écran prête à l'emploi.
• Profils par personnage, copie et partage par texte.
• 10 langues : français, anglais, allemand, espagnol, portugais, italien, russe, chinois simplifié et traditionnel, coréen.
• Assistant d'installation au premier lancement.
Ce qu'il contientInterface
| Module | Ce qu'il fait | Commande |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cadres d'unité | Joueur, cible, cible de la cible, focalisation, familier, boss, arène ; barres de sort, auras, ressources, totems actifs du chaman, minuteur de coups blancs, icône de raid réglable. Un seul éditeur pour tous les cadres. | /corp cadres |
| Groupe et raid | Cadres de groupe et de raid à nous : débuffs, dissipation, soins entrants, aggro, icône de raid, réglages pour les soigneurs. | /corp groupe |
| Barres d'action | Neuf barres, barre du familier, barre des totems, bouton de sortie de véhicule ; taille, espacement, fond, visibilité par condition, fondu au survol ou hors combat, raccourcis rapides façon ElvUI. | /corp barres |
| Menus | Barre des postures et formes, micro-menu et barre des sacs, réglables comme les barres d'action. | /corp menus |
| Barres de sort | Barres d'incantation du joueur, de la cible et de la focalisation ; sort non interruptible, interruption prête. | /corp incantations |
| Auras | Buffs et débuffs du joueur et de la cible, filtres par listes. | /corp auras |
| Expérience | Barre d'XP : quêtes, repos, XP par heure, temps avant le niveau. | /corp xp |
| Minicarte | Minicarte carrée avec zone, coordonnées et heure ; icônes rangées dans une boîte. Points de vol sur la carte du monde : bleu pour l'Alliance, rouge pour la Horde, vert pour les deux factions. Icône de la plante, du minerai ou du coffre à la place du point jaune des recherches. Boutons des addons dans un tiroir à chevron, du côté du bord de l'écran. | /corp minicarte |
| Barres d'infos | Jusqu'à dix bandeaux : or, sacs, durabilité, FPS, latence, heure, coordonnées, amis, guilde. | /corp infos |
| Suivi de quêtes | Quêtes suivies et leurs objectifs, couleur de difficulté, progression du groupe dans l'infobulle, menu au clic droit. | /corp quetes |
| Plaques de nom | Plaques des unités : sort en cours, tes débuffs, points de combo, cible actuelle, icône de raid. | /corp plaques |
| Infobulles | Infobulles au style CorpUI, prix de l'hôtel des ventes, objets possédés par tes personnages et ID de l'objet. | /corp infobulles |
| Chat | Fenêtres de discussion au style CorpUI : onglets détachés, colonne d'icônes, champ de saisie encadré, onglets par défaut, historique, copie du texte et des liens. | /corp chat |
| Compteur | Fenêtres façon Details : dégâts, soins, absorptions, interruptions, dissipations, morts, et la menace du groupe sur ta cible avec alerte avant l'aggro. | /corp compteur |
| Sacs | Tous les sacs en un seul, recherche et tri ; banque. Maj + clic pour partager une pile ; double clic pour copier l'ID d'un objet (aussi dans AtlasLoot). | /corp sacs |
| Butin | Fenêtre de butin et jets de groupe (Besoin, Cupidité, Passer). | /corp butin |…

• Double clic sur un objet des sacs, de la banque ou d'AtlasLoot : une petite boîte avec l'ID déjà sélectionné (Ctrl+C) et le nom.

2. Relance complètement le jeu : un /reload ne voit pas les nouveaux addons.

Tes réglages, profils et commandes /corp restent les mêmes.
Nouveautés
• Leveling (/corp leveling, page Outils) : un guide pas à pas pour monter de niveau, dans l'esprit de RestedXP.
• Une route pour toute la zone : prendre toutes les quêtes d'un pôle, enchaîner les objectifs sans allers-retours, rendre, puis prendre les suites des chaînes. Chaque quête garde son ordre prendre → faire → rendre.
• Les quêtes à prendre autour de toi, même celles que la carte du jeu n'affiche pas : CorpUI embarque une base des quêtes de Forever (donneurs, positions, objectifs). Il les filtre selon ton camp, ta race, ta classe, ton niveau et les quêtes déjà faites ou préalables.
• Les étapes au même endroit sur une seule ligne : « Prendre 3 quêtes », « Faire 2 quêtes ici » (chaque quête avec ses objectifs, ceux qui sont finis en vert), « Rendre 2 quêtes ».
• Les étapes numérotées se cochent toutes seules quand elles sont faites. Les deux dernières restent affichées en gris.
• Une flèche CorpUI vers l'étape en cours : verte devant, rouge derrière, avec la distance. En option, le repère de Blizzard (épingle sur la carte et navigation).
• Une route stable, gardée par personnage. Elle est recalculée au changement de zone, avec le bouton « Recalculer la route » ou avec /corp leveling route.
• Clics sur une étape : clic gauche pour y pointer la flèche, clic droit pour ignorer la quête. /corp leveling reset fait revenir les quêtes ignorées.
• La fenêtre reprend le dessin du suivi des quêtes et se déplace avec « Déverrouiller l'interface ».
• Version dépassée : quand un joueur de ta guilde ou de ton groupe a un CorpUI plus récent, un message en orange le signale dans le chat. Il donne la version, le joueur qui l'a et le lien de téléchargement. Le rappel revient à la connexion, une fois par version.
Corrections
• Plaques : les icônes de raid (crâne, croix…) n'apparaissaient plus sur les plaques de CorpUI. Elles sont de retour et se règlent dans /corp plaques, section « Icône de raid » : affichage, position (au-dessus, à gauche, à droite ou sur la barre), taille, opacité et décalages. Tant que les réglages sont ouverts, un crâne d'exemple s'affiche sur les plaques visibles.

Installation
1. Télécharge CorpUI-2.0.0.zip ci-dessous (pas « Source code »).
2. Décompresse-le dans World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\ : tu obtiens le dossier CorpUI (le noyau) et un dossier CorpUI_Xxx par module.
3. Pour une mise à jour, supprime d'abord les anciens dossiers CorpUI et CorpUI_Xxx (tes réglages sont gardés : ils sont dans WTF), décompresse, puis relance le jeu.
⚠️ Mise à jour depuis une version 1.x
CorpUI n'est plus un seul dossier : l'archive contient le noyau CorpUI et un dossier CorpUI_Xxx par module (31 dossiers en tout).

1. Supprime l'ancien dossier CorpUI dans Interface\AddOns (tes réglages ne sont pas dedans : ils sont dans WTF et sont gardés).
2. Décompresse l'archive dans Interface\AddOns.
3. Relance complètement le jeu : un /reload ne voit pas les nouveaux addons.

Rien d'autre à faire : tes réglages, profils et commandes /corp sont les mêmes.
Nouveautés
• Chaque module est un addon. Dans la liste des addons du jeu, CorpUI regroupe ses modules sous son nom, chacun avec son icône et un nom clair : « CorpUI [Barre d'infos] », « CorpUI [Hôtel des ventes] »… La couleur du nom suit sa famille, comme les catégories de /corp : bleu pour l'interface, orange pour le groupe et le raid, vert pour les outils, rose pour les jeux.
• Un module coupé n'est plus chargé du tout (avant, il était chargé sans rien faire) : moins de mémoire et une connexion plus rapide quand tu n'utilises pas tout.
• Page Modules (/corp modules) : couper ou rallumer un module désactive ou réactive son addon, pour tous tes personnages, puis demande un rechargement. Un addon coupé dans la liste du jeu apparaît coupé dans la page. Même chose dans l'assistant d'installation.
• Les modules qui ne vont pas l'un sans l'autre restent ensemble : Cadres d'unité (cadres, groupe, barres de sort, auras), Compteur (compteur, dégâts, menace), Marchand (marchand, réactifs), Barres d'action (barres, micro-menu), Hôtel des ventes (HV, désenchanteur), Mini-jeux (jeux, podomètre), Butin (butin, fil du butin).
Sous le capot
• Le noyau CorpUI garde tout ce que les modules partagent : réglages et profils, options, polices, sons, couleurs de classe, raccourcis rapides, erreurs Lua, échanges entre joueurs CorpUI.
• L'ordre de chargement est le même qu'avant, et chaque module a été vérifié seul avec le noyau, puis avec tous les autres sauf lui.

Installation
1. Télécharge CorpUI-1.7.2.zip ci-dessous (pas « Source code »).
2. Décompresse-le dans World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\ : tu obtiens un dossier CorpUI.
3. Pour une mise à jour, remplace l'ancien dossier CorpUI (tes réglages sont gardés : ils sont dans WTF), puis relance le jeu.
Nouveautés
• Points de vol sur la carte du monde : tous les maîtres de vol de la carte affichée, en bleu pour l'Alliance, en rouge pour la Horde et en vert pour les deux factions (la carte du jeu ne montre que ceux de ta faction).
• Même taille à l'écran quel que soit le zoom ; les clics passent à la carte.
• Au survol : nom et faction. Ceux de ta faction pas encore découverts sont estompés.
• Réglages dans le panneau de la minicarte (page Carte & infos) : afficher les points de vol, et aussi ceux de l'autre faction.
• Une carte qui reste vide alors qu'elle a des points de vol : ouvre-la puis tape /corp minicarte vols pour le diagnostic.
• Trousseau de clés dans les sacs : il a son bloc sous le sac de composants (les sacs de CorpUI remplaçant ceux du jeu, il n'était plus accessible).
• Un bouton clé, à côté de celui des emplacements de sacs, l'affiche ou le cache.
• Dans les options des sacs : toutes les cases, ou seulement les clés.
• Les places libres ne comptent pas le trousseau.
Performances
CorpUI fait beaucoup moins de travail inutile, surtout en combat, en groupe et avec plusieurs fenêtres habillées :
• Un seul pilote fait tourner les tâches régulières des modules (avant : des dizaines de pilotes appelés à chaque image, même fenêtres fermées ou module coupé). /corp perf affiche la mémoire de CorpUI et le temps passé par chaque tâche (/corp perf reset remet les compteurs à zéro).
• Cadres de groupe et de raid : chaque événement va directement au bon cadre (avant : les 44 cadres parcourus), seule la partie qui change est relue (vie, puissance, état), les changements de groupe en rafale sont regroupés.
• Barres d'action : recharge, utilisable et état relus séparément, une seule passe par image, barres cachées sautées puis rattrapées à l'affichage.
• Plaques, auras, menace, buffs, ressources, compteur : nettement moins de relectures.
• Infobulles et barre d'infos : plus de calculs à chaque image ; or, sacs et durabilité relus sur leurs événements.
• Langues : seules la langue choisie et l'anglais restent en mémoire après la connexion (environ 1 Mo de moins).
• Sauvegarde plus légère : les descriptions des sorts d'entraîneur déjà connus du jeu ne sont plus gardées (environ 200 Ko de moins), et l'historique des prix de l'HV ne garde que les jours utilisés (14, ou la durée de ta moyenne si elle est plus longue).
Corrections
• Sorts à venir : chez un entraîneur, la liste se relisait en boucle tant que la fenêtre restait ouverte, et un filtre décoché de la fenêtre de l'entraîneur pouvait se retrouver coché.
• Comptabilité de l'HV : une vente pouvait être comptée deux fois (d'abord sans le nom de l'acheteur, puis avec), ce qui gonflait les ventes et le bénéfice. Les doublons déjà enregistrés sont fusionnés à la connexion ; les opérations de plus de 90 jours sont retirées.
• Erreurs Lua : une même erreur répétée en boucle est seulement comptée, sans ralentir le jeu.

Wetlands, City of Dalaran): the game has no map art for them, so the addon shows the maps of

Underbelly as a second map level. Their rooms light up and their bosses tick themselves off.

addons.description:
Chinese to English chat translation for WoW: Forever and retail World of Warcraft, in two parts:
• addon/Translate: the in-game addon. One folder loads in both clients (## Interface: 16001, 120105).
• companion: a small Rust app that runs next to the game, translates through any OpenAI-compatible API, and draws the English over your chat box.

WoW addons cannot reach the internet, and WoW only writes its chat log at logout, so the addon hands new lines to the companion through the screen and the clipboard. Nothing presses keys for you.
How it works
1. Automatic: when a Chinese line arrives, the addon draws it as a small strip of colored blocks in the top-left corner of the screen (256 x 32 pixels). The companion finds the strip on screen, decodes it, translates the line and shows the English in a see-through, click-through overlay that you place over your chat frame.
2. Click to translate, inside the game: Chinese lines get a blue [T] link. Clicking it opens a small window with the line already highlighted. Press Ctrl+C, wait for the overlay to say the line is ready, then click the lower box and press Ctrl+V. The English is printed in chat under an [EN] tag.
3. Replying: type English in the companion's reply box and press Enter. The Chinese is put on your clipboard, ready to paste into WoW chat.

Reading the strip is screen capture: it only reads pixels and never sends input to the game, but Blizzard's terms do not clearly allow or forbid it. Turn the strip off with /tr strip to rely on the click-to-translate route alone.

Changes in 2.4.0
• Added support for World of Warcraft: Forever
• Updated for Midnight (Retail 12.1.0)

• Updated for The Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary (2.5.6)
• Updated for Classic Era (1.15.9)
• Updated for Wrath of the Lich King Titan Reforged
• Fixed no sound playing for any loot on Retail since 11.1.5, which changed how item links mark their quality (also needed for WoW Forever)
• Fixed heirlooms not being detected on Retail; artifacts now play the legendary (orange) sound
• Fixed a Lua error on Midnight when looting during boss encounters, Mythic+ and PvP, where loot messages are hidden from addons; items you take from the loot window still play their sound there (items that go straight to your bags stay silent while messages are hidden)
• Bonus-roll loot plays its sound again
• Turning off "Received" now silences received items on French, Spanish and Portuguese clients even with "Crafted" on (they were being mistaken for crafted items)
• Added an adjustable volume setting (0-100%) with a slider in the config panel; it temporarily scales the chosen audio channel while a sound plays, then restores it without overriding any volume change you make in the meantime
• Loot detection now uses Blizzard's own localized strings, so it works in every language (including Korean and Russian grammar forms) instead of only English clients, and other players' loot no longer triggers your sounds on Korean clients
• The config panel's dropdowns are only built while the panel is open, avoiding interference with Blizzard's own dropdowns
• /zl opens the ZeldaLoot settings page again instead of the game's Controls page
• /zl reset now refreshes the config panel immediately if it is open
• Fixed /zl dump throwing a Lua error
• Sound selection is now clamped to what the chosen sound set actually contains (e.g. OOT has 4 sounds)
• Scripts no longer load twice on login
• Removed dead code and duplicated logic; fixed TOC metadata (website link, BugGrabber name)

We support every live client: Retail (Midnight), World of Warcraft: Forever, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Cataclysm Classic, Wrath of the Lich King Classic and Titan Reforged, The Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary, and Classic Era (including Hardcore and Season of Discovery).
Sounds
4 new sounds for different item qualities, from uncommon (green) to legendary (orange). Note inherited objects (linked to account) can play sound when received too (same as for legendaries items). Sounds provided by: Darth Killer, from Zelda Ocarina of Time (original from games), and Chrisgess, from Zelda Ocarina of Time Orchestrated album www.zreomusic.com, even higher sound quality!

The audio plays on the SFX audio channel.
Interface
Configure which sounds you want and when: loot from enemies, received (letterbox, seller, etc), crafted (professions and some special items like Eternal Water). Settings will be saved between sessions for all your characters. Type /zeldaloot or /zl for the settings menu.

English, French, German, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese are supported. • Edit your language's file in the Locale folder (e.g. ZL_deDE.lua) and open a pull request, or
• Open an issue with the corrected text, or leave a comment on CurseForge.

If you play in a language that isn't listed, or sounds aren't playing for you in your language, please let me know.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that shows the live values of the transmog "situation" triggers
(location, movement, specialization, equipment set, racial form, weather, time of day).
Blizzard's Situations tab lets you configure these triggers but never displays what they
currently evaluate to; TransmogSituations does.

Targets WoW Forever and stays compatible with live Retail.
Features
• Live trigger values rendered inline on the transmog Situations tab, under each category title.
• A movable standalone panel with the same values, for use outside the transmog window.
• Chat commands to inspect values, options and raw ids.
• Experimental: a client-side reconstruction of which outfits are eligible right now, with a
command that checks the outfit Blizzard actually applied is one of them (Blizzard picks among
eligible outfits at random).
Slash commands
/ts and /transmogsituations are equivalent.

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| /ts | Current value of every situation trigger |
| /ts panel | Toggle the standalone panel |
| /ts eligible | Outfits matching the current situation (experimental) |
| /ts verify | Check that the outfit Blizzard applied is one of the eligible ones |
| /ts scan | Record every outfit's situations; transmog window must be open |
| /ts list | Trigger options for the viewed outfit, with the live value marked |
| /ts dump | Raw option ids and player state, for diagnosing mismatches |
| /ts debug | Toggle extra output |
| /ts help | Command list |
How eligibility works
The game has no way to ask which situations an outfit is bound to, so TransmogSituations records
each outfit's assignments whenever you view it on the Situations tab. Until an outfit has been
viewed, /ts eligible lists it as "never viewed" rather than guessing. /ts scan records every
outfit in one go: open the transmog window first, and apply or undo any pending changes (the scan
refuses to run over them, because switching outfits would discard them).
Known limitations
• Weather on Retail shows n/a: Retail has no API to read the current weather. An outfit bound
to a specific weather can still be applied by Blizzard there, but TransmogSituations cannot match it.
• Time of Day band boundaries are an estimate and are marked * in /ts.
• Equipment sets have no "currently equipped set" API. When you swap an item out of the set you
last applied, the value is shown with ~ as an approximation.
• Eligibility is a reconstruction of Blizzard's rules. /ts verify says whether it agrees with the
outfit Blizzard applied; a disagreement is worth reporting with a /ts dump.

addons.changelog:
[1.3.1] - 2026-10-30Added
• XP/hour measured over: a new option (Text tab, Advanced) picks what XP/hour and the time to next level are worked out over: the last 15 minutes, the last hour (the default) or the whole session.
• Ask the game for played time at login: a new option (Text tab, Advanced), off by default. When on, the addon asks once after login while your level time isn't exact yet, and keeps the reply out of chat.
• Kills to level: the bar tooltip, the Stats window and the LibDataBroker tooltip show how many kills you still need to level, from the average XP of your last 20 kills (only this level's once you have 3, before that those of the last two levels), with rested XP counted. Quest, gathering and exploration XP are left out. A new option (Text tab, Advanced), off by default, adds it to the rate text under the bar; the Leveller preset turns it on. It works in every game language.
• Gradient fill: a new option (Visual tab) for the Flat, Vertical and Classic bars paints the XP fill and the rested and quest overlays as one gradient across the bar, from a darker to a lighter shade of their colors.
Changed
• XP/hour now follows how fast you are levelling right now. It used to average your whole time on the level, so it was slow to notice a change of pace and kept an AFK break for the rest of the level.
• XP/hour starts low and rises over the first minutes of a session instead of starting high, so the time to next level is never too short.
• Handing in quests right after a level-up no longer makes XP/hour jump to a huge number.
• The addon counts your time on the level itself, from your level-up, and keeps it across reloads and logouts. It no longer asks the game for your played time at every login.
• /xpbe resetstats keeps your level and played time, which come from the game, and also clears the kills behind Kills to level.
• When the addon hasn't seen your level-up (after installing it, or after levelling with it off), the level time shows with a "+" ("1h 12m+", "at least" in the Stats window). Level up or type /played once and it becomes exact.
Fixed
• Changing a setting in the options no longer folds the Advanced section away, so you can change several settings in a row.
• The secondary bar no longer catches clicks while it has nothing to show (no watched faction, for example): it used to sit invisible over the strip above the main bar.
• The bar no longer flickers for one frame while it holds at 100% during the level-up animation.
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that replaces and enhances the default experience bar with richer visuals, quest XP overlays, session statistics, and full color customization.

Retail and Classic branches · Vanilla 1.15 · Forever 1.60 · Burning Crusade 2.xx · Wrath 3.xx · Cataclysm 4.xx · Mists 5.xx · Retail 12.xx · Version 1.3.1

XP Bar Enhanced uses one manifest. The client interface build is resolved to a
product flavor, and that flavor activates the supported feature set.
Features
• Multiple Bar Styles — None (Blizzard default), Classic, Flat, Vertical, Circular, Minimap Ring, Terminal, and Orb
• Quest XP Overlay — See pending and completed quest XP directly on the bar
• Session Tracking — Track XP gained, time played, levels gained, and XP/hour rate
• Session Breakdown & Rate Window — Session stats include quest XP vs other XP totals; XP/hour and the time to level are measured over the last 15 minutes, the last hour (default) or the whole session
• Kills to Level — How many kills you still need to level, from the average XP of your last kills with rested XP counted, in the tooltip, the Stats window, the LibDataBroker tooltip and optionally under the bar; works in every game language
• Level Time Without /played — Time on the current level is counted by the addon from your level-up and kept across reloads and logouts; until it is exact it shows as "1h 12m+". The server is only asked for played time if you turn that on, and its reply stays out of chat
• Statistics Window & Session Charts — Detailed breakdown of your leveling progress, with an XP/hour histogram and a quest-vs-other split chart
• Profile System — Create, rename, delete, and switch between named settings profiles; Blizzard-style dropdown with inline actions and a global shared profile option
• Bar Size Presets — Scale the Flat and Vertical bars to Small, Default, Large, or Huge without distorting text or overlays
• Reputation, Companion, Housing, Honor, and Profession Tracking — The secondary bar can track watched faction progress (including Delve companion flavor), Housing Favor, Honor (PvP) levels, or a profession's skill
• Secondary Source Selector — Choose Reputation, Housing Favor, Honor, or Profession as the secondary bar source (with a first/second/auto profession selector)
• Main Bar at Max Level — Optionally repurpose the main bar to display the selected secondary source once you reach max level
• Style-Aware Secondary Bars — Secondary progress display adapts to the active style (Classic label ticker, Vertical side bar, Circular inner arc, Minimap arc toggle, Terminal single-line phosphor bar, companion Orb)
• Color Customization — Full control over bar and overlay colors, with an optional gradient fill on the Flat, Vertical and Classic bars
• Minimap Button — Quick access to options and stats
• Animations & Celebration — Smooth fill, flash-on-gain, two-phase level-up animations, and an optional golden-glow level-up celebration
• Level Progress Notifications — Announces 25%/50%/75% level progress with the estimated time to ding
• LibDataBroker Feed — XP/h and time-to-level datatext for Titan Panel, Bazooka, or ElvUI
Bar Styles
| Style | Description |
| --- | --- |
| None | Blizzard's default XP bar only |
| Classic | Blizzard-style bar with atlas textures and quest overlays |
| Flat | Wide draggable bar with milestone ticks |
| Vertical | Vertical bar with animated XP fill |
| Circular | Progress ring with configurable size, segments, and scalable center text |
| Minimap Ring | XP ring anchored around the minimap with optional button collection |
| Terminal | ASCII-style retro bar with phosphor-green progress display |
| Orb | Diablo-style filling sphere with glass highlight and metallic rim, plus a companion orb for the secondary source |

• The addon no longer prints "Loaded!" in chat at every login, or the two "Time played" lines when it checks your played time.

Game versions
• Logging in on the Forever beta no longer disconnects you.
• Characters on the Forever beta now keep their profile and statistics between sessions.
• On Retail, the bars no longer fail to load while you are watching a paragon faction.
• On Classic, quest XP now includes quests on your current map and quests under a collapsed header.
• If your game version doesn't offer the chosen secondary bar source, every profile now switches to one it does, not only Global Settings.
• If one part of the addon fails to start, the bars still appear.

Blizzard's bars and bar positions
• Blizzard's own XP or reputation bar no longer reappears next to the addon's after Edit Mode, at max level, or on Retail while you track a house.
• Turning off "Classic bar draggable" now sticks after a reload, and the fixed Classic bar sits where Blizzard's bar does.
• Reset Bar Position no longer moves the Minimap Ring or a fixed Classic bar to the middle of the screen.
• Each profile keeps its own secondary bar position: resetting it on one profile no longer moves it for your other characters.

XP per hour and timers
• XP per hour now shows the same number on the bar, in its tooltip and in the Stats window, and the bar text no longer flickers between two values.
• After a level-up, XP per hour no longer drops by about half, and the time-on-level readout keeps running instead of disappearing until your next loading screen.
• XP per hour waits about a minute before showing, so a quest turned in right after login no longer reads as millions per hour.
• The Stats window's time on level and time to level now count up while you play.
• The rested percentage in the quest summary can now go up to 150% instead of stopping at 100%.

• Session reputation no longer jumps by a huge amount when faction data briefly fails to load, and a renown level-up no longer counts an extra level.
• Reputation past the renown cap is now tracked as paragon, and paragon gains are counted correctly when you earn a reward.
• The Classic and Terminal reputation bars now use standing colors (Friendly, Honored, and so on) for regular factions, and the housing bar no longer takes them from your house level.
• Housing favor earned on another character, or while you were offline, no longer counts toward this session.…
