addons.description:
A field journal for the creatures of Azeroth. Hostile NPC deaths reported in a catalogued zone are recorded in the journal. The addon reads names, levels, ranks and placements from the player’s Forever QuestieDB; the catalogue follows that database as it updates. Rare creatures keep separate personal records, and each observed death has a 1-in-500 shiny roll.

Field Guide Forever is cosmetic only. It never grants player power, changes combat or calls a protected function.
Features
• A live catalogue of creatures across outdoor zones, dungeons and raids, including NPC levels, families and ranks from QuestieDB.
• Uncapped recorded-death totals, with a separate ten-step mastery track: Discovered, Observed, Studied and Mastered.
• Character-local first sightings and first observed deaths, plus first rare and shiny records.
• By default, shared cumulative records and earliest firsts are exchanged with guild and group addon users; disable this
in the options to stop sending/receiving. Local tracking continues when sharing is off.
• /fgf leaderboard ranks observed kills and always includes your character. Peer totals are player-reported.
Kill totals include every species; detailed shared creature records cover the most recent observations.
• An Instances page for bosses reported by encounter events, with local first clears, attempts, kill totals and
difficulty records. Entries appear after the client reports an encounter; this is not a verified world-first board.
• Common, rare and shiny variants. A rare species needs three sightings to confirm its rare variant; a shiny is a
1-in-500 roll on every kill.
• A session sighting log, so the day's walk stays with the journal until the client closes.
• Search, status filters and CREATURES, RARES, SHINY and INSTANCES tabs.
• Tracking for the species you are currently working on.

addons.description:
The shared floor under the WoW: Forever addon suite: one objective-tracker column, the grip and Lock switch that move
it, the section order that stacks it, and the Questie bridge that keeps it clear of Questie's own quest list.

Interface: 16001 (WoW: Forever, live client folder forever, beta _classic_beta_)
What it is for
Adventure Guide, Legacy, Shortest Path and SkillUp each draw sections into the same floating column beside the quest
tracker. Before this addon, each one carried its own copy of that column, so a layout fix or a Lock toggle meant four
identical pull requests and four copies that could drift apart between releases.

Forever Core also owns shared error capture (Core/SafeCall.lua), the report and issue window, and the Forever-family
link box. All five addons vendor those files so error reporting, command handling, selection behavior and link copying
stay consistent.

Forever Core is the one copy. The four addons vendor these files byte for byte (docs/adoption.md), and the first
Forever addon to load publishes the column as ForeverTrackerHost; every later one adopts it. A player with three of
them installed still gets one column, and a player with one installed gets the same column with no extra dependency.

Installing Forever Core itself is optional. It is there so the shared code has a home, so a fix can be developed,
tested and released on its own, and so a future addon can adopt the column without copying it.

The repo also owns a reusable offline UI mock renderer in tools/wowmock/. It centralizes
client asset extraction, BLP decoding, font and atlas lookup, native widgets and frame compositing. Addon scene
scripts remain specific to the feature each repo owns.
What it does not do
It draws no sections of its own and knows nothing about quests, routes, professions, challenges or creatures. Sections
belong to the addon that owns the feature: see the suite's ownership boundaries in docs/handoff/boundaries.md.

addons.description:
Classic profession-levelling numbers inside WoW: Forever's Professions window.

SkillUp Forever shows skill-up chances, recipe costs and colour thresholds in the Professions window. Its side panel has levelling routes, shopping lists and crafted gear.

From 48 to 60 the rows re-sort by cost per skill-up, and Handstitched Leather Bracers turns green at 55.

Each row shows its chance and cost; the tooltip beside the window prices each reagent. This character skins, so Light Leather is free.

The recipe tooltip draws the thresholds on the game's own bar with your skill marked, then each reagent's price and the cost per skill-up.
Features
• Recipe rows and tooltips show skill-up chance, cost and colour thresholds.
• Sorting orders recipes by difficulty range start, chance or cheapest skill-ups. Default restores the game's categories and filters.
• Levelling routes list crafts, trainer visits, skill books and rank quests to your target skill, including fees, tools and stations. Steps allow for unlucky skill-ups. Cheaper crafted reagents become their own steps; a route that stops short names recipes that could extend it. Right-click a recipe to pin it for skill-ups or choose Not this recipe to plan without it. Route details.
• Shopping lists count reagents against your bags and bank. Buy reagents chooses whether materials your professions gather are free or bought. Track the list beside quests, buy vendor stock and keep an Auctionator list up to date. At the auction house, search a recipe's reagents for as many crafts as you choose. Shopping details.
• Trainer annotations show chance and cost, with a green arrow on the recipe that best extends or cheapens your route.
• Reagent tooltips show what tracked routes need. Hold Shift for every recipe that uses the item and still skills up.
• Gathering nodes show the Herbalism or Mining skill they need, coloured at yours, on English clients.
• Crafted gear shows the newest item you could craft for each slot, with its recipe, reagents and learning location. Enable its tab in settings. Gear details.

The route tab from 48 to 73: belts to 56, then train the pants, cure the hides they need and craft the rest of the way, with where each reagent comes from.

The shopping list groups what is missing by source, shows bag and alt holdings alongside current prices, and can start a vendor trip.

The gear tab, turned on in settings: each slot shows the newest thing this character could craft for it.

Tracked, the same route sits beside your quests: the next trainer visit and what's still missing.

At the trainer, every recipe shows its chance and cost; a green arrow marks the one that best extends or cheapens your route.

Hover a reagent to see how much your tracked routes need.

/su leaderboard (or /su stats) ranks distinct recipes SkillUp has observed as learned on your character against totals reported by guild and group members. Repeated scans and relearning the same recipe do not increase the total. Recipes in linked or guild profession views do not count.

Sharing defaults on. Turn it off with /su share off or the checkbox in Settings > AddOns > SkillUp Forever. This stops sending and receiving totals and hides other players while keeping your local observations. /su share on resumes sharing. Reported totals are not verified.

addons.description:
ActionBarSaver:Reloaded is an addon for saving and restoring action bar profiles. It is based on the original ActionBarSaver addon but is a full re-write.

All sets are saved by class rather than by character. Additionally, when you list profiles, you will only see profiles that pertain to your class.

Features such as rename have been deleted for simplicity. To perform a rename, simply save the set with a new name and delete the old set. Additionally, restoring a set will no longer try to re-create macros that do not exist. It will simply notify you of the missing macro and restore nothing for that slot. ABS:R will not work properly if you have multiple macros with the same name, and will warn you of potential issues if you restore a set that has a macro with a shared name.

A new feature has been added for setting up aliases for spells. A common use case for this would be restoring a single set for two characters that share a class but have a different race. For example, you could create a set on a troll shaman that contains Berserking and then add an alias for War Stomp using /abs alias 20554 20549. If you do this, when you restore a set it will first try to restore the proper spell but will also try each alias that you set up. A spell can have as many aliases as you want.
Usage
/abs save - Saves your current action bar setup under the given \
/abs restore - Restores the saved \
/abs delete - Deletes the saved \
/abs list - Lists all saved sets\
/abs alias - Adds an alias with to \
/abs unalias - Removes all aliases associated with \
/abs aliases - List all spell aliases

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that extends the default chat.
Features
• Clickable web links: web addresses in chat (https://..., www....) become links. A click
opens a small dialog to copy the address.
• Copy chat: a button in the button bar of every chat window opens its whole content as plain
text to copy.
• Longer chat history: the number of lines each chat window keeps is configurable (default 128).
• Input history: the arrow keys go through the lines entered before without Alt, and the last
32 lines are kept across logouts and reloads.
• Link tooltips: item, spell, quest, achievement and similar links in chat show their tooltip
on mouseover.
• Mouse wheel: with Shift to the first or last line, with Ctrl a page at a time; optionally back
to the newest line some time after scrolling.
• Short channel names: optional, e.g. "[1. General - Elwynn Forest]" becomes "[1. G]". Blizzard's
channels have default short names, every channel can get an own one.
• Options: all settings on an own page in the game options, the short channel names also in the
chat settings of every chat window.

The full description for CurseForge and Wago is in docs/addon-description.md,
for WoWInterface (BBCode) in docs/addon-description-wowinterface.txt.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that extends the default mailbox.
Features
• Inbox search: filters mail by sender, subject or attached item as you type, and suggests own
characters.
• Filter presets: own characters, friends, recent allies, guild, unread, read, auction house,
gold and C.O.D. They work together with the search box.
• Open Filtered: while a search or filter is active, "Open All" only opens the matching mail
(still skipping C.O.D. and GM mail).
• Recipient dropdown: next to the "To" field of "Send Mail", lists own characters that can
receive mail from the current one, friends, guild members and recent allies.
• Mail log: a "Log" tab with collected, sent, returned and deleted mail, including gold and
items, with the same search and filters as the inbox. Stored per character.
• Chat summary: after "Open All" / "Open Filtered", what was collected.
• Options: automatic messages, the days the log keeps and removing known characters, on an
own page in the game options (Esc > Options > AddOns > GryphonMail).

The full description for CurseForge and Wago is in docs/addon-description.md,
for WoWInterface (BBCode) in docs/addon-description-wowinterface.txt.

addons.description:
Three friends made this World of Warcraft addon to get the most out of their Bláto LAN party in WoW Forever.
If you are three friends playing your own LAN party together, feel free to use it.
What it does
The Bláto Journal window (minimap button or /blato) looks like WoW Forever's own windows (the options also offer a parchment page and a classic look) and has these tabs:

| Tab | What is on it |
|---|---|
| Commands | Every party feature as a button: tonight's statistics (including who was AFK and for how long), quest sharing, arrows to trainers and vendors, a meeting point, alert cards, the Group Check before a dungeon, threat, auction house and crafting helpers, bets, the "One more quest?" vote and the options. Switches have a check box; hovering a button shows what it does and its command. |
| Dungeons | The addon Dungeon Journal by Exehn (CurseForge): bosses, loot, quests and maps, shown right inside the journal window. It is installed on its own, see below. |
| Journey | What the three of you have done together: time, shared quests, dungeons (runs, clears, bosses) and the firsts you shared. Below that, your own character's path, level by level. |
| Places | The zones and dungeons you have visited. |
| Quests | The quests you handed in, and for each one who of the three of you has done it (✓), has not (✗) or is not known yet (?). On top: quests your friends have done and you have not. |
| Notes | Notes with reminders ("I owe my buddy 12 gold"), and a notepad shared with your party: tick "Share with the party" and your friends read the note too. |

Most party features come alive when all three of you run the addon. Your party mates are the two players you have spent the most time grouped with.

addons.description:
Your guild already knows how to make it. Recipe Registry tells you who.

Stop asking "can anyone craft this?" in guild chat and waiting. Recipe Registry
builds a searchable directory of every recipe your guildmates know, keeps it up
to date by itself, and tells you who to whisper — who is online right now, and
who can help when they log back in.

Available for WoW: The Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary and **WoW:
Forever**.
At a glance
• Find a crafter in seconds — search a recipe, or a material you are
holding, and see who in the guild can make it, online ones first.
• Zero upkeep — open your professions once; the directory fills and syncs
itself between everyone running the addon.
• Your whole book in one table — every recipe your professions can learn,
what you already know, and where to go for the rest.
• Tooltips that answer the question — hover almost any craftable item and
see who can make it.
• Know the margin — material cost, sale price and profit, with
TradeSkillMaster or Auctionator.

Search it like you think about it
Type the name of what you want. Or type a material you are sitting on and see
what it turns into. Filter to one profession, sort by rarity — or, on Forever,
by the skill level a recipe is learned at — star the crafts you ask about most
and keep them on top. Categories and subcategories drill
down through big professions without scrolling through hundreds of rows.
Know who to ask, and when
Every recipe lists the guildmates who know it, online ones first. One button
whispers them. Another links the recipe to guild, party, raid or say — and hover
almost any craftable item in the game and the tooltip quietly tells you who can
make it, without opening anything.
See the whole book, not just what you know
The Collection tab is your own professions laid out end to end: every recipe
they can learn, the ones you already know ticked off, and the rest showing the
skill they ask against the skill you have. Each profession is headed with how
far along you are — "Blacksmithing (185/385)" — so you can see the holes at a
glance, and narrow the list to what you could go and learn today.

For the ones you are missing it tells you where to go: the trainer, the vendor,
the drop or the quest, the zone, and on Forever the map coordinates too.
Know what a craft is worth before you make it
With TradeSkillMaster or Auctionator installed, the details panel adds what the
materials cost, what the result sells for, and what is left over. Vendor prices
are learned from merchants you visit, so vials, thread and spices are priced at
what you actually pay instead of whatever the auction house is asking. One
switch hides everything that comes out at a loss.
It keeps itself current
Open a profession once and it is recorded. From then on the addon shares with
guildmates running it and takes their data in return, quietly, pacing itself so
the game stays smooth and holding off during combat and instances. Learn a new
recipe and it is in the directory within seconds — on Forever, without even
opening the profession window.

A Guild members tab shows who else is running the addon and on which version, so
you can tell someone out of date from someone who simply has not installed it.

Getting started
1. Install it, and open each of your profession windows once.
2. Open the window from the minimap button or with /rr.
3. Ask a couple of guildmates to install it too — that is when it gets good.

The first sync takes a moment in a large guild. After that you can forget it is
there.
Commands
Most people only ever need /rr. The rest is there when you want it:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /rr | Opens the main window |
| /rr options | Settings |
| /rr rescan | Queues a fresh profession scan |
| /rr share guild | Shares the selected recipe (also party, raid, say, reply) |
| /rr prices | Checks market data for an item |
| /rr adoption | Prints who in the guild is running the addon |

• Your professions are read and shared on their own. Open a profession once
and it is recorded. You never have to press a button to publish anything.
• A recipe you learn appears by itself. Learn a pattern in a dungeon and it
is in the directory within seconds, wherever you are -- there is no need to go
back to town and open the profession window for it to count.
• All twelve professions, gathering ones included. Alchemy, Blacksmithing,
Cooking, Enchanting, Engineering, First Aid, Fishing, Herbalism,
Leatherworking, Mining, Skinning and Tailoring. Fishing, Herbalism and
Skinning have recipes of their own on this game, so they get a tab like
everything else instead of being treated as professions with nothing in them.
• A recipe database for this game's content. 2519 recipes with their
materials, what they produce, the skill level they are learned at and the
point where they stop giving skill-ups. It is built from the game itself, so
recipes added by a patch are in it rather than missing until someone updates
the addon.
• A Collection tab: your own professions' book. Every recipe your
professions can learn, with the ones you already know ticked off and the rest
showing the skill they ask for against the skill you have. Each profession is
a section you can fold away, headed with how far along you are.
• Where to learn it. The Collection tells you who teaches or sells each
recipe, or where it drops -- with the zone, the map coordinates in a column of
their own, and an Alliance or Horde mark on vendors only one side can reach.
The Merchant's Favor quartermasters of both factions are in it.
• Sort and filter the Collection by any column. Left-click a header to sort
by it, right-click to narrow the table: what you can learn today, what is
still out of reach, only vendor recipes, only the ones needing a
specialization.
• Three ways to order the recipe list. Alphabetical, by rarity, or by the
skill level a recipe is learned at, lowest first.
• Recipe details in one panel. What it makes, what it takes, and every
guildmate who can craft it, so you know who to whisper.
• Crafters on item tooltips. Hovering an item you cannot make says who in
the guild can, in the tooltip, without opening the addon.
• What a craft is worth. With TradeSkillMaster or Auctionator installed, the
details panel adds what the materials cost, what the result sells for and what
is left over, and a switch keeps only the crafts that come out ahead.
• Favourites. Star the recipes you keep coming back to; they gather at the
top of the profession list, above Alchemy.
• A Guild members tab. Who else is running the addon, and which version, so
you can tell an out-of-date guildmate from one who simply has not installed it.
• Stays out of the way when it matters. The addon stops talking to other
players while you are in an instance and picks up again when you leave.
• A minimap button and /rr, either of which opens the window.
Known limitations
• Where-to-learn data is partial. Forever does not ship it in the game
files, so it is being collected by hand, a vendor and a trainer at a time. Some
recipes have no source yet, some have no coordinates, and a few entries may be
wrong. The Collection says so at the top.
• Some recipes have no skill level. Where neither the recipe item nor the
original game says what level a recipe is learned at, the column shows a dash
instead of guessing.

addons.description:
Buffs and consumables, without the scavenger hunt.

Sometimes the real raid mechanic is getting the Mage to press Arcane Intellect.

Questions, bugs or ideas? Come say hi on the Consecrated Hammer Discord. Bug reports go in #bug-reports, or you can open a GitHub issue.

Buffsmith shows the self-buffs, party buffs and consumables you're missing as a small bar of clickable icons. If something needs attention, it appears. Once it's sorted, it gets out of the way.
What it does
• Missing self-buffs, picked up from your spellbook. Buffs shorter than a minute are listed but start switched off, so things like seals don't nag you.
• Rogue poisons on Retail, with separate lethal and non-lethal reminders.
Each spec remembers the last poison you successfully applied in each group,
including casts from your action bars. Only learned poisons are offered.
Any active poison in a group satisfies that reminder until it nears expiry.
On WoW Forever, poison items appear under Weapon enhancements and coat a
bare main-hand weapon first, then a bare off-hand weapon. Buffsmith remembers
flyout choices for each hand and leaves existing coatings in place. These
item actions pause in combat.
• Consumables from your bags, like food, flasks, elixirs, scrolls and weapon enhancements. Drinks and other items that give a timed buff, such as the Keg of Thunderbrew, go under Other buffs. Hover a consumable to see your other choices, and whichever you use becomes the new default.
• Party buffs. Buffs you can give to your target, party or pet show up too, and grey out when the game can tell the player is out of range.
• Party coverage reminders. When someone's missing a buff another class in the party could give, an icon says so. Clicking it reports it in chat; it never casts anything.
• Tracking. Find Herbs, Find Minerals and other tracking spells can sit on the bar until you turn them on. Gathering tracking starts ticked, class and racial tracking start off.
• One key for the lot. Bind Buff trigger in the game's key bindings and press it to work down the bar one missing buff at a time.
• Optional thank-you. Buffsmith can whisper, say, post in party or emote a thanks when someone buffs you. It's off by default.
Getting started
Install, then type /buffsmith (or /bs) for settings. Preview on screen, at the bottom of the settings list, draws a test bar where yours will sit, so you can place and size it without deliberately removing half your buffs first.

On the bar:
• Left-click an icon to cast the buff or use the item.
• Right-click to dismiss it until you change zones.
• Shift-right-click to ignore it for good. Ignored buffs and consumables are listed on the Ignored page, where you can bring them back.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /buffsmith or /bs | Open settings |
| /buffsmith toggle | Show or hide the bar |
| /buffsmith lock / unlock | Hide or show the drag handle |
| /buffsmith reset position | Move the bar back to the centre |
| /buffsmith preview | Show or hide the on-screen preview |
| /buffsmith scan | Rescan your bags for consumables |

Every Consecrated Hammer addon also has help, version, about, debug, startup, minimap, reset settings and quiz.
Combat
By default the bar only shows out of combat. Visibility can be set to Always, Never, or any mix of In combat, Out of combat, Solo, In a party and In a raid group.

If you do keep it up in combat, it stays as it was when combat started. Buffsmith deals with protected buttons, and WoW gets rather particular about addons rearranging those mid-fight, so nothing is rescanned or rearranged until combat ends.
Limits
• Tracking on WoW Forever is one at a time. The game only allows one tracking type there, so you pick which one Buffsmith offers. Selecting a different one puts it on the bar so a click swaps over.…

addons.description:
Decursive-style dispelling, one click per party member.

One click to cleanse them all, and in the options bind them.

Questions, bugs or ideas? Come say hi on the Consecrated Hammer Discord. Bug reports go in #bug-reports, or you can open a GitHub issue.

Salve gives you one box per group member. When someone picks up a debuff you can remove, their box lights up with that debuff type's colour and icon, and you click it to cleanse them. As a long-time Decursive user, I wanted to keep that simple rhythm: see the colour, click the box, cleanse the party.
What it does
• One box per group member, in a small grid you can size and place anywhere.
• It lights up straight away. A box shows the dispel type's colour and icon (Magic, Curse, Poison or Disease) the moment that member catches something you can remove, and dims when they're clean. Stack counts are drawn by the game itself.
• One click to cleanse. Left click uses your primary dispel. If your spec has a second dispel covering other schools, it goes on right click automatically. Every detected action can be rebound.
• Every dispelling class: Paladin, Priest, Druid, Shaman, Monk, Evoker, Mage and Warlock. Your spells are picked up automatically when you change spec or, for Warlocks, when your demon changes.
• Movement removal for you. Enable a spell like Blessing of Freedom on the Actions page and your own box lights orange when Blizzard reports a root or snare on you, with optional on-screen or chat text. These movement alerts are in beta and live on the Movement (beta) page.
• Optional sound alerts for known dispellable debuffs in the current dungeon or raid.
Getting started
Install, then type /salve for settings.

The panel starts in the centre of your screen with a small gold grip above it. Drag the grip to move it (the boxes themselves are buttons, so the panel can't be dragged directly). Use /salve lock or right-click the minimap button to hide the grip once you're happy with it.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /salve | Open settings |
| /salve toggle | Show or hide the panel |
| /salve lock / unlock | Hide or show the drag grip |
| /salve reset position | Put the panel back in the centre |
| /salve forever | Copy a WoW Forever cure and spellbook report, handy for bug reports |
| /salve whatsnew | Show what's new in recent releases |
| /salve cooldowns | Show how the cooldown icons read each spell; works in combat |
| /salve snares | List the root and snare spell IDs Salve has captured |
| /salve learned / learned clear | Show or clear the learned spell catalogue |

Every Consecrated Hammer addon also has help, version, about, debug, startup, minimap, reset settings and quiz.
Detected actions
The Actions page only lists spells your character knows. Movement actions stay off until you turn them on and bind them. "Area movement" is a ground-placed spell, so drop it where the affected players can reach it.

| Class | Dispels | Frees movement (ally) | Area movement | Self only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paladin | Cleanse: Magic, Poison, Disease; Cleanse Toxins: Poison, Disease | Blessing of Freedom; Blessing of Protection | None | Divine Shield |
| Priest | Purify: Magic, plus Disease with Improved Purify; Purify Disease: Disease | None | None | None |
| Druid | Nature's Cure: Magic, plus Poison/Curse with Improved Nature's Cure; Remove Corruption: Poison, Curse | None | None | Travel Form; Cat Form |
| Shaman | Purify Spirit: Magic, plus Curse with Improved Purify Spirit; Cleanse Spirit: Curse | None | Wind Rush Totem (Jet Stream only) | Spirit Walk; Ghost Wolf |
| Monk | Detox (Mistweaver): Magic, plus Poison/Disease with Improved Detox; Detox: Poison, Disease | Tiger's Lust | None | None |
| Evoker | Naturalize: Magic, Poison; Expunge: Poison; Cauterizing Flame: Poison, Curse, Disease | None | None | Hover |
| Mage | Remove Curse: Curse | None | None | Blink; Shimmer; Ice Block; barriers with Energized Barriers (snares only) |…

releases.changelog:
Fixed
• Show lockout debuffs on WoW Forever now times Forbearance at 1 minute
instead of 30 seconds. It also follows every rank of Blessing of Protection
and Divine Shield, plus Divine Protection and Templar's Bulwark, and no
longer starts from Lay on Hands. Sacred Duty's reduction isn't read, so the
icon can stay up to 10 seconds longer than the debuff.

Added
• A Cooldowns settings page. The cooldown bar and lockouts are off by
default.
• Sweep style on the cells: Auto (the default), Whole cell or
Icon. Icon shows each spell's icon on the cell only while it's on
cooldown, with its sweep and countdown, so names stay readable. Movement
sweeps such as Freedom get their own icon beside it. Auto uses Icon when
names are on and the whole-cell sweep when they're off, so cells without
names look as before. Icon size and Icon position set where they
sit.
• A cooldown bar beside the grid for the spells bound on Actions, such as
Cleanse, Freedom and Blessing of Protection. Each spell shows only while
it's on cooldown, or dimmed when ready with Show when ready. Pick its
side, gap, icon size and spacing, run it horizontally (the default) or
vertically, and switch individual spells off. Match Salve panel, on by
default, uses the cell height, cell spacing and box borders so icons line up
with the cells.
It moves with Salve, including when attached.
• Show lockout debuffs shows Forbearance, with its timer, after you cast
Blessing of Protection, Blessing of Spellwarding or Lay on Hands on someone,
or Divine Shield on yourself. Show on puts it on the cooldown bar with
the member's name (the default, and the bar appears for it even with the
spells off), on their cell, or both. It only shows while it lasts. It
follows your own casts, from a Salve cell or anywhere else, so another
paladin's Forbearance isn't shown. Off by default.
• /salve cooldowns shows how the cooldown icons read each spell. It works
in combat, which is where it matters.
• A What's new window after updates, listing new features with one button
per settings page. News from your other Consecrated Hammer addons shares the
same window. It never opens on a fresh install or in combat.
Turn it off with Show what's new after updates on Visibility, and reopen
it with /salve whatsnew or the About page.
Changed
• Updated the bundled HammerCore library, which adds the What's new window,
quiz questions grouped by category and a minimap click fix.

Added
• A Sorting settings page. Sort by keeps the game's group order
(the default), or sorts by role or by name. Role order picks any order of
tank, healer and DPS, with members who have no role last. Your cell pins
your own box first or last, and Reverse order flips the rest. The preview
follows the same settings.
• Boxes re-sort when roles change, while in Role mode.
• An Attach settings page. Attach to DandersFrames or EllesmereUI group
frames, whichever are loaded. Left and Right line each cell up with
its member's frame at the host's spacing, in the host's order, with raid
groups kept in their own columns or rows. Top and Bottom keep Salve's
grid together above or below the host. Gap sets the distance, and for
Left and Right, Align (top, centre or bottom of each frame) and
Up / down fine-tune where the cells sit. Salve moves when the host's
frames move, and uses its saved position whenever the host's frames aren't
on screen.
Fixed
• When someone joins or leaves mid-fight, box names now update straight away.
The boxes themselves still wait until combat ends to rebuild.

Added
• A Movement (beta) settings page for root, snare and slow alerts. The
movement sound, movement text, destination and preview controls moved there
from Alerts, with a link to Actions for binding movement spells.
• Enable movement alerts (beta) turns off all automatic movement text,
sounds and the orange player-cell cue. Movement-spell bindings and dispel
alerts keep working. It stays on by default, so existing behaviour doesn't
change until you switch it off.
• Include inferred slows (beta), off by default. When on, a sharp drop in
your run speed shows movement text and lights your box orange, pointing at
your existing movement-spell mouse binding. Inferred slows stay silent.
Enabling either beta option prints a warning that it may not work correctly.
• Dispel sound coverage for Living Bomb in Ruby Life Pools and Venomfang,
Icebound Flames, Essence Rend, Tempest and Congealing Bolt in The Venomous
Abyss.
• Coverage for both Curse of Darkness effects in Windrunner Spire and Energy
Bomb in Algeth'ar Academy.
• Instance-scoped sound data for Devouring Essence and Curse of Hesitation in
Torment's Rise, and Void Toxin in Venomfall Deeps.

These 12 entries use reviewed current boss-addon dispel metadata. Sounds still
require the matching cure school and the relevant instance, with dispel sound
alerts enabled. Actual playback of the added entries remains to be checked in
game.
Changed
• Inferred speed drops no longer show movement text unless **Include inferred
slows (beta)** is on. Reported roots and snares are unaffected.

Added
• Separate Alerts options for learning scope-change and newly learned-spell chat
messages, including captured roots and snares. Muting messages keeps learning
active. Existing message behaviour is retained until the options are changed.
• Orc Shatter Curse as an optional personal dispel on WoW Forever build 70425
or later. Bind it on Actions to arm only your own cell, leaving ordinary
class dispels unchanged. A small R cue uses the native Curse filter and
disappears while its cooldown is active or unreadable. It adds no sound
alerts. Actual Forever cue behaviour and Bane classification still need a
client check.

addons.description:
Cooldown Manager Utils adds missing-buff and reactive-proc reminders to World of Warcraft's built-in Cooldown Manager.
Features
• Adds a Buff Reminders tab to the side tabs of Blizzard's Cooldown Manager settings.
• Adds a separate Proc Reminders tab. On Retail it lists the Essential and Utility spells of the Cooldown Manager; on WoW Forever Warriors, Rogues, and Hunters it lists their reactive abilities (Overpower, Revenge, Riposte, Mongoose Bite, Counterattack). Selected abilities appear on the Proc Reminder bar only while Blizzard marks their reactive combat window active.
• Lists active spells from all class spellbook tabs (on Retail: class and current specialization) that apply a buff to your character, independently of Blizzard's Auras tab.
• Includes the gathering tracking abilities Find Herbs, Find Minerals, and Find Fish when they are available to your character. Their reminders disappear while the matching minimap tracking is active.
• Also covers temporary weapon enchants cast by you, such as the Shaman weapon imbues (Rockbiter, Flametongue, Frostbrand, Windfury, Earthliving) and the Paladin rites. Tracked weapon enchants are checked together against every equipped weapon (main hand and, when dual wielding, off hand; shields only if a shield imbue is tracked): they stay hidden while every weapon carries one of them, otherwise the tracked enchants that are not active on any weapon are shown (or all of them, if each one is already active on another weapon).
• Add Buff at the top of the Buff Reminders tab opens a search window: find a spell of your class by name or spell ID and click it to add it as a Buff Reminder. Spells added this way are marked with a warning triangle, may not work correctly, and can be removed with a right-click. Contact D4KiR on Discord to get a missing buff or proc added properly; the link is shown below the contact note and can be copied there.
• Sorts available entries into Tracked Buffs/Abilities, Not Displayed, and Not Learned. Learned entries can be moved by drag and drop; unlearned or currently unselected talent spells are shown disabled but retain their spell tooltip.
• The Buff Reminder bar shows an icon for every tracked buff that is currently missing on your character. The bar is hidden while nothing is missing.
• The separate Expiring Buffs bar shows selected buffs when they are missing or approaching expiration. Seconds before expiry controls the warning window (1–60 seconds) and is available in both the add-on options and the bar's Edit Mode settings. Both controls use the same value.
• Group buffs (Blizzard's Group Buffs list, plus Mark of the Wild, Blessing of the Bronze, Arcane Intellect, Power Word: Fortitude, Skyfury, and Battle Shout) are also checked on every eligible party or raid member. Their reminder appears as soon as one living, connected, visible member in range is missing the buff, and the icon shows how many eligible members have it, for example 2/5 or 3/40. Offline, dead, invisible, and out-of-range members are excluded from both numbers. Disable Check buffs on the group in a bar's Edit Mode settings to check only your own buffs instead. Group checking is enabled by default.
• Paladin Blessing reminders work as one group: every eligible party or raid member needs any recognized Blessing cast by you. addons.description:
ExpansionUtils by D4KiR combines a character overview with shortcuts and small improvements for World of Warcraft expansion features. Track your alts, weekly progress, professions, money, and played time in one place.
Character overview
The overview stores data from characters you log into with the addon enabled. It includes the following columns where the corresponding game systems are available:
• Character: class-colored name, level, specialization, and equipped item level.
• Mythic+: rating, best runs for the current season's dungeons, and current keystone.
• Raids: weekly progress and expansion-wide boss progress, separated by supported difficulty.
• Professions: both primary professions, skill levels, and unspent knowledge points where supported.
• Great Vault: raid, dungeon, and world activity progress. Unclaimed rewards appear as a green "Rewards waiting" message across the visible vault columns.
• Played time: total time played and time played at the current level.
• Money: gold, silver, and copper for each character.

Click column headers to sort the list and hover over cells for additional details. The footer shows total money and played time for the stored characters, including recorded Warband bank money where supported.

Customize the overview through its footer and settings:
• Filter the list to max-level characters.
• Adjust the font size from 8 to 18.
• Show, hide, and reorder column groups and their subcolumns.
• Resize the window and open settings with the footer's gear button.

Alt data reflects the last time each character was updated; log into an alt to refresh it. Missing values appear as ?, and weekly data is marked as outdated after a reset. Account totals use the characters already recorded by the addon.
Great Vault
On Retail, the Great Vault minimap button provides quick access to the overview and the vault. Its tooltip shows activity progress, example reward item levels when available, and whether rewards are waiting.

| Button | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Toggle the character overview |
| Right-click | Toggle the Great Vault outside combat |

The button can be shown or hidden in settings and is omitted where the Great Vault system is unavailable.
Valeera XP bar
On Retail, a movable XP bar tracks Valeera's Delve companion level and progress toward her next level. It appears while she is an active companion and has XP left to earn.

The bar and its tooltip show current XP, remaining XP, XP gained during the current Delve, and saved XP highscores by Delve and tier. Drag the unlocked bar outside combat to move it; its position is saved account-wide.

Toggle the bar:

Toggle the position lock:

Reset its position:

Clear saved XP highscores:
Other conveniences
• Reshii Wraps: on Retail, a shortcut beside the back slot in the character window opens the upgrade interface while Reshii Wraps are equipped.
• Mythic+ preparation: the keystone window gains a ready-check button with group readiness feedback and countdown buttons for 10, 5, and 3 seconds. Countdowns use DBM, BigWigs, or the built-in party countdown when available.
• Non-interruptible casts: on non-Retail clients, target and focus cast bars gain a shield indicator and gray coloring for non-interruptible casts, including support for DragonflightUI cast bars.
Settings and access
On Retail, use the main ExpansionUtils minimap button:

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Toggle settings |
| Shift + left-click | Toggle the character overview |
| Right-click | Hide the main minimap button |

Open settings with either command:

Use the language selector in the top-left corner of settings to choose between the eleven supported languages. The selection is saved account-wide and updates addon labels immediately; game-provided names follow the client language.…

SpeakStone 4.1.2
Voices similar to the in-game characters. Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment.

Version 4.1.2 covers the base add-ons, every retail sound pack and every WoW Forever pack.
What's new
• About 1,300 more lines re-recorded after player and owner reports, mostly Kul Tiran, Tauren, Goblin and Dracthyr characters.
• 51 characters who had lines waiting without a voice now speak, including Breem, Ba'kel, Katy Stampwhistle, One-Eyed Thak and the Mnemis keepers in Bastion.
• Nine characters the game shows as either a man or a woman now have a voice for each, and you hear the one that matches the character in front of you (for example Alliance Worker, Dark Iron Grenadier, Forsaken Dreadmage, Zandalari Vagrant and Tortollan Seeker).
• Colonel Troteman (Redridge Mountains) has a new voice that fits him.
• Goblin voices were shared out more evenly, so fewer goblins sound alike.
• Quest titles, character names, books and greetings in the Audio Library updated to match the new lines.
Thank you
Thank you to everyone who sent in quest text, flagged a line or reported a problem. Want to help? Send in quest text, report a line or flag a voice at https://speakstone.beanw.co.uk.

3.2.0 (October 2026)
This release starts a new phase for SpeakStone: polishing the voices and making sure names are pronounced the way you hear them in the game. Thank you to everyone who reported a line that sounded wrong. Keep the reports coming.

Every SpeakStone add-on is now version 3.2.0: SpeakStone, SpeakStone Forever and every voice pack. Update all of them together.
Pronunciation
• Place names that were read as the wrong words are now said properly, among them the Deadmines (it was "Dead Means"), Darkshire ("Dark Shear"), the Burning Steppes, the Plaguelands and Auchindoun.
• Also corrected: Gorefiend, Bonechewer, Gnarlpine, Runewood, Felrage, Scourgeholme, the Timeways, Blademoon, Barrowknoll, Leyhollow and Westrift.
• About 1,600 lines re-recorded in the same voices as before, in both retail and WoW Forever.
Greetings
• Characters who greeted every player by one class or race ("Greetings, warlock" from Fyrenz Vishonar, the Stormwind transmogrifier) now address everyone as "hero" or "traveller". About 230 lines fixed.
New lines
• 38 new lines sent in by players through the website, mostly character greetings.
Fixes
• Quest queue: a greeting no longer holds up a quest, and queued lines keep the character's portrait (from 3.1.6, now in every add-on).

Thanks to the players who reported the Deadmines, Darkshire and the Stormwind transmogrifier.

Version 4.1.2 covers the base add-ons, every retail sound pack and every WoW Forever pack.
What's new
• About 1,300 more lines re-recorded after player and owner reports, mostly Kul Tiran, Tauren, Goblin and Dracthyr characters.
• 51 characters who had lines waiting without a voice now speak, including Breem, Ba'kel, Katy Stampwhistle, One-Eyed Thak and the Mnemis keepers in Bastion.

• Goblin voices were shared out more evenly, so fewer goblins sound alike.
• Quest titles, character names, books and greetings in the Audio Library updated to match the new lines.

Changelog4.0.1
Fixes
• Narration now finishes after you close the quest or gossip window when "Stop narration when the window closes" is off. It plays at your Master volume, because the game cuts the Dialog volume channel when a window closes.
• The SpeakStone Guide names the character you hear giving each quest. Quests that start from a board, poster or note still show that.
• What's new lists these changes and the optional Dialogue UI follow-along.

Voices (arrive with the voice packs)
• Corrected pronunciation of Primalists, Nozdormu, Murozond, Khadgar, Kel'Thuzad and Runecarver.
• Jesper (Hallow's End) has a child's voice; new takes for Archmage Khadgar and Chromie.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment. The voices are similar to the in-game characters.
4.0.0
New
• Subtitles: the line being spoken is shown over the world in its own small bar, with the word being read highlighted. Off by default; turn it on in settings.
• Dialogue UI: quest text can follow the voice inside Dialogue UI's own window (optional).
• A redesigned SpeakStone Guide and settings window, with themes and font choices.
• The Guide shows each quest's zone and who gives it, and can group by NPC.

Voices (arrive with the voice packs)
• Corrected pronunciation of Primalists, Nozdormu, Murozond, Khadgar, Kel'Thuzad and Runecarver.
• Jesper (Hallow's End) now has a child's voice.
• New takes for Archmage Khadgar and Chromie.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment. The voices are similar to the in-game characters.
3.2.6 (October 2026)Greetings
• NPC greetings play even when the game's text differs slightly from ours: dashes, quotation marks and capital letters no longer stop a line from playing.
• Greetings for about 250 more lines are recognised, among them all nine of Orweyna's.
What's new
• A new What's new button in the settings window (beside Profiles, or /ss whatsnew) lists the changes in each release, newest first, with dates.
Fixes
• Fixed a rare error in the speech frame on WoW 12.x.

Unofficial; not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment.
3.2.3
Settings
• The settings window has tabs: Playback, Sound, Speech frame and Interface. The status cards stay on the left.
Playback
• New: Skip quests I've already heard. Autoplay leaves a quest passage alone once you have heard it, on any character. Read Quest still plays it, and /ss forget clears the list. Off by default.
• New: Stay quiet in combat, and in dungeons, raids and battlegrounds. Two separate options, both off by default. Read Quest and the keybind still work.
Sound
• New: Lower music and ambience while speaking, with a slider for how far. WoW cannot set a volume for one sound, so this turns the others down instead and puts them back when the line ends. Off by default.
Missing voices
• A small muted-speaker icon beside Read Quest shows when the quest text on screen has no voice yet. Hover it for how to send the text in. Can be turned off under Interface.
Audio Library
• New Favourites and Recent tabs. Click the star on any row, or on the speech frame while a line plays, to keep it in Favourites. Recent lists the last 50 things played.

• WoW Forever: quest lines have moved from Chatter to Audio Pack 2, and lines for quests that are not in WoW Forever have been removed. Update all three Forever packs together.
Characters
• Every child, boy or girl, now has the same child voice, in both games.
• Brokers and several other characters now have voices that match what they are.
• Eris Havenfire's greetings now all use the same voice.…

addons.description:
Free & open leveling guides for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Lodestar is an in-game, step-by-step guide engine — a community-built alternative to paid guide addons. It routes you (Alliance & Horde), automates the tedious quest clicks, and points an arrow at your next objective. No gating, no nag screens, no telemetry — 100% MIT-licensed.

Install it, log in, and Lodestar automatically loads the best guide for your level and zone. That's it.
Why this addon exists
Forever keeps its quest text, objectives and coordinates on the server — the client ships
bare quest IDs and nothing else. Lodestar's routes are generated from the open QuestieDB
(Forever flavor), which now carries Forever's own content — the new Skyborne starting zone,
Zephras Isle, included. For what no database has yet, the only way to get it is by being there,
so Lodestar collects it while you play and gives it back, open.

See docs/forever.md for the measurements and what is still open.

FeaturesGuidance
• Clean step window with your current objective, checkboxes, and a preview of what's next.
• On-screen waypoint arrow, a compass strip at the top of the screen, and the route drawn as
dots on the minimap and the world map — flights along their real track, boats and zeppelins
along their crossing.
• Travel planner — the fastest trip by travel time, leg by leg: walking, the flight paths you know
(and new ones you pick up on the way), boats, zeppelins, the Deeprun Tram, your hearthstone and
class teleports. It replans as you go, and the flight map highlights where to fly.
• Walks follow the terrain — the walking part of a route goes around mountains, cliffs and
lakes instead of a straight line (from the game client's own terrain; enclosed cities still
fall back to a straight line).
• Boat and zeppelin times — once Lodestar hears a zeppelin master or shipmaster announce an
arrival (or you ride one), it learns that transport's schedule: the route uses the real wait, the
arrow counts down ("leaves in 1m20s", "board now") and an alert sounds 30 s before it docks.
• Goes where you need — your guide step, your corpse while you're a ghost, a Shift+click on the
map or minimap, a typed coordinate, or the nearest class/profession trainer, repair, vendor, inn,
bank, auction house, flight master or stable (nearest by travel time, not straight line). All in the
Travel panel — the compass button in the guide header.
• Multiple guides open at once as tabs — switch, add, or close routes on the fly, with a clean empty state when none is loaded.
Automation (never get stuck)
• Auto-accept, auto-turn-in, and optional auto-reward (off by default; picks the best reward using a class-aware gear score).
• Auto-selects the right gossip/quest option and auto-shares quests with your party.
• Auto-skips a step whose NPC no longer offers its quest — imperfect data never stalls you.
Leveling companions
• XP/hour pace HUD with ETA-to-level and ahead/behind tracking.
• Gear Advisor — pings you when a bag item is an upgrade.
• Target markers on tooltips & nameplates; player coordinates on minimap and map.
• Death counter and a shareable end-of-run Report Card (with "ghost racing").
⭐ Quest collection — /ls scan
Part of Forever's new content is not in any public database yet, so Lodestar harvests it as you play: who gives
and who ends each quest, with NPC ID and coordinates, the objectives, and the waypoint the server
itself points at. It goes to LodestarDB.scan, and tools/ turns it into routes.

Nothing personal is collected. Nothing leaves your machine unless you turn on **Share quest
locations with the family** (off by default), which whispers only the where — quest ID, NPC ID, map
and coordinate — to guildmates running the companion, so the guides grow. Nothing about your character
goes in the message, and the addon on the other side drops who sent it. Off, sharing a harvest stays
what it always was: a file you hand over on purpose.
For contributors…

addons.description:
Not everyone has a beastmode PC. ForeverSettings finds the graphics settings that fit yours.

The graphics menu is a wall of sliders with names like "Compute effects" and "SSAO". Most of us either crank everything up and stutter in the busy places, or drop it all to Low and lose a beautiful game.

ForeverSettings measures your PC, tells you in plain words what each setting costs in frames per second, and picks settings for the frame rate you want. It shows you what you're giving up, so it's your call.

An addon for WoW Forever.
Get it
• Wago: addons.wago.io/addons/foreversettings
• GitHub: the zip on the Releases page.
• Install by hand: unzip into the game's Interface/AddOns folder so you have one ForeverSettings folder (for Forever: World of Warcraft/forever/Interface/AddOns/ForeverSettings), then start the game or /reload. The details are in INSTALL.md.
Try it in four steps
1. Stand somewhere quiet and click the minimap button, then Find my best settings.
2. Pick the frame rate you're aiming for (your monitor's refresh rate is a good choice) and press Start. It takes roughly 5 to 10 minutes and runs on its own. Don't move or open windows while it runs.
3. See what each change does, then Save. Your own settings are put back after the test.
4. Later, in a busy place (a city, a raid): Find my crowded settings.

See the price of every level
My settings (minimap menu, or /fset settings) has a page list on the left. The settings pages list every setting with what each level costs in frames per second against the level you have, how much it matters to the picture, a total for your choices, and what everything at the highest would give. Save as Everyday and Save as Crowded, at the bottom of the page list, keep the settings you have in the game now.

The Home page switches profile and starts the tests. The Picture size page has a slider for picture sharpness, up to 200% for this session only, with a warning that high values can crash some graphics cards.

Profiles
| Profile | What it is |
|---|---|
| Original | Your own settings, hands off. The addon records them before it first changes anything. Choose it to put everything back. |
| Everyday | The settings you saved for normal play. |
| Crowded | The settings you saved for raids and busy cities. |
| Maximum | Everything at the highest level the addon has learned. It needs plenty of graphics memory. |

Switch from the minimap button, or type /fset profile everyday (also crowded, maximum, original).

Good to know
• Nothing is forced on a first install.
• It never changes a setting during combat or while a test is running.
• It doesn't collect or send anything.
• /fset reset puts back everything the addon changed. /fset settings opens My settings, /fset size 50 to /fset size 200 sets the picture sharpness for this session, and /fset minimap hides or shows the button.
• Built for and tried on WoW Forever. Retail is untested.
Problems and ideas
Open an issue with a screenshot and what you clicked. If a test stopped, the window says why; include that.
For developers
The addon is Lua 5.1. The tests run under Node with fengari against a simulated game (tests/harness.lua):

tests/run.js also holds the mutation table: each rule in the code has a deliberate breakage that a named test must catch. docs/specs/ holds the design specs. Releases are made by pushing a version tag; see RELEASING.md.

Home switches profile and starts or shows the tests, and the Everyday and Crowded switch sits above the settings pages.
• Save as Everyday and Save as Crowded buttons at the bottom of the page list keep the settings you have in the game now.
• Picture size: a slider from 50% to 200% for picture sharpness (also /fset size 50 to /fset size 200, and /fset size off). It lasts for this session only: the game goes back to your normal setting when you log out. Above 100% it warns that some graphics cards crash at high values. The page also says whether the game's dynamic render scale is on.
• My settings shows a live total under the list: "Your Everyday settings: about N fps".
• A test warns when dynamic render scale is on, because it changes the picture size during a test and spoils the numbers. The "Before you start" list says to turn it off.
• /fset probe asks the game which settings it has.
• Releases are now packaged and uploaded automatically. The addon itself is unchanged.

Early release for testers. Install: unzip into the game's Interface/AddOns folder so you have one ForeverSettings folder, then see INSTALL.md in the repository for first use.
0.9.0
• New profile Maximum: every setting at its highest level the addon has learned (it needs plenty of graphics memory). From the minimap menu, /fset profile maximum or a Switch to Maximum button in My settings.
• My settings shows what each level costs in frames per second, how much each setting matters to the picture, and what everything at the highest would give.
• A guided test explains why its step count can grow (a reading is taken again when the frame rate isn't steady).
• A first install forces nothing.

Built for Forever and retail 12.1.5. Tested against a simulated game and by the author in the real one; reports with a screenshot are welcome.

addons.changelog:
Changelog1
• This is a work in progress. In groups and busy fights, the addon can still mistake other players' hits for yours, so some of your numbers can be wrong or missing, mostly melee hits and misses. If you see it happen, a recording of that fight (/nsctr record) helps a lot.
• Type /nsctr record to record your combat events, then type it again to stop. Attach the recording to a bug report, so problems in groups, raids, and battlegrounds can be fixed.
• Your damage and your pet's damage now show above enemy nameplates, and so do misses and dodges. Your combat log filter needs to show them.
• Your numbers show the icon of the spell that made them when the addon is sure which spell it was. Your melee hits and misses show the Auto Attack icon, and your pet's show the pet Attack icon. Most procs such as poisons, and your pet's spells, have no icon. A wand's Shoot gets its icon from its second hit, once the addon learns your wand's school, and again from the second hit after you change wands. With "Display Icon Only" on, a hit with no known spell shows its number. To clear what the addon learned, type /nsctr forget or press "Forget learned spells" in the Icons options.
• Your and your pet's melee hits use the "Auto Attacks" animations. With "Use Damage Type Color" on, yours show in white and your pet's in orange, as in NameplateSCT, so they no longer look like physical abilities. Once in a while, when you and your pet swing close together, your pet's number can show your colour and icon, or the two numbers can swap them.
• To hide the numbers of some spells, list them in the Filters options, one name or spell ID on each line, and turn on "Enable". Turn on "Inverse Spell Filter" to show only those spells. A spell's name covers all of its ranks. You can also list melee for your and your pet's melee hits and misses, missed for every miss, or unknown for hits whose spell the addon isn't sure of (melee never counts as unknown). Each character keeps its own list.
• In the Filters options, you can also hide numbers on some kinds of enemies: Boss, Rare, Elite, Normal, or Minor (totems and critters). Turn on "Inverse NPC Filter" to show numbers only on the kinds you check. "Enable" turns on both filters, and a number shows only when both let it through. This filter never hides numbers on enemy players. Your NPC choices count for all your characters. Unlike NameplateSCT, there's no list of NPC IDs, since the game hides which NPC is which in instances.
• The game's own damage numbers over the unit you hit are hidden while the addon is on. Turn off "Hide Blizzard Target Text", or the addon, to get them back the way you had them.
• Your numbers no longer go missing when a mob hits a friendly player near you.
• Numbers finish their animation when an enemy's nameplate disappears, so you see your killing blow, even when the game reports it just after the nameplate goes.
• The bottom of the main options page credits NameplateSCT, which this addon is based on.
• If your enemy nameplates are off when you hit something, a chat message tells you which key turns them on, once each time you log in.
• If your combat log filter doesn't send your and your pet's damage and misses, each kind of line in its own colour, or mixes in other players' lines that look like yours, a window offers to fix it with one click and a reload. The fix gives each kind of line in your Combat Log tab its own colour (spells, ticks, melee, shots, misses, heals), so the addon can tell them apart, and it stops the filter showing what others do to you, since those lines would look like yours. Since every filter lacks these colours before the fix, the window shows once for everyone. Until then, the numbers that can show still do.
addons.description:
NameplateSCT's scrolling combat text, drawn above enemy nameplates, for WoW: Forever.

Forever closes the combat log to addons, so the original NameplateSCT can't tell which hits are yours. This version works it out from what the game still sends. Your damage, misses, and your pet's damage show above the enemy you hit, with the original's animations and options.
Work in progress
Solo, the addon tells your hits apart well. In groups and busy fights, it can still mistake other players' hits for yours, so some of your numbers can be wrong or missing. Melee hits and misses get mixed up the most.

I'm still working on this. If you see it happen, a recording of that fight (/nsctr record, see below) helps a lot.
addons.name: NameplateSCT Reforged

Changelog2
• SCT Mover now runs on TBC Anniversary too, with the same options as on Forever
1
First release, for WoW: Forever (the 1.60 client).
• Lift or lower the text above your target with the "Target height" slider, so it clears the nameplate. It only changes two game settings, so your choice stays even if you turn the addon off
• Draw the text near your character above other UI elements with one checkbox
• Move the text near your character anywhere on the screen: drag a box in Move Mode (with sample text to show the result), or set exact values with the "Horizontal" and "Vertical" sliders
• Share self text settings across all your characters, or give one character its own with a checkbox
• Open the options with /sctm or /sctmover, and start dragging with /sctm move
• Show the version and locale at the bottom of the options, for bug reports
• Add machine translations for German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese
addons.description:
A simple WoW addon for Forever and TBC Anniversary to allow you to move your scrolling combat text where you choose. Your font, your float mode, and every other combat text setting stay the way you set them.
What it does
Target text (the damage, heals, and misses above your target)
• One "Target height" slider lifts or lowers it, so it clears the nameplate
• It only changes two game settings (WorldTextScreenY_v2 and WorldTextCritScreenY_v2), so your choice stays even if you turn the addon off

Self text (the damage you take, heals you receive, and similar, near your character)
• "Show self text above other UI elements" draws it on top of whatever was covering it
• "Move" gives you a box to drag to where the text should start, with sample text so you can see the result
• "Horizontal" and "Vertical" sliders set exact values
• Settings are shared by all your characters, and one checkbox gives a character its own

Each section has a "Reset position" button, and a fresh install changes nothing until you move something.
How to use it
Open the game options and pick SCT Mover under AddOns, or type /sctm (or /sctmover). /sctm move jumps straight to dragging the self text.
Good to know
• Built for WoW: Forever (the 1.60 client) and TBC Anniversary (the 2.5 client). Other versions of WoW aren't supported yet.
• Target text can only move up and down. The game has no setting for left and right.
• Target text always draws behind nameplates. The game gives addons no way to change that, so lift it with "Target height" until it clears the plate.
• Self text has to be turned on in the game's own options for the self text settings to do anything.
Languages
English, plus machine translations for German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. If a line reads wrong in your language, a fix to the file in locales/ is very welcome.
Bugs and ideas
Open an issue at github.com/dbspringer/sct-mover. The version and locale at the bottom of the options panel help a lot in a bug report.
Develop
Symlink the repo as SCTMover into the AddOns folder of each client you test
(_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns for Forever, anniversary/Interface/AddOns
for TBC Anniversary). Lint with luacheck ., run the specs with
busted (on Lua 5.1 or LuaJIT, since that's what WoW runs), and package with
the BigWigs packager. Releases are plain numbers that go up by one each time
(1, 2, 3), and pushing that number as a tag cuts the release.

Until the release workflow has CurseForge and Wago keys, ./export.sh [destination]
builds the same zip by hand, for example ./export.sh 1 ~/Desktop. It ships
exactly the files the TOC loads, plus the license.

Every release gets an entry in CHANGELOG.md, and the packager uses that file for the release notes.

Changelog1
First release, for WoW: Forever (the 1.60 client).
• See at a glance whether each ore is worth more smelted or sold raw. The Smelt Table lists every smelt, including Forever's new Azerothium and Heavy Thorium bars (their exact recipes are still being worked out, so the addon corrects itself once you've learned them), with what the ore and the bars sell for after the 5% auction house cut, and a verdict: Smelt, Sell Raw, or Toss-up when the difference isn't worth your time
• See what you'd make buying the ore at today's prices, smelting it, and selling the bars
• Get prices from Auctionator. Hover a row to see each price and how long ago it was seen, and a warning icon shows when a price is older than you'd like (1 hour by default)

• Open the table with /smelt, the ingot button on the auction house, or the addon compartment
• Get told when a smelt in the game differs from what the addon knows. It uses the game's version right away, and a report helps fix it for everyone
• Add machine translations for German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese
addons.description:
A WoW: Forever addon that tells you whether your ore is worth more smelted into bars or sold raw.
What it does
The Smelt Table lists every smelt on one screen, from Copper to Forever's new Azerothium and Heavy Thorium:
• What the ore sells for, and what the bars sell for, both after the 5% auction house cut
• A verdict for each one: Smelt, Sell Raw, or Toss-up when the difference isn't worth the time it takes to smelt
• What you'd make if you bought the ore at today's prices, smelted it, and sold the bars
• Alloys like Bronze and Steel get their own row, with the bars and Coal they use

Prices you can trust
• Hover a row to see each price and how long ago it was seen
• A warning icon shows when a price is older than you'd like (1 hour by default)
• A smelt with no price shows "No data" instead of a guess

Your characters
• Once a miner opens their Mining window, the smelts none of your characters can do are greyed out
• The tooltip says which of your characters can do the rest, counting any you can mail ore to
How to use it
1. Scan the auction house with Auctionator, so there are prices to compare
2. Open your Mining window once on each miner
3. Type /smelt, click the ingot on the auction house, or pick Smelt It/Dealt It from the addon compartment next to the minimap

/smelt options (or the gear on the table) lets you hide the smelts you don't care about, set how big a difference has to be before smelting is worth it, and choose when a price counts as old.
Good to know
• You'll need Auctionator for prices
• Built for WoW: Forever (the 1.60 client). Other versions of WoW aren't supported
• The auction house deposit isn't counted, since you get it back when the item sells
• A price is only as fresh as your last scan. A search for a single ore freshens just that ore
• If a smelt in the game ever differs from what the addon knows, it uses the game's version and asks you to report it
• Azerothium and Heavy Thorium are new in Forever, and their details are still being worked out. The addon assumes 1 ore makes 1 bar for now, and corrects itself once a character who knows them opens their Mining window
Languages
English, plus machine translations for German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. If a line reads wrong in your language, a fix to the file in locales/ is very welcome.
Bugs and ideas
Open an issue at github.com/dbspringer/smelt-it-dealt-it. The version and locale at the bottom of the options panel help a lot in a bug report.
Develop
Symlink the repo into the Forever AddOns folder as SmeltItDealtIt
(_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns). Lint with luacheck ., run the specs with
busted (on Lua 5.1 or LuaJIT, since that's what WoW runs), and package with
the BigWigs packager. Releases are plain numbers that go up by one each time
(1, 2, 3), and pushing that number as a tag cuts the release.

Until the release workflow has CurseForge and Wago keys, ./export.sh [destination]
builds the same zip by hand, for example ./export.sh 1 ~/Desktop. It ships
exactly the files the TOC loads, plus the license.

addons.author: Dezolve Labs
addons.changelog:
Initial public release for the WoW Forever beta.

Highlights:
• Slim, standalone XP bar with configurable position, size, and scale
• Earned, rested, and remaining XP visualization with 20 five-percent divisions
• Completed quest projections, session XP, XP/hour, and estimated time to level
• No external dependencies

See CHANGELOG.md for the full release notes.
addons.description:
A slim, standalone experience bar for WoW Forever, by Dezolve Labs.

Better Forever XP keeps the always-visible interface compact and puts the
details one hover away. It shows exact and abbreviated XP values, rested XP,
completed-quest XP, session pace, time to level, and progress measured with
20 visibly divided Blizzard-style five-percent bars. Under After turn-ins, its hover tooltip shows how much
ready-quest XP would spill into the next level (0 XP until the level threshold
is reached), plus the percentage of the following level's requirement.
Classic-curve estimates are marked ~; unknown curves show the XP amount
without inventing a percent. Earned XP is
electric blue while any rested XP remains, switching to classic purple when
rested XP runs out. The addon has no external dependencies.

Blizzard's original silver exhaustion-tick artwork marks 50% along the top
border as a single, filled, centered chevron, without covering XP labels or
capturing mouse input. It is on by default and can be hidden with
Show 50% marker in the Options panel.

The XP track has soft top-to-bottom tube shading, a single aligned metallic
rim with height-adjusting curved ends, and all 19 dividers for 20 XP segments.
Straight top/bottom lines meet the curved cap edges without a
second rectangular border or extra dark top stripe; blue/purple/rested
top sheen and bottom shading now carry through the rounded caps. The tube's background and earned/rested XP fills
now extend through genuinely curved endcaps rather than a square hidden track,
and dividers/XP fill boundaries now agree at exact percentages across the
entire visible tube width.
Each divider keeps its full-height muted steel-silver reflection centered
inside a gunmetal groove. Thin bars (10–24px) use a lighter 2-physical-pixel
groove, while taller bars retain the original 3px treatment, without
changing the divider positions or creating offset bars. The 50% Blizzard chip gets a subtle cool-steel tint to match. Markers remain aligned
to physical pixels at different bar sizes and scales. The Blizzard silver arrow is anchored directly to the white center of
the 50% groove. XP remains blue while rested and purple when unrested;
the rested extension stays dark navy. Its blue earned fill now uses a
deeper Blizzard-style cobalt gradient, the rounded ends no longer have a
mismatched blue stripe, and large white labels have thicker dark outlines
for contrast over the segment dividers. The level, current XP and remaining
XP labels now have separate non-overlapping regions; they automatically
shorten to fit their measured font widths at taller sizes. A very subtle
shadow only behind the actual large-label text reduces interference from
bright 5% lines. Settings provides three XP text modes: Tooltip only
(the clean default), Text on hover (bar labels while hovering), or
Always visible (permanent labels). The full tooltip remains available
in every mode, and previous hover/permanent choices are migrated. Completion uses two decimals below 1% (e.g. 0.02%) and one

addons.changelog:
KickAlert1.2.1 (2026-10-13)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Bump 1.2.1
• Untrack local agent memory
• Add CI tests and fix Wago ID
• Handle secret values on 12.x clients
Add explicit WoW Forever (1.60.x) detection and harden Compat/Detector logic for 12.x secret values. Interrupt protection now falls back only to UNIT\SPELLCAST\(NOT\_)INTERRUPTIBLE state, and interrupt cooldowns are deduced from player/pet cast success events when cooldown APIs are secret, using learned out-of-combat durations first then flavor-based defaults. Update status/localization strings, README behavior notes, tests for secret-value scenarios, and bump addon version to 1.2.0.
• Update README.md
• Update .gitignore
• Add packager release workflow
Add BigWigs packager metadata and a GitHub Actions release workflow that builds and publishes tagged releases to CurseForge, Wago, and GitHub. Also add the project IDs needed for release distribution.
• Add CVar mirror persistence
Store KickAlert settings in a mirrored Blizzard table and CVars so they survive on WoW Forever, which does not re-read account SavedVariables. Adds /ka wipe to reset both the SavedVariables table and the mirror, plus locale, README, and test updates.
• Update KickAlert.toc
• Handle secret cast shields in status
Track interruptibility fallbacks more explicitly, clear shield state on target/focus changes, and add cast serials so repeated starts and combat-log-only casts do not reuse stale alerts. Also keep SetFont outline flags non-nil on recent clients, add target cast diagnostics to /ka status, and extend tests/mocks for the new behavior.
addons.description:
World of Warcraft addon for every client (Classic Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, MoP Classic, retail).
Standalone version of the MyBossSuite Kick alert (Modules/InterruptAlert), with an added
screen glow and a graphical options panel.

When your target or focus casts an interruptible spell and your interrupt is
ready (and in range), three independent alerts fire:
• Text: configurable word (default KICK), font, size, outline, color (color picker),
adjustable pulse, free position.
• Glow: glowing border on all 4 edges of the screen, color and intensity (alpha through the
color picker), thickness, adjustable pulse.
• Sound: preset (alarm, raidwarning, readycheck, ping, murloc), SOUNDKIT id or
file (Interface\AddOns\X\kick.ogg).

Each alert is enabled, tuned and turned off separately.

On top of these three target/focus alerts, a KICK word can show above the nameplate
of any hostile unit casting an interruptible spell, without having to target it.
Detection (taken from MyBossSuite)
Three conditions, checked together and continuously during the cast:
target (or focus) is casting, the cast is not protected (notInterruptible), your interrupt
is actually ready and in range. A 0.15 s ticker runs during the cast: no event reports a kick
coming off cooldown in the middle of a cast.

The interrupt is detected, not configured: a per-class table filtered by what the character
actually knows (Classic ranks are covered by the spellbook). /ka spell forces a case
the table does not cover.

On clients where UnitCastingInfo returns nothing for a hostile unit, the combat log
(SPELL_CAST_START) takes over and the spell is assumed interruptible.

On the 12.x engine (retail Midnight, WoW Forever), the client hides values from addons in combat
("secret values"): whether the target's cast is protected is only known through the
UNIT_SPELLCAST_(NOT_)INTERRUPTIBLE events (a cast protected from its very start is assumed
interruptible), and your interrupt's cooldown is deduced
from your own casts (UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED on player) plus the spell's base cooldown, or the
last cooldown read outside combat. /ka status tells which source is in use.

addons.description:
Advanced graphics settings for World of Warcraft, in one panel.

Many graphics options are only available through /console commands. Panorama puts them in a
window of its own with sliders, checkboxes and dropdowns. It reapplies your values every time
you log in.
Features
• 58 settings grouped by theme: view distance, vegetation, shadows and lighting, environment,
image, camera and interface, nameplates, advanced, floating combat text.
• Your values are kept: a value set with /console beyond a slider's range is kept and written
again at login. The game itself limits what it accepts.
• Safe on your client: a setting that your client does not support is hidden and never
written.
• Starts from your current values: on first install, the panel reads your current game
settings. Nothing changes until you move a control.
• Stays in sync: a change made in the game's Graphics menu or with /console shows in the panel.
• Reapply on login: your values from the last session are written again at login, in case the
game changed them between sessions (Config.wtf, automatic detection). You can turn it off.
• Combat safe: changes made during combat are applied when combat ends.
• Graphics restart button: it applies settings such as anti-aliasing without leaving the game.
• Presets: Low, Medium, High and Extra set every graphics setting at once. They do not change
camera, mouse or comfort settings.
• Default button on every line: it puts that setting back to its default. Advanced settings,
nameplate class colors, size, pets and totems, zoom speed, text size and combat text use the
game's own default.
Settings
| Section | Settings |
|---|---|
| View distance | Scenery distance, horizon distance, volumetric fog |
| Vegetation and details | Ground details, grass density, grass distance |
| Shadows and lighting | Shadow quality, soft shadows, shadow resolution, sun shafts, SSAO, screen space effects |
| Environment | Water detail, sky detail, weather intensity, physics |

ForeverMeter1.15.1Changed

1.15.0Changed

instead (aggro, insecure aggro, above the tank), without numbers. The warning goes off when your
status is "above the tank". The window says "unavailable" only when the status is hidden too.

1.13.0New
• Options button: a gear in each window's title bar opens the options (after combat if you are fighting).

• A title too long for a narrow window is cut with "…" instead of wrapping over the first bar.
1.12.0New
• Your bar always shown: when you rank below the visible rows, your bar takes the last row with your real rank.
1.11.2New
• Mouse wheel on the title: scroll down for the next mode, up for the previous one.
1.11.1Fixed
• Death recap: events are shown oldest to newest even when the game lists the killing blow first.
• Threat against a boss: secret threat values now show "threat unavailable" instead of a Lua error.
• Damage rows in combat: totals use a format that accepts secret values, so they no longer raise an error.
