• A locked window no longer moves when its title is dragged, and /fm lock during a drag no longer leaves it stuck to the cursor.
• Copy as text: the window no longer opens empty when every source line is secret.
• /fm options in combat: the options now open when combat ends, instead of being blocked.
• Adding a window no longer raises an error when another window has no position yet.
• Reports use C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage, so they work without the deprecated chat fallback.
1.11.0New
• Automatic reset (option, off by default): the data is cleared on entering an instance other than the last one,
or on joining a group. Coming back to the same instance after a death, a login or a /reload does not clear it.
1.10.1Fixed
• Damage per second no longer drops after the target dies: meter windows now update when the game sends new data,
like the Blizzard meter, instead of every 0.2 s.
• With two threat windows, the second one showed 0/s.
• Threat per second no longer shows a false spike on the first update after a target change.
• The threat warning sound plays again on a new target.
Changed
• Less work out of combat and in raids: windows are redrawn only when their data changes, and group units are cached.
1.10.0New
• Copy as text (window menu): opens a box with the window's lines already selected; Ctrl+C to copy them,
for a paste into Discord, Escape to close. Out of combat only: amounts are secret in combat.
Lines holding a secret name (creature in an instance) are left out.
1.9.0New
• Auto show (option): windows show in combat or in a group, and hide 10 s after a solo fight.
• Bar text columns (options panel): total, per second and percent can each be shown or hidden.
In combat the percent is never shown, as the amounts are secret.…
addons.description:
Damage, healing, damage taken and threat meter for WoW Forever (client 1.60, 12.x engine).
Pure Lua, no libraries required: one main file, a settings mirror and 11 locale files.

> First install: restart the game once. The game only loads new texture and font files at startup,
> so /reload is not enough the first time. After an update, /reload is usually enough; restart if something looks missing.
What's new in 1.15.1
• Threat warning with MuscaUI: ForeverMeter no longer plays its sound when MuscaUI already warns.
1.15.0
• Threat against a boss: the game hides the numbers, so each bar shows the threat status instead
(aggro, insecure aggro, above the tank). The warning goes off when you are above the tank.
• Threat warning: the sound plays again only after your threat has stayed below the threshold for 3 seconds.

Earlier versions: see CHANGELOG.md.
Why a dedicated meter
On this engine, COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED is forbidden to addons (ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN popup).
Data comes from C_DamageMeter, Blizzard's server-side meter. In combat, names, amounts and GUIDs
are "secret values": they can be displayed, but not compared or summed. The addon shows the bars
in the order returned by the API and fills in the rest (percentages, per-spell breakdown) out of combat.
Threat comes from UnitDetailedThreatSituation. Against a boss, where the values are secret, the bars
show the status from UnitThreatSituation (aggro, insecure aggro, above the tank) without numbers.

addons.description:
Local, transparent and reversible noise control for public chat in
WoW Forever. It hides close repeats, optional bursts from one author and
literal terms that you choose, while keeping normal conversation, group
calls and legitimate trading visible.

Version 1.0.0 for WoW Forever 1.60.1 (Interface 16001).
What it does
• Observe first. On first start nothing is hidden: ChatGuard lists what
it would have hidden so you can judge its rules.
• Repeated text. Same author, same channel, same text within 30 s
(5–120 s). Exact match after harmless normalization: colours removed, spaces
collapsed, A–Z lowercased. Prices, digits and item links are kept, so
10g ≠ 100g and two different items with the same name are different.
• Bursts (off by default). More than 5 messages from one author in one
channel within 10 s (both adjustable).
• Your terms (off by default). Literal words or phrases, case-insensitive
for A–Z. There is no built-in word list: words such as WTS, LFG or gold are
never filtered unless you add them. A short term also matches inside longer
words.
• Allow and block lists of authors (Name-Realm); the allow list wins.
• Quarantine. Hidden or would-be-hidden messages stay viewable for the
session with time, channel, author and reason. Nothing is ever re-sent.
• Only the channels you select (none at first start). Whispers, party,
raid, guild, system and combat messages are never filtered.

Nothing leaves your computer: no network, telemetry, shared blacklists,
automatic reports or messages. Chat text is never saved to disk.

addons.description:
Guild bank and guild helper tools for E Pluribus Unum on WoW: Forever.

| Folder | What it is |
|---|---|
| EPUGuild/ | The WoW addon. Everyone in the guild installs it. See its README. |
| epu-discord/ | Discord companion bot. One officer runs it. See its README. |
| updater/ | One-click updater for guildmates (Windows). Ships as EPU-Updater-x.y.z.zip on each release. |
| tests/ | Simulators that run the addon outside WoW, with stubbed game functions, plus the Discord file round trip. |
Getting the addon (guildmates)
• Easiest: download EPU-Updater-x.y.z.zip from the latest Release, unzip it somewhere you'll keep it, and double-click Update EPU Guild Tools. It finds WoW: Forever, installs the addon, and updates it whenever you run it. Double-click Update automatically at startup once and it keeps itself current.
• WowUp: pick your Forever install from the dropdown at the top, then Get Addons > Install from URL, paste https://github.com/Donaga/epu-guild-tools and click Install. WowUp updates it like any other addon.
• By hand: unzip EPUGuild-x.y.z.zip into World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns\, then /reload.

In game, the addon tells you when a guildmate has a newer version. On Discord, the bot announces each release and /download gives the links.
Making a release
1. Commit changes to main. The Tests workflow runs on every push.
2. Add a line to CHANGELOG.md.
3. On GitHub: Releases → Draft a new release. Type a new tag such as v0.4.0 (target main), paste the changelog lines, then Publish release.

The Release workflow then runs the tests, stamps the version into the .toc, and attaches EPUGuild-0.4.0.zip, EPU-Updater-0.4.0.zip, epu-discord-0.4.0.zip and WowUp's release.json to the release. It takes about a minute. Within 30 minutes the Discord bot announces it, and guildmates' updaters pick it up the next time they run.

The repo must be public for the updater and WowUp to download releases.

addons.description:
Context-Aware Lore Codex, Investigative Dossiers & Field Journal for World of Warcraft: Forever

ChronicleWeaver transforms your journey across Azeroth in World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface: 16001) into an interactive, spoiler-safe archivist's investigation.

Unlike static lore databases, ChronicleWeaver observes what you actually discover in-game—zones and dungeons you step into, notable figures you target, quests you complete, multi-page books and plaques you read, NPC dialogue you archive, and item flavor text you inspect—and weaves them together into a living Lore Web and 18 Grand Archivist Case Files (Dossiers).

✨ Key Features🕵️ Grand Archivist Investigative Dossiers (ARCH-01 – ARCH-18)
• Cross-Zone Case Files: 18 handcrafted investigative dossiers connecting WoW: Forever custom zones/dungeons (Zephras Isle, The Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands, City of Dalaran, The Drowned City, Riverglades & Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison, Shen'Dralas, Blackmaw Hold, Shaper's Terrace, Mount Hyjal) with classic Warcraft history.
• Live Investigation Progress Bar: Tracks Uncovered Evidence: X / Y Clues (Z%) across linked Zones, Dungeons, NPCs, Quests, Books, and Relics.
• The Archivist's Synthesis & Field Directives: Each Dossier contains a hidden Archivist's Synthesis deduction that remains sealed under Spoiler-Safe protection until you uncover field clues in Azeroth, plus actionable Field Directives pointing you toward the zones and dungeons that hold the next piece of the mystery.
📖 Automatic Multi-Page Book, Quest & Relic Harvesting
• Multi-Page Book & Plaque Harvester: Automatically archives every page of in-game books, monuments, and plaques you read, complete with origin zone, coordinates, and a live [OK] ChronicleWeaver: Page Archived HUD badge on ItemTextFrame.
• Pure-Story Quest & Gossip Archiver: Records narrative quest descriptions and completion resolutions (automatically stripping out kill counters like 0/10 Slain), plus a 1-click [+] Archive Lore button on GossipFrame to preserve NPC story dialogue.
• Dynamic Relic Flavor Harvester: Automatically detects and archives items with quoted lore flavor text when inspected in your bags or tooltips.
🕸️ Bi-Directional Lore Weaving & Strict Category Navigation
• Automatic Keyword & Entity Weaving: Dynamically highlights known entities, zones, dungeons, and dossier keywords inside every chronicle you read, generating clickable Connected Lore & Mentioned In backlink pills.
• Strict Per-Category Top Tabs: Dedicated tabs for Zone, Dungeon, NPC, Relic, Book, Quest, and Dossier.
• Dungeon, NPC, Relic, Book, and Quest tabs organize entries into collapsible Zone folders (with * Favorites pinned at the top), or toggle to a flat list.
• Zone and Dossier tabs present clean, scannable direct lists.
• Dual-Theme Engine: Switch seamlessly between Royal Archivist Parchment and Midnight Obsidian (Theme: Parchment / Dark).
• Strict Spoiler-Safe Mode: Undiscovered entries stay hidden from your index and redacted on Dossier Evidence Boards until you encounter them in Azeroth (with an optional manual reveal button).
• World Map Waypoints & Personal Field Notes: Pin any location-tagged entry directly to your World Map with UiMapPoint super-tracking, and jot down auto-saving personal field notes on every entry.

⌨️ Slash Commands & Controls
| Command / Input | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| /cw or /lorecodex | Open / Close the ChronicleWeaver Tome |
| /cw theme | Toggle between Parchment and Dark themes |
| /cw spoilers | Toggle Spoiler-Safe Mode (Hidden / Shown) |
| /cw toast | Toggle animated Discovery Toast fanfare banners |
| /cw scan or /cw quests | Backfill narrative lore from your active Quest Log |
| /cw help | Print command reference in chat |
| Minimap Addon Compartment | Left-Click: Toggle Tome \| Right-Click: Toggle Spoiler-Safe Mode |
| Sidebar Entry Row | Left-Click: Read Chronicle \| Right-Click: Toggle * Favorite |

🗂️ Project Architecture

addons.description:
One bag window for WoW: Forever where you choose where items sit.

Your backpack and bags open in a single window. Save an item to a spot and it stays in that spot: when you use it up, the spot stays reserved (shown as a faded icon), and the next one you pick up goes right back to it.
Saving an item to a spot
• Alt+click an item to save it to the spot it is in. Alt+click it again to free the spot.
• Dropping an item on a faded spot puts it in your first empty bag slot, and it shows up in the saved spot.
• A small gold mark on an item means it has a saved spot. Spots are saved per character, by item (so every stack of Hearthstone lands in the same cell).

Spots are virtual. Baggie never moves anything in your real bags, so it is instant and safe. If saved spots would push a real item off the bottom of the window, the window grows by a row so nothing is ever hidden.
Bank
The bank and guild bank open as Baggie windows too, with the same saved spots. A Deposit button opens a menu of quick deposits from your bags (or Ctrl+Alt+click an item). On a character that has not bought a bank tab yet, the window says so and shows a Buy tab button with the price. Escape closes the bank and ends the banker conversation properly.
Quest item cleanup
Shift+Alt+click a quest item to mark it with a small red cross. Alt+click the minimap button (or type /baggie toss) to destroy the marked items. Baggie reads the game's own quest log and keeps anything a quest you have could still want (Questie, if installed, adds a second check). If it cannot read the log it keeps everything, it checks again just before each item goes, and it asks you to confirm first. /baggie toss list shows the marks and /baggie toss clear removes them.
Glows
New items, quest items, quest starters and currencies each have their own glow switch and color under /baggie options. Currencies that the game files as quest items (Blood Shard and the like) only glow if you turn that on. New-item glow only marks items that came in from outside (loot, mail, bank, vendor, trade). Items that start a quest also get a yellow ! in the middle of the slot until you accept the quest (optional). Quality glows have their own brightness slider, and one more sets how far all the glows reach past the slot.
Also
• Search box: dims everything that does not match a name or item type.
• Quality borders, dimmed grey junk, cooldowns, free slot counter, money.
• Sort button (manual only, uses the game's own bag sort). Bags never rearrange on their own.
• Options window (/baggie options): themes and color pickers for the window, title bar, slots and borders; border style and thickness; slot size, spacing and padding; gold and slot-counter display; item level; vendor helpers and more. Backgrounds, borders, fonts, glows and text positions are all adjustable. Right-click the minimap button for the options. The bank and guild bank open as Baggie windows too. Window backgrounds include textures and a custom texture path, every color can be copied and pasted as a hex code, and opacity is adjustable for the window, border and title bar.
• When Follow GreedUI is enabled, its look is applied only while Baggie draws its windows. Your Baggie settings and profiles are not rewritten; turn sync off to immediately restore Baggie's saved appearance.
• Replaces the default bag windows and the bag keys (B, F12 etc.). /baggie default gives the default bags back.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /baggie | Open or close the bags |
| /baggie pins | List saved spots |
| /baggie unpin all | Free every saved spot |
| /baggie cols 4-24 | Cells per row |
| /baggie scale 0.6-1.6 | Window size |
| /baggie borders | Quality borders on or off |
| /baggie keyring | Show or hide the keyring |
| /baggie default | Switch between Baggie and the default bags |
| /baggie toss [list|clear] | Destroy marked quest items, list or clear the marks |
| /baggie reset | Put the window back at its default position |

MIT licensed.

addons.description:
A fishing helper for WoW: Forever, in the spirit of Fishing Buddy.
• Right-click to cast, right-click to catch. With a pole in hand, a single right-click on the world
casts Fishing. When the bobber splashes, right-click again and the fish is looted without aiming at the
bobber. Both are plain right-clicks; the game needs a real click for each. Prefer a double-click to cast?
Switch "Cast with" to double-click in Setup. With no pole in hand, a double-click equips one.
• Automatic lures. When your pole has no lure, the double-click applies the best one in your bags
(Aquadynamic Fish Attractor, Flesh Eating Worm, Bright Baubles, Nightcrawlers, Shiny Bauble ...).
Click again to cast.
• Fishing outfit. Put on your fishing gear, type /fishie save, and from then on /fishie switch (or
right-click the minimap button) swaps between it and your normal gear.
• Catch log. Everything you fish up is counted per zone and per session, with catches per hour.
• Sound boost. Effects up, music and ambience down while your line is out, restored afterwards.
• Options like Fishing Buddy: double-click speed, an optional Shift/Ctrl/Alt to hold, strongest or weakest lure first, replace a lure that is about to run out (with a chat warning), auto-loot while fishing, go back to your normal gear after a quiet spell, a minimap button you can hide, and a key binding (Options > Key Bindings > Fishie).
• On-screen box (/fishie hud): time since your cast, lure time left and this session's catches.
• Skill display and a small window (/fishie) with session stats, catches by zone and settings.

The game needs a real click for every cast, so casting is never fully automatic.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /fishie | Open the window |
| /fishie switch | Fishing outfit on or off |
| /fishie save | Remember what you're wearing as your fishing outfit |
| /fishie stats / reset | Print or reset this session |
| /fishie doubleclick, lure, pole, sound, announce, refreshlure, warnlure, autoloot, hud | Toggle a feature (add on or off) |
| /fishie minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |
| /fishie debug | Explain every click, cast and catch in chat |
| /fishie probe | Show what the game reports about your pole and lures |
Notes
If something doesn't work, run /fishie probe and /fishie debug on, and report what they say.

addons.description:
Recruit on autopilot. Players whisper you a phrase, Guildie sends the guild invite, and when they join it posts your custom welcome in guild chat.

Built for WoW: Forever.
Features
• Whisper-to-invite: set a phrase like guild inv. Anyone who whispers it gets an invite.
• Exact or loose matching: require the exact phrase, or catch it anywhere in a whisper.
• Custom welcome message: posted in guild chat when a new member joins. Use {name} and {guild}.
• No double welcomes: by default Guildie only welcomes players it invited, so several officers can run it at once.
• Reply whisper: optionally tell the player their invite is on the way.
• Spam protection: per-player cooldown.
• Confirm mode: the game blocks addons from sending guild invites on their own, so Guildie shows a popup; its Invite button puts /ginvite Name in your chat box and you press Enter to send it. Guildie only marks the player as invited once that command goes out.
• Activity log and stats right in the settings window.
• Guild Armory (/guildie armory): gear, talents, professions and gold of guildmates who run Guildie, with alts grouped under their main and their gold added up.
• Zone tab (/guildie zone): who's in your zone and who else has quests from it.
• Dates tab: join dates and birthdays, logged and shared automatically, with anniversary and birthday shout-outs.
• Crafters, recruit tracking, loot help and a raid-time schedule.
How to use
Open settings with /guildie, the AddOns button next to the minimap, or Options → AddOns → Guildie.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /guildie | Open settings |
| /guildie on / off | Toggle auto-invite |
| /guildie phrase | Set the invite phrase |
| /guildie welcome | Set the welcome message |
| /guildie preview | Preview the welcome in your chat |

Your guild rank needs permission to invite.
Notes
• Guild chat messages wait until chat is unlocked (for example, after a boss encounter) and then send.
• Some Forever beta builds don't reload saved settings reliably. Guildie keeps a per-character copy as a backup.

Bug reports and ideas welcome!

addons.description:
A gear advisor for WoW: Forever. Tell it your class and spec and it rates the gear in your bags against what you wear, tells you where to get better gear for your level, and shows the best buys in the Auction House.

Open it with /outfit, the minimap button, or the addon list.
What it does
• Inventory. Every piece of gear in your bags is read from its real tooltip, scored for your spec, and compared with the item you would replace. Only the best upgrade per slot is listed (two for rings and trinkets). An empty slot always gets the best item you can use.
• Equipped. Every equipped item with its score, and which slots are empty.
• What to get. Known quest rewards, dungeon drops, vendor and crafted items for your level, scored the same way, with where to get each one. For every class it also lists gear your other characters carry in their bags or bank, and gear one of your characters can craft (this part reads Profiteer's saved data, so install Profiteer). Built-in lists of quest, dungeon and vendor gear cover Mage, Warlock and Priest so far; the Auction tab works for every class. Tick boxes along the bottom pick which kinds (Quest, Dungeon, Battleground, Vendor) each character sees.
• Auction. Reads the prices Profiteer saved from your last Auction House scan and shows the best gear for sale per slot, with its price (red when you cannot afford it yet). Needs Profiteer.
• Tooltips. Hover any item for a line saying whether it is an upgrade, worse or about the same compared with what you wear.
• Minimap button (left click opens, right click opens What to get, drag to move) and a chat alert when a new upgrade lands in your bags.

Everything is limited to what you can use now: items above your level or that your class cannot wear are never suggested.
Spec and weights
Outfitter guesses your spec from your talents. Pick a different one from the drop-down in the window, or /outfit spec to cycle. Each spec has its own stat weights (/outfit weights prints them).
Commands
| | |
|---|---|
| /outfit | Open or close the window |
| /outfit spec | Next spec |
| /outfit weights | The numbers the current spec uses |
| /outfit tip | Tooltip line on/off |
| /outfit minimap | Minimap button show/hide |
| /outfit alert | Chat alert for new bag upgrades on/off |
| /outfit gain N | Only suggest items at least N% better |
| /outfit debug | Print what the game reports about your bags |

The item text is read in English. MIT licensed.

What to get uses the quest database from Questie (QuestieDB) when it is installed, so every class gets quest, vendor and dungeon suggestions.

addons.description:
A mailbox upgrade for WoW: Forever.

Everything Postage adds lives inside the normal mailbox, so it looks and works like part of the game.
Inbox
• Select. A checkbox on every mail. Shift-click a checkbox to select a range, ctrl-click to
select everything from that sender. Then Open or Return the checked mail.
• Open All. Opens every mail with gold or items attached, of the kinds you choose
(right-click the button: auction sold/won/expired/cancelled/outbid, Postmaster, players).
COD mail is always skipped and reported. It keeps bag slots free if you ask it to, and tells
you how much gold it collected.
• Express. Shift-click a mail to take it, ctrl-click to return it. Scroll the mouse wheel
over the inbox to change pages.
• DoNotWant. Each mail shows how long it has left: yellow means it goes back to the sender,
red means it will be deleted.
• Pending auction gold. A readout at the top of the inbox totals auction sales whose gold
hasn't arrived yet, and when the next one lands. Hover it for each sale.
Sending
• BlackBook. A contacts button next to the To: box with your alts, people you've mailed,
friends and guild. Names autocomplete as you type. Your alts are listed once you've logged in
on each with Postage, or add one by typing its name and choosing "Add ... to Alts". Each alt shows its professions in shorthand (LW, ECH, ALC...; main professions only).
• Keep recipient. Tick it to keep the name in the To: box after sending, so you can send
several mails to the same person.
• Alt-click an item in your bags to attach it; shift-alt-click attaches every stack of it.
• QuickAttach. Buttons beside the Send Mail frame attach everything for a profession in one click (tailoring, skinning, leatherworking, mining, blacksmithing, cooking, herbalism, alchemy, enchanting, engineering, first aid and more: cloth, leather, ore, herbs,
cooking, elemental, enchanting or engineering materials in one click.
• Wire. Leave the subject empty when sending gold and it is filled in with the amount as soon as you type the gold, so Send is never greyed out.
Reading
• Copy shows a mail's text in a box you can copy from.
• Forward starts a new mail with the same subject and text (attachments aren't forwarded).
Other
• TradeBlock declines trades and guild charters while the mailbox is open.

addons.description:
Find out which crafts actually make money. Profiteer reads the recipes your characters know, prices the materials and the finished item from the Auction House, and ranks every craft by profit and return on investment, across all of your characters.

Built for WoW Forever (beta client 1.60.x).
What it does
• Ranks your crafts. For every recipe any of your characters knows: material cost (auction price, or the vendor price if that's cheaper) against what the finished item sells for after the auction cut. Shows profit, ROI, how many are listed, and how many you can craft right now from your bags and bank.
• Click through to the materials. In the results window, click a craft to search the Auction House for its materials (through Auctionator's Shopping list if you have it), shift-click to search for the finished item, and right-click to track a craft so it stays pinned at the top.
• Works across your whole account. One window lists each craft once, with every character who can make it.
• Scans automatically. Opens the Auction House, takes one full scan in the background without hitching the game, and refreshes whenever the data is stale.
• Price history and sales estimates. Every scan adds a snapshot, so you get a market median, a trend, and an estimated sales-per-day figure for the items you craft.
• Recipe tracker. A recipe item's tooltip (Recipe, Pattern, Formula, Plans...) tells you which of your characters already know it, which could still learn it, and which have no such profession. Open each character's profession windows once to fill it in.
• Auction House tabs. Shopping, selling and cancelling pages with price gaps, relist prices and totals.
• Item tooltips. Lowest auction price, listing count, market median and trend, and vendor price on any scanned item.
• Lives in the Auction House. A Profiteer button on the Auction House window opens the ranking over it. There is also a minimap button.

• Ledger fix: auction deposits are matched to the auctions being created, so a slow posting no longer shows up as "AH purchases".
• Ledger: new "Unrealized: listed, not sold yet" section. For each character it shows how many auctions you have up, their total asking price and an estimate after the AH cut, any sold items whose gold is still in the mail, and your biggest listings. • Crafts: new "Buy up to" column and tooltip section. Walks each material up the AH price ladder from your last scan and tells you how many crafts you can buy materials for before the next one stops paying (and how much of each material, at what top price, and the total profit). Notes when the AH simply runs out of a material.

• Ledger character dropdown now shows "Name - Realm", so same-named characters on different realms are told apart.

addons.description:
A character showcase for WoW: Forever. Your character on a full-screen stage, your gear around them, and a photo studio.

Open it with /vanity, the minimap button, the addon list, or a key (Options > Key Bindings > AddOns > Vanity). A button on the character window is available in Settings.
What it does
• Full-screen rotatable model. Drag to turn, right-drag to move, mouse wheel to zoom, slow turntable (/vanity spin).
• Item cards. Every equipped item shows its details beside its slot, no hovering needed: name in quality color, item level, main stats, enchant, equip/use effects and any problems. Hover for the full tooltip, shift-click to link in chat.
• Warnings that matter. A red ! on any item that is missing an enchant (from level 40) or has an empty gem socket, with a summary list on screen.
• Average item level and durability (average and lowest).
• Stats panel: attributes, armor, attack power, crit, dodge, parry, block, haste, health, power.
• Pose picker. The Pose button opens a menu of 22 poses and emotes (salute, wave, bow, cheer, applaud, laugh, cry, flex, point, dance, sit, sleep, kneel ...). One-shot emotes repeat until you pick another.
• Photo mode (/vanity photo): hides the interface, then a studio bar with backgrounds, the same pose picker, turntable, and a screenshot button that hides the controls first.
• 14 backgrounds: Midnight, Class color, Faction, Ember, Frost, Forest, Void, Gilded, Sunset, Slate, Pure black, Studio white, Green screen and The world.
• AFK screen. Go AFK (or /vanity afk to preview) and Vanity fills the screen with your character, a big timer, a clock and your gear and stats, cycling poses. Your active buffs show with tooltips. Move or press a key to return.
• View target: look at another player's model.
Settings
/vanity settings: background, brightness, camera framing (full body, waist up, bust, portrait), turntable, panels, item cards, game-interface hiding and AFK options.
Commands
| | |
|---|---|
| /vanity | Open or close the showcase |
| /vanity photo | Photo mode |
| /vanity afk | Preview the AFK screen |
| /vanity bg | Cycle the background |
| /vanity spin | Turntable on/off |
| /vanity settings | Settings |
| /vanity reset | Reset the camera |
| /vanity minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |

Vanity is built from scratch (it shares no code or art with any other addon). MIT licensed.

addons.changelog:
Forever Suite 2.0 – beta10

> 🧪 Beta für Retail: Bis WoW Forever startet, wird die Suite in Retail (Midnight) getestet. Dies ist eine Testversion, die Daten darin sind Testdaten.

Spiel ganz beenden, die Forever…-Ordner unter Interface\AddOns löschen, die neuen aus dem ZIP hineinkopieren, Spiel starten. Eure Daten bleiben erhalten.
Wichtig bei diesem Update
• Vorher sichern: Bitte den Ordner WTF kopieren, bevor ihr das Spiel mit der neuen Fassung startet.
• Alle möglichst gemeinsam aktualisieren: beta10 tauscht über einen eigenen Kanal (Protokoll 6). beta9 und beta10 tauschen keine Daten miteinander, ein Hinweis im Chat nennt ältere Fassungen.
Bekannte Einschränkungen
• Die erste Reisesuche nach dem Login kann 9–11 Sekunden dauern, danach geht es deutlich schneller. Das Spiel läuft währenddessen weiter.
• Bei Wegsuchen kann es vereinzelt kurz ruckeln.
• In einem unbekannten Haus reicht eine neue Route manchmal zunächst nur ein kurzes Stück. Sie wird neu gesucht, sobald ihr eine Tür benutzt oder die Seite wechselt.
• Die Zwei-Client-Prüfung lief gegen eine ältere Austausch-Fassung, nicht gegen ein echtes beta9-Paket. Meldet bitte, wenn der Austausch mit Mitspielern hängt.

Neu seit v2.0-beta9:
Basis (Core) 0.4.56 (vorher 0.4.52)
• Suche: Lange Ergebnislisten lassen sich mit dem Mausrad und den Pfeiltasten durchgehen
• Suche: Rechts neben der Liste ein Scrollbalken zum Ziehen
• Kartenpunkte: Lernt das Spiel die Größe einer Karte erst nach dem Login, gehen abgelegte Punkte nicht mehr verloren
• Protokoll: Kein Lua-Fehler mehr beim Laden, wenn BugSack aktiv ist
Navigation 0.5.96 (vorher 0.5.83)
• Route: Eine Suche, die wiederholt von Datenänderungen überholt wird, liefert keinen veralteten Weg mehr
• Route: Ohne Tür aus einem Haus keine lange rote Linie mehr
• Route: Beim Betreten eines Hauses verschwindet eine gute Route nicht mehr
• Route: Eine an bekannten Boden endende Route wird beim Verlassen des Hauses sofort neu gesucht
• Route: Aus einem unbekannten Haus führt der Weg sofort durch die eben benutzte Tür
• Route: Ohne bekannte Tür keine rote Linie mehr durch die Wände zum nächsten Haus
• Route: Eine beschädigte Route, die kürzer als die Luftlinie zum Ziel ist, wird beim nächsten Nachschauen ersetzt
• Route: Die Suche gibt den Frame nach Zeit zurück, das kappt lange Scheiben
• Route: Eine Suche übernimmt keinen Weg über eine inzwischen geänderte Tür mehr, sondern sucht neu
• Reisen: Ein selbst gelaufener neuer Zugang zählt sofort
• Protokoll: Der längste Frame einer Suche wird aufgeschlüsselt
• Route: Die Türen einer Karte werden nur noch nach einer Änderung neu berechnet, das verkürzt Suchen und Ruckler
• Protokoll: Jede Wegsuche nennt Wartezeit, Rechenzeit und längsten Frame, bei laufender Messung im Protokoll
• Route: Findet nach dem Abweichen schneller einen neuen Weg, auch wenn du weiterläufst; die Reisehilfe sagt, dass gesucht wird
• Route: Die Meldung nennt jetzt die unbestätigte Tür
• Route: Weniger Ruckler beim Suchen einer neuen Route, die Türen werden pro Suche nur noch einmal berechnet
• Reisen: Ein Ziel in einer Unterkarte (Nordhain) führt über den gelaufenen Grenzübergang statt in gerader Linie durchs Gelände
• Reisen: Liegt das Ziel auf einer anderen Karte als das Ende des bekannten Wegs (Nordhain vom Wald von Elwynn aus), führt die Route nach dem Grenzübertritt nicht mehr zurück
• Reisen: Die nächste Etappe wird über mehrere Frames berechnet – kein Ruckler mehr bis zu zwei Sekunden
• Reisen: Bist du während der Suche weitergelaufen, wird von dort neu gesucht
• Route: Keine Linie mehr quer durch die Stadt, wenn die Suche ihre Grenze erreicht – der schon gefundene Weg bleibt, jede Strecke wird nur einmal gesucht
• Route: Drinnen kein Sprung mehr von Raum zu Raum durch die Wand, der Weg geht über die Tür; ohne bekannte Verbindung zwischen zwei Räumen gibt es keine Linie
• Route: Zerfällt nicht mehr beim Teleport hin und zurück; der Stopp an der Tür bleibt auch nach einem Umweg…

addons.changelog:
• Everything starts collapsed and opens on click. Bosses are headers now: click one for its drops, and right-click it for its Wowhead link. The same goes for each quest on the Dungeons and Raids tabs (click for where it starts and its rewards), and for search results, the Wishlist's groups, a set's bonuses and pieces, a profession's groups and the Quests tab. Closed headers say how many items or quests they hold. Shift-click any header to open or close every section, including the bosses inside wings.
• A Quests tab. Every dungeon and raid quest, with where it stands for you and how to get it. Open a quest to see who starts it and where, where to turn it in, its optional lead-in, every quest that comes before it in order with your progress on each, and its rewards. The Defias Brotherhood shows its six earlier quests from Westfall to Stormwind and back; the longest, Return to Bodley in Blackrock Spire, has 24. 328 of the 626 dungeon and raid quests need earlier quests.
• "Quests you can do", the tab's first page: the dungeon and raid quests you can pick up now, have in your log, or can work toward now, with the next quest to pick up under each and who gives it. Grey quests too easy for you are left out.
• Map pins. The pin button next to a quest giver puts the game's map pin, and its arrow in the world, on them. A TomTom arrow too, when TomTom is installed. 603 quest givers have a spot.
• Each quest shows the mark a quest giver would: a yellow "!" when you can pick it up, a grey one when it needs earlier quests, a higher level, more reputation or a profession skill, a "?" in your log (yellow when it's ready to turn in), a check when you've done it. It says what's missing: "3 quests first", "At level 30", "Honored with Argent Dawn" (the Naxxramas attunements, Zandalar Tribe quests, the Thorium Brotherhood's), "Blacksmithing 275". Lead-in quests close once you've taken what they lead to, taking one of two alternatives closes the other, and quests for another race or class are left out. The marks update as your quest log changes.
• Levels are Forever's own (A Fine Mess needs 20, not Classic's 24).
• On the Dungeons and Raids tabs, an open quest has a line saying who starts it, where, and how many quests come before it. Click it for the whole chain on the Quests tab. The quest's tooltip names the next quest to pick up, or the one in your log and who takes it in. Quests for another race or class are left out there too.
• Items that start a quest are no longer listed as quests, including the ones with a faction (Strange Water Globe, Small Scroll, Tattered Note, Head of Nefarian, An Unsent Letter, Shattered Necklace). Quests nobody can pick up in Forever are left out: Waking Naralex, When Dreams Turn to Nightmares, and old copies of Baron Aquanis, The Glowing Shard, The Last Element and Attunement to the Core. The live versions of The Glowing Shard and Attunement to the Core are listed now.
• Quests Forever added that start from an item say which: Crest of Lordaeron, Bloodied Insignia, the Abominable Head (Unending Torment) and others.
• New quests: Starving Arcane and Heart of Disruption in Dalaran, and Past Due in Scarlet Monastery.
• New drops: Golemsight Long Gun (Relic Guardian), Thermaplugg Medal of Honor (Crowd Pummeler 9-60), Quilrager Throwing Axe (Agathelos the Raging), Thorncursed Grips and Death Prophet Spine (Aggem Thorncurse), and Ebony Boneclub (Razorfen Downs trash). Six drops whose boss wasn't known are now on their bosses: Thornweaver Drape and Geomancer Headdress (Roogug), Quillord Mail Leggings (Overlord Ramtusk), Painwalker Buckler (Interrogator Vishas), Polished Skullcap (Bloodmage Thalnos) and Spellsever Crossbow (Arcanist Doan). addons.description:
A WoW: Forever addon with dungeon and raid loot tables, dungeon quests, item sets, profession recipes, a search across all of them, and a wishlist of gear to chase.
• Click the minimap button (or type /fl) to open it. The window is built from the game's own parts (portrait frame, side tabs, search box, dropdowns, checkboxes and scroll bars), so it looks like the rest of WoW: Forever's interface. The tabs down its right edge are Dungeons, Raids, Quests, Sets, Professions and Wishlist.
• Dungeons are sorted by level. Level ranges are colored by how hard the dungeon is for you, as the quest log colors quests; dungeons at your level have gold names, and New marks dungeons added in Forever.
• Raids has Forever's new raids (The Barrow Deeps and Hyjal Summit), Onyxia's Lair, and the Classic raids: Molten Core, Blackwing Lair, Zul'Gurub, Ruins and Temple of Ahn'Qiraj, and Naxxramas. The list shows each raid's size. New marks Forever's new raids, and Classic marks Classic raids Forever hasn't announced.
• Everything starts collapsed. Click a header to open it, click again to close it, and shift-click any header to open or close every section at once (the bosses inside wings too). Closed headers say how many items or quests they hold. What you open stays open while you're logged in.
• Click a dungeon or raid to see its bosses, then click a boss for its drops (right-click it for its Wowhead link). Its quests are in the Quests section at the bottom (quests for the other faction are left out): click one for where it starts and its rewards. Each quest has the mark a quest giver would show you (a yellow "!" you can pick it up, a grey one not yet, a "?" in your log, a check once it's done). An open quest has a line saying who starts it, where, and how many quests come before it; click that line for the whole chain on the Quests tab.
• Quests is every dungeon and raid quest with how to get it. Its first page, "Quests you can do", lists the quests you can pick up, have in your log, or can work toward now, with the next quest to pick up under each (grey quests too easy for you are left out). Pick a dungeon or raid for all of its quests: click one to see where it starts and where to turn it in, its optional lead-in, every quest before it in order with your progress on each, and its rewards. The pin button next to a quest giver puts the game's map pin (and its arrow in the world) on them, and a TomTom arrow when TomTom is installed. Quests you can't take (another faction, race or class) are left out, and one that needs reputation or a profession skill says which. The page updates as your quest log changes.
• Sets lists every item set with a piece in the dungeon, raid or quest loot: its set bonuses, and where each piece comes from. Sets your class can wear have gold names.
• My class and Hide Classic (next to the search box) filter the Dungeons, Raids and Sets tabs and their searches. My class keeps what your class can use: your armor types (for Warriors, Paladins, Hunters and Shamans also the type they wear before level 40), your weapon skills, shields and relics where they apply, and class-only items for your class. Rings, necks, cloaks and trinkets always show. Each character keeps its own settings.
• Every item tooltip in the game (bags, chat links, the auction house, loot) gets a Forever Loot section saying which bosses drop it, which quest gives it, and which profession makes it. /fl tooltip turns it off.
• Hover an item for its tooltip. Shift-click links it in chat, Ctrl-click previews it, right-click puts it on your wishlist, and a plain click gives you a copyable Wowhead link. Right-click a boss or quest bar for its Wowhead link; the Wowhead button does the same for the dungeon.

addons.changelog:
v0.1.5 (2026-10-09)
Everything in v0.1.5-beta1, plus the fixes from a code review of the protocol and persistence:
• A character whose name merely extends ours ("Dea Onex", "Deaone", or our first name alone) can no longer replay our hello and become our identity, taking our hosted games' ownership with it (#62, #72). On classic realms the realm is part of the identity too (#76).
• Another host can no longer poison a game's squares by announcing a set under that game's hash: a set is trusted only when its hash comes out of its content and it came from the game's own host, in memory and in the saved library (#63, #73).
• A snapshot that arrives after newer calls no longer rolls the game back and erases them (#64).
• A follower that missed the last call before a game closed now recovers it: the host stays around to answer, keeps answering until the final state is through, and History ends up with the full result (#65, #74).
• Handing a game over is reliable: a recipient that missed a call before the handoff, or the handoff message itself, still takes over; the old host resends until the new host's first card and refuses to call meanwhile (#66, #75).
• Logging in on an alt no longer rejoins the main's games; joined games are saved per character (#67).
• A join whose request or welcome was lost is asked again, a few times, before the addon says it could not join (#68).
• /dea undo on a square that was never called no longer calls it (#69).
• The chip and the toast anchor come back where they were dragged after a reload (#71).
• CI fails when the headless client smoke fails (#70).
addons.description:
Raid Bingo, played inside World of Warcraft: Forever. One person starts a game and calls the
squares, everyone gets the same 24 squares in a different order, and every board ticks over
live. The same rules as raidbingo.com, without leaving the game.

Made for the Drip Enforcement Agency, and it works for any guild or group.
Playing
• Open the window with the minimap button, /dea, or the addon compartment.
• Start a game from the Games tab: give it a title, pick who can join (your guild
anywhere, or whoever is grouped with you), fill the 24 squares by pasting a list or
starting from a previous game, and open it.
• Join a game from the toast that appears when someone opens one, or from the Games tab.
• Calling: the host, and anyone the host lets call, clicks a square to call it. Clicking
a called square undoes it, and an undo leaves no trace; nothing asks for confirmation,
since any call can be undone and redone. There is also an alphabetical caller list with
a filter under the calls panel.
• Five in a row wins. The night continues past the first bingo; winners are ranked by time.
• The chip at the top of the screen keeps the score while the window is closed. Nothing
pops or makes a sound during combat.
• History keeps the last 20 finished games readable. Options has the theme, sounds,
the chip and the minimap button.
What it shares and keeps
Squares usually name real guildmates, so it is worth knowing where they go.
• Opening a game broadcasts it. The title, all 24 squares and the list of players go to
everyone who can hear the game. In Guild mode, the default, that is every guild member
online, in the raid or not. In Raid mode it is everyone grouped with you, pugs included.
Pick Raid mode only when the squares are fit for strangers.
• Nothing is ever posted to chat. Everything travels on the addon channel, which only
other copies of the addon read. Players without the addon see nothing.
• Kept on this computer, in the game's SavedVariables files in plain text: every set of
squares you have hosted or played, the last 20 finished games with each player's character
name and bingo time, and the games you have been offered. Tools that back up or sync your
WTF folder carry these along. Deleting the addon's SavedVariables file clears them.

releases.changelog:
v0.1.5 (2026-10-09)
Everything in v0.1.5-beta1, plus the fixes from a code review of the protocol and persistence:
• A character whose name merely extends ours ("Dea Onex", "Deaone", or our first name alone) can no longer replay our hello and become our identity, taking our hosted games' ownership with it (#62, #72). On classic realms the realm is part of the identity too (#76).
• Another host can no longer poison a game's squares by announcing a set under that game's hash: a set is trusted only when its hash comes out of its content and it came from the game's own host, in memory and in the saved library (#63, #73).
• A snapshot that arrives after newer calls no longer rolls the game back and erases them (#64).
• A follower that missed the last call before a game closed now recovers it: the host stays around to answer, keeps answering until the final state is through, and History ends up with the full result (#65, #74).
• Handing a game over is reliable: a recipient that missed a call before the handoff, or the handoff message itself, still takes over; the old host resends until the new host's first card and refuses to call meanwhile (#66, #75).
• Logging in on an alt no longer rejoins the main's games; joined games are saved per character (#67).
• A join whose request or welcome was lost is asked again, a few times, before the addon says it could not join (#68).
• /dea undo on a square that was never called no longer calls it (#69).
• The chip and the toast anchor come back where they were dragged after a reload (#71).
• CI fails when the headless client smoke fails (#70).

v0.1.5-beta1 (2026-10-09)
• The game tab can also shrink in height, to 440; the other tabs keep the full minimum and the window grows back on leaving the game tab (#61).

v0.1.4 (2026-10-09)
• Addon messages sent while the Forever client is in a chat lockdown (encounters) wait in a queue and go out, in order, when it lifts; only the newest heartbeat per game is kept. /dea status says whether the lockdown is on and how many messages wait (#43).
• A send made in the second after a lockdown lifts no longer overtakes the messages still held (#45).
• The queue keeps the newest heartbeat, hello and sync request per destination, and no longer lets a whispered heartbeat evict the broadcast one (#46).
• One held message failing to send no longer loses the ones behind it (#47).
• A held group message goes out on the channel the group has when it leaves, not the one it had when it was held (#48).
• During a lockdown a follower no longer marks the host away or reports a held call request as lost; the timers restart when it lifts (#44).
• A join request held through a lockdown still gets its welcome accepted when it finally goes out (#49).
• A sender or guild roster name the client hands over as a secret value no longer reaches the debug tap or the roster match (#52).
• The window built by a reload mid-fight comes up dimmed and unclickable, like one that saw the fight start (#53).
• In combat the window's header stays live: the close button and the title-bar drag work while the rest is dimmed (#54).
• A text box that had the keyboard when combat started lets it go, so keys reach the game again (#55).
• A confirmation card closes with the window (Escape, a reload) and when combat starts, instead of staying up with a stale action behind its button (#56).
• Calls that land in a burst after a fight make one tick, not one per call; a bingo always sounds (#57).
• A send the client refuses for a lockdown that began after the check, or that the chat library had already spooled, goes back to the front of the queue; /dea net counts refusals and /dea debug shows the client's result code (#50).
• The queue also drains the moment the client reports the restriction over, not only on the next tick (#51).
• The game tab can shrink to the board alone: below the full width the standings and calls rail hides and the board takes the window; the other tabs keep the full minimum and widen the window back (#59).
• A hello held through a lockdown still teaches the client its own server-side name from the echo when it finally goes out (#60).

v0.1.3 (2026-10-09)
• Standings: each player on two lines, the whole name (Forever names are two words) then the meter and the CALLER flag, so rows no longer collide (#40).
• Hover a player in the standings to see their grid as dots, like the chip's: called squares lit, a winning line brighter. Positions only, never their square text (#41).
• Calling: a caller's click calls the square, a click on a called square undoes it, with no confirmation; any call can be undone and redone. Others still click a square to read its full text (#42).

v0.1.2 (2026-10-09)
• Version shown on the Options tab and in the minimap tooltip, with a note on the Options tab when a newer release is around.
• Resizing the window: the History and Games lists now widen with it, and the Options rows no longer lose their hints and buttons.
• The website's footer one-liners, retold for the addon, in the window footer on the Games, History and Options tabs. A new one every 30 seconds.

addons.description:
Steam Deck presets for World of Warcraft: Forever. Pick a preset, keep it or let it revert
after 15 seconds, done. Every preset was measured on a Steam Deck OLED: frame rate, 1% lows and
battery draw, in the open world and in a capital.

Designed to go with the DeckForever app, which installs
Battle.net and WoW: Forever on the Steam Deck, adds them to the Steam library, and can repair, back
up or uninstall the setup. The app gets the game running; this addon tunes it. The addon also works
on its own if you set up the game another way.
Presets
| Preset | Frame rate | What you get | Deck TDP limit | Battery life* |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Battery | 30 fps | lightest look, steady everywhere, even in cities | 8–10 W | ~4.3 h |
| Balanced | 45 fps | Battery plus real shadows and shading | 10 W | ~3.7 h |
| Max FPS | 60 fps | sharp, longer view, full power (cities ~50 fps) | Off | ~2.8 h |
| Max Quality | 30 fps | everything high: lighting, shadows, reflections. Plug in; not for cities | Off | ~2.5 h |

\*Steam Deck OLED, questing. Capitals are limited by power on any handheld; Battery at 30 fps is
the preset that stays smooth there.
Features
• Controller friendly. D-pad moves a focus ring, A selects, B closes, shoulders switch tabs.
Large buttons, no dropdowns, nothing that needs hovering.
• Safe to try. Your own settings are saved before the first preset; Restore previous puts
them back. Each apply shows a 15-second Keep / Revert dialog. Nothing is changed in combat.
• Customize any preset setting with steppers that use the game's own names. Changes show in
gold; one button resets a preset.
• Steam Deck tab: the Quick Access settings (refresh rate, frame limit, TDP) that go with each
preset. An addon can't change those, so the tab tells you what to set.
• UI scale for the 7-inch screen. The game locks its own UI Scale option in Forever; the addon
scales the interface instead.
• Reload UI button in the window, and a minimap button with a quick menu.
• Raid and battleground settings (a separate set in the game) follow the preset, a notch lower.
Commands
| Command | |
|---|---|
| /deckforever | Open the window |
| /deckforever apply battery\|balanced\|performance\|quality | Apply a preset (performance is Max FPS, quality is Max Quality) |
| /deckforever restore | Back to your own settings from before the first preset |
| /deckforever preview
| List what a preset would change |
| /deckforever customize [preset] / deck [preset] | Open the Customize / Steam Deck tab |
| /deckforever set
/ reset
[setting] | Override or reset preset values |
| /deckforever uiscale \|default | Interface size (about 0.75 suits the Deck) |
| /deckforever minimap on\|off, raid on\|off, reminder on\|off\| | Options |
| /deckforever fps, status, help | Information |

addons.description:
Addon for World of Warcraft Forever (classic 1.x-line client, v1.60.1)
that covers spider models with a nameplate-attached UI element. UI-layer
only: no model swaps, no game-file modification. Covers are always
click-through and always fully opaque.

Status: v1.1.0. This README documents current behavior only; the
change history lives in Git.
How it works
• Every cover is a child of the spider's nameplate, so native plate
movement and scale carry the cover between polling ticks. No targeting,
mouseover or input is needed; tracking is on by default.
• Cover size is a percentage of the nameplate width (/as scale,
whole number 40–130, 100 = default).
• Near-field boost (automatic): the client holds nameplate apparent
size in a narrow band (~73–90 UI px) while the model keeps growing as
you close in, so a plate-proportional cover would under-cover close
spiders. Every 10 Hz tick multiplies the tracked size by a smooth ramp
of the plate's apparent width: no boost at/under 75 UI px, full ×3.0 at/
above 85 UI px. There is no setting to change it; /as debug on shows
the per-plate values on the AS| near: line.
• When the client removes a dead unit's nameplate, the cover goes with
it. When the addon observes an accessible spider death, a centered,
click-through LOOK AWAY warning appears for 1.75 seconds. It warns
that the corpse may be visible; it does not cover the body.

addons.description:
everbuff.gg WoW addon
Gameplay recording for data nerds.

The in-game half of everbuff.gg. It records your WoW run the way a flight
recorder records a flight: every fight with a replay you can scrub, every pickup with where it came from,
every death with what killed you, every quest, standing and skill point, and where your gold went. Nothing
to start or stop. Play, and it fills in.
What you get
Five tabs, one question each. No tab is named after a data type.

| Tab | The question | What is in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Home | How is my run going? | Level, XP per hour and time to level, gold per hour, time played, the story of this session, and one row per play session with XP and gold bars |
| Combat | What happened when I fought? | Dungeon runs boss by boss, every fight with a scrubber that shows your buffs, your group's buffs, the monsters' buffs, gear and items used at any second, and every death with the corpse run and gear lost |
| Loot | What did I get? | Every pickup with its source (the mob, the node, the object, the mail, the auction) and the map coordinates, a by-item view, gold in and out down to repairs, flights and postage, and your auctions: what you posted at what price, what sold and for how much after the house cut, what you bought, what came back |
| Character | How is my character growing? | Quests done and in progress with where you did them, standing with every faction, professions with skill bars and milestones, and crafting: every item you made with the profession and where you made it, every recipe learned |
| Settings | | The on-screen flag, notifications, capture health, disconnect protection, stored data |

The flag in the corner is the part the everbuff desktop app reads: it marks the moments in your video
recording. Drag it anywhere, right-click to snap it to a corner, size and fade it in Settings.
Why an addon and not just a combat log
The combat log knows damage. It does not know your level, your gold, what you looted or from where, what
you were wearing, which potion you drank, what your party's buffs were at the second the tank died, or
where on the map any of it happened. This addon records all of that, timestamped to the same clock as the
combat log and the video, so the desktop app can put the three together.

It also handles the awkward client. On the Midnight and "WoW Forever" builds most combat values are
Secret Values that addons cannot read, and the client hides your own buffs a few seconds into every fight.
The recorder is built around that: identities that survive hiding, guards that never record a phantom buff
loss, and a replay that bridges any gap. Verified against real fights.

addons.changelog:
For players
Get the Everloot addon and installation instructions

Version 0.3.10 records item tooltip stats, NPC services and gathering locations for the player-built database. The desktop companion can also supply public drop-source information for item tooltips.

Compatibility: targets WoW: Forever. The raid buff list uses game build 1.60.1.70532. These changes have not yet been verified in the live Forever client; treat this as a test release and report problems through GitHub or Discord.

You can already use the free talent calculators and raid planner in your browser.
Detailed changesAdded
• Addon, protocol and site: item numbers players see. When the game shows an item's tooltip, the addon records
its armor, block, damage per second, stats and resistances for the plain item, with the client build (record
kind item_fact, protocol package 1.15.0, record protocol 1.8.0). The item page, the site's hover card and the
embeddable card show a number in place of its [?] once three installs on the newest build agree, with the
installs, the build and when it was last seen; a line installs disagree on stays [?] and says so. MCP tools
are unchanged. Not yet run in the Forever client.
• Addon and desktop app: item tooltips show where an item drops. The Desktop App writes the public drop rates
(three installs looted the source) into the EverlootPrices file beside the prices, at most once a day; the
tooltip and /everloot price show up to three sources as drops of loot windows, with installs and the upload
date. With the file in the game, a missing price or drop source is said in one grey line. Nothing new is
written to SavedVariables. Design: docs/design/specs/2026-10-21-addon-value-loop-design.md.
• Places for the world map. When an NPC's window opens (merchant, gossip, quest, trainer, flight map, bank,
auction house, stable, innkeeper) the addon records where you stand as that NPC's place, with the service the
window offered, once per NPC, service and zone. When you loot a herb, ore vein, chest or other object, its loot
row gets where you stand, how you opened it (from the spell you cast) and the object's name. Trainer rows name
the trainer. Event names and spell arguments not yet seen on the Forever client are read defensively: a missing
one records nothing. Launch-day checks: docs/2026-10-21-addon-0.3.10-launch-checklist.md.
Changed
• Targeting or mousing over the same NPC at the same spot (to 1 unit on the map's 0 to 100 scale) records it
once, not every time. NPC window rows and object loot rows have their own 2,000-row room, apart from
targeting rows and creature loot, so a full targeting or corpse share pauses only itself.
• An object's name comes only from a herb, ore or chest cast, never from another spell's target (such as a
player you healed). A fishing cast counts for 30 seconds, for a slow bite.
• The raid buff list (/everloot raid) is read from the game files of build 1.60.1.70532.

What's Changed
Other changes
• data(kb): new blue posts and builds by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/278
• data(kb): refresh GitHub facts for the ecosystem tracker by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/268
• fix(web): one row per announcement on /changes, with every region it was posted in by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/279
• feat(web): chat keys per provider, and API keys with purpose, scopes and expiry by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/273
• fix(web): weapon damage and per-second lines in item tooltips by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/281
• feat(addon): record NPC positions at service windows and node positions at looting by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/266
• docs(kb): wiki drafts for Forever's new dungeons, Skyborne and the raids by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/275
• chore(desktop): release 0.1.6 by @CDVolvik in https://github.com/Everloot/everloot/pull/282…

Release channel: Alpha

Live-client verification is pending. This is a pre-release for WoW: Forever 1.60.1, not a verified stable build.
None of the changes below has been run in the Forever client yet: the one-line login message, the price-file hint,
the /ask no-answer message, /everloot link, the fuller recipe read and the auction fallback sample still need
an in-game check. The 0.3.14 Home window and the collection checks listed there also remain unverified.
Added
• /everloot link and /everloot link clear, for tying the character you are playing to your everloot.app
account. Linking is not open yet: everloot.app does not hand out link codes, so there is no code to type for now.
The command itself is in place. A code in the right shape (like EL-7K3Q-9P) saves your own character's name,
realm, race, class, level and faction in your Everloot file and asks you to /reload; a code in the wrong shape
is refused. Nothing is sent from the game. /everloot link on its own explains the command and how many link rows
your file holds, and /everloot link clear deletes them all. At most 10 are kept.
Changed
• Logging in or /reload prints one line instead of the full status: the version, how many modules are on and off,
any that could not start and any collection paused at capacity. /everloot status still shows everything.
• /ask messages name the Everloot Desktop App (with Ask turned on) instead of the companion.
• Raid buff data now comes from the game files of build 1.60.1.70707.
Fixed
• Without the Desktop App's price file, item tooltips showed only your own scans and never said why. The first
tooltip now says once per install, in chat, that community prices come from the Everloot Desktop App, and that
/everloot price [item] shows what Everloot has for an item.
• A question asked with /ask that still has no answer two loads later now says so once, and tells you to open the
Everloot Desktop App with Ask turned on (from everloot.app/addon) and /reload. The question stays saved until answered.
• Recipe recording reads the full recipe list when the game offers it, keeps each recipe's id and whether you have
learned it, and no longer counts a recipe you have not learned toward your craftable skill ranges. Your
profession window filters are left as they were. Turning profession collection off also stops a read in progress.
• When an auction scan you start cannot run or times out, Everloot can fall back to a browse search that records
real listing prices as a partial sample, clearly labelled as such. It respects the auction house's query limit,
stops when you close the auction house or turn collection off, and never presents the sample as a full scan.

Changelog
Player-friendly release notes for Craft Alert.
[Unreleased][1.0.0] - 2026-10-30
• First release. Craft Alert watches chat for people asking for something one of your characters can craft and lets you greet them with one click. One folder works on Retail, WoW: Forever and the Classic flavors (Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath, Cata, Mists of Pandaria).
• Open each profession window once and Craft Alert knows that character's recipes, across every character on the account. On Era and TBC that includes Enchanting's craft window.
• Recipes from older expansions start muted: Craft Alert alerts only for the newest expansion's recipes of each profession, and when you first open a profession after a new expansion it switches to that one (your own mutes for that profession are replaced, and a chat line says so). "Only " on the Crafters page does the same on demand.
• A recipe you learn while playing matches right away. On Classic it matches by name until you next open its profession window, which stores it for good.
• Reading profession windows and building the recipe list happen in the background, a little each frame, without stalling the game.
• Craft Alert listens in Trade and Services by default; General, LookingForGroup, Guild and Communities can be turned on where the game has them. "Only where Trade chat exists" keeps it listening wherever you have the Trade channel.
• Requests are matched by item and recipe links, written item names, slot and armor words ("LF plate belt"), and profession words ("LF enchanter", "bs", "jc", "jewelcraft", "leatherwork", "insc"). A line needs a request word: LF, LFC, LFRC, WTB, WTC, need, looking, anyone and a few more by default. Edit the request words and add your own slang in Settings → Keywords.
• "Recraft", "recrafter" and "recrafting" work like "crafter", "leg" works like "legs", "off hand" and "off-hand" name the off hand, and "enchs" names Enchanting.
• A line that names two slots matches either one.
• A request that names a slot without an armor type ("LF belt", "LF head crafter") uses the asker's class, enchant requests excepted: a warrior's request alerts only for plate, a mage's only for cloth. On Forever and Classic the class is read as max level (a level 30 hunter counts as mail).
• A bare "LF crafter" alerts the profession that makes the asker's armor: Blacksmithing for plate, Leatherworking for mail and leather, Tailoring for cloth. It needs profession-word alerts on, and only works for a line that names nothing else: "LF crafter for flask" or "LF crafter, ring" makes no armor guess.
• Ads are left alone: lines with WTS, LFW or "selling", lines with "/w me" but none of LF, LFC, LFRC, WTB or WTC, and "LF work" (but not "LF work order") make no alert. "Trinket" on its own picks no profession; name the trinket instead.
• A toast pops up beside the launcher, on the side facing the middle of the screen, when someone asks for something you can craft. It says what they want and which of your characters can craft it (an alt by name, in its class colour), shows their whole message with item and recipe links you can hover, and what matched in its tooltip. Left-click to greet them, shift-click to edit the greeting first, ctrl-click for an empty whisper, right-click to dismiss; a click on a link only opens the link. A newer request replaces the shown one and counts "+N more". Dragging the toast moves the launcher.

addons.description:
Craft Alert watches Trade chat for people asking for something one of your characters can craft, then shows a toast so you can greet them with one click. Open each profession window once and it knows your recipes across every character on the account. It never whispers on its own: every message comes from your click or keybind. Works on Retail, WoW: Forever, and the Classic flavors (Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath, Cata, MoP) from one folder.
Screenshots
A toast beside the launcher ring when someone asks for something your alt can craft:

The leads window, with the selected request, who can craft it and the greeting that Greet sends:

Hover the day's counts for the last 7 days:

Settings, opened with the gear on the window's title bar. The Crafters page picks a main crafter per profession and mutes recipes:

The same mute switch sits on each recipe in your profession window: click the speaker to mute or unmute it.

With WhisperMessenger installed, the leads move into its Craft Alert tab:
What it does
• Listens in Trade and Services where the game has them (General, LookingForGroup, Guild and Communities can be turned on) for requests such as "LF plate belt", "WTB [item link]" or "LF enchanter".
• Shows a toast beside its launcher ring with what the customer wants and which of your characters can craft it. Left-click greets, shift-click lets you edit the greeting first, ctrl-click opens an empty whisper, right-click dismisses.
• Opens the greeting in the chat box for you to send instead when you are AFK, greet more than six times a minute, greet the same lead twice, or click a lead that just appeared.
• Keeps every open request in a leads window: the list on the left, the selected request in full on the right, with Greet, Whisper and Dismiss buttons.
• Counts the requests you saw, greeted and got a reply from each day, and tells you what came in while you were AFK.
• Picks the best of your characters for each request, and lets you choose a main crafter per profession.
• Turns itself off in dungeons, raids, battlegrounds, arenas and delves.
• With WhisperMessenger installed, the leads move into a WhisperMessenger tab and greetings open as WhisperMessenger conversations.

Changelog
Player-friendly release notes for Craft Alert.
[Unreleased][1.0.0] - 2026-10-30
• First release. Craft Alert watches chat for people asking for something one of your characters can craft and lets you greet them with one click. One folder works on Retail, WoW: Forever and the Classic flavors (Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath, Cata, Mists of Pandaria).
• Open each profession window once and Craft Alert knows that character's recipes, across every character on the account. On Era and TBC that includes Enchanting's craft window.
• Recipes from older expansions start muted: Craft Alert alerts only for the newest expansion's recipes of each profession, and when you first open a profession after a new expansion it switches to that one (your own mutes for that profession are replaced, and a chat line says so). "Only " on the Crafters page does the same on demand.
• A recipe you learn while playing matches right away. On Classic it matches by name until you next open its profession window, which stores it for good.
• Reading profession windows and building the recipe list happen in the background, a little each frame, without stalling the game.
• Craft Alert listens in Trade and Services by default; General, LookingForGroup, Guild and Communities can be turned on where the game has them. "Only where Trade chat exists" keeps it listening wherever you have the Trade channel.
• Requests are matched by item and recipe links, written item names, slot and armor words ("LF plate belt"), and profession words ("LF enchanter", "bs", "jc", "jewelcraft", "leatherwork", "insc"). A line needs a request word: LF, LFC, LFRC, WTB, WTC, need, looking, anyone and a few more by default. Edit the request words and add your own slang in Settings → Keywords.
• "Recraft", "recrafter" and "recrafting" work like "crafter", "leg" works like "legs", "off hand" and "off-hand" name the off hand, and "enchs" names Enchanting.
• A line that names two slots matches either one.
• A request that names a slot without an armor type ("LF belt", "LF head crafter") uses the asker's class, enchant requests excepted: a warrior's request alerts only for plate, a mage's only for cloth. On Forever and Classic the class is read as max level (a level 30 hunter counts as mail).

addons.description:
The mouseover tooltip you already know, with the info you actually want, and nothing that slows your game down.

Why players install it
• See what matters at a glance. Item level, Mythic+ rating and best key, the mount they're riding, who they're targeting.
• Quest mobs tell you what's left. "6/10 Boar slain (4 left)", finished objectives in green.
• It stays out of the way. Blizzard's tooltip look, no extra frames, no libraries. Disabled options do no work at all.
• Hide tooltips in combat and hold Shift when you do want one.

Plays nice with other addons: the lines on the right come from AllTheThings.
Settings
Options > AddOns > Mouseover Tooltip, or type /mot. Every line can be turned on or off. The panel's Defaults button resets everything.

The minimap button opens the same panel; drag it to move it around the minimap.
Game versions
Retail, Classic Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, Mists Classic and WoW: Forever. Features a game version doesn't have (Mythic+, PvP rating, some inspect data) are hidden there.
Performance
• No per-frame updates: the tooltip follows the cursor using the game's own anchoring.
• Other players are inspected at most once every 1.5 seconds, and results are kept for 5 minutes (up to 100 players, never saved to disk).
• Events are listened to only while they are needed.

• First release: choose how many raid groups share one line, and the rest wrap onto a new line.

addons.description:
Blizzard's raid frames, but eight groups no longer stretch across your whole screen.
Why players install it
• Pick how many groups sit on one line. Four groups per row turns one long strip into a tidy 4×2 block.
• It's Blizzard's raid frames. Same frames, same order, same spacing. Only the line breaks change.
• Works both ways. Groups side by side wrap into new rows; stacked groups wrap into new columns.
• Nothing to learn. The slider sits right under the Raid Frames settings in Edit Mode.
ScreenshotsSettings
1. Open Edit Mode and click the Raid Frames.
2. Pick one of the Separate Groups layouts.
3. Use the Groups Per Row (or Groups Per Column) slider under the settings window.
Tick Odds / Evens to put odd groups first, then even groups, wrapped at your per-row setting (for example 1-3-5-7 over 2-4-6-8 at 4 per row, or 1-3-2-4 in a 20-player raid).

8 is Blizzard's normal layout. Your choice is saved for all your characters.

Combine Groups layouts already have Blizzard's own Row Size option, so the slider only shows for Separate Groups.
In combat
WoW doesn't let addons move raid frames during combat. If your raid changes mid-fight, or you open Edit Mode in combat, Blizzard's layout shows until combat ends, then your layout comes back on its own. The slider is greyed out while you're in combat.
Game versions
Retail and WoW: Forever.
Performance
• No per-frame updates and no timers: it only runs when the game itself rearranges the raid frames.
• At 8 groups per line it does nothing at all.
• No libraries.

Changelog
Player-friendly release notes for ShoulderCam. This file covers the current 1.x series; older series live in archive/changelog/.

All releases: 1.0.x (current) · 0.1.x
[Unreleased][1.0.0] - 2026-10-15
• Options are now one page with tabs, plain-English names, a description when you hover any option, and units on sliders.
addons.description:
Over-the-shoulder action camera with separate on foot, combat and mounted setups, and nothing that slows your game down.

Why players install it
• The game's own action camera, tamed. Shoulder offset, enemy and interact focus, dynamic pitch, all from the normal options window.
• A camera for every situation. On foot, Combat and Mounted each get their own shoulder offset, focus, pitch and zoom distance. The camera switches by itself when you mount up or enter combat.
• Smooth moves. The camera glides to each mode's zoom distance and slides over to the shoulder instead of snapping.
• Remembers your zoom. Scroll to a distance you like and that mode keeps it.
• No nag popup. The "experimental feature" warning stays away.
• It stays out of the way. No per-frame updates, no libraries. Timers run only while the camera is moving.
Settings
Options > AddOns > Shoulder Cam, or type /shouldercam (or /shc). Every change takes effect immediately. Hover any option to see what it does.
• General tab: turn the addon on or off, zoom speeds, max camera distance and shoulder offset.
• Camera feel tab: how strongly the camera turns toward your target and tilts.
• On foot, Combat and Mounted tabs: each situation's own camera. Druid travel forms can count as mounted.

The Defaults button resets everything. Key bindings (Options > Keybindings > Shoulder Cam): Toggle Shoulder Cam and Swap shoulder. The addon menu button on the minimap (Retail) opens the settings too.

A Shoulder Cam button on the minimap edge opens the settings with a left-click and turns the camera on or off with a right-click. Drag it to move it around the minimap. Untick Show minimap button on the General tab to hide it.

Using ActionCamPlus? Turn it off first: both addons change the same camera settings.
Game versions
Retail, Classic Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, Mists Classic and WoW: Forever. If a game version has no action camera, Shoulder Cam does nothing and says so on its settings page.

• No per-frame updates: zoom uses the game's own camera movement, and the shoulder slide runs on a short timer that stops when it arrives.
• Mount and combat events are listened to only while that mode is turned on.
• Switching modes changes only the camera settings that actually differ.
• Each settings tab is built the first time you open it.

addons.changelog:
A recent WoW Forever client update stopped the companion from starting combat logging inside dungeons. This release fixes it.

What changed
• Start logging works again inside dungeons. The button used to run /combatlog for you, which the new client now ignores inside instances. It now starts logging directly.
• It keeps trying until logging sticks. Right after a loading screen the client ignores logging requests for a few seconds (about 10 in Ragefire Chasm). The addon retries for up to 30 seconds and tells you if logging still did not start.
• Correct on/off state. The addon no longer thinks logging is on after you turned it off with /combatlog.
• Asks again when you walk back in. Leaving a dungeon and re-entering shows the start prompt again, and the stop prompt only shows once.
• New /flc trace shows why it did or didn't start logging, handy if a future client patch changes things again.

Install: extract the zip into Interface\AddOns\ and /reload.
addons.description:
Automatic /combatlog for WoW Forever

Starts combat logging when you enter a dungeon or raid, so every run is ready to upload to foreverlogs.gg.

What it does
• Asks before it starts. Entering a monitored dungeon or raid pops up
Start /combatlog?. Say no and nothing is written.
• Asks before it stops. Leaving a zone where it started logging asks
whether to stop or keep going (handy between pulls and dungeons).
• Silent mode. Skip both prompts: logging starts on zone entry and stays
on until you turn it off yourself.
• Keeps trying until it sticks. Right after you load into a dungeon, WoW
Forever ignores logging requests for a few seconds (about 10 in Ragefire
Chasm). The addon retries for up to 30 seconds and tells you if logging
still did not start.
• Turns on Advanced Combat Logging. Without it the combat log has no gear,
talents or stats, and your reports show no specs or item levels.
• Leaves your own logging alone. If you already typed /combatlog, it
never switches it off.

It does not read the combat log or send anything anywhere. It only switches
the client's log writer on and off, the same as typing /combatlog.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft add-on for the guild's member database and Fellowship roster: who each player is, which characters are their mains and alts, and the alias they choose to be called. It supports WoW Forever and WoW Retail from one source tree.
