Forever 0.9.89 / Retail 0.9.102-retail

Syncs the cast prediction tables with WoW: Forever build 1.60.1.70753 (the live build before launch; read from the client's DB2 tables) and Blizzard's launch notes of 3 Nov. Spell numbers that come from tooltips update by themselves.
• Arcane Blast: its buff is now 12% of Intellect as spell power per stack, which the spell power API already holds, so the +10% a stack multiplier is removed. Arcane Blast's own spell coefficient follows the new client data (0.714 to 0.429).
• Lava Burst (the +20% against Flame Shock, Call of Flame) and Piercing Ice are removed together with the spell and the talent.
• Fire Power is held back: it is now 3% per Fire effect on the target, up to 12%, and counting those effects is not read yet.
• Ice Barrier: Frigid Power (+15% Frost for a minute) and the shield's own +5% are read, on Forever only. Power in Light also counts Shadow Word: Pain. Fingers of Frost is x4 (still not applied until verified).
• Shadow and Flame stays at the client's 2% a point. Blizzard announced 4% for launch; it is added once a build or a live description shows it.
• Retail behaviour is unchanged; its package only carries the version bump and the shared files.

Verification: compiled both packages under Lua 5.1, ran a mock of the aura and talent tables, checked the regenerated coefficient table against the repo file entry by entry, and had the change reviewed twice by an independent hostile review. Both ZIPs were verified against source. Not tested in game.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload (a full restart for new files). SHA-256 checksums are attached.

Forever 0.9.88 / Retail 0.9.101-retail
• Parse German and English food descriptions that restore a percentage of health and mana over time as percentage healing, not a flat healing amount. Flat-value item healing is unchanged.

Verification: exercised the real item parser and ComputeItem path with readable and hidden maximum-health values; compiled the changed Lua files and verified both ZIPs against source. Not yet confirmed in-game.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload. SHA-256 checksums are attached.

Forever 0.9.87 / Retail 0.9.100-retail
• Fix cast impact/calibration identity, stale overlays and nameplate recycling; keep hidden native healing values intact.
• Track targeted Renew, Rejuvenation, Regrowth, Riptide and Wild Growth estimates independently of SpellDamageInfo display settings. Different ranks refresh one effect instead of adding duplicates.
• Preserve readable healing power at login, equipment/player-aura changes and leaving combat, including when SpellDamageInfo is disabled. Fixes the first combat HoT losing its precombat bonus.
• Do not invent selected-target HoTs for Lightwell clicks, Tranquility/Mend Pet channels or conditional heals.
• Binding Heal uses the correct spell-power coefficient per recipient. Holy Shock, Penance and Holy Nova show both damage and healing labels. Dark Sacrifice shows health cost, mana gain and cost duration.
• Penance damage uses its described three-bolt schedule; the immediate bolt is already spent. Channel timing changes update remaining bolts; unknown linked coefficients are not invented.
• Correct DoT API snapshots, parser diagnostics, custom-frame resolution and passive quest reward eligibility.

Verification: compared 3052 EN/DE client descriptions and 6104 cast-view variants; exercised real Lua event handlers and before/after failure cases. All 52 Lua files compile under Lua 5.1; both ZIPs checked member-by-member against committed source. No unit-test files added.

Limitations: no in-game confirmation. HoT dispels, talent-modified healing and exact/group Wild Growth effects remain unverified or unsupported. Wild Growth is a linear estimate on the known primary target only. If healing power has never been readable this session, only description amounts are available. Native direct-heal projections are unchanged.

Replace the entire UsefulPlatesAndTooltips addon folder with the appropriate ZIP and /reload. Settings are preserved. SHA-256 checksums are in SHA256SUMS.txt.

Forever 0.9.85 / Retail 0.9.98-retail

A Retail fix: the cast marker and the kill icon no longer promise the damage a physical shot loses to the target's armor.

CastPrediction (Retail)
• A Retail description holds your own numbers (spell power, talents) but not the target's armor, which takes a share off a direct physical hit and cannot be read for an enemy. The saved Retail log of a hunter shows it: Steady Shot read 86 and hit for 60, 61 and 60; read 101 and hit for 69; read 115 and hit for 80 and 81. That is 0.70 of the description every time (mean 0.698, spread 0.008), so the marker and the kill icon promised 30% more than the shot dealt.
• Retail now learns from non-crit direct physical hits, with the same running mean Forever uses (about nine hits' memory, shown pulled toward the description by two hits' worth). On Lua mocks that run the real Core.lua in Retail mode, a shot that reads 86 and hits for 60-61 shows 86 on the first cast, then 77, 73 and 69 on the second, third and fifth, 65 on the tenth and 63 from the twentieth. Casts of a spell whose hits never come within reach of the estimate (heavier armor than the learning window takes: under about 0.65) are tallied; /upt castpred learned lists them.
• Magic is not reduced by armor and stays as the description says: nothing is learned from it on Retail. Forever is unchanged (every school learns, as before).
• Learn from hits (/upt cast) switches it off; Reset forgets what was learned. The learned factors are shared by every character of the account.

DoTInfo
• The log of unread descriptions (kept to help clients in other languages) skips texts without a number: a DoT's text always has one, and lines like "Summon a chauffeur" pushed useful lines out of the 500-line log.

What was looked at on Retail and needed nothing
• The saved BugGrabber errors: four, none from this addon.
• A rogue run in the DoTInfo log (Garrote, then Rupture at 5 combo points; both estimates ran down together and were removed once the target was out of combat and no longer carried them): nothing in it looks wrong.
• The 47 German texts the action bar numbers once could not read: the current parser reads the three that carry an amount of your own damage or healing (Rupture, Crimson Vial, Recuperate); the other 44 are utility, crowd control, defensive cooldowns given in percent, pet heals as a share of the pet's health and a healthstone item.

What is not verified
• The armor learning has not been seen in the game; it was checked with Lua mocks that drive the real Core.lua in Retail and Forever mode, and the 0.70 comes from one hunter's saved log (six hits). Spells that hit several times, and pets or auto attacks of the same school landing within the 1.5 s window of a cast, can pull a factor the way they can on Forever.
• No unit tests were created or modified; every TOC-listed file compiles under Lua 5.1 (91 across the two packages).

Replace the whole UsefulPlatesAndTooltips folder (Forever ZIP for _classic_beta_, Retail ZIP for retail) and restart the game or /reload. Settings are preserved. SHA-256 checksums are in SHA256SUMS.txt.

addons.description:
Quest text you can read is already here. This is the part you can listen to: the
German a quest giver hands you, spoken, and any single word out loud when you
click it.

Current packaging: two quest narration archives and word audio inside the
German Dictionary. The delivery contains 237,278 quest master clips and 121,904
word clips. Counts and measurements below describe the original generation
baseline; see Packaging and the delivery reports for the current layout.
Why it has to be pre-generated
The WoW client cannot synthesise speech. There is no API for it and no way to
reach one from an addon. Everything the pack says has to be generated in
advance, encoded as Ogg Vorbis, and shipped as files the client plays with
PlaySoundFile.

That decides the shape of the project. It is not an addon with a tool beside it;
it is a generation pipeline whose output happens to be an addon.
Historical measured baseline
Measured, not estimated, against the German corpus in
WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-DE:

| | clips | audio |
|---|---:|---:|
| quest passages — offer, progress, hand-in | 237,264 | 281.3 h |
| dictionary words | 104,274 | 28.8 h |
| total | 341,538 | 310.1 h |

Objectives and quest titles are not in it. Nobody says them out loud — they are
read off the screen.

The clip count is sentences, not passages: there are 71,775 passages, and each
is cut into one clip per sentence so a reading can be followed, paused and
resumed a sentence at a time.

Both hour figures are measured rather than projected, which they did not use to
be. The quest hours are the sum of every value in the eleven packs' own duration
tables; the word hours are read off the clips themselves. The table used to say
368 h and 397 h, extrapolated from the 107,489 clips that existed at the time at
5.59 s each — the finished corpus averages 4.27 s, and carrying the early mean
across the rest is where the extra 87 hours came from. It also said no word had
been spoken yet, which stopped being true the day the word pack was committed.

At the pace an RTX 4090 runs the reader, that is days of generation, not weeks,
and it only has to happen once. Afterwards each run does the new quests and
whatever text Blizzard rewrote.
Choosing the reader
Four readers were measured on the same fifty real passages, with the same
reference recording, and the output transcribed back with Whisper and compared
to the text it was given. That number is what a listener hears as a fault: a
reader that stutters gains a word, one that gives up loses several.

| reader | word error | insertions | word for word |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chatterbox Multilingual 0.1.7 | 23.5% | 16.2% | 24 of 50 |
| Chatterbox Multilingual V3 | 11.6% | 2.2% | 23 of 50 |
| Qwen3-TTS 1.7B | 9.2% | 4.1% | 36 of 50 |
| Voxtral 4B | — | — | chosen on listening |

Insertions is where the fault this project kept hitting lands: a reader given
a single word says it and then carries on inventing sentences, because nothing
in a one-word prompt tells it to stop. The dictionary is 104,274 single words,
so that column decides more than the first one does.

Two things came out of the measuring that were not about the models at all.
The references were being destroyed before the reader ever saw them — a
silenceremove filter set to remove pauses was also removing the quiet parts of
words, so "ich habe sie bei einem Absturz verloren" reached the reader as
"...bei einem Absturz". Repairing that halved Chatterbox's rambling on its own.
And a reference cut off mid-sentence made Qwen finish the sentence before
starting the one it was asked for, which looked exactly like a model defect and
was not.

Voxtral 4B (Mistral, March 2026) is what ships. It is twice the size of the
next largest, German is one of nine languages rather than one of twenty-five,
and it was chosen by ear against the others on the same lines.

Its licence is CC-BY-NC-4.0, inherited from the voice datasets it was…

addons.description:
VendorGuardKnow before you buy.
Vendor highlights and compact gear comparisons for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Version: 0.3.1 · Game version: 1.60.1 · Interface: 16001 · Dependencies: None

Releases · Report an issue

VendorGuard adds subtle color fills to the default merchant window so you can spot unmet requirements, unrelated profession tools, and lower weapon DPS before spending your money. Optional comparison labels put the numbers directly beside vendor items. Open settings with the minimap button or /vg.
See it in action
| Mage: weapon comparisons | Hunter: ranged comparisons |
| --- | --- |
| | |
| Walking Stick shows +1.5 DPS against the equipped staff. Stiletto shows its own 3.3 DPS because switching to a dagger changes the weapon setup. | Lower-DPS bows show negative comparisons. Quivers and ammo pouches are usable; guns this character cannot currently use remain red. |

| Mage: bags and ammunition | Your settings |
| --- | --- |
| | |
What the colors mean
| Color | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 🔴 Red | An unmet proficiency, class restriction, or other requirement. Also flags arrows, bullets, and ammo bags for classes that do not use them. |
| 🟠 Orange | Lower weapon DPS, a missing skill requirement, or a specialty bag/basic tool for a profession you do not have. |
| 🟡 Yellow | Higher character level is the only detected obstacle. |
| 🟢 Green | Gear or a bag you can use now. Green is not an overall upgrade rating. |

Requirement warnings take priority over DPS comparisons. Ordinary food and crafting materials stay neutral. Highlights have no added outlines, and VendorGuard never resizes the merchant window or its item rows.
Comparisons at a glance
• +1.5 DPS / -3.1 DPS — weapon-DPS difference against equipped gear when a direct comparison is available.
• 3.3 DPS — the weapon's own DPS, with no gain/loss claim. Used for hand-setup changes, two possible replacement hands, empty slots, or missing equipped data.
• +2 Agi / -1 Sta — a compact stat difference for other comparable equipment.
• L12: … — a comparison preview for an item whose level requirement you have not met.
• No data — a comparison cannot be confirmed. Unreadable equipment is not assumed to be an empty slot, and missing weapon DPS is not described as equal DPS.

Tight rows use compact text such as +1.5DPS. Labels sit beside the price or below the name; if both locations are full, the label is hidden rather than covering existing text. No hover is needed to see a displayed label.

These are base item comparisons, not character-DPS simulations or best-in-slot scores. Abilities, procs, set bonuses, and stat weights are not scored. If a weapon can replace either equipped hand, a DPS loss against either hand can trigger orange. Unknown DPS is never treated as zero.

Full stat-comparison tooltips are left to your other addons. VendorGuard adds only its requirement and warning explanations on hover. Pawn is not required or used.
Profession and ammunition checks
Specialty bags warn orange when you lack their associated profession. Leatherworking storage bags accept either Skinning or Leatherworking. Ordinary bags do not require the profession that crafted them.

Basic tools are checked by item ID, not by matching words in their names:

| Tool | Relevant profession |
| --- | --- |
| Mining Pick | Mining |
| Skinning Knife | Skinning |
| Blacksmith Hammer | Blacksmithing or Engineering |

These basic tools do not display combat-DPS labels or receive DPS downgrade warnings. The orange warning indicates usefulness; it does not claim the tool is impossible to equip. Unknown profession data is not treated as a missing profession.

Quivers, ammo pouches, arrows, and bullets are recognized for Hunters, Warriors, and Rogues. Other current classes receive red warnings. Weapon training and item requirements still apply. This follows Forever's bow, crossbow, and gun data.

• Blacksmith Hammer recognizes either Blacksmithing or Engineering; leatherworking bags recognize either Skinning or Leatherworking.
Beta limits
Green means usable, not best-in-slot. Weapon DPS is a base item comparison, not a character-DPS simulation. Hand-setup changes and ambiguous replacement slots show the weapon's own DPS when available. Full stat-comparison tooltips are left to other addons. The tooltip-DPS fallback supports English clients; replacement merchant interfaces and other WoW clients have not been validated.

Validated with 118 automated tests, plus user testing on Mage and Hunter characters. The install ZIP contains only the six runtime addon files.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that learns how your spells scale with spell power, attack
power and your other stats while you play. It then writes the coefficients into your spell
tooltips, the way modern games show them:

> Hurls a fiery ball that causes 87 to 96 (42.9% Fire SP) Fire damage and an additional 36 (20% Fire SP) Fire damage over 4 sec.

Nothing is datamined or hardcoded. Every number is worked out from your own character, so it
stays correct as Blizzard tunes spells during the beta.
Why it works this way
Forever runs retail's Midnight-era addon rules. Addons can't read the combat log, and damage
numbers are hidden from them, so "watch the damage and work backwards" isn't possible.

Forever's spell tooltips are live, though: the numbers in them already include your current
spell power. So whenever your stats change (gear, buffs, levels), SpellScale reads the
description of every spell in your spellbook and talent tree, and stores the numbers next to a
snapshot of your stats. That turns out to be better than damage logs anyway. Tooltips have no
crits, resists or random damage rolls in them, just rounding.
How it learns
Every number in a tooltip is a formula, base + coefficient × stat, rounded to a whole number.
For each stat it might depend on, SpellScale works out the exact range of coefficients that
reproduces every reading it has seen. For example:
• Your spell power goes from 100 to 105 and Fireball goes from 150 to 152. Rounding could hide
up to a point of difference, so the coefficient is anywhere from about 20% to 60%.
• Your spell power goes from 100 to 300 and Fireball goes from 150 to 236. Now it's between
42.5% and 43.5%.

Each reading narrows the range further. A stat that doesn't explain the numbers runs out of
possible coefficients as soon as your gear moves stats in a different proportion, which is how
the addon tells spell power apart from intellect, healing, and so on.

Many classic spells also gain base damage as you level, until the rank tops out. Your stats
rise at a level-up too, so SpellScale compares readings taken at the same level, and lets the
base step up between levels. It also keeps two rules every tooltip follows: numbers grow with
stats, and a stat can't account for more than the whole number.

The stats it considers: spell power (overall and per school), bonus healing, spell power plus
a third of bonus healing (Forever's healing-to-damage rule), attack power, ranged attack
power, main-hand weapon damage, shield block value, strength, agility, stamina, intellect,
spirit, and character level.
Reading the annotations
| Annotation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| (42.9% SP) | Learned, precise to a tenth of a percent |
| (43% SP) | Learned; your stats haven't spread far enough yet for a decimal |
| (~43% SP) | Still rough (more than ±5%); sharpens as your stats spread out |
| (43% SP?) in gold | It scales, but your gear has only ever moved two stats together (say spell power and healing) |
| (+2.0 per level) | Scales with character level rather than a stat |
| (25% Holy SP + 15% AP) | Scales with two stats at once |

Numbers that don't scale, like durations and ranges, are left alone.
Talents
SpellScale reads your whole talent tree the same way, including talents you haven't taken, so
you can see what a talent scales with before you spend points on it. The annotations show up
in the talent window's tooltips too.
Teaching it faster
• Change one thing at a time. Swap a ring that only has spell power, or take a buff that
only raises intellect. Two readings that differ in just one stat settle the question
immediately.
• At low levels, undress. Taking off all your gear outside combat, then putting it back on,
gives it a zero-spell-power reading next to your geared one. That's the widest spread you
can make, and the spread is what makes the numbers precise.
The browser
Type /ss (or click SpellScale in the minimap's addon menu) to open a window that lists every…

addons.description:
CurseForge
Wago
WoW Interface

SurroundFix is a simple and lightweight AddOn that fixes the problems associated with running WoW at Surround/Eyefinity/Triplewide resolutions!
Features
• Constrains the UI to the middle display
• Automatic vertical resolution detection
• Automatic middle display aspect ratio detection
• Extremely lightweight and simple, every Blizzard UI element acts as if you're just using a single display
• Almost every addon also works, so long as their frame handling is done properly!
• Will do nothing if using a single display, no need to disable it!
• Ability to set a manual aspect ratio for the UI - Want 16:9 on your 21:9 monitor? No problem!

Configure various options with /sfix or /surroundfix. Typing the command will open up the Blizzard AddOn options menu, allowing you to choose Auto or from a selection of common aspect ratios. You can also set a custom aspect with "/sfix aspect x:y". Just type the command and any arguments for more help!

For the curious, the mod essentially resizes the UIParent frame to the resolution of your middle monitor. This means that every UI element and AddOn sees a normal sized display rather than a crazy wide one, so they perfectly orient themselves on the middle display.

This is a much better solution than manually positioning every UI element, and also means that if you switch back to a single display your UI won't break! In fact, it can handle switching between Triplewide and single on the fly!
Known Bugs
• Certain AddOns will not be positioned correctly, and moving them will be strange. Unfortunately there isn't much I can do about this, since it's an issue with how the AddOn causing issues handles it's frames. Any AddOn that is designed to properly use UIParent should have no issues.
• If you for some reason have a 21:9 display with two side 4:3 displays, the UI will be 16:9. It's either this or potentially have issues with bezel correction.
• If the aspect is set to a compact aspect such as 4:3, after a reload the main bar will be anchored to the bottom left of the screen instead of the centre to prevent overlap with the menu bar. If you then change to a wider aspect such as 16:9, the bottom bar will be offset to the left. This is fixed after a /reload, and is behaviour of the default Blizzard UI.
• If a UI element is moved with edit mode, it will no longer obey the UIParent positioning system. This is due to objects positioning themselves relative to "BOTTOM" or "TOP" on UIParent if placed in the corners, resulting in them not being adjusted by SurroundFix. The only workaround is to position them slightly above the bottom or top edges so they anchor to "LEFT" or "RIGHT".

Wanderer Campfire Game 0.3.0
First release, an extension of Wanderer (0.43 or later).
New
• A campfire game in a tall window, read at a glance: the fire always in sight, the tabs at the bottom (the fire, the camp, the companions, the expeditions, more), pages opened from others with their way back. Light animations and the game's own icons.
• A clicker: stoke the fire, buy its producers, their ranks and the click's upgrades. The embers count up while you look, and the fire burns while you are away (twelve hours, more with the ashes).
• Seven tiers of the fire; the seventh, the eternal blaze, never ends, each of its levels asking more. Very large numbers said with letters past Q (AA, AB...).

addons.description:
Shield Aura Forever v1.1.0
A lightweight absorb HUD for World of Warcraft: Forever. Shield Aura Forever displays the player's remaining damage absorb as a single movable HUD near the character, with an optional numeric absorb value. Choose a curved or horizontal layout, segmented or solid styling, and class-labeled color presets.

Shield Aura Forever is a clean-room addon inspired by the general segmented shield-HUD concept. It does not include or reuse nanShield / WeakAuras source code or artwork.
Features
• Curved or horizontal single-bar absorb HUD (movable in either layout)
• Segmented or solid styles for both shapes
• Automatic class colors for new installations, or selectable class-labeled color presets such as Warlock - Purple and Hunter - Green
• Original Gold color option, retained automatically for v1.0.1 upgrades
• Separate saved positions for curved and horizontal layouts
• Exact remaining absorb amount
• Tracks the player's total current absorb
• Dynamic depletion as damage is absorbed
• Optional shield-loss animation
• Configurable top-first or bottom-first drain direction
• Mirror the curve for left- or right-side placement
• Absorb value can be shown above or below the bar
• Movable and scalable HUD
• Movable standalone settings window
• Minimap button with adjustable angle and radial distance
• Blizzard Options → AddOns integration
• AddOn Compartment support
• Per-character shield calibration
• No external libraries or dependencies
Compatibility
Shield Aura Forever is developed specifically for World of Warcraft Forever. This release adds HUD appearance and positioning options while retaining the existing absorb-tracking and calibration logic.

The existing v1.0.1 behavior was tested during the official Forever beta with:
• Priest Power Word: Shield
• Warlock Voidwalker Sacrifice
• Sacrifice values that include the current Forever spell-healing scaling
• Live absorb loss as damage is taken
• Shield expiration and removal
• Top-first and bottom-first drain directions
• Mirrored curve, animation toggle, movable HUD, minimap button, and settings persistence

The addon displays the player's total current absorb, so simultaneous absorb effects are combined.

Can Openerv1.2.0 (2026-09-20)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• feat: Add 128 WoW: Forever openables
Sweeps Wowhead's Forever database (all 22,289 items, tooltip-checked
for "Right Click to Open" / "Locked") and adds every container that
exists only on Forever, i.e. whose ID is missing from the retail
database:
• 30 Forever-new items (Captain Sander's Locker, Pack of Apprentice
through Artisan Supplies, Coin Pouches, Theramore/Darkspear care
packages, Whirleygig's Supply Stash, A Winter Veil Gift)
• 93 Season of Discovery carry-overs present in the Forever client
(rune containers, Otherworldly Treasure, the spec-pick Tier 0.5 set
boxes, Damaged Undermine Supply Crates)
• 5 vanilla-range IDs that only exist or only open on Forever
Six are flagged as lockboxes. Practice Lock, Lucius's Lockbox and
Rogue's Diary share their IDs with retail items that are not lockboxes
there, so they live here instead of the shared Classic.lua.
Skipped QA template kits ("Level 60 Mining Supplies" and friends) and
DEPRECATED/[DNT]/[PH] entries.
• feat: Separate retail and WoW: Forever openables
Each Openables file now gates itself on the game flavor so retail and
Forever items are never registered on the other flavor:
• BurningCrusade through Midnight return early unless
CanOpenerGlobal.IsRetail.
• New Openables/Forever.lua (loaded after Midnight) holds Forever-only
items and returns early unless CanOpenerGlobal.IsForever.
• Classic.lua stays shared: vanilla-era items exist on both flavors with
the same item IDs, as confirmed by Wowhead's Forever database.
• feat: Add WoW: Forever support
One package now loads on both retail (12.1) and WoW: Forever (1.60.x):
• TOC lists interface 120100 and 16001; the BigWigsMods packager maps
16xxx to the Forever game type on CurseForge automatically. The stale
120007 entry is dropped.
• Helpers.lua detects the flavor from the interface number, since Forever
reports WOW\_PROJECT\_ID == WOW\_PROJECT\_MAINLINE just like retail. Exposes
CanOpenerGlobal.IsRetail / IsForever / InterfaceVersion.
• The Rousing option (settings checkbox, /co rousing, help text) is
retail-only; Rousing elements do not exist on Forever.
• Bag scanning is unchanged: Forever has the reagent bag like retail.

Dyre's Buff Reminders 1.7.0ChangesFeatures
• Combo Point Chimes: a new note set, "Dyre's Bassoon", a quick comic climb to a held F, is the new default. "Dyre's Sax" stays as the second set. The "Point notes" switch is now a "Note set" dropdown: Bassoon, Sax, or Same as Full (each point plays the Full sound). The Full and Spend sounds follow the set unless you chose your own. Players on 1.6.0's defaults move to Bassoon; with your own Full or Spend sound, you keep the Sax. Bassoon needs Dyre's Sounds 1.4.0; an older one plays the Sax notes.
Notes
• For WoW: Forever and WoW Classic Era. Built for Forever beta 1.60.1,
build 70450, Interface 16001, and Classic Era 1.15.9,
build 70003, Interface 11509. DBR runs on later builds
while the client provides the APIs it needs, and says so in chat if they are missing.
• Buff reminders for Mages, Warlocks, Druids, Priests, and Paladins: a pulsing
icon for each class buff missing on you or your group, or about to run out,
out of combat. Click it to cast the buff. Paladins also get a seal timer.
• Cooldown chimes for every class: a sound just before your chosen spells are
ready again, also in combat, and proc sounds (Clearcasting, Nightfall, and
so on). The sounds come from Dyre's Sounds.
• Settings in Options > AddOns, or /dbr; /dbr unlock to move the icons.
addons.description:
Your class buffs, each in its own icon, cast with one click, with a red
border when one drops, also in combat; ammo and reagent counts; a Paladin seal
timer; cooldown chimes; and proc chimes. For World of Warcraft: Forever. Settings are in **Options → AddOns → Dyre's
AddOns → Buff Reminders**, or type /dbr. They are saved per character.
• Druid: Thorns follows your tank. With a member set to the Tank role,
Thorns watches that tank and a click casts it on them. Solo, with no tank,
as the tank yourself, or when the tank is dead, offline, or out of range,
it watches you.
• Hunter: Aspect and combat aspect. A click recasts your last combat
aspect, never Cheetah or Pack, and never takes an aspect down. Start a
fight with Cheetah or Pack up, and an icon with your combat aspect appears
at once: one click puts it up, with an optional sound.
• Warrior: Battle Shout, Overpower, and Revenge. A Battle Shout
reminder, and a sound the moment Overpower or Revenge
becomes usable, also in combat.
• Ammo for any bow, gun, or crossbow (Hunters, Warriors, and Rogues): the
count, red and pulsing when low, and "Equip your arrows" when none are
equipped. It counts in combat too.
• Each buff its own icon, always shown, in a place you choose that never
moves: the buff with its time left while it is up, a red border you click
to cast when it is missing, yellow and flashing before it runs out, moved
and sized with Dyre's Toolkit.
• Also in combat: if a buff on you expires, is dispelled, or is
cancelled, its red reminder shows at once, and a click recasts it.
• Reagents: Rebirth's seeds (Druid), Arcane Powder (Mage), Infernal
Stones and Demonic Figurines (Warlock), counted with the ammo.
• Hidden on flight paths; each icon shows the spell a click casts.
• In combat AddOns cannot read buffs, so group members' buffs (and Thorns on
the tank) are checked again after the fight; the seal timer, the combat
aspect icon, the ammo and reagent counts, the chimes, and the proc sounds
keep working.
Buff reminders
An icon for each of your class buffs, with a border that tells you where it
stands: red while it is missing, yellow and flashing while it is about to run
out, none while it is up. Each buff has its own icon in its own place,
which never moves on its own; one you do not know or have switched off shows
nothing. They start in two rows: buffs that can go on another player above,
your own below.
• Always shown. While the buff is on you, the game draws it in its place
with its time left, in and out of combat alike, so nothing appears or
disappears when a fight starts or ends.
• When it is missing (expired, dispelled, or cancelled) the reminder
shows there at once with its red border, also in combat, and a click recasts it on
you. In combat the game itself hides the buff's icon (AddOns cannot read
buffs then), so the reminder underneath shows through.
• Out of combat the reminder also shows while anyone in your group lacks
the buff, or yours is about to run out (with a countdown), with the smart
click (group members, the tank, the group version). That stays as it is
through a fight; your group is checked again after it.
• Unlocked, every icon shows (the buffs that are on, dimmed).

| Class | Buffs |
|---|---|
| Mage | Arcane Intellect (also for group members who use mana), Armor (Frost, Ice, or Mage Armor), Dampen or Amplify Magic (off at first; either counts, a click recasts the last one) |
| Warlock | In a group where you aren't the tank, a message on screen while the Voidwalker's Torment or Suffering is on autocast; Demon Armor (Demon Skin counts before you learn it); Pet (your demon): red while you have no demon, also in combat, and a click summons the last demon you summoned, else the Imp (not after a Demonic Sacrifice, nor while mounted) |…

Dyre's Crit Mayhem 0.2.0ChangesFeatures
• Naturalist (18+), a new theme for Druids and nature, mature and a touch gory:
melee crits mix claw scratches (two to four), bites, and splatter, at
any angle, in blood that sometimes drips straight down (tick "Claws
only in Cat or Bear form", under the theme, to keep them to Cat and
Bear form and a Hunter's pet, with Brutal's splatter otherwise);
Wrath-like crits a murky green burst with
insects and torn leaves bursting out; arcane silver fireworks that fade;
fire charred, burning leaves and embers on a scorch; frost frozen leaves
with ice shards on frozen blood; holy a harsh searing flare; shadow
rotting black leaves on dark ichor. Crit heals sprout vines and green and
gold smoke, never flowers; a new record darkens the screen's edges in
deep green. Growls, a tiger, angry cats, and bear and lion roars.
• Brutal in Cat or Bear form: your melee crits (and a Hunter's pet's)
are claw scratches, bites, and splatter in Brutal's red, dripping
straight down; out of form and for every other class, its blood
splatter as before.
• Effects by damage school: every theme keeps its own look, and a crit's
school adds a color and a small touch. Brutal is always wounds: charred
blood with embers for fire, frozen blood with an ice shard for frost,
blood-soaked leaves stuck on the wound for nature, slowly smearing
down, black ichor, blood with a violet crackle, seared
wounds with a light flare. Fel is always its smoke and cracks, with
hellfire flame licks, rime, a leaf that catches fire and falls to ash,
violet, or pale light. Spellburst is always its bursts, colored by
school, with a flame or ice shard inside, and a puff of leaves blowing
up out of its green burst. Melee crits are blood in every theme but Tame (on Spellburst
only with the 18+ box, else a white flash). Tame has cartoon looks: a
pow, little flames, snowflakes, leaves, dusky puffs, twinkly stars, gold
sparkles, never blood. A spell of two schools shows one, magic first:
fire, frost, shadow, arcane, nature, holy.
• Random Effects (Tame, off by default): tick it for Tame's playful mix of
stars, butterflies, and sparkles on every crit, whatever its school.
• Leaves for nature: a Michigan maple, an oak, and a birch leaf. Tame's
nature crits are a tumble of them in autumn colors, maple most, with a
puff of leaves blowing out and drifting down; Spellburst's blow out and
up; Brutal's are soaked in blood and stick; Fel's burn to ash.
• Tame has rainbows: a little cartoon rainbow joins its stars, butterflies,
and sparkles (and its holy crits), in its own colors.
• Others' crits: anyone's crit on your target and on nearby enemies (with
a nameplate shown) now plays the effects and sounds too, in a group and
solo. Choose Off, My target, or Nearby enemies (the default). Others'
crits are trimmed so a raid stays readable (one effect each, a few per
half second); yours always play. Your records stay yours alone.
Other changes
• Fel's own sounds (Dyre's Fel Sounds, Dyre's Sounds 1.4.0): a wet smash,
a mud splat, or a heartbeat on each crit, a deep demon growl for a new
record, and now and then a heartbeat from Medium. With an older Dyre's
Sounds, Fel keeps its earlier sounds. Needs Dyre's Sounds 1.4.0 for them.
• "Guess my crits in a group" (WoW: Forever) is gone: in a group, a crit on
your target or an enemy nameplate plays as others' crits, and no records
are kept from it.
Notes
• Opt-in mayhem for your crits, as much as you dial up: an intensity from
Off (the default) to Total Mayhem, staying longer each step, with a "Stays on
screen" slider, in a theme: Tame (pastel butterflies and stars, the
default) or Brutal (blood splatter; 18+, locked until you tick "I'm 18 or
over"). More themes to come.
• Personal records: each ability's highest hit and crit on this character,
with a records window (/dcm) and optional party, guild, and on-screen
announcements.
• Classic Era and Anniversary: everything, from the combat log. WoW: Forever…

Dyre's Quest Targeting 1.2.0ChangesFeatures
• WoW Classic Era and Anniversary: the game has no quest focus there, so DQT follows Questie's tracker focus. Without Questie, quest targeting is off, but the macro and the box still keep your hit list; chat says so at login.
• The Quest Target box shows also with no focused quest, with a line on how to focus one, so you can always change the hit list from it.
• With no target, the hit list's plus opens a small box under the Quest Target box to type a mob's name (Shift-click for the exact name). It never opens in combat.
• On those clients, "Follow Questie's tracker focus" shows on and greyed (it is the only focus), "Keep Questie's and the game's focus in sync" is greyed (nothing to sync), and the "On a mob, also" list reads your spellbook there too.
Notes
• For WoW: Forever and WoW Classic Era 1.15.9 (build 70003,
Interface 11509). Built for Forever beta 1.60.1, build 70450,
Interface 16001. DQT runs on later beta builds while the client provides
the APIs it needs, and says so in chat if they are missing.
• Keeps the character macro "! Target (DQT)" up to date with the mobs and NPCs
your focused quest needs, and marks what it finds.
• With QuestieDB installed, it also targets the mobs that drop quest items and
the NPC you turn the quest in to.
• /dqt add and /dqt add_exact add your own targets; settings
in Options > AddOns, or /dqt; /dqt list shows what the macro targets.
addons.description:
Shows your Focused Quest and builds a "hit list" and targeting macro based on
what you're trying to accomplish.

Dyre's Quest Targeting (DQT), for World of Warcraft: Forever, keeps
one character macro, ! Target (DQT), up to date with the mobs and NPCs
your focused quest needs. Put it on an action bar and press it to find, target, and mark the
nearest one. Type /dqt for the settings (see Settings).
Everything is saved per character. Works best with Questie and TomTom;
both are optional.

It replaces the one part of RestedXP's guides the author still wanted, built
from Forever's own quest journal instead of a guide.
What the macro targets
• Your focused quest: focus a quest in the game's quest log or on the map
(the map and minimap then point the way), or with Questie's tracker
(right-click, Focus Quest or Focus Objective; Questie hides the game's
tracker by default). Whichever you set last counts; at login, Questie's.
A Questie objective focus targets only that objective. "Follow Questie's
tracker focus" in the settings turns Questie's focus off. When the focused
quest changes, chat says so: "Focused quest changed via Questie (Assessing
the Threat), targeting updated to Redridge Poacher." Only the focused
quest counts, not every tracked one.
• Kill objectives it still needs, the first objective first.
• With QuestieDB installed (it comes with Questie, and also installs on its
own), also the mobs that drop the quest's items (with Questie, the six
best by Questie's drop rates, the best one wanted most; /dqt list shows each
rate),
every mob a shared kill objective counts, and, once the quest is done, the
NPC you turn it in to. Without it, only kill objectives are targeted:
the client names no mobs for quest items.
• Your hit list: names you add, for any mob, quest or not. They win over
the quest's:
• /dqt add Goretusk finds anything whose name contains it (/tar), such
as Great Goretusk.
• /dqt add_exact Great Goretusk finds only that name (/targetexact).
• With nothing typed, both add your target, which can be a dead one: target
the corpse and the macro finds the next.
• /dqt remove [name] and /dqt reset take them away; the quest's names stay.
• /dqt reads macro conditions in brackets, so a macro of your own,
/dqt [mod:shift] remove; add, adds your target on a click and removes
it on Shift-click.
• Finished objectives drop out by themselves as the quest log updates, and
chat says so: "Redridge Mongrel removed: Quest Assessing the Threat
objective completed. Use /dqt add if you want to keep targeting them." In
combat the macro cannot change, so it catches up when combat ends.

Quest names always use the exact name. A macro holds 255 letters, about six
names with every line on; /dqt list says which names did not fit.
What it does with what it finds
The macro clears your target, looks for each name, goes back if what it found
is dead, then:
• Marks it: a skull on a mob, a green triangle on an NPC (anything you
cannot attack). A second press leaves the mark. Both markers can be changed,
and "Mark what the macro finds" turns marking off. In a raid, only leaders
and assistants can mark.
• On a mob, also (off by default): start attacking, or cast a spell you
pick from your spellbook, such as Moonfire (Rank 1) to tag a mob. The list
holds only harmful spells that cast in 1 second or less, rank by rank.
Never on an NPC. The macro casts it with /use [harm,nodead] Name(Rank N)
(/use casts the spell like /cast, and is one letter shorter).
Talking to NPCs and clicking quest objects
A macro cannot interact, and /targetexact cannot find objects. Use the
game's own Interact key: Options → Controls → Enable Interact Key, then
bind it. It talks to the NPC, loots the corpse, or clicks the quest object in
front of you.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /dqt | Opens the settings (out of combat) |…

addons.description:
A shield display for any class in World of Warcraft: Forever, and the one
shield display for all of Dyre's AddOns: Mage Tools Forever and Warlock Tools
Forever use it too. Settings are in **Options → AddOns → Dyre's AddOns →
Shields Up, or type /dsu. They are saved per character. Needs Dyre's
Toolkit** 2.0 or later, which the CurseForge app installs with it. Formerly
Shields Up Forever (/suf).
Shield display
A segmented crescent beside your character that fills with your remaining
shield, full when it lands and draining as it absorbs, with the amount as a
number below. It tracks live, also in combat, and drops away the moment the
shield is used up.
• Any absorb on you counts: a Priest's Power Word: Shield (white), a
Mage's Ice Barrier (blue), Fire Ward (orange), and Frost Ward
(pale blue), a Warlock's Shadow Ward and Voidwalker Sacrifice
(purples), and any other absorb (a trinket, a potion, or one Forever adds)
in a neutral gold.
• With several shields up, the crescent shows their combined total, refilled
as each one lands, and a row of icons under the number shows which are up,
each in its own spot. Each icon drops the moment its shield breaks or ends,
also in combat.
• The icon row holds your own class's shields first, then the ones anyone can
put on you: Power Word: Shield and Blessing of Protection. A Priest sees
those two; a Mage sees Ice Barrier, Mana Shield, Fire Ward, and Frost Ward
first; a Warlock Shadow Ward and Sacrifice; a Paladin Divine Shield and
Divine Protection.
• Shields with no absorb amount drain with their time left instead: a Mage's
Mana Shield in a thinner purple crescent nested inside, and Paladin
bubbles (Divine Shield, Divine Protection, **Blessing of
Protection**) in a gold crescent innermost of all.
• Display size shrinks or grows the crescents from their center
(50-150%). The number and the icons keep their size; Text size and
Icon size set them (50-150% each), and Reset size puts all three
back to 100%. The number can be turned off, and a sound can play when a
shield ends or breaks, also in combat. The sounds come from **Dyre's
Sounds**, which the CurseForge app installs with DSU; otherwise get it from
CurseForge or github.com/jbedworth/DyresSounds. Without it, DSU works but
plays no sound.
• Tiny absorbs (under 25 points or 5% of your health, whichever is larger,
such as a Paladin's Seal of Righteousness) never show.
• Locked (the default), it never blocks clicks on the world. Unlocked, it
shows a full sample of every part, outlined, to drag; /dsu reset puts it
back.
With Dyre's Toolkit
Dyre's Toolkit gives all of Dyre's AddOns one layout mode and one
settings home, and DSU needs it (2.0 or later): the shield display is one of
its widgets, placed, dragged, sized, and saved by the toolkit. The CurseForge
app installs it with DSU; without it, DSU stays off and says once at login to
install it from CurseForge.
• Unlocking (/dsu unlock, /dyre unlock, the toolkit's minimap button, or
Unlock frames on the Dyre's AddOns page) unlocks every Dyre's AddOn's
frames at once, and locking locks them all. Frames always start locked at
login.
• Dropped near another Dyre's AddOn's frame, the shield display snaps beside
it; Shift-drag moves a snapped group; with the toolkit's "Snap to the grid"
on, it snaps to the grid.
• DSU's settings page sits under Dyre's AddOns, and DSU is listed under
Dyre's Toolkit in the in-game AddOn list.
With Mage Tools Forever or Warlock Tools Forever
Mage Tools Forever (1.2.0 and later) and Warlock Tools Forever (1.3.0 and
later) leave the shield to Dyre's Shields Up and require it, so the
CurseForge app installs it with them. The first time Dyre's Shields Up runs
on a character, a Mage's shield settings from Mage Tools Forever (or a
Warlock's from Warlock Tools Forever) are copied once: place, sizes, the
number, and the sound. DSU says so in chat. A character that already has DSU
settings keeps them, and the other AddOn's own settings are left as they are.…

The sounds and sound picker that Dyre's AddOns share, for World of Warcraft:
Forever (beta). It is a library: it does nothing on its own. Install it when
one of Dyre's AddOns asks for it.
What it has

vanish, and magical disappear sounds), first in every sound menu.
• Dyre's Speed, Dyre's Cats, Dyre's Bears, and Dyre's Water: 22 more, by
theme: speed boosts and engines for travel spells, and meows, growls, roars,
and splashes for the Druid's forms.
• Dyre's Aggression: 11 battle cries and shouts, for Charge and other
Warrior moves.

slices and splats to slaps, kisses, and sword swings.

octave, for chimes that count up (combo points).

without it, they play no sounds and say once in chat what to install.

For the Forever beta client 1.60.1 (Interface 16001). WowUp users
(2.24.0 or later) can install it from the repository URL; GitHub releases
carry the Forever metadata WowUp needs.

Dyre's Toolkit 2.5.0ChangesOther changes
• For AddOn authors: the first part of the shared tracking engine. SpellbookIDsByName, SpellSet, IndexSpells, KnowsAny, and PetKnows find a spell by name in every client's spellbook; CreateMacroKeeper, OutOfCombat, MarkLine, and FocusCastMacro keep character macros, out of combat only, and take over another Dyre's AddOn's macro by its name instead of making a second one; CreateAnnouncer, FormatAnnouncement, GroupChannel, and RAID_MARKERS send group messages; ClassData holds the Warlock and Mage spell tables. Contracts 1 and 2 are unchanged.
• For AddOn authors: CreateControlTracker is the crowd-control bar of Warlock Tools Forever and Mage Tools Forever in one engine: a row per mob you Fear, Banish, or Polymorph, its click to cast again on your focus, the Focus box, timers under nameplates, the group messages, and the macros. ClaimOwner, IsOwner, and OnOwnerChanged make sure that with two Dyre's AddOns on, only one shows a bar, writes the macros, or tells your group: a class's own Tools AddOn first.
• For AddOn authors: CreateDotTracker, CreatePlateDots, and CreateDotPredictor are Warlock Tools Forever's DoT tracker, nameplate dots, and damage to come in one engine. The ticks each DoT has shown are now kept once for every Dyre's AddOn, and Warlock Tools Forever's are carried over the first time.
Notes
• For WoW: Forever and WoW Classic Era 1.15.9 (build 70003,
Interface 11509). Built for Forever beta 1.60.1, build 70450,
Interface 16001. It runs on later beta builds while the client provides
the APIs it needs.
• One layout mode for every Dyre's AddOn: /dyre unlock and /dyre lock, a
grid, snap to grid, and frames that snap across AddOns.
• A minimap button (left-click: lock or unlock; right-click: menu) and one
"Dyre's AddOns" settings home; /dyre opens it.
addons.description:
The shared toolkit for Dyre's AddOns on World of Warcraft: Forever. It does
nothing on its own; the Dyre's AddOns you install use it. The CurseForge app
installs it with them.
What it gives you
• One layout mode. /dyre unlock shows every Dyre's AddOn's frames, so
you can drag them where you want; /dyre lock locks them all again. Each
AddOn's own unlock command does the same.
• Snapping. A frame you drop near another snaps beside it, also when the
other frame belongs to a different Dyre's AddOn. Shift-drag moves a group of
snapped frames together.
• A grid while frames are unlocked, with red lines through the center of
the screen. Its size is a setting. With Snap to the grid (on by default), a dropped
frame near a red center line centers on it, or puts its nearer edge on it.
Elsewhere, an edge within a quarter of the grid size (8 at 32) of a grey
line lines up with it. When both edges (left and right, or top and bottom)
are that close, the one that moves the least wins, so the frame may line
up at its lower-right corner rather than its upper-left: check both.
Snapping to another Dyre's frame comes before the grid; a Shift-dragged
group snaps to the grid as one block. Hold Ctrl as you drop a frame to
place it exactly, with no snapping.
• Move without unlocking. Hold Ctrl and drag a frame by a button or
a box's header to move it while frames are locked, as with Questie's
tracker. It goes exactly where you drop it. Frames move only out of combat.
• A minimap button. Left-click locks or unlocks frames. Right-click opens a
menu: lock or unlock, the grid switches, the settings, and each installed
Dyre's AddOn's settings. /dyre minimap hides or shows the button.
• One settings home. Options → AddOns → Dyre's AddOns holds these
settings, with each Dyre's AddOn's page under it. /dyre opens it.

Frames always start locked when you log in. Frames move only out of combat.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /dyre | Opens the settings (out of combat) |
| /dyre unlock, /dyre lock | Unlocks or locks every Dyre's AddOn's frames |
| /dyre grid | Shows or hides the grid while unlocked |
| /dyre snap | Turns snapping to the grid on or off |
| /dyre minimap | Shows or hides the minimap button |
| /dyre debug | Until you reload: says in chat when another AddOn's hook into the toolkit fails, and lists those so far |

/dyretoolkit works the same, in case another AddOn uses /dyre.
For nameplate and unit frame authors
Dyre's AddOns that predict DoT damage draw a block and a DIES badge on
mob health bars. If your AddOn draws its own bars, or the badge covers
something of yours, DyresToolkit.HealthBars lets you say where your bar
is, where the badge goes, and when to draw nothing. You can also read the
prediction to show it your own way. See
docs/HEALTHBARS_API.md.
Compatibility
For the Forever beta client 1.60.1, build 70450, Interface 16001.

addons.description:
Quality-of-life tools for Mages in World of Warcraft: Forever (beta). Each tool
has its own switch on the main settings page and its own settings page in
Options → AddOns → Mage Tools Forever, or type /mtf. Settings are saved
per character.

**Shields, buff reminders, and cooldown chimes come from Dyre's Shields Up
and Dyre's Buff Reminders.** Since 1.2.0, MTF no longer has its own copies:
Dyre's Shields Up draws the shield display, and Dyre's Buff Reminders
shows Arcane Intellect, your armor, and Dampen or Amplify Magic, and plays the
cooldown chimes, for every class. The CurseForge app installs both with Mage
Tools Forever, and they take over your MTF settings once. MTF's Shield, Buff
Reminders, and Cooldown Chimes settings pages each have a button that opens
their settings. Without one of them, MTF works and says once in chat what to
install (or enable).

Needs Dyre's Toolkit 2.5. Dyre's Toolkit is the home of all of Dyre's
AddOns: one layout mode for every Dyre's AddOn's frames, a grid, and one
settings page. The CurseForge app installs it with Mage Tools Forever. MTF's
settings are under Options → AddOns → Dyre's AddOns → Mage Tools Forever.
Without Dyre's Toolkit 2.5 or later, MTF stays off and says once in chat what
to install.
Conjure
A small bar with Water, Food, Food & Water, and Mana Gem
buttons. Bar size on the Conjure settings page shrinks or grows it
(50-150%); see Moving frames to put it where you want.

Water and food

| Click | Friendly player targeted | No one targeted |
|---|---|---|
| Right | Conjures the best rank they can use | Conjures your best rank |
| Left | Trades them your share stack size of the best they can use, or all you have of it if less | Eats or drinks your best |
| Middle | Eats or drinks your own best | Same |
• Share stack size (Conjure settings, 1 to 20, default 10): how much one
left-click trade gives. It never gives more, so the rest stays for the next
party member. As you click, MTF makes one stack of exactly that much, using
no extra bag space where it can: it tops up a smaller stack you already
have, or merges small ones. Only when all you carry is bigger stacks does
it need one free bag slot to split into, and then it tells you. It puts
the stack into the trade window and whispers the player (at most once
every 30 seconds per player; see Announce). Click Food after Water to add both to the same trade. You press
Trade yourself.
• Someone opens a trade with you? While the trade window is open the
buttons serve your trade partner, whoever you have targeted: left-click
puts their share straight into the window, and right-click conjures what
they can use.
• With none they can use, MTF tells you to conjure some first.
• One cast doesn't make a full stack: right-click again until you have enough.
The button shows how many of the item it would use or give you carry.

Food & Water, the third button, does both at once:
• Left-click with a friend targeted (or a trade open) trades them a share
of water and food in one click, with one whisper. With no one targeted,
it eats and drinks your best.
• Right-click conjures water, then food, in turn: the game allows one
spell per click.
• Middle-click always eats and drinks your own best.

Mana gems
• Left- or middle-click uses your best mana gem; right-click conjures the best
rank you don't carry (you can carry one of each).
• Before you learn Conjure Mana Agate (level 28), the button is greyed out and
tells you when it comes.

Macros for your action bars: MTF keeps ! Water, ! Food,
! Food & Water, and ! Mana Gem in your character macros (each once you know its spell). Drag
them from the Macros window to a bar: left-click eats, drinks, or uses;
right-click conjures, also in combat. Turn Keep conjure macros off to
remove them. (On Forever, /click macros do not press AddOn buttons, so these
use the game's own /use and /castsequence.)

addons.description:
Quality-of-life tools for Warlocks in World of Warcraft: Forever. Warlock Tools
Forever (WTF) is a suite of small modules, each with its own switch and
settings page: Soul Shard management, Soulstone and Healthstone buttons with
trading and reminders, summon and Soulstone announcements, a DoT tracker for
several mobs, and a Fear and Banish control bar.
Compatibility
WTF is for World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1 (tested on build 70450),
Interface 16001, Lua 5.1. It does not check the client version or build,
because builds change often. At login it checks for the APIs it needs and
disables itself with one message if any are missing. It runs on Warlocks only;
on other classes it prints one message and stays off.

On WoW Classic Era and Anniversary, the DoT tracker, the nameplate DoT dots,
and the Fear and Banish bar read your auras themselves (those clients have no
aura engine for AddOns), with the same look and settings. As on Forever, a
mob shows its timers while a nameplate, your target, or your focus shows it.
Dyre's Shields Up and Dyre's Buff Reminders
In version 1.3.0, four features moved out of WTF into two of Dyre's AddOns
that every class can use:
• The shield display (the crescent for Shadow Ward, Sacrifice, and
other shields) is in Dyre's Shields Up (/dsu).
• The cooldown chimes, the Nightfall sound, and the **Demon Armor
reminder are in Dyre's Buff Reminders** (/dbr). Its Demon Armor icon
casts your armor when you click it, as WTF's did.

The CurseForge app installs both with WTF. They copy your WTF settings for
these features once, the first time they run on a character. If one is
missing, WTF still works and says once at login to install it from
CurseForge (or to enable it in the AddOn list). WTF's Shield, Cooldown
Chimes, Alerts, and Demon Armor settings pages now have a button that opens
that AddOn's settings. WTF no longer plays any sound, so it no longer needs
Dyre's Sounds.
Dyre's Toolkit
Dyre's Toolkit gives all of Dyre's AddOns one layout mode and one
settings home. The CurseForge app installs it with WTF. With it:
• WTF's settings are under **Options → AddOns → Dyre's AddOns → Warlock
Tools Forever**, and WTF's own pages (Soul Shards, Stones, and the rest)
are under that.
• /wtf unlock, /dyre unlock, or the toolkit's minimap button unlock the
frames of every Dyre's AddOn at once. WTF's frames snap to the frames of
Dyre's other AddOns, and the toolkit draws the grid (with **Snap to the
grid** on its settings page).
• In the game's AddOn list, WTF is in the Dyre's AddOns group.

Since WTF 1.5.0 the DoT tracker, the nameplate DoT dots, the Control bar
(with its macros and announcements), and the DoT damage prediction run on
Dyre's Toolkit 2.5's shared engines; WTF keeps their settings and pages.

addons.description:
Save and restore named weapon configurations in World of Warcraft: Forever.
Weapon Sets Forever uses WoW's native per-character equipment sets. It is small,
needs no other AddOn to work, and does not use SavedVariables.
Purpose
Swapping between weapon loadouts (for example, a shield set and a two-handed set)
should not require managing complete outfits. WSF saves only the main-hand,
off-hand, and ranged slots as native equipment sets, ignoring every other slot,
so armor, trinkets, and the rest of your gear are never part of a swap.

Native sets are used deliberately: they persist per character without AddOn
storage, and they work with the game's own /equipset command and macros.
Compatibility
WSF is tested on the Forever beta, 1.60.1 build 70450, Interface 16001,
Lua 5.1. It does not check the client version or build, because beta builds
change several times a week. Instead it checks at login for the native
equipment-set APIs, constants, and weapon slot identities it needs, and
disables itself with one message if any are missing. Retail and other Classic
clients are not supported. WSF can load on Classic Era and Anniversary for
testing (it falls back to their older slot lookup and Character panel frames),
but those clients are not tested or supported yet.
Features
• Save main-hand, off-hand, and ranged configurations, including shields and held
off-hand items. Keep intentionally empty weapon slots in the snapshot.
• The ranged slot is part of every set: a set also equips its bow, gun, wand, or
thrown weapon, or a paladin's libram, a druid's idol, or a shaman's totem.
• Ignore native non-weapon equipment slots rather than manage complete outfits.
• Use the Save and Equip icon buttons in the Character equipment panel.
They sit beneath the left and right slot columns, clear of the stat text that
other AddOns draw beside the slots.
• Use /wsf save for saving and native /equipset for command or macro swaps.
• Use /wsf export to print equipped item IDs by slot, or a saved set, as JSON.
• Keep sets per character through native WoW persistence.
• Provide dark-brown save/equip panels with gold borders and warm text.

Automatic switching, talent-spec-specific sets, and general outfit management
are outside the project's scope.
Quick start
1. Equip the weapons you want to save.
2. Open the Character equipment panel and close the native Equipment Manager pane.
3. Click the Save icon (the WSF shield logo, beneath the wrist slot), enter a name, and
click Save or press Enter.
4. Repeat with another weapon configuration.
5. Outside combat, click the Equip icon (a sword, beneath the lower trinket
slot) and select a saved set.

Hover over either icon for help text.

At login, WSF prints its title, version, and author, then a short ready hint.
If the client is unsupported, the second line gives the reason instead.

The custom name field accepts a literal name. Spaces need no quotes there.
The equip list shows eight sets per page. You can browse it in combat, but WSF
blocks UI equipping. Combat entry closes the save panel, not the equip list.
Commands and names
/wsf, /wsf help, or any unknown word shows one line that lists every
command. /weaponsets is a backup command that works the same as /wsf. If
another AddOn also uses /wsf or /weaponsets, WSF says so once at login and
names the other command to use.

/wsf save requires exactly one non-empty name. Spaces separate arguments;
multi-word names require double quotes. Missing names, malformed quotes, and
extra arguments are rejected before changing a set. /wsf save Tank Weapons
does not silently create or overwrite Tank.

Names can contain at most 16 letters, including spaces, matching the native
Equipment Manager name field. WSF counts UTF-8 characters rather than raw Lua
string bytes. Control characters and | are rejected.

Native /equipset has its own parser. Do not apply the save quoting rules to it.
There is no /wsf set command.

addons.description:
Track the skills you are leveling, right on your screen, in World of Warcraft:
Forever. Weapon skills and professions are normally hidden on the Skills tab of
the Character window. Weapon Skills Forever shows up to six weapon skills and
six other skills as bars in a small box, so you can see at a glance when a skill is capped and it is time
to switch weapons or move on.
Purpose
Leveling a weapon skill, or grinding a profession, means opening the Character
window again and again to check progress. WSK keeps those numbers visible while
you play, and colors each bar by how close it is to the cap.
Compatibility
For World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1 (tested on build 70450, Interface
16001, Lua 5.1). WSK does not check the client version or build, because
client builds change often. It checks at login for a skill API it can use
and disables itself with one message if there is none: C_SkillInfo on
Forever, or the classic skill-line functions (GetNumSkillLines,
GetSkillLineInfo) on clients such as WoW Classic Era and Anniversary.

On those classic clients (for testing; the release targets Forever), a skill
is known by its name, and the weapon group by its English header name or by
its Defense line in any language. In other languages, Class Skills and
Languages are not hidden. A tracked skill under a collapsed group shows the
last values seen this session, or a note until the group is opened once.
Using it
• The skill box shows each tracked skill's name and a bar from 0 to the
skill's current cap, filled to your base rank. The bar text shows
rank / cap, with any bonus in green, for example 297 (+5) / 300.
• Red: more than 5 ranks below the cap.
• Yellow: within 5 ranks of the cap.
• Green: at the cap.
• Drag the box to move it. The position is saved per character. With
Dyre's Toolkit, type /dyre unlock (or /wsk unlock) first; see below.
• The view toggle (the sword or book icon beside the gear) switches the box
between weapon skills and other skills, such as professions. Each view lists
its skills in the Skills tab's order. Weapon skills are everything in the
Skills tab's Weapon Skills group, including Defense.
• The gear button opens the setup panel. Check up to six weapon skills
and six other skills to track. Skills are grouped as on the Skills tab. Skills with a single rank,
such as armor proficiencies, Class Skills, and Languages are not listed.
Group headers work like the Skills tab: click + to expand a group and
− to collapse it, which changes the Skills tab the same way. As there, a
collapsed group hides all its skills; tracked skills always stay in the box.
• Bonuses, such as racial weapon bonuses, are shown but do not count toward the
cap, matching Blizzard's Skills tab: a bar turns green when your base rank can
rise no further.
• When the game hides skill values (for example in combat), the box keeps the
last values it saw and updates when the game shows them again.
• Options → AddOns → Weapon Skills Forever (with Dyre's Toolkit, under
Dyre's AddOns; or /wsk) has the same
controls in the game's settings: show or hide the box, lock it (without
Dyre's Toolkit), reset its position, choose tracked skills, and set the opacity of the box
background (default 50%) and of the skill rows (default 90%). Layout
(horizontal) and theme options are shown there as previews and are not yet
available.

addons.description:
An addon for WoW Forever 1.60.1 / Interface 16001. Save your custom graphics settings and switch between configurations using a compact window, a favorites bar, or a keyboard shortcut.
Getting started
Copy this repository's contents into forever/Interface/AddOns/ForeverProfiles in your World of Warcraft installation. The ForeverProfiles.toc file must be directly inside that folder. If you added the addon while WoW was running, restart the game so it discovers the new folder. Enable Forever Profiles in the addon list.

1. Configure your graphics in the game's options and click Apply.
2. Open /fp, click Save current settings, and name the profile "High quality".
3. Configure and apply your performance settings in the game, then save a second profile.
4. Select the profile you want and click Apply profile.
5. Add up to three favorites with the Favorite button. Open the Favorite bar tab and enable Show favorite quick bar to switch with one click.

Selecting a profile lets you inspect it. Only applying a profile changes your game settings. Creating or duplicating a profile captures or copies settings without applying them. Profiles are not automatically applied at login.
Features
• A WoW-style window with charcoal surfaces, metallic edges, gold headings, beveled buttons, and a red Apply profile action. Profiles and Favorite bar tabs keep profile management separate from bar preferences.
• Up to 40 profiles, with renaming, duplication, updating, and deletion. Updating or deleting a profile requires confirmation.
• General graphics settings, separate raid/battleground settings, and the native raid settings toggle saved together, when exposed by the client.
• Render scale, antialiasing, vertical sync, and FPS limits supported by the client.
• A movable bar with 3 favorites: drag its handle or background to move it. The FP button opens the main window.
• A Lock favorite bar checkbox in /fp → Favorite bar: fixes the bar's position and hides its drag handle while keeping its buttons usable. Uncheck it to move the bar again. The lock setting is saved between sessions.
• Bar scale adjustable from 60 to 180% in the main window or with the mouse wheel over its handle. Buttons and text scale together. Position and scale are saved between sessions.
• Independent width and height in /fp: width from 160 to 1,000 and height from 28 to 120. Buttons share the available space without stretching the text. Dimensions are set before the overall bar scale and saved between sessions. Auto width restores sizing based on the number of favorites. On small screens, each dimension is constrained separately to the available space.
• Restore previous settings returns to the configuration captured before the last switch. This temporary backup lasts for the current session; /reload or restarting the game clears it.
• Active, Modified, and Applied partially statuses based on current values. After a partial application, the profile shows settings that differ, with their reasons in tooltips.
• A movable window that adapts to small screens and closes with Escape.
• The interface, dialogs, tooltips, shortcut labels, and messages stay in English on every client locale. Existing profile names are preserved as entered.
• Configurable shortcuts under Options → Key Bindings → Forever Profiles for the window, three favorites, and restoration. An entry is also available under Options → AddOns.
Commands
| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| /fp or /foreverprofiles | Open or close the window |
| /fp save High quality | Save current settings under this name |
| /fp apply High quality | Apply the named profile |
| /fp restore | Restore the configuration preceding the last switch |
| /fp quick | Show or hide the favorites bar |
| /fp list | List profiles and their statuses |
| /fp diagnostics | Show the version and number of accessible settings |
Storage and compatibility…

SessionScout 0.1.0 - Forever

Choose how much time you have and see up to three unfinished personal tasks that fit.

This first regular release brings the tested session planner and task-management redesign together:
• This session focuses on your time budget, suggested tasks and next-session reminder.
• My tasks separates unfinished and completed tasks, with a dedicated editor and Undo.
• Custom minutes accepts 1-240 whole minutes. Invalid entries keep your current budget.
• If nothing fits, the planner explains the shortest unfinished estimate and offers a route to your tasks.
• Existing tasks, completion and reminders keep the same saved-data format.

Open /scout. In My tasks, choose New task and enter your own time estimate and priority. Return to This session and select a preset or enter Custom minutes, then Apply. Task definitions are shared across characters; completion can be per-character or shared. Editing or deleting a definition affects every character.

Targets WoW Forever 1.60.1 (interface 16001). The new controls were exercised in 1.60.1.70450 using physical mouse and keyboard input: create/edit/cancel, complete/undo, confirmed deletion, 120/90-minute budgets and invalid input. After one reload, all 11 original tasks, completion records and character settings matched their pre-test values. The disposable task was removed. The release differs from that tested alpha.4 package only in its two version strings.

Validation includes 71 automated model, mocked integration and Python tooling checks. Actual reset crossings, alternate characters, combat transitions, extreme UI scales, long sessions and every restart/bag/durability case remain unverified. Earlier scoped checks include reminder persistence; this latest window preserved the existing empty reminder. No full Lua-error or taint audit was performed.

This is a manual task planner. It does not discover game activities, detect quest completion, measure how long tasks take, or calculate gear upgrades. It has no external service or telemetry. CurseForge-app detection, installation and updating for Forever have not been verified.

To install manually, close WoW and extract the SessionScout directory into your Forever Interface/AddOns folder. SessionScout/SessionScout.toc must be directly inside it. Keep your WTF/SavedVariables data when updating.

Source and issue reports: https://github.com/jdlarssen/SessionScout
Validation record: https://github.com/jdlarssen/SessionScout/blob/codex/sessionscout/docs/CLIENT_TESTING.md

An opt-in test build for WoW Forever 1.60.1, interface 16001.
The default client-tested release remains 0.1.0 on CurseForge.
Fix: completed reminders after a reset
A daily or weekly task could still show Task completed / Undo after its
recorded server reset when Scout was closed and no inventory/combat event
refreshed the screen. Its completion had already expired in the task model.

The visible completion card now refreshes every 30 seconds and clears on the
first refresh after that reset. It does not choose another task. Hiding,
dismissing or undoing the card stops the timer; unfinished and one-time tasks
do not start this timer. Task definitions, saved completion rules and the
SavedVariables format are unchanged.

This build also includes the alpha.3 default-position adjustment for a tracker
without a saved position. Existing saved positions are retained. The default
can still overlap other UI; drag the tracker background to suit your layout.
Included from alpha.2
Choose your own task, keep its reminder visible with Scout closed, and use
Done, Undo, Open Scout or Choose next from the tracker. An optional
Guide: Library books link opens the separately installed
Librarian Books Forever
journal. Opening a guide does not complete a Scout task. No companion addon is
required for ordinary tasks, and none is bundled.
Validation and limits
92 automated checks passed: 15 model, 58 mocked WoW integration and 19 tooling
checks, plus Lua 5.1 syntax and source CI.
Two new regressions reproduce the stale card against the old UI and pass with
the fix. Checks also cover timer cancellation, no automatic selection and
preservation of unrelated progress and settings.

The new timer has not been tested at an actual server reset in WoW. Earlier
scoped client checks used alpha.2 and covered task selection, tracker display,
Done/Undo and opening Librarian. Manual movement was subsequently reported on
the local alpha.3 build. Restoration of a moved position and chosen task after
reload still needs client verification. These earlier checks are not an
alpha.4 client-test claim. See the tracker test record.
Manual installation
Download SessionScout-0.2.0-alpha.4-forever.zip, not GitHub's source-code
archives. With WoW closed, back up the existing addon and extract the ZIP's
SessionScout folder into your Forever Interface/AddOns directory. The
current beta uses _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns. Keep your SavedVariables
when updating. Start WoW, enable the addon and use /scout.

• Task estimates, priorities, saved-data format and selection rules are unchanged. A 120-minute task still does not fit a 90-minute session.
Use and installation
Open /scout, enter the time you actually have in Custom minutes, and press Apply. Choose 120 only when you have two hours. Tasks and completion remain manual.

Download SessionScout-0.1.0-alpha.3-forever.zip from Assets below. With WoW closed, extract the ZIP's SessionScout folder into _classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns. SessionScout/SessionScout.toc must be directly inside that folder. Existing tasks are stored separately in SavedVariables. This file targets Forever 1.60.1 (interface 16001); Retail and other Classic flavors are not supported by this file.
Validation and remaining checks
Source commit: 888a47b7ced501687dda3c7563550800cdf1d7fe.
All 62 automated checks passed: 15 model, 28 mocked integration and 19 Python checks, plus Lua 5.1 syntax validation. Six regression cases cover the custom-budget correction. CI results.

The package was installed locally on Forever beta 1.60.1.70374. The client executable now reports 1.60.1.70450; runtime compatibility on that build is unverified. Actual rendering, font wrapping, keyboard interaction and focus behavior for the new control have not been verified. Earlier scoped alpha workflows were tested on build 70338; they do not prove this new control works. Real reset crossings, alternate-character behavior, combat, other UI scales and long sessions remain incompletely tested. No telemetry or automatic activity catalog is included.

Client record and release scope · Report problems.
