addons.changelog:
Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog.
[4.1.0-universal] - 2026-09-28Added
• WoW Forever support: UnitFramesImproved_Camelot.toc (## Interface: 16001). Forever's game
type is "Camelot" in Blizzard's UI code, and _Camelot.toc is the suffix both the client and the
CurseForge packager pick up for it. Forever runs Retail's Mainline unit frame templates (plus small
Camelot-only overrides that don't touch anything styled here), so it loads the Retail styler
unchanged.
• Options page (Options -> AddOns -> UnitFramesImproved, also opened by /ufi) built on Blizzard's
native Settings API, with a Status Text dropdown (Numeric Value / Percentage / Both / None) -
WoW Forever has no visible setting for showing health/mana numbers on the unit frames. It's backed
by the same statusText/statusTextDisplay CVars as Blizzard's own Status Text option, so the two
stay in sync on every client. Switching between two shown modes (e.g. Numeric to Both) turns
statusText off and back on within the same frame, since Blizzard's status bars only redraw their
labels when that changes - so the new mode shows right away. Changes picked in combat or under an
addon restriction (encounter, Mythic+, PvP match, restricted map) are held until it ends, since
the change runs Blizzard's status bar updates synchronously from addon code.
• build.ps1 deploys to _classic_beta_ (the WoW Forever beta install) too.
• tests/: offline regression tests (Python + lupa, a real Lua 5.1 runtime) that load the addon
into a stubbed WoW client once per TOC and check loading, events, styling, the options page, and
packaging. Never loaded in game or packaged.
Changed
• Removed the Ace3/LibStub dependency (AceAddon, AceEvent, AceConsole, CallbackHandler). Events now
go through one private event frame and slash commands through SlashCmdList - Blizzard's own APIs,
identical on every client. No more .pkgmeta externals, Libs/ folder, LICENSE-ACE3.txt, or
library fetching in build.ps1 (which still recognizes the old Libs//LICENSE-ACE3.txt when
replacing a previous deploy).
• /ufi and /unitframesimproved now open the options page instead of printing a message.
• The "Initializing... / Initialized." chat lines on every login are gone (they came from the Ace3
OnInitialize hook).
Fixed
• Retail: stopped writing forceShow/textLockable onto PlayerFrame/TargetFrame/FocusFrame.
Nothing reads those on the unit frame (Blizzard's text logic reads them on the status bar), so they
never forced the text visible - they only wrote addon fields onto Blizzard's secure frames.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/kiforsbe/UnitFramesImproved/compare/4.0.2-universal...4.1.0-universal
addons.description:
"Improve upon the standard Blizzard unit frames, without going beyond the boundaries they set."

A minimal-footprint reskin of Blizzard's own Player, Target, and Focus unit frames - not a
replacement unit frame system. UnitFramesImproved keeps Blizzard's own frame logic (health/mana
updates, portraits, PvP/faction icons, classification handling, combat behavior) fully intact and
only changes how the frames look. Nothing to set up - it just works.
Key Features
• Class-colored health bars, with tap-denied targets shown gray.
• Status text (numbers, percentages, or both) follows the game's own Status Text setting, with large
numbers abbreviated automatically (e.g. "12.4k/45.3k"). On clients that don't show that setting,
like WoW Forever, it's available under Options -> AddOns -> UnitFramesImproved.
• Built to work reliably with Blizzard's newest protections - no errors or glitches in combat.
On Classic (Classic Era & Classic progression)
• Custom targeting-frame-style textures for the Player, Target, and Focus frames, including
elite/rare/rare-elite border variants.
• Health bar and status text repositioned to match the custom textures, staying lined up correctly
even after Blizzard UI updates.
Platform Support
One download works for Retail, WoW Forever, Classic (currently Mists of Pandaria Classic), Wrath
(Titan Reforged), TBC Anniversary, and Classic Era.
How It Looks
Blizzard's own unit frames next to UnitFramesImproved's, in every supported version. It covers the
player frame, including its vehicle and other looks, the target frame for each kind of target,
target of target, and boss frames. The sheet is drawn by
tools/compare_unitframe_art.py from the game's own UI code and
the addon's, and is redrawn for every release. It's stamped with the commit it shows.
addons.name: UnitFramesImproved

Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

[4.0.2-universal] - 2026-09-05Fixed
• PlayerFrame health bar no longer misaligns against the vehicle frame art - Blizzard resizes/
re-anchors the same health bar for vehicle state (PlayerFrame_ToVehicleArt), and our own
styling re-runs on every PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD/PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED (e.g. combat ending
while seated), so it was clobbering Blizzard's vehicle-art dimensions with our player-art ones.
Our styling is now skipped while PlayerFrame.state == "vehicle" and reapplied immediately via
a PlayerFrame_ToPlayerArt hook the moment Blizzard returns the frame to player state.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/kiforsbe/UnitFramesImproved/compare/4.0.1-universal...4.0.2-universal

Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog.
[Unreleased][4.0.1-universal] - 2026-09-01Fixed
• Classic-family TOC files (_Vanilla, _Mists, _TBC) failed to load at all - each started
with a plain # comment line before ## Interface:, which the client silently treats as an
unparseable TOC (confirmed by comparing against ~200 real installed addons: only Questie's
deliberately-broken placeholder TOC shared that pattern, used intentionally to produce this
exact effect). ## Interface: is now always the first line.
• UnitFramesImproved_Classic.toc renamed to UnitFramesImproved_Mists.toc - Mists of Pandaria
Classic has its own dedicated TOC suffix (confirmed via other installed addons, e.g.
TomTom_Mists.toc, BetterBags_Mists.toc); the generic _Classic catch-all suffix wasn't being
reliably matched for it.
• MoP Classic Interface declaration corrected and broadened to 50500, 50501, 50502, 50504 -
50504 is this client's actual running interface (/dump select(4, GetBuildInfo())), which has
to be present in the list since "out of date" triggers whenever the declared Interface is lower
than the client's, not merely different from it.
• Removed ## AllowLoadGameType from all TOC files - redundant with, and murkier than, the
per-flavor TOC suffix split already in place.
• ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED error calling MultiBarBottomLeft:ClearAllPointsBase() during combat -
UpdateTextStringWithValues (hooked onto the shared, game-wide TextStatusBar_UpdateTextStringWithValues)
redundantly re-ran Blizzard's own "hide when inactive" logic from insecure code, including
statusFrame:Hide(), on every status bar update in the game. Blizzard's own call already handles
that case securely just before the hook fires, so the branch was both dead weight and a taint risk
to whatever secure frame-position pass runs next. Removed.
Added
• UnitFramesImproved_TBC.toc for the Burning Crusade Classic Anniversary client (anniversary,
product wow_anniversary) - a separate product from Classic Era, not a continuation of it.
• build.ps1 now auto-detects and deploys to a anniversary install alongside the existing
retail/classic/_classic_era_ flavors, and ships CHANGELOG.md in the built addon
folder/zip.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/kiforsbe/UnitFramesImproved/compare/4.0.0-universal...4.0.1-universal

Changelog
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog.
[Unreleased][4.0.0-universal] - 2026-09-01Fixed
• Classic: player frame health bar not showing the player's class color - Style_PlayerFrame was
silently erroring on hooksecurefunc("TextStatusBar_UpdateTextStringWithValues", ...) on clients
that have migrated to Blizzard's mixin-based TextStatusBarMixin system, aborting the rest of the
function (including the class-color update) before it ever ran.
• Classic: player frame health bar reverting to Blizzard's default green shortly after showing the
correct class color - lockColor wasn't set, so Blizzard's own native health-bar update kept
repainting over it on every health change.
• Classic: Player/Target frame health bar X/Y position drift and hardcoded offsets - position is now
derived from Blizzard's own live anchor plus a fixed, named addon-specific delta, instead of
hardcoded absolute values or a full copy of Blizzard's live position.
• Classic: Target frame Background texture anchored to the wrong corner with stale offsets.
• Retail: Secret Values taint crash in Style_PlayerFrame when health/mana is a secret value at the
moment of a forced text update.
• Potential crash in UpdateStatusBarColor when frame/frame.healthbar is nil (e.g.
target-of-target frames that may not exist, or lack a .healthbar alias, on every client).
• Target frame ending up with a mix of addon and Blizzard styling when switching targets in combat -
InCombatLockdown() guards were narrowed to only the genuinely combat-restricted operation
(creating new regions); repositioning/recoloring already-existing regions isn't restricted.
Added
• PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED catch-up that re-applies styling on leaving combat, so anything actually
skipped by a combat-lockdown guard gets retried instead of staying unstyled for the rest of the
session.
• Local build.ps1 script that fetches the same Ace3/LibStub externals .pkgmeta declares and
stages a build for testing without going through the CurseForge packager - defaults to
deploy/UnitFramesImproved only, with -DeployToWow (or -WowInstallPath/-TargetPath) to also
copy that build into a local WoW install.
• .github/workflows/release.yml: manually-triggerable (Actions tab -> Run workflow) packaging and
CurseForge publishing via the BigWigsMods/packager action, which also attaches the built zip to
a matching GitHub release using this changelog as the release notes.
• IconTexture metadata in all three TOC files, so the addon shows an icon in the in-game AddOns
list instead of the default blank/placeholder icon.
• build.ps1 now also zips the staged build into deploy\UnitFramesImproved-.zip.
Changed
• Debug "Loading config... / Config loaded." messages now only print on the very first load, not on
every zone transition or post-combat re-application.
• UnitFramesImproved_UpdateTextStringWithValues moved off the global namespace onto
UnitFramesImproved.UpdateTextStringWithValues.
• README.md rewritten for players only, in the style of the CurseForge listing description;
build/release instructions moved to the new DEVELOPMENT.md.
• Addon author metadata updated to kiforsbe / KawF.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/kiforsbe/UnitFramesImproved/compare/3.0.0-universal...4.0.0-universal

So, some major changes coming up with release 3.0.0 of UnitFramesImproved.

Known issues (Classic & Cata):
• The functionality to scale the frames has not been re-implemented (yet?)
• The functionality to anchor the frames to each other has not been re-implemented (yet?)

If you have any issues, please report them on the GitHub.

addons.description:
Crafting profit helper for the WoW Forever client (Interface 16001), using Auctionator prices.

Deutsch weiter unten.
Features
• Profit list – every recipe of your character with reagent cost, sale price (after the 5% AH cut) and profit, sorted by profit.
• Prices from Auctionator – full scans, normal searches and the selling tab all feed the list. Vendor prices for reagents (thread, salt, flux …) are used when cheaper.
• Sub-recipes – reagents you can craft cheaper yourself (e.g. Cured Light Hide) are calculated at their crafting cost, recursively.
• Market check – number of listings at the AH, median price, warnings for old prices (~) and price spikes (!).
• Queue & shopping list – queue recipes with quantities; the shopping list subtracts bags and bank and is sent to Auctionator as list ForeverProfit.
• Craft list – craft the queue step by step (“Craft next”), intermediate steps first. The queue counts down automatically.
• Professions bar – left-click opens a profession, right-click filters the list.
• Leveling mode – recipes that still give skill, sorted by estimated cost per skill point.
• Custom prices – /fp price [item] 1g20s.
• German and English (follows the client language).
Requirements
• WoW Forever client (_classic_beta_, Interface 16001)
• Auctionator

addons.description:
Small quality-of-life features for World of Warcraft: Forever, in one addon. Each feature has its
own on/off switch, so you keep what you want and turn off the rest.

Download the latest release

| Feature | What you get | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Quest Trash | A keep or delete verdict on quest item tooltips. /fqt lists everything in your bags (and bank) you can throw away. | QuestieDB |
| Kill Value | Expected gold per kill on creature tooltips: coins plus each drop's chance times its price. Learns real drop rates from what you loot. | Nothing (Auctionator optional) |
| Setups | Save a character's action bars, keybindings, macros, Edit Mode layout, interface settings and addon list, then apply them to another character. New characters can start from a saved setup. | Nothing |

All three are on by default.

Kill Value tooltip (earlier 1.12 version; a Forever screenshot is coming).
How it behaves
• Advice only. Quest Trash and Kill Value never delete, sell, loot or click anything for you.
Setups is the one feature that changes your UI: only out of combat, only when you click Apply (or
for a brand-new character, if you marked a setup for that), and always with an undo snapshot first.
• Plays by Forever's addon rules. Nothing reads combat data Blizzard hides from addons. Every
feature checks for hidden ("secret") values and steps aside instead of erroring. Inside instances,
where creature tooltip data is hidden, Kill Value shows nothing.
• Errors stay out of your way. Tooltip and event code runs protected, so a bad value skips a line
instead of throwing a Lua error.

Install with WowUp · Latest release · Report an issue

Screenshots are rendered from the addon's own code in a test harness, ahead of the WoW Forever launch.
Everything your crew can do, in one window
Open Bondfire from the minimap button. Find who can craft what, ask them for it, and see where everyone is, without typing a single command.

| | What you can do |
| :--- | :--- |
| 🔎 Find a crafter | Type three letters to search every recipe your crew knows. Shift-click an item in chat or in your bags to search for it. |
| 📜 Ask for a craft | Pick a crafter, set the amount and send the request. Bondfire shows which materials to bring; your counts stay on your computer. |
| ✉️ Never miss a request | Requests to offline crafters wait and go out when they log in. Mark requests for you as done or declined. |

| 💰 Skip vendor chores | Junk is sold and gear repaired with your own gold when you open a vendor. Hold Shift to skip once. |

Your crew at a glance

Hover anyone for details. Click a row to see what they can craft.

Set up from the window

Choose who your crew is, how the vendor behaves and how Bondfire looks.

Make it yours
Switch between Arcane, Ember and Journal in Settings. Each style has its own colors and fonts, and the change applies right away.

Ember

Journal

No guild needed
Your crew is everyone on your WoW friends list who runs Bondfire. It is enough that one of you has the other as a friend. Bondfire talks through addon whispers, so friends without the addon see nothing.

1.0.4 (2026-11-02)
• Large restructuring and refactor: Unit Frames, Nameplates, Aura Reminders, Cooldown Manager, Skins, Profiles and the shared aura code were reorganised and rewritten module by module, with cleaner code and many old leftovers removed.
• Nameplates options: new layout. Visual cards with their own icons replace the tabs, the live preview sits above every section at a larger size, and each card shows only its own options, with the duplicates gone.
• Nameplates: the preview and the plates show each class resource with the game's own art, centred under the plate. Pips default to the colour of each resource.
• Nameplates: in the Friendly card the preview dims the health bar when it is off or set to show names only.
• Aura Reminders options: new layout with section cards, a preview column and a settings column, plus a new zone dialog and error flash.
• Resource Bars: the anchor block was redesigned, and a resource the unit frame already draws is no longer repeated.
• Resource Bars: Tip of the Spear for Survival and Whirlwind for Fury.
• Skins: new surface material across windows, and buttons no longer keep their default red look in the Group Finder, AddOn List, Auction House and other windows.
• Game Menu: new frame styles, crests and button styles, with position, order and visibility options for the KUI buttons and a live preview.
• Enhancements: new Battleground History, recording each battleground with filters and a summary.
• Layout: Focus, Pet, Target of Target and the combat timers follow their unit frames, and frames around Player and Target keep their gaps when the scale changes. Default positions now depend on client and resolution.
• Art: new portrait, nameplate, bar, cursor and category icons, plus lighter packaging with unused fonts and textures removed.
• Fixed: Enhancement Shaman nameplates no longer raise an error, and Maelstrom Weapon shows its stacks.
• Client detection: KUI now recognises the Forever client properly, so its own group finder skin, default layout and bar look apply, and Aura Reminders settings are kept between sessions. Existing profiles move to the Forever name automatically.
• Forever Visual Style: Action Bars default to the Blizzard button style.
• Fixed: a damaged profile string can no longer freeze the game on import. It now shows a clear message.
• Fixed: nameplates follow a specialization change without a reload, and the resource of the previous spec no longer stays.
• Fixed: nameplate settings for Friendly text now show the real values instead of blanks.
• Fixed: Blizzard plates come back correctly when a unit stops being hostile.
• Fixed: pips reappear when a resource returns to its higher maximum, and the Stagger bar handles missing values.
• Fixed: Aura Reminders no longer hides your reminder because of the same buff from another player, repeated talents now give feedback, and dragging icons during a refresh no longer breaks their order.
• Fixed: debug messages in chat are gone, and the Group Finder leader role icon shows again.
• Translations: new option labels and messages translated into every language, and garbled characters in the changelog window repaired.

Configuration changes after updating:
• Aura Reminders: a preferred flask saved by an older version returns to Last Used. Choose it again if you want a fixed one.
• Cooldown Manager: a bar anchored with an older saved value returns to its saved position.

If you update from 1.0.3 or lower, restoring defaults from the installer is recommended.

EzPersistencev1.0.0
• First release for WoW Forever.
• /ep save saves this character's macros (and the account's), EzEmote chains, key bindings, action bars, game settings and Edit Mode layouts.
• /ep restore puts them back on any character, all at once or one part at a time; /ep status shows what differs.
• /ep layouts [n] [name] opens a saved Edit Mode layout to copy into Edit Mode's Import; on a character with none saved, it names the characters that have some.

addons.description:
Save your macros, key bindings, action bars, settings and Edit Mode layouts with one command. Put them back on any character, or on a new client, with another.

New client install, new PC, a new character, or a server reset? Your macros, bindings and bars stay behind with the old one, and you rebuild them by hand. EzPersistence keeps a copy you control: /ep save today, /ep restore wherever you play next.

Made for WoW Forever.
Quick start
1. Log in on your main and type /ep save.
2. On the character (or client) you want it on, type /ep restore.
• Different character name? Add the name you saved: /ep restore aelra.
3. Done. Chat tells you what was created, changed or skipped.

Not sure what will change? /ep status compares first and changes nothing.
What gets saved
• Macros: this character's macros and your account-wide ones. If you use EzEmote, its custom lines and chains too.
• Key bindings: every bound key, including keys bound to macros, spells and other addons' buttons, and whether they were account-wide or for this character only.
• Action bars: every slot on every bar. Spells, items, macros and equipment sets are put back; mounts, pets and flyouts are left as they are.
• Settings: the game options you changed from their defaults (interface, nameplates, combat text, sound volumes…). Graphics and hardware options stay with the PC.
• Edit Mode layouts: saved as Edit Mode share text, ready to paste back in (see below).
Commands
/ep (or /ezpersistence)

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /ep save | Save this character's macros, key bindings, action bars, settings and Edit Mode layouts |
| /ep restore [part] [name] | Put them back on the character you're playing |
| /ep status [part] [name] | Show what differs from the saved copy, without changing anything |
| /ep list | List the characters you've saved |
| /ep layouts [n] [name] | Open saved Edit Mode layout number n (default 1), ready to copy into Edit Mode |
• [part] is macros, bindings, bars, settings or layouts. Leave it out for everything.
• [name] is the first name of the character you saved. Leave it out to use the character you're on.

Examples:
• /ep restore — everything you saved on this character, back on it.
• /ep restore aelra — everything Aelra saved, on the character you're playing now.
• /ep restore bars aelra — only Aelra's action bars.
• /ep restore macros bindings — only macros and key bindings.
Restoring on a different character
Saves are kept per character, under the name of the character that ran /ep save. Any character on the same account can use any of them: add that name to the command (/ep restore aelra).
• Spells the new character doesn't know (another class, or not learned yet) are skipped and listed in chat. Everything else is placed.
• Happy with the result? /ep save on the new character so it has its own copy and plain /ep restore works there.
Moving from the beta to WoW Forever
Your saves are stored in the client's WTF folder, so the WoW Forever client starts empty. The beta and WoW Forever are separate folders inside your World of Warcraft install:

| Client | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| Beta | C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\ |
| WoW Forever | C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\forever\ |

Bring your saves along by copying one file:

1. On the beta: /ep save on every character you want to keep, then exit the game (the file is written when you log out).
2. On WoW Forever: install EzPersistence, log in once so the game creates your account folder, then exit the game.
3. Copy EzPersistence.lua
• from C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\EzPersistence.lua
• to C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\forever\WTF\Account\\SavedVariables\

Replace the file if there's one there already.
4. Log in on WoW Forever and type /ep restore (or /ep restore if the character has a different name).
5. Import your Edit Mode layouts (below).

Good to know:…

Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Add BellularGaming preset for enhanced graphics settings
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for Retail and WoW Forever that saves your video
settings as named profiles and lets you swap between them.

A profile stores the video CVars listed in CVars.lua: display mode and
resolution, frame rate limits, anti-aliasing, the graphics quality presets
(including raid quality) and the advanced settings. CVars the running client
doesn't have are skipped. Profiles are shared by every character on the
account.
Usage
Type /vp or open Options > AddOns > VideoProfiles. Select a profile on
the left; the right side shows what differs from your current settings, or
from another profile picked from the Compare with list. Show all
lists every value in the profile instead, highlighting the ones that
differ. The buttons below the list save, copy, apply, update, rename, delete,
export and import profiles.
Presets
A preset usually sets only a few settings, such as a creator's recommended
raid effects. Applying one changes just those and keeps everything else as
you have it. The list shows your own presets under Presets, followed by
the suggested ones that come with the addon (in blue). Selecting one shows its
notes and how its values compare with your settings.

To make one, set the game up the way you want, click New on the Presets
heading, then tick the settings it should set under Pick settings. Ticking
a setting takes your current value, which you can change in the box next to
it; Update later sets them all to your current values. Notes and Author are shown with the preset and carried
in its export string, so you can share it like a profile.

Bundled presets can't be changed, but Copy turns any preset or profile into
a new profile (your current settings with the preset's values on top) or a new
preset you can edit.

To ship a preset with the addon, add a file to Presets/ (see
Presets/Examples.lua) and list it in VideoProfiles.toc. It can call
ns.AddPreset with a name, author, notes and CVars, or simply
ns.AddPreset({ string = "VP2:..." }) with a string made in game with
Export.
Export and import
Export gives a compressed string (about 330 characters for a profile) you
can copy to another computer and paste into Import there. Import adds
profiles as profiles and presets as presets. Every setting is stored with
its CVar name, and unknown names are skipped on import.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /vp or /vp show | open the profiles in Options > AddOns |
| /vp save | save your current video settings as a new profile |
| /vp update | overwrite a profile with your current settings |
| /vp apply | switch to a profile |
| /vp applyreload | switch to a profile and reload the UI at once, handy in macros |
| /vp diff [> ] | list differences from current settings or another profile; presets are compared on the settings they set |
| /vp copy [> ] | copy a profile, or make a preset into a profile of your own |
| /vp preset list | list the presets (also /vp presets) |
| /vp preset apply | apply a preset's settings, keeping the rest of yours |
| /vp preset new [> ...] | make a preset from your current values of the listed CVars |
| /vp preset add / remove > ... | add or take out CVars |
| /vp preset set > | set a value in a preset |
| /vp preset update, rename, delete, copy, export | as for profiles, for your own presets |
| /vp preset notes / author > | set the text shown and shared with a preset |
| /vp rename
> | rename a profile |
| /vp delete | delete a profile |
| /vp export | show a profile as a string to copy to another computer |
| /vp import [string] | add a profile or preset from an export string, or open a box to paste it into |
| /vp list | list your profiles |
| /vp cvars | show which video CVars this client supports, with values, in a copy box |
| /vp help | list the commands |

Applying a profile is refused in combat. When display CVars such as resolution
or MSAA change, the graphics engine restarts. Afterwards a popup offers to…

Changelog1.3.0
• New: the enemy list, a window with every mob that is fighting you: its name, its health, whom it is attacking and
your own threat on it, and a strip that shows at a glance whether you hold it (as a tank: green = yours, red = loose
or on a healer or dps). The mobs that need you first (a tank: the ones that are not on them) come first.
• New: as a tank, a red "!" on the nameplate of each mob that is not on you, so you know which one to click to take it
back (the game does not let an addon target a mob from a list). It can be turned off in the preferences.
• New: the enemy list appears in combat, by default only when you are a tank (or the game doesn't say what you are);
the preferences also offer "Always" and "Never", and how many enemies it lists. With it on, the aggro window no
longer shows its "Other mobs" section.
1.2.2
• Fix: the welcome windows of several addons no longer show their text, buttons and links through each other when they open together: each one opens in front, with all its content, and a click brings it forward.
1.2.1
• Fix: the welcome window is opaque, so when the welcome windows of several of the author's addons open together each one hides the previous one instead of showing through it.
1.2.0
• New: the welcome window links to the other addons of the same author, to copy and paste in a browser.

hides the role, class and name of whom an enemy is attacking from addons in combat; they are now
never compared, joined to text or tested. A hidden name is shown as it is, without color or icon.
The same care is taken with every other value that comes from a unit.
• Fix: "attempt to perform numeric conversion on a secret number value" when measuring a line of the "Other
mobs" section: a text field that has shown a hidden name answers its size with a hidden number, so the
width is now measured on a field of its own that never gets one.
• Fix: the mob that is your target is told apart from the others by the game (not by its GUID).
1.1.1
• Fix: "Show other mobs in combat" raised an error in combat on clients that hide whom a mob is
attacking from addons ("attempt to perform boolean test on a secret boolean value"). Those lines
now simply don't say whether the mob attacks you, a pet or a player.
1.1.0
• Fix: the alert sounds when you take the aggro from someone else (your pet, say) even if your threat
jumped over the warning zone between two updates of the game; and it no longer sounds when the pet
takes the aggro back while your threat is still high. It re-arms only when your threat drops well
below the threshold.
• Faster "about to pull" alert: your own threat is checked every 0.1 s on its own (it used to wait for
the window to redraw, up to a quarter of a second), and the window redraws 0.05 s after a threat
event instead of 0.1 s. The game's own threat updates still set the limit.
• New: "Show other mobs in combat" (Preferences, off by default): under the list of your target,
one line per other mob you are fighting -- its name and whom it is attacking, with your own
threat on it where the client has it; the ones attacking you in red. A shield marks the tank
holding a mob and a paw a pet (alone, your pet is your tank). Needs enemy nameplates.

addons.description:
World of Warcraft addon: a small, movable aggro window for your target.
• Lists who has the aggro of your current target and how close the others are, in order (the one
holding it on top), with each player's class color and a tank / healer / dps icon.
• Optional sound (and red window border) when you are close to taking the aggro; the threshold and
the sound are in the preferences.
• Opens with /aggreao (/agg): prefs, toggle, lock / unlock, minimap, reset, changelog,
version. Right-click on the window or the minimap button also opens the preferences.

How well it works depends on what each client tells addons about threat: where
UnitDetailedThreatSituation is available it lists everybody's threat; where it gives nothing (or
the values are not readable by addons) it falls back to showing only the mob's current target as the
one with the aggro. Roles come from the group's assigned roles, the player's spec, or are guessed
for classes that can't do anything else (mage, rogue, hunter, warlock).

Supported clients (see Aggreao.toc): Retail, TBC Anniversary, Classic Era and
the Classic "Forever" beta. Development targets Forever for now.

1.2.1
• Fixed: the window comes above the windows of the author's other addons when it is shown or clicked (it was drawn under their contents and looked see-through).
• Fixed: the welcome window is opaque, so when the welcome windows of several of the author's addons open together each one hides the previous one instead of showing through it.
1.2.0

that item as an ingredient.
• New: right-click on an item opens the item menu wherever right-click would do nothing else (nothing to use or equip, and no vendor, bank, mail,
trade or auction window open).
1.1.1
• New: the welcome window links to the other addons of the same author, to copy and paste in a browser.
1.1.0
• New: a small public API for other addons, EmbolsaoAPI: the other characters with items saved, how many of an item they
have in their bags and banks, and who has it. (Fabrikao!! uses it to count ingredients across your characters.)
1.0.8
• Fixed: a stray scrollbar (arrows and thumb) could be left floating over the
right border of the window when the list didn't actually need one. The
bar now stays hidden unless the layout has made room for it, and the
layout is re-checked when the two disagree.
1.0.7
• Fixed (Classic "Forever" beta): the reagent bag and its items had vanished
from the bags window. Forever client 1.60.1 reports its own project ID
instead of passing as retail, and the addon took that to mean "no reagent
bag".
1.0.6

everything you wear into your bags (only if it all fits -- otherwise
nothing moves), whether or not "Unequip everything else" is ticked;

empty gearset offered no Equip at all.

menu the tabs have (Edit, Equip/Unequip, Hide, Delete).…
addons.description:
World of Warcraft addon (Retail, TBC Anniversary, Classic Era and the Classic
"Forever" beta) that replaces the built-in bags -- and the bank -- with its
own window: a merged/virtual inventory (identical items grouped into one
stack), category filter tabs, a name search box, sortable listing, Recent and
Junk groups, and empty-slot counters to drop new stacks into. The bank opens
in the same window, side by side with the bags.

A small nod to Apparcao.
Repo layout
The repo root is the addon (Embolsao.toc, .pkgmeta) — this is what release
tooling and CurseForge expect to package directly as Embolsao/. The code is
split by area under Modules/, in the same spirit as
Questie, each file with its unit tests
right next to it (X.lua + X.test.lua):
• images/ — source icon artwork (unprocessed).
• .github/workflows/release.yml — manual (workflow_dispatch only) release
pipeline via BigWigsMods/packager,
packaging the repo root and uploading to CurseForge. Tests are left out of
the package (.pkgmeta).
• .github/workflows/tests.yml — runs the tests on every push and PR.
Tests
Unit tests use busted's syntax and run
outside the game against a fake client (test/WowApiMock.lua): every test gets
a fresh one, then loads the addon's own files the way the game does (in .toc
order, sharing one namespace). From the repo root:

test/busted.lua is a small runner for the subset of busted the tests use, so
nothing has to be compiled on Windows. A new module gets its X.test.lua next
to it, starting with dofile("setupTests.lua").
Localization
UI strings live in Embolsao.L (Locales/), keyed by string ID. enUS.lua
defines every key as the English base and always loads first; other locale
files only override the keys they translate and early-return on
GetLocale() mismatch. Any key without a translation for the active client
locale falls back to English automatically — no addon crash, no missing text.

Currently translated: enUS (base), esES/esMX. To add another locale,
copy Locales/esES.lua, rename it, swap the locale check and the strings,
and list the new file in Embolsao.toc (must load after enUS.lua).
How it works
• Modules/Core/Core.lua scans every bag (backpack, bags, reagent bag) via C_Container
and groups identical items into a virtual inventory
(Embolsao.VirtualInventory), summing quantities across stacks — this can
be turned off per-item-type in Preferences (Consolidate Stacks), which
keys each physical stack separately instead of merging by itemID. Also
tracks every genuinely empty slot (Embolsao.EmptySlots).
• Modules/Filters/Filters.lua defines the single built-in tab ("All") and the matching logic
for custom tabs, which can combine whole categories/subcategories and
per-itemID overrides. Tabs come in two independent sets, the bags' and the
bank's (Embolsao:GetFilters(domain)).
• Modules/UI/UI.lua builds one standalone, resizable window (reusing Blizzard's own
frame templates -- PortraitFrameFlatTemplate, the bare ItemButton
widget type, UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate, the Blizzard_Menu API) holding up
to two panes side by side, bank and bags, each with its own tabs, search box
and footer. It takes over display duty from the native bag and bank frames
whenever the player opens them.
• Modules/Core/Compat.lua papers over the API differences between clients (namespaced
vs. global functions, the old vs. modern bank).
For other addons
Modules/API/API.lua exposes the global table EmbolsaoAPI, so another addon can use what Embolsao saves of the
other characters (bags and bank, account-wide) without its private namespace. It hands out copies and numbers only:
• EmbolsaoAPI.version -- the API's version (1)
• EmbolsaoAPI.GetCharacters() -- { { key, name, class, time }, ... }, the other characters with items saved, by name
• EmbolsaoAPI.GetOthersItemCount(itemID) -- bags, bank: how many the other characters have in all
• EmbolsaoAPI.GetItemHolders(itemID) -- { { key, name, class, bags, bank }, ... }, who has the item, by name…

addons.changelog:
Changelog0.5.0
• New: under a recipe in "You can learn", the creatures that drop the pattern or recipe that teaches it (with their level and chance, and the map and waypoint icons) and the containers it is found in, after the trainers and vendors; an item that drops from any creature says so. The "nobody is known" message is only for recipes with no source at all.
• New: Classic Era and TBC Anniversary. The same addon now loads on those clients (one folder, a TOC per client), with the recipes of each game, including Jewelcrafting in TBC.
• New: on those clients, what a character knows is read from its profession windows the first time they are opened (and every time after), so open each profession once. The Craft button opens the profession's window on the recipe.
• Fix: on Classic Era and TBC, the Craft button no longer closes the profession's window when it is already open; it just picks the recipe in it.
• New: on Classic Era and TBC, the tooltip of what a recipe makes also shows what you wear in that slot (both slots for rings, trinkets and weapons), with a green "Equipped" title on it, with no key to hold. Forever already does it by itself.
• Data: the recipes of Classic Era and TBC come from the game's own tables and open databases: trainers with their cost and the skill they ask, drop and skinning chances, and the books and quests of the Expert and Artisan ranks.
0.4.6
• Data: the trainers of several professions, as the public databases have them now.
0.4.5
• Data: recipe data with a few more recipes, sources and trainers, as the public databases have them now.
0.4.4
• Data: fresh recipe data, as the public databases have them now.
0.4.3
• Fix: the next rank of a profession ("Can train: Journeyman") shows up as soon as the skill is the one a trainer asks for (50 of 75, 125 of 150, 200 of 225...), instead of waiting for the skill to reach the cap of the current rank.
0.4.2
• Fix: "You can learn" no longer lists recipes that nobody teaches out of season: the Winter Veil ones (Gingerbread Cookie, Egg Nog, Green Holiday Shirt, Edge of Winter, Winter's Might, Winter Clothes and Boots) and the Lunar Festival fireworks launchers. They are still in the profession's page.
0.4.1
• Fix: the "View Quest" button in the panel of a recipe that comes from a quest is Completao!!'s icon, next to the map and waypoint icons, instead of a text button drawn under them.
0.4.0
• New: an icon at the right of "You can learn" orders its recipes by proximity (as before, the default), by level or by name; the choice is kept.
• Data: fresh recipe data, as the public databases have them now.
• Fix: the welcome windows of several addons no longer show their text, buttons and links through each other when they open together: each one opens in front, with all its content, and a click brings it forward.
0.3.0
• New: look at your other characters' professions. A picker above the professions ("My professions" and each alt) shows an alt's professions and
the recipes it knows as if it were the one playing, with its skill levels and how many it could make with its own bags (from Embolsao!!'s
copies, when installed). The window turns blue and says whose they are, as Embolsao!! does with another character's bags, and there is no
crafting. An alt appears once you have logged in with it with this version.
• New: a button above the professions lists the professions you have not learned too, so you can browse their recipes.
• New: the start screen has your professions (top left), what you can craft now (bottom left: what your bags allow, orange first, with
how many; a click opens the game's profession window on that recipe, as the Craft button does) and, on the whole right side, what you
can learn: the ranks a trainer can teach and the recipes your skill reaches that you don't know, by profession, the ones with the
nearest trainer or vendor first. A click on…
addons.description:
World of Warcraft professions addon. Your professions companion: browse recipes, plan what to craft, and find out where to get every recipe and ingredient.

For WoW Forever (Fabrikao.toc: interface 16001), Classic Era (Fabrikao_Vanilla.toc: 11508, 11509) and TBC Anniversary
(Fabrikao_TBC.toc: 20506). What it does is in CURSEFORGE_DESCRIPTION.md and CHANGELOG.md: the
character's professions, every recipe of the game (known or not) with filters, a table and a detailed view, a panel with everything
known about a recipe, a search of every recipe, trainers, vendors and creatures on the map (and TomTom waypoints), and optional
the professions and known recipes of your other characters (read only), and optional integrations with Embolsao (items of the other
characters) and Auctionator (prices).

addons.description:
WoW Forever (beta, client 1.60.1) port of DPSPulse.

DPSPulse Forever shows a realtime rolling DPS graph and current DPS value during combat, with a Details-style dual-series overlay (rolling window + full-session).

This port began as a straight port of DPSPulse tag v0.3.0. The graph and damage-tracking behavior remain unchanged, while the WoW Forever edition now adds native in-game options and a choice of window skins.
Status
• Interface: 16001 (confirmed via in-game GetBuildInfo() on build 1.60.1.69893).
• CurseForge project ID: 1719813; WoW Forever 1.60.1 release uploads are enabled.
• Version 0.2.0 adds an Esc > Options > AddOns panel and a live, persistent Blizzard/native skin.
WoW Forever combat log limitation
WoW Forever hard-taints (ForceTaint_strong) any addon that registers COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED, so this port uses the taint-free UNIT_COMBAT event instead. That comes with real caveats vs. the TBC original:
• Damage is only counted while the mob is your current target. If you tab off mid-fight (or the mob dies before you retarget) any in-flight events are lost.
• Group content may over-count. UNIT_COMBAT fires for damage the unit takes, not damage you deal — in a party/raid, other players' hits on the same mob will inflate your numbers. Solo and small-group tuning is where this port shines.
• DoTs and environmental damage may not be surfaced. UNIT_COMBAT skips much of what the combat log covers.
• Only WOUND actions are tracked (actual damage). Misses/dodges/parries/blocks are ignored for DPS math.

This is intentional — WoW Forever's design philosophy on combat log privacy is respected. See PLAN.md for the upstream API investigation notes.
Options and commands
All display settings are available under Esc > Options > AddOns > DPSPulse Forever (with a legacy Interface Options registration fallback). The panel controls visibility, position lock, rolling window (2–60 seconds), UI scale (0.5–2), debug mode, Classic/Blizzard skin, session reset, and window-position reset. Changes apply immediately and persist in DPSPulseForeverDB where applicable.

Slash commands remain available:
• /dpspulseforever (alias /dpsf) — toggle frame.
• /dpsf show, hide, lock, unlock, reset, or debug.
• /dpsf window and /dpsf scale .
• /dpsf skin and /dpsf resetposition.

addons.description:
Play live in Musician using a simplified keyboard based on the Guid Wars 2 bindings.

This aims to be an alternative to Ayalaes's Musician Options that is no longer maintained.

It's still a work in progress. Feel free to join our Discord server to discuss about the plugin.
Bindings
• 1-8 or NUMPAD1-NUMPAD8 : Play note
• 9 or NUMPAD9 or LEFT : Octave down
• 0 or NUMPAD0 or RIGHT : Octave up
• SPACE (hold) : Sustain
• SHIFT + 1-8 : Toggle note semitone shift. You can't shift a key if the resulting note is the same as the one next to it.

addons.description:
Play live with Musician using a MIDI keyboard.
Table of contents
• How it works
• Choosing the translator
• Setting up the translator
• Solution 1: Bome MIDI Translator Classic
• Solution 2: Bome MIDI Translator Pro
• Solution 3: Musician MIDI Pico Translator
• Configuration for macOS
1. Function keys configuration
2. Permissions
• How to play
• Deal with audio delay
• Using a hardware synthesizer
• Using a software synthesizer
1. Install Sforzando
2. Install FlexASIO (optional, Windows only)
3. Configure Sforzando
4. Configure MIDI thru (optional)
5. Play!
How it works
There is no possible way to use MIDI in World of Warcraft. The trick is to translate the MIDI note events that come from your MIDI controller into PC keyboard keystrokes, that can then be captured by the add-on interface.

The translator can be either:
• a third party application that runs on your computer and emulates a PC keyboard

or
• a custom MIDI interface that connects directly to your MIDI controller using a 5-pin DIN connector on one side, and to your computer as a standard USB PC keyboard on the other side.
Choosing the translator
There are 3 translator solutions available to you, each of them having their pros and cons. It's up to you to choose the most suitable for you:
1. Bome MIDI Translator Classic : recommended solution if you play on Windows and already have a standard MIDI interface or USB MIDI controller. It's simple to configure and easy to use. It's a charged program for commercial use (29 €) but you can use it for free without any limitation (remember WinRAR).
2. Bome MIDI Translator Pro : recommended solution if you play on macOS and already have a standard MIDI interface or USB MIDI controller. As for the classic version, it's simple to configure and easy to use but it's quite expensive (79 €). You can use the free trial version but you have to restart it every 20 minutes.
3. Musician MIDI Pico Translator : Plug and play DIY solution for MIDI controllers with a 5-pin DIN MIDI output. The parts are inexpensive (less than 10 €) and easy to source from online and local retailers. The building process is straightforward and just requires basic tools such as soldering iron. It's recognized by the computer as a standard USB keyboard so no additional software or driver is required. It also includes a MIDI to USB interface that can be used with music production software or a software synthesizer to mitigate the audio delay issue.

| | Solution | Type | OS | Price | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Bome MIDI Translator Classic | Software | Windows | 0 - 29 € | Free | Windows only |
| 2. | Bome MIDI Translator Pro | Software | Windows / macOS | 79 € | Works on macOS | Expensive |
| 3. | Musician MIDI Pico Translator | Hardware | Windows / macOS / Linux | ⚠️ If you're running macOS, a few extra configuration steps are required regardless of the solution you chose. Check out the Configuration for macOS section when you're done.

> ⚠️ If you need a 5-pin DIN MIDI to USB interface to use with Bome MIDI Translator, make sure to use a quality product like the Roland UM-ONE mk2 to avoid problems. Avoid the cheap off-brand models from Amazon and AliExpress.

Feel free to join our Discord server for further assistance.
Solution 1: Bome MIDI Translator Classic
Download and install Bome MIDI Translator Classic.

1. Connect your MIDI controller.
2. Start Bome MIDI Translator Classic.
3. Open the Musician preset.bmtp file that is provided in the Interface/AddOns/MusicianMIDI folder.
4. Open the Midi In menu.
5. Select your MIDI input device.

Solution 2: Bome MIDI Translator Pro
Download and install Bome MIDI Translator Pro.

1. Connect and turn on your MIDI controller.
2. Start Bome MIDI Translator Pro.

===================

WoW Dings allows you to add funny symbols into your chat messages such as smilies, arrows, hearts etc. Just type the code corresponding to the symbol you want in your message, it will be automatically replaced. For example, :) will be replaced by ☺, (l) will become ♥ and so on. Of course, other players do not need the addon to see the symbols you insert. However, the symbols may not be visible to players who have changed the default font of the game by another one that does not include the symbols.

Also works in Battle.net discussions.

Doesn't work for /say, /yell and /raidwarning messages.

Also implements the following macro shortcuts:
• (here) Name of your current location
• (pin) World map pin of your current location (WoW Retail only)
• (t) Detailed information about the targeted player

Type /wd to display the list of available symbols.

addons.changelog:
Changelog1.0.0
First release, for World of Warcraft: Forever and Retail.
• Rain and snow on demand, anywhere, for as long as you want. When the server
sends its own rain or snow, Comfy Rain steps aside and lets the real thing fall.
• Four intensities each, plus monsoon and blizzard.
• /comfy auto matches the server's current weather in one shot.
• Layered ambience built from the game's own weather loops, with wind gusts and
distant thunder. Two beds of unequal length run under each other so the loop
never settles into a recognisable cycle.
• A Volume slider for the rain and snow that leaves your game volume alone.
Thunder and wind follow the game's own volume for now.
• Gusts drive the rain, the sound and the light from one shared signal.
• Rain streaks and snow flakes are smaller and far more numerous, so heavy
weather reads as a downpour or a real snowfall rather than as bars and
snowballs drawn over the screen, and the distant layer is visible again
behind the near one. Blizzard streaks no longer read as scratches on glass.
• Time-of-day grading: hold the world at dusk, or run it on your own clock.
• Fades down under a roof rather than raining on the ceiling.
• A settings window at /comfyrain. Every control shows the slash command it ran.
addons.description:
Rain or snow wherever you are, for as long as you want.

World of Warcraft decides when it rains. The server picks the weather, it picks it per
zone, and a lot of zones never get any. Comfy Rain is the switch the game does not give you:
type /comfy and it is raining, in Durotar, in Elwynn, at the top of a mountain, on the
deck of the boat. Type it again and it stops.

Works on WoW Forever and Retail. The Classic versions are not supported yet (issue #20).

It knows when to get out of the way. If the server sends a real storm, Comfy Rain stands
aside and lets it fall: the game's own rain is 3D, so it stops under an arch or a bridge
the way rain should, and where the real thing exists it is simply the better of the two.

What you get
| | |
|---|---|
| Rain and snow | Four intensities each, from a drizzle to a monsoon or a whiteout blizzard |
| Sound | Blizzard's own weather loops, layered and endlessly varied, with distant thunder |
| Wind | Gusts that move the rain, the sound and the light together, not on a timer |
| Time of day | Hold the world at dusk, or run it on your clock instead of the realm's. Works on its own, with the rain switched off |
| Indoors | Fades down under a roof instead of raining on the ceiling |
| The game's own weather | When the game is raining or snowing for real, Comfy Rain hides so you never see both, and comes back when it stops. It cannot stop the game's weather; no addon can. /comfy defer off keeps yours on top |
| Scenes | /comfy preset cozy, storm, snow or overcast sets a whole weather; dusk or night sets just the time of day. Each leaves the other alone, so night with no rain is /comfy off plus /comfy preset night |
| A settings window | /comfyrain, the minimap button, the addon compartment, or a keybind of your own. Every control shows you the command it ran, so you learn them by using it |
Getting started
That is the whole thing. Everything below is optional.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /comfy | Turn the weather on or off |
| /comfy preset cozy · storm · snow · overcast | A whole look in one go. Also buttons at the top of the settings window |
| /comfy preset dusk · night | Just the light. The weather stays as it is |
| /comfy rain · /comfy snow | Pick which |
| /comfy light · normal · heavy | How hard |
| /comfy monsoon · /comfy blizzard | The two extremes |
| /comfy auto | Match whatever the server is doing right now |
| /comfyrain | Open the settings window |

The rest of the commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /comfy indoors off \| dim \| on | What happens under a roof. dim is the default |
| /comfy sound on \| off | The ambience bed |
| /comfy volume 0.5 | How loud, over the weather only |
| /comfy thunder on \| off | Lightning and thunder |
| /comfy channel Ambience \| SFX \| Master | Which of the game's volume sliders owns it |
| /comfy time local | Light the world by your clock, not the realm's. Works with the rain off |
| /comfy time 21 · /comfy time +9 | Hold one hour, or shift the realm's by that many |
| /comfy time strength 0.6 | How far towards that hour. The rest is in the settings window |
| /comfy status | What it currently thinks it is doing |
| /comfy reset | Back to defaults |

/rain is an alias for /comfy, and /comfyui also opens the window.
What it is, honestly
Comfy Rain is a screen-space overlay. It draws scrolling layers of rain in front of the
camera and dims the frame behind them. It does not touch the game's 3D weather system,
its particles, its lighting or its sky, because addons are not allowed anywhere near any
of those.

In practice that means:
• It looks right when you are looking at the world. It is weather on your screen.
• It cannot put rain outside a window while you stand indoors. There is one overlay and
no way to ask the client which pixels are sky, so indoors it fades to a faint wash
instead. /comfy indoors off turns it off entirely.…

Navigation
• Waypoint Arrow marks the selected final destination; Journey and the yellow map route retain intermediate travel guidance.

• In-game Service Finder selects destinations through the local route planner. Ctrl-click navigation also works in the map quest list.
• Journey labels departure waits and ride duration, counts down known departures and arrivals, and identifies unknown schedules as estimates. Fixes the zeppelin observer error.
In-game interface
• Quest tracker supports header-only, nearby (200 yards), and full views. Empty nearby results collapse to the header.
• Journey fits its text and grows upward. Floating Heals and minimap labels retain black outlines.
• Updated square minimap, 12-hour clock, whole-number coordinates, consistent icons, action-button styling, and thin XP bar.
• Bag organization and category word filters; compact Heals and Quick Bar styling; matching resize controls.

Validation: 60 local regression test files plus Studio and updater checks. Live gameplay and visual verification remain important. Personal settings, SavedVariables and character snapshots are excluded.

Questie tracker
• Keeps Questie functionality with the WFK appearance: rounded panel, Arial Narrow text, orange title, and matching white icons.
• The selected quest is highlighted in neon orange and moves to a Current Selected section at the top. Changing selection scrolls to the top; ordinary objective updates do not.
• Adds a visible scrollbar, whole-row edge clipping, square appearance switch, and filled corner resize triangle that turns orange on hover.
• Fixes the resize lock error and Questie initialization error.
• Shows accepted WoW Forever quests from the native quest log when their records are missing from Questie’s database.

Navigation and package
• Hides TomTom’s arrow and coordinates when WaypointUI is loaded, while preserving TomTom waypoint support.
• Includes the bundled addon suite, including Questie, QuestieDB, TomTom, and WaypointUI. Personal settings are not included.
Updating

Changes in this Release:
• LootsUI 0.4.8: applies the Forever preset at login while the beta forgets your settings, with a switch to turn it off
addons.description:
Hide and show interface frames with macro conditionals, on every flavor of World of Warcraft.

Give a frame a rule like mod:ctrl show; hide and Loot's UI keeps it out of the way
until you want it. Action bars, unit frames, the minimap, bags, the objective tracker, the
cooldown manager, the damage meter and more, each with its own rule. On top of the game's own conditionals, LootsUI adds a few of its own,
so a rule can react to things the macro system has no idea about.

LootsUI was heavily inspired by DinksUI, which
showed how well macro conditionals work for driving what your interface shows. It was built to
take that idea further, with a set of custom conditions of its own and support for every flavor
of the game.
Getting started
1. Type /loots to open the options.
2. Pick a preset from the Presets tab to see it working, or go straight to a tab and write your
own rules.
3. Frames with an empty box are left alone.

Presets overwrite the rules in the active profile, and ask before doing it. See the Profiles
section below for keeping settings per character and backing them up.
Commands
| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| /loots | Opens the options |
| /loots show | Reveals everything without losing your rules |
| /loots hide | Puts your rules back in charge |
| /loots toggle | Flips between the two, handy in a macro |
| /loots status | Prints the rule in effect for each frame |
| /loots debug | Prints what LootsUI thinks is true right now |
| /loots trace | Prints what the saved settings looked like at each stage of the session |

/lootsui works the same as /loots.
Writing rules
A rule is a list of conditions and what to do when they match.

Several bracket groups in a row mean or, so mod:ctrl show; hide matches if
either is true. Commas inside one group mean and, so [combat,damaged] needs both. The
last part of a rule with no brackets is the fallback, which is why show; hide reads as "show
when something above matched, otherwise hide".

Your rule is handed to the game's own macro parser, so **anything valid in a macro is valid
here**, including [mod:alt], [flying], [group:raid], [form:1] and [@target,exists].
The full reference is the macro conditionals
documentation, with more background in the
macro documentation.
LootsUI conditions
These are added by LootsUI. Mix them with the game's own conditionals freely, use them inside
the same brackets, and put no in front of any of them to invert it.
Combat
| Condition | True when |
| --- | --- |
| [lastcombat] | You are in combat, or left it fewer than eight seconds ago |
| [lastcombat:15] | You are in combat, or left it fewer than the given seconds ago |
| [recentcombat] | The same as [lastcombat:8], for rules that read better without a number |

The game's own [combat] cuts off the instant a fight ends. These keep a frame around for a
moment afterwards, so the cast bar, cooldowns or a damage meter do not vanish while you are
still looking at them. Use [nolastcombat:30] to mean "well out of combat".
Health
| Condition | True when |
| --- | --- |
| [damaged] | Your health is below maximum |
| [damaged:70] | Your health is below 70 percent |

Retail and World of Warcraft: Forever sometimes keep health and resource numbers back from
addons, in PvP matches for instance. While they do, [damaged] and the resource conditions read
as false rather than guessing, and /loots debug says the value is hidden by the game. On
Forever the numbers are hidden most of the time, so build rules there on [recentcombat] and
the game's own conditionals instead.
Resources
| Condition | True when |
| --- | --- |
| [resource] | Your resource is below maximum |
| [resource:90] | Your resource is below the percent you give |
| [noresource] | Your resource is completely empty |
| [fullresource] | Your resource is full |

Resource means whatever your character is running on at that moment, mana, rage, energy, focus…

addons.description:
A complete mailbox for World of Warcraft. Collect, sort, send, search and track
your mail, on every version of the game from Classic Era to modern Retail, and
on World of Warcraft: Forever.

Parcel exists because Postal stopped being maintained and Mailbox Plus was
discontinued, leaving a gap where the most used utility addon in the game used
to be. It is a full replacement for the default mail window, not a set of buttons
bolted onto it: one click empties your mailbox, and a real scrolling window with
search, sorting and click shortcuts replaces the seven row pane.

Then it goes further than either addon it replaces.

History. Every mail Parcel sees is archived and stays searchable long after
it has left your mailbox. Find the item somebody posted you months ago, read the
letter again, and see what became of it.

Auction house data. What you earned, what sold, what the house took, and
what a listing actually netted after deposit and cut, all worked out from the
mail the auction house already sends you. No scanning and no second addon.

It works away from the mailbox. Open Parcel anywhere to search your history
and read your auction numbers. The inbox says plainly when it is showing records
rather than live mail.

It watches every character. At login Parcel tells you which of your alts has
mail about to expire, because it remembers what was waiting in their mailboxes.
Nothing else can tell you that.
Features
Inbox
• Parcel's own scrolling window in place of the seven row pane, with no paging
• Search as you type across senders, subjects, item names and mail text
• Sort by sender, subject, value or time remaining
• Hover a mail for every attachment, what is enclosed, and its fate on expiry
• An icon per row shows whether a mail returns or is deleted when it runs out,
and clicking it does that now
• Shift-click to take a mail, ctrl-click to return it, right-click to tick it
• Select a range, or everything from one sender, then Open or Return the lot
• Parcel's own reader opens beside the window with working attachments

Collecting
• One button empties the mailbox, gold and attachments, until nothing is left
• Never automates cash on delivery or Blizzard mail
• Full bags only hold back mail carrying items, so auction gold still comes in
• Keeps as many bag slots free as you ask, and still takes anything that tops up
a stack you already carry
• Handles mailboxes past the hundred mail cap, asking the server for the rest
• Collect only what you want: auction sales, wins, expiries, cancellations,
outbid notices, Postmaster mail and everything else are separate switches
• Shift-click Collect to take everything and ignore those filters for one run
• Reports every mail to chat with item links and a total when it finishes

History
• Every mail Parcel sees is archived and indexed, and outlives your mailbox
• Search with from: to: item: subject: body: type:, or plain words
• Mistype something and it falls back to near matches instead of nothing
• Filter by character, or look across all of them
• Reopen any archived mail in full, attachments and tooltips intact
• Records whether each mail was collected, returned, deleted or is still waiting
• Mark a record taken by hand when Parcel was not watching
• Keep as much or as little as you like, by days and by a hard entry ceiling

Auction house
• Earned, sold, house cut and spent, by day, week, month, year or all time
• Top sellers ranked by what they actually netted, not by how many moved
• Click any of them for its own panel: every sale, the average per unit, the
best one, and the span it sold over
• Every sale listed with the deposit and the cut broken out
• Profit and loss counts the gold you take at a vendor, so buying under the
vendor price and selling the difference reads as the profit it is
• Vendored items are matched back to the auction they were bought at, with one
line in chat when you leave the vendor…

• QuickKeybindMode 1.1.0: World of Warcraft: Forever support, and Retail 12.1.0
addons.description:
One command, straight into keybinding.
Overview
World of Warcraft has a built in Quick Keybind Mode: hover any action button, press a key, and it binds instantly. No dropdowns, no scrolling through a list of every command in the game. The catch is that it sits behind the Game Menu, then Key Bindings, then a button in the corner of that panel.

QuickKeybindMode puts it one chat command away. Type /kb and you are binding.
Usage
| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| /kb | Enters Quick Keybind Mode |
| /quickkeybind | The same thing, spelled out |
| /qkb | Replaces /kb when ElvUI is enabled, since ElvUI already uses /kb for its own keybind mode |

Once you are in, hover an action button and press the key you want. Press Escape or click Okay when you are finished to save your bindings.

If you type the command during combat, it tells you to wait, because the game does not allow binding changes while you are in combat.

An online member list and shared chat (/tcg) across multiple guilds on the same realm.
Supports WoW Forever (Interface 16xxx) and TBC Anniversary (20xxx). Classic Era, Wrath,
Cataclysm, MoP, and Retail are not supported. All participants need the same version.

TBC: the client does not allow addon messages to channels, and channel chat requires
player input. The addon therefore uses regular messages prefixed with GF1# in a hidden
transport channel. The addon hides this channel; members without the addon can see its messages.

on a keypress or click (roughly every four minutes), and through addon whispers while you are idle.
Players coming online receive direct replies from other participants. Inactive players are removed
after ten minutes. TBC support has not yet been fully verified in the game.

Free and open source
Three parts, on purpose:

1. The project. Sagalore is free and open source (MIT). The addon, the companion, and the API are in this repository. Anyone can read the code, run it, and host their own server on any host that runs containers (or a Go binary) and Postgres.
2. The official server. The easiest way to start is the official server at sagalore.app / api.sagalore.app, which is free to use. Your data is stored there, and you sign in with Battle.net.
3. The MCP. There is an official MCP that lets your AI create sagas. It is built on the open Sagalore API and runs on Smia, a platform we also make. The MCP is not in this repo: Sagalore stays independent of any one platform, and the listing is also a way to show people Smia. Want your own MCP? The API is documented — build away. See docs/API.md and docs/oauth.md.

The marketing site is a separate repository (sagalore/website). This product repo does not ship or serve the landing page.
Project status
Early public / alpha. One maintainer. Expect rough edges, unsigned binaries, and slow replies on issues.
• Built with heavy Cursor (AI) assistance for a lot of the code. Architecture and merge decisions are human-owned; review PRs as carefully as you would any agent-assisted codebase.
• Assets were AI-generated or AI-assisted too: logo / emblem / wordmark, landing copy, and UI frames / chrome. Treat the brand as provisional, not commissioned art.
• Day-to-day development and playtesting: macOS Apple silicon, WoW Classic Era (and Forever). The Windows companion is built in CI; in-game Windows play is not systematically tested.
• Not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. Unofficial software; ToS risk is yours.
• Release binaries are not signed. Gatekeeper and SmartScreen warnings are expected.
• Leaderboard finish times are client-reported (honor-based), not anti-cheat.
Try it locally
You need Docker, Go, and a WoW client. Postgres and the API come from Compose. Login in development uses SAGALORE_DEV_TOKEN so you do not need a Battle.net app for the first run.

That starts Postgres and the API, waits for /healthz, and seeds the Elwynn tutorial sagas. In another terminal:

The API container must have the same SAGALORE_DEV_TOKEN. make dev sets dev-token for local use only.

The companion installs Interface/AddOns/Sagalore. In game, /reload, then /sagalore or /sl.

If the database already has sagas and no group, set SAGALORE_BOOTSTRAP_GROUP=slug:Name before the API starts.
Self-host
Anyone can run the API + Postgres and point a companion at it. Short checklist and env table: docs/self-hosting.md. For a real (non-dev-token) login you need your own Battle.net app, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, and secrets as described there. Official release binaries bake SAGALORE_API_URL; self-hosted companions pass --api-url.
What you set before a real login
• Register a Battle.net application for this host. The redirect URI is {PUBLIC_BASE_URL}/v1/auth/bnet/callback. Blizzard will not accept a random loopback port, so the secret stays on the API.
• BNET_CLIENT_ID and BNET_CLIENT_SECRET on the API.
• PUBLIC_BASE_URL for that redirect and for signed cover URLs.
• Official release binaries get the public API URL from the GitHub Actions variable SAGALORE_API_URL (-ldflags). A self-hosted companion passes --api-url.
Groups
A player is a Battle.net account (bnet_account_id and BattleTag). Characters come from the addon. A name and realm sticks to the first account that linked it. If the character line includes a BattleTag, it must match the logged-in account.…

addons.description:
Sort options for the default quest tracker in WoW Forever and MoP Classic. It keeps
Blizzard's tracker and only changes the order of your quests, so the tracker still looks and
works as usual, with mouse or controller.
Features
• Sort tracked quests by zone (current zone first), level, level reversed, title or
distance (WoW Forever).
• Completed quests at the top or bottom.
• Sort menu: the filter button on the tracker's Quests header, the quest right-click
menu, R3 while the tracker has controller focus, or a key binding
(Key Bindings > AddOns). Fully usable with a controller: D-pad, A to pick, B to close.
• Objective sound: plays a sound when an objective of a tracked quest completes.

On MoP Classic the options are in the tracker header's right-click menu.
Commands
| | |
|---|---|
| /iqt | show the settings and commands |
| /iqt sort off\|zone\|level\|levelr\|title\|distance | sort mode |
| /iqt completed off\|top\|bottom | where completed quests go |
| /iqt zonefirst | toggle current zone first |
| /iqt sound | toggle the objective complete sound |
| /iqt menu | open the sort menu |
| /iqt debug | list tracked quests and whether the tracker shows them |

When the tracker is full, Blizzard only shows the quests that fit; the addon reorders the
tracked list so those are your top-sorted quests. Raise the Objective Tracker height in Edit
Mode to see more.

CraftBoard 1.0: from a crafting-order board to a crafting companion for Forever.
Added
• Find: "Hide what I can craft" in the Filter menu leaves out what you can get without anyone
else: what this character makes, and items your characters on this realm and faction make and
can mail you. An enchant only an alt knows stays listed (without a scroll it has to be put on
your gear in person), with the other players who know it. Professions with nothing left drop
out of the menu while it is on.
• Plan tab: your professions with their learned recipes by skill-up colour (orange, yellow,
green, grey), ready ones first. The card says how many crafts reach the next milestone, when you

Queue adds the planned crafts to your queue; Craft makes them while that profession's window is
open, one click per batch.
• Craft and Craft next on the queue: make a queued craft, or the next one your bags allow, from
the Requests tab while the profession window is open.
• Mats across alts: CraftBoard remembers bags and bank per character; reagent slots show "+12 on
alts" and item tooltips say which alt holds how many.
• Reagent tooltips: how many of your recipes use the item and what your queue needs of it.
• Recipe tooltips: which of your characters know the recipe, can learn it, or need more skill.
• Buy missing mats: at a merchant, one button buys the vendor reagents your queue still lacks.
• Cooldown-ready notice and trainer reminders (one quiet chat line each; options).
• The minimap button's tooltip sums it up: requests you can craft, the queue, ready cooldowns,
trainable ranks.
• Welcome window rewritten for the wider focus.
• Requests tab reworked: rows show what is wanted (item icon and name, "3x" for more than one)
and who asked, in a muted "Bob · 8m". New group order: "You can craft" (board requests and chat
asks one of your characters can make, ready ones first), "My queue", "Open requests", "Seen in
chat", "My requests". Rows older than 10 minutes are dimmed. A Filter with "Only what I can
craft", a right-click menu on every row, and a count on the Requests tab.
• The request card says whether you know the recipe (or which alt does), whether they bring the
mats, what you are missing, and how often they asked. The chat line is only quoted when it says
more than the title. Asking again for the same thing updates the one row instead of adding one.
• Crafter queue: "Queue" on a request you can craft; "My queue" lists them with an "All reagents"
row summing everything against your bags and bank. A trade that hands the craft over takes it
off the queue.
• Multi-crafter chains: when a craft needs an intermediate someone else makes (for example an
Elixir of Lesser Defense for Toughened Leather Gloves), reagent tooltips name who makes it,
"Post linked orders" asks the board for it, and Post request in Find posts those linked orders
with the request. Linked orders show on each other's cards and are retracted together.

left next to crafters in Find; /cb cd lists your characters' cooldowns.

chat), a button under the trade window casts it on their item in "Will not be traded". It
waits while the enchant's reagents aren't in your bags.
• Private "crafted for you" counts, read from completed trades and shown on crafter and request
tooltips. Never sent anywhere.
• "Back online" notice: one quiet chat line when a player whose request you can craft, or offered
on, logs back in (option, default on).
• Group tooltips: in a party or raid, item tooltips name the group members who can craft the item…
addons.description:
A crafting companion for World of Warcraft: Forever: level your professions, plan and craft,
and find crafters or customers.

Forever brought back the Classic world but not retail's crafting orders, so finding a crafter still
means repeating "LF LW, have mats" in Trade and hoping. CraftBoard adds a crafting board to the
game's own Professions window: see who can craft what, whisper them, or post a request that
crafters on your realm can see.

Download: CurseForge or the
GitHub releases. Works with the
CurseForge app and WowUp under the Forever game version.
Features
• Part of the Professions window. CraftBoard is a tab under your profession tabs, built from
the same frame, fonts and textures as Blizzard's window. Characters without professions get the
same board as a standalone window.
• Recipes shared automatically. Open each profession window once and every recipe you know is
shared with other CraftBoard users on your realm. Bind-on-Pickup crafts are never shared, since
nobody can hand those over.
• Find. Search any item and see everyone who can craft it, grouped by category like
Blizzard's list. Reagents show what you have and what is missing. "Hide what I can craft" in the
Filter menu leaves out what you or your alts can already provide (an alt's enchant stays, since
it can't reach your gear), so only crafts you need someone else for are listed.
• Requests. Post an order with a quantity and a note. Crafters see it on the board and offer
with one click.
• Seen in chat. Players asking for a crafter in Trade or General ("LF enchanter", "WTB [item]")
are listed on the Requests tab, with a green check when you can make it. This works even when
nobody else on your realm runs CraftBoard.
• Plan your leveling. The Plan tab sorts your recipes by skill-up colour, says how many crafts
reach the next rank, and reminds you when to visit your trainer.
• Craft from the board. Queue crafts from requests or your plan, then Craft next works through
them while the profession window is open. At a vendor, one button buys the missing thread,
vials and flux.
• Your alts count. Reagents on your other characters show up in slots and tooltips, and recipe
tooltips say which of your characters can learn a recipe.
• Queue and chains. Queue the requests you take on and see the reagents for all of them at
once. When a craft needs an intermediate someone else makes, post linked orders for it.
• Trade window help. One click casts a requested enchant on your partner's item, and
CraftBoard privately counts how often you've crafted for each other.
• Cooldowns. Transmute and Mooncloth cooldowns show next to crafters; /cb cd lists yours.
• Busy mode. Mark yourself busy and other users see you greyed out and can't whisper you from
the board. It turns on by itself in dungeons and raids.
• Advertise. One button posts a single plain line to Trade for players without the addon, at
most once a minute.
• In your language. English, German, French and Spanish.
• Easy to reach. Minimap button, addon compartment, a key binding, and /cb.
Principles
• Nothing happens on its own. CraftBoard never sends a whisper, invite, trade or chat line
without your click. No keyword auto-replies.
• No gold. Prices and tips are agreed in whispers, like always. Nothing here works like an
auction house or GDKP.
• Fair ordering. Online crafters are listed first, then shuffled each session. There are no
ratings, featured spots or anything you can pay for.
• Private by default. Chat lines are kept in memory for 30 minutes and never saved or shared.
"Crafted for you" counts stay on your computer.
• Non-combat. Unaffected by Forever's combat addon restrictions.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /cb | Open or close CraftBoard |
| /cb find [text], /cb requests, /cb plan | Open a tab (Find searches for the text) |
| /cb busy | Toggle busy |
| /cb cd | List crafting cooldowns on your characters |…

of your professions or a recipe you know; the card shows the chat line and, for a known
recipe, your reagents. Whisper opens the chat box to the player with
