Fixes #10

Titan [Reputation Continued]v12.1.0.3 (2026-10-04)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• feat: follow the faction shown as experience bar
Picking a faction as "Show as Experience Bar" in the reputation panel now
switches the button to it, and at login the button adopts it while it
shows no faction. Shift-click still picks another faction in between.
Auto Show Changed is disabled in the menu while a faction is shown as
experience bar, with a tooltip on how to use it again.
The panel fires no UPDATE\_FACTION for that pick, so the watched-faction
setters are hooked instead.

Titan [Reputation Continued]v12.1.0.2 (2026-10-04)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• chore(dev): drop IDE stubs of Titan routines removed in 9.3.3
68 of the hand-written stubs declared Titan globals that 9.3.3 no longer
has (moved into Titan\_G). The addon uses none of them, and keeping them
hid accidental calls from the language server, as happened with
TitanUtils\_GetAddOnMetadata.
• chore(dev): update TitanIDE from Titan 9.3.3
• fix: use singular time units for one minute or hour
Durations and time-to-level always used the plural unit ("1mins",
"1hrs 1mins"). Use the singular one for a count of one; hours get their
own singular string, as "h" is the per-hour rate unit.
• fix: keep collapsed sub-headers grouped in the tooltip
Rows put back for a collapsed header are read by ID, and the client
reports such rows as top-level ones: the factions of a collapsed
sub-header (e.g. Shattrath under The Burning Crusade) landed directly
under the expansion header, and a sub-header inside a collapsed
expansion became a top-level section. Take a restored row's nesting
from where it was remembered instead, and remember headers seen only
collapsed as well, so restored sub-headers are known to be headers.
The harness stub now reports rows read by ID the same way.
• feat: hint at collapsed headers whose factions are not known yet
A header collapsed in the reputation panel before the addon ever saw it
expanded has no remembered rows, so its section was simply missing from
the tooltip. Show the header with "(collapsed: expand once to list)"
instead. Sections with remembered rows need no hint: their values are
read by ID and stay current while collapsed.
• fix: keep collapsed sections in the tooltip and menu
The client only lists the rows of expanded headers, so collapsing a
header in the reputation panel removed its factions from the tooltip
and the menu, while the button and session summary kept tracking them.
Remember each header's rows per character while it is expanded
(TitanRep\_CharData.KnownChildren, faction IDs in list order) and put
them back in, read by ID, while it is collapsed. A header that was never
seen expanded has nothing to restore until it is.
• chore(dev): declare Classic-only reputation globals for the language server
GetNumFactions, GetFactionInfo, GetFactionInfoByID and IsFactionInactive
only exist on Classic clients (retail removed them in 11.0), so the
mainline annotations flag every call as undefined.
• feat: keep tracking factions under collapsed headers
Reputation gained with a faction whose header was collapsed went
unnoticed: no session summary entry, no standing change toast and no
Auto Show Changed. Look up the known factions the list scan cannot see
by ID and track them like the listed ones.
• fix: no new-faction toast when expanding a collapsed header
The list scan skips the rows of collapsed headers, so expanding one made
its factions look new to the session and could toast them as
discoveries. Remember the factions a character has seen in a saved
per-character set (TitanRep\_CharData.KnownFactions, IDs only) and judge
discoveries against it. Factions that appear because a header collapsed
in the previous scan was expanded count as revealed, which also covers
headers that stayed collapsed since before the set was filled.
• fix: keep showing the watched faction under a collapsed header
The button looked its faction up by name in the list scan, which only
sees rows of expanded headers: collapsing the header froze the button
text, and after a reload it showed "No Faction Selected". Save the
faction ID with the selection (name-only selections get it on first
sight) and look the faction up by ID when it is not in the list.
The per-row value computation moves into CreateFactionDetails so the
scan and the lookup by ID share it.
• fix: keep equally named sub-headers apart in the menu
Menu rows were attached to their parent by the parent's name alone, so…

addons.description:
WoW: Forever addon that explains how your talents change your character stats.

Supported: all nine classes (Shaman, Druid, Warrior, Priest, Paladin, Mage, Hunter, Rogue and Warlock), all three talent trees each. enUS client, Interface 16001 (beta build 1.60.1.70338).

Talents that change character sheet stats:

| Class | Tree | Talents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shaman | Elemental Combat | none (all spell-specific) |
| Shaman | Enhancement | Thundering Strikes, Ancestral Knowledge, Mental Dexterity, Anticipation, Toughness, Spirit Weapons, Mental Quickness |
| Shaman | Restoration | Tidal Focus (hit), Improved Reincarnation (health) |
| Druid | Balance | Nature's Majesty, Nature's Reach (hit), Moonkin Form (crit aura) |
| Druid | Feral Combat | Heart of the Wild, Feral Swiftness, Thick Hide, Sharpened Claws, Predatory Strikes, Leader of the Pack, Natural Instinct, Natural Reaction |
| Druid | Restoration | Living Spirit (Spirit) |
| Warrior | Arms | Deflection (parry), Weaponmaster (crit with an Axe or Polearm) |
| Warrior | Fury | Cruelty (crit) |
| Warrior | Protection | Shield Specialization (block with a shield), Anticipation (defense, plus 0.04% dodge, parry and block per point) |
| Priest | Discipline | Mental Strength (Intellect) |
| Priest | Holy | Spiritual Guidance (healing and spell damage from Spirit) |
| Priest | Shadow Magic | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Paladin | Holy | Divine Strength (Strength), Divine Intellect (Intellect), Holy Power (spell crit) |
| Paladin | Protection | Precision (hit), Anticipation (defense, as Warrior), Sacred Duty (Stamina), Toughness (item armor, approximated on total armor) |
| Paladin | Retribution | Deflection (parry), Conviction (crit), Champion of the Light (spell damage from Intellect) |
| Mage | Arcane | Arcane Mind (Intellect), Arcane Resilience (armor from Intellect), Arcane Instability (crit) |
| Mage | Fire | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Mage | Frost | none (all school- or spell-specific) |
| Hunter | Beast Mastery | none (pet and aspect talents) |
| Hunter | Marksmanship | Lethal Attacks (melee and ranged crit), Careful Aim (melee and ranged Attack Power from Intellect) |
| Hunter | Survival | Lightning Reflexes (Agility), Survivalist (health), Deflection (parry), Surefooted (melee hit) |
| Rogue | Assassination | Malice (melee and ranged crit) |
| Rogue | Combat | Lightning Reflexes (dodge), Deflection (parry), Precision (hit), Hack and Slash (crit with a Dagger or Fist Weapon) |
| Rogue | Subtlety | none (all ability- or situation-specific) |
| Warlock | Affliction | Suppression (hit) |
| Warlock | Demonology | Demonic Embrace (Stamina), Demonic Knowledge (spell damage from level, with a demon pet active) |
| Warlock | Destruction | none (all school- or spell-specific) |

Every other talent is listed too, so its tooltip explains it even though it does not change the sheet.

Party auras (Leader of the Pack, Moonkin Form) are attributed to your talent; if a groupmate provides the same aura, the client total already includes it.

Conditional talents depend on your form (Druid) or equipment (main-hand weapon type for Warrior and Rogue, shield) or an active pet (Warlock). When the condition is not met, the effect is shown in grey with its value under that condition, and it is not counted in the talent total.

Anticipation's 0.04% per Defense point is the Classic rule and is not yet confirmed on Forever.
What it shows
• Character panel next to the character window: each stat with the talents that contribute to it, including chained effects (for example, Ancestral Knowledge raises Intellect, which Mental Dexterity turns into Attack Power).
• Talent tooltips: what the talent gives you now and what the next point would add, using your current stats.
• Character stat tooltips: hovering a stat row (Intellect, Attack Power, ...) appends the talents behind it, in the native tooltip style.…

addons.description:
An unofficial companion addon for World of Warcraft Forever. RestedXP Guides
chooses the route; RestedXP Waypoint mirrors its resolved waypoint into Waypoint
UI's in-world navigation. It is not affiliated with either project.

See RestedXPWaypoint_Camelot.toc or /rxpw status for the installed version,
and CHANGELOG.md for release notes. Hybrid is the recommended default
for new installations; existing settings are preserved. Blizzard Waypoints
(native-first) remains experimental.
Requirements and installation
Verified environment: WoW Forever beta, build 1.60.1, interface 16001,
client flavour camelot. Other WoW clients have not been validated.

Install these addons separately:

| Dependency | Required folder | Verified version |
|---|---|---|
| RestedXP Guides | RXPGuides | v4.11.23 |
| Waypoint UI | WaypointUI | 1.7.3 |

1. Close WoW. Extract the release ZIP into your Forever client's
Interface/AddOns directory.
2. Check the resulting layout is Interface/AddOns/RestedXPWaypoint/, containing
RestedXPWaypoint_Camelot.toc, the Lua modules and Art/. Avoid a second
nested RestedXPWaypoint folder. Keep the folder name exactly as shown.
3. Enable RestedXP Waypoint and both dependencies in the character-selection
AddOns list, then start a RestedXP guide with a coordinate waypoint.
4. Type /rxpw status to confirm version, dependencies and the selected route.
Open /rxpw config to choose your settings.

Both dependencies are required for live synchronization. They are optional TOC
load dependencies so this addon's settings and missing-dependency messages can
still load when one is absent. The package does not bundle either dependency.
No build tools, Node or Python are needed to play. Restart the client after
installing or changing TOC/module files; /reload is sufficient for Lua edits.
Navigation strategies
The settings page lists them in this order; /rxpw mode and saved settings use
the identifiers.

| Settings name | /rxpw mode ... | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Hybrid (Recommended), default | hybrid | Use native quest tracking for eligible ready turn-ins; preserve intermediate and explicit travel points. |
| RestedXP Coordinates | coordinates | Always follow RestedXP's actual coordinates. Quest/service context changes presentation only. |
| Blizzard Waypoints | native-first | Also allow eligible .complete quest objectives, with structural and quest-log checks plus native destination verification; falls back to RestedXP coordinates. |

Native tracking is selected only when RestedXP's instruction structure supports
it. Routes, cave entrances, unrelated actions and ambiguous objectives stay on
coordinates. Multi-quest farming circuits can select one eligible quest without
repeatedly switching as patrol points cycle. Native targets are rechecked when
the same quest moves to a different activity area; failed checks fall back to
RestedXP coordinates. Item .collect instructions alone are not native objectives.

Manual pins and quest selections pause automatic navigation even while RestedXP
advances. After external tracking is cleared, navigation resumes at the current
RestedXP destination after one second of idle tracking. At login, one inherited
quest can serve as an unknown-origin baseline; a same-quest selection made before
reload cannot be distinguished from inherited automatic tracking. Pins remain
protected. During a pending native transition, an external selection cancels
delayed work. Use /rxpw off
for a longer pause; /rxpw sync explicitly applies the current route even while
auto-sync is off. Invalid or stale RestedXP data leaves existing navigation alone.
Icons, colours and labels
Coordinate waypoints retain RestedXP's destination and instruction label, including
live objective counts such as 1/15 Windstone Cluster. Ambiguous labels fall back
to Step N. Quest icons show Available (!), Incomplete (silver ?) and Complete
(gold ?), with supported campaign/repeatable variants.…

releases.changelog:
Changed
• Updated for the latest Forever client (build 1.60.1.70658).
• Loot lists refreshed for the dungeon bosses. The Stormwind Stockade now shows all its loot.

New
• Works with OpenMap. If you use the OpenMap addon, a click on one of its dungeon icons now opens the Dungeon Crawler dungeon map, with bosses, loot, quests and routes. Several dungeons at one icon, such as the Scarlet Monastery wings, show a small list to pick from. OpenMap's own buttons step aside while our map is open, and our map sits above its frames. You can turn this off in the options ("Open this addon's map from OpenMap's dungeon icons").
• Level range under the entrance icons. Each dungeon entrance on the zone maps shows its recommended levels, coloured for your level like quests: orange when you are in the range. Where several dungeons share an entrance, one combined range.
• One icon per entrance. Dungeons and wings that share a door (Scarlet Monastery, Dire Maul, Blackrock) are now one icon with a list, instead of a cluster of icons.
• A new route editor bar. Edit route now opens a toolbar over the map in the same style as the sidebar. It has tiles for Previous, Next, To the end, Cut here, Join here, Delete, Undo and Start over, plus Save route and Reset to Default. It also shows the stops of the route as numbered badges (click one to select it; hover for your best time), the split timer switches, and a close button in the corner.
• Route buttons in the corner. A red Hide route or Show route button sits above the red Edit route button, bottom left on the map.
Improved
• The map covers Blizzard's quest panel when it is open, instead of showing the quest list next to ours.
• Tooltips on the route buttons open under the editor bar or beside the corner buttons, so they no longer cover the button.
• Gnomeregan: Grubbis has a second Forever item, the Skullduggery Belt, from the latest AtlasLoot.
Fixed
• Boss pictures are no longer squeezed. The pictures that come from the Encounter Journal are twice as wide as high and were being pressed into a square; the middle of the picture is used now.

New
• Sunken Temple route. A built-in route through the whole temple, with its stops, stairs and triggers. Tick Show route to see it.
• Cutting a route is much clearer. The Cut here button is always in the bar while you draw (greyed until you select a dot), with a tooltip that walks you through it. After a cut the old part turns dark grey, a red ring marks the cut, and a new Join here button joins your new section to any point of the grey part, including stops and steps that the mouse cannot click.
Improved
• Route stops now always sit on their boss's pin, so a route never drifts away from a boss whose position was refined. Removing a stairs or door marker also removes its route steps.
• Better positions for Hazzas, Morphaz, Jammal'an and Ogom in Sunken Temple.
Fixed
• Rare bosses now get the silver ring in the boss list and the boss header, not only on the map pins.

New
• Draw your own route. Under the Show route box there is now an Edit route button. Click the map to add points, a boss to add a stop, and stairs or doors to add a step. Click a dot to select it and drag it to move it, or Ctrl-click a line to add a point on it. Cut the route at a point to draw a new section; the rest turns grey until you join it up again. Undo takes back the last thing you did, whatever it was. Save route keeps it, and Reset to Default brings back the built-in route.
• Routes for more dungeons. Built-in routes now cover Ragefire Chasm, Deadmines, Shadowfang Keep, Stockade, Wailing Caverns, Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs, Blackfathom Deeps, Uldaman, Gnomeregan, all four Scarlet Monastery wings, Zul'Farrak, Maraudon, City of Dalaran and Ruins of Lordaeron. Routes stay hidden until you tick Show route.
• Options at a glance. The options page is split into sections (Map, World map entrances, Dungeons and raids, Bosses and loot, Routes, Timers), and there is an Options button with a gear at the top of the map's side panel.
• Missing bosses and rares added:
• Scarlet Monastery: Azshir the Sleepless, Fallen Champion and Ironspine in the Graveyard, and Scarlet Commander Mograine with Whitemane in the Cathedral.
• Zul'Farrak: Sandarr Dunereaver, Dustwraith, Zerillis and Ruuzlu.
• Maraudon: Maraudos and Veng, two of the five Khans.
• City of Dalaran: Lyn the Ignored is marked as a summoned boss and names the item you need, the Tome of Dalaran. A marker shows where to talk to Grindle Firespark to free the Fel Ancient.
Improved
• More boss positions and activation markers recorded, for example in Razorfen Downs and Zul'Farrak.
• The route colours are easier to tell apart: the purple leg is now darker.
Fixed
• No more "blocked from an action" popup if the map redraws during combat while a rare is selected.
• Start over on a dungeon that only has the built-in route now gives you an empty route to draw.

New
• The split timer can start by itself. It now starts when you enter a dungeon, and there is a Start button on the timer window. If you prefer the old behaviour, turn off "Start the split timer when I enter a dungeon" in the options and it starts with the first fight.
Fixed
• "Blocked from an action only available to the Blizzard UI" popup when pressing Escape. The addon no longer touches the game's own popup list, so Escape works normally again.
• Lua error when opening the world map (M) a second time, and a game crash when opening a dropdown on the map's top bar. The addon no longer hooks into the world map; it follows the map with its own light-weight watcher instead.
• The dungeon map's top bar now looks and behaves like the game's own: same spacing, colours and arrows. Clicking a place name leaves the dungeon and opens that map.

addons.description:
A small WoW addon that sticks a marker on your mouse cursor so you can actually find it during busy fights.

Works on Retail and all current Classic versions.
Features
• Use a raid marker (Star, Skull, X, ...) or a class/spec icon as the cursor marker.
• Recolor icons and shapes with a color picker.
• Show it only in combat, or all the time.
• Optional global cooldown sweep: the marker flashes and refills clockwise while the GCD runs.
• On Retail, settings are saved per spec, and the icon switches when you change spec.
• Doesn't touch actual raid targets, so it won't conflict with DBM, BigWigs, MRT, etc.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| /co | Show help |
| /co config | Open settings |
| /co combat on/off | on: always show the marker, off: only in combat |
| /co scale | Change marker size |
| /co whatsnew | Show what changed in recent versions |
Custom textures
1. Convert your image to a TGA with the Python script in Tools/ (see Tools/INSTRUCTIONS.md).
2. Put the file in Textures/Custom/.
3. Restart the game (a /reload won't pick up new files).
4. In settings, pick "[!] Custom File" as the shape and type the filename.

addons.description:
The guild finder that World of Warcraft Forever doesn't have.

Players post a "looking for guild" ad, guilds post a recruiting ad, and both
sides browse each other in game. There's no website and no external tool:
ads go from player to player over a hidden addon channel. Guild Finder only
knows what other players running it share, so the lists grow with every
player and guild that posts an ad. Tell your guild and friends!

Changelogv0.1.0
First release. Guild Finder Forever is community driven: it only knows the
ads of other players running it, so the lists start short and grow with
every player and guild that posts one.
Find guilds
• Guild ads as cards sorted by how well they fit your own ad, with faction
crest, goals as coloured chips and a raid box (style, raid days and time,
wanted classes per role, whether your class fits).
• Search box and filters: faction, language, goals, raid style, "wants my
class" and, on Forever, "same ruleset".
• Details dialog with the full text, raid schedule and wanted classes by
role. Opening it checks in the background whether the poster is online
and in that guild.
Find players
• Compact list of player ads with class, level, roles, languages and goals,
sortable by any column.
• Filters for role, level range and class; a click on a row shows the text.
My ad
• Player ad per character and guild ad per guild (members who may invite),
with a live preview and the number of matching ads.
• Raiding guilds add style, raid days, start and end time, raids per week and
a class × role table of wanted classes.
• Ads can name several languages: the seven UI languages plus Czech, Danish,
Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Norwegian, Polish, Romanian, Swedish,
Turkish and Ukrainian.
• Ads are renewed on login and expire after 14 days without one.
• Play times are switched off for now.
Contact and moderation
• Whisper opens a whisper and checks the poster via /who.
• Hide an ad, Block a character or guild (/gff blocked, /gff unblock).
General
• Ads travel player to player over a hidden addon channel; nothing is sent
during encounter lockdown, queued messages go out afterwards.
• Welcome dialog on first start, minimap button, addon compartment entry,
settings (minimap button, chat notice for new matching ads).
• Chat commands: /gff, /gff ad, /gff settings, /gff sync,
/gff status, /gff debug (sync traffic in chat, for bug reports).
• UI in English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Russian and Portuguese.
• Runs on WoW Forever and, until Forever launches, on retail (Midnight).
Known limitations
• No cross-faction sync: the addon channel is separate per faction.
• The ruleset list for the "same ruleset" filter is not final until Forever
launches.

addons.description:
Per-addon, runtime-switchable UI language override for World of Warcraft
addons, plus a bundled-font manager for scripts the WoW client can't render
(e.g. Thai). Embeddable via LibStub.
Status
v0.3.5 -- runtime per-addon language override; a script-aware bundled-font
manager covering most of the world's scripts (with Latin merged in, so embedded
brand/command text never boxes); locale-native numerals; full button and
native-dropdown fonting that sizes to the width a non-Latin label is actually painted
at; a client-locale resolver (GetClientLocale) for chat/print output in a
chat-renderable language; right-to-left support (Hebrew + Arabic / Persian / Urdu,
with Arabic contextual shaping); and optional AceGUI integration -- a two-column language
picker and an automatic tab-font handler. Consumers that hard-depend on it: FastGuildInvite
(the first) and Dibs, on every client each one ships for, WoW: Forever included.

LibStub MINOR 18. The three satellite files carry their own version stamps and
upgrade independently of the core: _aceguiMinor 4, _rtlMinor 3, _namesMinor 1.

v0.3.5 is a fix for WoW Forever and Retail. Those clients hand addons secret strings
for some Blizzard text (tooltip lines, for example), and tainted code errors on comparing
one. Every entry point that reads text now asks issecretvalue first and leaves a secret
untouched; Classic clients have no such function and behave exactly as before. No API
change.

v0.3.4 added no API and changed no behaviour. It widened the TOC's ## Interface list to
cover World of Warcraft: Forever (16001) and Retail 12.1 (120100) -- a hard dependency
the client flags out of date stops the consumer loading -- and adds a spec that asserts
the list against the installed consumers and client rather than transcribing it. v0.3.3
was the correctness release before it: an offline test suite at 100% line coverage and
three behaviour fixes (retail's |cn: colour tokens, Urdu NOON GHUNNA shaping,
and the button auto-fit no longer writing widths onto buttons it has no business sizing).

Supported clients (one TOC, comma-separated): Classic Era, Anniversary / TBC, Wrath,
Cataclysm, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Retail (Midnight), and WoW: Forever.
Why not AceLocale-3.0 / AddonLocale?
• AceLocale keeps only the client-locale table + the default and resolves the
language once at load (GetLocale() / GAME_LOCALE). It can't switch a
language at runtime, and GAME_LOCALE is a single global that retargets every
AceLocale addon at once -- antisocial toward addons you didn't write.
• AddonLocale is a standalone, global user wrapper around GAME_LOCALE.
Same global limitation; no per-addon picker; no fonts.
• Neither handles fonts for non-renderable scripts.

This library keeps every registered locale table, merges them on demand
(enUS baseline + chosen locale on top), per addon, switchable live -- so
picking Dutch for one addon never touches another. The locale-merging engine is an
original implementation.
APIGuarantees
Promises the library has made to consumers. These are contracts, not implementation
details -- they are safe to build on, and changing one is a breaking change.
Fonting never resizes what it fonts
ApplyFontToFrame and ApplyFontToButton change how text renders. They never change
a widget's size, position, anchors, parent or layout -- with exactly one exception.

The exception: a button with all of a non-empty label, SetWidth/GetWidth, and a
width not derived from two opposing horizontal anchors may have its width set, and
nothing else. Never its height, points or parent. The width is only ever raised above the
button's own captured design width or restored back down to it, so a button can never end
up narrower than it was built.

Two opt-outs, both honoured: give the button no label, or anchor it on both horizontal
edges. (button.lloFitPad tunes the padding but does not exempt it.)
Other invariants…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.6.1] (2026-10-20) - Every tab is the same size; the Craft button is a plain button for trade skills; the close path runs onceBug Fixes
• **The Cooldowns and Guild tabs were smaller than the rest, so switching to
or from them made the window jump** (operator, in game 2026-10-20). Those two
tabs were locked at 720x500, while Crafting and the Profit Planner need at
least 820 and 920 wide, and the other tabs shared a resizable size of their
own. Every tab now uses one shared size, resizable, whose floor is the
largest minimum any tab declares (920x540 today), so a tab switch never moves
the window. Pinned by a new spec in Tests/mainwindow_spec.lua. Two
existing size specs there were moved to the new floor, because the change
made them fail (run 20261020-223619.605, red) rather than because they were
wrong: the "restores a saved size that fits" case now saves 960 wide instead
of 800 (below the new floor), with a new spec that a smaller saved size is
raised to the floor; and the uncapped shopping-list control uses ten recipes
instead of six, since 30 rows now fit in the taller tab. Green after the
edit on run 20261020-223845.589. Location:
GUI/MainWindow.lua, GUI/CooldownsTab.lua, GUI/GuildTab.lua.
• Clicking the main window's title bar closed the window (operator, in
game 2026-10-19). The temporary chat trace never caught it: the one trace
captured (on WoW Forever) was an ordinary Close-button click. No cause was
identified. The operator reports it no longer happens in Classic Era
(2026-10-20). The temporary trace is removed. Location: GUI/MainWindow.lua,
Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua.
• Closing the window from code ran its close-down twice. Close() releases
the AceGUI frame, and AceGUI hides it before clearing its callbacks, so the
frame's own close callback re-entered the release mid-way and the bottom-row
cleanup, the clamp restore, the Craft button re-check and the Crafting
engine's window-closed handler all ran a second time. On a close from code the
second run also undid the clamp restore, so the pooled frame always went back
to AceGUI unclamped whatever its earlier setting (the X button ran the
cleanup once and restored it correctly). The release path now returns at
once when AceGUI is already releasing the widget. Found by Peer Review by
reading. In Tests/mainwindow_spec.lua, two specs reproduce the bug and were
seen failing before the fix (one close for Close(); a frame clamped before
opening is still clamped after Close()), and one is a regression guard that
already passed (one close for a direct hide). Location: GUI/MainWindow.lua.
• The Craft button showed greyed and took no clicks for a trade skill
(in game 2026-10-18), while the debug line reported it enabled and above the
window. The cause in the secure button was not found. Trade skills no longer
use it: Craft is now a plain button inside the detail panel, built like
Craft Max (which kept working), and crafts the selected recipe at the
stepper's quantity through the same engine call. A trade-skill craft needs
only the click, so nothing secure is required. The secure button now shows
for Enchanting alone, where the enchant goes through a secure /cast
(whether DoCraft itself is protected is not verified), and lost the
trade-skill crafting it no longer used. An enchant with no name to cast,
which got no button at all, now gets the plain button labelled Enchant, which
opens Blizzard's Craft window. Craft, Craft Max and the queue's Craft Next
and Craft All are disabled in combat, matching the Enchant button, which is
hidden then. An enchant picked during combat is what the Enchant button casts
once combat ends; it used to keep the one picked before. Craft Next and Craft
All also come back after combat when the selected recipe left the list during
it; they used to stay greyed until the queue next changed. Not yet seen in
game. Location: GUI/CraftingTab.lua, Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua.…
addons.description:
Formerly TOG Profession Master.

Stop whispering every alchemist in your guild to ask "is your transmute up?" and stop logging into five different alts to remember who knows the recipe you need. Ultimate Profession Master keeps a live, shared view of every guildmate's professions, recipes, and cooldowns — and lets you mail reagents straight to the crafter without typing a single character name.

Works on Classic Era / Anniversary, TBC Classic, Wrath Classic, Cataclysm Classic, and Mists of Pandaria Classic, with early support for WoW Forever and Retail.
Quickstart
1. Install via CurseForge (recommended — handles dependencies automatically) or drop the folder into Interface\AddOns
2. /reload or restart WoW
3. Click the UPM minimap button to open the main window
4. Open your own profession windows (Alchemy, Tailoring, etc.) at least once on each character — UPM scans them automatically and starts syncing with the guild

That's it. Within a minute or two you'll see your guildmates' recipes and cooldowns alongside your own.
What it does
Profession Browser — Every recipe known by anyone in your guild, with a list of crafters per recipe. Filter by profession, search by name, see who's online, right-click to whisper the crafter.

Cooldowns Tab — Every guildmate's active and ready profession cooldowns in one view: transmutes, Mooncloth, Salt Shaker, Northrend Research, Icy Prism, Truegold, Living Steel, JC daily cuts, and more. Hit the one-click [Mail] button to send the crafter a pre-composed supply mail with every reagent of that cooldown on it — one mail per cooldown, even for a two-reagent transmute like Arcanite; the click splits whatever stacks need splitting, attaches them all and fills in the recipient, and it sends nothing at all if you are short of any reagent. A crafter on another realm gets the mail on their own realm, and if the game refuses the mail, chat says why. Click [Mail] again once the mail is ready and it sends. A Sent column then shows how long ago you supplied that crafter ("5m ago", "3h ago", date and time on hover), and clears itself once they use the cooldown. The reagent column is white when your bags hold enough of it to fill that mail and grey when they don't, so a glance down the list tells you which cooldowns you can actually feed — and it recolours as you loot or send things, without a tab switch.…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.6.1] (2026-10-20) - Every tab is the same size; the Craft button is a plain button for trade skills; the close path runs onceBug Fixes
• **The Cooldowns and Guild tabs were smaller than the rest, so switching to
or from them made the window jump** (operator, in game 2026-10-20). Those two
tabs were locked at 720x500, while Crafting and the Profit Planner need at
least 820 and 920 wide, and the other tabs shared a resizable size of their
own. Every tab now uses one shared size, resizable, whose floor is the
largest minimum any tab declares (920x540 today), so a tab switch never moves
the window. Pinned by a new spec in Tests/mainwindow_spec.lua. Two
existing size specs there were moved to the new floor, because the change
made them fail (run 20261020-223619.605, red) rather than because they were
wrong: the "restores a saved size that fits" case now saves 960 wide instead
of 800 (below the new floor), with a new spec that a smaller saved size is
raised to the floor; and the uncapped shopping-list control uses ten recipes
instead of six, since 30 rows now fit in the taller tab. Green after the
edit on run 20261020-223845.589. Location:
GUI/MainWindow.lua, GUI/CooldownsTab.lua, GUI/GuildTab.lua.
• Clicking the main window's title bar closed the window (operator, in
game 2026-10-19). The temporary chat trace never caught it: the one trace
captured (on WoW Forever) was an ordinary Close-button click. No cause was
identified. The operator reports it no longer happens in Classic Era
(2026-10-20). The temporary trace is removed. Location: GUI/MainWindow.lua,
Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua.
• Closing the window from code ran its close-down twice. Close() releases
the AceGUI frame, and AceGUI hides it before clearing its callbacks, so the
frame's own close callback re-entered the release mid-way and the bottom-row
cleanup, the clamp restore, the Craft button re-check and the Crafting
engine's window-closed handler all ran a second time. On a close from code the
second run also undid the clamp restore, so the pooled frame always went back
to AceGUI unclamped whatever its earlier setting (the X button ran the
cleanup once and restored it correctly). The release path now returns at
once when AceGUI is already releasing the widget. Found by Peer Review by
reading. In Tests/mainwindow_spec.lua, two specs reproduce the bug and were
seen failing before the fix (one close for Close(); a frame clamped before
opening is still clamped after Close()), and one is a regression guard that
already passed (one close for a direct hide). Location: GUI/MainWindow.lua.
• The Craft button showed greyed and took no clicks for a trade skill
(in game 2026-10-18), while the debug line reported it enabled and above the
window. The cause in the secure button was not found. Trade skills no longer
use it: Craft is now a plain button inside the detail panel, built like
Craft Max (which kept working), and crafts the selected recipe at the
stepper's quantity through the same engine call. A trade-skill craft needs
only the click, so nothing secure is required. The secure button now shows
for Enchanting alone, where the enchant goes through a secure /cast
(whether DoCraft itself is protected is not verified), and lost the
trade-skill crafting it no longer used. An enchant with no name to cast,
which got no button at all, now gets the plain button labelled Enchant, which
opens Blizzard's Craft window. Craft, Craft Max and the queue's Craft Next
and Craft All are disabled in combat, matching the Enchant button, which is
hidden then. An enchant picked during combat is what the Enchant button casts
once combat ends; it used to keep the one picked before. Craft Next and Craft
All also come back after combat when the selected recipe left the list during
it; they used to stay greyed until the queue next changed. Not yet seen in
game. Location: GUI/CraftingTab.lua, Modules/Crafting/CraftingEngine.lua.…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.6.0] (2026-10-17) - Allied guild tags; Reagent Tracker scale, opacity and background; cross-realm supply mailNew Features
• Allied guild members carry a short guild tag after their name, like
Ahmbrai , so it is clear at a glance who is in which guild
(operator, 2026-10-17: "The Old Gods (TOG) and The Other Gods (TOG) show
you the problem"). The tag is worked out automatically from the first word
that tells the guild names apart once filler words ("the", "of") are dropped,
cut to five letters, and never shared by two guilds -- so The Old Gods and
The Other Gods read
and . Settings -> Cross-Guild has an
"Allied guild tags" box (Guild Name = Tag, one per line) to pick your own,
and lists the tags in use. Home-guild members carry no tag. The tags are
LibGuildRoster's (MINOR 35, GuildRoster 1.4.0), at the operator's direction
("it should feed that to every addon that consumes a sister guild"; inbox
49703e36): the library derives them and stores your own tags account-wide
under the home guild, so every TOG addon shows one guild under one tag.
TOGPM's readers (GetGuildAbbrev, GetCharGuildAbbrev, the Settings box)
are thin wrappers over GetGuildTag / GetCharGuildTag / SetGuildTag,
the name columns repaint on the library's OnGuildTagsChanged, and
MigrateGuildTagsToLibrary (from OnRosterReady) moves any tags a working
copy kept in profile.guildAbbrevs into the library once and deletes them.
Under an older GuildRoster there are no tags and the Settings box is greyed
out. Typing a tag another allied guild already shows keeps it (your choice)
but says so in chat, naming that guild, from SetGuildTag's second return
(Peer Review G1, inbox 2899de7d) -- once, when that tag is changed, not on
every later save, and in the form the library stored (trimmed, at most 12
characters). TOGPM's own derivation is gone; its spec fixtures now run against the
library's. Specs in Tests/sisterguild_spec.lua. Location:
TOGProfessionMaster.lua, GUI/Settings.lua, Locale/enUS.lua.
• A supply mail the game refuses now says why in chat. After the Cooldowns
tab fills in a mail, the game's own mail error (and a failed send) is
repeated in chat with the recipient's name and the error's ERR_MAIL_ name
until the mail goes or the mailbox closes. Only mail errors are repeated --
the first cut also blamed unrelated ones such as "Out of range." on the mail
(Peer Review F1, inbox 60941923). Added for the operator's report of a mail to an allied-guild member
that loops on the "might be someone you don't know" confirm (cause not yet
known; GuildRoster asked to check its mailbox autocomplete, inbox 9aa8c30f).
Spec in Tests/cooldownmail_spec.lua. Location: GUI/CooldownsTab.lua.
• Scale and opacity sliders for the Reagent Tracker (the shopping-list
window opened by right-clicking the minimap button). Settings -> Display now
has "Reagent Tracker scale" (50-150%) and "Reagent Tracker opacity"
(0-100%) right below the main window's pair, and both apply live. Changing
the scale keeps the window's top-left corner on the same spot on screen.
Saved per profile as trackerScale / trackerOpacity. Specs in
Tests/reagenttracker_spec.lua. Scale checked in game on Classic Era.
• **The Reagent Tracker has a dark background, and the opacity slider sets
only that.** It had none, so the list read as see-through over bright ground.
A black panel (50% at 100% opacity) now sits behind the rows; the slider
fades just the panel, never the text, icons or buttons, and 0% removes it,
matching the old look. The first cut faded the whole window, text included.
Not yet checked in game.
Location: GUI/ReagentTracker.lua, GUI/Settings.lua, Locale/enUS.lua.
Bug Fixes
• **The Professions tab kept showing the recipe list from login until a
/reload** -- a guildmate learning a recipe, or someone leaving the guild,
never reached it. CallbackHandler keeps one handler per (event, self) and a
second registration under the same self replaces the first (Ace3…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.5.0] (2026-10-13) - Guild tab: search and filter by crafting skill; the Reagent Tracker stays open and minimisesNew Features
• Guild tab filter strip, built from LibAceGUIWidgets. The library's
search box and two of its number steppers (Min skill / Max skill) sit
above the list in toolbar slots.
• The search matches every label on the page: a profession whose name
matches keeps everyone in it, a specialization whose name matches keeps
all its members, and otherwise only characters whose name matches are
kept (case-insensitive, realm ignored; "You" finds your own characters;
an account-mate's name finds its main, whose row reads "Alt (Main)").
It is applied in GuildTab:BuildTree, which recounts from what it
keeps. Branches open when a search starts and close when it is cleared,
never on a refresh in between.
• The skill steppers filter on CRAFTING skill in the profession being
counted, and run from 1 to addon.SKILL_CAP (300 Classic Era, 375 TBC,
450 Wrath, 525 Cata, 600 MoP; on Retail the highest recorded skillMax,
else 100). The full range is no limit, and a bound filters only once
moved off its end. A character with no recorded skill in a profession
is hidden from it while the range is narrowed. The range is applied per
profession in BuildCounts, so headcounts read "how many matching".
Empty rows are left out while filtering.
• The list re-lays its rows when its scroll box changes size. Before, the
library re-laid only on its outer frame's resize; in game every row was
40px wide and the profession names drew as ".." while the scrollbar sat
at full width, so the last layout read the scroll box before it had its
width (inferred from the screenshot, not instrumented). LibAceGUIWidgets
MINOR 42 fixes it in the library (contract 0f350cea), so the hook is
installed only on an older copy (GuildTab:NeedsRelayoutHook).
• The character counts form one 80px column, centred under the
"Characters" header, which is itself centred over that column; the space
right of it is left free for later columns. The list's valueColumn
option is LibAceGUIWidgets MINOR 42 (contract a79b0269); an older copy
ignores it and keeps the counts at the row's right edge. The library
scales that column by its shared scale (another addon can set it), so
the headers are sized through GuildTab:ColumnWidths with
W:ScaledSize, and a scale change redraws the window while the Guild
tab shows.
• The steppers are parked across draws by the new
addon.GUI.ToolbarStepper (GUI/SharedWidgets.lua), like the other
toolbar controls, so a guild sync redrawing the tab mid-typing keeps
the box and its number.
• A debounced search that fires after a tab switch is dropped (per-draw
token cleared on release), so it cannot write the Guild count into
another tab's status bar. The tab's help tooltip describes the strip.
Location: GUI/GuildTab.lua, GUI/SharedWidgets.lua, specs in
Tests/guildtab_spec.lua.
• The Reagent Tracker stays up like Questie's tracker, and minimises.
It is no longer in UISpecialFrames, so Escape does not close it. Whether
it is open and whether it is minimised are saved per character beside its
position (RT:State(), db.char.frames.reagentTracker), and
PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD reopens it (RT:Restore) after a logout or
/reload. A new -/+ button left of the close button folds it to its title
bar. Dragging now writes the position fields into that record instead of
replacing it, so the flags survive a move. The window is always anchored
by its top-left corner (RT:PinTop, on build and after every drag):
anchored by its centre, as the default spot and the game's own drag anchor
could be, minimising pulled the title bar down toward that centre. A
position saved as a centre anchor by an older build moves its top once,
by half the difference between the old height and 200, on the first
open. SetDontSavePosition(true) keeps the client's own layout cache
from competing with that saved anchor, and the window is clamped to the
screen. Location:…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.4.0] (2026-10-11) - Item tooltips: an on/off setting for every line, no duplicate sell price, no doubled crafter namesNew Features
• Every line TOGPM adds to an item tooltip has its own on/off setting.
Settings > Item tooltip gains five toggles: recipe difficulty, recipe
sources, your characters who haven't learned the recipe, vendor buy price
and vendor sell price. Crafters and IDs already had one each. The vendor
rows had no setting at all; they were driven by one hidden key,
tooltipVendorPrices, which addon:MigrateVendorPriceToggles carries onto
both new keys once (off stays off) and then deletes -- at login and again on
every profile switch or copy, since a login only reaches the active profile.
A row switched off is not priced at all. The recipe-details
mode still decides whether the recipe block may appear at all, so its three
part toggles are greyed out under "Never". A part switched off is dropped
before the block's "is there anything to show" test, so a block left with
nothing still writes no heading. Location: GUI/Settings.lua,
GUI/SharedWidgets.lua, TOGProfessionMaster.lua, Locale/enUS.lua.
Bug Fixes
• **The crafters line and the IDs checkbox read a missing setting the opposite
way from each other.** Tooltip.lua treated a missing tooltipShowCrafters
as off although crafters has shipped on since v1.0.7 and its checkbox read
it as on; the IDs checkbox read a missing tooltipShowIds as on although
IDs ship off. Every reader now takes the shipped default. A spec that
asserted the old silent default was rewritten to the shipped one. Location:
Tooltip.lua, GUI/Settings.lua.
• **The Item tooltip header shared order 19.5 with the cooldown reminder
field**, a tie between the two. The header is now
19.505. Location: GUI/Settings.lua.
• The vendor block repeated the game's own sell price. Classic's client
prints "Sell Price:" on item tooltips while a vendor window is open (its
OnTooltipAddMoney script, classic_era GameTooltip.lua:297), and Retail's
tooltip data has a SellPrice line type for the same thing
(TooltipInfoSharedDocumentation.lua:45; when Retail emits it was not
checked). Our "Vendor Sell" row then showed the same number a second time. The hooks now notice the game's line and our
sell row stands down; the buy row, which the game never shows, stays. Whether
the Classic OnTooltipAddMoney script fires before or after our item hook
on every client has not been checked in game: where it fires after, the
duplicate remains as before. Location: Tooltip.lua, GUI/SharedWidgets.lua.
• A crafter who makes an item through two professions was listed twice
("Bob, Bob"). The crafters line deduplicated per character AND profession,
and seven Vanilla items come from two (Gold Bar is Mining's Smelt Gold and
Alchemy's Transmute Iron to Gold). Deduplicated per character now. Location:
Tooltip.lua.
• **The crafters line and the IDs line scanned every shipped recipe on every
item hover** (~1,565 on Vanilla, twice with the IDs line on). They read the
cached item-to-recipe index the recipe block already used, filtered to
crafted items so a teaching scroll is never credited to the recipe's crafters.
Each item's recipes are sorted, so "the first recipe" the recipe block and
the IDs line describe no longer depends on table layout; the sort falls back
to comparing as text, so a non-numeric key cannot make it raise. Location:
Tooltip.lua.
• **The legacy OnTooltipSetItem hook skipped any item while the previous
item's flag was still set.** It tested the flag for truthiness instead of
comparing it to the hovered item, the same defect the Show fallback had
already fixed for itself. The vendor block's per-hover guard had the same
shape and now compares to the item too. Location: Tooltip.lua,
GUI/SharedWidgets.lua.
• A tooltip could carry two TOGPM labels. The crafters and IDs lines open
with "[TOGPM]" and the recipe and vendor blocks with their own "TOGPM"…

TOG Profession Master Changelog[v1.3.1] (2026-10-07) - The CurseForge app installs LibDBIcon again; Missing Recipes shows recipe namesBug Fixes
• **The CurseForge app stopped installing LibDBIcon on every client except WoW
Forever.** The copy of LibDBIcon bundled for the Forever TOC still had the
packager's @curseforge-project-slug: libdbicon-1-0@ marker on line 1. The
BigWigs packager scans every packaged .lua for that marker and lists the
slug as an embedded library for the whole upload, which overrides
.pkgmeta's required-dependencies (release.sh 1880-1890). So the upload told
CurseForge LibDBIcon was embedded, and the app did not install the standalone
addon that the Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, Mists and Retail TOCs need before they
can load. The marker is removed, and Tests/loadorder_spec.lua (PKG-EMBED-001)
now fails if either Forever-embedded file carries one. Found by
TOGBankClassic's and Peer Review's audits (inbox 5503f91c, 5d7eaf86). Whether
the v1.3.0 file on CurseForge shows LibDBIcon as embedded was not checked on
the site. Location: Libs/LibDBIcon-1.0/LibDBIcon-1.0.lua.
• **Missing Recipes cut recipe names to about ten characters and the window
could not be widened** (Discord, 2026-10-07: "I cannot read what the recipe is
without scrolling over it and there is no way to move columns to the right to
read it"). The tab was locked at 720x500 to match Cooldowns, and Sources took
a fixed 180 px for a word like "Drop". Recipe is the list's auto-width column,
so it got only what was left over. The tab is now resizable and shares the
saved size of Professions, Crafting and Profit Planner, and Sources sizes to
its widest text (autoFit, minimum 60), so the space goes to Recipe. Three
specs in Tests/missingrecipes_spec.lua. Verified in game (operator,
2026-10-07: "the rows are indeed much wider"). Location:
GUI/MissingRecipesTab.lua, GUI/MainWindow.lua (comments).
• **The shopping list on the Professions tab could draw as an empty box with a
scrollbar** (operator, 2026-10-07: "i can't see the stuff on my shopping list
anymore", one recipe on the list). Since the move to the LibAceGUIWidgets
RowList in v1.2.0, the section was sized to exactly its rows plus the
InlineGroup's 40 px of chrome. The client snaps anchors to whole pixels, so the
row area could come out a fraction short. The RowList floors height / row
height, so one row became zero, and a longer list lost its last row. The
section now gets 2 px of slack (SL_SLACK). A new spec in
Tests/browserdetail_spec.lua takes half a pixel off the content and
requires the one row to still draw; it fails without the slack. The diagnosis
is read from the code and fits the screenshot, but not yet confirmed in game.
Location: GUI/BrowserTab.lua.

[v1.3.0] (2026-10-04) - Retail support; WoW Forever's borrowed ProfessionDB values are shown as unconfirmedNew Features
• **Retail (operator, 2026-10-04: "lets add retail support, i belive PDB was
updated enough for that").** A new TOGProfessionMaster_Mainline.toc
(Interface 120005 / 120007 / 120100) loads the same files with the same
dependencies as every other TOC; each required library already lists those
interfaces, and LibProfessionDB MINOR 13 ships its own Retail data tree.
Retail runs the C_TradeSkillUI scan and craft path built for WoW Forever.
addon.isRetail (Interface 100000+, the bound LibProfessionDB uses) makes
Jewelcrafting, Inscription and Archaeology available and hides First Aid.
Retail has no single expansion skill cap, so addon.SKILL_CAP is nil there
and the Guild tab shows the scanned max. Retail recipes carry a per-expansion
skillLine, and their skill numbers are on that line's scale: the new
addon:GetRecipeSkillRank reads the local character's rank for that line
live (C_TradeSkillUI.GetProfessionInfoBySkillLineID) for "Can learn now" and
the scroll tooltip's Requires line, and answers "unknown" (no gate) for
another character, whose per-line ranks are not synced yet. The profession…

Ultimate Profession Master Changelog (formerly TOG Profession Master)[v1.10.1] (2026-10-31) - Enchant button clickable again; Guide stops once the scroll is boughtBug Fixes
• **The Enchant button on the Crafting tab was dim and took no clicks, on
every enchant** (Discord 2026-10-30, Classic Hardcore, with a screenshot of
Agility 7 boots selected and materials for two). The secure button lives
off the pooled window on a UIParent holder, and the AceGUI Frame is
Toplevel, so a click on the window Raised it above the button. TOGPM's own
placement code for that button (holder, strata and level sync, the OnUpdate
watcher, the placement key, the regen re-sync) broke three times and is
deleted. The button is now LibAceGUIWidgets'
W:CreateSecureOverlayButton (MINOR 48, LibAceGUIWidgets v0.10.0, inbox
contract 48ef6be4), which draws it in the strata above the panel, follows
the panel, hides it for combat and detaches it when the window or tab is
released. The draw re-attaches it with SetPanel after parking the
session-lifetime detail panel, because the library now detaches on the
innermost widget's release (a tab switch). Feature-detected: with a
LibAceGUIWidgets older than MINOR 48 enchants use the plain button, which
opens the game's Enchanting window. The reagent list and cost line now end
at W:ScaledSize(230), re-applied on OnScaleChanged, because the
library's button grows with its size slider and would have run over the
reagent list above a scale of about 1.06 (arithmetic, not seen in game).
Location: GUI/CraftingTab.lua (EnsureCraftButton, AdoptCraftButton,
HasSecureCraft, SyncCraftButton, ApplyControlsWidth, Draw). Spec:
Tests/craftingtab_draw_spec.lua.
• **[Guide] on Missing Recipes kept guiding to the vendor after the scroll
was bought** (Discord 2026-10-30: "will not quit after you talk to the
vendor and buy"). Questbook never clears a place on arrival, so the guide
is now ended by TOGPM: [Guide] records the scroll's bag count and watches
BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED; when the count rises it stops the guide through
WhereStopTracking and says so. If Questbook is no longer guiding, the
watch just ends. KNOWN COST: Questbook has no public read of what it is
guiding, so a track the player started in Questbook after our [Guide] is
the one this stops. The start message now says the guide stops by itself.
Location: GUI/MissingRecipesTab.lua (Guide, StopGuide,
OnGuidedBagsChanged), Locale/enUS.lua. Spec:
Tests/missingrecipes_spec.lua.

[v1.10.0] (2026-10-26) - Missing Recipes shows Auction House prices and a Vendor only filter; German clients scan professionsNew Features
• On AH column on Missing Recipes (Discord 2026-10-24: a player ran an
ItemDB scan, closed the AH and saw nothing for a listed Pattern: Red Linen
Robe, because the [AH] button answers from the live AH session only). A
sortable column shows each scroll's cheapest buyout at the last ItemDB
scan, read through Price.GetLastScanListing, which answers from the live
session while the AH is open and otherwise from ItemDB's public
GetScanRecord (LibItemDB MINOR 47, inbox contract a583dabb). The row
tooltip adds the listing count and the scan's age. A scroll the scan did
not see sorts last in both directions. No read of ItemDB's private price
store: with an ItemDB older than MINOR 47 the column is blank. Location:
GUI/MissingRecipesTab.lua (AHPrice, BuildRowList, SortList,
ShowRowTooltip), Modules/Price.lua, Locale/enUS.lua. Specs:
Tests/price_spec.lua, Tests/missingrecipes_spec.lua.
• Vendor only filter on Missing Recipes (Discord 2026-10-24: "filter
missing recipes to just the ones you can run around and buy from a vendor
and if they are faction vendors, only show if you have the faction to get
them"). Keeps a scroll when LibItemDB's places for the player's faction
include a vendor; a scroll only the other faction's vendors sell is
dropped; with no LibItemDB vendor at all, ProfessionDB's vendor source
decides. With LibItemDB GetRequiredReputation (MINOR 47, inbox contract…

• First release, made for World of Warcraft: Forever (beta 1.60.1).

Installation

• The Edit Mode category is off by default: moving those elements from outside Edit Mode can clash with it.

addons.description:
Move and resize any window or interface element in World of Warcraft: Forever

🇪🇸 Español

What it does
AnyMove Forever lets you move and resize the windows and interface elements of WoW Forever, grouped in three categories:

| Category | What | Default | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | Character, spellbook & talents, professions, map, bags, bank, merchant, mail, auction house, trade, quests, friends, achievements, collections, calendar, settings... | On | Drag them directly |
| Interface | Top widgets, error messages, zone texts, alerts, group loot, totems, combo points... | Off | Move mode |
| Edit Mode | Action bars, unit frames, minimap, chat, bags bar, buffs, quest tracker... | Off | Move mode |

Edit Mode already moves most of the HUD, but not the windows: that is the part this addon adds. The Edit Mode category is off by default because moving those elements from outside Edit Mode can clash with it.
Features
• Drag any window and it stays there, even when the game reopens it.
• Move mode: a box over every enabled element. Drag to move, mouse wheel to resize (30–250%), right-click to reset.
• Everything is saved between sessions.
• Protected frames are never touched in combat: changes wait until combat ends.
• A checkbox per element in Options → AddOns → AnyMove Forever, plus Reset everything.
• Translated to every client language.

addons.description:
Diminishing returns (DR) of crowd control on your target, your focus and you, for World of Warcraft: Forever

🇪🇸 Español

What it does
Every crowd control of the same type in a row lasts less: the first one in full, the second half,
the third a quarter, and after that the enemy is immune, until 18 seconds after the last one ends.
DR Tracker Forever shows it as icons above your target, focus and player frames: the border and
the text say how long the next one lasts (50%, 25%, 0%) and the spiral shows when it resets.

WoW Forever hides the combat log from addons and its own DR system is switched off, so the DR is
counted from your casts and your group's, the misses and immunities the game reports, and the
effects the game lets addons see (all of them out of combat).
Commands
• /drf — settings
• /drf unlock / /drf lock — move the icons
• /drf test — sample icons for 20 seconds
• /drf clear — forget every tracked DR

addons.description:
Always-visible health and power text on the player, pet, target and focus frames for World of Warcraft: Forever

🇪🇸 Español

📸 Screenshots
Health and power text on the frames

Options

What it does
By default, WoW Forever only shows your health and power numbers when you hover the bar. Health Bar Text Forever keeps them always visible on the player, pet / minion, target, target of target, focus and target of focus frames, in the format you choose for each one.

| Format | Example |
|---|---|
| Value | 1.203 / 1.500 |
| Percent | 86% |
| Short | 13K / 14K (999 / 1K below 1,000) |
| Both | 86% 1.203 / 1.500 |
Features
• Always-visible health and power (mana, rage, energy...) on the player, pet / minion, target, target of target, focus and target of focus frames.
• Turn each frame on or off: an off frame goes back to Blizzard's default behavior.
• Four formats, chosen per frame: value, percent, short or both.
• Optional text on the power bars (on by default). Turn it off and those bars go back to Blizzard's default behavior.
• The text hides with no unit or a dead one, so it never covers the game's own "Dead" label.
• Lightweight, no libraries. Settings live in the game's own Options → AddOns panel.

addons.description:
No more green world map in non-English World of Warcraft: Forever clients

🇪🇸 Español

📸 Screenshots
Before: green map

After: original map art

The problem
In the WoW Forever beta (1.60.1), the new world maps (the world map, Kalimdor, Durotar, Zephras Isle, Hyjal and the other redrawn zones) only shipped for English clients. In any other language the client can't find them (Logs/AsyncFile.log: "Can't find file in build manifest") and draws them solid green, both the zone map and the explored areas.
What it does
Map Fix Forever ships the original map textures of the English client (build 1.60.1.69913, 1554 textures in 55 map folders) and swaps them in whenever the game draws one of those maps. Your map looks exactly like it does in English, explored areas included.
• Nothing to set up: install it and open the map.
• On English clients the world map is left alone (only the minimap fix below runs).
• Only post-hooks: Blizzard's map code is never replaced.

Grey minimap in Orgrimmar and Stormwind (build 1.60.1.70291, every language): inside those two cities the minimap turns light grey and black. The addon hides the broken city minimap and draws the ground minimap tiles the game already has underneath, following your position, zoom and minimap rotation. Icons stay on top. Outside those cities nothing changes.

1.0.0
Terminal 1.0, for WoW Forever's launch.

Share by invite
• .share invite invites a friend, guild member or Battle.net friend who's online (Tab lists them); they type .share accept. Terminal makes the group a code nobody can guess and hands it over only after their yes, only to that character, within 10 minutes. The empty prompt suggests the yes, and the badge shows invites.
• .share code gives a group's code to someone out of reach of an invite; they type .share join (typos are caught). .share new makes a group, .share rename calls it something else: names are yours alone.
• Typed passwords are gone: anyone in your guild could guess one at home. Groups made with a password are forgotten at login, with a line saying how to make them again. Your friends need this version too: invite them again.
• No kick: a group has no owner. To leave someone out, start a new group with the friends you trust. .share and the badge show who's connected.

In your language
• Simple mode's questions in German, Spanish, French, Russian and Chinese: "Quests zum Abbrechen", "où est mon corps", "мои аукционы", "我的邮件" and 45 more. English works on every client as before.
• Stats, food, drink and weapon damage by your language's words ("Ausdauer Essen" finds stamina food); your language's little words are left out of a search ("Essen, das Ausdauer gibt"); shorthand finds places as your client names them ("brd": Schwarzfelstiefen); Chinese typed without spaces is read as the words it's made of.
• Trainers are found by their translated titles ("Bergbaulehrer"), Chinese searches find only names with the characters you typed, and every font choice shows Russian, Chinese and Korean letters.

Also
• After an update, one line in chat says how many new things there are; .changelog shows them.
• English searches answer as they did, as fast.

• Trainers are found by their translated titles ("Bergbaulehrer"), Chinese searches find only names with the characters you typed, and every font choice shows Russian, Chinese and Korean letters.

Also
• After an update, one line in chat says how many new things there are; .changelog shows them.
• English searches answer as they did, as fast.

0.69.0
!t: your guild asks Terminal
• Someone in your guild or group types !t nearest innkeeper (or !t where is hogger, !t what drops thunderfury) and one Terminal in the guild answers in the same channel, from their side: nearest to where they stand, their class trainer, their level. World facts only, never your bags, mail, alts or position.
• Off until you switch it on: .ask guild on, .ask group on, .ask whisper on (whispers only from friends, guildies and your group). .ask test shows what it would send. Your own !t is answered in your chat only.
• Several Terminals in a guild agree on one answer, and share the limits: 10 s per asker, once a minute per question, 6 a minute per channel. Never in a battleground's chat; a question in another language is left unanswered.
• Answers are headed as >>> heads a list in your own chat: "Nearby innkeeper (15): ...", "Vendor in Ratchet (12): ...".

Spells by what they do
• Your spellbook's and every class's spells (@spell) are found by their descriptions: "spells that stun", "druid spells that root", @spell movement speed.
• Four new filters, as the game gives them: cast:instant, cast:<2; cost:0, cost:mana, cost:<100; range:melee, range:30; cd:0, cd:<10. In Simple mode: "instant spells", "spells with no cooldown", "spells that cost no mana", "30 yard spells", "spells under 100 mana", read only in a line about spells or abilities.

Cooking fires and moonwells
• "nearest cooking fire" lists every fire you can cook at: campfires, bonfires, braziers, stoves, cauldrons, meat racks, about 2,000 places (the objects the server marks as a cooking fire, from Mangos Zero's object table; scenery fires stay out). Each row says what it is ("Campfire", "Cozy Fire").
• "nearest moonwell" lists QuestieDB's moonwells. Advanced: @cookingfire, @moonwell with sort:distance, near: and in:. Both need Questie or QuestieDB.
• The object lists (mailboxes, forges, anvils, cooking fires, moonwells) are made the first time you ask, not at login, and let go after 10 minutes unused.

Simple mode understands more of how people ask
• "nearest" after a request's opening words: "where is the nearest mailbox", "find the closest innkeeper", "show me the nearest anvil". "near me" anywhere: "repair near me", "innkeeper near me in stormwind".
• An object or a role said alone is the nearest of them: "mailbox", "anvil", "inn", "repair"; "mailboxes in westfall" those there.
• Roles in the plural ("nearest innkeepers", "banks", "flight masters"), "nearest auction house", "deadmines entrance", Stormwind by its name alone.
• A word naming the kind you want looks only there: "hogger quest", "quests in westfall", "npcs in westfall", "linen recipes".
• "where to learn tailoring", "who teaches mining", "where to learn warrior", "where can i learn riding": the nearest trainers.
• "who drops spiritshroud leggings", "vendors that sell woven vest", "which vendors sell ice threaded bullet": where to get it. An item only the other faction sells says who: "Sells it to the other faction only". A name beginning with "the" or "a" is found whole ("where to get the collector's ring").
• A place said with nothing there says so: "None of those in Moonglade that Questie knows of." A place on another continent lists what's there, with no distance.
• Names come first: "thrall" names Thrall, not his advisor; "dalaran mage" and "stockade guard" are those NPCs, not a mage in Dalaran; a quest named like a question ("What Is Going On?") is the quest.

Typos as hands make them
• A neighbouring key ("linrn"), a key pressed twice ("linnen"), a key missed ("lien", "hoger"), two keys swapped ("marhsal") or a neighbouring key pressed as well counts as one slip, on your client's keyboard (QWERTZ in German, AZERTY in French). A key far from its place counts for more.
• A word that is exactly a name is never a typo: "linken" is the NPC Linken, not your Linen Cloth. Simple mode corrects names only Questie knows: "marshal dughn" finds Marshal Dughan.

Alt+…

0.68.0
A console
• .console (also .tty): a Linux-like console over everything Terminal knows. Every list is a folder and every row a file: ls, cd, cat shows a row's tooltip, grep searches stats and tooltips, with pipes, aliases, history and z.
• Up to four tiled panes, themes and prompts; the panes come back after a /reload. Lines wider than a pane slide sideways (Shift+wheel, or Left/Right with nothing typed). Passwords typed into it are masked.
• .console and .atop now live in Terminal Extras and load the first time you use them.

Smaller saved data
• Terminal.lua now keeps only your settings, tabs, picks and search history. What Terminal records and learns (logs, item and loot indexes, talents, mail, recipes, the console's history) moves to a new TerminalCache.lua, written about half the size and safe to delete. Your old file is moved over by itself.
• .saved shows how big each part is. .saved keep
off|small|normal|large (or .saved keep all minimal|normal|everything) sets how much is kept between sessions; .saved clear
forgets one. By default the loot log keeps 250 drops, the combat log 150 (deaths first) and item details 4000 items.

Report a problem
• .report [what happened] (also .bug) puts a report in a window to copy and paste as a comment on Terminal's CurseForge page (a GitHub issue works too): versions, the addons found, the searches that found nothing, errors and Terminal's last steps. Your characters', alts' and guild's names are left out.
• It's offered when a search finds nothing, on a result's right-click menu (Report a problem with this result) and after an error.

Nearest forge and anvil
• nearest forge and nearest anvil (also closest, farthest, 2 anvils), for blacksmiths and engineers: the closest first, an arrow pointing the way, Enter shows it on the map. Needs Questie or QuestieDB. Advanced: @forge, @anvil, with sort:distance, near: and in:.

Simple mode reads your line once
• The search, the bar, Alt+ and .explain share one reading of the line. Alt+ keeps your capitals and writes linen to csv as linen >>> csv.
• not in my bank or not on my alts on its own lists your items that aren't there.
• Unticking a typed filter on the bar takes out exactly the words that said it, never another filter's or anything inside a "quoted phrase".

World data from the game's own sources
• Flight paths, dungeon and raid entrances, zone levels and fishing skills come from the game's own data and public sources, each cited in docs/DATA_SOURCES.md. Dungeon levels are the Group Finder's; with Questie or QuestieDB, entrances show at their doors.
• @cvar lists the console settings WoW Forever's own interface uses, each explained in the options panel's words, in your language.
• Your race's capital counts as a learned flight path from the start (a Windshaper's: Orgrimmar).

Fixes
• The combat log kept between sessions keeps deaths over crits, so what killed me still answers after a /reload.

New files: restart the game once after updating, not just /reload.

0.67.0
Plain words for numbers, levels and dates
• Numbers: swords between level 20 and 30, quests under level 25, items worth more than 1g, bags with at least 10 slots, gear under 50% durability.
• Levels from yours: quests 3 levels above me, dungeons around my level, gear for next level. They move with you as you level, in a saved search or alias too.
• Dates: loot from yesterday, mail older than 20 days, auctions sold this week, what killed me today, in the last 3 days.
• Advanced: lvl:me+3, lvl:me-2..me+3, value:>1g, slots:>=10, since:yesterday, older:20d.

Top N
• the 3 nearest mailboxes, top 5 upgrades, my 10 most valuable items, the closest innkeeper. Orders in words too: cheapest, most valuable, highest level. The footer says "3 of 41".
• Advanced: | first 3.

Compare two searches
• cloth but not in my bank, linen plus my alts. Advanced: | except @bank, | also @stored.

Sort by more than one field
• sort:quality,-level sorts by quality, then by level on a tie; sort:level,distance puts the nearest first among equals. In Simple mode, Shift on a Sort pick makes it the "then by".

Undo in the prompt
• Ctrl+Z undoes your last edit (a word, a Ctrl+W, a paste); Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes it.

Understand a search
• Point at an Advanced line in the prompt to read it in plain words, or .explain it ("Vendors, that sell arrow, nearest first"). .explain alone explains the last line you ran.
• Why is this here? in a row's menu: the words it matched and where, the filters it passed, its sort value, and for an upgrade what it gains.

Upgrades
• With no tree picked, upgrades are judged for the talent tree holding most of your points, and follow a respec. .weights all goes back to that.
• Hit past your cap counts for nothing: 5% melee and 3% spells below 60; 9% and 16% at 60. .weights says where you stand.
• upgrades i can buy (vendor upgrades): the friendly vendors selling a clear upgrade for you, nearest first, with what it gains and any standing it needs. Advanced: @npc sells:upgrade. Needs Questie.
• ah upgrades: bind-on-equip upgrades at Auctionator's last-scanned price, the most gain per gold first. Needs Auctionator and AtlasLoot.

Fixes
• Upgrades are always judged against what you wear, including a worn piece whose stats the game didn't give (it counted as nothing) and random-suffix gear.
• Names with a date or level in them ("Tonight We Dine", "Last Day of Summer") are still found.

0.66.0
Your own key, on any keyboard (a player on CurseForge: "how can I keybind the terminal on a German layout?")
• Bind any key to Terminal (Key Bindings > AddOns > Terminal, or .bind) and in the open terminal it does what does: it closes it, Alt+ it writes the search in Advanced mode, Tab+ it is pure fuzzy finding. Keys like ^, ², Ctrl+Space, Shift+Space or Alt+Q work; letters, digits and the characters a search needs still type.
• The hints, F1's keys and the windows' footers name your key. With bound, nothing changes.

Quests that reward bags
• quests that reward bags (bag quests, quivers from quests, quests that reward ammo pouches) lists the bags your race, class and faction can still get, the most slots first, each saying which bag and its slots; the footer says how many you've done already. Needs Questie.
• Advanced: @questie reward:bag -is:done sort:slots (reward:quiver, reward:ammo_pouch) lists the same in the same order, with the bag and slots in each row.

Sort either way
• Simple mode's Sort shows an arrow by the sort in use: down for the highest (or Z) first, up for the lowest (or A) first. Pick it again to turn it round. Numbers start with the highest, names with A.
• Advanced: a - turns a sort round (sort:-level, sort:-name, sort:-quality).

Nearest or farthest
• sort:distance lists the nearest first, sort:-distance the farthest (sort:nearest and sort:farthest still work). In plain words: farthest innkeeper, farthest mailbox. Sort's Distance starts with the nearest; pick it again for the farthest.
• A row whose distance isn't known (on another continent, in an instance) counts as infinitely far: last when nearest, first when farthest.

Upgrades by talent tree
• .weights picks a tree: .weights arms, fury, prot, holy, resto, shadow, bear... ("tank" and "healer" pick your class's). One at a time; none picked, your class's levelling tree.
• New weights made for WoW Forever, one scale per tree for levels 1-60: healing is its own stat, a school's spell damage counts for its tree, a ranged weapon's DPS is apart from a melee one's, block value apart from block chance, a feral's weapon DPS counts.
• Your own weights: .weights set str=2 agi=1.5, or paste a Pawn scale string (.weights pawn opens a window for it). .weights custom picks them again, .weights clear forgets them.
• An upgrade search's footer says .weights is how to judge them otherwise.

Fewer commands
• .xp, .history, .durability, .mail, .combatlog and .lockouts are gone: their lists are searched like anything else. .forget drops an alt's mail, experience and lockouts; .forget history and .forget combatlog clear those; .set mailWarn off stops the login warning about expiring mail.
• .talentdebug and .profdebug are .debug talents and .debug professions.

Fixes
• An answer sorted by distance is in that order; sort:-distance is faster.
• reward:pouch (satchel, sack) finds items with that name; reward:bag is every bag.
• Turning "nearest mailbox" round on Sort gives "farthest mailbox"; a typed nearest or farthest wins over the bar.
• Advanced bag searches ask the game for bags it hasn't loaded yet, and read their slots in other languages too.

addons.description:
> 🎨 Artists wanted! The journal already records map coordinates, creature IDs and item IDs for everything it sees — it just doesn't draw any of it yet. If you can make icons, portraits, or a journal-style map, see issue #6. No Lua required to contribute a mockup or asset set.

Open the journal with /fj or /fieldjournal. This version has four tabs:
• Quests keeps the quest log text, observed NPC dialogue, readable notes, kills and picked up quest items in chronological margins. It links speech from a recent quest giver when the speaker and location match one unambiguous quest. Previous quest stages and completed objectives are crossed out.
• Daily diary records newly learned spells, group joins, and merchant purchases and sales when the client exposes enough information.
• Bestiary counts creatures seen falling, their locations, and items actually looted from those creatures. Counts are personal observations, not drop rates.
• Crafting & gathering records loot from world objects, completed crafts reported by the client, and skill milestones at 20, 25, 35, 40, 50, 75, 100 and every 25 thereafter.

The addon never registers the protected combat log event. Kill detection uses party kill and observed unit death events; missing client events can leave gaps. Loot is attached to a creature or object only when the loot window supplies its source GUID and the item is actually taken. Merchant entries compare bags and money while a merchant is open; unrelated simultaneous changes can affect the account. Speech and note links can be changed manually from the quest tab.

See CHANGELOG.md for the version history.
Current status
This is beta software, developed and tested against one live account. The codebase is split into a namespaced module layout (Core/, Data/, UI/) with a hand-rolled Lua test suite (tests/run_tests.lua).

Journal data is stored per character via AceDB-3.0 (FieldJournalDB.char). Existing data from before this migration is imported automatically, once, the first time each character logs in — see CHANGELOG.md for details. The old data is never deleted, only read, so it remains a fallback if anything about the migration ever needs to be redone.

Each character also keeps a rotating ring of five automatic backup snapshots, taken at login, plus a second complete copy in its own per-character saved-variables file. /fj repair restores from those snapshots. There is still no manual export/import, and no guarantee that a manual edit to an entry survives auto-regeneration or a future merge — see Roadmap below.
Roadmap
This follows a phased resilience plan (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-phase1-resilience-design.md in this repo's history, not distributed with the addon). See the milestones and open issues for what's up for grabs — issues labeled good first issue are small, self-contained, and don't need deep addon-development experience.
• Export / Import — a manual /fj export / /fj import safety valve so players can back up or transfer their own data without touching SavedVariables files directly.
• Edit-safety guarantees — a per-record edited flag so a manual correction (via the note editor) is never silently overwritten by auto-regeneration, a merge, or a backup restore.
• Repository polish — a CLAUDE.md for future coding-agent sessions, once the data layer above has proven stable. (Contribution guidelines now live in CONTRIBUTING.md.)
• Phase 2 (UI/UX) and Phase 3 (visual polish, art) — exploratory, no design work started; see the open issues.

None of this is scheduled; it lands as time allows.
