addons.changelog:
What's new in 1.2
ForeverLootMover now runs on Classic Era 1.15.9 — Hardcore realms, Season of Discovery — as well as on WoW Forever. One package, whose TOC lists both interfaces (16001, 11509).

Nothing in the search for the bars had to change. They are found by their frame names, then by walking the container, and the roll buttons are recognised by both naming schemes of their art, the atlas of Forever and the old UI-GroupLoot files. No Blizzard function is called by name. If the bars do not move on your client, type /flm scan and send the output: it lists what your client really has.

No backup copy on Classic Era. The workaround for the Forever beta saving bug is switched off there: the game keeps its saved variables, so the addon creates no macro and no CVar, and takes none of your macro slots. It only does so on a build it knows to be Classic Era; on any other it stays on, which is the safe side of a wrong guess.

The close button of the options menu works on every client. The strip that lets you drag the menu spans its whole top at the very same frame level as the cross, so on Classic Era it took the click. The cross has its own level above the strip now, and closes the menu itself.
Two zips, one addon
ForeverLootMover1.2.zip and ForeverLootMover-Classic1.2.zip hold exactly the same files. Take whichever carries the name of your game.
Install
Extract the ForeverLootMover folder into the Interface\AddOns folder of your game, then relaunch it:
• WoW Forever: World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns
• Classic Era / Hardcore: World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns

The folder must be named ForeverLootMover.
addons.description:
Move, resize and stack the group loot roll bars in World of Warcraft: Forever.

-c8a14a)

The group loot roll bars appear in the middle of your screen, right on top of the boss you are
fighting and the raid frames you are watching. ForeverLootMover pins them wherever you want, at the
size you want, stacking in the direction you want — and keeps them there no matter how often the
game tries to put them back.

It is a rewrite of the idea behind LootRollMover, built from scratch for the Forever client. No
libraries, no dependencies.
Why a new addon
The older movers hook the game's own loot functions by name (GroupLootContainer_Update,
GroupLootFrame_OnShow, …). The moment a build renames or rewrites that code, those hooks are
never called and the addon silently does nothing — which is what happens on Forever.

ForeverLootMover never looks up a Blizzard function by name:
• the roll bars are found by name, then by walking the loot container, then by looking for any frame
holding a rollID;
• their own SetPoint is hooked on the object itself, so the addon is told whenever the game
moves them, whatever code did it;
• a watchdog re-checks the layout five times a second while a roll is on screen, and only ever
writes a position that is actually wrong — a layout that is already right costs nothing.
Features
• The game's own bars, untouched. Nothing is redrawn or reskinned: the roll bar keeps the look
this client gives it, it just lands where you put it.
• No fourth square. The transmog button this build draws next to need, greed and pass is taken
off the bar, on every roll.
• The loot toast follows. The "You received" panel the game shows once an item is yours lands on
the same spot as the roll bars, instead of somewhere else on the screen. Optional.
• Smooth. A bar appearing is placed in the same frame it is shown, so it never flashes at its
default spot first, and it fades in; when a roll is over, the bars left slide into their new slot
instead of snapping.
• A test button. Two of the game's own roll bars, borrowed and filled with a real item, so the
size and the spot are judged on the real frame. They are inert — no roll is started, nothing can be
clicked — and they are handed back after 30 seconds, on a second click, or the moment a real roll
starts.
• Place them from anywhere. A stone frame in the usual World of Warcraft look shows the exact
footprint the bar will take, with an arrow for the stacking direction — so the spot can be chosen
standing in a town, without waiting for a dungeon to hand out loot.
• Drag anywhere on the stack, and the real bars follow while you drag.
• Size from 50 % to 300 %, with the mouse wheel over the preview or with the slider.
• Stacking direction — new rolls pile up above or below the first bar.
• Gap between bars, 0 to 30 px.
• Settings that stick — position, size and options survive a reload, a relog and a full restart
of the game, even with the Forever beta bug that resets other addons (see below).
• Options menu in the World of Warcraft style, in English and French.
• Minimap button and addon compartment entry.
• /flm scan prints what the current build actually has, so a future patch can be sorted out in
minutes.
Options menu
Open it from the minimap button (right-click) or with /flm options.

| Section | What you can change |
| --- | --- |
| General | Addon on / off, minimap button, keep the bars on screen, move the loot toast too, smooth movement |
| Position | Stacking direction, bar size, gap between bars, place the bars, test with an item, default position |

Nothing in the search for the bars had to change. They are found by their frame names, then by walking the container, and the roll buttons are recognised by both naming schemes of their art, the atlas of Forever and the old UI-GroupLoot files. No Blizzard function is called by name. If the bars do not move on your client, type /flm scan and send the output: it lists what your client really has.

No backup copy on Classic Era. The workaround for the Forever beta saving bug is switched off there: the game keeps its saved variables, so the addon creates no macro and no CVar, and takes none of your macro slots. It only does so on a build it knows to be Classic Era; on any other it stays on, which is the safe side of a wrong guess.

The close button of the options menu works on every client. The strip that lets you drag the menu spans its whole top at the very same frame level as the cross, so on Classic Era it took the click. The cross has its own level above the strip now, and closes the menu itself.
Two zips, one addon
ForeverLootMover1.2.zip and ForeverLootMover-Classic1.2.zip hold exactly the same files. Take whichever carries the name of your game.
Install
Extract the ForeverLootMover folder into the Interface\AddOns folder of your game, then relaunch it:
• WoW Forever: World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns
• Classic Era / Hardcore: World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns

The folder must be named ForeverLootMover.

What's new in 1.1
The transmog square really goes now. It survived 1.0 for two reasons, both found by reading what
the client actually has instead of guessing. The roll buttons are not children of the bar but of a
container inside it, so the whole little tree has to be walked; and this build names its art by role
in an atlas — lootroll-toast-icon-need-up, -greed-up, -transmog-up — where older builds use the
UI-GroupLoot-Dice / Coin / Pass files. Both naming schemes are understood now.

Need and greed no longer disappear with it. Only what is positively recognised as transmog or
disenchant is hidden. A roll button whose art says nothing — the pass button here carries a bare file
number — is kept: an unknown button left on the bar is better than a missing need or greed.

The test works again. Its table of items was called ITEMS, which is already a Blizzard global
holding a piece of text, so the lookup quietly returned nothing and the test raised instead of
opening. It also shows every roll button the bar has, so the transmog square can no longer sit on top
of a hidden coin.

The "You received" toast lands on the same spot as the roll bars. It belongs to the game's alert
system rather than to the roll bars, so it is handled on its own: the alert subsystems are told to
measure from the anchor, and failing that the alert host frame is pinned to it.

Smooth and alive. A bar is placed in the very frame it is shown, so it no longer flashes at its
default spot first, and it fades in. When a roll ends, the bars left slide into their new slot
instead of snapping.

The addon has its own artwork, on the minimap button, the options menu, the addon compartment and
the addon list.

Options. The loot toast line reads "Move the loot toast too", and the transmog checkbox is gone:
the square is always taken off now, which is safe since only a button positively recognised as
transmog is ever hidden.

/flm scan says more: every button with the art it wears and the role it was given, plus the
state of the alert system. That is what made the two fixes above possible.

What's new in 1.0
First release.

Move the loot roll bars. Put the group loot roll bars anywhere on the screen, at any size between 50 % and 300 %, stacking up or down with the gap you choose. The bars themselves are left alone: no reskin, no redraw, they keep the look this client gives them.

Place them from anywhere. A stone frame in the usual World of Warcraft look shows the exact footprint the bar will take, with an arrow for the stacking direction. Drag it, wheel over it to resize, right-click when it is good.

Test with a real item. One click borrows two of the game's own roll bars, fills them with a real item and shows them where they will appear. They are inert - no roll is started, nothing can be clicked - and they are handed back after thirty seconds, on a second click, or the moment a real roll starts.

No fourth square. The transmog button this build draws next to need, greed and pass is taken off the bar, on every roll.

The "You received" toast lands in the same spot as the roll bars, instead of somewhere else on the screen.

Smooth. A bar is placed in the very frame it is shown, so it never flashes at its default spot first, and it fades in. When a roll is over, the bars left slide into their new slot instead of snapping.

Nothing is hooked by name. The older movers hook Blizzard functions that this client no longer has, so they quietly do nothing. Here the bars are found as frames, their own SetPoint is hooked on the object itself, and a watchdog re-checks the layout five times a second while a roll is on screen.

Settings survive a restart through the CVar and macro copies used by the other Forever addons, so the position is not lost to the beta saving bug.

Options menu in the World of Warcraft style, English and French, with a minimap button and an addon compartment entry. /flm to place the bars, /flm options for the rest.
Install
1. Download ForeverLootMover1.0.zip below.
2. Extract the ForeverLootMover folder into your WoW Forever Interface\AddOns directory:
World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns\ForeverLootMover
3. Launch the game. The folder must be named ForeverLootMover.

What's new in 1.5
Nothing new to set: 1.5 only changes how the voices move between the settings you already have.
• Voices that fade instead of stepping. A position is shared every two seconds, and the volume moved at every one of them: someone walking towards you got louder in steps. Their position is now walked from the old one to the new one, so the distance changes all the time and the voice follows it.
• The volume is followed twelve times a second instead of four, and its fade is taken from the time really elapsed rather than counted in ticks.
• The range, the curve and the volume up close are unchanged. They are simply reached without the staircase.
• Each member's name and group slot are looked up four times a second instead of at every volume step, so the faster fade costs nothing in a raid.
Install
Extract the ForeverVoice folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named ForeverVoice.

In the game settings, turn on Voice Chat and set your microphone and talk mode. Everyone needs the addon for proximity to work: a player without it doesn't share their position and hears the whole channel at normal volume.
addons.description:
Proximity voice chat for your guild or your party in World of Warcraft: Forever.

-c8a14a)

Walk into a zone, cross a guildmate on the road, and just talk to them. ForeverVoice turns
Blizzard's built-in voice chat into proximity voice: you hear the players close to you, their
voice fades as they walk away, and they go silent once they are out of range.

No external program, no Discord, no server to host. ForeverVoice uses the game's own voice
chat and only changes how loud each player is. No libraries, no dependencies.

How it works
1. ForeverVoice joins the voice channel you picked when you log in: your guild, your
group, or Auto (the guild, else the group).
2. Every player who has the addon shares their position with the guild, using a small hidden
addon message.
3. Your addon sets the volume of each player based on how far they are: full voice up
close, a smooth fade, then silence.

> Everyone needs the addon. Proximity is applied on the listener's side. A guildmate
> without ForeverVoice doesn't share their position, and hears the whole channel at normal volume.
Features
• Proximity volume: full voice up to a distance you choose, then a fade (linear, natural
or smooth), with silence past the maximum range. A live graph in the options shows the curve.
• "X is in voice range" alert: a sound and a message when a guildmate comes within earshot.
• Group audible in dungeons: the game hides positions in dungeons and battlegrounds, so
your group stays audible there.
• Always hear someone: right-click a player in the window to hear them at any distance,
for example a friend or a raid leader.
• Voice window:
• who is in the channel and who is talking;
• how far each player is and how loud you hear them;
• your own line with your push-to-talk key.
• Speaker above heads: a green speaker icon above the players who are talking (needs
friendly nameplates, Shift + V by default), and above your own character while you talk.
• Minimap button with a tooltip listing who is in range, and a halo while someone talks.
• Guild or group: pick the voice channel in the options (Auto, Guild or Group). In Group mode,
you join group voice as soon as a group forms.
• Join and leave voice in one click: the join button asks "Guild or Group?".
• English and French, switched in one click.
• Settings that stick, even with the Forever beta bug that resets addon settings (see
below).
• Safe: ForeverVoice only changes volumes, never the Blizzard mute. Everyone is put back to
full volume when you turn proximity off, leave voice or log out.
Controls
Minimap button

| Action | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Options menu |
| Right-click | Proximity on / off |
| Middle-click | Join / leave voice |
| Shift + click | Show / hide the window |
| Drag | Move the button around the minimap |

Slash commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| /fv | Show / hide the window |
| /fv options | Open the options menu |
| /fv on / /fv off | Turn proximity on / off |
| /fv join / /fv leave | Join / leave voice |
| /fv join guild / /fv join group | Switch to guild or group voice |
| /fv range 40 8 | Silent from 40 yards, full voice up to 8 yards |
| /fv who | Who in the guild has the addon, and their version |
| /fv debug | Voice, positions and settings backup status |
Options
| Section | What you can change |
| --- | --- |
| Range | Full voice distance (0-30 yd), silent distance (10-100 yd), fade curve with a live graph, volume up close |
| Behavior | Voice channel (Auto, Guild, Group), proximity on / off, auto-join voice, group audible in dungeons, hear players without the addon, in-range alert, icon above heads, minimap button |
| Window | Show, lock, only players in range, your own line, size, background opacity |

addons.description:
A clean, lightweight and fully customizable XP bar for World of Warcraft: Forever.

-c8a14a)
-c8a14a)

MyXPBar replaces the default Blizzard experience bar with a sleek, readable bar you can place
anywhere on your screen. Inspired by the popular Luxthos WeakAuras look, it shows your rested XP,
estimates how many mobs you still need, and comes with a full in-game options menu built in the
World of Warcraft style. No libraries, no dependencies.
Features
• Replaces the Blizzard XP bar — the default bar is hidden automatically, and comes back at max
level for reputation and honor.
• Profiles with names — make one from the bar you have, name it, and pick it again on any
character from the list at the bottom of the menu. Position, size, colors, style, texture,
options: everything lives in the profile, and everything you change goes into it right away,
with nothing to save by hand.
• A switch for the bar — one checkbox, a middle click on the minimap button, a key binding or
/mxp off hides the bar at any level, without disabling the addon. The bar of the game stays
hidden too, as long as you asked for it to be.
• Reputation at max level — instead of disappearing at max level, the bar can show your tracked
faction, standing and progress (optional).
• Told when it is updated — one line in the chat after an update and a short "What's new" panel,
once per version. /mxp news shows it again, and the option can be turned off.
• 11 bar textures — default, smooth, flat, glass, shine, steel, stripes, ticks, grain, edge and
fade, each one a swatch in the options.
• 6 bar styles — classic, gold framed, segmented, thin line, spark and split rested, switched in
one click with a live preview.
• Smooth and alive — the bar slides to its new value, a floating +245 XP rises on every gain,
and the bar flashes on level up. Both can be turned off.
• Rested XP overlay — a translucent layer shows exactly how far your rested XP will take you.
• Mobs-to-level estimate — how many kills you still need, based on your last XP gain.
• Detailed stats — level, current / max XP, percentage, and projected percentage with rested XP.
• 7 languages — English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Italian, picked from a
drop-down in the options menu.
• Settings that stick — position, size, colors, style and options survive a reload, a relog
and a full restart of the game, even with the Forever beta bug that resets other addons
(see below).
• Full screen width — one click and the bar runs from one edge of the screen to the other,
at any resolution.
• Reputation bar — a thin bar with your tracked faction, standing and progress, under the XP
bar or beside it when vertical space is tight. It wears the style you picked, like the XP bar.
• Reputation only — the bar can show your tracked faction instead of the XP at any level, not
only at max level.
• XP per hour and time left — your rate since login, and the estimated time to the level
you aim for.
• XP of finished quests — the XP of the quests you finished but did not turn in yet, in gold
on the bar, with the list on hover. Tells you when turning them in will level you up (optional).
• Reputation on hover — mouse over the bar to see your tracked reputation: faction, standing
and progress.
• Lightweight — texts are only redrawn when they change, and nothing runs while the bar is
hidden.
Options menu
Open it from the minimap button or with /mxp. The menu is built in the World of Warcraft
style — stone frame, gold ornaments, gothic titles, Blizzard checkboxes — and every change is
applied live.

| Section | What you can change |
| --- | --- |
| Style | Classic, gold framed, segmented, thin line, spark, split rested |
| Texture | Default, glaze, satin, minimal, glass, bevel, tube, brushed, linen, diagonal, ember |
| Size | Width (200 px up to the width of your screen), height (8 to 60 px) and target level |…

• No backup copy on Classic Era. It only does so on a build it knows to be Classic Era; on any other it stays on, which is the safe side of a wrong guess.

Install

• WoW Forever: World of Warcraft\forever\Interface\AddOns
• Classic Era / Hardcore: World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns

The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.8
• The reputation bar can sit beside the XP bar. Tick Reputation beside the bar and it moves to the right of it instead of under it, at the same height, so it costs no vertical space at all. Asked for by a player who keeps the bar under his hotbars, where space is a premium. Ignored while the bar runs the full width of the screen, since there is no room left on the side.
• It wears the style you picked, like the XP bar: the gold frame and its shine, the separators of the segmented style, and the thin line, which it follows down to the bottom of the bar.
• New "Reputation only" option. The bar shows your tracked faction instead of the XP at any level, not only at max level. With no faction tracked there is nothing to show, so the bar goes and the Blizzard one stays hidden with it.
• A switch flicked in the options now applies while the menu is open. The menu keeps the bar on screen so it can be styled where there is no XP left to show, and that was hiding what "Reputation only" did until you closed the menu.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.7
• Profiles have names. Create one from the bar you have in front of you, give it a name, and pick it again on any character. The list sits at the bottom of the options menu, next to the language: New makes a profile out of what is on screen, Delete removes the one in use and sends the characters that had it back to the first one.
• Nothing to save. Move the bar, change a colour, a texture, an option: it goes into the profile that character uses, right away. Another character picking the same profile gets the same bar, and a character that picks another one keeps its own.
• Your settings were kept. What every character shared becomes the first profile, and a character that had its own settings in 3.6 keeps them as a profile of its own, named after the character.
• The Character profile checkbox of 3.6 is gone: picking a profile in the list is what gives it to a character now.
• The minimap tooltip says which profile is in use, and the list names the character it is about.
• On the Forever beta, the macro copy carries the name of the profile: a character finds the one it picked again after a full restart of the game.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.6
• One profile per character. Move the bar on one character and your others keep theirs. Position, size, colours, style, texture, every option: a character can have its own set, or use the ones shared by the whole account. Tick Character profile in the options — its tooltip names the character and says which settings are in use.
• Two buttons at the bottom of the menu to go with it: Copy the shared ones puts the shared settings back on this character, Share these settings turns what you see into the ones every other character starts from.
• Everything you had set up becomes the shared profile, so no bar moves on any character when you update.
• A switch for the bar. Bar enabled hides the bar at any level, not only at max level, without disabling the addon — and the bar of the game stays hidden with it, as long as Hide Blizzard XP bar is checked. Four ways to reach it: the option, a middle click on the minimap button, a key of your own (Game Menu > Key Bindings > MyXPBar), and /mxp off / /mxp on.
• Reputation at max level. Instead of simply disappearing at max level, the bar can show your tracked faction, its standing and its progress, in the place of the XP. Optional, off by default, and the bar still disappears when you track no faction.
• The addon tells you when it was updated. One line in the chat and a short What's new panel, once per version and never again. /mxp news opens it whenever you want, and Announce updates turns the whole thing off.
• The narrow options menu is gone, and with it the Wide options menu option from 3.2. Stacked in one column the menu was around 1240 units tall where a screen offers 768: its lower half, the buttons included, was out of reach. The menu is always two columns side by side now.
• The language is now saved for the whole account, next to the profiles, so it no longer changes from one character to the next.
• On the Forever beta, a character with its own profile keeps a character macro of its own (MyXPBarChar), so its bar is still there after a full restart of the game. It is deleted again if you send that character back to the shared settings.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

What's new in 3.5
• Bar textures, asked for by a player on CurseForge. Eleven of them: the game's own one, which stays the default, plus ten drawn for the addon — glaze, satin, minimal, glass, bevel, tube, brushed, linen, diagonal and ember.
• They are grey on purpose: a bar multiplies its texture by the colour you picked, so every texture wears your own colour instead of imposing one. Nothing else in your settings changes.
• They are chosen from a drop-down that shows each texture under its name, already painted in your bar colour, so you see what you are picking before you pick it.
• The texture applies to the whole bar family: XP, rested, the finished quests and both reputation bars.
• Each one carries the crisp top light and bottom shadow that make a bar read as solid, and the patterns are anti-aliased, so nothing turns into a staircase when the bar is stretched across the screen.
Install
Extract the MyXPBar folder into World of Warcraft\\Interface\AddOns, then relaunch the game. The folder must be named MyXPBar.

Also available on CurseForge.

addons.changelog:
v0.7.0
Turning up counts. A fairness review: regulars roll first, real attendance, tighter rules for officers, and a one-click installer.

New:
• Regulars roll first. Players who came to at least 3 of every 4 recent raids (75% of the last 8 in that instance) roll first on items they want. This replaces "no loot last raid rolls first".
• Attendance is real time in the raid: you count as there if you were in the group and online for 75% of it. Nights under 10 players in the group don't count (bench does not make up the 10), and raids within 12 hours of the night's first raid count as one night.
• Officers can mark a player Bench for the night. Bench counts as present. Players on v0.6.1 no longer reload the whole raid each time someone is benched.
• A one-click installer for Windows (Install-RaidLootController.bat) and Mac or Linux (install-raidlootcontroller.command). It finds WoW: Forever, installs or updates, and keeps your settings. Run it again to update. If the game folder needs permission, it offers to try again as administrator. A linked addon folder (a dev checkout) loses only the link, never the files.
• A glowing next-step button for every role, and a "Next:" line at the top of the window.
• History shows removed items and wins taken back. Stats shows attendance. The Raid tab lists tonight's regulars.
• Adding an item when loot is not on Master Looter, and it is not in your bags, warns that whoever looted it must trade it.

Fairer:
• A reserve pays out as a second item only for regulars. For anyone else, a normal win uses it up.
• Several players on one reserve: those without an item roll first.
• Reserves close when the first boss is pulled, even if nobody clicked Start raid.
• In a tie or a roll-first pass, a player who already has an item can no longer win a second.
• A spec first picked after the raid started is judged by class only on items open to everyone. It can be picked between items (not mid-roll, not for an item you already asked for), so a player without a spec is never stuck.
• A reserve used up by another win no longer pays out when its item comes up.
• Without the addon (no loot spec), you can roll only on items that suit every spec of your class. Skipping the addon no longer lets a fury warrior roll on tank plate. An officer can set your spec with Set spec.
• Undo win keeps the player locked if they hold a free win they could have asked for normally.
• A reserved item that falls back to normal rolls keeps its class limit.
• Best for: healing gear goes to healers and spell damage gear to casters. Ranged attack power is for hunters only, feral attack power for cat and bear. Use: lines, hit and crit now count. Dodge and parry no longer make an item tank-only. Protection paladins no longer roll on spell damage gear, and cat and bear are told apart.

Officers held to the rules:
• No unlock, spec change or Who can roll change while a roll is open, and no Give to player or Undo win on another item.
• No Close roll in the first 15 seconds, unless only some players may roll (reservers, regulars, a tie) and all of them rolled. The Close roll glow follows the same rule.
• No Call roll during a boss fight. A boss pull during a roll wipes it after the fight, and everyone rolls again.
• No spec change for a player holding a reserve once reserves close.
• The officer log never drops gives, take-backs, closes, removals or unlocks to make room: a flood of one kind only pushes out its own kind. Starting a raid twice is refused.
• Undo win keeps the old winner and rolls on the item, for History.
• A master looter giving a raid item to someone other than its winner is logged for everyone, once per item, and only for a player in the group.
• A resync from the raid host never shortens your officer log.

Fairer and steadier. A second security review, fixes for a crash and for raids that could lock players out.

Loot rewards the time you give, not points you save up. Everyone gets one item before anyone gets two, and the players who turn up week after week roll first. Why the rules are the way they are, and how they were tested against players trying to game them: docs/FAIRNESS_AUDIT.md.
addons.name: Raid Loot Controller

releases.changelog:
v0.7.0
Turning up counts. A fairness review: regulars roll first, real attendance, tighter rules for officers, and a one-click installer.

New:
• Regulars roll first. Players who came to at least 3 of every 4 recent raids (75% of the last 8 in that instance) roll first on items they want. This replaces "no loot last raid rolls first".
• Attendance is real time in the raid: you count as there if you were in the group and online for 75% of it. Nights under 10 players in the group don't count (bench does not make up the 10), and raids within 12 hours of the night's first raid count as one night.
• Officers can mark a player Bench for the night. Bench counts as present. Players on v0.6.1 no longer reload the whole raid each time someone is benched.
• A one-click installer for Windows (Install-RaidLootController.bat) and Mac or Linux (install-raidlootcontroller.command). It finds WoW: Forever, installs or updates, and keeps your settings. Run it again to update. If the game folder needs permission, it offers to try again as administrator. A linked addon folder (a dev checkout) loses only the link, never the files.
• A glowing next-step button for every role, and a "Next:" line at the top of the window.
• History shows removed items and wins taken back. Stats shows attendance. The Raid tab lists tonight's regulars.
• Adding an item when loot is not on Master Looter, and it is not in your bags, warns that whoever looted it must trade it.

Fairer:
• A reserve pays out as a second item only for regulars. For anyone else, a normal win uses it up.
• Several players on one reserve: those without an item roll first.
• Reserves close when the first boss is pulled, even if nobody clicked Start raid.
• In a tie or a roll-first pass, a player who already has an item can no longer win a second.
• A spec first picked after the raid started is judged by class only on items open to everyone. It can be picked between items (not mid-roll, not for an item you already asked for), so a player without a spec is never stuck.
• A reserve used up by another win no longer pays out when its item comes up.
• Without the addon (no loot spec), you can roll only on items that suit every spec of your class. Skipping the addon no longer lets a fury warrior roll on tank plate. An officer can set your spec with Set spec.
• Undo win keeps the player locked if they hold a free win they could have asked for normally.
• A reserved item that falls back to normal rolls keeps its class limit.
• Best for: healing gear goes to healers and spell damage gear to casters. Ranged attack power is for hunters only, feral attack power for cat and bear. Use: lines, hit and crit now count. Dodge and parry no longer make an item tank-only. Protection paladins no longer roll on spell damage gear, and cat and bear are told apart.

Officers held to the rules:
• No unlock, spec change or Who can roll change while a roll is open, and no Give to player or Undo win on another item.
• No Close roll in the first 15 seconds, unless only some players may roll (reservers, regulars, a tie) and all of them rolled. The Close roll glow follows the same rule.
• No Call roll during a boss fight. A boss pull during a roll wipes it after the fight, and everyone rolls again.
• No spec change for a player holding a reserve once reserves close.
• The officer log never drops gives, take-backs, closes, removals or unlocks to make room: a flood of one kind only pushes out its own kind. Starting a raid twice is refused.
• Undo win keeps the old winner and rolls on the item, for History.
• A master looter giving a raid item to someone other than its winner is logged for everyone, once per item, and only for a player in the group.
• A resync from the raid host never shortens your officer log.

Fairer and steadier. A second security review, fixes for a crash and for raids that could lock players out.

Fixed:…

v0.6.1
• The minimap button no longer has a black disc spilling past its gold ring.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.6.0...v0.6.1

v0.6.0
Harder to cheat, lighter to run, and a family look. A security and performance review, and the shared look with WoWClearance.

Safer:
• A raid can no longer be started with a faked start time, and a flood of new raids is cut off, so saved history and the "rolls first" list cannot be pushed out or rigged.
• Once a raid ends, its old host can no longer change it.
• If two players in the group share a name spelling, their rolls and messages are refused rather than credited to the wrong one.
• One raider can no longer hold up live rolls by asking for resyncs or toggling "I want this" over and over.
• The loot catalogue only takes drops from your own group, ignores items the game does not know, and limits how much one guildmate can add.

Faster:
• The Raid tab no longer scans your bags on every redraw to show trade time left.
• A catalogue search shows the first 200 matches and stops re-reading every item; the Stats tab no longer recounts all history on every roll.
• A large catalogue share is no longer cut short at 5000 entries.

Looks:
• Help looks like WoWClearance's: gold section headers, blue questions, more space between answers, a "no matches" line, and open or closed sections are remembered.
• The minimap button uses a background that exists on this client, and starts at a different spot from WoWClearance's so the two never overlap. Its tooltip has the same layout as WoWClearance's.
• Chat lines start with "RaidLoot:".

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0

v0.5.0
Tighter and lighter. An audit against the Forever API, a performance pass, and ideas from RCLootCouncil, Gargul and RollFor.
• No addon? Reserve by whisper. Players without the addon whisper the raid host !rlc reserve , and the host's addon whispers back. Same rules as the Reserve button.
• Master loot is confirmed. An item only counts as delivered once it leaves the loot window. If the give fails (full bags, a unique item, out of range), it goes on the "still to trade" list instead of being lost.
• Trade time left. The "still to trade" list on the Raid tab shows how long each bound item can still be traded.
• Safer trade window. Won items go into the trade window one at a time, and stop if the trade closes. If the game hides who you are trading with, you are told.
• Out of date? If the raid host's addon sends something yours does not know, you get one line with the download link.

Faster:
• A resync after a reload sends a third less, so live rolls wait less behind it.
• Less work on every message, bag update and tooltip: history is no longer copied on each change, bags are only repainted when the "still to trade" list changes, and your spec is read from talents once.
• The catalogue search waits until you stop typing, and only one raider shares each drop with the group. Catalogue sharing waits until a fight ends.
• Saved data is smaller: gear notes are dropped once an item is won, and old catalogue kill records are cleared.

Fixes:
• Boss names, item links and chat senders that the game hides during a fight are now checked properly before use.
• A resync no longer prints "X won Y" a second time.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.4.1...v0.5.0

v0.4.1
Master Looter is the way to run it.
• The master looter hands items over, not only the raid host. Make the host or an officer master looter: their addon gives the winner the item straight from the loot window, and anything left goes on their "still to trade" list.
• A master looter who wins an item now gets it from the loot window too.
• The README and Help explain why Master Looter matters: without it the game's own Need/Greed rolls come first, and the addon only gets items everyone passed on.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/powerfulqa/RaidLootController/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1

addons.description:
A customizable way to view your equipped gear within the default character UI

Feedback on this AddOn or any others that I develop/maintain is always welcome. If you enjoy using any of my AddOns and would like to support future development, it is greatly appreciated.

Highlights
• Allows for a wide range of text customization (size, color, outline, and more to come!)
• Lets you know when items are missing sockets, gems, and enchants
• Can show gear information when inspecting players
• Provides an interface for customizing the order of secondary and tertiary stats under the Enhancements category based on class and specialization
• Shows abbreviated names for item enchants to reduce visual clutter
• Allows quick showing/hiding of enchant text if you are only concerned with the quality of the enchant (Dragonflight enchants and onward)
• Indicates when equipped items have embellishments
• Option to expand Character Info window so that gear information is more easily readable
• DataBroker integration for quick access to options via minimap icon or other DataBroker AddOns
Summary
PranGearView allows you to display customized information about your character in the Character Info window. If you want to know what item level each equipped item is, whether any sockets, gems, or enchants are missing, or what each equipped item's durability is, then this AddOn will serve you well. It is designed to be used on top of Blizzard's default Character Info window with the goal of not needing to install entire UI packs to have this information available.

As mentioned earlier, this AddOn was developed to work on Blizzard's default Character Info UI, so this may cause unexpected interactions when run with other AddOns or UI packs. If you would like to report any issues, please reach out with a description of the problem along with a list of all AddOns that were enabled when this was observed. Screenshots can also be helpful in troubleshooting and fixing these types of issues.
Current Locales/Languages Supported:
• English (enUS)
• French (frFR)
• Portuguese (ptBR)
• German (deDE)
• Russian (ruRU) [partial]
• Traditional Chinese (zhTW) [partial]
Usage
You can use the options window to modify all available options. To open the options window from the Chat window, type the slash command /pgv.
Options Window
• Item Level: Display item levels for equipped items
• Upgrade Track: Display upgrade tracks for equipped items
• Gems: Display gem and socket information for equipped items
• Enchants: Display enchant information for equipped items
• Durability: Display durability percentages for equipped items
Customization Options
• Item Level: Change text size, outline, and color
• Option to place item levels on top of equipment icons
• Upgrade Track: Change text size, outline, and color
• Gems: Change icon size, show missing gems and sockets, only show missing gems and sockets for max level characters
• Enchants: Change text size, text outline, show missing enchants, only show missing enchants for max level characters, show or hide button to display enchant text, change text color
• Durability: Change text size, show as bar, change colors used for durability thresholds
• Inspect Window: Choose which information to display when inspecting other players
• Character Stats: Set stat order based on class and specialization, show stats with decimal places
• Main options page: Show minimap icon, increase the size of the Character Info window, show embellishments, show decimals for equipped item level, hide shirt & tabard info, show debugging messages (you should never need to enable this)
Slash Commands
All slash commands can be invoked using the prefix /prangearview or /pgv. Examples listed here use /pgv for brevity.
• /pgv: Opens the Options window
• /pgv help: List all available slash commands for the AddOn
• /pgv ilvl: Toggle showing item level
• This is the same as clicking the Item Level checkbox in the Options window…

addons.description:
Automatically keeps Find Herbs minimap tracking enabled on WoW Forever.
Features
• Re-enables Find Herbs after login, UI reload, resurrection, and tracking changes.
• Finds the tracking entry by spell ID, independent of the client's language.
• Does nothing on characters without Find Herbs.
• Appears under Professions in the AddOns list with a flower icon.
• No settings, slash commands, dependencies, or saved variables.

While enabled, the addon intentionally turns Find Herbs back on if you disable
it manually. Disable the addon if you want herb tracking to remain off.
Compatibility
Targets the WoW Forever beta client, interface 16001, using
C_Minimap.GetNumTrackingTypes, C_Minimap.GetTrackingInfo, and
C_Minimap.SetTracking. Retail and other Classic clients are not claimed as
supported without in-game testing.

addons.description:
Less scrolling, better groups. Native-first role, class, and level filters
that fit naturally into WoW Forever's familiar LFG interface.

Better LFG extends the existing Groups and Players results instead of
replacing Blizzard's finder UI. It adds filters to the native options menu,
reuses Forever's Retail-style level-range widget, and preserves the existing
Show All Level Ranges option.
Filters
The filters are available from the Groups list's options cog.

Group requires
• Needs Tank, Needs Healer, and Needs Damage keep groups with an
open slot for each checked role.
• No \ already in group hides groups that already have a player of
your class.
• Has Tank and Has Healer require a current member with that role.
• Group fit requires enough open slots for your current group's members
and their assigned roles. When solo, any selected LFG role can fit.

Player requires
• Has Tank, Has Healer, and Has DPS keep players advertising any
selected role. With none selected, no role filtering is applied.
• The Player level range uses the Retail-style level-range widget. The
minimum and maximum are inclusive, and the default 1-60 range covers the
in-game level range. Saved values outside this range are clamped on load.
• Player class checkboxes keep any selected class. With none selected, no
class filtering is applied. Role, class, and level requirements combine.

Group fit is disabled with a red reason if your current group has 4 or more
members, at least 2 tanks, or at least 2 healers. Filter choices are saved per
character. When upgrading, the previous My role open setting maps to a
role-specific Needs option if one role was selected. Blizzard's **Show All
Level Ranges** setting remains in the menu. Group filters only evaluate
multi-member group listings; player filters only evaluate solo player listings.
addons.name: Better LFG filters

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that shows remaining time on failed spell or item casts.
Features
• Displays cooldown alerts for spells and items
• Compatible with multiple WoW versions (Classic, TBC, Wrath, Retail)
• Listed under User Interface in the AddOns list with a pocket-watch icon
Project Structure
The addon is split into small, single-purpose modules, loaded in this order (see CooldownAlert.toc):
• Libs/PsyUtils/ - reusable helpers shared across PsyKzz's addons.
• Core/ - constants, client-capability detection, API compat wrappers, bag cache, and settings persistence.
• UI/ - the on-screen cooldown text/icon display.
• Core/Bootstrap.lua / Core/EventHandler.lua - wires everything together; loaded last since it depends on Core and UI.

Open Options > AddOns > Cooldown Alert to change the font size (12-48, default 28). Moving the slider saves and applies the size immediately and shows a four-second countdown preview at the alert position. No Save button is needed.

Full Changelog Previous Releases

Full Changelog Previous Releases

Cooldown Alert0.0.6 (2026-09-22)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Merge pull request #11 from psykzz/feature/modularize-into-libs-core-ui
Modularize into Libs/Core/UI structure
• Clarify duration-object preference doesn't apply to threshold gating
Round-2 /code-review (Standards) flagged CooldownAlert.ShouldShowAlert as violating AGENTS.md's 'duration-object APIs must be used over raw math whenever supported' rule, since it always uses the raw (startTime, duration, isSecret) wrappers for its thresholds even on duration-object-capable clients.
That's intentional and unavoidable: duration objects are opaque by design (no readable magnitude), so there's no duration-object equivalent for a numeric threshold decision like 'is this cooldown long enough to alert on'. Rather than leave the doc and code silently disagreeing, clarify AGENTS.md with the exception and cross-reference it from ShouldShowAlert's doc comment.
• Fix secret-cooldown handling, item-cooldown fallback, alert gating, and countdown format
Addresses remaining code-review + PR feedback:
• Core/ApiWrappers.lua: GetSpellCD/GetItemCD now also return isSecret, and
never collapse a real (secret) cooldown to the same (0, 0) shape as 'no
cooldown' -- fixes a HIGH-severity bug where secret cooldowns were
incorrectly treated as no cooldown at all. Also normalizes nil
startTime/duration to 0 so callers get the documented (0, 0) fallback
instead of a possible nil-arithmetic error.
• Adds CooldownAlert.ShouldShowAlert(spellID, itemID), restoring the
pre-modularization gating (skip trivial/GCD-length cooldowns and cooldowns
already about to expire; always show on secret values since we can't
measure them). EventHandler.lua now calls this before showing either
display, fixing 'alerts show without cooldown validation'.
• UI/CooldownDisplay.lua + UI/TextDisplay.lua: resolving the active
cooldown now falls back to the spell's cooldown when the item's is
unavailable, instead of only ever checking the item.
• UI/TextDisplay.lua: secret cooldowns are shown with a generic '...'
countdown (governed by the hold/fade timer) instead of being hidden
immediately. FormatCountdown/UpdateElement are no longer exported on the
CooldownAlert namespace now that the settings-preview consumer is gone.
• UI/CooldownDisplay.lua: best-effort font application via
SetCountdownFont where the client supports it (previously position-only).
• Libs/PsyUtils/PsyUtils.lua: PsyUtils.Format.Countdown restores the 's'
suffix that was dropped during modularization (e.g. '3s' instead of '3').
Syntax-checked all changed files with a standalone Lua parser (fengari);
not smoke-tested in a live client (no local WoW test harness available).
Deliberately not changed (documented, not fixed):
• UI/CooldownDisplay.ApplySettings has no equivalent for textFormat: the
native Cooldown widget renders its own countdown text from the duration
object, so a custom format can't be computed without secret-value
arithmetic.
• The duplicated fade/update loop shape between TextDisplay.lua and
CooldownDisplay.lua is left as-is: the two widgets are different enough
(custom FontString vs. native Cooldown frame + duration objects) that
forcing a shared abstraction looked more like premature generalization
than a real fix.
• CooldownAlert.ApplySettings's dispatch-to-whichever-display-exists shape
is intentional (exactly one of TextDisplay/CooldownDisplay is ever
created), not treated as a Middle Man to remove.
• Move copilot-instructions.md to root AGENTS.md
Also fixes the stale shim-location claim flagged in code review: the doc said issecretvalue/FormatRemainingDuration shims 'live at the top of CooldownAlert.lua', but that file was deleted by the Libs/Core/UI modularization. Point at the actual current locations (PsyUtils.Secrets.IsSecret in Libs/PsyUtils/PsyUtils.lua, call sites in Core/ApiWrappers.lua and UI/TextDisplay.lua, and CooldownAlert.SupportsCooldownDurationObjects() in Core/ClientCapabilities.lua) instead.…

addons.description:
Track herbs or minerals - not the toggle.

Forever Tracking remembers your active Find Herbs or Find Minerals
choice and brings it back after a login, UI reload, zone change, or resurrection.
Turn tracking off whenever you like; it stays off until you select either one
again.
Features
• Remembers your pick: Saves the last active tracking spell per character.
• Handles the interruptions: Restores it after login, reloads, zoning,
death, and resurrection.
• Respects your choice: Turning tracking off pauses automatic restores;
selecting Find Herbs or Find Minerals again resumes them.
• Works in any language: Identifies spells by ID, not translated names.
• Stays lightweight: No settings, slash commands, or dependencies. Does
nothing if neither tracking ability is available.
How to use it
Enable the addon and play as usual. On first use, it selects Find Herbs when
available, otherwise Find Minerals. After that, it remembers whichever
supported tracking spell you use.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon that removes the Auction House buyout confirmation popup for enabled item categories. Clicking Buyout immediately purchases the selected auction, similar to TradeSkillMaster's quick buy. The cheapest auction is selected for you by default. Commodities use Buy to purchase the quantity shown once the server confirms a quote at or below the displayed total.
Features
• One-click buyout - no confirmation popup for enabled item categories; armor and weapons are enabled by default.
• Category settings - enable or disable individual item classes in Options > AddOns > Quick Buyout. Other item categories are opt-in; obsolete classes are hidden.
• Buys what you selected - pick any auction in the list and Buyout purchases exactly that one.
• Cheapest selected by default - when you open an item group, and after each purchase, the cheapest buyable auction (skipping your own and bid-only listings) is selected, so you can click Buyout repeatedly.
• Double-purchase guard - extra clicks are ignored while a purchase is in flight, and auctions already bought are never retried while the result list catches up.
• Commodity support - buy the selected quantity of linen cloth, herbs, and other commodities in enabled categories with one click. Price increases, unavailable quotes, and insufficient funds cancel the purchase with an error. Changing the item or quantity, leaving the commodity view, or closing the Auction House cancels a pending quote.
• Everything else unchanged - disabled item categories, bids, and Blizzard's unique-crafted-item warning keep their normal confirmations.
Compatibility
Works only with the modern (retail-style) Auction House UI (Blizzard_AuctionHouseUI):
• Retail
• Mists of Pandaria Classic
• Classic Era / Anniversary clients that use the new Auction House UI

Clients using the legacy Auction House UI are not supported.

addons.description:
A personal combat meter for WoW Forever. It shows you and your pets, and nobody else.

No raid syncing, no comparing yourself to the group, no plugin system. One small window that answers "how did I do?" and gets out of the way.
How it works
WoW Forever runs on the Midnight client, where addons can no longer read the combat log. Blizzard's own damage meter does the collecting and exposes it through the C_DamageMeter API. Metails! is a personal view over that data: it finds your row in each of Blizzard's meters and shows your spells, your targets and your deaths. That means it only ever shows what Blizzard tracks, and it costs almost nothing while you play.

During a fight the client hands addons locked numbers. Metails! still draws them live, straight onto the bars and text, and fills in sorting, percentages and tooltips the moment the numbers unlock.
Features
• Nine views: damage done, damage taken by spell or by attacker, avoidable damage, healing, absorbs, interrupts, dispels and a death log.
• Per-second rates for damage and healing, overall and per spell.
• Hover a row for per-second, overkill and the top five targets or attackers.
• Pet spells show with the pet's name on the row.
• Fights: the current fight, the previous one, an overall total, and every fight Blizzard still holds, named after the encounter.
• Report any view to say, party, raid, guild or a whisper.
• Open a second window to watch damage and healing at once.
• Hide automatically in or out of combat, change rows, opacity, bar texture and font size.
• Minimap button, a keybind, and an entry under Options, AddOns with the command list and the main buttons.
• Boss records: kill a dungeon or raid boss without dying and your damage, rate, time and spells are saved. Next time that boss starts, a separate movable box shows up to three damage bars on one scale: Best, Previous kill, and Current, live. Previous is left out when it is the same kill as Best. Best and Previous fill by elapsed time at an even pace, so a longer Current bar means you are ahead. Turn it off with /metails racing off.
• Real curves from your combat log: Metails turns combat logging on whenever you enter a raid or dungeon and off when you leave. With Sam's WoW Helper running (a small program that ships separately and installs with one double-click, no Python needed), a boss kill makes Metails flash a few coded pixels in the corner of the game window, the watcher sees them and rebuilds your records within seconds. Reload and the curve is there. Without it you still get the meter and the pace race. It reads the log, builds a per-second damage curve for every boss kill, and writes them into a small Metails_Records addon next to Metails. After a reload, the race box plays your record's actual damage second by second instead of an even pace. The kill prints how you did and updates the record if you beat it.
Views
| View | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Damage Done | Your damage by spell, with DPS |
| Damage Taken | Damage you took, by spell |
| Damage Taken by Source | Damage you took, by attacker |
| Avoidable Damage Taken | Damage Blizzard flags as avoidable, by spell |
| Healing Done | Your healing by spell, with HPS |
| Absorbs | Shields you cast, by spell |
| Interrupts | Your interrupts by spell |
| Dispels | Your dispels by spell |
| Deaths | Your most recent death, hit by hit, with your health after each |
Controls
| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Left-click | Next view (shift for previous) |
| Right-click | Menu: pick a view or fight, report to chat, lock, reset |
| Mouse wheel | Next or previous fight |
| Drag | Move the window |
| Hover a row | Details for that spell |

The minimap button shows or hides the window on left-click, opens the menu on right-click, and can be dragged around the minimap. A keybind to show or hide the window is under Key Bindings, AddOns, Metails!. The same command list and the main buttons live under Options, AddOns, Metails!.
Commands

addons.description:
LuaWorkbench is a Lua editor for World of Warcraft. Write and run code in-game, save snippets for later, and keep them organized in folders. It works on its own and does not require another addon.

The editor includes syntax highlighting, code search, and a separate output panel for printed messages, return values and errors. You can also search through all your saved snippets, including their code.
• Run code with the Play button, Ctrl+Enter, or F5.
• Save with Ctrl+S, recover drafts after a reload, or return to the last saved version.
• Run saved scripts at startup, login or on a WoW event you choose.
• Adjust fonts, indentation, bracket completion and the output limit in Options.
• Resize the window, give the code editor more space, or minimize it while you play.

Open it with /lua, /le, /luaeditor or /luaworkbench. The ? button lists the shortcuts and explains the available options.

Supports Retail, Forever and TBC, with translations for all 11 WoW languages.

Please keep in mind: This runs real Lua code in your game. Only run scripts you trust. A running script cannot be interrupted; an infinite loop can freeze the game. Automatic runs are off by default. Enable startup, login or a custom WoW event for each script; only its saved code will run.

LuaWorkbench's own code is MIT-licensed. Bundled libraries keep their original licenses and notices. The repository is private during initial development; contributions and translations will be welcome when it opens.

addons.changelog:
SpellPad Studio 1.5.0
The SpellPad can now tell a button's state without color, and its icon colors can be adjusted for color vision.
New
• Options > Color Aids. A new tab next to Look. Everything on it is off by default, and every example is a small live button that cycles between the normal look and the effect, so you can see what a box does before you tick it.
• State badges. Three boxes put a small badge in the corner of a SpellPad button: an arrow when its spell is out of range, a droplet when you lack the mana, and a crossed circle (with the icon turned gray) when it can't be used. The red, blue and gray tints still work and stay on top; the badge is the second signal for players who can't rely on color. They also work in combat.
• Icon color mode. Off, Grayscale, or Mute Red, Green or Blue with a strength slider. It changes how every SpellPad icon is drawn. This is a contrast aid, not a color-blindness correction: WoW doesn't let an addon remix color channels, so it can only turn one channel down or remove color.
• State colors. The tint of the out-of-range, no-mana and unusable states can be set with the game's color picker or a hex code, with a Reset button each. The Red-Green Friendly and Blue-Yellow Friendly presets now set them too (yellow against blue for red-green, red against pink for blue-yellow). They are not tested on real color vision differences, so the badges are the dependable aid.
Changes
• The out-of-range badge and the red tint are independent: you can have the badge without the red tint. The same goes for the no-mana and unusable states and "Dim unusable buttons".
• A preset you applied before now reads "Custom" until you apply it again, because presets cover three more colors.
• The !PAGE navigation buttons (Next Page, Previous Page, a page number) are never grayed, tinted or badged as unusable on the SpellPad.
• Items you create yourself (a mage's Conjured Mana Bun, a warlock's Healthstone, and others once the game has seen them) now show their real icon on cards and the SpellPad even when none is in your bags, instead of a question mark. On the SpellPad a consumable you have none of is dimmed, and its count reads 0.
• Single-Button Assistant in the Arsenal (Retail). It is listed first under General on the Spells tab, so you can put it on a card or SpellPad button with a click or a drag. Import Action Bars now imports an action bar slot that holds it, instead of skipping it.
Known issues
• Forever: not tested there yet; it will be checked at Forever's launch.
SpellPad Studio 1.4.5 (beta)
Pages can now live in folders, and a folder can switch by itself when its context starts.
New
• Page folders. A folder is a named set of pages. In Page Options, "Page folder" puts the page in a folder (Default, a folder you have made, or None to skip it) or makes a new one. The Pages list always shows its folders as headers, with the page count and, if the folder has a context, its icon. Pages in a folder get a thin gold bar on their left edge.
• !PAGE Forward and !PAGE Backward stay inside the folder of the page you are on, and wrap around at the ends. Pages set to None are skipped. Pages that have a context of their own step through the pages that share that context.
• A folder can have a context. When it starts (you mount, enter a dungeon, the fight begins) the folder's first page is shown, and while it holds, Forward and Backward move inside it without snapping back. Choose the context in Page Options (it then applies to the whole folder) or right-click the folder's header in the Pages list: the menu has Rename Folder and the same context list, one click each. A folder with the context In Combat only ever shows its first page, because pages can't change during a fight.…
addons.description:
A macro and keybind manager with action bars of its own. Built for Stream Deck and other macro pads.

Put a spell, item or macro on every key. See them all in one window, and on screen as a button pad. Made for WoW Retail (Midnight), and it works the same on WoW Forever.

Works with: Elgato Stream Deck, Corsair iCUE, other macro pads and keypads, a numpad, or just your keyboard.

Download: SpellPad Studio on CurseForge
Your own action bars
SpellPad Studio is a second set of action bars that lives inside the addon.
• Up to 36 buttons per page, and dozens of pages.
• It doesn't use Blizzard action bar slots. Your own bars stay as they are, and you can still work with them: drag a spell off a Blizzard bar onto a card and it stays on the bar, or hold the middle mouse button on a SpellPad button to copy its spell or item onto a bar.
• Your saved Key Bindings are not changed. A card's key works as a temporary override while the addon is running. The original binding stays in the game's Key Bindings screen and works again as soon as the card no longer uses that key. If a card takes a key the game already uses, the card tooltip, the Audit and the import preview tell you which action it overrides.
• Pages switch by themselves: mounted, stealthed, in a group or raid, in combat and more.
• Every button is a key you choose. Page 1 starts at ALT-1, ALT-2 and so on. Any key works.
What you can do with it
• See every key in one place. A card for each key, with a name, icon and macro. Search them, drag them to reorder.
• Build macros by clicking. No syntax to remember. The SpellPad Builder shows in plain English what a macro does.
• Know it works before you start. The setup guide checks that your keypad really reaches the game.
• Never lose your work. A backup (snapshot) is saved before every risky change.
Features
Organize
• One card per key, with a name, icon and macro.
• 4 to 36 cards per page, in any grid shape that fits your device.
• Search your pages and cards. Drag pages to reorder them.

Build macros
• Ready-made macros for your class, travel and teleports, target markers, world markers, group tools and emotes. (Forever also has consumable and raid-prep sets.)
• Macro text is colored and flags mistakes as you type. It suggests spell names too.
• Arsenal: click or drag a spell or item you know onto a card, or pick a ready-made macro or one of your game macros on its Easy Macros and My Macros tabs.
• SpellPad Builder: build a macro by clicking and dragging, with conditions like mouseover, focus and modifier keys.

The SpellPad (on-screen buttons)
• A copy of your macro pad on screen. Set its size and shape to match your device.
• Icons work like a normal action bar: cooldowns, charges, counts, range and procs.
• Click a button to run its macro.

Bring in what you already have
• Import Game Macros and Import Action Bars (footer > Tools) copy them onto new pages. Nothing is replaced, and you see a preview first.

Stay safe
• Snapshots: go back to how a page looked before a change.
• Audit: one list of every problem on every page. Click an entry to jump to it.
• Import preview: see what a shared page or profile will do before it is applied.

Share and customize
• Export and import pages and profiles as text. Keep several profiles per account.
• Save a card as a normal game macro.
• 7 window styles, a macro font size slider and many SpellPad options.
Getting started
1. Install the addon (below) and log in. A setup guide opens by itself the first time. To open it again, type /sps setup.
2. Tell it how many buttons you have, and whether the pad is wider than tall or taller than wide.
3. In your keypad app (Stream Deck, iCUE or another), make the top-left button send Alt + 1, the next one Alt + 2, and so on. The guide shows the key for every spot, and lights a spot up when the game receives it.
4. Click a spell in the Arsenal (or drag one onto card 1), then press the button.…

When it starts (you mount, enter a dungeon, the fight begins) the folder's first page is shown, and while it holds, Forward and Backward move inside it without snapping back. Choose the context in Page Options (it then applies to the whole folder) or right-click the folder's header in the Pages list: the menu has Rename Folder and the same context list, one click each. A folder with the context In Combat only ever shows its first page, because pages can't change during a fight.
• Drag pages between folders. Drag a page in the Pages list: drop it between two pages of a folder to join it at that spot, on a folder's header (or just under its last page) to be its first (or last) page, on the Default header to leave the folder, on the Skipped header to skip it. The ghost reads, for example, "Heal to Mounted, position 3". Moves the page can't make (a page with a context of its own onto Default) turn the ghost grey and do nothing.
• Pages with a context of their own group together. Pages that share the same context sit side by side under "Context pages". The first time you change a folder or a context, the whole list is tidied this way, after a snapshot (Restore can undo it) and with a chat line saying so; !PAGE n cards follow their pages.
Changes
• Context rules now belong to the profile. Before, a character's context rules were shared by every profile it used, so a new profile showed the context icons of the page numbers in your old one. Rules are now stored per character, specialization and profile; a new profile starts with none. If you used more than one profile, only the profile in use when you first load this version keeps your existing rules.
• Flying and Swimming win over Mounted. On a flying mount both Mounted and Flying are true, and the page with the lowest number used to win, so a Mounted page ahead of your Flying page stayed on screen after lift-off. The more specific context now wins; other pairs of contexts still go to the lower page. "Enable context override" still beats everything.
Known issues
• Forever: these changes haven't been re-tested there since Forever's beta went offline. They will be checked again at Forever's launch.
SpellPad Studio 1.4.0
Most things now take two clicks. Ready-made macros, your game macros and the new import tools live in one place, and the footer has a Tools menu.
New
• The Arsenal has four tabs: Spells, Items, Easy Macros and My Macros. Easy Macros replaces the old Easy Macros menus (Class, Group & Raid, Emotes, Advanced) with one searchable list, in categories: Class, Group & Raid, Emotes, Advanced, Travel, Interface. Search looks through every category. My Macros lists the macros saved in the game's own Macros window. On both tabs a click puts the macro on the selected card, and you can drag one onto any card or SpellPad button. The card is left waiting for Save & Apply, and a snapshot is taken first.
• A + button on every empty card. It selects the card and opens the Arsenal on the Easy Macros tab.
• A Tools menu in the footer next to Save & Apply: Audit, Restore, Import / Export, Import Game Macros, Import Action Bars and the Setup Guide.…

• Window style and Colors presets are now clickable tiles and chips instead of drop-down lists: one click from Options.

Changes

RCPartyOrbs ChangelogVersion 2.3.1
• Wrath Titan Reforged supported (client 3.80), checked in the Chinese game language.
• Release jobs updated to GitHub's newer Node 24 actions (no more Node.js 20 warning).
Version 2.3.0
Works on every WoW client: Retail (Midnight), MoP Classic, Cata, Wrath, TBC Anniversary, Classic Era and WoW Forever.
Retail and WoW Forever
• Party orbs keep working in combat. These clients hide party members' exact health and power from addons during combat; the orbs now fill from the game's readable percentage instead, and the numbers still show.
• Fixed errors from removed aura functions (UnitBuff / UnitDebuff are gone on Retail). Dispel colors and the purge highlight on the target orb work again, out of combat; in combat the game hides debuff types, so the orbs simply don't recolor then.
• Threat borders, range, offline and dead checks no longer error on values the game hides.
All clients
• Right-click menu works again on the Classic clients. Classic Era, TBC, Cata and MoP Classic moved to Blizzard's newer menu system and removed the old party/player dropdowns, so right-clicking an orb did nothing there. It now uses the newer menu wherever it exists.
• Color pickers fixed on the Classic clients for the same reason (they use the newer color picker now).
• WoW Forever runs the Retail interface, so it now takes the Retail code paths instead of the Classic Era ones.
• TBC Anniversary and WoW Forever are supported (new TOC files), and the version numbers for Retail 12.1 and Classic Era 1.15.9 are current.
• Fixed the options window sliders using an old function some clients no longer have.
• RC Party Orbs now lives on GitHub; releases are built and uploaded to CurseForge automatically.
• Checked end to end on every client: every options control and slash command, debuffed, dead, offline and out-of-range party members, raids, vehicles, every event the addon listens for, and nothing touches protected frames in combat.
Version 2.2.9
Bug Fixes
• Target orb now flips above the party orb on the first pass - The
"flip the target above when the orbs are near the bottom of the screen"
decision read the player orb's live GetCenter(), which is stale at load and
immediately after any reposition (the frame hasn't settled into its applied
position yet). It reported mid-screen, so the flip never triggered and the
target went below - until you toggled orientation, which re-ran the layout
after the orb had settled. That's why swapping horizontal/vertical and back
"fixed" it.
• The flip is now computed from the player orb's intended (saved) anchor
instead of live geometry, so a bottom-anchored layout puts the target above
immediately on login with no toggle needed. Falls back to live centre, then
screen centre, if no saved position exists.
Version 2.2.8
Bug Fixes
• Target orb no longer sits buried under the party orb - Two causes.
(1) Target orb containers are created at a lower frame level than party
orbs (2 vs 10, an intentional click-priority choice), and since the orb
bodies share the LOW strata, any overlap meant the party orb drew
completely over the target. (2) The unit name sits ~35% of the orb height
ABOVE each orb; in horizontal layout the target orb goes above/below the
party orb, so that name text landed in the gap and collided.
• PositionOrbs now adds the name overhang into the target orb's vertical gap
so names clear the neighbouring orb, and clamps negative target spacing to
zero so orb bodies can never physically overlap (a negative saved spacing
was enough to bury the target completely).
• Click targeting is unaffected: it relies on the hit-rect dead zone between
orbs, not on frame level.
Version 2.2.7
Bug Fixes
• Fixed 5 XML parser warnings from the minimap button - The icon TexCoord
element was singular; the UI schema element is TexCoords (plural). The
parser rejected the whole element and then each of its four attributes,
producing:…
addons.description:
Replaces the party frames with animated fire orbs: health and power orbs for you, your party and your target, threat borders, debuff colors, click to target, and modifier+click to dispel or resurrect.

Works on Retail (Midnight), MoP Classic, Cata, Wrath, TBC Anniversary, Classic Era and WoW Forever. On Retail and WoW Forever the game hides exact health, power and debuff types from addons in combat; the orbs then fill from the game's readable percentage.

Type /fpo in game for the options and commands.

Maintained by Raw Card.
Tests
pip install lupa && python3 tools/test_clients.py loads the addon (TOC, XML frames and Lua) on a simulated copy of every client and class, joins a party and plays a fight with debuffed, dead, offline and out-of-range members, a raid and a vehicle, clicks every options control, runs every slash command and fires every event the addon listens for. Retail and WoW Forever get hidden combat values, and touching protected frames in combat counts as a failure. It runs on every push.
Releasing (for the maintainer)
1. Update ## Version in every .toc file and add the notes to the top of CHANGELOG.md.
2. On GitHub: Releases → Draft a new release → Choose a tag → type v plus the version (for example v2.3.1) → Create new tag on publish → Publish release.
3. The Package and release job (Actions tab) builds the zip, attaches it to the release, and uploads it to CurseForge (project 1435676). It needs the CF_API_KEY secret (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions).

"flip the target above when the orbs are near the bottom of the screen"
decision read the player orb's live GetCenter(), which is stale at load and
immediately after any reposition (the frame hasn't settled into its applied
position yet). It reported mid-screen, so the flip never triggered and the
target went below - until you toggled orientation, which re-ran the layout
after the orb had settled. That's why swapping horizontal/vertical and back
"fixed" it.
• The flip is now computed from the player orb's intended (saved) anchor
instead of live geometry, so a bottom-anchored layout puts the target above
immediately on login with no toggle needed. Falls back to live centre, then
screen centre, if no saved position exists.
Version 2.2.8
Bug Fixes
• Target orb no longer sits buried under the party orb - Two causes.
(1) Target orb containers are created at a lower frame level than party
orbs (2 vs 10, an intentional click-priority choice), and since the orb
bodies share the LOW strata, any overlap meant the party orb drew
completely over the target. (2) The unit name sits ~35% of the orb height
ABOVE each orb; in horizontal layout the target orb goes above/below the
party orb, so that name text landed in the gap and collided.
• PositionOrbs now adds the name overhang into the target orb's vertical gap
so names clear the neighbouring orb, and clamps negative target spacing to
zero so orb bodies can never physically overlap (a negative saved spacing
was enough to bury the target completely).
• Click targeting is unaffected: it relies on the hit-rect dead zone between
orbs, not on frame level.
Version 2.2.7
Bug Fixes
• Fixed 5 XML parser warnings from the minimap button - The icon TexCoord
element was singular; the UI schema element is TexCoords (plural). The
parser rejected the whole element and then each of its four attributes,
producing:
Unrecognized XML: TexCoord plus Unrecognized XML attribute: left/right/top/bottom
The icon was silently rendering untrimmed (full 0-1 coords) instead of the
intended 0.07-0.93 crop.
Version 2.2.6
Bug Fixes…

1.5.2

• No flashing on your action bars while you're mounted. The HUD still shows what's next; the
flashes come back as soon as you dismount. Missing buff reminders also wait until you dismount.
• All action-button flashes pulse in step: the red missing-buff flash pulses together with the
rotation flash, so you can pick at a glance whether to attack or buff.
• In a party or raid, your raid buff (Fortitude, Kings, Mark of the Wild, Brilliance, Dark Intent,
shouts, Horn of Winter...) is also checked on everyone near you. If someone in range is missing
it (and has no equivalent buff), the reminder shows; hover it to see who.
• Paladin blessings and Warrior shouts: you can only keep one of your own up, so only one is ever
reminded and flashed. Kings (or Battle Shout) by default; Might (or Commanding Shout) when someone

Rotation page. Press Ctrl+C in the box that opens, then paste the link into your web browser.

import, What's new and copy-link boxes line up to the right of the menu (the row shrinks a little
if it wouldn't fit on your screen). Drag any of them to move the whole row. Closing the menu
closes them all.

and every role, through fights where the game hides combat data from addons (secret values),
and checks a spell is always suggested and flashed. It runs on every update.
• WoW Forever: a few more checks (is the target alive, hostile, targeting you) now treat a hidden
value as unknown instead of risking an error.

combat (the bar fades through the game's own secret-safe call).
• WoW Forever: the menu, picker, import and What's new windows no longer measure wrapped text.
The original Forever Rotation found that this can freeze the Forever client.

and Thorns (bear), Fortitude, Inner Fire, Divine Spirit and Shadowform, Arcane Intellect and an
armor, a paladin blessing and aura (any of yours or another paladin's counts, Greater ones too)
and Righteous Fury (tank), hunter aspect, Trueshot Aura and pet, shaman shield and weapon imbue,
rogue poisons, warlock armor and demon (the one you summoned last), Battle Shout. Group buffs

Rotation helper for WoW Forever (the camelot client, interface 16001) and the Classic clients (Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, MoP).

It shows the next three abilities on a small HUD, flashes the matching action-bar button, and also tracks heals, long defense buffs, interrupts, purges, cleanses, and weapon imbues. It does not cast spells for you.

Maintained by Raw Card
