RC-Translator 3.4.63
• Wrath Titan Reforged (client 3.80) is listed as supported again, so CurseForge offers this version to Titan Reforged players. Checked in the Chinese game language.
• Release jobs updated to GitHub's newer Node 24 actions (no more Node.js 20 warning).
RC-Translator 3.4.62
• RC-Translator now lives on GitHub. Releases are built and uploaded to CurseForge automatically.
• Retail and WoW Forever: the game can hide chat text from addons (for example in instances during combat). Those lines now pass through untouched instead of risking errors; everything else is translated as before.
• WoW Forever: its own TOC file for the Forever client.
• Updated the supported client versions (Retail 12.1, TBC Anniversary 2.5.6, Classic Era 1.15.9).
addons.description:
Real-language chat translator for World of Warcraft. Highlights foreign words in chat, adds a clickable [T] to translate a line, and can show everything translated in its own chat tab. 38 languages, packed dictionaries that load only when used.

Works on Retail (Midnight), MoP Classic, Cata, Wrath, TBC Anniversary, Classic Era and WoW Forever. On Retail and WoW Forever the game can hide chat text from addons (in instances during combat, for example); those lines are left as they are.

Type /rct in game for the options and commands.

Maintained by Raw Card.
Tests
pip install lupa && python3 tools/test_clients.py loads the addon on a simulated copy of every client and runs chat through it, including hidden chat on Retail and WoW Forever. It runs on every push.
Releasing (for the maintainer)
1. Update ## Version in both .toc files and put the notes in CHANGELOG.md.
2. On GitHub: Releases → Draft a new release → Choose a tag → type v plus the version (for example v3.4.63) → Create new tag on publish → Publish release.
3. The Package and release job (Actions tab) builds the zip, attaches it to the release, and uploads it to CurseForge (project 1462550). It needs the CF_API_KEY secret (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions).

addons.description:
Controller-first radial rings for WoW Forever. Hold a button, aim with the stick, release. Your food, usable items and mounts are already in there, because the rings fill themselves from your bags.
Features
• Made for controllers. Aim with the right stick (or left stick / D-pad). Release to use, A to select, B to go back.
• Tap to repeat. Tap the ring button without aiming to use your last pick again: one tap to mount, one tap to eat.
• Feel it. A short rumble when the stick lands on a new slot, and smooth animations.
• Rings that fill themselves
• Food: food & drink from your bags, best first, plus one Eat & Drink slot that does both at once.
• Bag: every usable item (potions, scrolls, quest items…).
• Mounts: your favorites, or all usable mounts.
• Quest: usable quest items.
• Markers: the eight target markers, skull first. Hard to do on a controller otherwise.
• Main ring with sub-rings. One button for everything: Main → Food / Mounts / Bag / Tools / your own rings.
• Separate rings too. Every ring can also get its own button.
• Your own rings. Spells, items, toys, mounts, your own macros, and other rings as sub-rings.
• No keyboard needed. Setup, buttons, names and settings all work on a controller.
• Cooldowns and usability on every slot.
• Share rings. /frings export gives a short code; friends paste it after /frings import.
• Works in combat. Picking and using happen in secure code.
• Two styles. Clean (round, minimal) or Classic (Blizzard borders).
• Keyboard and mouse work too: aim by moving the mouse.
Getting started
1. The settings screen opens by itself the first time. Later: the Settings slot in your Main ring, Options > AddOns > Forever Rings, or /frings.
2. Select Main, press Y and press the button you want for it. L3 or back paddles work best: you aim with the right stick, and Blizzard's gamepad UI already uses the shoulder buttons for targeting and the triggers as action bar modifiers. (A and B are kept for selecting and going back inside rings.)
3. Close with B. Hold your button, push the stick toward a slot and release.
Settings screen
Fully playable on a controller. Mouse and keyboard work too.

| Button | Does |
|---|---|
| LB / RB | Switch between Rings and Settings, or between picker categories |
| D-pad | Move |
| A | Open a ring, choose a slot, pick an item |
| B | Back / close |
| X | Clear a slot, delete a custom ring (press twice) |
| Y | Set the button that opens a ring (in the ring editor: rename it) |

Fill slots from Bags, Spells, Mounts, Toys, Macros or other Rings (sub-rings). The preview shows the ring exactly as it will appear.
Commands
Everything in the settings screen is also available as a command (/frings help):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /frings new | Create a ring |
| /frings add | Add an action |
| /frings add main ring: | Put a ring inside the main ring |
| /frings remove | Remove slot n (see /frings list ) |
| /frings delete | Delete a ring |
| /frings bind | Bind a ring directly, e.g. PADLSTICK (L3) or PADPADDLE1 |
| /frings export | Get a share code for a ring |
| /frings import | Add a ring from a share code |
| /frings style clean\|classic | Switch style |
| /frings input rstick\|lstick\|dpad | Choose what you aim with |

Each ring holds up to 8 slots, one per stick direction. Use sub-rings for more.
Known limitations
• Ring contents update out of combat. During combat a ring shows what was in your bags when the fight started (counts do update).
• Early release: please report issues!

addons.description:
Spotify Wrapped for your WoW characters. Play World of Warcraft normally. WoWwrapped quietly records the night.
When you log out, it updates your character's Wrapped: one page of cards that sums up everything so far, or one
month, one year, or any range of nights. Underneath is a facts page for every night you played.

WoWwrapped is a memory layer, not a meter. It never automates anything, never reads protected combat data, and
never needs the network in game. It is not a guide either: it tells you what you did, never what to do.

Status: early. Forked from Rambleon, which its author used nightly on the World of Warcraft: Forever beta,
on macOS. Other WoW flavours and Windows are not supported yet. Free and open, MIT licensed.
What a Wrapped shows
One card per subject, made from what was recorded:
• time in Azeroth and the longest night; levels gained; quests turned in and the biggest night
• the enemies that fell most often; the zones where the time went; the companions who were there longest
• deaths and where they happened; loot worth keeping; dungeons and their bosses
• your rhythm (the weekday and hour you play most, the latest night out)
• your own /wrapped note lines, quoted as written, and your pictures
• a persona (The Wanderer, The Slayer, The Errand Runner, The Good Company, The Daredevil or The Chronicler),
chosen by fixed rules: the same nights always give the same answer

With Claude Code logged in, a writer adds one line per card and a closing
paragraph, using only the facts on the cards. Without it the page is complete from the facts.
What a night looks like
Each night gets a Markdown log and an HTML story page (recap, numbers, quests, timeline, pictures), built by
themselves after you log out. The Wrapped links to the nights it mentions.

addons.description:
Threat tracker for tanks on WoW Forever (Interface 16001): warrior, paladin, druid in bear
form, any class that holds aggro.
It tells you, before it happens, that you are about to lose a mob, with a UI that looks like
the game's own.

Version française plus bas.
Features
• Your hold on every mob: a discreet percentage next to the nameplate of each mob in combat
with you. 100 % = the aggro is yours and nobody is close; it falls as someone closes in;
0 % = lost. Colour by state (held, warning, danger, lost).
• Threat frame: a bar drawn like Forever's nameplates, with the name of the player closest
to taking your target.
• Mob list: every mob in combat with you, sorted by danger (the one you are losing on top),
your current target outlined.
• Alerts in the middle of the screen, with a sound: "Bob closing in", "DANGER", and
"AGGRO LOST to Bob: TAUNT!" (it names the new holder, even outside your group).
• Settings window (minimap button or /aggro): lock/unlock the frames, what to show,
alerts and sounds, the two thresholds, a colour per state, a 6-second test, reset.
• No false alarms on a fresh target you have not hit yet, nor at the pull.
ScreenshotsUsage
1. Install, log in, show enemy nameplates (V).
2. Click the minimap button (or type /aggro) and untick "Lock the frames" to place the
frame and the list, then lock them again.
3. Tank. Press "Test" in the settings to see every alert without a fight.
Commands
/aggro (or /threathelper) opens the settings. Others: lock, unlock, show, hide, warn
,
danger
, sound on|off, plate all|target|off|x |y , list on|off, minimap,
test, reset, help. For diagnosis: log on|off|clear, probe, debug on|off (written
to the SavedVariables file).
Compatibility and limits
• WoW Forever beta, Interface 16001, build 1.60.1.70450. English and French.
• Threat comes from the game's threat API (UnitDetailedThreatSituation,
UnitThreatPercentageOfLead). On bosses the game may hide some values ("secret values"):
the addon then falls back on the threat states. Not yet measured on a boss.
• Clicking a row of the list cannot target the mob: Forever forbids addons to target through
a nameplate (checked in game). Click the nameplate itself.
• In raids the per-mob figures skip reading every raid member, to stay light.

addons.description:
Better Level-Up! (Forever) is the WoW Forever (Classic beta, Interface 16001) build of BLU: replacement sounds for the level-up moments that matter, powered by RGX-Framework. Everything that cannot exist on the Forever client has been removed — this build ships only what the game can fire.
Features
• Level-Up sounds — a sound of your choice when you ding, with queueing, volume, and channel control.
• Quest sounds — accept, complete, progress, and turn-in triggers.
• Reputation sounds — rank-up triggers for faction grinds.
• Honor rank sounds — PvP rank progression triggers on the classic honor system.
• Combat triggers — Bloodlust/Heroism and proc-style combat cues through the RGXCombat integration.
• Collections tab — collectible milestone triggers (mounts, pets, toys, transmog) are reserved for the Forever client's Collections system.

• Full options panel — General, Combat, Honor, Level Up, Loot, Quest, Reputation, Profiles, and Sounds tabs with profile support.
• Custom sounds — add your own .ogg files, or choose from the bundled BLU defaults and shared-media packs.
Removed vs Retail BLU
WoW Forever is an Era-lineage client; these retail systems do not exist there and their modules, tabs, sounds, and defaults are gone: Achievements, Battle Pets, Collectibles, Delves, Housing, Prey, Renown, and the Trading Post.

addons.description:
RGX | Path of Exile Level-Up!RGX Mods - RealmGX Community Project

Overview
Path of Exile Level-Up! (POELU) replaces World of Warcraft's configured default level-up sound with a Path of Exile-inspired chime whenever the player gains a level. It is a small, automatic sound addon built on RGX-Framework.

The Kiwi Says: "Exile ding! Bwwiiiee."

Deprecation Notice
This addon is no longer receiving updates. Its functionality and Path of Exile sound are available in BLU | Better Level Up! and BLU Classic | Better Level Up!, which combine this sound with a larger sound collection.

Existing standalone users may continue to use this repository as-is, but new installations should prefer the appropriate BLU addon.

Behavior and Features
• Plays the selected Path of Exile-inspired sound on PLAYER_LEVEL_UP.
• Provides high, medium, and low OGG variants; medium is selected by default.
• Plays through the Master sound channel by default.
• Requests that RGX-Framework mute the configured default level-up sound while POELU is enabled.
• Persists enablement and sound-variant choices in POELUSettings.
• Shows a welcome message on login while that saved preference remains enabled.
• Includes a test command for checking playback immediately.

POELU does not alter leveling, experience gains, UI frames, or game data. It only handles the sound associated with the player's level-up event.

Requirements and Compatibility
RGX-Framework is a required dependency and must be installed and enabled. The current TOCs declare these game interfaces:

| WoW flavor | TOC | Interface |
|---|---|---:|
| Retail | PathOfExileLevelUp.toc | 120100 |
| WoW Forever (Beta) | PathOfExileLevelUp_Forever.toc | 16001 |
| Mists of Pandaria Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Mists.toc | 50504 |
| Cataclysm Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Cata.toc | 40402 |
| Wrath Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_Wrath.toc | 38002 |
| Burning Crusade Classic | PathOfExileLevelUp_TBC.toc | 20506 |
| Classic Era | PathOfExileLevelUp_Vanilla.toc | 11509 |

These values describe the current release metadata. The addon is deprecated, so they are not a promise of compatibility with later game clients.

Language Support
POELU is fully localized across all 12 World of Warcraft client locales. The addon ships a single data/locales.lua that selects a locale block via GetLocale(), with an unconditional enUS base table providing the structural fallback — every key is present in every block. Supported locales (enUS plus eleven translations):

| Locale | Native name | Block |
|---|---|---|
| enUS | English (base/fallback) | unconditional base table |
| deDE | Deutsch | deDE |
| esES | Español (Europa) | esES |
| esMX | Español (Latinoamérica) | esMX |
| frFR | Français | frFR |
| itIT | Italiano | itIT |
| koKR | 한국어 | koKR |
| ptBR | Português (Brasil) | ptBR |
| ptPT | Português (Portugal) | ptPT |
| ruRU | Русский | ruRU |
| zhCN | 简体中文 | zhCN |
| zhTW | 繁體中文 | zhTW |

Each TOC declares ## X-Localizations listing all twelve locales. ptBR and ptPT use separate blocks; esMX has its own dedicated block (no longer sharing esES's block). Every block translates the complete key set — including the shared RGX_MODS_PREFIX brand key — so no untranslated key can leak into the game UI.

• Fixed: disabling now re-shows debuffs on visible nameplates in place, without a nameplate rebuild flash; hide no longer clears BuffFrame anchors.
v3.3.7-beta.3 - 2026-09-25Changes
• Disabling no longer forces a full nameplate rebuild (removed the visible ~0.3s blink of all enemy plates); restore happens in place. /rnd test keeps the manual rebuild fallback.
v3.3.7-beta.2 - 2026-09-25Changes
• Fixed: disabling the addon now re-shows debuffs on already-visible nameplates (forced nameplate rebuild after restore); hide no longer clears BuffFrame anchors.
v3.3.7-beta.1 - 2026-09-25Changes
• Maintenance beta for the early-beta release cycle, built and verified against RGX-Framework v2.7.8.
• No functional changes since v3.3.6.
v3.3.6 - 2026-09-19Changes
• Added Classic Era beta interface 16001 (WoW Forever, build 69913, project Camelot) to the TOC so the addon loads without the out-of-date flag.
• Fixed: Settings now survive SavedVariables loss. RND mirrors all settings into RGXFrameworkDB (RGX-Framework's SavedVariables) and restores them — with a visible chat warning — when RNDSettings comes back empty. • Synced the runtime version with the TOC metadata.

• Updated release metadata for the active supported client interfaces.

• TOC bump: Updated universal interface versions to 11509 (Classic Era), 20506 (TBC Anniversary), 50504 (MoP Classic), 120007 (Retail). Removed Cata (40402) and legacy Retail eras (110207, 120000, 120001).
v3.3.2 - 2026-06-30Changes
• Updated for WoW Retail 12.0.7 (Interface 120007).
v3.3.1 - 2026-04-29Documentation
• Added the v3.3.0 per-release changelog entry.
• Synced addon version metadata for the v3.3.1 documentation release.
v3.3.0 - 2026-04-25Changes
• Migrated to RGX-Framework: minimap button now uses RGXMinimap:Create() â€” drag, angle persistence, tooltip, and show/hide handled by the framework.
• Migrated events and periodic timer to RGX:RegisterEvent() and RGX:Every().
• Fixed: Minimap tooltip status now updates in real-time after left-clicking to toggle.

addons.description:
The RGX-Framework reference addon and its in-game testing suite, in one install. It exists for two audiences at once:

> The TOCs own RGX-Hello's version and minimum Framework version. The source reference tracks the Framework stable release for strict release conformance; source metadata is not a new release announcement.
• Addon developers — data/core.lua is the canonical "hello world": the smallest complete RGX addon, written in the declarative RGXAddon style you should copy when starting your own.
• Framework development — data/visualtest.lua is the visual QA harness used to test RGX-Framework's features in-game before releases. As the framework grows, this suite grows with it; the goal is coverage of every framework feature.
Source Contract Conformance
RGX-Framework owns the runtime Lua API and the reusable declarative contract, generation, validation, audit, MCP, and editor/authoring infrastructure. Its tools/rgx-mcp/ transport is a private source-tree contract-conformance fixture, not a separately published product or part of the player addon. Developer tooling is optional: RGX-Hello and the framework runtime do not depend on MCP, Node.js, or an editor. A future RGX Studio application is a downstream consumer of that foundation, not the owner of runtime semantics or a shipped prerequisite. RGX-Hello remains wired into the fixture in both directions:
• rgx_generate_addon can reproduce data/core.lua's structure from a short spec — the hand-written file and the generator's output are kept convergent.
• The framework's end-to-end test (tools/rgx-mcp/test/test-rgx-hello.mjs) runs the real MCP server against this repo: it validates core.lua's opts table against the schema and audits every Lua file here for unsafe patterns. If this repo drifts from the contract, the framework's own test fails.

That loop has already paid off: its first run caught a framework bug (the declarative slider's suffix was silently dropped — this addon's own Volume slider shipped without its "%" until RGX-Framework v2.4.1 fixed it).
The Hello World (data/core.lua)
That single call gives you saved settings with automatic persistence, a tabbed options panel with declarative pages/card grids and db-bound controls, a named repeating timer, a slash command, a minimap button, branded chat output, and framework-scoped startup logic. No event frames, no C_Timer, no SLASH_X globals, no SavedVariables boilerplate.
The Testing Suite (data/visualtest.lua)
A hand-built options panel exercising the framework's manual API (RGX:GetUI(), RGX:GetColorPicker(), RGX:GetDropdowns(), RGX:GetFonts(), RGX:GetTextures()) — this is also the reference for going beyond the declarative surface.

| Command | Opens |
|---------|-------|
| /rgxhello | RGX-Hello's own options panel (the hello-world addon) |
| /rgxvisual or /rgxviz | The full test suite (tabs below) |
| /rgxcolor or /rgxcp | The color picker directly |

Current coverage:

| Tab | Framework features exercised |
|-----|------------------------------|
| Colors | RGXColorPicker (SV box, hue bar, HEX/RGB inputs, presets, OK/Cancel), UI:CreateColorPicker swatches + Reset |
| Controls | UI:CreateToggle, UI:CreateSlider, UI:CreateVolumeSlider, reset buttons, label word-wrap |
| Dropdowns | RGXDropdowns:CreateNestedDropdown (groups, separators, checked state) |
| Media | RGXFonts font dropdown, RGXTextures statusbar textures |
| Tooltip | RGXTooltip — Tip:Attach builder, manual Show/Hide, HookNative("item") injection |
| Auras | RGXAuras — accessible-only player/target scans, WatchUnit + OnApplied/OnUpdated/OnRemoved live log, phase counter snapshots, restricted-target suppression, unsubscribe |
| Minimap | RGXMinimap — MM:Create (icon, tooltip, drag, persistent angle), Toggle/IsShown |
| Design | RGX:Font one-call styling, RGXDesign CreateButton/CreateSectionHeader/CreateDivider, theme tokens |
| System | declarative every.heartbeat self-cancellation, RGX:After, RGX:Every, RGX:CancelTimer |…

Stand Upv1.0.0 (2026-10-19)
First public release, for WoW Forever.
• "Sedentary" debuff after 45 minutes of play, +1 stack every 15 minutes.
• Clears when you go AFK, log out, left-click it or type /stretched, and gives a 10-minute "Well Rested Legs" buff.
• Right-click to snooze for 15 minutes. The ding waits until combat ends.
• Sits beside the minimap by default; /standup unlock to move it.
addons.description:
A World of Warcraft add-on that reminds you to get up and stretch, using a debuff that looks like it belongs in the game.

After 45 minutes of play you get Sedentary. It gains a stack every 15 minutes until you take a break. Walk away from the keyboard and it clears, and you get a 10-minute Well Rested Legs buff for coming back.

Built for WoW Forever (interface 16001).
What it does
| | |
|---|---|
| First stack | After 45 minutes of play without a break |
| More stacks | +1 every 15 minutes |
| Where it shows | A red-bordered icon beside the minimap, with the stack count and the time to the next stack. Movable. |
| Reminders | A soft alarm-clock ding when a stack is added (held until combat ends) and a slow pulse at 3+ stacks. No popups or screen effects. |
| Tooltip | Gets snarkier with each stack, and shows how long you've played since your last break |
| Clearing it | Go AFK (the game flags you after about 5 minutes away), log out, left-click the icon, or type /stretched |
| Snooze | Right-click the icon to stop new stacks for 15 minutes, for a raid or a dungeon you can't leave |

Time spent AFK or snoozed doesn't count. A /reload doesn't count as a break; logging out for a minute or more does.
Commands
• /stretched: clear it (I stretched!)
• /standup: minutes played since your last break
• /standup test: jump to 3 stacks to preview it
• /standup unlock / /standup lock: drag the icon somewhere else
• /standup reset: put the icon back beside the minimap

releases.changelog:
Before you update
Type /reload in the game after updating. No restart needed.
Fixed
• Handing out an item from the game's loot menu in the open world no longer asks how it was won; the question is only asked inside dungeons and raids.

Before you update
Type /reload in the game after updating. No restart needed.
Fixed
• Officers in a party now see "party chat" instead of "raid chat" in the add-on's award, correction and undo messages.
• Each new update is now prepared correctly even when the previous one was published at the same moment a change was merged.

Before you update
This is the first release: a fresh install, nothing to update.
New
• The add-on installs in WoW Forever; type /bf version in chat to check which version you have.
• Each release now lists its changes for officers in plain English.
• The add-on now follows each master loot hand-out until the game confirms the item arrived.
• The add-on can now work out who should get each drop (hard reserves, then soft reserves, then an open roll); officers will see it in the loot pop-up in a later release.
• The add-on can now read and check the reserves text copied from the site (the paste box comes in a later update).
• Officers can open a window with /bf (or the minimap button) with Awards, Reserves and Sync tabs; the version now shows with /bf version.
• The add-on now keeps loaded raids' reserves between sessions (the paste box and raid list come in a later update).
• The add-on now remembers which raid your awards go to, or that a run is not a guild run (choosing it on screen comes in a later update).
• The add-on now loads every upcoming raid's reserves from the desktop helper when you log in or type /reload, so officers with the helper don't need to paste them.
• The add-on now keeps its own record of the raid's awards, undos and corrections, saved between sessions.
• Officers can see the raid's reserves by boss in the Reserves tab, and see who reserved an item by hovering over it.
• Officers can now produce the copy-out text of a raid's awards to paste into the site's import (shown in the Sync tab in an upcoming release).
• The Reserves tab now marks bosses the raid has killed, and the add-on keeps track of which boss each drop came from.
• Officers who log in late or reload now catch up on the site's awards and voids from the desktop helper, and the add-on turns on the chat log when the helper is running.
• Officers can type /bf log to see what the add-on has noted this session.
• The Sync tab now loads a raid's reserves pasted from the site, lists the loaded raids, and lets you remove a pasted raid.
• Pending voids from the site are now remembered between sessions, so a voided award stays voided when it reaches you later.
• Officers who are loot master will get a loot pop-up that says who reserved each item; this change prepares what it shows, and the window itself follows in a later release.
• Groundwork for officers sharing awards: the add-on can now record an award into a specific loaded raid.
• Boss kills are now matched by the game's encounter id when the site's raid data has one, so kill-based loot suggestions work in non-English game clients.
• When you open a corpse as loot master, a pop-up now lists each item with who reserved it and who should get it (the buttons don't act yet).
• In the Sync tab, officers can now choose which raid awards go to, mark a run as not a guild run, and see who chose it and when.
• Officers' add-on can now build the raid-chat lines for awards, undos and corrections (not yet used by any button).
• Officers can now copy a raid's awards from the Sync tab to paste into Import awards on the guild site, and the minimap tooltip shows the selected raid.
• Officers' add-ons can now receive each other's awards from the group, ready for sending to be switched on in a later update.
• Officers can now give an item to its winner with one click on the loot pop-up: the add-on hands it out, announces it in raid chat and records the award, and waits out boss fights while the game locks chat.
• The Sync tab now lists awards made while no raid was chosen, and lets officers attach them to a raid or discard them.
• Officers' add-ons can now send their awards to each other over the group, paced so the game doesn't throttle them and held during boss fights, ready for the loot pop-up to use in a later update.
• When the game doesn't confirm a hand-out, the add-on now records it as not confirmed and can try again, give the item to someone else, or mark it as not handed out.…

addons.description:
NiceDamage (Reloaded) is a lightweight combat text font addon for World of Warcraft that allows you to customize the appearance, size, and animation behavior of damage and healing numbers.

It modifies Blizzard's implementation of combat text fonts. Meaning it should not have any performance impact.

⚠️ Important: Application of Changes
Due to how the World of Warcraft engine handles 3D world text:
• Changing the Font File: Requires you to Log Out to the character selection screen and log back in. A /reload will NOT work for the initial font load.
• Changing Size, Gravity, or Duration: Takes effect instantly without needing to relog or reload.

Features
• Custom Font Selection: Choose from a curated list of popular combat fonts including Pepsi, Bangers, Big Noodle Titling, and Expressway.
• Font Scaling: Real-time adjustment of damage number sizes.
• Animation Control: Fine-tune the "physics" of your combat text by adjusting Gravity (how fast numbers fall) and Ramp Duration (how long they stay on screen).
• SharedMedia Support: Automatically detects fonts from other addons installed in your game.

Configuration
Access the settings panel using:
• Escape > Options > Addons > NiceDamage (Reloaded).
• Type /nicedamage or /nd ingame.

Included Fonts
NiceDamage (Reloaded) comes bundled with a curated selection of fonts:
• Pepsi Modern: The classic look (Default for all clients).
• Zero Cool: A bold, high-energy font.
• Pepsi Cursive: A stylized cursive variant.
• Technical/Pixel Fonts: Pf Tempesta Seven, Prototype, Expressway.
• Thematic Fonts: Die Die Die, LifeCraft, Big Noodle Titling.

addons.changelog:
[1.0.114] - 2026-10-31

Added

Foundry.Settings: launcher entries. F.Settings:New({ title = ..., buttonText = ..., launch = fn }) registers an entry under AddOns in the Settings panel that holds one button. Clicking it calls your function with no arguments, which should show your own options window. Use it when your options live in your own window instead of building a placeholder panel. The entry's title and button text are found by the Settings search. Settings moves to API_VERSION 2 and the library to API_VERSION 7. Only one Foundry copy runs, the first one loaded, so it may be older than the copy you shipped (see Which copy runs, and why). To raise an error on an older copy, call F:RequireModule("Settings", 2). To fall back instead, check F.Settings and (F.Settings.API_VERSION or 0) >= 2 before using it.
addons.description:
Foundry is a modern addon library for WoW authors who want to build on Blizzard's current toolkit: the Settings API, the new menu system, ScrollBox, tooltip hooks, and the rest. It is an Ace3 alternative for authors who want one, and it works alongside Ace3 if you would rather adopt it a piece at a time.

By BawrLabs.
What it is
Foundry exists to give addon authors a focused, modular toolkit built on Blizzard's modern API surface.

Foundry is:
• Bridges where bridges are missing. Foundry covers modern Blizzard APIs that don't have actively maintained community wrappers (the new menu system, modern tooltip hooks, ScrollBox).
• Less boilerplate, never less control. Each module collapses a verbose native pattern into a few readable lines, and :GetNativeHandles() always hands back the raw Blizzard objects, so you trade typing, not control.
• Adopt incrementally. Start with a single module, keep using Ace3 (or anything else) right alongside it, and add more as they ship, with no all-or-nothing commitment.
• Grows by demand. Modules ship when a real addon actually needs them, proven against real use before they land, and you can propose the next one.
Why
Foundry started as a refactor of my own addons (Homestead and BawrSpam) to use more of the in-game toolkit. Since that was happening anyway, making it available to other authors was a no-brainer. The goal isn't to replace Ace3 because it isn't going anywhere. It's just to offer a smaller option for authors who want one.

Ace3 is great, widely used, and still actively maintained. But it was designed against an earlier API surface than what's available today. Blizzard has shipped years of new addon APIs since: the Settings API, the new menu system, ScrollBox, modern tooltip hooks. Foundry is for authors who want a toolkit built on those newer APIs from the start.
Modules
Foundry-1.0 delivers a focused set of modules covering what most addons reach for:

| Module | What it does | Blizzard surface | Ace3 equivalent | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commands | Slash command registration with a per-consumer controller, auto-help, guard checks, and longest-prefix dispatch for multi-word names. | SlashCmdList, SLASH_* globals | AceConsole-3.0 | Available |
| Events | Owned event registration with automatic cleanup, scoped to the consuming addon. | CreateFrame event frames, RegisterEvent | AceEvent-3.0 | Available |
| Lifecycle | Honest hooks over the game's load and login signals, including an optional pre-unload hook that distinguishes reload from closing the client. | ADDON_LOADED, PLAYER_LOGIN, ADDONS_UNLOADING, PLAYER_LOGOUT | AceAddon-3.0 (lifecycle portion) | Available |
| DB | SavedVariables management with defaults, profiles, and per-character data. Reads existing AceDB save files unchanged. | SavedVariables, SavedVariablesPerCharacter | AceDB-3.0 | Available |
| List | Bridge over Blizzard's modern scrolling-list system, which is powerful but punishing to use directly. | ScrollBox, ScrollBoxListView, DataProvider, ScrollUtil | No direct Ace3 equivalent | Available |
| Settings | Options panel registration through Blizzard's modern Settings API, plus a searchable launcher entry with one button that opens your addon's own options window. | Settings.RegisterCanvasLayoutCategory, RegisterVerticalLayoutCategory, RegisterInitializer, RegisterAddOnCategory; CreateSettingsButtonInitializer | AceConfig-3.0 / AceConfigDialog-3.0 | Available |
| Tooltip | Bridge over Blizzard's modern tooltip-hook system. Current and supported, but under-documented for addon authors. | TooltipDataProcessor (added in Patch 10.0.2) | No direct Ace3 equivalent | Available |
| Menu | Bridge over Blizzard's modern menu system, which replaced the deprecated UIDropDownMenu in Patch 11.0.0. | Blizzard_Menu, MenuUtil | LibUIDropDownMenu (community library, now unmaintained for current retail) | Available |…

[1.0.113] - 2026-10-28

Changed

Foundry.Settings now always uses Blizzard's Settings API. Every client Foundry supports has it, so addons on those clients see no change, and GetNativeHandles().mode is always "settings". On a client without the Settings API, Settings:New registers nothing. Dev builds raise an error. Release builds print a message and return without registering, instead of falling back to the old InterfaceOptions panel.

[1.0.112] - 2026-10-26

Fixed

Foundry.Tooltip no longer skips a handler during a render when another handler of the same tooltip type destroys a controller and then creates a new one. The new controller now runs in that same render too, including when the handler that created it destroyed itself and was the last handler in the list.

Changed

If your addon still holds a destroyed tooltip controller, it keeps later controllers of the same tooltip type from being freed until you release it. Set your reference to nil after calling Destroy.

[1.0.111] - 2026-10-21

Fixed

Foundry.List now refuses a NaN or infinite config.extent, and handles a NaN or infinite value from extentCalculator the same way, matching how it already treated zero and negative values. Dev builds raise an error. Release builds print a message and then refuse the list (config.extent) or fall back to an extent of 1 (extentCalculator).

Changed

The TOC notes and README now describe Foundry as a modern addon library and Ace3 alternative.

[1.0.110] - 2026-10-13

Changed

Updated for patch 12.1.5 and includes minor internal cleanup.

Updated the bundled Foundry-1.0 library to v1.0.114.

Blocking a player by hand now also hides their guild, officer and community chat in your chat windows. Their messages still show in the guild and Communities window.

Guild Discord chat from a blocked player stays visible unless you turn on "Hide players you blocked in guild Discord chat" in Config > Blocked. It is off by default and only appears on clients that have guild Discord chat.

History labels these rows Guild, Officer and Guild (Discord). Community rows show the community's name, or Community when the name is not available. The stats line now counts Guild.

The block confirmation on the guild and community roster now says which chats are hidden and which still show.

Updated for patch 12.1.5.

v1.5.1 (2026-10-07)

Removed the developer section from Config and the /bdev commands. They were meant for testing Sift.

Reset Settings now sits in the UI section of Config.

v1.5.0 (2026-10-05)

Reworded the Config and History tooltips, help text and navigation hints in plainer English, and the History stats line label now reads OTHER.

The keyword detail line in History shows only the phrase you typed.

Reworded the "Always allow" and "Restore + Always allow" tooltips, and the empty Allowlist message and the /sift rebuildstats message. The Report entry in the History row menu now uses the same label as the detail pane.

The "Filtering by" sender chip in History now has its own row instead of covering the column header and the first row.

v1.4.1 (2026-09-29)

Sift supports WoW Forever, alongside Retail, Classic Era, Anniversary and MoP Classic.

Upgrading from BawrSpam now brings your allowlist, blocked list, settings and History across to Sift. Anything you already changed in Sift stays as it is, and players you blocked by hand stay marked as blocked by you.

A small "Sift (legacy data)" entry now appears in your addon list. It runs no code and only holds your old BawrSpam saves so Sift can bring them across.

Added "Block (Sift)" to the guild and community roster right-click menus, with a confirmation before it blocks.

Right-clicking the name of someone you just blocked in chat now shows them as blocked, instead of showing Block as unavailable.

Config > Blocked now marks the players Sift blocked on its own, and long names are shortened so they no longer run under the Remove button.

Added hover tooltips across the History window, and reworded the Config and History tooltips in plainer language.

Tidied the History and Config layout: column headers and buttons size to their own text, the category filter chips wrap to a second row, the window shrinks to fit the Config tab and returns to full size for History, and the Config status line is larger.

Pressing Enter in Add from History now adds the name.

The Report action in History now works. It opens the game's report window with the sender and chat line already filled in.

On WoW Forever, Sift now shows players by first name and surname, and Add from History and /sift allow accept the full name.

Updated the bundled Foundry-1.0 library to v1.0.106.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that shows enemy and friendly player nameplates only while you're in combat. It's the "combat plates" option from Leatrix Plus on its own, plus friendly plates that follow health and a friendly-left / enemy-right layout.
• Entering combat turns nameplates on.
• Leaving combat turns them off.
• Logging in, reloading, or zoning out of combat turns them off.

If you press V (or Shift+V for friendly plates) to show nameplates outside combat, they hide again at the end of your next fight. Uninstalling leaves them off; press V / Shift+V to turn them back on.
Options
Open the panel with /ddn-options, or Esc > Options > AddOns > Dynamic Display Nameplate. Every switch starts on except the engaged, group, names and missing-health ones. The panel scrolls if it doesn't fit.
• Enemy plates only in combat: turns enemy plates on when you enter combat and off when you leave it.
• Enemy plates only for mobs fighting your group: hides the plate of any enemy NPC that isn't your target, has nobody in your group (you, party or raid members, and pets) on its threat list, and isn't targeting one of you. Enemy players always show. Off by default. Hidden plates still take up room when plates stack.
• Friendly player plates only in combat: same for friendly player plates.
• Friendly player plates only for your party or raid: hides the plate of any friendly player who isn't in your group, so solo you see none. Friendly NPCs aren't affected. Off by default.
• Fade friendly plates at full health: while a friendly player is at full health, their plate is faint (30% opacity) in combat and hidden out of combat. It turns solid as soon as they lose health. Hidden plates still take up room when plates stack.
• Show hurt friendly plates out of combat: keeps friendly plates on outside combat, so anyone below full health still shows. Only while "Friendly player plates only in combat" is on; with that off, the addon leaves friendly plates alone.
• Only the name of friendly players at full health: in place of fading or hiding them, friendly plates at full health show just the name, in class colour, in and out of combat. The health bar appears as soon as they lose health. Turns on Blizzard's class-coloured friendly names and turns off Blizzard's own name-only setting (which hides the bar even when they're hurt); turning it off puts both back the way they were. Off by default.
• Missing health on friendly plates: friendly plates show how much health is missing (-0 at full health) in place of Blizzard's health number. Off by default. This used to be the Deficit Plates addon; while that one is still enabled, it keeps the health text and this option waits.
• Friendly plates on the left, enemy plates on the right: friendly plates shift left of the character and enemy plates right. On clients with the nameplateMotion setting, plates also stack instead of overlapping, and turning it off puts your old setting back. WoW Forever doesn't have it, so there plates only shift.
Inside dungeons and raids
Blizzard keeps friendly plates off limits to addons there, so the friendly-plate options (group only, fade, missing health, sides) don't apply to them; they look the way Blizzard draws them. Enemy plates work as usual. For missing health in a dungeon, set the party frames to show health lost in Blizzard's options.
Commands
• /ddn-help lists the commands.
• /ddn-options opens the options panel.
• /ddn-enemies [on|off] sets whether enemy plates follow combat. On by default. When off, the addon leaves enemy plates alone.
• /ddn-friends [on|off] sets whether friendly player plates follow combat. On by default. When off, the addon leaves friendly plates alone.
• /ddn-engaged [on|off], /ddn-group [on|off], /ddn-fadefull [on|off], /ddn-showhurt [on|off], /ddn-names [on|off], /ddn-deficit [on|off] and /ddn-sides [on|off] switch the other seven options.…

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon for immersion. The whole UI hides the way Alt+Z hides it, and comes back only when you need it:
• in combat,
• while you have a living target,
• while a window is open (character sheet, spellbook, quests, vendors, the game menu…).

Being in a group doesn't bring it back; only combat does. A dead target doesn't either: loot it and only the loot window shows.

Out of combat, the world map, the loot window, your bags and any window you open from a minimap button show on their own, with the rest of the UI still hidden; Esc closes them. Chat works too: press Enter and type as usual, and chat fades away 5 seconds after you're done. The minimap, tooltips, the breath bar and the yellow quest progress text ("Wolf Pelt: 3/8") always show.

Your arrow on the world map is hidden, so you find your way from the landmarks.

Press Esc to bring the UI back until something changes (a target, a fight, a window); Esc again opens the game menu as usual.
Options
Open the panel with /dui-options, or Esc > Options > AddOns > Dynamic Immersive UI. Every switch starts on.
• Hide the UI out of combat: the main switch. Off, the addon leaves the UI alone.
• A target brings the UI back: shows the UI while you have a living target.
• Map, loot window and bags on their own: also windows opened from a minimap button. Off, these bring the whole UI back like any other window.
• Minimap always visible: keeps the minimap on screen while the rest of the UI is hidden.
• Hide your arrow on the world map: party and raid members still show.
Commands
• /dui-help lists the commands.
• /dui-options opens the options panel.
• /dui-hide, /dui-target, /dui-solo, /dui-minimap and /dui-arrow take on or off; with no argument they toggle.
• /dui-status shows what the addon sees. Its output is also saved in the addon's saved variables; include it in bug reports.

Settings are saved per account.

TurboFace 0.20.0
TurboFace 0.20.0 adds a saved sticky note and weapon-stone reminders, fixes
class spell-rank detection after trainer visits, and prevents a dungeon
swing-timer error involving protected target identities.
New features
• Sticky Note: Enable it in Options > Speedrun, then open it with
/tf note or /tfnote. Drag the header to move it, collapse it to the
header, or close it. Text, position, and collapsed/open state persist per
character. The dark background is easier on the eyes, and the feature
remains dormant when disabled.
• Weapon stones: The Class reminder queue now checks both hands for an
uncoated melee weapon and a compatible, level-eligible sharpening stone or
weightstone in your bags. Supports ordinary Rough through Dense stones.
Existing temporary enchants, poisons, and imbues satisfy the reminder.
Enabled by default, with a toggle in Class Features; hidden during combat
and while dead. Keep the queue's “Only show while in combat” option off to
see this out-of-combat reminder.
Fixes
• Class Training uses explicit learned spell IDs and client-specific rank
replacement chains across all nine classes, preventing starter-rank aliases
from incorrectly hiding later ranks.
• Trainer visits preserve rank metadata when the client omits rank labels,
and resolve ambiguous spell families using catalog rank and level data.
• The training queue respects the same learned-rank result as the list.
• Target and nameplate swing timers reject unreadable GUIDs before cache
lookup, avoiding the secret-table-key error reported in dungeons.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79. Existing settings and
character data are preserved.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.20.0.zip — Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.20.0.zip — Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to one
TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.4
TurboFace 0.19.4 fixes starter-rank detection in Class Training, including
Forever spellbook aliases that could hide untrained Warrior abilities.
Highlights
• Learned-rank detection prefers the base spellbook slot identity over an
active spell override. Heroic Strike and Rend Rank 2 remain available for
training when the character still knows only their starter ranks.
• Catalog level requirements cap impossible future-rank aliases, keeping
Battle Shout Rank 2 in a level-10 Warrior's future training list. The cached
snapshot refreshes when the character's level changes.
• Heroic Strike Rank 2 now correctly requires Rank 1 instead of itself.
• Both Classic and Forever include the shared training fixes and modern
spellbook compatibility fallback.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.19.4.zip — World of Warcraft Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.4.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to a
single TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.3
TurboFace 0.19.3 adds a safe mover for Forever's native target-unit castbar
and refreshes the built-in Rumblecrush preset from the latest live profile.
Highlights
• Forever players can position Blizzard's native Target Unit Cast Bar from
TurboFace's Blizzard Movers section. TurboFace moves only the native bar's
anchor and leaves cast state, rendering, animations, and interaction under
Blizzard ownership.
• The mover reapplies its position after Blizzard target and aura layout passes,
defers protected writes during combat, and restores Blizzard's layout when the
mover or the global Movers module is disabled.
• Position-only movers do not expose Hide or Click Through controls, preventing
those generic controls from changing native-frame behavior.
• /tfmove targetcastprobe reports the resolved native frame, protection state,
anchor ownership, deferred state, geometry, and last write error.
• Rumblecrush's Preset is refreshed from the 2026-10-06 profile export. It
positions the native target castbar at CENTER (145, -375), moves Target of
Target to CENTER (350, -260), and enables nameplate swing timers and
Speedrun Splits.
• The Forever-only native castbar mover data is safely inert in the Classic
package; the shared preset updates continue to apply normally.

Portable SavedVariables remain at schema version 79.
Downloads
• TurboFace-Classic-0.19.3.zip — World of Warcraft Classic Era 1.15.9
• TurboFace-Forever-0.19.3.zip — World of Warcraft Forever 1.60.1

Install only the package matching your client. Each archive extracts to a
single TurboFace/ addon directory.

TurboFace 0.19.2
TurboFace 0.19.2 makes nameplate combo points persist on their actual target
while preserving Classic's single-target ownership rules.
Highlights
• Combo points remain visible on their target's nameplate after deselecting it
or selecting another unit, much like retained nameplate debuffs.
• Only the current target is queried. TurboFace stores the last readable count
in addon-owned per-nameplate state and never probes protected non-target data.
• Earning the first combo point on a different target transfers ownership and
immediately clears every older visible combo snapshot.
• Nameplates with zero combo points show no combo row, whether selected or not.
Positive snapshots continue to display the full five-slot progression row.
• Nameplate removal and pooled-frame reuse clear retained snapshots so combo
points cannot leak onto another unit.
• Forever's detached aura guides release or restore combo-row spacing whenever
a retained row changes visibility, without reanchoring secret-bound aura
containers.
• Druid form transitions hide retained rows outside Cat Form and restore valid
positive snapshots on returning to Cat Form.

TurboFace 0.19.1
TurboFace 0.19.1 is a focused hotfix for movable nameplate combo points and
starter-spell ranks in Class Training.
Highlights
• Forever nameplate debuffs now follow an addon-owned movable anchor guide.
Moving combo points downward dynamically releases their reserved space, while
the default upper position continues to keep debuffs clear of the combo row.
• The aura fix does not reanchor Blizzard's secret-bound AuraContainer after it
has been attached, preserving the Midnight-safe ownership boundary.
• Class Training now matches the exact spell ID in each live spellbook slot to
the class rank catalog.

Strike and Heroic Strike—no longer lose Rank 2 while still showing Rank 3.

addons.description:
Addon para WoW Forever que guía al jugador del nivel 1 al máximo: qué hacer a continuación, por qué y cómo. Interfaz en español e inglés, sin conexión durante la partida.
Qué hace ya
| Pestaña | Contenido |
| --- | --- |
| Progresión | Objetivos con su motivo y nivel de confianza: mazmorras para tu nivel (o la próxima), misiones que recoger antes de entrar, misiones de clase, zona recomendada y ranuras de equipo débiles. Se pueden marcar como hechos, posponer u ocultar. |
| Mazmorras | 42 mazmorras y bandas, incluidas las nuevas de Forever, clasificadas para tu personaje. Cada ficha tiene Información (entrada, cambios en Forever, jefes), Misiones (requisitos, recompensas, experiencia y si ya las hiciste), Botín (iconos, calidad, filtrado por lo que tu clase puede usar y mejoras frente a tu equipo) y Mapa. |
| Equipo | Mejoras en tus bolsas: compara por estadísticas cada objeto equipable de tus bolsas con lo que llevas, con pesos según tu clase y especialización, y muestra la diferencia («+5 Intelecto, −2 Aguante»). También el equipo actual con su nivel de objeto y ranuras débiles. |
| Misiones | Misiones de mazmorra y de élite disponibles para tu nivel, y tu registro actual. |
| Profesiones | Profesiones y nivel de habilidad. |
| Buscador | Mazmorras, jefes, misiones y objetos, en los dos idiomas. |
| Opciones | Idioma, icono del minimapa, registro de observaciones y restablecer objetivos o ventana. También están en Opciones → AddOns del juego. |

En la cabecera se elige la clase y especialización que se consulta. Por defecto son las de tu personaje, y las listas salen del propio cliente, así que solo aparecen las de Forever.

Datos: mazmorras (incluidas las nuevas de Forever), misiones con requisitos y recompensas, objetos con icono y calidad, zonas, misiones de clase y raros vienen de Forever Companion, que reúne ForeverChanges, Wowhead y Zockify. Se actualizan solos cada 6 horas.

Los mapas de las mazmorras se leen del propio cliente cuando los tiene. Los rangos de nivel y el resto de datos indican su procedencia: vistos en Forever, heredados de Classic, anunciados o verificados por jugadores. Ver cómo se actualiza.

Icono en el minimapa: clic izquierdo abre la guía, clic derecho abre las opciones y se puede arrastrar alrededor del minimapa.

Comandos: /wfg (o /guia) abre la guía; /wfg opciones abre las opciones; /wfg minimapa muestra u oculta el icono; /wfg es|en|auto cambia el idioma; /wfg info muestra versión y estado; /wfg test hace una autoprueba y muestra un informe; /wfg traducir recoge del juego los nombres de objetos y misiones en tu idioma; /wfg errors lista errores; /wfg collect off desactiva las observaciones.
Instalación
• Desde una versión publicada: descarga el .zip de Releases y descomprímelo en World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\. Con WowUp puedes instalarlo desde la URL de este repositorio para recibir las actualizaciones automáticamente.
• Desde el código: copia o enlaza la carpeta ForeverProgressionGuide/ en la misma ruta.

Si el juego lo marca como desactualizado, activa Cargar addons desactualizados en la selección de personaje.
Documentación
| Documento | Contenido |
| --- | --- |
| docs/ACTUALIZACION.md | Cómo se mantienen al día los datos, configuración de GitHub y lista de pruebas en el juego |
| docs/COBERTURA.md | Auditoría de fuentes: qué hay, qué falta y qué se puede redistribuir |
| docs/PLAN.md | Plan técnico maestro |
EstructuraDesarrollo
Requiere Python 3. Las pruebas del addon usan lupa, que ejecuta Lua 5.1, la misma versión que WoW.

Para cambiar datos, edita data-sources/seed/ o añade observaciones, nunca ForeverProgressionGuide/Data/. CI comprueba que los datos generados están al día.

Para publicar a mano una versión, sube una etiqueta: git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0.

Download
| You have | Download | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.4.0-windows.exe | Close WoW, double-click it. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: More info then Run anyway. |
| Linux | ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.4.0-linux.tar.gz | tar xzf ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.4.0-linux.tar.gz && ./ForeverChronicaller-Installer |
| Any (manual) | ForeverChronicaller-0.4.0.zip | Unzip into Interface/AddOns/ |

No Python needed for the installers. They find your WoW: Forever folder (or ask for it) and install the addon. The same program also does Discord/phone notifications and updates: run it with setup, watch or update.

Adds an install-time disclaimer (privacy, permissions, risks). Telemetry is built and tested but switched off by a feature flag: this version collects nothing. It's planned to be switched on with the Grafana dashboard in 0.4.1.
Changed
• Telemetry is behind feature flags that are off (FEATURE_TELEMETRY = False in the companion, FC.FEATURES.diagnostics = false in the addon). There's no opt-in question at install or setup, no telemetry command or --telemetry flag, no in-game diagnostics option or /chron diagnostics, and nothing is timed, collected or sent, even if a config file says "enabled". The disclaimer and PRIVACY.md say "no telemetry in this version" and describe the planned opt-in design separately. The code stays tested with the flags switched on in tests, and new tests check the shipped flag-off behaviour. The release smoke test checks that telemetry is unavailable.
Added
• (Built but switched off, see Changed.) Opt-in anonymous telemetry (OpenTelemetry, OTLP/HTTP JSON; new companion/fc_telemetry.py, standard library only). Off by default.
• The installer and setup ask once, with the default answer No, and remember the answer. --yes never opts in; only answering yes or --telemetry does.
• telemetry status | on | off | show | send. off deletes the random install ID and all locally stored diagnostics.
• Traces: spans for every command and step (install.verify_zip, install.swap, update.check, update.download, watch.*, http.post) with parent/child links, status and scrubbed exception events.
• Metrics: fc.operations, fc.operation.duration (latency histogram), fc.errors (by type, code location and operation).
• Addon errors linked to a version: fc.addon.errors (by addon version, File.lua:line, handler) plus addon.error spans with stack locations.
• In-game latency: fc.addon.handler.duration and .errors histograms per handler.
• Every free-text value is scrubbed (quoted text, paths, URLs, e-mail addresses, long numbers, colour codes), and only code names are accepted as labels. A test fills the saved data with personal data and checks that none of it appears in what would be sent. Payloads were checked against the official OTLP protobuf schema.
• Destination: the OTEL_ENDPOINT / OTEL_HEADERS repository secrets baked into release builds, or the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* environment variables. Without an endpoint, opted-in data stays in a local spool file. Sending never blocks or breaks the program.
• Addon: errors now record the addon version and the handler that failed (local /chron errors log). (Switched off:) opt-in Performance diagnostics (options page or /chron diagnostics on|off, off by default): every event, message and command handler is timed into local latency buckets, which reset when the version changes and are deleted when turned off. The addon itself still sends nothing.
• The release workflow bakes in the telemetry endpoint from secrets (if set), and the smoke test checks that telemetry is off out of the box.
Fixed
• Companion network functions (GitHub, Discord, ntfy) are looked up when called, not when defined, so tests can no longer accidentally reach the internet.
• /chron diagnostics off no longer re-records its own timing after deleting the data.…

There's no opt-in question at install or setup, no telemetry command or --telemetry flag, no in-game diagnostics option or /chron diagnostics, and nothing is timed, collected or sent, even if a config file says "enabled". The disclaimer and PRIVACY.md say "no telemetry in this version" and describe the planned opt-in design separately. The code stays tested with the flags switched on in tests, and new tests check the shipped flag-off behaviour. The release smoke test checks that telemetry is unavailable.
Added
• (Built but switched off, see Changed.) Opt-in anonymous telemetry (OpenTelemetry, OTLP/HTTP JSON; new companion/fc_telemetry.py, standard library only). Off by default.
• The installer and setup ask once, with the default answer No, and remember the answer. --yes never opts in; only answering yes or --telemetry does.
• telemetry status | on | off | show | send. off deletes the random install ID and all locally stored diagnostics.
• Traces: spans for every command and step (install.verify_zip, install.swap, update.check, update.download, watch.*, http.post) with parent/child links, status and scrubbed exception events.
• Metrics: fc.operations, fc.operation.duration (latency histogram), fc.errors (by type, code location and operation).
• Addon errors linked to a version: fc.addon.errors (by addon version, File.lua:line, handler) plus addon.error spans with stack locations.
• In-game latency: fc.addon.handler.duration and .errors histograms per handler.
• Every free-text value is scrubbed (quoted text, paths, URLs, e-mail addresses, long numbers, colour codes), and only code names are accepted as labels. A test fills the saved data with personal data and checks that none of it appears in what would be sent. Payloads were checked against the official OTLP protobuf schema.
• Destination: the OTEL_ENDPOINT / OTEL_HEADERS repository secrets baked into release builds, or the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* environment variables. Without an endpoint, opted-in data stays in a local spool file. Sending never blocks or breaks the program.
• Addon: errors now record the addon version and the handler that failed (local /chron errors log). (Switched off:) opt-in Performance diagnostics (options page or /chron diagnostics on|off, off by default): every event, message and command handler is timed into local latency buckets, which reset when the version changes and are deleted when turned off. The addon itself still sends nothing.
• The release workflow bakes in the telemetry endpoint from secrets (if set), and the smoke test checks that telemetry is off out of the box.
Fixed
• Companion network functions (GitHub, Discord, ntfy) are looked up when called, not when defined, so tests can no longer accidentally reach the internet.
• /chron diagnostics off no longer re-records its own timing after deleting the data.…

Download
| You have | Download | Then |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.3.1-windows.exe | Close WoW, double-click it. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher: More info then Run anyway. |
| Linux | ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.3.1-linux.tar.gz | tar xzf ForeverChronicaller-Installer-0.3.1-linux.tar.gz && ./ForeverChronicaller-Installer |
| Any (manual) | ForeverChronicaller-0.3.1.zip | Unzip into Interface/AddOns/ |

No Python needed for the installers. They find your WoW: Forever folder (or ask for it) and install the addon. The same program also does Discord/phone notifications and updates: run it with setup, watch or update.

First release published automatically, with standalone installers for Windows and Linux (no Python needed).
Added
• The companion can be built as a standalone program (no Python needed):
• It finds the addon zip embedded inside itself.
• Run with no arguments (double-clicked), it starts the installer, shows any error instead of just closing, and waits for Enter at the end.
• Messages show the program's real name instead of python fcompanion.py.
• The companion updates from SaffronG/ForeverChronicaller by default.
• Tests for standalone mode, plus a check that the companion's VERSION matches the .toc version.
• Automatic releases (.github/workflows/release.yml): pushing a new .toc version to main runs all checks, then builds standalone installers on real Windows and Linux machines with PyInstaller (Python bundled in, so players don't need it). Each one is smoke-tested by installing into a fake WoW folder, both normally and in double-click mode. Then GitHub release v is published with the Windows .exe, the Linux .tar.gz, the addon zip, the Python installer bundle, and download instructions plus the changelog as notes. The Linux binary is built on Ubuntu 24.04 so it also runs on older distros.
Changed
• CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs on pushes to main and on pull requests, and the release workflow can reuse it. Companion tests now run on Linux and Windows with the current Python 3. The old 3.8 setting failed because ubuntu-latest (Ubuntu 26.04) no longer has Python 3.8.
• Releases no longer need a hand-pushed tag. The release workflow creates the tag.

to each specialization of the profession, the one you pick remembered: Weaponsmith (and a weapon mastery after it)
or Armorsmith, Gnomish or Goblin Engineer, Dragonscale, Elemental or Tribal Leatherworking. Each step has its quest
givers on the map, says when a quest is in your log or done, and counts what it asks for against your bags and bank
("2 / 4 Moonsteel Broadsword"). The recipes it takes say whether you know them and where to learn the rest; what's
still missing is made or bought, whichever costs less, with its ingredients and the total still to spend.

more disenchanted than sold, the best first, in red when making it costs more than disenchanting brings; grey when

addons.description:
Craft Ladder is a smart profession leveling and crafting optimization addon for World of Warcraft: Forever. It helps you find cost-efficient routes from skill 1 to 300 using auction house prices, vendor costs, and materials already in your bags.

Whether you're leveling Engineering, Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Tailoring, Cooking, or gathering professions, Craft Ladder creates a step-by-step plan showing what to craft, how many items you need, where to learn each recipe, and how much it will cost. It also helps you discover profitable crafting opportunities and gathering zones.

Download Craft Ladder on CurseForge
Professions
• Crafting: Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Leatherworking, Tailoring, Cooking, First Aid, Poisons
• Gathering: Mining, Herbalism, Skinning, Fishing, Lockpicking
Modes
• Vendor sales (gathering: Skill): level up for the least gold you're sure to spend. What you make is counted
as sold to vendors only: no auctions to post or wait for (gathering: the fastest points).
• AH sales: level up counting what the auction house pays for what you make too: cheaper than Vendor sales if it
sells (gathering: where an hour earns the most on the way).
• Profit: no ladder, just what you can make now that earns the most per craft (for gathering: the zones where an
hour earns the most at your skill).
• Food (Cooking): the dishes worth eating for your class, grouped by role, by what their Well Fed raises, each in
its skill-up colour.
What each step tells you
• The recipe, the skill range and about how many crafts it takes, coloured as the game colours it.
• Where to learn it: trainer, vendor, quest, auction house or a recipe already in your bags, with the NPC and its
place.
• Every reagent: bought at a vendor, at the auction house, or made by you, and what the whole step costs (red, with a
minus) or earns back (green, with a plus).
• What you already have counts: bags and, with Bagnon, the bank. A step you can make from your bags goes first, and
each step says how many of its crafts what you have covers ("12 ready"; vendor reagents aside).
• The recipes you know are read from your profession window; a recipe you just learned counts at once.

For gathering: the zones to level in, the nodes, herbs, creatures or fishing pools that still give a point, and the
gold an hour each zone earns.
Also
• Auction house tab: the ladder as a shopping list, a row per step with its reagents. With Auctionator, its
Search button opens Auctionator's Shopping tab with exactly what to buy.
• Merchant's Favor recipes: the supply camps' quartermaster recipes, with their favor prices and what one craft
takes (your bars and ore counted first), and a Favor mode in the auction house tab to buy it. They can join the
ladder too.
• Camp: what each camp feature gives around a campfire at your level, in the order your role wants them, and how
to get it.
• Specialization (Blacksmithing, Engineering, Leatherworking): the steps to each specialization, with the quest
givers on the map, the quests done or in your log, what they ask for against your bags and bank, the recipes you
know or still need, and what's left to make or buy.
• The range to level: From and To over the ladder (or a rank's name under the skill bar), Reset for your skill
to 300.
• A minimap button and the addon compartment; the window remembers its size, scale and place.
Screenshots
Profit: what earns the most per craft now.

Mining in AH sales: the zones to level in, the nodes there and what they're worth.

The auction house tab, and what its Search button opens in Auctionator.

Camp: the camp features in the order your role wants them.

Cooking's Food mode: the dishes worth eating for your class.

addons.description:
Hearthtale keeps a journal for your World of Warcraft character as you play.
Quests, close calls, new places and the people you travel with become entries
written in your character's voice. Each race has its own way of telling the
story. On Hardcore, a death closes the journal with an epitaph and saves it
in the Hall of the Fallen.

You can read the books in game or on hearthtale.app.
The optional Ravenpost companion
uploads them after you log out or reload.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of Warcraft:
Forever. One download covers both games.
In game
Type /hearthtale or /ht, or click the minimap button to open the journal.
Each login says in chat whether you're resuming an entry or starting a new
one.
Choose an entry from the list to read it. The second tab holds the Hall of
the Fallen, which you can also open with /ht hall. The third holds your
fellow travellers: the players you have grouped with, when and where you met,
the days you spent together, and a note of your own on each. They stay on your
computer, never in the book or on the site.

An entry follows the time between rests. Logging out at an inn, in a city
or by a campfire closes it. Logging out in the wild records a night outdoors
and keeps it going. After four hours of play, the next logout closes the entry
wherever you are. A character you already play starts with a prologue, then
builds a journal from that point on.

Use an entry's Edit button to give it your own title or add a note. You
can also use /ht title [N] TEXT and /ht note [N] TEXT. Leave out N to
change the latest entry. Your words are kept separately from the journal's
text.

A finished entry keeps its words, even after an update improves the
writing. /ht rewrite writes the whole journal again with the current
version, after asking. Your titles and notes stay.
Read on hearthtale.app
Install Ravenpost and click Sign in with Battle.net in its window. For
Forever characters, or any character Battle.net cannot find, get
a code from Link a character on the site and enter /ht link CODE in
game. Your book arrives after your next logout or /reload.

The website is optional, and books are private unless you choose to share
them. Your notes stay out of a shared book and the Hall. Setup instructions
are at hearthtale.app/start.

The interface is available in English and French.

The journal is written in English, on any game client. On other clients the
game's names in it (places, creatures, people, quests, items, trades, spells)
are kept in English too. In Forever dungeons, the journal can
only tell kills that a quest also counts.
Settings
The welcome page appears once per character. Open it again with
/ht welcome. Settings are under Options > AddOns > Hearthtale, through
/ht settings or by right-clicking the minimap button.

Choose the alert when a book closes and the minimap button's visibility and
position (chat lines always show). You can mark a character as Hardcore when
the game cannot identify it. Settings are saved per character and can be
transferred with /ht export and /ht import CODE. Use /ht minimap to
show or hide the button.

Hearthtale shares its book style with its author's other addons, listed on
its store page. Each addon works independently.

The full store description is in addon/CURSEFORGE.md.
PLAN.md records the design decisions, and CLAUDE.md
describes how the journal is written and the rules its sentences follow.

addons.description:
Keyring gathers your addons' minimap buttons into a drawer, leaving one key on
the minimap. Click the key to open the drawer, and close it with Escape,
another click on the key or a click elsewhere.

One download covers Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. Keyring speaks English and French. Other
clients get English.
Using Keyring
• Left-click the key to open or close the drawer.
• Right-click the key for the settings.
• Drag the key to move it around the minimap.
• Untick a button in the settings to leave it on the minimap instead.

The drawer arranges buttons in a grid and follows your minimap's scale. The
drawer stays open while you use a menu opened from one of its buttons.

Keyring finds buttons made with LibDBIcon, which most addons use, and other
addons' buttons on the minimap that it recognises by name. The game's own
buttons stay where they are: tracking, mail, the clock, the zoom buttons and
Forever's addon compartment. So do map pins and anything over twice the size
of a minimap button. Buttons hidden by their own addon stay hidden. Protected
buttons are left in place because the game restricts moving or hiding them
during combat.

The key uses the game's minimap ring and highlight, with a painted keyring
icon. Keyring works as soon as you install it.
Commands
• /keyring opens or closes the drawer.
• /keyring settings opens the settings.
• /keyring list shows in chat the buttons in the drawer and those left on the
minimap.
• /keyring reset puts the key back in its place.

addons.description:
Lorekeeper's Codex adds a book of Azeroth's lore that fills in as you explore.
Visit Kharanos, speak with King Magni, defeat a Frostmane troll or finish a
quest, and you might discover a page about the history behind it. Each page
is an original text written as a note from Archesonus, Royal Historian of
Ironforge. A Horde character's copy comes from Parqual Fintallas, a historian
of the Undercity, who adds notes of his own in the margins.

The Codex has 441 pages in 44 chapters, or **456 pages in 46 chapters on
Forever**. It covers the original world's zones, landmarks, figures, peoples,
classes and history. Each race gets its own foreword.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. One download covers all of them. See
FOREVER.md for Forever support.
In game
Type /codex or click the minimap button to read. Browse by chapter, search
your discovered pages or filter by type. Related pages link to each other.
Each character keeps a separate codex, with the date, level and location of
every discovery. Undiscovered pages stay hidden.

Pages unlock by exploring, meeting people, defeating creatures, finishing
quests, gaining reputation and reading books or inscriptions. A chat link,
an alert and a sound announce each discovery. Tooltips point out creatures
and players who can unlock a page.

The lore covers the world's past up to the original game, using Warcraft I
to III, WoW's quests and books, and the novels and histories about that
period. Later expansion events and answers to mysteries left open in the
original game are kept out. The Codex reads in English and
French. Other clients get English,
with the places and the Library's titles in their own language. Most unlocks
use game ids, and reading-based unlocks
recognise titles in every client language. Where you found a page is kept by
the game's ids, so it follows your client's language, even after you switch.

On Forever, kill-based unlocks work in the open world. Creatures inside
dungeons and raids are hidden from addons, so kills there cannot unlock pages.
Some pages, paragraphs and unlocks differ between Classic and Forever.
Library and achievements
The Library saves the books, notes, quest letters and plaques you read
in the world. Texts are copied in full, with where and when you found them,
so you can return to a quest letter after handing it in. Letters written by
players are never copied. The top of the shelves brings back the Library at a
glance: what each shelf holds and the texts copied lately.

The Achievements tab tracks page milestones, completed chapters, Library
progress, notable encounters and feats. Each achievement records the day
and level you earned it. Open the tab with /codex achievements.
Settings and commands
The welcome page appears once per character. Use /codex welcome to see it
again. Settings are under Options > AddOns > Lorekeeper's Codex, through
/codex settings or by right-clicking the minimap button.

Choose the alerts for new pages and for achievements, their duration,
sounds, tooltip hints and the minimap button (chat lines always show). Each character has its own settings. Copy another
character's settings in the same game, or transfer them with /codex export
and /codex import CODE.
• /codex minimap shows or hides the minimap button. Drag it to move it.
• /codex banner toggles page alerts.
• /codex reset clears this character's codex after confirmation.
• /codex where prints your position and target for writing new pages.
• /codex scan on records areas, creatures, quest texts and books to help
write Forever content. scripts/scan-export.lua converts the saved data
to JSON.

Known Library texts also follow your client's language (English and French
for now). Original game wording is used where available, with documented
translations for missing bodies. Unrecognised copies stay as recorded.

The full store description is in addon/CURSEFORGE.md.…

addons.description:
Quests and conversations with NPCs in a panel beside them, read and answered
from the keyboard, in the look of its sibling addons.

One download for Classic Era and World of Warcraft: Forever.
Using it
Talk to an NPC: their words, their quests and their options open in a
panel in the look of its siblings, the NPC's face in its corner and the NPC
still in view.
• Space (or Enter) answers yes: Accept, Continue, Complete Quest.
• Escape says goodbye, with the keys on or off.
• 1 to 9 pick a line, or the reward to take when a quest offers a choice.

A key acts when you let it go, and only on the page you pressed it on: a
held Space never accepts the next quest. On a page longer than the panel,
Space or Enter first scrolls down, so you never accept a quest with its
rewards unseen. In combat, while typing or with a modifier held, the keys stay
the game's. Drag the panel to move it.

A quest's offer shows what the game's own window keeps quiet: its level in
the colour of how hard it is for you, whether it's elite, a dungeon, a raid
or PvP, where it sits in its chain, like part 2 of 7, and the group size the
game suggests.

Books, letters and plaques open in the same panel. Space turns the page,
Backspace turns back.

While you talk or read, the game's interface fades away, so only the panel and
the one you speak to stay on screen. It comes back for a fight, a vendor, a
trainer or a question from the game. Keep it on screen with /palaver hud or
the game's Options.

your client's language. Palaver's few words of its own are in English and French.
Thanks
