addons.description:
Second Wind gives you a debrief after a close call or death in World of
Warcraft. Once the fight is over, it shows the hits that hurt most, how
your health fell, and which potions or abilities were ready but went unused.
After a few debriefs, you can compare what your dangerous fights have in
common.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever, in English and French. Nothing pops up
during combat. Duels and battlegrounds are excluded.

Get it from CurseForge,
Wago or
GitHub releases.
One download covers all of them.
In game
Type /secondwind or /wind, or click the minimap button to open the book.
By default, surviving below 15% health counts as a close call. The threshold
can also be set to 10%, 20% or 25%.

The Debriefs tab shows individual fights, with a health graph, foes,
large hits, healing, stuns and fears, and the tools you used or left ready.
Patterns compares close calls after your third debrief. Lifelines
shows the emergency supplies you carry now and their cooldowns.

Debriefs are saved across your account, separately for each game. A fallen
Hardcore character's last fight remains available from your next character.
An optional word before a pull gives, in chat, the counts of your close calls
against foes like the one you target.

Forever limits the health and combat information addons can read. Second
Wind reconstructs health estimates from damage, healing and the game's
low-health warning or death recap. That warning must stay on
(Options > Combat). The debrief shows when a health value is an estimate.

Second Wind reads in English and French. Other clients get English, with the game's own names for your foes, spells,
items and places in their language. Debriefs keep them by the game's ids, so
they follow your client's language, even after you switch.
• /wind copy opens a text version of the debrief for you to copy.
• /wind lifelines opens the Lifelines tab.
• /wind probe reports what the game let the addon read after your next fight.
• /wind settings opens settings for thresholds, alerts and the word before a pull.
• /wind welcome reopens the welcome page.
• /wind minimap shows or hides the minimap button.
• /wind export and /wind import CODE transfer settings.
• /wind reset clears this character's debriefs after confirmation.

Second Wind shares its book style with the other addons of the family. Each
works independently, and Keyring can gather their minimap buttons behind one button.

The full store description is in addon/CURSEFORGE.md.

addons.description:
Yonder gives you riddles to solve, rare creatures to hunt
and a record of what you find along the way. Follow a clue to a forgotten
grave, track down a rare you've never fought, or fill in your bestiary while
levelling. Notes from an Explorers' League naturalist accompany your finds.

For Classic Era, Hardcore, Season of Discovery and World of
Warcraft: Forever. One download covers all of them.

Yonder was called Explorer's Field Journal until version 0.8.0: another
addon used the same folder. A character's old journal moves over on its own
at its first login with Yonder, through the small FieldJournal folder in the
download (on Classic Era, removed in a later update).
What's in the journal
• Expeditions. 162 riddles and 38 rare hunts across the original world.
Forever adds four riddles and a hunt on Zephras Isle. Riddles lead to
overlooked places and are solved by reaching a spot, speaking to someone,
reading something or working out a gesture from the verse. They never
require a kill.
• Bestiary. Around 3,500 creatures in 96 families, each with a
naturalist's note. Creature pages keep your first sighting, observed levels,
kill counts, loot and drop rates. Rares and bosses become trophies.
• Finds. Fish, plants, ores and gems, cloth and leather in one tab,
with a naturalist's note for every item. Gathering professions open their
collections, while cloth is available to everyone. Once opened, a collection
stays with you even if you change professions.
• Atlas. The zones you've visited, with maps, explored places, surveyor's
notes, flights, deaths and close calls.
• Achievements. For exploring, completing expeditions, collecting
trophies, fishing and gathering.

Each riddle has two optional hints: a clearer clue, then a location marked
on the world map. Solve it without hints for a gold seal and an extra piece
of the story. Rare hunts have posters describing the creature and its
haunts. Track a hunt to mark those haunts on your map, or complete it without
tracking for a gold seal. You can pin a riddle or a poster to your screen.

Creatures join the Bestiary when you first kill them. Kills by you, your pet
or your group count, including damage over time and area spells. A tagged
creature finished by another player also counts when your quest credits
the kill. A chat link announces each new creature, without a banner or sound.
Rares and bosses have a trophy sound.

Search by family or creature name, sort your records and browse trophies.
Tooltips show whether you've recorded a creature and how many you've killed.
Each character has its own journal. Undiscovered creatures stay hidden,
with no count showing how many remain.

Forever hides creatures inside dungeons and raids from addons, so the
journal cannot record them there.

Yonder reads in English and French. Other clients get English, with the game's own names in their
language: creatures, places, flight points, fish, and the riddles' and
quarries' answers. The journal keeps everything
by the game's ids, so what you recorded follows your client's language, even
after you switch.
Opening the journal
Type /yonder or click the minimap button. The journal opens on Expeditions.
Each login says in chat what the journal holds.
Settings are under Options > AddOns > Yonder, or /yonder settings.
• /yonder welcome reopens the welcome page.
• /yonder where shows your current map and position.
• /yonder minimap shows or hides the minimap button.
• /yonder export and /yonder import CODE transfer settings.
• /yonder reset clears this character's journal after confirmation.

addons.description:
Waypoint Tracker: the 3D waypoint arrow and quest finder for WoW Forever

Set a waypoint. Follow the arrow. That's it.

Screenshots ·
Treasure hunt ·
Install ·
Set a waypoint ·
Colours ·
Settings ·
Commands ·
FAQ

Waypoint Tracker is a free, open-source addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (WoW Forever, the new classic-style World of Warcraft, sometimes called Classic+). A 3D arrow over your character points to your waypoint, shows the distance and time to arrive, turns from gold to green as you get close, and clears itself when you arrive. Set waypoints from coordinates (/way 42 65), the world map, or by name: the built-in Find tab searches quests, NPCs, enemies, objects and items, including WoW Forever's new content. Share any spot in chat as a clickable map pin.

It's a TomTom-style arrow and a quest and NPC finder in one addon, with nothing to configure.

Open /wp or left-click the minimap button for one window with Waypoints, Find and Routes tabs. Editors, imports and help stay inside the tabs; Back returns to the previous page. Feedback appears below the title, above the tab content. Right-click the minimap button for the quick menu; Shift + left-click adds a waypoint where you stand. The Addon Compartment also opens the window or quick menu.

| | |
|---|---|
| Game | World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.1, interface 16001) |
| Price | Free, MIT licence, no ads |
| Get it | CurseForge, Wago or GitHub Releases |
| Website | sanjaygbhat.github.io/wowforever-waypoint-tracker |
| Commands | /wp (window), /way (coordinates or a name), /wp find, /wp treasure, /wp share |
| Works with | Quest guides, rare and treasure trackers, and anything with a "Send to TomTom" button |
| Languages | English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese |

📜 Quest: Find Your Way
> Quest giver: every adventurer who has ever run in circles looking for a quest mob
>
> "You there! You've got coordinates from a guide, a guildmate or a map, and no idea which way to run. Take this arrow. It points where you need to go and turns green when you're close. Nothing else to learn."

Objectives
• [ ] Set a waypoint: open the window with /wp, or just type /way 42 65
• [ ] Follow the arrow until it turns green
• [ ] Arrive. The waypoint clears itself and the arrow moves on to the next one.

Rewards

✨ Why players like it
• Set a waypoint your way: a small window, /way, a quest or place name, the Find tab, or Ctrl + Right-click on the map.
• An arrow that tells you how close you are: gold far away, green as you get there. It never catches mouse clicks, so right-click to attack always works.
• One window: Waypoints, Find and Routes tabs, with settings in Blizzard Settings and placement in Edit Mode.
• Typing is forgiving: pick zones from a list that filters as you type. Typos, accents and capital letters don't matter, and pasted coordinates like 45.2 67.8 or 45,2 67,8 work in the Add box.
• Find built in: quests, NPCs, enemies, objects, items and places, including WoW Forever's new content, plus a Nearest menu for services.
• Share in one click: send any spot, or where you are, to chat with a clickable map pin, without setting a waypoint first.
• Treasure hunt (beta): a ping when a chest or rare appears near you, and the arrow points at it.
• Works with your other addons: quest guides and anything with a "Send to TomTom" button put their waypoints on this arrow.
• Built for WoW Forever: interface 16001, the game's Edit Mode, and nine languages.

📸 Screenshots
The arrow on the way to a waypoint in the Barrens, with its name, distance and time to arrive.

See the map screenshot and capture notes for more in-game views.

addons.description:
Track how much gold you're making from pickpocketing. Logs every coin looted, item grabbed, and Coin of Air earned — totals it up per session and keeps lifetime stats across all your rogues.

Built for Retail (The War Within, 12.0.x). Rogue only — if you log in on a non-rogue, the addon stays out of your way. You can still check your combined haul with /pp account from any character.
What it does
Pickpocket a mob and the addon catches the gold and any items that drop. Gold shows up immediately in the haul window. Items show as "pending" until you vendor them — at that point the sale price gets added to your total.

The haul window is a small bar you can drag anywhere and resize. The text auto-scales to fit the window width. Hover it for a tooltip breakdown of gold looted, items sold, and pending vendor value. A green * appears when you've got unsold pickpocketed items sitting in your bags.

The addon distinguishes between fence items (items with a vendor sell price) and unsellable loot (quest items, etc). Both are tracked for display and stats, but only fence items count toward your pending vendor value and are eligible for auto-sell.
Auto-sell
When enabled, opening a vendor automatically sells your tracked pickpocket fence items one at a time. The queue/ticker approach avoids conflicts with other auto-sell addons and only sells items the addon is actually tracking — it won't touch non-pickpocketed items even if they share the same item ID. If a stack in your bags is larger than the tracked pickpocket quantity, it's skipped to avoid overselling.
Coins of Air
Enable Coins of Air tracking in the Display settings and a second small window appears with your session count. Hover it for session total, currently held, and lifetime stats. Both windows share the same capabilities: drag, resize, lock, icon toggle.
Bar graphs
The options panel has two bar graphs comparing your rogues against each other:
• Character Earnings — horizontal bars in rogue-yellow showing total gold + item sales per character. Hover for total, pickpocket count, and average per pick.
• Coins of Air — horizontal bars in monk-green showing lifetime coins earned per character.

Both graphs have independent "Max Characters to Display" sliders (1–10). Characters beyond the limit are grouped into an "Other Characters" bar. Toggle both graphs on or off with the "Show Character Graphs" checkbox.
Blizzard integration
The addon registers in two places in the Blizzard UI:
• Addon Compartment — the minimap addon list (11.0+). Shows the addon with a coin icon for quick access without a standalone minimap button.
• Settings panel — Game Menu → Options → AddOns → Pick Pocket Tracker. Has a button that opens the main options window.

addons.description:
IsThisNew? is a tiny World of Warcraft: Forever addon that answers the question the alternate timeline asks on every loot drop and every mouseover — "is this new, changed, or am I misremembering Classic?" It adds one line to item and NPC tooltips — Forever Exclusive or Changed in Forever — for the things its sourced database knows about, with a short note on what changed or where it comes from. Anything it doesn't know about stays untagged, because untagged means unknown — this addon never guesses that something is Classic. It ships with 35 records transcribed from cited Forever guides (the same sources behind the SecretGPS catalog), a /itin lookup command that answers from chat with the same honesty, and a /itin dump collector that prints real item/NPC IDs in game so the database can graduate from name-matching to verified ID-matching after launch.

See also: FEATURES.md (full feature list), DESCRIPTION.md (store-listing copy), CHANGELOG.md (version history), docs/SPEC.md (build spec), docs/VERIFICATION.md (what has and hasn't been proven).
What it does
• Item tooltips — a provenance line for seeded items: the Cozy Sleeping Bag, the Library Books reward tiers (Truthseeker's Bow, Scholarly Pendant, …), Rockslicer, Coldflame Saber, Wolf's Bane, the Partners in Crime rings, Malignant Root, the Tome of Dalaran chain items, and more.
• NPC tooltips — the same for seeded NPCs: Lyn the Ignored, the Stormwind and Undercity librarians, Brother Zendraas, the Ruins of Lordaeron secret bosses — and Archmage Ataeric, tagged Changed in Forever for his new role in the Tome of Dalaran chain.
• A note, not just a label — each tag carries a one-line note (what it is, where it comes from), and an optional source line names the guide behind the record, so any tag can be audited.
• /itin lookup — asks the database from chat. A miss answers honestly: "no record — unknown, which is not proof it is Classic."
• /itin dump — the collector: prints the mouseover/target NPC IDs and the last item tooltip's ID, the raw material for the verified-ID database in v0.2.
Commands
• /itin or /isthisnew — help
• /itin on / /itin off — tagging on/off
• /itin note — toggle the note line
• /itin source — toggle the source line
• /itin lookup — ask the database
• /itin dump — print item/NPC IDs for data collection
• /itin stats — database size
• /itin debug — version, client build, hook mode

Asset SHA-256: d1ce6d539c7d90903b15e1aceaa6cec81d77de10797c748f309665b97f85857c (12,035 bytes)
addons.description:
LFG Lens is a tiny World of Warcraft: Forever addon that untangles dungeon chat. Forever has no dungeon finder, so groups form in public channels, in acronyms, at scroll speed — and Forever's nine new dungeons collide head-on with twenty-year-old abbreviations: ST is now both the Sunken Temple and Shaper's Terrace, BD is both Blackrock Depths and the new Barrow Deeps raid, DM still means two dungeons at once. LFG Lens turns every dungeon acronym in channel chat into a clickable link: hover it for the full name, level range, entrance and an explicit "this can also mean…" warning; click it to pin that post into the small Lens window, where dungeon posts are collected with age stamps instead of scrolling away. A /lfglens alias command lets you repoint any acronym the moment your server's slang settles — your word wins over the shipped dictionary, which marks every new-dungeon acronym as what it honestly is: a proposal, not settled slang.

See also: FEATURES.md, DESCRIPTION.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/VERIFICATION.md.
What it does
• Chat links — acronyms in public channels (General, Trade, LFG…) become links. Forever-new dungeons are sky blue, classic dungeons grey, ambiguous acronyms amber. Hover: full name, kind, level range (or an honest "not yet published"), entrance hint, notes, and both meanings when there are two.
• The Lens window (/lfglens) — the last 20 dungeon posts with age stamps; unpinned posts fade after 2 minutes. Filter: All / New in Forever / Classic / My level. Click a post to open a whisper to its author. Click an acronym in chat to pin/unpin its post and focus its meaning at the top of the window.
• A dictionary you can overrule — /lfglens list prints all 33 entries (9 new dungeons, 3 raids, 21 classic). /lfglens alias ST = Shaper's Terrace repoints an acronym everywhere, stored between sessions; /lfglens unalias ST restores the built-in meaning.
Commands
• /lfglens or /lens — toggle the Lens window
• /lfglens list [new|classic|raids] — print the dictionary
• /lfglens alias = / /lfglens unalias
• /lfglens clear — empty the feed · /lfglens on|off — annotation
• /lfglens debug — version, dictionary size, hook status

First build of MulePost for WoW: Forever (Interface 16001).

Category routing rules (cloth to your tailor, herbs to your alchemist, junk to your bank alt) turn a bag scan into a mail plan — reviewed by you, per mail, before anything sends. The send pass is event-driven and stops at the first failure. Gold can never be attached: no code path exists that could do it, and the build gate greps the source to prove it. Quest items are never routed.

Install: unzip into your Forever client's Interface/AddOns folder.
Status: gate-verified locally (parse + classifier audit + money audit + harness). Runtime at a live mailbox is Unverified — Forever launches Nov 4, 2026. First live test: use a throwaway alt and low-value items.

Asset SHA-256: 5520ca36208a2c1897fba14526328bacd8d11173d4777a67a7d1b119f3041033 (9,426 bytes)
addons.description:
MulePost is a World of Warcraft: Forever mailbox addon for anyone with crafting alts and a bank alt. You teach it your routing once — cloth → your tailor, herbs → your alchemist, ore → your miner, greys → your bank alt — and from then on, a mailbox visit is: open the mail, click Route my bags, read the plan, click Send. The plan groups your bags into mails of up to 12 stacks per recipient with an estimated postage total and a guard that warns when a plan's postage exceeds a cap you set. Nothing ever sends without the review screen and your Send press — there is no auto-send mode and there never will be. And the gold promise is structural, not a setting: the addon contains no code path that can attach money or set a COD (the build gate greps the source to prove it), quest items are never routed, and items whose data the client hasn't cached yet are skipped and counted out loud instead of guessed at.

See also: FEATURES.md, DESCRIPTION.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/VERIFICATION.md.
Setup (once)
Up to 8 rules; first match wins, and the other rule catches whatever no specific rule claims. Categories: cloth, herb, ore (the client's "Metal & Stone"), leather, enchanting, consumable, junk (grey items), other.
Commands
/mp review window · /mp route scan + plan · /mp rules · /mp rule add · /mp rule del · /mp cap / /mp cap off postage guard · /mp debug

First build of Party Quest Roll Call for WoW: Forever (Interface 16001).

One click asks your party who has, has done, or still needs each quest in a set — answers arrive over the addon channel into a matrix window. Privacy by construction: clients answer only the quest titles a request names. Seed set: the Cozy Sleeping Bag chain (names only — no source publishes Forever quest IDs, and none are invented here). Tracked quests capture real IDs from your own log; learn mode harvests IDs for future dungeon sets.

Install: unzip into your Forever client's Interface/AddOns folder. Party members need the addon to answer.
Status: gate-verified locally (parse + seed audit + protocol harness). Runtime in a live two-client party is Unverified — Forever launches Nov 4, 2026.

Asset SHA-256: 3852dfbe712d6b5753d4471be84f4efcd2d25452382d27856afa141d4af78ea0 (9,618 bytes)
addons.description:
Party Quest Roll Call is a World of Warcraft: Forever addon that replaces the pre-dungeon typing ritual — "have you got the tome quest? …you? …hello?" — with one click. Pick a quest set, hit Ask party, and every party member running the addon answers automatically over the addon channel: Has (in their log), Done (the game says completed), Need (not done, not held), or ? (unknown — no addon, or a quest whose state honestly can't be checked yet). Answers land in a small matrix window, quests down the side, party members across the top. The privacy rule is built into the protocol, not promised in a tooltip: a client only ever reports the quests a request explicitly named — nothing else in its log exists as far as the addon is concerned. Because Forever's dungeon quest data isn't published yet, v0.1 ships the full engine with one sourced quest set, a tracked-quests set you build from your own log, and a learn mode that harvests real quest IDs in game so proper dungeon sets can land as data updates.

See also: FEATURES.md, DESCRIPTION.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/SPEC.md, docs/VERIFICATION.md.
The honest part (read this first)
• The seed set is the Cozy Sleeping Bag chain — six quest names transcribed from the guide behind the SecretGPS Forever catalog. No quest IDs ship in the data, because no source publishes them and the beta's level cap left dungeon quests largely untestable.
• A name-only quest in your log answers Has (matched by title). A name-only quest not in your log answers ? — never "Need" — because without an ID the game can't be asked whether you finished it months ago.
• Every answer teaches the addon: responses carry the quest IDs the responder knows, so your client learns them, and /qrc learn prints the harvest. Dungeon quest sets with real IDs are the v0.2 data update, built from live-client harvests after the November 4 launch — the same bootstrap the sister addons (IsThisNew?, LFG Lens) use.
• Your own tracked quests work fully today: /qrc track adds a quest from your log with its real ID captured at that moment, so tracked sets answer Has/Done/Need properly.
Commands
• /qrc or /rollcall — toggle the matrix · /qrc ask — ask the party
• /qrc set [id] — show or choose the quest set
• /qrc track / /qrc untrack — your tracked set
• /qrc learn — harvest quest IDs from your log · /qrc debug

A World of Warcraft: Forever addon for friends who don't always play at the same time. It shows everyone's characters, levels and whereabouts, and tells you what your friends did while you were away. No server, no account, and no shared guild needed.
What it does
While you were away. On login, every ding, death and new character your friends had since you last played.

Your whole crew. Every friend's characters, levels and whereabouts, and when each was last seen.

Cheer every ding. One click sends a cheer for a ding, respects for a death, or a welcome for someone new.

Level up together. Goals the whole crew works towards, and trophies for what you do together, like clearing a dungeon. Nobody is ranked.

Pass on spare gear. Offer an item to your friends. Whoever claims it first gets it by in-game mail.

When everyone plays. A heatmap of the hours each friend usually plays, in your own time zone.

Who crafts what. Every friend's professions and skill in one grid, so you know who to ask for a craft.

Dungeons together. See which friends are close to your level, and the dungeons you can run together.

Start a crew
1. Everyone in the group installs BFF.
2. One friend types /bff start and shares the crew code.
3. The others type /bff join .

addons.changelog:
Simple Loot Council is out of beta. This is the first full release.

New
• Your Loot Master promotion is now remembered after you leave the raid. When you lead a raid with Simple Loot Council active and the player you last promoted is in it, a prompt asks whether to promote them again or clear the promotion. You stay the Loot Master until you answer, and whenever that player isn't in the raid.
• The Loot Master card in the options window now has an "(name) auto-promotion" line naming the player you last promoted, while that promotion isn't in force. The line shows the name without the realm. If it's cut off, hover it to see it in full.

Changed
• Handing loot to another player is now called a promotion instead of a delegation, in every language. This covers the /slc lootmaster help line, the Loot Master card, the queue window, the promote prompt and the "Drop prior Loot Master promotion when passed lead" setting. The setting keeps your choice.
• The prompt a raider gets when the Loot Master turns on Simple Loot Council now reads "Join (Loot Master)'s Loot Council?" and gives a plainer explanation. Its buttons are "Roll Normally" and "Join & Auto-Pass", and an "Always join automatically" checkbox replaces "Don't ask again". The guild guard prompt uses the same buttons.
• On the Loot Master card, the Loot Master's name and the player in the auto-promotion line are shown in their class colours, even when that player isn't in your group.
• /slc activetest (/slc at) now stays on after a /reload or relog, as /slc on does. It stays on until you turn it off or your group changes between solo, party and raid.

Fixed
• The "Use Simple Loot Council for this raid?" question no longer closes by itself as soon as it opens when raid lead is passed back to you. The same fix covers any window that another window replaces in the same moment.
• The promote prompt no longer closes as soon as it opens when you turn Simple Loot Council on from the "Use Simple Loot Council for this raid?" question.
• The "Use Simple Loot Council for this raid?" question now closes when you leave the group or the raid is converted to a party, and is only asked in a raid.
• Several texts are now translated in every language: the "Join the Loot Council?" question with its buttons and checkbox, the note that the loot response tab is now off by default, and the "council window did not open" warning. Item levels on council rows now use the game's own wording.
• The /slc help line for /slc log history now shows the actual words you type in Spanish and Korean, not a translation of them.
• Hovering a council member who was added by name no longer shows a stray colon after their name.
• Closing the settings window no longer hides a tooltip that another window is showing.
• The README included with the addon has been updated to match this release. It now covers the four-hour trade window, the guild loot funnel guard (on by default), history import (CSV only), Loot Master promotion and the full command list.
addons.description:
SimpleLootCouncil is a loot council for Retail and Forever raids. Where there is no Master Looter, the council votes on items sitting in a raider's bags inside the four-hour trade window. Raiders answer, the council votes, the Loot Master awards, and the holder's trade window fills itself.

Built for Retail Loot and WoW Forever
Votes happen on items still inside their trade window. When an item is awarded, its holder is told, and opening a trade with the winner fills it automatically. An award only counts as delivered once the item has actually changed hands.

On WoW Forever, the Master Looter loot method is back. The Master Looter is the Loot Master: the drop goes to their bags, the council votes the same way, and a trade hands it to the winner.
Light on Screen Space
SimpleLootCouncil gives you compact frame options for the council voting frame and the loot response frames, taking up less screen real estate, making it easier to keep playing while managing loot.
Performant at Any Scale
Answers from a 40-player raid cost about 0.04 ms each, so a full raid's answers never stall your game, and closed windows cost almost nothing.
Bring Your History
Import award history from RCLootCouncil or Loothing by pasting a CSV export, so your council isn't starting blind.
Features
• Live council voting
• Custom response buttons
• Council by name or guild rank
• Loot from council members' bags, with sessions the council can request or start
• Loot Master promotion, remembered for your next raid
• Autopass on unusable gear
• Equipped-gear and tier-set comparison
• Bonus-roll tracking
• Rolls, asked or generated
• Whisper answers for players without the addon
• Raid team view by guild rank
• Attendance
• CSV export
• WowUtils, Guilds of WoW and wowaudit wishlist support
• SimulationCraft export
• Settings search, window opacity and window scale
Languages
SimpleLootCouncil runs on every World of Warcraft client language: rolls work in every language, plurals and punctuation follow your language, and Cyrillic, Korean and Chinese text draws in the right font.

English (enUS, enGB) · Deutsch (deDE) · Français (frFR) · Español (esES, esMX) · Italiano (itIT) · Português (ptBR) · Русский (ruRU) · 한국어 (koKR) · 简体中文 (zhCN) · 繁體中文 (zhTW)

The interface is translated into every language above. Not every translation has been checked by a native speaker yet, so translators are deeply desired, and any interested parties are encouraged to join the Discord!
Getting Started
Install it from CurseForge or Wago, or with WowUp: Install from URL with this repo's address. Everyone who takes part needs it. The group leader is the Loot Master by default. Add your council with /slc council add Name-Realm, and type /slc for settings or /slc help for every command. The feature guide covers the rest.

• While a loot session runs, the Response buttons section is greyed out, and hovering it says "Response buttons locked while loot session is active".
• Loot to Trade is redesigned: each item has its own line, with the player's name, then the trade timer, the item and the Trade button. Out-of-range players are faded, and offline players grey and faded. Names over 22 letters are cut with "...". The window is wider, and the urgent count reads "1 Urgent" at the top right.
• Window tags (item count, Compact/Expand) match the close button's height, use the accent colour, and have no background fill. The LIVE and ENDED tags are gone from the council window.
• Compact/Expand is now an arrow beside the close button, down-left to compact and up-right to expand. The window keeps its top-right corner when it changes size.
• The response window says "ilvl", and the wishlist and sim info sits beside it on the same line. The note button is as tall as the response buttons.
• "Add loot response frame as a tab in Loot Council frame?" is off by default for new installs. Your current choice is reset to off once with this update.

• The Discord and Ko-fi link boxes centre their text, drop the OK button and the empty space under the address, and fit their size.

• Whispering an answer for an item that was awarded and traded is now refused with " has already been awarded and traded to
."
• Options: "Loot funnel in which groups?" and "Automatically join SLC sessions?" swapped places, as did "View loot in council members' bags" and "Council Members May Vote For:".

Fixed

addons.changelog:
0.53.0
ORGANIZED COMPLEXITY. We audited the big character-stat addons (ExtendedCharacterStats,
DejaCharacterStats, Details!, Pawn, ElvUI, Titan Panel) and applied the conventions they
converged on: keep every number, put the depth one gesture away.

Less space, your call
• Collapse the Matrix: a new title-bar chevron shrinks the Foresight Matrix down to
just its title bar - the Details!-style minimize. Remembered per character.
• Both windows close together: closing the character menu now closes the Matrix with
it, by default. Want it to stay? Turn on the new "Pin the Matrix open" option.
• Forged chrome: gold corner brackets and studs on the panels - drawn in code, in
your class color, so they match any UI skin (ElvUI included).

Hold Shift for the full breakdown
Talent hovers now lead with the verdict: the at-max value, what the next point does to
your actual abilities, and the Synergy/Chains lines. The depth - the full affected-spell
list, the stat-fold context, your crit baseline - appears while you hold Shift, and it
appends live mid-hover. Works on the talent frame and the planner, both flavors.

Classic synergy truth
Vanilla hardcodes its stat-conversion auras to Spirit - our classic decode now honors
that, so Spiritual Guidance correctly chains Spirit into spell damage and healing (the
modern-shaped column had it misread as Strength). Classic talent hovers now carry the
same Synergy: and Chains: lines Forever gets, and /foresight synergy reads like a
report: grouped by talents / racials / buffs instead of one long dump.

Every release still passes the full test suite on BOTH flavors before it ships
(Forever 304 checks, Classic 259).
addons.description:
The layman's oracle for official WoW: Forever. Foresight answers the question every
talent point and every stat on gear raises: "+2 Spirit - so what?" Answers always end
in human terms: extra casts per fight, seconds of regen saved, damage per swing. It's
not here to simplify the game or play it for you - it's here to give you insight, built
on a crowd-sourced, live-verified Forever database that sharpens as more players use it.

Three pillars (the first is the shipped core; the others are the roadmap):

1. Talent, Item & Consumable Impact Map - what each talent, stat, item, and buff
actually does to your character, with what-if modelling before you commit - plus
the opt-in crowd compare (ladders + daily challenges at wow-foresight.web.app).
2. Panic Advisor - what to press when things go wrong (planned).
3. What-to-press HUD - suggest-only rotation help (planned).

Status: pre-release, built against the Forever beta (Interface 16001, data build
1.60.1.70338). Forever launches 2026-11-04.
Official download channels
When released, Foresight will be distributed only through:
• CurseForge
• Wago Addons
• GitHub Releases on this repository

Anything obtained anywhere else is unofficial and may have been tampered with. The
login message prints the addon version plus the game data build it was generated
from; if yours does not match a release on this page, you are not running our build.
Account safety, by construction
Foresight is a normal Interface\AddOns addon using official APIs only, and it is
display-and-advice only: it never casts, targets, moves, uses items, or automates
any protected action. There is no memory reading, no input injection, no game-file
modification, and the addon never talks to the network.

This is enforced, not just promised: pipeline/check_compliance.py statically bans
every automation/protected API and sandbox escape, runs as the first step of the ship
gate, and a red result blocks any release. The full source is public so you can check.

FORESIGHT COMES TO CLASSIC ERA. One addon, two games: alongside the WoW: Forever build,

honest tooltips, Matrix, and ladders, running on data generated from the classic client's
own files.

Classic, done faithfully
• The planner uses the real classic talent trees (432 talents, all nine classes, with
prerequisite arrows) - and 321 of them carry exact datamined per-rank values.
• Vanilla math is vanilla: Fireball rank 1 really is 14-22, Arcane Intellect rank 1 really
is +2, and spell coefficients follow the classic cast-time law (the data column modern
tools trust is wrong in the 1.15 export - we checked, and don't use it).
• Vanilla item truths preserved: Elixir of the Mongoose is a 1-hour elixir here, your 8
classic races are exactly that, and anything only verified on Forever honestly starts
as "(p) presumed" on Classic until your own scans confirm it.
• Synergies, chains, the catalog, and the ability map all work on classic talents.

Quality gate, doubled: every release now has to pass the full test suite on BOTH
flavors before it can ship.

Forever players: everything from 0.51.0 and earlier is unchanged in this release.

0.51.0
Chained synergies, and one math for every gear number.
• Chains: see where a point really pays out. Talent tooltips (in the planner and on the
real tree) now show a "Chains:" line when a talent's stat feeds a converter - a talent
boosting Intellect chains through Mental Quickness into spell damage. Not just which
talents push the same lever, but where the lever leads.
• One math for gear. The "vs equipped" dimension rows, the headline upgrade verdict, and
the "Best for your spells" lines are now computed from the same single swap model - they
can never disagree with each other.
• The stats panel now appears even when another addon makes the character frame load late.

arrows, cross-impact tooltips (credited to talentsforever.com), the ElvUI-friendly window

menu over them. The Matrix stays pinned like a Details! window - close it with its X.
• Windows behave like windows: the one you click comes to the front, nothing can be
dragged off-screen, the Matrix no longer hides underneath other addons' frames, and the
options window remembers where you put it.
• One scale slider for everything: the Layout panel-scale setting now sizes the planner,
options, and export windows too - the lever for fitting Foresight beside a scaled ElvUI.
• Text stays organized at any size: the planner header can't overlap its controls
anymore, a long build summary pushes the trees down instead of running under the buttons,

the requirement is met in your plan, gold once it is.
• Tree plates with class-colored headers, per-tree "points invested" footers, engraved
slot rims, and a clear "N points left of 20" budget readout that turns red (with the

them ("Affects: ... / At max: ... / Synergy: ..."), and an honest **"Interacts with:

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon. Download locations: CurseForge | Wago

Slacker's Addon Depot (SAD) is a simple but powerful addon manager that lets you enable and disable addons - automatically, if you'd like.

Create manual profiles and apply them to any character that SAD has seen before.

Or use SAD's flagship feature: Login Profiles. This lets you enable addons automatically for matching characters. GatherMate for your herbalists and miners? Auctionator for your AH alts? Once you set them up, SAD will apply them for you automatically.

If SAD has not seen your character before, you will be prompted to reload to apply all matching Login Profiles.

> [!WARNING]
> Addons not in any matching login profiles will be disabled on login. This is because multiple login profiles can be valid for any one character. If you choose to work with Login Profiles, it is recommended to take a moment to set them up properly.

Other features:
• A character list with all seen characters, including those from different realms.
• Use Shift+click to quickly (de)select multiple addons.
If you are experiencing issues
• Check if the issue occurs with only this addon enabled, or if the issue is a feature you can disable from the addon's settings menu.
• If you run into any issues or if you have other feedback, feel free to join the Discord and ask in the #slackers-addon-depot channel, or create a ticket on GitHub. :)

addons.description:
A compact Oak browser for WoW Forever's shared player and group listings.
Targets interface 16001; reviewed against Blizzard UI source for 1.60.1.70235.

Browse players and groups together in a familiar Oak window, then whisper a
leader or invite a solo player using Forever's native group finder flow.
Features
• One sortable list with All, Groups, and Players filters.
• Role, activity, text, and new-player-friendly filtering.
• Class-colored member names, levels, classes, and roles in tooltips.
• A pinned row for your own listing.
• Native whisper and invitation actions, plus access to Blizzard's listing editor.
• Draggable minimap button, keybinding, saved window position, and scale options.

Download releases
| Report an issue

Tagged GitHub releases publish through the marketplace workflow to CurseForge
project 1729476 and Wago project rNkg0BNa. The repository needs CF_API_TOKEN
and WAGO_API_TOKEN Actions secrets; the workflow warns separately if either
one is missing.
Use
• /sorter or /oaklfgforever: open or close the window.
• /sorter reset: reset position and scale.
• Keybindings: under Oak LFG Sorter - Forever, bind Open / Close Sorter.
• Minimap button: left-click to toggle, right-click for options, drag to reposition.
• Choose a category and one or more activities, then browse the results.
• All / Groups / Players filters share one list. Your listing stays pinned first.
• Click column headings to sort; click again to reverse. Scroll for more rows.
• Role filters match a player's advertised roles or roles already in a group.
• The text box filters loaded names, activities, notes, and playstyles.
• Select a listing and click Whisper to open an unsent chat draft.
• Invite is available for eligible solo listings, subject to native permissions,
group capacity, and combat. It does not use Retail applications.
• List yourself / Edit listing opens Blizzard's listing editor. Blizzard opens
its normal browser. Use /sorter to return.
• Options includes scale, beginner-friendly listings, Blizzard's level filter,
and an optional auto-open setting. Auto-open defaults off.

The default window is 660 x 484 with nine pooled rows, Oak's font and portrait,
gray panels, class-colored names, and blue activity text. Drag the title bar to
move it. Escape closes it when the search box does not have keyboard focus.

addons.description:
Hear your quest progress: "Work, work." when you finish an objective, "Work complete." when the quest is done. Prefer the Alliance? Switch to the Human worker ("More work?" / "Job's done!").

On top of the quest sounds come a bunch of small quality-of-life tweaks, each one individually toggleable. Works in Retail, WoW Forever, Classic Era, Anniversary and Mists of Pandaria Classic.
What's new in 1.5
• 🤖 Quest automation — accepts and turns in quests for you, with an override key to pause it.
• 🎨 Colorful unit tooltips — class colors, guild, level, faction and health on the bar.
• 🔗 Wowhead links — copyable links in the quest log and achievement window, plus a Show web link key binding for whatever is under the mouse.

The new features are off by default. 1.5 adds new files, so restart the game after updating (a /reload is not enough). See the changelog for the full release history.
Features
Quests
• 🔊 Quest sounds — Peon or Human worker voice lines when you finish an objective or a whole quest.
• 🤖 Quest automation — accepts regular, daily and weekly quests and turns in completed ones. Never picks a reward for you and never hands in gold, currency or non-quest items.
• 📡 Smart Quest Radar — a quest icon and objective counts (e.g. 2/8 · 1/5) above the nameplates of units you still need.
• 🏷️ Nameplate objective counts — quest progress above relevant nameplates.
• 🧭 Auto-track new quests in the objective tracker.
• 🎨 Colored quest progress — counts like 3/10 go from red through yellow to green, in chat and in the quest tracker.
• 📖 Adventure Recap — a window with this session's quests, reputation, playtime and top faction.

Character, reputation & XP
• 🧾 Item level and speed on your player frame.
• 🎨 Colored XP/reputation numbers, plus percentage left and standing on the reputation bar.
• 🤝 Auto-watch reputation — switches to the faction you just gained reputation with.
• 🧠 Reputation Memory — returns to your preferred faction 10 seconds later.
• ✨ Floating reputation gains — +25 Rep — Valarjar near the screen center.

Group
• ⏱️ Ready check countdown and ⏳ LFG queue pop countdown.
• 👥 Party member levels on the party frames.

Interface
• 🎯 Target in unit tooltips — who the unit is targeting, with a red You when it is you.
• 🎨 Colorful unit tooltips.
• 🔗 Wowhead links and the Show web link key binding.
• 🏹 Range icon and distance to your target on its nameplate.
• ✅ Hide completed achievements by default.
• 🖋️ Custom damage text font and 🖱️ cursor shake highlight.
Classic clients
The quest sounds and most features work everywhere. A few need Retail-only parts of the UI and are simply left out of the options in the Classic clients: Smart Quest Radar, nameplate objective counts, auto-track, the range icon and the colored counts in the quest tracker. Classic Era and Anniversary also have no achievements or group finder, so those two features are only in Mists of Pandaria Classic.
Settings
Open the options window from:
• 🧩 a LibDataBroker display such as Bazooka or Titan Panel,
• 📋 the addon compartment menu by the minimap,
• 🗺️ the optional minimap button (/sqol minimap), or
• 💬 /sqol config.

Esc → Options → AddOns → SMoRG's QoL has a button that opens the same window, and every option has a chat command. Type /sqol help for the full list.
Translations
The addon follows your game language: English, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. The voice lines are always in English.

⚠️ The translations have not been checked by native speakers yet. If something reads oddly, please suggest a better wording on CurseForge or GitHub.

addons.description:
LibLog is a structured logging library for World of Warcraft addons.

Out of the box, LibLog prints readable messages to the chat window, and that's all most users will ever see. Behind the scenes, each log also records its
values as named properties, which other addons (called sinks) can capture and inspect:
• LogSink: Table shows logs in an in-game window.
• LogSink: SavedVariables writes logs to your saved variables.

See API.md for the full API reference.
Features
• Simple logging API with well-known levels: trace, debug, info, warning, error, and fatal.
• Configurable minimum log level per addon.
• Structured logging using Message Templates.
• Custom sinks to capture and process logs in real-time.
• Works out of the box with AceAddon-3.0 addons and modules.
Why structured logging?
Traditional logging writes plain text:

This is easy to read, but hard to analyze. Who cast Bloodlust? Whose casts failed? Who cast the most spells? Answering that means parsing text, which only
gets harder in a 20-player raid.

Structured logging keeps the values separate from the text. LibLog uses Message Templates, where each {placeholder}
in the message becomes a named property:

A sink can now filter, group, or count logs by any of these properties.
Getting startedEmbedding
LibLog must be embedded into your addon. With AceAddon-3.0, add it to the list of libraries:

Without AceAddon-3.0, embed it manually using LibStub. Make sure your addon has a name field, LibLog uses it to identify your addon:

Then start logging:
Log levels
| Level | Method | When to use |
| --------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FATAL | LogFatal | A critical or otherwise unrecoverable error that must halt execution. |
| ERROR | LogError | A high-severity logic issue that leaves functionality unavailable or expectations broken. |
| WARNING | LogWarning | User error, or other non-breaking issues. |
| INFO | LogInfo | General status updates and runtime milestones. |
| DEBUG | LogDebug | Code paths and state changes that help determine how something happened. |
| TRACE | LogTrace | High-frequency, noisy data that is rarely enabled outside of debugging. |

Logs below your addon's minimum log level are ignored. The default minimum is INFO.
Formatting
Placeholders support string.format specifiers, without the leading %:

Values are matched to placeholders by position, not by name. Placeholder names may only contain letters and digits.
Configuring the log level
Change the minimum log level of your addon with:

LibLog doesn't save the log level between sessions, that's up to your addon. The easiest way is to pass your saved variables to
SetLogLevelFromConfigTable on startup:

With AceConfig-3.0, you can add a dropdown that changes and saves the log level:

Building your own dropdown? Use LibLog.LogLevel, LibLog.configKey, SetLogLevel, and GetLogLevel.
Advanced usageExpensive logs
If a log needs expensive work to gather its values, that work is wasted when the log is filtered out. Pass a function instead, and it will only run when the
log is actually processed:

Alternatively, check the level yourself with IsLogLevelEnabled:
Fatal logs
LogFatal logs like any other level, but also raises a Lua error, which halts execution just like error(...) and shows up in BugSack or the default error
frame.

All log functions return nil, so you can log and exit in one statement. This is especially useful for LogFatal, since language servers such as LuaLS
don't know it never returns:
Additional properties
You can add properties to every log from your addon, without including them in the message. If the value is a function, it's called for every log, so the
value is always up-to-date.

To avoid having to pop properties manually, use WithLogContext, or create a separate logger with ForLogContext:

Enum values are often just numbers, which aren't very useful in a log:…

addons.description:
A small World of Warcraft: Forever addon for a fixed circle of friends. It
shows what happens to your friends, whether you play together or each on
your own: who levelled up, who died (again), who drowned, and who walked
into a dungeon. You also get a leaderboard to settle who the Death King is.

> Working title. Free, open source, no ads, no donation requests.

Status: v0.2.0 (Ticker, stats, leaderboard with Hall of Fame and Hall of
Shame, ranked duels and the PvP tab, Tonight, profiles, Friends' inventory
with wishlists, friends list). A profession directory
and bets are planned. See
STATUS.md.
Fair play
LooserPiml only uses the official in-game Lua API. It never automates game
actions and never writes into visible chat. Friends' clients talk to each
other through hidden addon messages, which are throttled and paused while
the game restricts them (boss encounters). LooserPiml talks **only to
players on your LooserPiml friends list who added you too**: nobody else
ever receives anything from it, not even a hidden message. If a value is
protected ("secret") the feature is skipped instead of worked around.
Details are in STATUS.md.
For friends: installWowUp (recommended, updates automatically)
1. Install WowUp. WoW: Forever support started in the
v2.24.0 betas, so use that version or newer.
2. In WowUp, select your WoW: Forever client.
3. Get Addons → Install from URL → paste
https://github.com/snoopjust/LooserPiml → Install.
4. That's it. WowUp picks up new releases by itself.
Manual (fallback)
1. Download the latest LooserPiml-vX.Y.Z.zip from
Releases.
2. Extract it into your Forever client's AddOns folder so that this file
exists: World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns\LooserPiml\LooserPiml.toc
(beta folder; the folder name at launch may differ).
3. Restart the game. To update, repeat with the new zip.

If the addon list shows LooserPiml as "out of date" after a game patch,
tick "Load out of date AddOns" until a new release is out.
Beta versions (for testers)
Test versions are GitHub releases marked Pre-release (tags like
v0.2.0-beta.1). Normal installs never get them.

WowUp: WowUp only looks at pre-releases if the addon channel of your
Forever installation is set to Beta. Without that it installs the latest
normal release instead.

1. WowUp → Options → WoW → your WoW: Forever installation →
Default Addon Channel → Beta.
2. Get Addons → Install from URL → paste
https://github.com/snoopjust/LooserPiml → Install. If LooserPiml
is already installed, use Check for Updates instead.
3. The version column shows the newest pre-release (or a newer normal
release).
4. To get only normal releases again later, set the channel back to
Stable. The next normal release replaces the beta.

Manual (fallback): open
Releases, pick the
newest release marked Pre-release, download its
LooserPiml--forever.zip and
install it like the manual install above.
Usage
One thing to set up: add your friends.

1. Group up with them once and add them on the **LooserPiml friends
list: minimap button › tab Friends** › "Add from group" (or type
"First Surname"). Ask them to add you too.
2. Also add them on the WoW friends list (Social › Friends › Add
Friend) if the game lets you.

For now: group up to connect. LooserPiml can only tell that a friend
is online if you're in a group with them, or if they're on your WoW friends
list. On the Forever beta the WoW friends list didn't work between all
players, so until that's confirmed on the live servers, connect while
grouped. You still play wherever you like: the group just has to exist.

LooserPiml shares nothing with anyone who isn't on your list or hasn't
added you. Once you're connected (Friends tab: "connected"), your friends'
events show up as a banner in the middle of the screen and as a line in
your chat window (only you see it).

If LooserPiml says a friend's message "arrived damaged" or "incomplete",
both of you type /lp selftest and compare what it says.…

addons.description:
Rear-paddle action panels for WoW: Forever, nested in the native gamepad crossbar. Built for the Xbox Elite Series 2; also works with the PlayStation DualSense Edge and any other controller whose extra buttons can be mapped to keys on PC.

Backhand is part of the SNRN addon family, next to Rummage, Tally, Valet and Grimoire. It was called PaddleSlots up to version 0.7.9.

Forever's crossbar gives you the d-pad and face buttons on four layers (no trigger, LT, RT, LT + RT). Backhand adds a 2 x 2 group for the P1-P4 paddles to each layer: 16 more actions without taking your thumbs off the sticks. The panels use Blizzard's own crossbar art, expand and highlight exactly like the native bars, and sit next to the bar that uses the same trigger combination.

Built for World of Warcraft: Forever only (Interface 16001). It relies on Forever's native crossbar and gamepad API and does nothing on other clients.
Quick start
1. Map each paddle to a key WoW does not use. Xbox Elite with the Xbox Accessories app: paddle to F9, F10, F11, F12. Steam Input or reWASD (Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge, others): paddle to F13, F14, F15, F16.
2. In game open Settings > AddOns > Backhand (or type /backhand), click Assign P1-P4 and press each paddle in turn.
3. Drag spells, items or macros onto the paddle slots. Hold LT, RT or both to fill the other layers.

Panels can be moved in WoW's normal Edit Mode, or with Unlock panels outside Edit Mode in the settings. /backhand reset puts them back into the crossbar.
Settings
Open:

Settings → AddOns → Backhand

or use:

/backhand

Options include:
• Unlock panels outside Edit Mode
• Only show in gamepad mode (panels hide in mouse-and-keyboard mode, stay visible while unlocked or in Edit Mode)
• Controller (Auto, Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge, Generic; Auto detects the connected controller)
• Paddle inputs (one row per paddle, click to assign by pressing), Assign P1-P4, Setup guide
• Paddle behavior (per paddle: Backhand actions, or previous / next crossbar page), and whether paging paddle slots show their arrows
• HUD scale
• Inactive panel opacity (1.00 = native, no fading)
• Focus highlight and strength
• LT / RT modifier icons (off by default; the native crossbar shows the same prompts)
• Paddle prompts on the focused panel
• Diagnostics
Paddle inputs
On Windows the Xbox Elite Series 2 does not report its paddles to games, and the DualSense Edge's back buttons arrive as copies of the face buttons. WoW only sees whatever the Xbox Accessories app, Steam Input or reWASD maps a paddle to, so Backhand listens for a configurable input per paddle instead of assuming the native PADPADDLE1-4 keys.

Backhand never takes over a button the native gamepad UI uses. Settings -> AddOns -> Backhand -> Paddle inputs shows one row per paddle whose button reads the current input; click it and press the paddle to assign a new one. Accepted inputs are only ones WoW does not use:
• physical keyboard keys with no WoW binding (F9-F12 on a compact keyboard; also F6-F8, Page Up/Down, Scroll Lock, Pause, or Numpad keys), for the Xbox Accessories app's keyboard key mapping,
• the Share button (unused by the native UI, if Xbox Accessories offers it for your controller),
• keyboard F13-F24, for Steam Input or reWASD sending keys that are not on the keyboard,
• the native paddle keys, for controllers that actually report paddles.

Assign by pressing opens a prompt and assigns each paddle to whatever the controller sends when you press it. If that is A, B, X, Y, a stick click, or any other native button, the prompt refuses it, explains that the controller profile is mirroring the paddle, and keeps waiting. Keyboard keys that already have a binding are refused too. Setup guide opens an in-game window with the step-by-step instructions for both routes and a live "last input detected" line.

Two routes:…
addons.name: SNRN Backhand

releases.changelog: • Option to hide the page arrows. Under Paddle behavior on the Settings page, Show page arrows on paging paddle slots (on by default) can be turned off to leave the slots of a paddle that pages the crossbar empty on all four panels, for when you know your paging paddles by heart. The paddle still pages, in combat too. The setting is account-wide and can be changed in combat.

• Controller profile. Backhand now recognises which paddle controller is connected: Xbox Elite (four paddles), DualSense Edge (two back buttons) or a generic controller. It reads the active controller's vendor and product IDs and name, and updates when a controller is connected, disconnected or switched, without a reload. Nothing changes on screen yet; the profile is groundwork for controller-specific layouts. Steam Input and some drivers hide the real controller, so the Settings page has a Controller button (Auto, Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge, Generic) and /backhand controller [auto|elite|edge|generic] sets it from chat. Changing it never touches paddle keys or actions. /backhand diag shows the controller's name, IDs, label style and the resolved profile (#2).
• Native button states on paddle slots. Paddle slots now show the same states as the native crossbar buttons: the selected ring while a spell waits for a target or a toggle (stance, aura, tradeskill) is active, the red flash while Auto Attack or Auto Shot is running, and the green border on equipped items. A macro shows the state of the spell or item it currently casts. Works for native-storage slots and fallback slots. In combat the game may hide these states from addons; a hidden state shows as off (#9).
• Spell charges and loss-of-control cooldowns. Paddle slots now show the same cooldowns as the native crossbar buttons: the charge count and the moving recharge edge for charge-based spells, and the red loss-of-control swipe while you are stunned, silenced or locked out of a spell school. A lockout that outlasts the normal cooldown replaces it, like on the native buttons. Fallback slots holding a spell now show its charge or use count too. Works for native-storage slots and fallback slots (#10).
• Page the crossbar with a paddle. Each paddle now has a behavior: its Backhand actions (the default, so nothing changes until you pick something else), or the previous or next native crossbar page. Set it under Paddle behavior on the Settings page or with /backhand paddle [1-4] [actions|prev|next]. Navigation paddles click the crossbar's own page button through hidden secure buttons, the same path as the native LB + RB + Left / Right chord, so they work in combat and on every layer (bare, LT, RT, LT + RT). Their slots show only the native left or right arrow icon and page the crossbar when clicked as well; the actions in them are kept for when the paddle goes back to Backhand actions. On every page change, the native chord included, the new page number shows above the crossbar and fades out. The paddles wrap past the special S page (the pet / possess bar page), also in combat. /backhand diag lists each paddle's behavior and the current crossbar page, and the action bar page, which must stay at 1: any other page shifts every native crossbar button by one bar (#16).
• The addon icon and logo are the new SNRN badge.

• Proc glow on paddle slots. When a proc lights up a spell (spell activation overlay), the paddle slot holding that spell, or a macro that casts it, now shows the same animated glow as the native crossbar buttons. It uses Blizzard's own spell alert template at the native size, follows the slot as the panel expands and collapses, and clears when the proc ends or the slot's action changes. Like the native buttons, only real procs glow: reactive abilities such as Mongoose Bite do not. The glow also works in combat, where the proc state is hidden from addons. One exception: a macro with conditionals ([mod], [stance], ; alternatives, /castsequence) cannot glow while the game hides which spell it is about to cast. Works for native-storage slots and fallback slots. /backhand glowtest shows the glow on every filled slot, and /backhand diag lists the recent proc events and what each slot resolves to (#8).
• Backhand is listed under the SNRN category in the AddOns list, next to the other SNRN addons.

• Panels collapse when a menu has gamepad focus, like the native crossbar. Opening the game menu, bags, settings or any other controller-navigable window used to leave the selected paddle panel expanded. Backhand now follows the same check the crossbar uses (only the core gameplay bindings are active), so the panel collapses, its focus background, button prompts and LT / RT prompt hide, and it expands again when focus returns. The selected layer and the paddle bindings do not change. /backhand diag shows "Native crossbar focused" and "Visual expanded" (#5).

addons.summary: Extra action slots for controller back paddles (Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge, Steam Input back buttons), built into WoW: Forever's native gamepad crossbar.

addons.changelog:
• Buff food and plain food are separate macros. SmartFood now only uses buff food (Well Fed), by your stat priority as before. The new SmartPlainFood eats food without a buff, most health first, so healing up between pulls no longer spends buff food. Saved food priorities and /rummage food are unchanged.
• Fixed macros not updating until /reload. A bag item's tooltip read before the client had loaded the item or its "Use:" spell text was cached for the whole session, so freshly looted bandages, potions or food of a kind you had not carried since login could be ignored (for example after running out). Incomplete tooltips are no longer cached; Rummage requests the missing data and rescans when it arrives.
addons.description:
One macro per item type that always uses the best item in your bags. Type /rum, drag an icon onto an action slot, and that slot keeps pointing at the right item as your bags change.

Built for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). It only uses standard bag, tooltip and macro APIs, so it should also work on other clients that have them.
Categories
| Category | Macro | Picks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| food | SmartFood | Buff food by your stat priority, read from the Well Fed text |
| plainfood | SmartPlainFood | Food without a buff that restores the most health |
| drink | SmartDrink | The drink (water, juice, conjured water) that restores the most mana |
| flask | SmartFlask | Flasks and elixirs by your stat priority |
| healthpotion | SmartHealthPotion | The potion that restores the most health |
| manapotion | SmartManaPotion | The potion that restores the most mana |
| bandage | SmartBandage | The bandage that heals the most, used on yourself |
| quest | SmartQuestItem | The usable quest item for the quest that matters most right now |

Every category skips items above your level. Percent-based potions are valued against your current maximum.
Quest items
The quest log attaches a usable item to some quests (the one the objective tracker shows a button for). SmartQuestItem always points at the most relevant of those in your bags, in this order: the super-tracked quest, quests on the current map, tracked quests, everything else in the log, then bag items that start a quest. Items for quests you have already completed drop to the bottom unless the quest still needs the item to turn in. The macro follows quest log, tracking, super-tracking and zone changes.
Food
Food is split in two macros, so you can eat to heal up without spending buff food:
• SmartPlainFood eats food that gives no buff, the one that restores the most health first. It never touches Well Fed food.
• SmartFood eats buff food only. Rummage reads the Well Fed text of every food item in your bags and ranks by the stats you care about:
• Food with your top-priority stat wins. Among those, the largest amount wins.
• If you carry nothing with a listed stat, buff food with any other stat comes next.
• Drinks that only restore mana are ignored; they have their own drink macro.

Pick your preferred buff in the /rum window, or set the whole order by command:

Words accepted: stamina sta stam spirit spi strength str agility agi intellect int haste crit critical mastery mast versatility vers hit expertise exp ap attackpower sp spellpower armor mp5 health mana.
Flasks and elixirs
Same priority mechanism as food, with its own list (/rummage flask str agi int). Until you set one, the default follows your class and talents (based on the Icy Veins WoW Forever guides):

| Class / role | Default order starts with |
| --- | --- |
| Warrior, Retribution/Protection Paladin, Enhancement Shaman, Feral Druid | Strength, Attack Power, Agility |
| Rogue, Hunter | Agility, Attack Power |
| Mage | Spell Power, Spirit, Intellect |
| Warlock | Spell Power, Stamina, Intellect |
| Priest, and Holy/Restoration/Balance/Elemental hybrids | Spell Power, Intellect/MP5, Spirit |

Hybrids without a talent tree yet get a mixed list (druids lead with casting). Stamina, Health and Armor are always on the list as a last resort. Elixirs that only give stats your class gets nothing from (Strength or Agility on a mage, Intellect or Spirit on a rogue) are skipped instead of wasted, and show as "no use to your class". Add the stat to your priority if you want them used anyway. Battle and guardian elixirs are not told apart yet: the macro uses the single best match, so keep the other elixir type on a separate slot if you use both.
Drinks
SmartDrink uses whatever you sit down and drink that restores the most mana: water, juice, conjured water, and food that restores mana as well. Mana potions are not drinks and stay on SmartManaPotion. No priority to set.
Potions and bandages…

addons.description:
Small chores done for you. Valet sells your grey items, repairs your gear and restocks what you use at a merchant, empties your mail at a mailbox, accepts and turns in quests, clicks through one-option gossip, turns away duel requests, guild invites and guild charters, and clicks through a few popups that never needed a question. Tick what you want once and forget it.

Valet is part of the SNRN addon family, next to Backhand, Rummage, Tally and Grimoire.

Built for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001). It only uses standard merchant, mail, social and popup APIs, so it should also work on other clients that have them. Every chore that answers a popup is especially welcome with a controller, where each popup means moving the gamepad cursor.
What it does
| Chore | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sell grey items | On | Sells every grey item in your bags when you talk to a merchant |
| Repair all gear | On | Repairs everything at a merchant that can repair, after the greys are sold |
| Use guild funds for repairs | Off | Pays from the guild bank when your rank allows it and the guild covers the whole bill |
| Never spend below | 0 gold | Restocking and Train All stop before your money drops below this |
| Take gold from the mail | On | Takes the gold from every letter when you open a mailbox |
| Take items from the mail | Off | Takes the attached items too, until your bags are full |
| Delete the letters it empties | Off | Deletes a letter Valet emptied once nothing is left to read |
| Take from | Everyone | Everyone, auction house and friends, or auction house only |
| Accept quests | Off | Accepts quests from NPCs, objects and items, and picks them from an NPC's list |
| Turn in finished quests | Off | Hands in finished quests when there is no reward to choose |
| Take a quest's only reward | On | With turn-ins on, also takes a quest's single reward |
| Skip gossip with only one option | Off | Clicks through gossip that has one option and no quests |
| Accept quests shared by people you know | Off | Accepts quests shared by friends, guildmates and (see next) group members |
| Count group members for shared quests | On | With shared quests on, also trusts anyone in your party or raid |
| Decline duel requests | On | Declines every duel request |
| Decline guild invites | On | Declines every guild invite |
| Close guild charters | On | Closes a guild or arena charter someone offers you to sign; your own still opens |
| Accept group invites from friends and guildmates | Off | Joins right away when a friend, Battle.net friend or guildmate invites you |
| Decline group invites from strangers | Off | Declines invites from anyone who is not a friend, Battle.net friend or guildmate |
| Confirm Bind on Pickup loot when solo | On | Picks up Bind on Pickup loot without the warning when you are not in a group |
| Accept resurrection | Off | Accepts right away, unless the player casting it is in combat |
| Accept summons | Off | Accepts right away when you are out of combat |
| Release in battlegrounds | Off | Releases your spirit right after you die in a battleground |
| Skip cinematics you have seen | Off | Stops a cinematic or movie that already played on one of your characters |
| Say in chat | Summaries | Everything, summaries, problems only or nothing; see below |
Selling and repairing
• Greys are sold one at a time, a moment apart, so the server does not drop sales. Chat shows the count and the total.
• Grey quest items and anything the merchant will not buy are never sold. Greys you keep with Tally (/tally keep) are not sold either.…

SpellClarity 1.0.0
The first stable release of SpellClarity: clearer equipment tooltips and optional Shift details for your spells and abilities.
Features
• Short, readable labels for supported equipment bonuses.
• Separate spell damage and healing values, including equipment comparisons.
• Hold Shift over a learned spell to inspect supported base values, spell-power contributions, coefficients and calculated estimates.
• Details for supported damage, healing, periodic effects, absorbs and weapon-ability components.
• Native tooltip frames and fonts, with English labels by default and optional Swedish labels.
• Independent installation with no required addons.
Compatibility
Targets the Classic beta / Forever client 1.60.1.70338, Interface 16001. Other builds receive an update notice instead of numerical spell estimates. Estimates exclude talents, critical strikes and target effects; unsupported formulas retain the original spell description.

SpellClarity pauses when Aevum Tooltips or the older ForeverUI/ForeverSkin tooltip addons are loaded. Disable that tooltip addon and reload to use SpellClarity.
Installation
Extract the SpellClarity folder directly into Interface/AddOns and fully restart the game after the first installation. Use /spellclarity sv or /spellclarity en, followed by /reload, to change labels.
Validation
The owner approved in-game testing and this stable release. The publication workflow retests the exact release revision and verifies the packaged files before CurseForge upload.
addons.description:
Clearer tooltips. Understand what your spell power adds.

SpellClarity makes equipment bonuses easier to read and adds a closer look at your learned spells and abilities. See supported base values, bonus contributions and coefficients without replacing the game's familiar tooltips.

Built for the World of Warcraft Classic beta / Forever client, SpellClarity works independently and requires no other addons.
Read equipment bonuses at a glance
Known equipment bonuses become short, readable lines such as +19 Fire spell dmg or +24 Ranged attack power. Combined spell damage and healing bonuses are separated so each value is clear.

For example, a supported bonus granting 3 spell damage and 9 healing becomes:
• +3 Spell dmg
• +9 Healing

Equipment comparisons use the same concise labels while preserving the game's positive and negative values and their colors. Unknown descriptions, conditional effects and procs keep their original text.
Hold Shift for the details
Hover over a learned spell or ability and hold Shift to expand its supported details. Depending on the spell, you can see:
• Base damage, healing or absorption.
• The contribution from your current spell power or healing power.
• Spell coefficients and calculated estimates.
• Periodic values per tick and available tick intervals.
• Known weapon-ability components and relevant attack power.

Release Shift to return to the compact tooltip. The original spell description stays in place.
Familiar tooltips, independent addon
SpellClarity keeps the game's tooltip frames, fonts and native text colors. It adds readable information without a replacement interface or a separate settings panel.

English labels are enabled by default. To switch labels, use:
• /spellclarity sv for Swedish.
• /spellclarity en for English.

Run /reload after changing the language. Your selection is saved between sessions. Equipment-text recognition currently supports English descriptions; the Swedish option translates SpellClarity's own labels.
Compatibility and calculation limits
The included spell data targets client build 1.60.1.70338 with Interface 16001. Numerical spell estimates are guarded by this exact build. On a different build, SpellClarity shows an update notice instead.

Calculations cover supported formulas and are estimates before talents, critical strikes and target effects. They are not a prediction of your final combat damage or healing. Periodic values are shown per tick; weapon abilities may show components rather than a final total. When a formula is unavailable, SpellClarity says so and leaves the original description available.

If Aevum Tooltips, ForeverUI Tooltips or ForeverSkin Tooltips is loaded, SpellClarity pauses to avoid duplicate additions. Disable that tooltip addon and reload to use SpellClarity. Other Aevum addons can remain enabled.

German, French, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Brazilian Portuguese,

addons.description:
Damage you deal and take, and healing you receive, broken down per spell.

On WoW Forever: live, worked out from your own actions
Midnight removed the addon combat log (COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED registers and never
fires), and C_DamageMeter hides every figure until a fight is over. What the client still
sends live is UNIT_COMBAT, the event Blizzard's own portrait hit-numbers use: each hit on
a unit with its amount, school, crit flag or kind of miss, but never who made it or with
which spell.

So on Forever the feeds are live again, with one difference that matters: **your hits are
worked out, not read.** Your casts (with their spell) and your weapon swings are readable,
and each hit on your target is matched to them by timing and school, helped by what each
spell's own description says it does.
• Damage Dealt is per spell again, with crits, schools and mana spent. Counting every
enemy (the default), it also reads other enemies' nameplates (so enemy nameplates need to
be shown), and once the fight ends its numbers are set to Blizzard's damage meter's, so
they end exact.
• Killing blows count. A bolt that kills is reported on the dying enemy's nameplate just
after your target clears, and is taken from there; a killing swing is never reported, and
is filled in from Blizzard's damage meter once the fight is over.
• Weapon procs go on their own line: a seal, poison, oil, weapon enchant or shaman
imbue you applied, matched to the hits of its school that land as you swing. Not yet
checked in game; a paladin's, rogue's or shaman's /gct trace would settle it.
• Actions is back: your target's dodges, parries and resists, matched to your swings
and casts.
• Damage Received is grouped by school (Physical, Fire, ...): the game says how you
were hit, not by what.
• Healing Received counts every heal on you. Your own are on their spell; everyone
else's share one Healing line.

Solo the matching is close to exact, because almost everything hitting your target is you.
In a group, a teammate's hit of the same school landing inside your window can be counted as
yours. /gct probe after a fight shows how many hits came through readable and how each was
placed.

The approach and its timing windows come from Forever Combat Text by Tarolg
(MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Tarolg), which measured them in real fights.

On the Classic clients nothing changes: the combat log is still there and every feed reads
it directly, exactly as before.

> Client support. Runs on WoW Forever (interface 16001) and on the
> TBC Classic / Anniversary client (interface 20505) from the same files.
> Forever serves Classic content from the Midnight 12.x client, so it reports a
> Classic project id but only exposes the modern namespaced API — every call that
> moved is feature-detected rather than switched on project id.

A focused, dependency-free combat-text addon: running tallies of the **damage you deal to
your current target, the damage you take (per enemy), and the healing you receive**
(per spell). It's completely standalone — no other addons required.
Features
• ⚔️ Damage dealt (per target) — the cumulative damage you deal to your current target,
one ever-growing number/row per source (melee, each spell, wand, pet, totem),
school-colored, with an optional combat-time header. By default (Count: Every enemy)
it adds up everything you hit as one set of totals for the fight; with **Count: Your
target** it tracks each target separately and can remember their totals when you re-select
them (Actions has the same choice).
• 🛡️ Damage received (by type) — the cumulative damage you take this fight from **all
enemies combined, grouped by attack type** (all melee together, each incoming spell, each
environmental type), school-colored.
• 🎯 Actions — the attacks avoided this fight, both ways, as count rows: in red, your
attacks your target (or every enemy) dodged, parried, blocked or resisted; in green, the…
