Garu Combat Textv2.1.0 (2026-10-18)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Keep Thorns counted through the fight, as the trace showed it
The first trace with Thorns up showed three things the damage-shield rule got
wrong, which is why it only came right once the fight was over and the meter
corrected it.
Order. The shield's hit on the attacker is reported at once; the report of the
melee blow on you that set it off comes 0.30-0.36 s later, every time -- as
melee always is on this client. The rule waited 0.15 s for the blow, so every
shield hit gave up just before it came. It now waits 0.6 s, and each blow claims
one waiting shield hit, oldest first, so two mobs striking give two. A blow
reported first still claims a shield hit within 0.15 s. A blow absorbed or
blocked whole still counts: it still sets Thorns off.
Hidden buffs. Thorns was placed at 26.20 and then not even considered at 28.24,
still up. In combat the game hides your buffs from addons, and the reader stopped
at the first hidden one, so a re-read mid-fight found nothing and let Thorns go.
Now the known shields are asked for by spell (C\_UnitAuras.GetPlayerAuraBySpellID)
before any list is walked; the walk steps over hidden buffs instead of stopping;
and in combat no shield is let go -- only out of combat, when the buffs can be
read and it is really gone. What is read goes to the recorder as A lines.
The blow that kills. A mob that dies in the shield's moment never has its blow
on you reported, so a waiting shield hit on your target that cleared in that
moment is the shield's anyway. That also needed the fight to be known after a
/reload in the middle of one, when no PLAYER\_REGEN\_DISABLED comes: the state is
now asked of the game at PLAYER\_ENTERING\_WORLD.
The recording is the third fight in tests/fights/, replayed every run: 19 of 19
hits placed. The replay learned A lines, a /reload restarting the recorder's
clock, and PLAYER\_ENTERING\_WORLD on a P line. Engine tests cover the measured
gap, two mobs, a hidden buff ahead of a shield, Thorns found by spell with the
list hidden, and a shield kept through unreadable combat then let go after.
Six more mutants, 39 in all.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Count Thorns and other damage shields
Thorns damage went uncounted on both clients, for two different reasons.
Forever: a damage shield's hit has nothing of yours to be matched to. Thorns was
cast minutes before, on yourself; its damage lands on whatever melee-hits you,
in that same moment. So a Nature hit with no cast, DoT or swing to explain it
was taken for someone else's. Now, while a damage shield of yours is up, an
otherwise unexplained hit of its school on an enemy is the shield's when it
comes in the moment (0.15 s) a melee hit landed on you -- or, the order of the
two not being fixed, when that hit follows within the moment. Your casts and
DoTs are asked first, so a Wrath landing then keeps its hit. Which shields are
up is read from your buffs (C\_UnitAuras, checked for secrecy first, as FCT
does): Thorns, Lightning Shield and Retribution Aura by spell, every rank as
PrettyTooltip's SpellRanks lists them -- the recorder showed Thorns' description
not loading when cast -- and any other by its text ("damage to attackers", "any
enemy that strikes"). Only one you cast counts: another druid's Thorns on you,
or a party paladin's aura, is theirs. A spell hitting you does not set it off.
Classic: the combat log reports a damage shield as DAMAGE\_SHIELD, which the
feeds never listened for. Damage Dealt now counts it, Actions its resisted form,
and Damage Taken an enemy's shield hurting you.
Engine tests cover Thorns in both orders, without a blow on you, after a spell
on you, beside a Wrath landing that moment, someone else's Thorns, and a shield
known only by its text; the load test sends DAMAGE\_SHIELD through the Classic
combat log. Six more mutants, 33 in all.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

Target any enemy in World of Warcraft (Retail, WoW: Forever or TBC Classic) and instantly see its loot table.

> WoW: Forever accuracy. The bundled Classic-side loot data comes from a TBC-era database,
> but Forever's content is Vanilla. Drop rates, which creatures drop what, and which items exist
> can therefore be inaccurate on WoW: Forever. Treat the lists there as a guide, not gospel.
> Retail uses retail data and is not affected.

> Client support. One download runs on Retail (interface 120100), WoW Forever
> (16001) and the TBC Classic / Anniversary client (20505). Forever serves Classic content
> from the Midnight 12.x client, so it reports a Classic project id but only exposes the modern
> namespaced API; every call that moved is feature-detected rather than switched on project id.

> Languages. The interface is translated into English, Deutsch, Español (España and México), Français, Italiano, Português (Brasil), Русский, 한국어, 简体中文 and 繁體中文; the game client's own language is used automatically. Item and creature names follow your client too, where the client can tell us them: on a non-English Classic client the browser's search and the quest view work in your language (the first search collects the item names in the background, a few at a time, and remembers them), and creature names are asked of the client one at a time as they are shown. Anything the client can't name stays in English, and searching in English always works. Check what your client gives with /loot names.

WhatItDrops shows you what whatever you are looking at drops, with no website and no alt-tab.
Target a mob, open the window, and see its loot and how often it drops. Search items or creatures
by name, drill into "who drops this", list the bosses of the instance you are standing in, and see
which items a quest needs and where they come from.
Features
• 🎯 Loot table for your target, via /loot, a keybind, or auto-show on target.
• 🔎 Item and creature browser. Search by name; click an item to see every creature that
drops it, or click a creature to open its loot table.
• 🐉 Instance boss list. With no target inside a dungeon or raid, the keybind lists that
instance's bosses, each clickable to its loot.
• 📜 Quest loot. A "Loot Needed" button in the quest log shows the items the selected
quest needs and where they drop. Quest-class drops are flagged with a yellow !.
• 🧍 Player gear. Target another player to see what they have equipped.
• 🗺️ Retail bosses from the Encounter Journal. Current dungeon and raid bosses are read from
the game itself, so they stay current. The Journal has no drop rates, so those rows show the
item slot instead.
• ✨ Loot window polish. A drop-rate bar behind each row, quality-coloured icon borders, a
sparkle on rare-or-better drops under 2%, rows that fade in, and an optional 3D model of the
target. Each effect has its own switch.
• 🎨 Settings window. Themes (Blizzard, ElvUI, Slate, Parchment), accent colour, opacity,
scale and row height, all applied live. Every setting is explained in a panel as you hover it.
• 🗺️ Minimap button. Left-click reloads the UI, right-click does a loot lookup, drag to
reposition. Toggle it in the settings.
• 🪶 Lightweight. Per-region data loads on demand, so memory tracks where you actually
play. On the Classic clients, item and creature names are baked in (no GetItemInfo
flicker); on Retail they come from the game.
Usage
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /loot (or /fullloot) | Loot table for your current target. |
| /loot browse [text] | Search items or creatures by name. |
| /loot bosses | The bosses of the instance you are in. |
| /loot quest | Items the selected quest needs, and where they drop. |
| /loot names | Non-English clients: how many item and creature names your client has given us, and whether it names the creature you are targeting. |
| /loot auto | Toggle auto-show on target. |
| /wid (or /loot config) | Open the settings window. |…

Square, sharp action buttons with a thin border, plus buff timers on buttons, for World of Warcraft: Forever.

Install: download ForeverCleanButtons-1.2.7.zip below, unzip the ForeverCleanButtons folder into World of Warcraft/forever/Interface/AddOns/. If the game is already running, type /reload. Settings: /fcb.
New in 1.2.7
• Seal of Command, Lightning Shield, Thorns and other buffs whose hits set off a spell of the same name no longer jump back to full time each time they go off.

addons.description:
The default action buttons have rounded masks and heavy frame art, and you can't tell at a glance how long your buffs have left.

Forever Clean Buttons makes your action bars square and sharp with a thin pixel border, and shows the time left on your buffs right on their spell buttons. Built for World of Warcraft: Forever.
• Square icons, 1-pixel border, no rounded masks or blurry frame art
• Works with Dominos or the default bars, bag and menu buttons included
• Border thickness, colour and icon zoom, with a live preview
• Buff timers in big numbers on the spell's button, updated when you recast in combat
• A green frame on buttons whose buff is on you
• Turn the square look off and the usual buttons come back; buff timers are a separate option
• English and Russian
• Minimap button
• Settings: /fcb

Dominos is recommended: it keeps the bars minimal without replacing the whole interface. It works with the default bars too; there, turn on "Hide Bar Art" for the main bar in Edit Mode to remove the gryphons and the frame around it. That's optional, but it gives the cleanest look.

Download: CurseForge or the latest GitHub release.

Install: unzip the ForeverCleanButtons folder into World of Warcraft/forever/Interface/AddOns/. If the game is already running, type /reload.

addons.description:
A shared toolkit that gives you a modern error handler, a profile manager, a macro editor, a Lua console, and more all in one place.

What Does This Addon Do?
Lib's - Addon Tools adds a handful of useful tools to your game. You don't need to be a developer to use them! Here's the short version:
Error Handler
Ever get random Lua errors popping up while you play? This addon replaces WoW's default error popup with a cleaner, more detailed error viewer. Errors are captured quietly in the background and you can browse them whenever you want.
• Show All formats every error into one clean, copyable block perfect for pasting into Discord or a GitHub issue.
• Minimap button shows how many errors happened this session. Click it to open the error window.
• Ignore errors hide the ones you don't care about.
• Auto-popup optionally have the window open automatically when a new error happens.
• Errors are color-coded and easy to read.
Profile Manager
Import and export your addon settings so you can share them with friends or move them between characters.
• Works with most popular AceDB-based addons automatically.
• Built-in support for addons like Bartender4, Masque, and more.
• Export creates a shareable text string copy it, paste it in Discord, done.
• Import lets you paste a string and load it into your current profile or a new one.

Open it with /profiles.
Macro Editor
This addon gives you a full-size macro editor with more room to work than WoW's default.
• Lists all your Account and Character macros.
• Big text area so you can actually see what you're writing.
• Icon picker built in.
• Drag-to-action-bar support.
• Character count so you know when you're near the 255 limit.

Open it with /macros.
Lua Console (CLI)
A mini code editor inside WoW. Type Lua code, hit execute, and see the output. You can save scripts for later too.

Open it with /lua.
Setup
Addons that use this library share one setup window. When you install one, the window opens once after login (never in combat) and walks you through a few quick choices. Each choice has a Recommended pick, and you can skip any addon. Updates with something new show a small note instead of the whole window.

Open it anytime with /setup, or /setup databar for one addon.
Quick Commands
| Command | What It Does |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| /libat | Shows all available commands |
| /errors | Opens the error viewer |
| /profiles | Opens the profile manager |
| /macros | Opens the macro editor |
| /cli or /lua | Opens the Lua console |
| /log | Opens the log viewer |
| /setup | Opens the setup window |
| /rl | Reloads your UI (safe, won't reload during combat in instances) |

For Developers
Everything below is aimed at addon developers who want to integrate with or build on top of Lib's - Addon Tools.
Getting Started
Lib's - Addon Tools is an AceAddon-based framework. It registers itself globally as LibAT (_G.LibAT). All systems are accessible through this namespace.
Logger System
A structured logging framework with 5 severity levels: Debug, Info, Warning, Error, and Critical.

Logs are organized in a three-level hierarchy: Category → SubCategory → SubSubCategory (auto-detected from dotted source names). Each module can override the global log level or inherit from it.
Registering a LoggerLogger Methods
| Method | Description |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| log.log(msg, level?) | Log at optional level (defaults to Info) |
| log.debug(msg) | Log at Debug level |
| log.info(msg) | Log at Info level |
| log.warning(msg) | Log at Warning level |
| log.error(msg) | Log at Error level |
| log.critical(msg) | Log at Critical level |
| log.RegisterCategory(name) | Create a new sub-category logger |

Logs are viewable in-game via /logs or the DevUI Logs tab. See Logger-TechDoc.md for the full technical reference.

Click "Import Now" and instantly see all your characters' played time—no need to log into each one!
FeaturesTime Tracking

Display Options
• Minimap button: Quick access via left/right click
• Data Broker: Works with any LDB display addon (like Libs-DataBar)
• Popup window: Standalone window with collapsible groups, status bars, and scroll support

Grouping

• Class - Color-coded by class
• Realm - Grouped by server

• Newest Wins (default) - Use most recent data

addons.description:
Magely is a lightweight buff manager for mages, inspired by PallyPower. It tracks
Arcane Intellect (and Arcane Brilliance), Amplify Magic and Dampen Magic across your party
or raid and lets you rebuff with a single click.

This is the World of Warcraft: Forever edition (client 1.60.1, Interface 16001).

> Buffy is the new consolidated version. It combines
> Magely, Priestly and Wildly in one addon on the same engine, and picks Mage, Priest or Druid
> buffs for the character you log in. It starts with fresh settings rather than importing
> Magely's, so disable Magely while you use it, or you get two buff windows.

*Earlier-build screenshot. The cooldown-request pane shown here is not in the current Forever
version; the buff window has since gained additional controls.*

> Playing TBC Classic Anniversary? Install v0.1, the last release for that client. It stays
> available on CurseForge for the Anniversary game version. The Anniversary line is no longer
> being developed.

Magely shares its engine and window with Priestly and Wildly through the
LibGroupBuffs library, so a fix to one reaches all
three.

Features
• One row per group, per buff, colour-coded by how many people are missing it, with the lowest
remaining timer on the bar.
• One-click buffing. Left-click casts Arcane Brilliance, right-click buffs the first person
missing Arcane Intellect. No targeting.
• Works before you have Arcane Brilliance. While you only know Arcane Intellect, left-click
simply buffs whoever needs it. Nothing is wired to a spell you do not have.
• Amplify and Dampen Magic when they matter. Each has its own setting: always, when someone in
the group already has it, or by instance - with a list of Forever's dungeons and raids to tick.
Both rows can show at once.
• Per-member popover. Mouse over a row for the full list with range indicators and per-person
click casting.
• Group-aware. It follows party and raid changes, subgroups, and pets.
• Reagent tracking. The Arcane Powder count, once you know Arcane Brilliance.
• Your spec's look. The header, title and icon follow Arcane, Fire or Frost.
• Window controls. Minimize without closing, lock its position, adjust opacity and choose
which side the member popover opens on.

Usage
Use the header - to minimize to the title bar and + to restore. Requests in
combat wait until combat ends. Minimized state lasts for this session; /reload
or logging in expands the window again. X closes the window.

In the popover, ? beside the class icon means spell range is unknown.
? instead of a timer means the buff cannot be read and there is no cached reading.

The window opens on its own when you join a group. On other classes Magely shows nothing and
says nothing, unless you type /magely, which answers with one line.
Settings and window position persist between sessions.

Row colours: green = everyone has it · yellow = some missing · red = nobody has it ·
grey ? = buff state cannot be read right now (the client hides aura data during combat, so
Magely keeps counting down from the last reading instead of guessing).

addons.changelog:
The nameplate range setting is gone
On Forever, nameplates appear at about 40 yards whatever the setting says, so raising it never made plates
reach further. Stakeout no longer changes it. Beyond nameplate range, hover over or target an NPC to detect it.
Distance in target tooltips
Hover a target button to see roughly how far its NPC is (for example, "Distance: 25-30 yd"). It updates as
the NPC moves while a nameplate, your target or your mouse shows it. The method comes from NameplateDistance by Nedyar.
Experimental quest targets
Off by default. Type /stakeout quests on to try it: a mob you see whose
name is in one of your unfinished kill objectives gets its own button (left-click targets a live one,
right-click also marks it). That's all it does for now. Turn-in NPCs and the mobs that drop quest items need
quest data from Questie, which comes later. Like your other settings, it's off again after a full restart
while the beta doesn't reload addon settings: type the command again.
Target buttons skip corpses
Once you'd killed a few of a mob, clicking its button could target one of the dead ones lying nearby.
Now the click targets a live one when one is in reach, and otherwise leaves you with no target.
Right-click never marks a corpse either.
addons.description:
Stakeout is a lightweight World of Warcraft: Forever addon that watches for the NPCs you choose.
When one appears, it tells you and gives you a button that targets it in one click.

It's useful for rare hunting, patrol watching, event NPCs, or any time you want to react fast when a
specific NPC shows up. The target button was inspired by RestedXP's targeting system.

> Forever only. Stakeout 2.0 targets WoW: Forever (1.60.1). TBC Classic Anniversary players can use
> Stakeout 1.0.2, which stays available on CurseForge.
Features
• Watch a list of NPCs by exact name
• Detects them on nameplates, as your target, or under your mouse
• A small frame with one button per NPC found: left-click targets it, right-click targets and raid-marks it
• Chat message, taskbar flash and sound alert (17 sounds, plus 7 more with DBM-Core)
• Experimental quest buttons for mobs named in unfinished kill objectives (/stakeout quests on)
• An approximate distance in a button's tooltip while its NPC is visible
• Two NPCs with the same name keep their button until both are dead
• Movable, lockable, scalable frame
The Forever beta and your settings
The Forever beta client currently doesn't load addon settings back after you log out. It's a Blizzard bug
that affects every addon. Your watch list and options start empty each session. Stakeout tells you at
login while this is happening.

The easy way: type /stakeout macro on, or tick Save list in a character macro in the config.
Stakeout then keeps your watch list in a character macro called Stakeout List (plus Stakeout List 2
and 3 for long lists), updates it whenever the list changes, and reads your list back from it at every
login, with nothing to click. It uses one character macro slot, or up to three for a long list
(roughly 30-40 names of typical length fit; Stakeout tells you if some don't). /stakeout macro off deletes them. Stakeout only touches a macro with that name if it wrote it, so one of yours is safe.

By hand, if you'd rather not use a macro slot:

1. Before you log out, while your list is still there, open the config (/stakeout) and click
Export, or type /stakeout export. Export copies the list you have now; it can't bring back a
list that is already gone.
2. Each line in the box is a complete /stakeout add ... command that fits in one macro. Put each line in
its own macro, or keep the lines in a text file.
3. After logging in, click the macro(s), or paste the lines into chat. Your whole list is back.
Usage
NPC names must match exactly, spaces included (/stakeout add Captain Flat Tusk).
Configuration
• Alerts: taskbar flash, sound on/off, and which sound (it previews when you pick it).
• Raid marking: turn the right-click mark on or off, and pick the marker. Right-clicking again clears the mark.
• Target frame: lock the position (Alt+drag still moves it), the button icon, and the scale.
• Look: WoW Forever (the default) or Glass, a smoked glass look shared with other glass addons. It
applies to every Stakeout window after a /reload.
• Glass UI: with Glass UI loaded, Stakeout wears its look (its glass,
tint and accent) by default. Untick Use Glass UI appearance to use your own look instead (after a /reload).
What changed from the TBC version
Blizzard's Forever client doesn't allow some of what Stakeout did on TBC:
• No proximity scanning. The targeting trick that sensed NPCs outside nameplate range fires for every
name on Forever, so it can't detect anything. Nameplates, target and mouseover do the detecting now.
• Marks come from your click. Addons can't place raid marks by themselves any more, so right-click
a button to mark.
• The combat log is closed to addons. Deaths are tracked another way, with the same result for you.
Notes
• Stakeout never moves, shows or hides its frame during combat. Changes wait for the fight to end.
• It's designed for your own list, not a built-in rare database.…

• Window controls. Minimize without closing, lock its position, adjust opacity and choose
which side the member popover opens on.

Usage
Use the header - to minimize to the title bar and + to restore. Requests in
combat wait until combat ends. Minimized state lasts for this session; /reload
or logging in expands the window again. X closes the window.

In the popover, ? beside the class icon means spell range is unknown.
? instead of a timer means the buff cannot be read and there is no cached reading.

The window opens on its own when you join a group. Wildly does nothing on other classes.
Settings and window position persist between sessions.

Row colours: green = everyone has it · yellow = some missing · red = nobody has it ·
grey ? = buff state cannot be read right now (the client hides aura data during combat, so
Wildly keeps counting down from the last reading instead of guessing).

addons.description:
Basically addon I built for myself. As such many choices that are made are not let's say user friendly.

Goal for the addon is to be able to control as much as possible from what Blizzard allows us to. That said some choices I have made are specifically targetting me, basically saying this UI addon is not for everyone and probably never will cater for everyone

Still very much in not stable state, nor likely ever will be. It's as usable as it is for me to play the game.

Also I ain't gonna lie, have been using AI for this a bit. Core of it isn't AI but some newer features are. So if that's a turn off for you, I get that. I do test stuff here so it's not like I am going in totally blind. To other addon authors, I have looked through the code and I don't think there's anything that has been stolen, but if you see something, feel free to contact me on Discord or make Issue on github and I will remove it.
Features
• Unit Frames
• Single unit and group (party/raid) unit included
• Action Bars
• Resource Displays
• Simple resource displays for Energy, Rage, Holy Power, DK Runes etc.
• Aura Displays
• Customizable aura displays where you can set any filters that Blizzard allows, and adjust them visually however you want
• Cooldown Displays
• Display spell, item cooldown icons, stacks and adjust them visually
• Minimap
• Simplistic minimap styling with button configuration
• Data Broker displays
• Fairly basic text displays for data broker providers, like showing clock, friends, guild or anything else from other addons
• Raid Tools
• Ready Check and Pull Timer buttons, Encounter Time and Battle Res displays
• XP Bar
• Inspired from Luxthos old WA to show you your current XP bar and some statistics of how fast you are leveling
• Custom Objective Tracker
• Basic M+ Timer display
• Notifications that show couple different QoL things like low bag space/repair needed/ what loot you received
• Custom Character Frame
• Skinning
• Skinned blizzard frames

addons.description:
Are you tired of looking at your minimap and not knowing if that flower can be picked? Not sure you
are skilled enough to get a wee bit of ore?

Well search no more! Nope Node will make your life as a gatherer much simpler.

Mouse over a node on the minimap and like a tinkerers dream, the node is recolored. But don't worry,
quest text on the same tooltip is left alone.
Colors
Your skill is your current rank plus any bonus. The node's required skill is the point where it
turns orange and can be gathered.

| Color | Is it Nope or Run for it! |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Red | Nope! You cannot gather it |
| Orange | Gather that thing! Always get a skill point |
| Yellow | Keep on gathering! But don't fret when you don't skill up, it happens |
| Green | Up to you and your needs, odds are you're only getting mats and no skill point |
| Gray | No skill points, but free coin can be had! |
Nodes
Herbs: Peacebloom, Silverleaf, Earthroot, Mageroyal, Briarthorn, Stranglekelp, Bruiseweed, Wild
Steelbloom, Grave Moss, Kingsblood, Liferoot, Fadeleaf, Goldthorn, Khadgar's Whisker, Wintersbite,
Firebloom, Purple Lotus, Wildvine, Bloodvine, Arthas' Tears, Sungrass, Blindweed, Ghost Mushroom,
Gromsblood, Golden Sansam, Dreamfoil, Mountain Silversage, Plaguebloom, Icecap, Black Lotus.

Ore: Copper Vein, Tin Vein, Incendicite Mineral Vein, Silver Vein, Ooze Covered Silver Vein,
Lesser Bloodstone Deposit, Iron Deposit, Indurium Mineral Vein, Gold Vein, Ooze Covered Gold Vein,
Mithril Deposit, Ooze Covered Mithril Deposit, Dark Iron Deposit, Truesilver Deposit, Ooze Covered
Truesilver Deposit, Small Thorium Vein, Ooze Covered Thorium Vein, Hakkari Thorium Vein, Rich

addons.description:
Easy to see vital character information for Classic and Retail WoW.

Vital Frame is a compact, movable HUD for name, level, XP, reputation, professions, and Classic/Forever skill bars. It is built for Retail, Classic Era, other Classic clients, and WoW Forever.
Features
• Name, class icon, and level on a small frame
• XP, reputation, and crafting skill bars
• Optional hunter pet XP on Classic clients
• Streamer Mode (shows class name instead of character name)
• Hide the default Blizzard watch bar
• Separate Skills frame on Classic/Forever (professions, secondary skills, weapon skills)
• Edit Mode on Retail; /vf config to unlock layout on Classic
• Theme: Auto (silver on Classic/Retail, brown on Forever), or lock Classic / Forever
Commands
| Command |Action |
| ------------------- |------------------------------------------ |
| /vitalframe or /vf |Toggle the frame |
| /vf show / /vf hide |Show or hide |
| /vf reset |Reset position and size |
| /vf config |Unlock layout on clients without Edit Mode |

On Retail, use Edit Mode to move the frames and open options.

addons.changelog:
Changelog
Notable changes to LootToastMover. The format follows
Keep a Changelog.
[4.15.1] - 2026-10-13Changed
• Updated for patch 12.1.5, so the game does not flag the addon as out of date. Regions
that patch later in the week keep loading it on 12.1.0 until they update.
[4.15.0] - 2026-10-13Added
• Help translate LootToastMover. Any translation can now be improved on CurseForge,
through the project's Localization page, and every release includes what translators have
written there. Until someone improves a string, you see the same translation as before.
Changed
• The text on the anchor box now breaks after "Drag me." in every language, instead of in
the middle of the second sentence.
[4.14.0] - 2026-10-13Added
• LootToastMover now speaks your language. The anchor box, the tooltips, the options
panel and the chat messages follow your game client's language: German, French, Spanish,
Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Korean, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese, as well as
English. The description in the in-game addon list is translated too, and the options
panel's buttons widen to fit a longer translation.
• Slash commands stay the same in every language, so /ltm test and the rest work exactly
as before.
• These translations are first drafts, not written by native speakers. If something reads
awkwardly in your language, suggest a better wording on GitHub.
[4.13.0] - 2026-10-12Added
• Now loads in every version of World of Warcraft that Blizzard runs. Alongside retail
and Forever, the same download now covers Mists of Pandaria Classic, Classic Era,
TBC Anniversary and Titan Reforged Classic. The anchor box, /ltm test, the minimap
button, the options panel and the broker plugin all work the same in each of them, and
nothing changes for retail or Forever players.
• The Classic games send far fewer alerts through the frame this addon moves. Loot never
goes through it there, so what the anchor moves is mostly achievement toasts, in the
games that have achievements. Classic Era has none, so very little appears there at all.
/ltm test fires a real loot toast in every game, so you can always check the position.
• The Addon Compartment only exists in retail and Forever. In the Classic games, use the
minimap button, the options panel or /ltm.
[4.12.0] - 2026-10-02Added
• Now also loads in World of Warcraft: Forever. One download covers both games. Forever
runs on the retail game client, so the addon itself needed no changes to work there: the
anchor box, /ltm test, the minimap button, the options panel, the broker plugin and the
Addon Compartment are all the same as in retail. Nothing changes for retail players.
• Installing by hand for the Forever beta? The folder is
World of Warcraft/_classic_beta_/Interface/AddOns/.
[4.11.2] - 2026-09-15Fixed
• Opening the options panel threw a Lua error instead of opening anything. Every route
in was affected: right-clicking the minimap button, right-clicking the broker plugin,
right-clicking the Addon Compartment entry, and /ltm config. The options panel itself
was fine and always had been — nothing could reach it. Introduced in 4.11.0.
• If a future game patch changes that call again, the addon now says so in chat rather than
throwing an error popup, and the slash commands keep working.
[4.11.1] - 2026-09-14Changed
• LootToastMover is now explicitly MIT licensed, and the licence ships with the addon.
[4.11.0] - 2026-09-13
You can actually find the addon now. 4.9.0 left Blizzard's Addon Compartment as the
only way in, which meant an installed addon looked like a missing one. Three ways back,
and still with no bundled libraries.
Added
• The minimap button is back — the bag icon on the minimap ring. Left-click shows or
hides the anchor box, right-click opens the options panel, and you can drag it anywhere
around the ring. Hide it from the options panel or with /ltm minimap.
• An options panel, under Game Menu → Options → AddOns → LootToastMover, with buttons…
addons.description:
A small World of Warcraft addon that lets you move the loot toast alerts
(AlertFrame) anywhere on screen instead of leaving them in Blizzard's default
position near the top center. One download works in every version of the game Blizzard
runs: retail, World of Warcraft: Forever, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Classic Era,
TBC Anniversary and Titan Reforged Classic.
What it does
Blizzard's alert system anchors loot toasts, achievement popups and similar alerts to a
fixed screen position managed by the UI's frame position manager. LootToastMover opts
AlertFrame out of that manager and re-anchors it to a draggable anchor box you position
yourself. The position is saved account-wide and reapplied on login.

addons.description:
Version 3.1.1 | Requires Sharpie's Gear Judge | Works on WoW Forever and TBC Anniversary
Overview
• The Laboratory ("The Lab") is a plugin for the Sharpie's Gear Judge (SGJ) addon.
• It is a side-by-side gear comparator: build two gear sets and score them with your stat weights, without needing to own or equip the items.
• Whether you are importing a "Best-in-Slot" list from SeventyUpgrades, testing a single upgrade from a chat link, or checking what the Roadmap's picks are worth, the Lab shows which set is better and by how much.
Features
• Dual Set Comparison: Build two full gear sets (Set 1 and Set 2) and see a direct score comparison.
• A Profile for Each Set: Each set has its own scoring profile: your raid profiles, your leveling roles and, with Sharpie's Gear Judge Talents, its builds for your class. Put the same gear in both sets to see how it holds up for another spec or build. Each item shows its own score on its icon.
• Level Look-Ahead: A level slider scores both sets with the stat weights of another level, so you can see whether a piece is worth keeping for later. Items you can't wear yet at that level are tinted red. Now returns to your own level.
• Cap Check: Under each set's score you see its hit (or spell hit) for damage dealers, or defense for tanks, against the same targets as Gear Judge's Stat Logic rings. Red is short, green is there, yellow is well past it.
• Enchants: As Linked scores each item with its own enchant; Best Enchants fills every enchantable slot with the best enchant for your level. Each set shows how many slots are unenchanted and what the best enchants would add.
• Multi-Format Import: Import gear from SeventyUpgrades (JSON), SimulationCraft / Raidbots (SimC), plain item lists, or a string exported from the Roadmap or the Lab.
• Live Score Difference: Shows which set is better and by exactly how much. When the two sets use different profiles, the Lab says so instead of comparing scores on different scales.
• Stat Breakdown: A scrollable panel with Set 1, Set 2 and difference columns for every stat, color-coded.
• Smart Slotting: Handles 2H vs. 1H weapon conflicts and automatically fills empty Ring/Trinket slots.
• Save/Load System: Save your theorycrafted sets for each character, load them later, or delete them.
How to Use
• Open the Lab: Click the "The Lab" tab in the main Sharpie's Gear Judge window.
• Add Items to the active set (outlined in gold):
• Shift-Click any item in chat, your bags (bag addons like Baganator and Bagnon included) or AtlasLoot.
• Equipped: pulls in your character's current gear.
• Best in Bag: builds the highest-scoring set from your bags. Shift-Click it to equip those upgrades for real (items that would bind to you are listed in chat for you to equip yourself).
• Import String: paste data from SeventyUpgrades, SimC/Raidbots or the Roadmap's Export.
• Inspect Target: loads the gear of the player you have targeted (scored with your profile).
• Roadmap Picks: loads your gear with the Roadmap's recommended upgrades swapped in, for the dungeon selected in the Roadmap or the whole set built in its Chain Mode.
• Edit: Right-click or shift-click a slot to empty it. Use Copy Set 1 to Set 2, Export Active Set and Clear All to manage sets.
• Compare: Pick a set with its button above the gear to edit it.
• Analyze: View the score difference under the sets and the detailed stat changes in the right-hand panel.
• Click the ? button for in-game help.
Translations
• The Lab is translated into English, German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean and Traditional Chinese.

addons.description:
Version 3.2.2 | Requires Sharpie's Gear Judge | Works on WoW Forever, Classic Era and TBC Anniversary

Roadmap is a progression planning tool for Sharpie's Gear Judge. It scans every dungeon, plus the quest rewards in every zone, to build a personalized "Upgrade Leaderboard" showing which dungeons and quest zones offer the biggest power gains for your character.
Key Features🗺️ Dungeon Leaderboard
• Scans every dungeon for your game version:
• WoW Forever: every Forever dungeon with a known loot table, including the new ones such as Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands and City of Dalaran. Multi-wing dungeons (Scarlet Monastery, Dire Maul, Stratholme, Blackrock Spire) are one row each, with the wing shown next to the boss.
• Classic Era: all Classic dungeons, plus Zul'Gurub and Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj.
• TBC Anniversary: all Classic and TBC dungeons (Normal and Heroic), plus the G'eras badge vendor.
• Ranks them by Total Upgrade Score, so you know exactly where to go next.
• Hover a row to see its top 3 upgrades. The dungeon you're viewing is highlighted.
📜 Quest Rewards
• Dungeons | Quests tabs: the leaderboard ranks dungeons and quest zones separately. Quest zones are scored by the best upgrade per slot that their quests give, and each row shows how many quests give upgrades, how many are in your quest log, and whether you're in that zone.
• Quest list: click a quest zone to see its quests in place of your character model: each quest's best reward and gain ("best of N" for a choose-one quest), its level and chain step, and whether it's in your log, available now, or at a later level. Hover for the quest giver and where to find them (WoW Forever).
• World Quests: each zone gets its own "Quests" row in the leaderboard (for example "Elwynn Forest Quests"), including class, profession and event quests.
• Dungeon Quests: rewards from a dungeon's quests sit in that dungeon's row next to its boss loot, marked "Quest:".
• On WoW Forever, nearly 2,000 equippable quest rewards are included. Each counts from the level its quest can be picked up, not the lower level printed on the item.
• Only quests you can get: rewards from the other faction's quests, other classes' quests and other races' quests are hidden. For example, Zephras Isle and the rest of the Skyborne starting chain only show for Skyborne characters.
• Holiday quests only during the event: Darkmoon Faire, Lunar Festival, Midsummer and Scourge Invasion rows show while the event runs (from the in-game calendar).
• PvP Quests: Alterac Valley quest rewards have their own checkbox, off by default.
• Quest chains: the Epic Quests and Legendary Quests rows are marked "(quest chains)".
• Profession quests only with the profession: rows like "Fishing Quests" show only for characters who have that profession.
• Only quests you haven't done: rewards from quests this character has already turned in are left out.
• One reward per choice: when a quest lets you pick one of several rewards, the Roadmap suggests at most one of them.
🧰 Scan Settings
• Mode: score with PvE or PvP stat weights.
• Profile: use your current profile (Auto) or pick another one to plan for a different spec or role.
• Focus: only suggest upgrades that carry a chosen stat.
• Dungeon Loot / Dungeon Quests / World Quests / PvP Quests: choose what a scan includes. All but PvP Quests are on by default, and your choice is remembered between sessions.
• Level Range Bar: drag the two handles to choose which dungeon levels to check. Raise the high end to plan upgrades above your level; raise the low end to focus on endgame dungeons. Right-click resets it to 1 through your level. A live count shows how many dungeons the next scan will check.
• TBC only: Heroic Only, Include Badges and Sort by Efficiency (score per badge spent).…

releases.changelog:
🚀 v3.2.2🎨 New Look
• Matches Gear Judge's new window: colored section titles, slimmer bars and your class color as the accent.

🚀 v3.2.1🗺️ Dungeon Loot Updated to the Latest Beta Build (WoW Forever)
• 9 new trash drops: 7 in the City of Dalaran (Violet Sorcerer's Sandals, Leggings and Wraps, Roused Nature Footwraps, Construct's Grips, Tattered Kirin Tor Cloak, Guardian's Emblem) and 2 in the Excavation Site (Ancient Cleaver, Excavated Dagger).
• 27 drops now show WoW Forever's required level instead of Classic's (Gnomeregan, Scarlet Monastery, Razorfen Downs, Uldaman, Wailing Caverns), so they're suggested at the right level.
• Blindwatcher's Sight (Shadowfang Keep) is listed as cloth armor.
📜 Quest Rewards Updated (WoW Forever)
• 94 more quest rewards from the latest quest data (2,025, was 1,931), across about 30 zones: Wetlands, Desolace, Stranglethorn Vale and Arathi Highlands gain the most, plus new Shaman, Druid, Paladin and Rogue class quest rewards and new dungeon quest rewards in Uldaman, the City of Dalaran, Scarlet Monastery, Razorfen Downs and Kraul and the Stockade.
• A new quest zone, Shen'dralas.
• Five rewards are now marked as choose-one, two as Alliance-only, and Razorfen Kraul's "Mage-Eye" Blunderbuss is no longer a quest reward there.
📍 Bigger "You're Here" Marker
• The arrow on the quest zone you're standing in is half as large again, so it reads as the map's "you're here" arrow.

🚀 v3.2.0📜 A Quest View
• Dungeons | Quests tabs at the top of the leaderboard. Dungeons and quest zones are ranked apart, so a zone's quest rewards no longer compete with a dungeon run. Your tab is remembered, and after a scan an empty tab gives way to the other one.
• Quest zones show their quests. On the Quests tab each row is named by its zone, with how many of its quests give you an upgrade, how many are in your quest log, and "You're here" for the zone you're in.
• Click a quest zone for its quests. The character model makes way for a list of the zone's quests, best first. Each line shows the reward and its gain, "best of 3" for a choose-one quest, the quest's name, level and step in its chain ("step 2/4"), and whether it's In your log, Available, or available At level N. Hover a quest for the reward's tooltip, who starts the quest and where (with map coordinates), its chain, and which reward to pick. Shift-click links the reward. A Character button above the list switches to your character with the upgrades tried on, and Quests switches back. A line under the list says how many quests are hidden because you've done them or they're for another faction, class or race.
• Chain Mode keeps the zone you just added. Clicking a quest zone with Chain Mode on puts its best rewards in your chain set and recalculates; the list now keeps showing that zone's quests, with the rewards that went into the set marked In your chain set, instead of going blank.
• Quest zones are scored by what doing them adds: the best upgrade for each slot, each item and each choose-one quest counted once. A zone used to be ranked by its single best reward. Dungeons are still ranked by their best drop.
• WoW Forever quest details (giver, coordinates, level, chain) come from foreverchanges.pro; Classic Era and TBC quest rows show the quest list without them.
✅ Completed Quests Hidden
• Rewards from quests you've already turned in no longer show. The Roadmap now asks the game which quests this character has completed and leaves their rewards out of the zone "Quests" rows and the dungeon quest rewards, so it only suggests upgrades you can still get. All of a choose-one quest's rewards go once you've turned it in. The next scan after you turn a quest in picks it up. Works on WoW Forever, Classic Era and TBC Anniversary.
🎉 Holiday Quests Only During the Event
• Darkmoon Faire, Lunar Festival, Midsummer and Scourge Invasion quest rows only show while the event is running, read from the in-game calendar. Their rewards can't be earned the rest of the year. On a client without a calendar they always show.
⚔️ New "PvP Quests" Checkbox

addons.description:
Version 1.1.4 | Requires Sharpie's Gear Judge | Works on WoW Forever, Classic Era and TBC Anniversary

A lightweight, gear-aware experience bar plugin built for Sharpie's Gear Judge (SGJ).
🌟 Features
• Dynamic Tracking: Tracks your current experience, with optional milestone ticks or classic 20-segment brackets.
• Classic Rested Tail: A translucent blue "tail" beyond your current XP shows exactly where your Rested XP ends.
• Precision Tooltips: Hover the bar for current XP, XP remaining, Rested XP (how much of the level it covers and roughly how many kills it lasts), and session stats: session time, XP per hour, estimated time to level, and kill and quest XP.
• Standalone Stats Box: Optionally show everything from the tooltip in a box of its own. Shift-click it to reset the session.
• Native Integration: Ties into the core SharpiesGearJudge addon for a cohesive HUD experience.
⚔️ Gear-Aware Leveling
• Upgrades Waiting in Your Bags: See which bag items SGJ rates as upgrades once you reach their level, looking up to 5 levels ahead. The next one shows as an icon at the end of the bar.
• Mail/Plate Look-Ahead: Before 40, Warriors and Paladins see Plate (and Hunters and Shamans see Mail) under Upgrades Waiting, with a reminder to visit your trainer at 40.
• Level-Up Gear Alert: A "Ding!" alert lists the upgrades you can equip now (also in chat as clickable links) and any unspent talent points. Left-click opens your bags; right-click dismisses it.
• Stat Weight Change Warning: A heads-up before your leveling weights change, with the stats that shift the most, so you know which items may re-rank.
• Quest Turn-In Projection: A gold section on the bar shows where your completed quests will take you, and the tooltip says which of them reward an upgrade and whether turning them in will level you. Works on WoW Forever too.
• Gear Score Tracking: Your SGJ character score and how much it has grown this level, logged per level for each character.
🎛️ Options
Open Sharpie's Gear Judge (/sgj) and click the XP Tracker tab:
• What the bar shows and when: show the main bar, the standalone stats box, milestone ticks or 20-segment brackets, hide the Blizzard XP bar, auto-hide during combat, lock frames, and the bar text (both, raw XP, percent or none).
• Size and Look: bar width, height and background opacity, plus normal, rested, quest turn-in and text colors.
• Gear Judge Integration: turn each gear-aware feature on or off.
🌍 Translations
The XP Bar is translated into English, German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Korean and Traditional Chinese.

A tiny addon for World of Warcraft: Forever that brings the Target and Focus entries back to the minimap tracking menu, so your current target and focus show up on the minimap again.

addons.description:
A silly little addon for World of Warcraft: Forever: every crit deserves an uwu.
• You crit: a random anime uwu plays when you land a critical hit or heal. Every clip plays once before any repeats.
• Crits come fast? Between full uwus (at most one every 1.5 s) you get small, quiet uwus instead of a wall of noise.
• You get crit or take a big hit: an angry uwu, an ara ara or a startled kyaa. A big hit is one that takes at least 25 % of your maximum health.
• Floating uwu text: every sound pops a cute "uwu~", "owo~" or "ara ara~" over your character, like the game's crit numbers. Only you see it.

All sounds are leveled to the same loudness.

Options
Open Esc > Options > AddOns > Forever UwU, or type /uwu.
• Volume with a Play uwu test button. Sounds play on the Master channel.
• Crit uwus, small uwus, angry uwus and the floating text can each be switched off.
• Position of the floating text. Your character stands in the middle of the screen, so it sits at an offset from there.
• Cooldowns for full and angry uwus, and the big-hit threshold.
• Sounds page below it: every clip as a button, to hear each one. /uwu sounds opens it.

Test sounds: /uwu crit, /uwu small, /uwu hurt.
Good to know
WoW: Forever doesn't let addons read the combat log. Forever UwU uses the same hit events as the damage numbers on your unit frames instead. Those cover only you, your target and mobs with a visible nameplate, so crits on other mobs (Swipe, Cleave, Multi-Shot) need enemy nameplates turned on (default key V). The events don't say who hit, so a crit only counts when it lands together with your own swing, shot, spell or channel. Another player's crit at the same moment can still slip through, and crits from damage over time or your pet stay silent. Crits that kill a mob come without the crit flag; the addon guesses those from the hit size.

• Account mode: items another of your characters needs go to a new group "For alts", so you can collect them and mail them over. It counts profession materials that still give that character skill points and the class items of its class (candles, poisons, totems …), even when the AH would pay well. Your own needs always come first, and soulbound items never count. The tooltip names who needs it and why, e.g. "For alts: Amy (Tailoring), Bob (class item)".
• Alts are matched by ruleset and faction (on Forever the ruleset is the server), not by realm name. Each character has to log in once with this version.
• A table of your alts in the options: each one with its full name in its class colour, its professions, and switches for profession materials, class items and whether it counts at all (a bank character, an abandoned alt).
• KeepOrSell now tells characters apart by first name and surname. Before, two characters with the same first name shared their remembered recipes; each character moves its data over on its next login.
• The old option "Reagents for your other characters" is now the per-alt switch "Profession materials": if you had it off, it stays off for every character KeepOrSell knew when you updated. Filter texts no longer carry it (the alts are private), so an old filter's altReagents line is skipped.
• KeepOrSell has its own options window, in the style of the setup window: sections in a sidebar on the left, the options side by side on the right. /kos opens and closes it; the "? KoS" button and the setup window open it too. Esc → Options → AddOns → KeepOrSell now holds a button that opens it. It also works with the gamepad UI.
• The tooltip names every reason to keep an item, not only the first: e.g. a quest item that your profession and two alts also need shows "also: Profession · for alts: …" below.

addons.description:
Ever stood at a vendor wondering if that weird item in your bag is worth something? KeepOrSell sorts your bags for you. It tells you what to keep, what to put on the auction house and what's just junk.

Good for new players, and for everyone who's tired of hovering over every single item.
What it does
Your bag items end up in these groups:
• Quest: stuff a quest still needs. Keep it.
• Open: clams, boxes and everything else with "Right Click to Open". Each one takes its own bag slot, even when Baganator shows ten of them as one stack. Open them to free the space.
• Unstacked: several copies of something that doesn't stack (scrolls, for example). Baganator would show them as one stack; here you see every slot they take.
• Profession: materials for recipes that still give skill points, whether you know them already or can still learn them, plus those recipes themselves. Keep it, even if the AH pays well.
• AuctionHouse: sells for at least twice the vendor price on the AH. Put it up for sale.
• Junk: grey items, cheap trade goods nobody needs, gear your class can't ever wear, recipes you already know. Scrap sells it at the next vendor.
• For alts: profession materials and class items another of your characters needs (same ruleset and faction). Mail them over. Your own needs come first.
• Disenchant (enchanters only): green, blue and purple gear you'd otherwise sell, when its materials are worth more than the vendor or the AH pays. Soulbound gear you can't auction lands here too. The tooltip shows the average value and what you'll likely get, e.g. "80% Lesser Magic Essence ×1–2".

Hover over any item and the tooltip tells you which group it's in and why, for example "Auction house: AH 1g 20s, vendor 15s". For gear you can wear it also says what it would bring once you no longer need it: disenchanting, the auction house or the vendor, whichever pays most.

Not sure about an item? Then it stays. No auction price means no junk. And green or better gear you could wear never counts as junk, nor does anything saved in an equipment set.

Want to keep something KeepOrSell would sell? Alt+Right-click it in your bags. It stays from now on, also without Scrap; click again to undo. /kos kept lists what you marked. Forgot the shortcut? Hover the gold ? in Baganator's bag window.

A few extras
• Destroy button: bags full and no vendor around? Click it and the cheapest junk in your bags is gone. Hover it to see what's next. It never touches rare or better items, and skips junk in profession bags (that wouldn't free a slot for anything else).
• Loot coins: loot with full bags, and a gold coin marks the loot that's worth more than the junk it would replace. Hover the loot to see which item to destroy for it, and the destroy button lights up. Loot that still fits onto a stack or into a profession bag needs no room and gets no coin.
• Bag value: a small line shows what your junk and your auction items are worth, e.g. "Junk 1g 20s · AH 15g".
• Hints: if KeepOrSell needs something from you (like a fresh AH scan), a little button shows up in your bag window.
• Warnings: destroy or sell something KeepOrSell would keep (a quest item, a reagent, an item you marked) and a warning in chat says why.
• Account mode: KeepOrSell thinks of your other characters too. Reagents that still give one of them skill points and the class items of their class (candles, poisons, totems …) go to "For alts", with their name in the tooltip. Each character logs in once with KeepOrSell; in the options you can leave single characters out.
• Price sharing: in a group, everyone with KeepOrSell keeps each other's auction prices fresh. Whoever has the newer price shares it.

Sharing filters
A filter is your setup as plain text: the decision options (e.g. factor, minimum profit, price age and the junk, profession and disenchant switches), your keep marks and your own rules. Post it in a forum or Discord, or paste someone else's.…

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft: Forever addon that tells you which quests are new in Forever and which
are carried over from original Classic.

Forever deliberately blends its 1,000+ new quests into familiar zones without marking them.
ForeverQuest Marker adds a small, Classic-styled marker so you can tell at a glance whether the
quest in front of you is one you have done a hundred times or something you have never seen.

| Marker | Meaning |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Solid gold star | New in WoW Forever. Confirmed from Forever client data or player reports. |
| Hollow gold star | Likely new. Not in any Classic, Season of Discovery or Classic Era data, but not confirmed yet. |
| Half-filled blue star | Changed. An original Classic quest that players reported as modified in Forever. |
| Violet diamond | Season of Discovery. Not original Classic, but not new in Forever either. |
| No marker | Original Classic quest. |

The states differ by shape as well as color, and an option adds a short text label (New, New?,
Changed, SoD) for anyone who prefers words.
Where markers appear
• Quest window: before the quest title when a quest giver offers, checks or completes a quest,
and in quest details opened from the quest log or world map.
• Quest giver lists: on the corner of the quest icon in gossip and quest greeting windows.
• Quest log: on the corner of the quest's map marker button, left of the title.
• Objective tracker: on the corner of the tracked quest's map marker button.
• Tooltips: hovering any marker, a quest giver row, a quest log entry, a tracked quest, a world
map quest pin, or a quest link in chat explains the state.

If another addon replaces the quest window (for example Immersion), the addon prints the quest's
state in chat instead, so you still get the information.
How quests are classified
1. Quests reported as changed by players are marked as changed.
2. Quests in the original Classic quest list (QuestieDB) show no marker.
3. Quests confirmed new by player reports, or present in the Forever client's quest table but
absent from the Classic Era client's, are marked new.
4. Season of Discovery quests get their own marker.
5. Other quests that exist in the Classic Era client (cut, unused and event quests) show no marker.
6. Anything left is likely new.

The current data comes from QuestieDB and the quest tables of Forever build 1.60.1.70450 and
Classic Era build 1.15.9.70003: 4,257 original Classic quests, 1,808 quests found only in the
Forever client, 928 Season of Discovery quests and 495 other Classic Era quests. /fqm check
explains how any quest ID is classified. See docs/DATA.md for details.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| /fqm | Open the settings (Game Menu, Options, AddOns). |
| /fqm check | Explain how a quest ID is classified and why. |
| /fqm export | Open your recorded quests as JSON, ready to copy. /fqm export csv for spreadsheets. |
| /fqm status | Show data versions, which windows are marked, and recorder counts. |
| /fqm probe | List the quests the addon sees in the windows that are open right now. |
| /fqm errors | Show any errors the addon caught. |
| /fqm tune | Adjust marker size or position live; /fqm tune reset restores defaults. |
| /fqm reset recorder | Delete recorded quests (asks for confirmation). |
Helping the community list
The addon can remember the quests you meet that are not original Classic: ID, title, level, quest
giver, and where you were. Nothing leaves your computer unless you choose to share it. /fqm export
produces a document you can paste on the submission page,
; quests reported by several independent
players are promoted from "likely new" to "confirmed" in a later release. The export contains no…

• Every Cooking recipe in WoW: Forever (132) on ingredient tooltips: green when
known, red when not, with how to learn it.
• Recipe window with recipe counters and a Zone column ("Multiple Zones" when a

stack, e.g. zones inside each Known / Not known group. Recipes new in

whose food gives a chosen buff (Strength, Stamina, Spell Damage, ...).
• Detail pop-up per recipe: ingredients, required skill, where to learn it, and
the food's effect.

seen in game. When only one website names a place it is shown as
"Suggested" (with coordinates and a waypoint) until it is found in game;
recipes learned together with Cooking say "Automatic"; otherwise "Unknown".
Faction aware; map positions are cross-checked the same way.

as many recipes as you like, each shown as a Forever Chef icon on the world
map and the minimap (a light blue arrow on the minimap's edge points to ones
out of range); tracked recipes are highlighted, and each waypoint clears
once its recipe is learned, or with the Reset All Waypoints button.
• Cooking ranks window: how to reach Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert (Expert
Cookbook vendors) and Artisan (Clamlette Surprise quest line), with
requirements, costs and waypoints. Every Cooking trainer of your faction is
listed; a rank waypoint clears when you talk to that NPC or reach the rank.

positions while you play; /fchef export gives the ones the addon does not

addons.description:
A Cooking companion for World of Warcraft: Forever: which recipes use an
ingredient, which ones you know, where to learn the rest, and a map waypoint to
get there.
Features
• Ingredient tooltips. Hover any cooking ingredient to see every Cooking
recipe that uses it, in green if you know it and red if you don't, with
how to learn the unknown ones ("Vendor (Horde)", "Trainer", "Drop", ...).
All 132 Cooking recipes are built in, so this works right away, even on
characters without Cooking.
• Recipe window (the Forever Chef minimap button, the AddOns menu, or /fchef):
every Cooking recipe, whether you know it, how it is learned, and the zone
to learn it in ("Multiple Zones" when there is more than one). Click a
column header to sort; Status, Learn from and Zone also group the list.
Headers stack: click Status then Zone to see zones inside each status
group. Click an active header again to reverse it, a third time to remove it.
• New recipes. Recipes that are new in WoW: Forever (not in Classic) are
marked [New] in light blue after their name.
• Buff filter. The Buff drop-down above the list narrows it to recipes
whose food gives that buff (Strength, Stamina, Spell Damage, Fishing skill,
mana, camp features, ...), with how many recipes give each one.
• Recipe details. Click a recipe for its ingredients (and how many you
carry), required skill, every vendor, trainer, quest giver or drop that
teaches it, and the food's effect (health/mana and the Well Fed buff).
• Waypoints. Each place with a known map position has a radio button that
sets a waypoint. Track as many recipes as you like (one place each): they are
all shown in gold in the window and as Forever Chef icons on the world map and
minimap (a light blue arrow on the minimap's edge points to ones out of its
range), and TomTom (if installed) gets an arrow for each. A waypoint clears
itself when you learn its recipe. Click a selected radio again to stop
tracking it, or use Reset All Waypoints.
• Cooking ranks (button in the window, or /fchef ranks): your Cooking skill,
and how to reach each rank: Apprentice and Journeyman from any Cooking
trainer (every trainer of your faction listed; the one you pick stays marked
until you talk to them), Expert from the Expert Cookbook vendor, Artisan
through the Clamlette Surprise quest line, with requirements, costs and
waypoint buttons. Trainers you visit are listed with the ranks they teach.
• Faction aware. Sources your faction cannot use are hidden; a recipe only
the other faction can learn says so.
• Learns as you play. Opening a recipe vendor or a Cooking trainer (every
recipe it lists, even greyed out), looting a recipe, seeing a recipe as a
quest reward, or talking to a vendor, trainer or quest giver records where it
happened, which also turns Unknown recipes into confirmed ones. Recorded sources are shown first and can be shared
with /fchef export.
• Pop-up messages instead of chat spam: a small box above action bar 1
(Shift+drag its gold border to move it).
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /fchef | Open or close the Forever Chef window |
| /fchef ranks | Open the Cooking ranks window |
| /fchef status | How many recipes you know and how much has been recorded |
| /fchef export | Copyable text of what you found in game that the addon does not confirm yet |
| /fchef quiet | Turn the pop-up messages off or on |
| /fchef toast | Show a sample pop-up so you can move it |
| /fchef toast reset | Put the pop-up back above action bar 1 |
| /fchef debug | Print diagnostic messages in chat |
| /fchef reset | Erase recorded sources and NPC positions on this account |

addons.changelog:
WoW Pongv1.0.1 (2026-09-29)
Full Changelog Previous Releases
• Smooth network lag, send HITs promptly, faster paddles
• Predict a bounce off a remotely judged paddle and draw it at once; when
the real verdict arrives, the ball catches up along the real path and any
remaining offset fades out. Display only, behind the new
Smooth network lag option (on by default).
• MOVE-only batches leave one send token for the next HIT/MISS/SERVE: host
HITs reached the guest 0.6s late on average at 0.25s latency, now ~0.27s.
• Paddle speed 200 -> 270; bot reactions +0.12s to keep the same balance.
• tools/test\_smoothing.py.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Use actions/checkout v7 (Node 24) in the release workflow
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Package and upload to CurseForge on version tags
BigWigs packager workflow: a v* tag builds the WoWPong zip (addon folder
only) and uploads it to CurseForge project 1718303 and a GitHub release.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Note in the README that it's untested in-game
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Add README
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Add options menu, match length (first to 1/3/5/7) and rally counter
Options dialog (Display / Play / Social / General) with saved per-account
settings. Hosts pick the match length for their table (also used by
practice and Watch Bots); START, T and snapshots carry it, protocol
version 4. The board shows the live rally count and the longest rally
after a match, which stats keep vs players and per bot level.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Add gold betting with an honor ledger
Anyone at a table can post even-money offers on a seat; someone backing
the other seat takes them. Players may only back themselves, betting
closes at Play Now (unmatched offers void), and the host referees:
first take wins, seat changes void the round, the result settles
everyone's bets, and a host vanishing mid-match voids them. The host
can hand seat 1 to a bot to referee bot-vs-bot matches.
The addon can't move gold, so results go into a per-character ledger
(lobby Ledger view, /pong ledger, Settled buttons); trading with
someone you owe pre-fills the amount and completed trades update it.
Also: low-priority messages that waited 3s may use the last send token,
so the lobby's live score no longer freezes during a match. Protocol
version 3 (T carries matchNo).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Add minimap button, win/loss stats and invites
Step 5 of WoW Pong:
• Minimap button via bundled LibDBIcon (left-click tables, right-click
stats, record in the tooltip, /pong minimap) and an addon compartment
entry, with a generated icon.
• Per-character stats: record vs players (forfeits, streaks, points,
head-to-head by player id) and a separate record vs each bot level.
Lobby Stats panel and /pong stats.
• /pong invite [name] (or target) over the lobby channel with an
Accept/Decline popup; accepting seats the invitee at your table.
Also: table announcements, queries and keepalives now go through a
low-priority queue so they never delay match events, late paddle moves
still apply after a match ends, and fake clients seed math.random for
reproducible test runs (WOWPONG\_SEED).
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Let spectators join a match in progress
Step 4 of WoW Pong: a spectator arriving mid-match (or after it ended)
asks the host for a snapshot. The host answers at most every 2s with
one snapshot for everyone waiting; its unsent events are sealed into
numbered messages sent right before it, since the send budget is
always nearly spent mid-match. Spectators buffer match messages until
the snapshot arrives, skip what it already covers, retry, and fall
back to the next match if no snapshot comes.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5
• Add the lobby: table list with Sit/Watch, bot controls
Step 3 of WoW Pong: /pong opens a lobby listing tables heard on the
channel (host, players, open/ready/playing/finished with live score)…
addons.description:
1v1 Pong inside World of Warcraft, with spectators. Open a table, challenge a guildmate, and let anyone else watch. Click the board and your paddle glides toward the click at a fixed speed. The skill is predicting where the ball will end up.

Type /pong to open the lobby.

Made for World of Warcraft: Forever (Interface 16001).

> Early version: everything is covered by automated tests outside the game, but WoW Pong hasn't been played in-game yet. Expect rough edges, especially in matches between players. Bug reports are welcome in Issues.

How to play
• Click anywhere on the board and your paddle heads for that height. Everyone sees the same board: the table's host plays on the left, the challenger on the right.
• Where the ball meets your paddle sets its angle: the edges send it off at up to 60 degrees. The ball speeds up with every hit.
• Miss the ball and your opponent scores. First to 7 by default. The table's host can pick first to 1, 3, 5 or 7.
• Both players' target markers are shown, so you (and anyone watching) can see where each paddle is heading.
• Leaving, disconnecting or reloading during a match counts as a forfeit.
Features
• Lobby. See every open table with its players and live score. Sit down or watch with one click, or open your own table.
• Spectating. Watch any match, even one that's already underway. You catch up within a few seconds.
• Bots in three difficulties (Easy, Normal, Hard). Practice against one alone, watch two bots play, or add one to your table. The host can even put bots in both seats and let people watch or bet.
• Rally counter. The current rally is shown during play, and the longest rally when the match ends.
• Stats, per character: wins and losses against players (with forfeits, streaks, points and head-to-head records), your record against each bot difficulty, and your longest rallies.
• Invites. /pong invite (or your target) sends a challenge with Accept and Decline buttons.
• Gold bets. Players can post even-money bets on themselves and anyone at the table can take them. The addon can't move gold: it keeps an honor ledger of who owes whom and fills in the amount when you open a trade with that person.
• Minimap button and addon compartment entry. The tooltip shows your record.
• Quiet. Everything happens in the Pong window. The addon never posts results to chat and plays no sounds.
Options
Open the options with the lobby's Options button, with /pong options, by middle-clicking or shift-clicking the minimap button, or from the game's Settings > AddOns page.
• Display: window size and lock, paddle colors (blue vs red, me vs them, class colors, retro white), target markers, ball trail, hit flash, board darkness, center line.
• Play: bot difficulty, match length, hold the mouse button to steer, open the window when your match starts.
• Social: who can invite you (everyone, friends and guild, nobody), a chat notice when a table opens, hide tables running a different version, bets panel, trade fill-in.
• General: minimap button, reset window position, reset stats, restore defaults.

Options apply to every character on your account. Stats and the bet ledger are kept separately for each character.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /pong | Open the lobby (or close the window) |
| /pong practice [easy\|normal\|hard] | Play against a bot |
| /pong demo [level] [level] | Watch two bots play |
| /pong points 1\|3\|5\|7 | Match length for your table and practice |
| /pong host | Open a table (you take seat 1) |
| /pong join / /pong watch | Sit at someone's table, or watch it |
| /pong bot [level] | (Host) put a bot in seat 2 |
| /pong start / /pong leave | Play Now / leave the table |
| /pong invite [name] | Challenge someone (or your target) |
| /pong tables | List the tables you can see |
| /pong stats / /pong ledger | Your record / who owes whom from bets |
| /pong options | Open the options window |
| /pong minimap | Show or hide the minimap button |…

addons.description:
English | 简体中文

Forever AI combines a read-only game AddOn with a desktop chat Companion. Share a snapshot of your character, equipment and quests with AI to ask about drops, recipes or quest order, optionally adding a game screenshot.

Replies appear in the desktop chat window. Chatting with AI inside the game's chat channels is not currently supported. The desktop interface is in English; AI replies follow the language of your question.

This is a development prototype: Companion 0.4.3, AddOn 0.3.0. The AddOn uses TOC 16001 for the corresponding WoW: Forever client; compatibility with other retail, Classic or beta clients is not guaranteed.
Which download should I choose?
Windows 10 (2004+) / 11 x64: download ForeverAI-Setup-x64.exe. One setup wizard installs the desktop Companion and game AddOn. Python and the screenshot helper are included; no source download or compilation is needed.

1. Run ForeverAI-Setup-x64.exe and choose English or Simplified Chinese.
2. Keep the AddOn option selected and choose the Forever client folder containing Wow.exe or WowClassic.exe. Select the client you actually play, not the Battle.net launcher folder. You can skip the AddOn if you only want the Companion.
3. Finish installation and open Forever AI from the Start menu or desktop shortcut.
4. On the next full game launch, enable Forever AI | Snapshot in the AddOns list. Continue with Connect AI, then Ask your first question.

You still need your own model account or API key. The installer does not log in for you or restart the game. The installer is unsigned; Windows may show an unknown-publisher or reputation notice.

When updating the AddOn, setup preserves its previous folder in the client's Interface/ForeverAI-backups. Uninstalling the Companion leaves the game AddOn and these backups in place.

Other downloads are on the Releases page:

| Download | Use it for |
| --- | --- |

| ForeverAI-AddOn-*.zip | Game AddOn only; extract ForeverAI into the client's Interface/AddOns folder. |
| SHA256SUMS.txt | Checksums for the release downloads. |

macOS: a Mac installer is not included in this Windows release. Use the macOS source instructions below. GitHub's Code → Download ZIP and automatic Source code (zip / tar.gz) downloads are for source installation and development.
1. Install the game AddOn
The Windows installer can do this for you. These manual steps are for portable, AddOn-only and source downloads.

1. Locate the Forever client you actually launch, then open its Interface/AddOns directory. A folder name such as retail, classic or _classic_beta_ alone does not establish compatibility.

4. For a first installation, fully quit and restart the game. Enable Forever AI | Snapshot in the character selection screen's AddOns list. When updating an already loaded AddOn, you can usually run /reload manually instead.
5. Enter the game and type /fai while out of combat. The copy panel confirms that the AddOn loaded.

If the AddOn is missing, check the selected client version, installation path and all three files above. Starting the Companion itself does not install the AddOn.

addons.description:
Classic recipe colors for the WoW: Forever professions window. Every recipe name is colored by
how likely it is to raise your skill, the way the old trade skill window did, so you can see at a
glance what to craft next.

| Color | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Orange | Always a skill-up |
| Yellow | Usually a skill-up |
| Green | Sometimes a skill-up |
| Gray | No skill-up anymore |

Blizzard's skill-up arrows stay where they are; the color is added to the name next to them.
Unlearned and locked recipes keep Blizzard's own colors, the mouse-over highlight still turns a
name white, and guild or NPC crafting lists (which have no skill-ups) are left alone.

Under the selected recipe's name, Skill-Ups: 50 75 100 shows the skill levels where it turns
yellow, green and gray, each number in its color (hover it for the same in words). The numbers come
from the game's own data. Turn the line off in Options > AddOns > ColorCraft > Show Skill-Up Levels.

No slash commands. Install it and open a profession.
How it works
Each recipe row in Blizzard's professions list sets its name color when the row is built and when
the mouse leaves it. ColorCraft repaints the name right after both, through secure hooks, so
nothing of Blizzard's is replaced and the Craft button is never touched. The Skill-Ups line is
ColorCraft's own text under the recipe's name, added the same way.

The levels are in ColorCraftLevels.lua, made by tools/make_levels.py from WoW: Forever's
SkillLineAbility table: yellow and gray are in the table, green is halfway between.
Help and feedback
Questions, bugs and ideas: the ShamanPower Discord has a channel for every addon.
