The first release of the WoW Forever addons (interface 16001, the _classic_beta_ client).

| Addon | Version | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ICKit | 0.4.0 | The shared kit the others depend on: Forever theme, widgets, sliders, choices, scrolling lists, and a gallery (/ickit) |
| Stickies | 0.1.0 | Notes on the screen, with a minimap and Addon Compartment entry |
| RenderTuner | 0.3.0 | A panel with a live control for about 140 graphics console variables, upscaling and quality presets, search, undo, and a way back to your saved settings (/tuner) |
Install
Extract the zips you want into _classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns, then restart the client; a /reload does not pick up new addons. ICKit is required by Stickies and RenderTuner, so always take it too.
Know before you use it
• WoW Forever has no DLSS, DLAA, XeSS or FSR 2 and later. RenderTuner uses the FSR 1.0 render scale the client does have.
• Settings marked experimental in RenderTuner can crash the game. A warning appears the first time you open the panel. If the game will not start afterwards, delete _classic_beta_\WTF\Config.wtf.
• Headless tests pass (ICKit 40, Stickies 21, RenderTuner 29). RenderTuner 0.3.0's panel and Stickies' minimap click have not yet been confirmed in the real client; report anything odd as an issue.

Guides: ICKit, Stickies, RenderTuner.
addons.description:
World of Warcraft addons maintained for Impulse Control — that is what the ic- is —
organised by game flavor. They share one library, one palette and one heading in the
in-game AddOns list, so they read as one set rather than a pile of unrelated addons.

Each addon lives at AddonProjects/// and that folder is exactly what
ships: its .toc and Lua files, nothing else. Packaging zips that folder so the archive
extracts straight into Interface\AddOns.
Working on an addon
1. Link or copy the addon folder into the game client. scripts/deploy.ps1 creates a
directory junction so the game loads files straight from this repo:

2. Edit, then /reload in game. Check BugSack or the Errors folder for Lua errors.
Most addons also have their own checks: /maw test, /tm test, /gr test, /ictpl test.
3. Bump ## Version: in the .toc, the local VERSION load message where the addon has
one, and the row in AddonProjects//README.md. The linter checks all three.
4. Lint before packaging. There is no Lua on this machine, so this is what stands in for a
compiler:

5. Package for sharing with a guildmate:

The zip lands in dist/ (ignored by git) and carries ICLibs alongside the addon, so
one archive extracts into a working install.
Releasing to CurseForge
ICLibs is its own CurseForge project and the published addons each mark it as a Required
Dependency there, so an upload zip holds one folder and nothing else. One command builds
the whole set from main:

It lints, runs every addon's headless cases, and stops at the first failure. Then it
writes dist/curseforge/-.zip for ICLibs, MalexisAuctionWatcher,
TradeMaster, GuildRecruitment and MarkedForDeath, removing each addon's older zips, and a
MANIFEST.md with the version table, SHA-256 of every zip, and the recent commits per
addon to paste into the changelog box. Upload ICLibs first when it changed. -Addon narrows
the set, -OutDir points it somewhere else, -SkipTests skips the cases (lint still runs).
AuctionatorSellingTweaks, CutMaster and ICTemplate are not in the set on purpose.
Starting a new addon
Copy ICTemplate — a working addon whose window is a
live gallery of every shared widget beside the source that built it. The script does the
copy, the rename, the three registration rows and the lint run:

Docs/ICTemplate.md covers what to keep, what to throw away, and how to
do the rename by hand.
Branching
main is protected: no direct pushes, no force pushes, changes land only through a pull
request. Development happens on branches:
• feature/ for new work, fix/ for bug fixes. One addon or concern per branch.
• Commit early and often on the branch; push it so others can see it.
• When it is ready, open a PR (gh pr create fills in the template), run the in-game
checklist, then merge with a merge commit (gh pr merge --merge). Delete the branch
after merging. Commits are written to be read one at a time, so main keeps them:
a squash turns a branch's worth of separate, revertable changes into one entry that
says less than any of them did.
• Long-running addon work stays on its feature branch between releases, for example
feature/auction-watcher; rebase it on main after each merge.
Addons
| Flavor | Addon | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| anniversary | MalexisAuctionWatcher | Price tracking, history charts, recipe profit, Auctionator/TSM feeds. Guide: Docs/MalexisAuctionWatcher.md |
| anniversary | CutMaster | Jewelcrafting book scanning, trade chat/whisper customer detection, order tracking, income. Guide: Docs/CutMaster.md |
| anniversary | AuctionatorSellingTweaks | A confirm before posting far under the market, and an Expiry column in Auctionator's Selling price list. Guide: Docs/AuctionatorSellingTweaks.md |
| anniversary | TradeMaster | Crafting business assistant for any profession, generalised from CutMaster. Guide: Docs/TradeMaster.md |…

addons.changelog:
Changelog
All notable changes to GuildForge are listed here.
[1.0.5] - 2026-11-04Fixed
• Dropping a profession now clears it. If someone unlearns a profession, its recipes and cooldowns are removed for them and for the whole guild, so they no longer show up as a crafter of something they can't make. Guildmates who were offline catch up the next time they and that player are online together.
• Profession and skill changes made less than 15 seconds after the last update were never shared until the next login. They're now sent as soon as the 15 seconds are up.
• A profession update that lost part of itself on the way could make guildmates think a profession was dropped. Incomplete updates are now ignored.
[1.0.4] - 2026-11-03Fixed
• Profession ranks from trainers (like Apprentice Cook and Journeyman Cook) showed up in Not known in guild as if they were recipes. They're no longer saved or shared, and ones already saved are cleared.
Changed
• Not known in guild is now a simple list: each recipe shows its icon, name and the skill it needs. Nobody in the guild knows these yet, so there were never reagents to show, and the list no longer does the extra work of checking your bags for them.
[1.0.3] - 2026-11-02Fixed
• Nothing was being shared on Classic Era. A check meant to pause messages while WoW Forever blocks addon chat misread Classic's answer, so every message waited forever. Messages now only wait in instances or combat, when the game really says chat is blocked. /gf status shows whether sending is being held.
• Guildmates' data never arrived on realms whose names contain an apostrophe or other punctuation (like Nek'Rosh): every guild message was rejected as coming from the wrong sender.
[1.0.2] - 2026-11-02Changed
• The window title now just says GuildForge; the version number moved to the bottom of the Settings panel.
[1.0.1] - 2026-11-02Changed
• Re-release of 1.0.0 with no changes to the addon.
[1.0.0] - 2026-11-02
First release. Your guild's professions, all in one place. GuildForge shares every member's professions and known recipes over hidden guild addon messages, so you can see who can craft what, what it takes, and whether you already have the mats, without spamming guild chat.

Built for WoW Forever, and also works on Classic Era.
Features
• Every profession at a glance. Spellbook-style tabs with crafter counts, recipe counts and the top crafter for each profession.
• Crafters, ranked and live. Skill bars by rank, green dots for who's online, and when offline crafters were last seen.
• Recipes with reagents. Icons, item quality, who can craft it, and whether you have the mats in your bags (plus your bank).
• Ask a crafter. One click whispers the best online crafter with the item link and the mats you already have.
• Shopping list. Queue recipes and get one combined materials list, with "need 4 more" on item tooltips everywhere, including the auction house.
• Item tooltips. See which guildmates craft an item and which recipes use it.
• Cooldowns. Mooncloth, transmutes and the Salt Shaker are tracked and shared with the guild.
• Not known in guild. Recipes seen at trainers that nobody in the guild has learned yet, filled in by everyone's trainer visits.
• Search everything: recipes, crafters, professions and reagents, plus a Have mats filter.
• Light on guild chat. One short summary per player when you log in; only data that changed is downloaded. Built to handle large guilds.
• WoW Forever ready. Supports first and last names, holds messages while the game blocks addon chat (like combat in instances), and appears in Esc → Options → AddOns.
• Settings: minimap button, item tooltips, sync on login, quiet mode, window scale, re-share your recipes, and Clear my data to download everything fresh.
Getting started
1. Click the GF minimap button or type /gf.
2. Open each of your professions once so GuildForge can share your recipes.
3. Visit trainers to fill in Not known in guild.…
addons.description:
Your guild's professions, all in one place. GuildForge shares every member's profession skills and known recipes over guild addon chat, so you can see who can craft what, what it takes to make it, and whether you already have the mats — without spamming guild chat.

Built for WoW Forever, and also works on Classic Era.
FeaturesEvery profession at a glance
The All tab lists each profession with how many guildmates have it, how many recipes are shared, and the top crafter. Profession tabs run down the right side of the window, spellbook style, with their icons — professions nobody in the guild has yet are greyed out.
Crafters, ranked and live
Open a profession to see every guildmate who has it, ranked by skill with a color-coded bar (Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, Artisan). A green dot means they're online right now; offline crafters show when they were last seen. Click a crafter to show only their recipes.
Recipes with reagents and your mat counts
Every known recipe shows its icon, item-quality color, who can craft it, and whether you have the mats in your bags (Mats ready x17, Missing mats). Expand a recipe to see each reagent with what you have against what's needed, plus anything sitting in your bank.
• Ask a crafter — one click whispers the best online crafter with the item link and the mats you already have.
• Add to list — queue it on your shopping list.
• Shift-click any recipe or reagent to link it in chat; hover for the full item tooltip.
Shopping list
Collect the recipes you plan to make and GuildForge combines them into one list of materials, showing what you've gathered and how many more you need. The same "need 4 more" note appears on item tooltips everywhere — bags, vendors and the auction house.
And more
• Search recipes, crafters, professions and reagents (try "linen") across the whole guild, plus a Have mats filter for things you can craft right now.
• Item tooltips show which guildmates craft an item and which recipes use it.
• Cooldowns — Mooncloth, transmutes and the Salt Shaker are tracked and shared, so the guild can see who's ready.
• Not known in guild — recipes seen at trainers that nobody in the guild has learned yet, with the skill they require. Anyone's trainer visits fill in the list for the whole guild.
• Minimap button — a "GF" bubble with a badge counting guildmates online with GuildForge. Left-click to open, right-click to sync, drag to move.
• Light on guild chat — syncs send a short fingerprint of each recipe list, and guildmates only download lists that changed.
Settings
Click the gear next to Sync Guild to toggle the minimap button, item tooltips, syncing on login and quiet mode, adjust the window scale, or re-share all of your recipes. If your data ever looks wrong, Clear my data forgets everything you've received from guildmates (keeping your own professions) and downloads it fresh.

addons.description:
Animated emotes, a searchable visual browser, and chat completion for WoW Forever
(Camelot, interface 16001).
In game
Open the window with /te, /twitch, or the minimap button. Browse channel groups,
search by name, save favorites, or revisit recently sent emotes. Each Twitch channel
has one group; provider-wide emotes appear under General. General, Graycen,
Forsen, Erobb221, xQc, and Asmongold start enabled. There is no automatic first-run
setup. Use Channels or Settings > Choose channels to change the selection.
Browse and search any installed channel, including disabled ones. Its **Enabled in
chat** checkbox controls display without leaving Browse. Enabled channels have a
purple highlight and checkmark in the group list.

Click an emote to insert its plain name into chat. Type a colon followed by a name
to see suggestions with emote image previews; use Tab or the arrow keys to select, Enter to accept, and Escape
to dismiss. Hover over a chat emote for its name and source; Shift-click to insert it.
The addon sends ordinary text, so other players do not need it to read your messages.

Click an emote in chat for its menu, then choose Hide this emote to display that
name as ordinary text across channels and remove it from autocomplete.
Restore individual names under Browse > Hidden
or Settings > Hidden emotes. Shift-click still inserts a name into your draft.
Every Twitch global text face (:), :-P, :/, <3, O_o, B) and the rest), D:, and the
chat words 1G, BOP, Retail, and Classic start hidden. Restoring one overrides that default.

The purple and charcoal window includes a channel sidebar and a channel picker.
Additional channels can be enabled individually. When names overlap,
Settings lets you choose a preferred channel for the image. Identical provider
artwork shares a single texture file across packs.

Settings include an emote-size slider with a live preview (12–40 pixels, 28 by default),
chat channels, enabled groups, animation, the playback
limit (15, 30, or 60 FPS; 60 by default), and minimap visibility. Drag the minimap button to move it.
Animation follows each source's timing; the playback limit cannot add motion absent
from the source. A hovered chat line pauses its animation to keep the tooltip stable;
other visible lines keep animating. Editor completion and insertion pause when WoW restricts scripted
chat input.

Full Changelog Previous Releases
• 0.3.1: restore settings from the macro when its body has trailing whitespace
addons.description:
A hunter range indicator for WoW: Forever. One small bar that tells you, for your
current target, which of four places you are standing in:

| Bar | Meaning |
|---|---|
| IN RANGE (green) | 8 to 35 yards. Auto Shot works. |
| DEAD ZONE (red) | Too close to shoot, and melee is not landing. You can do neither: move. |
| MELEE (blue) | Your melee swings are landing. |
| TOO FAR (grey) | Past 35 yards. |

It also shows a distance bracket, such as IN RANGE 8-28 yd.

Forever uses the vanilla hunter rule: Auto Shot has a minimum range of 8 yards as well
as a maximum of 35, and melee reaches about 5. The few yards in between are the dead zone.
Nothing in the default UI tells you that you are standing in it.

Hunters only. On any other class the addon does nothing at all.
Commands
/dz or /deadzone

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| /dz unlock / /dz lock | Drag the bar where you want it |
| /dz scale 2 | Size, 0.5 to 4 (default 1.5) |
| /dz distance | Show or hide the distance bracket |
| /dz sound | A warning sound when you enter the dead zone (off by default) |
| /dz always | Show the bar even with no target |
| /dz keep on / off | Keep your settings in a macro (see below) |
| /dz reset | Default position and size |
| /dz probe | Show which range checks the client answers for your target |
Your settings and the beta client
The Forever beta client currently saves addon settings to disk but does not load them again,
so every addon starts from its defaults each time the game restarts. That is a Blizzard bug,
and it affects this bar's position and size like anything else.

Macros are stored with your account and do come back. /dz keep on copies this addon's few
settings into one general macro and reads it at login. It is opt-in because it uses one of
your macro slots; /dz keep off removes it. If Blizzard fixes the client, your normally
saved settings take priority and the macro is simply ignored.
How it works, and what it cannot do
Everything here was measured on the beta client (build 1.60.1.69913), in and out of combat.
• Can I shoot? comes from the game's own range check on Auto Shot. On this client that
answer stays readable in combat.
• Too close or too far? When Auto Shot says no, the 28 yard "follow" check says which.
• Melee or dead zone? This is the hard part. Nothing an addon can ask separates the
first 8 yards: melee abilities report "in range" at any distance, and Forever's new
swing-timer range function does not answer addons. So the addon watches the game's event
for each of your auto attacks. A main-hand swing in the last swing-and-a-bit means melee
is landing, and the bar shows MELEE. The catch: when something first reaches you, the
bar reads DEAD ZONE until your first swing lands, about one swing later. It errs on the
side of the warning.
• Distance is a bracket, not a number. The game does not tell addons how far away an
enemy is. It will only answer "is the target within N yards?" for a handful of values of
N, so the bar shows the gap between the nearest "no" and the nearest "yes". How tight that
is depends on how many of those checks this client answers; /dz probe lists them.

No libraries, no dependencies, no combat log. It polls ten times a second, and only does any
work while you have an attackable target.

addons.description:
A World of Warcraft addon for Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, and WoW: Forever that provides a comprehensive and feature-packed interface used for summoning entire raids or parties. Born from a need to organize summon requests and raid members running to the instance portal on my summoning alt, I created an addon so powerful that it's the only addon you need as a level 20 warlock when it comes to summoning.
Features
• List of all characters in the current raid group
• List of summon requests (in chronological order received) in a side panel to the main summoning interface
• Option to play a sound when someone is added to the list
• Left click to target the character, right click to summon
• Holding shift while right clicking turns on "silent mode" where it does the summon, but doesn't send out messages
• Customizable list of keywords automatically add people to the list of summon requests
• Starts off with anything containing "123", " 123", or " 123 ", can be expanded manually if a person's message didn't work
• Copy EasySummon's UI for the keyword list: a scrollable list of words with an input field and "Add" button above the list
• When a person is added to the list, play a sound
• After 2 minutes of being on the list, the character is automatically removed from the list
• This needs to persist through "/reload"
• Can remove a player's name from the list manually without broadcasting their name
• Maybe by middle clicking their name on the list? Maybe a small "X" button to the right of their name?
• Automatically send a message in /raid to let everyone know you're summoning a character, and to help click
• Message can be customized
• Default message: "Summoning [[character_name]], please help click!"
• Option to automatically whisper the target of the summon that a summon is coming
• Message can be customized
• Default message: "Summons incoming. Be ready to accept it. If you don't receive it within 30 seconds, let me know!"
• Disabled by default
• (Optional) When you click the button to summon someone, it first checks for 300+ mana; if you don't have at least 300 mana, it will prevent the summon (and messages) from going out, and alert you to the need for mana
• This might be accomplished by waiting for the cast to start, and if it doesn't start after 1 second, alert the user to low mana
• (Optional) When you begin casting summon, gets number of shards in your bags. After the cast, if the number didn't go down by one, alerts you to a failed summon
• Might be better accomplished by checking for SPELLCAST_FAILED
• (Optional) Shares summon request list with others in your raid that also have the addon
• Whenever you join a group, automatically request the updated list from others in the raid/party
• Removes characters from the shared list the instant you click on the button
Minimap Button
Left-clicking toggles the addon's summoning interface.

Right-clicking brings up a menu that allows you to select from the following options:
• Show summoning interface
• Hide minimap button
Slash commands
or - Opens addon's summoning interface
• Toggles minimap button visibility

Current hardening release: see HARDENING.md for confirmed fixes, validation and in-game checks. Download the rebuilt addon from dist/.

WoW Forever implementation of VoidMark. Version 1.1.0 ports the Classic Era changes through f6e6218, preserving the working Forever client adapters, complete character identities and existing saved data. Classic Era remains a read-only functionality reference.
Version 1.1.0
• Settings wheel: Distract Alert warns locally when an observed hostile player casts Distract. Readable visible-unit spell events work without combat-log access; readable combat-log casts also work. Duplicate observations share a three-second cooldown. Distract is ground-targeted, so the warning says it was used without claiming you were affected. The alert has its own module to avoid GankTracker's Lua 5.1 local-variable limit.
• Settings wheel: KOS Alert controls WHO sightings delivered by VoidLink (VMKOS1 or VoidMarkKOS_OnWhoResult). Banners combine names/classes and remain visible for ten seconds. Group matches can be shared; guild requester-only results stay private. Reasons are shared only when explicitly enabled. Complete Forever names are required; a matching primary name alone is insufficient. /vmkos shows options; on/off, share on/off, reasons on/off, sound on/off, and cooldown 30..1800 configure them.
• Kill Effects now separates normal 1–2 kill sounds from 3+ multi-kill sounds. Feign cancels only that victim's recent sound, using GUIDs or complete names. Sounds resolve from the installed VoidMarkForever folder.
• Damage Records has a POPUP switch. Hiding banners keeps recording and the existing chat announcements active.
• Enemy Moves uses LOW strata so stock bags and panels cover it. The separate options window keeps its dialog layer.
• Ride or Die retains blocked swaps and checks actual equipment after dismount/Sap recovery before reporting success.
• Gank Repository clears legacy automatic peer links once without changing history. Pairing requires PAIR on both clients within 14 seconds, then SYNC NOW for history reconciliation. Login/reload clears live session links; repeat manual pairing when needed. Background friend discovery and unsolicited pairing are disabled. KOS party sharing operates separately.
• Carries the PvP assist-credit constant and diagnostic locale fixes. GitHub Actions runs the Forever Lua 5.1 regressions on pushes and pull requests.

addons.description:
A grab-bag of quality-of-life (and silly) things for World of Warcraft. Tell your group a terrible joke, keep spirits up after a wipe, and dig into your talent data without leaving the game.

FeaturesJokes
• Type /tqol joke to tell a joke in your group's chat: raid, instance, or party, whichever fits. Nothing is sent when you're not in a group.
• Ships with over 450 jokes, from groan-worthy puns to a few written just for WoW players.
• Wipe jokes: after a boss wipe, tells your group a joke to lighten the mood. Turn them on in the Jokes Configuration page, and choose which content they play in: open world, each dungeon and raid difficulty, Mythic+, delves, scenarios, battlegrounds, and arenas.
• By default, jokes don't repeat until every joke on your list has been told, even across sessions. Uncheck it in Configuration for pure random picks.
Joke Editor
• Edit your joke list in game: add your own, fix the ones you don't like, and delete the ones that don't land.
• One joke per line, with line numbers and a highlight on the line you're editing.
• Reset to Defaults brings back the original list at any time.
• If you never customize your list, you get new jokes automatically as they're added in updates.
General
• Ready check response: when you answer "ready" to a ready check, sends a message to the channel you pick: say (the default), yell, raid, raid warning, party, or emote. "Yes chef!" by default, or type your own. Turn it on in the General page.
Talents
A sortable table of every talent in your active loadout, built for addon and WeakAura authors, theorycrafters, and the curious.
• Shows each talent's name, spell ID, entry ID, node ID, definition ID, icon ID, tree ID, ranks, and whether it's active.
• On Classic Era and The Burning Crusade Classic, lists every talent in your three talent trees instead: name, spell ID (of the rank you've learned), talent ID, tree, tab and index, icon ID, ranks, and whether it's learned.
• Click a column header to sort by it.
• Hover a row for the spell tooltip, or shift-click to link the spell in chat.
• Export the whole table as tab-separated text, ready to paste into a spreadsheet.
• Updates automatically when you change talents or specialization.
News
A popup shows what's new whenever a new version is released. You can turn it off, and reopen it any time with /tqol news.
Commands
| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| /tqol | Opens or closes the Twintop QOL window |
| /tqol joke | Tells a joke in group chat |
| /tqol jokes | Opens the Joke Editor |
| /tqol talents (or /tqol df) | Opens the Talents table |
| /tqol news | Opens the News window |
| /tqol help | Lists all commands in chat |

/twintopqol works anywhere /tqol does.
Feedback
Found a bug or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub.

About this fork
BlessingBuddy was created by Tom Steglitz. This repository is a personal fork, and the original work remains credited to Tom Steglitz under the MIT license (see LICENSE). I made the changes in this fork for my own use. This fork adds optional visibility settings and Blessing of Salvation for yourself and group members.

I do not plan to distribute this fork on CurseForge unless the original addon is confirmed abandoned. The current automated release workflow still uploads tagged releases to CurseForge, so the workflow must be changed before that intention is reflected in future releases. addons.description:
Quality of life, levelling tools and one-click character setup for WoW: Forever, in one addon. A new character gets your action bars, macros, key bindings and interface in one click; your trainer, vendors, bank and mailbox can be handled for you by rules you set; and the screen gets the bars and notes you ask for and nothing else.

Nothing acts for you until you turn it on. Installing Headstart does not touch your action bars, macros, key bindings, Edit Mode layout, chat windows or game settings, and it buys, moves, accepts and picks nothing. Its first login shows a small card - set up this character, show me around, or later - and turns nothing on; everything that spends gold, moves items or answers for you starts off, and says what it does before you switch it on. The one thing it does unasked is skip a cinematic, which on a new character is the opening flight over its zone: it says so in chat, and Skip intro cinematic is a switch (hold Shift as you enter the world to watch).

And you can always go back. Put back everything (General page, or /headstart putback) asks first, then puts your bars, macros, key bindings, game settings, Edit Mode layout and chat windows back as they were before Headstart first changed them, and turns its quality-of-life features and Character setup off.

Headstart does not come with levelling routes: you make your own from your runs, or paste in one someone shared.
Getting started
• /headstart (or the minimap button) opens the window. It has four tabs: QoL, Interface, Routes and Character setup. /hs goes straight to the settings.
• The first login shows a small card, not the whole window: Set up this character turns Character setup on and opens it (plan this class's bars, or save a character's bars, keys and interface for the others), Show me around opens the window with a short tour - a hint at a time points at where things are: the search, All features, the Automation group (everything that spends gold, moves items or answers for you), General, the Interface tab, Character setup - and Later closes it. None of it turns anything on. The Tour button or /headstart start brings the tour back.
• The settings can be searched, and every feature is one card with its switch in its head; a feature made of several choices keeps them while it is off. On All features the groups fold away.
New characters and your interface
• Character setup. Save your bars once per class, as a profile, and put them on every new character of that class in one click - or by themselves at its first login, a little at a time so nothing stutters: class spells up to a level, racials, professions, your own macros, items. Spells you haven't learned yet get a place that fills in as you train them.
• Your interface, once for the account. Edit Mode layout, which action bars show, chat windows, game settings, camera distance, key bindings, and graphics and sound, saved from one character and applied to the next - on another install too.
• Profiles. Several bar layouts per class under names of your own (Tank, DPS), switched from the window, the minimap button, a key or /headstart profile Tank.
• A planner to lay out a whole class's bars on a level 1 character, on your real action bars, with no main to copy from.
• A macro helper that makes your class's usual macros by ticking boxes.
• A RestedXP guide from the first login. Each race starts on a guide you pick, or RestedXP's own free starter: for a character at level 5 or below, with "RestedXP guide for a new character" on.
• Safe on a character you already play. It asks first and says what would go. Your bars and macros are written down before every change: /ysetup undo steps back one change at a time, and /ysetup undo first puts the bars back as they were before Headstart touched the character. Bars only leaves your interface alone. Chat windows and the Edit Mode layout are the two things an addon cannot put back, and the dialogs say so.…

and a browser for every quest in the game. It works on its own; sharing data with the PandaQuest
site is optional and off by default.

The site is : quest guides, NPCs, maps, flights and more, built from
Questie's data and from what players share.

This file covers the addon in short and then the repository. The full player guide (every
setting, slash command and FAQ) is PandaQuest/README.md.

addons.description:
贝尔工具箱 · Quality-of-life extensions for EllesmereUI on WoW Forever.

Author: Bel · License: MIT · Current version: 0.19.22

消耗品条：在 EUI → 贝尔工具箱 → 消耗品条开启（默认关闭）。鼠标移入展开，左键使用，展开项右键设为当前选项；支持食物、饮水、红药、蓝药、治疗石、法力宝石、绷带、合剂、药剂、抗性药水。空类别保留灰色按钮以保持位置稳定。未知或增益食物需手动指定，已知普通食物与魔法制造食物可自动选择。战斗中不根据背包变化自动切换物品，脱战后更新。位置使用 EUI 解锁模式；按键使用 EUI 快速键位绑定模式（/kb），并在原窗口保存或取消。

可开启“隐藏空类别”，设置每行按钮个数、按钮间距和类别顺序。达到设定个数后自动换行。按钮大小支持 18–64，间距为 0 时图标直接相接。开启 /kb 时空类别临时显示，便于绑定按键。鼠标移入自动展开同类物品，展开方向根据屏幕剩余空间自动选择；左键使用单个物品，右键设为当前选项，点击“自动”清除指定并恢复自动选择。展开项在战斗中也可通过安全按钮使用／指定，新增或耗尽物品在脱战后更新。类别勾选和排序使用 EUI 的可拖拽下拉设置。带增益的杂味炖肉等食物需手动指定。合剂、药剂和抗性药水也需手动指定默认项，避免自动选错职业效果或抗性类型；“自动”会清除这三类的指定。新类别追加在既有顺序之后，默认每行仍为 7 个，可在设置中调整。
Features
• Consumables bar: ten categories with secure hover flyouts, per-character choices, item counts and cooldowns, EUI drag ordering, adaptive expansion, configurable size/spacing/wrapping, and Quick Keybind Mode (/kb). Off by default.
• Mage Bar: teleport/portal flyouts, mana gems, conjure food and water, rank-specific casting and remembered spell selection. EUI drag ordering and visibility, automatic or manual expansion direction, 18–64 button sizes, 0–16 spacing and configurable buttons per row. Supports EUI Unlock Mode.
• Merchant assistant: Shift-click bulk purchases, a four-column merchant layout and learned-recipe markers. When EUI Bulk Buy is enabled, reuse its window with individual quantities for ordinary gold items; otherwise use the toolbox window.
• Bags and mail: offline inventory/bank snapshots, character-colored item counts, mail recipient shortcuts, favorites and recent contacts.
• Bag shortcuts: optional automatic weapon buff targeting and Mage comprehension-scroll shortcuts outside combat.
• Tooltips: item/spell title icons, AFK/DND status beside player names, class/reaction/quality borders and configurable text colors.
• Profession helper: estimated recipe-list profit and return percentage using installed Auctionator, TradeSkillMaster or CraftProfit price APIs; preserves skill-up arrows and supports difficulty-colored recipe names.
• Chat: configurable channel shortcuts, original micro-menu artwork, and an EUI chat-copy window with dragging, resizing, name/text search, channel colors and class-colored player names.
• Ship/zeppelin timers: countdowns below EUI world-map transport icons and, when installed, OpenMap's native dock icons. Labels follow each map's icon visibility and use the same built-in schedules and recorded-track calibration while standing aboard. Disabled by default.
• Interface utilities: quick focus with optional control marker, map resize handle, EUI window-movement integration, animated resting indicator, native quest-object sparkles and compact raid-tool extensions.

releases.changelog:
Bel Toolbox 0.19.22
• Added countdowns below OpenMap's native boat, zeppelin and airship dock icons, including the routes to Zephras Isle. Labels follow icon visibility and reuse existing schedules and calibration.
• Added separate EUI/OpenMap display switches in a native settings cog beside the transport timer master switch. OpenMap-only mode does not automatically enable EUI map markers; timers remain off by default.
• Fixed micro-menu icons for newer EUI versions using boolean style caches. Legacy rs selections migrate to EUI's supported Custom style, and Blizzard textures, atlases and portraits retain their native behavior.
• Added an optional player-class color setting in the Bel Toolbox icons cog. Turning it off restores EUI's current icon color.
• The Chat Bar Dungeon Journal button can open DungeonsForever or NeedRoll, selected in its settings cog. Right-click still opens loot history, and hover text follows the selected addon.

Bel Toolbox 0.19.16
• Added text, color-block and color-block-with-label styles for the chat bar, with configurable block width and spacing. Existing settings retain text mode by default.
• Added native EUI color-setting cogs for each chat button: independent block and font colors, immediate preview and restore defaults. Default colors follow channel settings without changing chat itself.
• Added centered, left and right main-bar growth for Mage and Consumables bars, independently of flyout expansion. Incomplete rows align to the selected direction.
• Added hover-only layout controls inside native EUI movers for button size, spacing, buttons per row and growth. Each link opens its corresponding setting; narrow movers show one combined Bar settings entry.
• Improved mover identification, control placement and rendering layers. Fixed clicked links becoming faded after closing settings popups.
• Unlock edits support Save/Discard and hide during combat. Added /belbareditdebug for in-game diagnostics.

Bel Toolbox 0.19.7
• Added Mage Bar category visibility and drag sorting, buttons per row, 18–64 button sizes and 0–16 spacing. Zero spacing removes icon gaps.
• Added automatic Mage flyout direction based on available screen space while preserving manual direction, legacy settings and remembered spell ranks.
• Improved Mage and consumable flyout tooltip placement to avoid covering expanded buttons; aligned consumable arrows with the actual expansion edge.
• Improved Mage Bar stability when changing spacing or categories: reuse cached spells for layout updates, preserve temporarily unavailable icons, position the root before its buttons and repair unresolved button coordinates with one deferred check.
• Layout and spell changes requested during combat are applied after combat ends. Expanded /belmagedebug diagnostics with button geometry and anchors.

Bel Toolbox 0.19.3
• Added an optional consumables bar for food, drink, healing potions, mana potions, healthstones, mana gems, bandages, flasks, elixirs and resistance potions. Enable it under EUI > Bel Toolbox > Consumables.
• Hover a category to expand its items. Left-click an expanded item to use it without changing the default; right-click to make it the default. Click Auto to clear the manual choice. Defaults are remembered per character.
• Flyouts automatically choose their direction using available screen space. Existing choices can be used or selected through secure buttons during combat; inventory-driven replacements wait until combat ends.
• Added EUI Quick Keybind Mode (/kb) support for category buttons, including keyboard, mouse side buttons and wheel bindings. Save or cancel using EUI's original binding window.
• Added EUI Unlock Mode positioning and native drag-reorder category controls, optional empty-category hiding, buttons per row with wrapping, 18–64 button sizes and adjustable spacing. Zero spacing now removes the icon inset as well.
• Improved cooked-food recognition, including Westfall Stew (733). Buff/unknown food, flasks, elixirs and resistance potions require manual selection to avoid choosing an unwanted effect.
• Preserved the seven-button default row width and existing saved category order. Empty categories temporarily appear in /kb for binding.
• Avoided repeated item-data requests for already-cached items above the player's level. Counts and cooldowns update through events rather than continuous polling.

Bel Toolbox 0.18.9
• Fixed quest-object sparkles on clients with normal or raid outlines enabled. Save and restore all relevant settings, reapply after graphics changes, and defer changes during combat.
• Added a persistent notice beside the setting: after disabling, fully exit and relaunch the game to clear existing sparkles; /reload is not enough. Enabling and the full-restart requirement have been confirmed in game.
• Added automatic releases when a stable version is merged into main. GitHub and CurseForge receive the same addon ZIP and current-version Markdown changelog; EUI is declared a required CF dependency.
• Added release validation, ZIP checksums and upload receipts to support recovery without duplicate CF uploads. Herb/ore sparkle effects are not included.

addons.description:
> 📸 A screenshot is taken only when you (or your pet) land the killing blow. If someone else finishes the enemy off, there's no screenshot. You can change this in the settings: turn off Only my killing blows.

Never lose a world PvP highlight again. HonorSnap takes a screenshot every time you get an honorable kill in the open world: ganks at the Crossroads, Tarren Mill vs Southshore, or someone who tried to stop you in Stranglethorn.
What it does
• 📸 Automatic screenshot on every honorable kill.
• 🟢 Honorable kills only. The game only gives honor for enemies that are not gray to you (green, yellow, orange or red level), so killing low-level players gives no screenshot.
• ⚔️ Real kills only. A screenshot needs actual honorable-kill credit from the game, so duels never count. HonorSnap also stays silent during a duel and for a few seconds after it ends.
• 🌍 Open world only. Battlegrounds, arenas, world battlefields during an active battle (Wintergrasp, Tol Barad), dungeons, raids and scenarios are ignored, so your Warsong Gulch games won't fill up the Screenshots folder.
• 🗡️ "Only my killing blows" option, on by default: a screenshot is taken only when you or your pet landed the killing blow. Turn it off to count any honorable kill, including group kills.
• 🙈 Hide the interface on screenshots (off by default). The interface disappears for a split second while the picture is taken; nameplates and names above heads stay visible.
• 😂 Emote after a kill: pick one of 21 emotes (laugh, roar, chicken, spit, salute, train…) and your character performs it at the victim right away, so the enemy sees it before releasing their spirit. Only emotes from the list can be used.
• ⏱️ Adjustable delay (0 to 3 seconds) so the corpse hits the ground before the picture is taken.
• 🔊 Optional camera shutter sound, off by default. It's replaced by the emote when one is selected.
• 💬 Chat messages (each off by default, only you see them, player names in class colors):
• My kills: "You killed Thrall." Also tells you about kills that gave no honor, with the pet's name if your pet landed the blow.
• Group kills: "Jaina killed Thrall." when someone in your group lands the killing blow.
• My deaths: "You were killed by Thrall — Fireball."
• 🔢 Screenshot counter with the date and time it started counting.
• ♻️ Reset buttons in the options: clear the screenshot counter or restore all settings to defaults (asks for confirmation first, saved screenshots are never deleted).
• ⚙️ Easy on/off: a checkbox in the options, a slash command, or a click in the retail Addon Compartment (minimap addon menu).
• 🌐 English, Ukrainian and Russian interface. By default the language follows your game client (Russian on Russian clients, English everywhere else) and can be switched in the options. Kill detection doesn't depend on the client language.

L'addon de la guilde WaR LegenD pour World of Warcraft Forever

Raid, butin, guilde et champs de bataille dans une seule fenêtre : /wl.

Contenu · Installation · Commandes · Nouveautés · Documentation complète

Contenu
La fenêtre a quatre onglets, chacun avec toutes ses sections visibles.

| Onglet | Section | Ce qu'on y trouve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raid | Organisation | Groupes de raid (presets : groupes et marques posés d'un clic), invitations, promotion auto, liste de summon, barre de marques. |
| | Préparation | Ready check et rappel des talents, checklist des consommables, assignation des buffs, préparation des raiders, inspection du raid. |
| | Combat | CD de raid, suivi d'auras, qui a pull, DoesItDie (tes DoT suffiront-ils à achever la cible) et journal de combat automatique. |
| | Butin et présences | Loot Council (vote, soft-res, nombre de loots reçus), présences, tableau de bord de la guilde, recrues en essai. |
| JcJ | Champs de bataille | Cadres ennemis et alliés (dissipations, contrôles), minuteurs de capture et de cimetière, historique et records des premades. |
| | Monde ouvert | Alerte danger, compte à rebours des duels, layers de la guilde. |
| Guilde | Membres | Métiers, recrutement et inactifs, la guilde par classe, carte de la guilde et transports, compagnons de leveling, classement JcJ Minotaure. |
| | Mes personnages | Rerolls, stock des persos banque, export pour simulateurs (SimulationCraft, MythicSim, OXM). |
| Options | Addon | Réglages (modules, profil, taille de la fenêtre), version, erreurs Lua, temps de chargement. |
| | Interface | Déplacer les fenêtres, options cachées du jeu, niveaux d'objet, outils de la carte. |
| | Petits automatismes | Qualité de vie, focus et alerte de contrôle, minuteurs, améliorations dans les sacs, tri du butin, objectif d'or, Myslot. |

> [!TIP]
> Un outil dont tu ne te sers pas s'éteint dans Options > Réglages > Modules : éteint, il ne fait plus rien.
> La case « Rechercher une option... » en haut de la fenêtre trouve n'importe quel réglage.

addons.description:
Wanted: Dead or... Dead
> Under heavy development through the WoW Forever beta. Expect frequent updates, and possible issues
> while we work through the game's changes.

> Found a problem? Press Report a bug at the foot of the addon's menu (or type /wanted bug): it sends your
> report to the developers through the Wanted app. Have an idea? Suggest a feature above it (or /wanted idea)
> sends it the same way.

The world PvP war on WoW Forever, as it's fought. Which side holds each zone this week, the battles
going on right now, who won the last one, and the price on every ganker's head. Counted from deaths other
players saw.

Every copy of the addon records the world PvP it sees and shares it with the others on your faction. The
free desktop app sends it to wanteddeadordead.com, where the whole server's
fighting becomes a war you can follow. In game, the addon runs the bounty board and keeps you aware of who
is around and who is on you.
The war, on wanteddeadordead.com
• Battle reports for every fight: who died, who killed, the top killers, healers and damage, the
guilds, the biggest moments, and a written report of how it went. Every name links to that player's or
guild's page.
• The front line. In contested zones like Hillsbrad, the site tracks where the fighting is between the
two bases every five minutes and draws it as a tug of war.
• Rounds and victories. Hold the enemy at their doorstep for 20 minutes and your side wins a round; the
side with more rounds wins the battle. Fights are sized as skirmishes, battles and major battles.
• Front-page news. The week's major battle leads the home page, with the latest victories under it and a
live ticker of the fighting going on now.
• The war this week. Which side holds each zone, with heat maps of where players die.
• Leaderboards for killing blows, streaks and multi-kills, healers, damage, guilds and Notoriety, a
season rank from Greenhorn to Legend.
• Only what someone else saw counts. A kill ranks once another player's records back it up, so nobody
can pad their numbers from one computer.

The addon works on its own. The app is optional: it puts your fights on the site and fills in the war.
In game
Bounty board
• Post a bounty on an enemy player, or on a whole guild (the first kill of any one member claims it). One per target; posting again adds
to it.
• Bounty hunters mark a bounty they're chasing, for a day at a time (renew to keep going). While anyone is
hunting it, the poster can't pull it.
• Sort the board by amount, newest, name, the zone a target was last seen in, or who was seen most recently.
• The file on every target: click a bounty for where they were last seen, the zones they keep to, the
hours they're usually about, every sighting by you and other Wanted users, and their deaths. Sightings of
wanted players are kept for a month.
• Kill the target and the claim files itself from your honorable kill. Another player's client that saw
the death witnesses it. The earliest kill wins.
• The poster confirms or disputes, then pays by mail in one click. Both sides' clients record the
payment, so paid and unpaid are facts, not claims.
• Kill proof: when your kill claims a bounty, a stamp with who, where, when and the kill id goes on
screen and the game saves a screenshot. Posters see you have proof; if a kill is disputed, post it in
pvp-salt on the Forever PvP Discord.
Your wanted poster
• The price on your head: every bounty the other faction has ever posted on you, paid or not, adds up.
You get an alert when someone puts a price on you.
• Open Your wanted poster from the menu (or /wanted poster): your own character on a painted poster
with your name and that total. Take screenshot saves it to share anywhere.
• Set amount shows any reward you like, just for fun. The poster marks it "(allegedly)".

Reputation from the record
• Bounty hunters get a level and a reliability rating from witnessed and confirmed kills.…

2.0.4 (2026-10-28) — Test Mode fixesBug Fixes
• Test Mode no longer shows your real buffs on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and WoW Forever. Whenever your buffs changed during a test, for example when you recast a seal, your real buff icons came back among the sample ones, and a buff that wore off during the test popped a real ready icon. A test now shows only its samples, and your buffs come back the moment it ends.
• Test Mode no longer shows debuffs you put on your target. With Offensives turned on, a debuff you cast on your target during a test on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic or Mists of Pandaria Classic appeared among the sample icons and stayed there after it wore off, until the test ended. On retail, a test started mid-fight could pick one up when combat ended. A debuff still on your target when the test ends shows again right away.
Improvements
• Marked compatible with retail patch 12.1.7. The retail .toc now lists the 12.1.7 interface version, so Cooldown Master does not show as out of date on that patch.
addons.description:
A timeline-style cooldown tracker for World of Warcraft. Your spells, items, potions, and trinkets glide along lanes toward a ready edge, with depleting bars and pop-up alerts the moment they come up. The visual companion to Blizzard's built-in Cooldown Manager. Install it and it just works. Your cooldowns show up automatically, in your own language, with deep customization there if you want it.

Runs on Midnight (retail 12.1), Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic, and WoW Forever from one code base, ships in seven languages, and registers a LibDataBroker launcher plus minimap button so panel addons like Titan Panel, Bazooka, Arcana, and other LibDataBroker displays pick it up automatically.

WoW Forever support is a work in progress, so expect bugs. Forever plays by the original game's rules, but it runs on the modern retail client, so Cooldown Master finds your spells there the Classic way and reads their cooldowns the Retail way. Wherever this page says Classic, it means Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, and Mists of Pandaria Classic. Forever is called out on its own wherever it differs, and Flavor differences has the full list.

Contents
Using it

1. What it does
2. How it works, and why Retail settles in after a few casts
3. Quick start
4. Lanes
5. Bars
6. Ready boxes
7. What gets tracked
8. Filters and routing
9. Highlights and flags
10. Custom cooldowns
11. Text tags
12. Test mode
13. Appearance and media
14. Masque
15. Profiles
16. Panel addons and the minimap button
17. Slash commands
18. Flavor differences
19. Languages

For developers

20. Midnight and the secret-value API
21. The localization pipeline
22. Building and running locally

Project

23. What is next
24. Credits
25. Found a bug or have an idea?
26. License

What it does
Cooldown Master shows you when your abilities come back, in three different styles, and you can use any mix of them at once.

Lanes are the signature view. Every ability gets an icon that travels along a lane toward a "ready" edge, at a speed set by its own cooldown. Long cooldowns sit at the far end, imminent ones crowd the ready edge, and the whole rotation fans out by urgency so you read it at a glance.

Bars are the classic view. A tidy list of depleting status bars, each with an icon, the spell name, and a live countdown, sorted by time remaining.

Ready boxes are alerts. An icon pops the instant a cooldown finishes, holds for a few seconds, then fades.

Out of the box you get three lanes, one bar frame, and one ready box, so you can see the three styles side by side and keep whichever suits you. Everything routes to Lane 1 except your potions, which start on Lane 2, and Lane 3 is left empty as a spare. Every cooldown can be sent to any combination of the three, either by category or one spell at a time.

Cooldown Master complements Blizzard's built-in Cooldown Manager rather than replacing it. On Retail it reads the same category sets. On the Classic flavors, which have no Cooldown Manager, and on WoW Forever, it scans your spellbook instead. Either way your abilities appear automatically with nothing to set up, and it adds the timeline, the bars, and the ready alerts that the built-in one does not have.

It only ever displays information. It never casts, queues, or automates anything.

How it works, and why Retail settles in after a few casts
To place an icon on a timeline, Cooldown Master has to know how long that cooldown really is, including your talents and your haste.

On Classic that number is readable at any time, so there is nothing to learn and nothing to wait for.…

releases.changelog:
2.0.4 (2026-10-28) — Test Mode fixesBug Fixes
• Test Mode no longer shows your real buffs on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and WoW Forever. Whenever your buffs changed during a test, for example when you recast a seal, your real buff icons came back among the sample ones, and a buff that wore off during the test popped a real ready icon. A test now shows only its samples, and your buffs come back the moment it ends.
• Test Mode no longer shows debuffs you put on your target. With Offensives turned on, a debuff you cast on your target during a test on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic or Mists of Pandaria Classic appeared among the sample icons and stayed there after it wore off, until the test ended. On retail, a test started mid-fight could pick one up when combat ended. A debuff still on your target when the test ends shows again right away.
Improvements
• Marked compatible with retail patch 12.1.7. The retail .toc now lists the 12.1.7 interface version, so Cooldown Master does not show as out of date on that patch.

2.0.3 (2026-10-27) — Ranked spell and retail combat fixesBug Fixes
• A spell with ranks no longer shows its cooldown twice on Classic Era and Burning Crusade Classic. After you cast rank 2 or higher of a spell that puts a buff on you and has a cooldown, such as Divine Protection, Divine Shield, Blessing of Protection or Sprint, a second copy of its cooldown appeared once the buff wore off: a second bar, a second lane icon and a second ready icon. Cooldown Master lists a spell under its first rank, so it took the higher rank's buff for a separate spell and then read the shared cooldown for it too. The buff still shows while it is up, and the cooldown now shows once.
• A higher rank's buff no longer pops a ready icon while its spell is still on cooldown. Casting Divine Protection rank 2, for example, popped a "Divine Protection" ready icon the moment its buff wore off, with nearly 5 minutes of cooldown left. A buff that outlasts its cooldown, such as Ice Barrier, still pops when it ends, since the spell really is ready by then.
• Ticking the Buff column on a spell with ranks now works at every rank, the same as at rank 1. It only ever matched rank 1's buff, so from rank 2 up the buff ignored the lane, ready box and bar you chose for it, and Filters > Buffs listed the spell twice.
• Aura gained custom cooldowns no longer raise a Lua error in every fight on retail. Since patch 12.1 the game raises an error when an addon reads your buffs during combat, where it used to hand back hidden values. With an Aura gained custom cooldown set up, that error came up again and again through every fight. Cooldown Master now reads your buffs only once combat ends, as it already did on WoW Forever. An Aura gained custom still cannot fire mid-fight on retail, because the game keeps your buffs hidden until combat ends. /cm buffs in combat now says the read was blocked instead of raising an error.
• Pressing Detect on a custom cooldown during a fight on retail no longer raises a Lua error or fills in a buff you already had. Detect now does nothing until combat ends, as on WoW Forever, so press it after the fight.

2.0.2 (2026-10-20) — Masque and WoW Forever fixesBug Fixes
• Turning off a Cooldown Master group in Masque no longer leaves its icons as black squares. Masque moves an icon behind its border while it skins it, and nothing moved it back when you switched the group off, so Cooldown Master's own black icon border covered the art until a /reload. Lane icons, ready boxes and bars now come straight back the moment you turn a group off, including icons that were not on screen at the time, and bar icons no longer keep a leftover Masque ring.
• Buffing a groupmate mid-fight on WoW Forever no longer shows up as your own buff. Forever blocks addons from reading your buffs in combat, so Cooldown Master follows what you cast, and until now it could not tell who a buff landed on. A blessing you put on a groupmate appeared on your own lane and could clear the icon of your own blessing until combat ended. Cooldown Master now reads who each buff was cast on. Seals and anything you cast on yourself restart at once, as before. When the buff you put on someone else shares its name with one you are wearing, or is a party-wide buff such as Arcane Brilliance or Prayer of Fortitude that may have reached you too, your own icon keeps its old timer and leaves quietly instead of popping a ready box, and comes back with its real timer if the buff is still up when combat ends.
• /cm help no longer lists the offensives commands on WoW Forever, where offensive tracking does not run.
Thanks
• yisisixu on GitHub — for the Filters page suggestions that shaped 2.0.0's search box, per-category defaults and Defaults overview, which went uncredited in 2.0.0's notes.

2.0.1 (2026-10-13) — Holy Strike fix for WoW ForeverBug Fixes
• A spell you use again the moment it comes off cooldown no longer gets stuck at the ready end of its lane on WoW Forever. Holy Strike showed it most, but any spell with ranks could do it, Hammer of Justice included. Forever reports the rank you cast, while Cooldown Master had the spell listed under a different rank, so it never saw the recast. The icon sat at the ready end through the whole next cooldown, its ready box came a full cooldown late, and it stayed stuck for as long as you kept using the spell the moment it came back. It now restarts the instant you cast. This is Forever only. Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and retail are untouched. Thanks to wimpby on Discord for the report.

2.0.0 (2026-10-12) — A new settings windowNew Features
• A brand new settings window. Cooldown Master's options now open in the same window as Everything Quests, EQ Objective Tracker and Everything Delves. A sidebar on the left holds Global, Lanes, Ready, Bars, Filters, Colors, Profiles and About, and each page is laid out in cards. Lanes, Ready and Bars open into their sections, and a switch across the top of each page picks which lane, box or bar frame you are editing. Click an open group again to fold it away. The window opens on the last page you used, per character. Every setting carries over exactly as you left it, and nothing resets.
• Unlock Frames and Test sit at the bottom of every page that changes what you see, so you can drag a lane or run a test without leaving the page you are tuning. Test turns into Stop Test while one is running, and closing the window ends it, as before.
• Click any slider's number to type an exact value.
• Find a cooldown in seconds. Each category's list in Filters has a search box that narrows it as you type, and the column headings carry the explanations instead of every row. The Defaults page now shows at a glance where each category sends its cooldowns, and clicking one opens it.
• What's New now appears only for releases that bring new features. A release with only fixes stays quiet, and the next feature release lists it too, so nothing is missed. If you have been away for several versions, it lists everything since you last looked, and a first install no longer opens it at all. The chat link option and Don't show these again work as before.
Improvements
• Settings that do nothing in your current setup are hidden, and settings a switch turns off are dimmed. Grow Direction and Height disappear for a Spread lane, for example, In Group and In Instance dim while Always is ticked, and Raise On Mouseover dims unless tooltips are on and frames are locked.
• A lane's labels are one table in its Text section, a row per label, with each label's position in percent or seconds to match how it is anchored.
• Bars has its own Text section for the name and time text, which makes its other sections much shorter.
• Highlight Style offers None, Border and Flash. Glow and Border + Flash always drew exactly what Flash draws, so they are gone from the list. If you had one picked, it keeps drawing as it always has and shows as Flash.
• Four tooltips that described their setting wrongly are corrected: a lane's Mode, Hand Off Below, Flags and Route by Cooldown Length. Many settings that had no tooltip now have one, and the bars' time font settings no longer claim to work on retail only. They work on every client.
• Medium Up To can no longer be set below Short Up To. Cooldown Master already treated it that way, so the slider now matches what it does.
• Copying a profile now asks first. It used to overwrite your current profile the moment you clicked. Everything in the window that erases or overwrites settings now asks in red: Copy, Delete, Reset, Import, Set All and deleting a custom cooldown.
• Profiles is one list. Your active profile is highlighted, and every other one has Switch, Copy and Delete beside it. New Profile, Duplicate Current, Export and Import are on the same page.
• The Colors page lists your own class first.
• Test Mode no longer offers Buff Bars on Classic Era, Burning Crusade Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic or WoW Forever, where that category does not exist.
• Links open in a copy box you cannot accidentally edit, for Discord, CurseForge, GitHub and exported profiles.
• The Options Window scale now stops at the largest size that fits your screen.
• The About page lists EQ Objective Tracker with the other addons.
• Escape closes the window out of combat. In combat, use its close button.

addons.description:
Your signature in Azeroth.

Download on CurseForge ·
GitHub Releases ·
Report a bug

Make your mark on every message.

Azeroth Signature automatically adds a signature of your choice to the chat messages you send, so everyone knows who's talking, whether that's on your alt, (( OOC )) for out-of-character chatter, or anything else you can think of. Set it once, pick the channels, and forget about it.
Why you'll like it
• Set it and forget it. Type your message as usual; the signature is added for you when you press Enter.
• You pick where it shows. Say, Yell, Party, Raid, Instance, Guild, Officer, Whisper and custom channels, each one a checkbox.
• Not on every character. Add the characters that should stay unsigned and Azeroth Signature leaves them alone.
• Plays nice with commands. Slash commands like /dance or /roll are never touched, and a message is never signed twice.
• Clean, native settings. A single options panel with a live preview, right inside the game's own settings.
• Tiny and standalone. One small addon, no dependencies, nothing running in the background.
Ideas for your signature
Anything up to 100 characters works. A few favourites:

| Signature | Great for |
|---|---|
| | Letting people know who's behind your alt |
| (( OOC )) | Marking out-of-character messages while roleplaying |
| [Tank] | Announcing your role in groups |
| ~ | A subtle personal mark |
FeaturesSignature
• Choose any custom prefix; a space is added automatically between it and your message
• Turn the whole thing on or off with one checkbox
• Live preview in the options, so you see exactly how a message will look: Hello, Azeroth!
Channels
Tick the channels that should carry your signature (all are ticked by default):

> Say · Yell · Party · Raid · Instance Chat · Guild · Officer · Whisper · Custom channels (/1, /2, …)

All and None buttons make it quick. If Raid is ticked, messages sent to Instance Chat are signed as well, because WoW reports /raid in an instance group as Instance Chat.
Excluded characters
Enter character names separated by commas (e.g. AltCharacter, Mage123, MyWarrior). Names are not case-sensitive. The Add current button adds the character you're playing right now.
Smart rules
| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| You type a slash command (/dance, /roll, …) | Not signed |
| The message already starts with your signature | Not signed again |
| You're in combat | Not signed (chat text isn't modified during combat, in line with Retail's restrictions) |
| The character is on your exclusion list | Not signed |
| The channel isn't ticked | Not signed |

addons.description:
The emote soundboard for your roleplay.

Download on CurseForge ·
GitHub Releases ·
Report a bug

Hit a button, play a beat.

Thespian turns your favourite roleplay lines and emotes into big, clickable buttons, like a soundboard, but for your character. Instead of retyping /me strokes their chin thoughtfully. for the hundredth time, you click once and get on with the scene.

Out of the box you get 70+ ready-made emotes. When they aren't enough, build your own in a few seconds and they'll show up as buttons right next to the built-in ones.
Why you'll like it
• One click, one beat. Greetings, gestures, emotions, actions and spoken lines are all a click away.
• Your voice, your buttons. Create custom emotes with their own label, channel and category.
• Target-aware. Write %t and Thespian swaps in your target's name, so nods in greeting to %t. becomes "Uther nods in greeting to Arthas."
• Looks like it belongs in WoW. Blizzard-style dialog frame, dark tooltip-style panels, gold accents, no foreign UI libraries.
• Light and standalone. One small addon, no dependencies, nothing running in the background.
• Works everywhere. Retail, Classic Era (including Hardcore and Seasonal), TBC Anniversary and Mists of Pandaria Classic, from the same download.
• Never speaks for you. Thespian only sends a message when you click a button or press Enter.
FeaturesThe soundboard
Six tabs, 15 buttons per page:

| Tab | What's in it | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Greetings | Hellos, goodbyes, salutes | Wave, Bow, Tip Hat, Clasp Arms, Well Met |
| Gestures | Body language | Cross Arms, Stroke Chin, Hand on Weapon, Raise Eyebrow |
| Emotions | Feelings you can see | Laugh, Sigh, Smirk, Tears Up, Tremble |
| Actions | Things your character does | Read Tome, Sharpen Blade, Study Map, Pour Drink |
| Speech | Spoken lines and OOC notes | Excuse Me, I Mean No Harm, To Arms!, (( brb )) |
| Custom | Whatever you invent | Anything you create |

Hover any button to preview exactly what will appear in chat.
The emote builder
Click + New Emote and pick:

| Type | Sends | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Emote (/me) | An emote line in orange | raises a tankard in toast. |
| Say | /s | Well met, friend! |
| Yell | /y | Hold the line! |
| Party | /p | (( afk 2 min )) |
| Standard emote | A built-in emote by token | WAVE, BOW, LAUGH |

You also choose which tab the button lives on, and a live preview shows you the chat line as you type. Your buttons are shown in green. Right-click one to edit or delete it.
Quick emote
A text box at the bottom of the window sends anything you type as a /me emote. It's handy for the line that doesn't deserve its own button.
Options
Open them from the Options button, the minimap button (right-click), /thespian options, or in the game's own settings under AddOns → Thespian:
• Show or hide the minimap button
• Close the window after using an emote
• Show or hide button tooltips
• Lock the window position
• Window scale (50%–150%) and opacity (40%–100%)
• Reset window position / reset options (your custom emotes are kept)
Minimap button
A golden theatre mask on your minimap. Left-click opens the soundboard, right-click opens the options, drag to reposition. It also works with square minimaps, and on Retail you'll find Thespian in the addon compartment too.

addons.changelog:
Changelog
All notable changes to nxPanels. Versions follow Semantic Versioning.
1.1.1 — 2026-10-23
• Retail: compatible with patch 12.1.5 (interface 120105).
1.1.0 — 2026-10-23
New:
• TBC Anniversary support (interface 20505 and 20506): layouts per talent group, like on WoW Forever.
• Every language of the game: German, Spanish (Spain and Mexico), Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Korean, in addition to English, French and Chinese. Reviews by native speakers welcome.
• Library: add all the files of a folder at once (paste the paths copied from the file explorer); the texture browser has a "My library" tab; your files work even when the game does not index them yet, and a full Windows path is reduced to the game path.
• What's new window, shown once at the first start of a new version; it can be turned off, and opened again from the settings.
• Welcome window after the import of your kgPanels / kgPanels Reloaded layouts, shown once: what changed, and how to open nxPanels. Players who already updated to 1.0.0 see it once too.
• The sidebar of the window shows the client and the exact version of the game, for troubleshooting.

Fixed:
• A script hiding its panel (self:Hide()) no longer sees it shown again by the addon (on target change, Shift, combat…).
• Borders are drawn exactly like the borders of the game (they were 1 pixel off).
• Import: a panel named like the frame it follows (for example "Minimap") follows that frame again; layouts already imported are repaired.
• A duplicated panel keeps the exact position of the original.
• No more Lua error from LibSharedMedia when a library file is not found by the game yet.
• When kgPanels is installed but not loaded by the game (made for another client), a message explains how to import its layouts.
• Clearer warning about scripts when importing a layout.
• Updated libraries: LibSharedMedia, LibSerialize, LibDBIcon.
1.0.0 — 2026-09-29
kgPanels Reloaded is now nxPanels, a complete rewrite. Nothing to do: your layouts, panels, folders, profiles and custom art are imported automatically on the first start. Your old data is never modified, and /nxp import imports it again at any time.
New
• Configuration window (/nxp): layouts, panels in folders, library, import / export, profiles, settings. Every change is shown at once. Three styles (Workshop, Ink, Night) and an accent color.
• Edit mode (/nxp edit): move and resize with the mouse, snapping, alignment guides, multiple selection, arrow keys, undo.
• Backgrounds: Blizzard images and a texture browser with thumbnails; automatic class, faction or target colors.
• Text variables without code: {zone}, {time}, {fps}, {latency}, {gold}, {currency:}, {item:}… and every game icon.
• Display conditions without scripts (combat, group, place, mount, target, pet battles, macro conditions), opacity in combat or under the mouse, fades.
• Templates, layouts per specialization (talent group on WoW Forever), profiles per class or faction.
• Sharing of layouts, folders and single panels with a text string; old kgPanels export strings are read too.
• Scripts with a syntax check that shows the line of the error.
• WoW Forever support, and full support for Chinese clients: English, French, Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
• API for other addons and media packs (nxPanels.RegisterMedia).
Good to know
• Old scripts keep working (kgPanels becomes nxPanels, same functions).
• The kgPanels_Reloaded and kgPanelsConfig_Reloaded folders only let nxPanels read your old data: keep them.
• Problem or question? Comments on CurseForge or GitHub.
addons.description:
Artistic panels for your World of Warcraft interface: backgrounds, borders, text and scripts,

placed anywhere and attached to any frame. Build an interface that is truly yours.

Features
Panels
• Backgrounds: solid color, gradient, your own textures, SharedMedia textures and Blizzard images (atlases), chosen in a browser with thumbnails.
• Borders from any border texture, with size, insets and color.
• Automatic colors: class, faction, reaction of the target.
• Text with the font of your client language, and live variables without code: {zone}, {time}, {fps}, {latency}, {gold}, {currency:}, {item:}… plus every game icon.
• Attach a panel to any frame of the game or of another addon (Bartender, Details!, chat…) and it follows it.

Display without scripts
• Show or hide on conditions: combat, group or raid, instance type, mount, target, pet battles, or any macro condition ([combat] show; hide).
• Opacity at rest, in combat and under the mouse, with fades.

Creation
• Configuration window (/nxp), loaded only when you open it: changes are drawn at once.
• Edit mode (/nxp edit): move and resize with the mouse, snapping to the screen and to other panels with guides, arrow keys, multiple selection, alignment, undo.
• Templates to start from (info bar, bar frame, chat background, combat glow…).
• Folders to organize large layouts.
• Scripts for advanced users (OnLoad, OnEvent, OnUpdate, OnClick…), with a syntax check that shows the line of the error.

Layouts and profiles
• Several layouts, switched in one click or automatically per specialization (Retail) or talent group (WoW Forever, TBC Anniversary).
• Profiles per character, class or faction.
• Share a layout, a folder or a single panel with a text string (!NXP1!…), with a warning when it contains scripts.
• Your own backgrounds and borders by file path, and an API for media packs (nxPanels.RegisterMedia).

Light: the display engine is small and always loaded; the window and the import module are separate addons.

addons.description:
Stop typing “DELETE”. Just click Delete.

Deleting a valuable item in World of Warcraft makes you type the word DELETE into the confirmation box every time. Easy Delete replaces that popup with a clean dialog that shows exactly what you are about to destroy: its icon, name, quality and stack size. One click on Delete, or a press of Enter, and it's gone.

Features
• One click to delete. No more typing “DELETE” for rare, epic or quest items. Enter deletes, Escape keeps the item.
• See what you delete. The item's icon, name in its quality colour, quality and stack size. Hover the item for its full tooltip.
• Quest items are flagged. A warning shows when deleting the item also abandons its quest.
• A modern look. Dark panels, thin borders and a crimson accent, matching Crescendo and EllesmereUI. With EllesmereUI installed, the dialog uses its font.
• Every version of the game. One download works on Retail, all Classic flavors and WoW Forever.
• Your choice of style. The first time you log in, Easy Delete asks which you prefer: its own dialog, or the game's popup without having to type “DELETE”. Change it any time in Options > AddOns > Easy Delete or with /easydelete.
• Plays nicely with other addons. If another addon has already dealt with the delete popup, Easy Delete stays out of its way, so you never get two dialogs.
